terminology.visibility: action/service surface classification: 'advertised' = declared in a shipped SCPD document AND (at service level) present in the served device_description.xml serviceList (16 of 17 services, everything except AudioIn); 'hidden' = service omitted from the serviceList even though its SCPD ships (AudioIn only); 'internal' = callable on the wire but not SCPD-declared; supported class, EMPTY on this build (verified: all 205 canonical actions appear in their service's SCPD actionList)
terminology.reachability: 'callable' = dispatched to a real implementation; 'hidden-callable' = reachable by action name on the control path but not SCPD-declared: EMPTY on this build
terminology.fault_vocabulary_caveat: identical fault-code vocabularies across builds do NOT prove identical error behavior; a fault-code vocabulary delta claim is made only where control flow was also compared

canonical_action_records.definition: every action object under services.*.actions in this dataset; 195 unique action names (some names recur across services)

scpd_defined.definition: actions declared in shipped SCPD documents (opt/htdocs/xml/<Svc>1.xml actionLists): all 205 canonical records + 2 removed SystemProperties actions (ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX, ResetThirdPartyCredentials) that remain SCPD-advertised but have no canonical record because they are absent from the 86.x dispatch surface
scpd_defined.source: documentation.json visibility field + SystemProperties dispatch note

device_advertised.definition: SCPD-defined actions on the 16 service registrations present in the served device_description.xml serviceList; excludes AudioIn whose service is hidden (SCPD ships but service unlisted); includes the 2 stale SystemProperties advertisements

binary_dispatched.definition: canonical records that resolve to a binary dispatch path; 199 reach a real implementation handler (141 ptr-table 'direct', 57 id-table 'virtual', 1 strcmp chain) and 6 resolve to the AudioIn reject-all stub
binary_dispatched.source: documentation.json dispatch records; extractor action_tables carry 195 rows across 14 tables - the shared ConnectionManager table 0x10f118d4 binds both CM services (6 records from 3 rows) and QPlay dispatches via a strcmp chain rather than a table

implemented_actions.definition: binary-dispatched records whose dispatch reaches a real implementation (excludes the 6 reject-all stubs)

removed_stale.definition: SCPD-defined actions removed from the live dispatch surface in 86.x: 6 canonical records dispatched to the AudioIn reject-all 401 stub + 2 SystemProperties actions absent from the dispatch table entirely (a stub name lookup miss faults 401 identically, so wire behavior matches the stubs)

meta.scpd_crossvalidation: SCPD ground-truth cross-validation (post-rootfs-sweep): all 16 advertised services in opt/htdocs/xml/*.xml compared against the extracted dispatch/SV tables. ACTION PARITY 206/208: the only SCPD-only entries are the two known advertised-but-removed SystemProperties ops ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX + ResetThirdPartyCredentials; the 6 AudioIn actions advertise AND dispatch to reject-all 401 stubs, consistent with prior findings. STATE-VARIABLE PARITY: all SCPD names present in the binary tables; binary additionally dispatches UNADVERTISED SVs: Queue {QueueID,QueueOwnerID}, RenderingControl {HeightChannelLevel,RoomCalibrationBondedZoneInfo,SonarCalibrationAvailable,SonarEnabled}, hidden state variables served by handlers but never declared in SCPD. ARGUMENT PARITY: full arg-name match on spot-checked services (AVTransport all 42 actions). This validates the binary-driven extraction pipeline against the shipped advertisement files end-to-end.

request_vtable.summary: For every inbound SOAP control call, the firmware builds a temporary TRequest object on the UPnP worker's stack. Action wrappers do not parse the raw HTTP request directly. They use TRequest to register named input arguments and retrieve their values by name, allocate output argument records, validate the parsed request, send SOAP faults, and serialize the final response.
request_vtable.vtable: 0x10f10f20. f_107310c8 installs this address into TRequest+0x0 at 0x1073114c.
request_vtable.constructor: f_107310c8. The tunneled-control path constructs TRequest at caller sp+0xd8 at callsite 0x10696404, immediately before f_1069388c dispatches it at 0x10696428. The constructor initializes fields through +0x3a78; deleting destructor f_10730b90 passes size 0x3a80 to the deallocator, proving the complete object size.
request_vtable.destructor: f_10730a94 is the ordinary destructor; f_10730b90 is the deleting destructor. The stack-resident request is destroyed by f_10730a94 at 0x1069649c after dispatch returns.
request_vtable.0x04: f_10730b90: deleting destructor; destroys TRequest then passes size 0x3a80 to the deallocator.
request_vtable.0x08: f_10730414: validate/materialize the queued input-argument records by name. At 0x10730480 it calls record vtable +0x0c (f_1055eb5c, loads record+0x34); 0x10730488 forwards the returned name as r4 to input backend +0x08 at 0x10730490. The backend at request+0x3a74 is set at 0x10731208 from constructor stack argument sp+0x5c. On the inbound f_106960f8 path, 0x106963a8 constructs the backend at caller sp+0x50 via f_109f02f4; 0x106963e0 supplies that address as the constructor's second stack argument. f_109f02f4 installs vtable 0x10f98720 at 0x109f0354, whose +0x08 is f_109f01f8. That method takes strlen(name) at 0x109f0238, hashes the string via f_10806d50 at 0x109f025c, selects a bucket at 0x109f026c..0x109f027c, and searches via f_109f07b0. The search checks key length at 0x109f086c..0x109f0878 and exact bytes via memcmp at 0x109f0890. A match returns its value pointer at 0x109f02a4; a miss returns null at 0x109f02e8. Thus sequential record allocation is not positional input matching. A found value is passed to f_10560708 and f_10560a58 at 0x107304a8..0x107304b0. Record flags +0x31 and +0x30 govern acceptance at 0x107304b4..0x107304c8, including on lookup miss. Returns 1 for zero records or when all records pass, and 0 when a record fails both flag checks.
request_vtable.0x0c: f_10730524: serialize and commit the SOAP success response through the response backend stored at TRequest+0x3a78.
request_vtable.0x10: f_10730714: alias thunk to f_10730524, the same success-response commit path.
request_vtable.0x14: f_1073029c: emit a non-success UPnP/SOAP result using the code supplied in r4 through the response backend at +0x3a78; action wrappers use this for faults such as 402.
request_vtable.0x18: f_10730354: fixed-code wrapper around +0x14 that supplies code 1000.
request_vtable.0x1c: f_1073017c: allocate the next sequential input record and register the argument name supplied in r4, not a positional-only input fetch. Slot word 0x10f10f3c points here. The function selects a 0x38-byte record from request+0x3168 using count +0x3a68, then forwards r4 unchanged to record vtable +0x08 at 0x107301c8. The constructor initializes these records via f_10561414 at 0x107311bc, which installs vtable 0x10eebf40 at 0x10561438. Its +0x08 is f_1055eb4c, whose store at 0x1055eb50 saves the name pointer at record+0x34. Request +0x08 later retrieves this name for backend lookup. In plain English, wrappers reserve input records in sequence, but each record identifies its input by the supplied name.
request_vtable.0x20: f_1073017c: same named input-record registration as +0x1c, not a separate positional-only path. Independently checked slot word 0x10f10f40 also points to 0x1073017c, so the unchanged r4 name reaches f_1055eb4c through the same 0x107301c8 call and is stored at record+0x34.
request_vtable.0x24: f_107300dc: allocate the next sequential output record from request+0x34e8 using count +0x3a6c, retaining the wrapper's output-name pointer rather than treating it as documentation only. Calls at 0x10730120 and 0x10730160 forward r4 unchanged through record vtable +0x08. Output records receive vtable 0x10f10e88 at 0x107311f0; its +0x08 is f_1055eaf0, which stores r4 at record+0x50 (0x1055eaf4). During response commit, 0x107305b8 calls record +0x0c (f_1055eb00, reads +0x50), and 0x107305c0..0x107305d4 forwards that name to response backend +0x1c. Allocation is sequential, but the name is retained for response generation.
request_vtable.0x28: f_107301ec: alternate output-record allocator; additionally binds record+0x48 to the request subinterface at TRequest+0x2c4c.
request_vtable.0x2c: f_1073167c: return TRequest+0x410, a 25-byte constructor-copied metadata string used by the tunneled request path. No canonical SOAP action wrapper calls this slot.
request_vtable.0x30: f_1073168c: return the u32 at TRequest+0x42c. Its constructor source is the first halfword of the 3-halfword descriptor produced by f_10759f1c; no canonical SOAP action wrapper calls this slot.
request_vtable.0x34: f_1073169c: return the embedded request/zone context at TRequest+0x430. GetZoneGroupAttributes proves its consumer shape: ctx+0x6c must be non-null and ctx+0x178 supplies the zone-group implementation object.
request_vtable.0x38: f_107316ac: return the current 16-bit request result/status field at TRequest+0x3a70. Service dispatchers use it after raising an action-name fault.
request_vtable.0x40: f_10730268, installed at vtable 0x10f10f20+0x40, writes fixed values into the caller's 8-byte descriptor at r4 and returns 1. It loads byte 0 (0x10730268), clears its upper three bits with clrlwi r9,r9,27 at 0x10730274 (byte 0 &= 0x1f) and stores it back at 0x10730278; it then stores byte 1 = 0x54 (0x10730280), byte 2 = 1 (0x10730288) and the 32-bit word at +4 = 0 (0x10730290). Byte 3 is not written, and no other input is read. SOAP caller: AVTransport GetTransportInfo (dispatch entry 0x10eb3108 names GetTransportInfo and points to f_102fbb60). The wrapper saves the request r4 in r31 at 0x102fbb88. After input validation and a zero implementation result, 0x102fbc78 loads request vtable +0x40 and 0x102fbc90 calls it with r3=request and r4=sp+0x14, an eight-byte zeroed descriptor. At 0x102fbc94..0x102fbca8, a zero return or descriptor byte 1 > 0x16 skips the state rewrite; byte 1 < 0x16 permits it, while byte 1 == 0x16 additionally requires byte 2 == 0 and the unsigned word at +4 <= 0xf653 (0x102fbd84..0x102fbd9c). The permitted rewrite compares the output state with TRANSITIONING at 0x102fbcb8 and replaces it with PLAYING at 0x102fbd7c only on equality. With this concrete TRequest implementation, byte 1 is always 0x54, so the rewrite is skipped and the implementation's state is emitted unchanged. In plain English, this request helper supplies descriptor data used by the wrapper to decide whether to report a transition as playback; the recovered TRequest always leaves the reported state alone. Another SOAP call through request +0x40 is recorded for ZoneGroupTopology BeginSoftwareUpdate at 0x10733284 and independently verified by the slot load at 0x10733278. The descriptor's broader protocol meaning is not inferred from these byte tests.
request_vtable.0x44: f_10731660: returns 1. IdentifyIRRemote at 0x10249dc8 and LearnIRCode at 0x10249f2c call this slot on every wait poll. Because the result is 1, the poll's compare against 0 does not end the wait.
request_vtable.layout: Key TRequest fields: +0x3168 input-record pool; +0x34e8 output-record pool; +0x3a68 input cursor/count; +0x3a6c output cursor/count; +0x3a70 current 16-bit result/status; +0x3a74 input/argument backend; +0x3a78 response backend; +0x410 tunneled metadata string; +0x42c descriptor word; +0x430 embedded request/zone context.
request_vtable.dispatch_chain: Inbound control path: f_106960f8 constructs stack TRequest via f_107310c8 at 0x10696404 -> f_1069388c performs SOAPAction/security handling -> (zp+0x3a8)->vtable[0x40] = f_10195810, an adjustor thunk that subtracts 0x3a8 and tail-calls the 13-service router f_101953c8 -> matched service vfunc +0x08 (for ZoneGroupTopology, f_10732ff8) -> matched action wrapper receives TRequest as r4. The request is destroyed after dispatch at 0x1069649c.
request_vtable.callsite_proof: GetZoneGroupAttributes f_10733878 directly verifies the externally relevant slots: +0x34 at 0x107338b0 returns the embedded context; +0x08 at 0x107338e4 validates inputs; +0x14 at 0x10733904 raises fault 402 on parse failure; +0x24 at 0x107339ac and following sites allocates output records; +0x0c at 0x10733a64 commits the success response. ZoneGroupTopology dispatcher f_10732ff8 raises 401 through +0x14 on an action-name miss, then tail-dispatches +0x38 to return the stored request result.
request_vtable.binary_evidence: Verified against rootfs-86.10-80260-1-9/opt/bin/anacapad, SHA-256 f60262a152aac48bd39bf0285d17d080e6820e37be12d0af9de7bffee8d3e257, version string 86.10-80260-dev-secbuild-20260826.
request_vtable.corrections: Earlier candidate request vtables 0x10ebc650/0x10ebd234 and the claimed request-at-route-container+0x288 were disproven. The exact constructor f_107310c8 and vptr store at 0x1073114c supersede those guesses. Slots +0x1c/+0x20 allocate input records sequentially and save names for the later name-based lookup in +0x08; +0x24 similarly retains output names for response generation. Sequential pool allocation does not mean argument names are ignored. Slot +0x38 is a status accessor rather than a finalize method.

/AlarmClock/Control.name: AlarmClock
/AlarmClock/Control.description: Advertised alarm and clock-settings service backed by the zone-player ac_impl engine. Its 17 action descriptors cover alarm creation/update/deletion/listing and clock, timezone, format and daily-index settings. The engine and its SOAP/list/event interfaces are statically constructed. In this build SetTimeNow and GetHouseholdTimeAtStamp are unconditional 401 workers after required-input validation, so advertisement does not imply clock-setting support. Service name misses fault 401 before any action worker executes; individual action faults are documented on their actions.

availability.notes: Service object constructed at zone-player init; always registered in this build - no feature-gate found at the registration site

CreateAlarm.description: Creates an alarm. Wrapper f_10734404 parses the ten SOAP inputs and dispatches the concrete ac_impl engine slot +0x34 -> f_1027a980. That method validates StartLocalTime, optional Duration, and Recurrence, builds the alarm record, persists it through f_1027a8f8 -> f_1027a7a8 -> f_10283998, publishes the new AlarmListVersion state, and returns record+0 as AssignedID.

AssignedID.validation: Produced only after the persistence path returns; value is the u32 written to alarm-record +0 by f_1028430c.

GetTimeNow.description: Returns current UTC and local wall-clock timestamps, the effective timezone rule, and the active time-source generation. Static engine slot +0x30 calls f_10273340. Disabled time source faults 800; normal success returns all four fields. This is a read, not a clock synchronization or timezone-table refresh.

implementation.description: Wrapper engine dispatch 0x107350cc -> f_10273340; engine+0x240 time-source slot +0x08 supplies UTC FILETIME, engine+0x232 supplies effective timezone, source+4 supplies generation.

CurrentUTCTime.description: Current system UTC converted from the active time source FILETIME and emitted as a space-separated date/time, without a timezone suffix.
CurrentUTCTime.accepted_values: Formatted calendar fields from FileTimeToSystemTime; no getter range validation.
CurrentUTCTime.special_values: No sentinel substitution; conversion failure is not surfaced as a fault.
CurrentUTCTime.validation: No input; conversion helper result is ignored.

evidence.notes: Locks engine+0x170. Calls time-source pointer engine+0x240 slot +0x08 at 0x102733cc with FILETIME output. Zero result formats the effective rule, unlocks, returns 800 at 0x102733f0 without copying outputs. Nonzero result saves source+4 generation at 0x10273464, formats effective rule engine+0x232 at 0x1027346c and unlocks at 0x10273478. UTC conversion f_10c3d4fc and local conversion f_10c3d9ec return values are ignored. Formats UTC/local using f_10c3c88c at 0x102734e0/0x102734f4, copies timezone/UTC/local with f_10906304 at 0x10273504/0x10273514/0x10273524, stores generation at 0x10273528, returns 0 at 0x1027352c. No other normal return code, persistence, or notification call. Guard failure at 0x10273534 aborts.

Engine constructor stores engine+0x248 at engine+0x240 (0x102762a8), installs time-source vptr 0x10eaa8ac at 0x102762b8, whose +0x08 entry 0x10eaa8b4 is f_10273800. Source+4 is initialized zero at 0x1027632c. f_10273800 tests source+4: zero returns false and may log NTPTimeOffset getUTCTimeNow is disabled (literal 0x10eaad58); nonzero calls gettimeofday at 0x102738a4, converts seconds/useconds to FILETIME and returns true. The gettimeofday status itself is not checked. It does not call a network time server on this read.

Format literal is %04hu-%02hu-%02hu %02hu:%02hu:%02hu, resolved through PIC table 0x11095d9c-0x8000. Reads year/month/day/hour/minute/second at +4/+6/+0xa/+0xc/+0xe/+0x10. Caller capacity 0x14 means at most 19 characters plus NUL, without T, Z, fractional seconds or offset. Year width is a minimum, not a range check. UTC helper f_10c3d4fc calls FileTimeToSystemTime at 0x10c3d53c; local helper f_10c3d9ec builds TIME_ZONE_INFORMATION from signed rule biases/transition fields and calls SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTime at 0x10c3dae4. Getter ignores their boolean results and does not map conversion failure to a fault; date objects were zero-initialized.

No inputs registered. Validation-zero loads 402 at 0x1073511c and faults through request slot +0x14 call 0x107350e8; worker nonzero uses same fault call. Success writes CurrentUTCTime, CurrentLocalTime, CurrentTimeZone via text slots at 0x1073514c/0x1073517c/0x107351ac, and generation via f_1055fcbc at 0x107351d0 (%u, literal 0x10f94c94). Commits through request +0x0c at 0x107351e4. Request validator f_10730414 returns 1 immediately at 0x1073051c for zero input records, so 402 is defensive and not reachable on the canonical fresh empty-input request. Wrapper stack guard at 0x107351ec aborts, not SOAP.

CurrentLocalTime.validation: No getter range check. Local conversion is after unlock and reads the live effective-rule pointer, not a private rule snapshot.

GetTimeZoneRule.description: Looks up an explicit timezone ID and returns its compact timezone rule, not XML or a timezone name. Wrapper f_107341cc calls the statically bound ac_impl slot +0x1c at 0x10eaa9b8, worker f_10273280. The worker reads timezones.xml through f_1015a6dc and serializes the selected 14-byte rule as 28 lowercase hexadecimal characters through f_10c3ce18. A missing or unusable table entry yields 28 zero characters with SOAP success, not an out-of-range fault.

Index.description: Required timezone ID to match against the ID attribute of a TimeZone entry in timezones.xml. This is independent of the player's currently selected timezone. It is not a positional array offset.
Index.format: Decimal strtol base 10, optional sign and leading whitespace; numeric prefix is sufficient. At most 23 lexical bytes survive NUL termination.
Index.accepted_values: Any present text passes this numeric conversion: no numeric prefix converts to 0, trailing nonnumeric text is ignored, and overflow follows 32-bit libc strtol saturation. The resulting 32-bit value is compared exactly with a nonnegative XML ID.
Index.range: No action-level range check; meaningful matches are nonnegative signed 32-bit IDs present in the table, not a compiled 0..N interval.
Index.special_values: Empty or nonnumeric text converts to ID 0. Negative results cannot match an eligible XML ID and produce the all-zero rule. Missing argument faults 402.
Index.validation: Request validation requires Index to be present. Type-tag 5 conversion does not check errno, end pointer, or numeric range. Unknown IDs do not fault.

TimeZone.description: A 28-character lowercase hexadecimal encoding of the 14-byte timezone rule. Fields in order are GMTBias (4 hex digits), standard Month, DayOfWeek, Day, Hour (2 each), standard Bias (4), daylight Month, DayOfWeek, Day, Hour (2 each), daylight Bias (4). Bias values are stored as 16-bit quantities, so negative minute biases appear in two's-complement form. This is the rule data, not a computed next-transition date.
TimeZone.semantic_type: packed timezone rule rendered as hexadecimal text
TimeZone.format: 28 lowercase hexadecimal characters, no separators or prefix; response buffer capacity 29 including NUL
TimeZone.unit: Bias fields are minutes; Month, DayOfWeek, Day and Hour retain the XML rule values.
TimeZone.special_values: 0000000000000000000000000000 means lookup failed or the table could not supply a usable complete entry; it is not an empty string. For entries without transition children, the initialized daylight Bias is -60 (ffc4) and other transition fields are zero.
TimeZone.default: none; always emitted on successful validation
TimeZone.validation: No output validity gate: even a failed lookup is formatted and committed.

SetTimeZone.description: Persists configured timezone ID and automatic DST flag through static engine +0x10 -> f_1027cf5c, reloads caches and updates change/version observers on success. Rejects negative parsed Index with 402, but does not require that a nonnegative ID exists in the timezone table. Missing entries can therefore be configured and produce zero cached rules.

implementation.description: f_1027cf5c -> f_10283998 TimeZone save -> f_10279c0c reload -> version/type-5 observer. Uses engine mutex +0x170.

Index.description: Required configured timezone ID. Parsed with permissive decimal strtol; the concrete setter rejects only negative resulting values, not unknown nonnegative IDs.
Index.format: decimal text with permissive numeric prefix conversion
Index.accepted_values: Nonnegative resulting signed 32-bit values; no compiled maximum or table-membership gate.
Index.special_values: Present empty/nonnumeric text becomes ID 0. Missing input faults 402. Unknown nonnegative ID is saved; lookup supplies zero rule.
Index.validation: strtol(text,NULL,10), no errno/end-pointer/range check; worker signed comparison with zero.

evidence.notes: Required Index registration f_10561514 type tag 5 at 0x10734338; required AutoAdjustDst f_10561444 type tag 1 at 0x1073435c. Canonical validator f_10730414 fetches and finalizes records; missing required records return false. f_10560a58 bounds/NUL-terminates 24-byte numeric text buffers, truncating to 23 bytes. Tag 5 uses strtol(text,NULL,10) at 0x10560b34 and stores 32 bits; no errno, end-pointer or range test. Tag 1 at 0x10560b78..0x10560bcc compares case-insensitively with 1, true, yes -> byte 1; every other value -> 0. Present empty/nonnumeric Index becomes 0; present empty/unknown flag becomes false. Worker rejects only negative resulting Index, not missing table entries.

Signed Index <0 returns 402 at 0x1027cf88 before locking. Nonnegative Index and byte flag are stored in stack TimeZone pair at +0x18/+0x1c. Locks engine+0x170, creates writer context vptr 0x10eaa93c with engine+0x214 directory, engine+0x7f08 identity and next version engine+0x7f2c+1. Calls f_10283998 at 0x1027d054 with only TimeZone argument r4 nonnull (alarm argument r6 is null). Nonzero save result unlocks and returns unchanged. Success calls f_10279c0c(engine,0) at 0x1027d078, copies identity to +0x7f10, increments +0x7f2c at 0x1027d0b0 and calls observer *(engine+0x7f00)->v[+0x14] with type 5, identity, version, zero at 0x1027d0b8, then unlocks and returns saved zero result.

If loaded Index or flag changed (comparison 0x1027a088 and 0x1027a3b4), writes engine+0x218 and +0x21c; f_10281dc0 updates timezone state; f_1015a6dc looks up ID from engine+0x7f0c, returning zero rule for missing/unusable entries. Copies raw rule to +0x224 and effective rule to +0x232, applies flag only to effective copy with f_10c3d094 at 0x1027a11c. Recomputes schedules with f_10276d7c and queues callbacks f_1027ca44/f_10276ba4 via f_10571cf8; marks +0x21d. Changed reload state invokes f_1067c6ec(engine+8) at 0x1027a2e8. Same pair skips timezone-cache recomputation, but outer setter still saves and increments its shared version.

Index.notes: Numeric text is bounded to 23 bytes before conversion. Overflow behavior belongs to strtol; no action-level check.

AutoAdjustDst.description: Required boolean text controlling the effective timezone rule. Case-insensitive 1, true or yes means enabled; every other present text means disabled.
AutoAdjustDst.format: case-insensitive truth spellings; all other text false
AutoAdjustDst.special_values: Present empty or unrecognized value -> false; missing input -> 402.
AutoAdjustDst.validation: No strict boolean rejection; flag is stored in TimeZone XML and applied to the effective rule only.

UpdateAlarm.description: Updates an existing alarm by ID. Wrapper f_107346ac parses ID plus the ten alarm fields and dispatches the concrete ac_impl engine slot +0x38 -> f_1027ac80. The engine validates StartLocalTime, optional Duration, and Recurrence, builds an update-mode alarm record (record+0x114=1), and commits it through f_1027a8f8 -> f_1027a7a8 -> f_10283998. The writer replaces the record whose ID matches and preserves all other alarms.

events.mechanism: Concrete source at engine+8 produces full/incremental direct e:propertyset XML. Its asynchronous sender reaches GENA NOTIFY encoding and plain/TLS writes. The same sender also publishes source topic 5 to registered Muse/WebSocket observers; the separate alarm-version producer publishes topic 6. Subscription eligibility, pending work and connection state gate delivery, so scheduling is not a delivery guarantee.
events.no_template_note: The concrete AlarmClock producer emits seven named e:property values directly. It does not emit a LastChange element; this follows the producer, not absence from a namespace-string registry.
events.wss_note: Source index 5 maps to alarmClock; f_102779a8 explicitly publishes index 6, alarmVersionChange. Shared source fanout reads source+0xc0, and both publications reach the concrete registered connection observer and WebSocket writer traced below. This proves static transport reachability for eligible subscriptions, not delivery to an absent or disconnected client.

evidence.notes: Constructor supplies AlarmClock name 0x10f96f34, topic index 5 (li r6,5 at 0x1027605c) and engine+8 to f_1067aec4 at 0x102760ec. That constructor stores topic index at source+0xc0 (0x1067afb0). Final source vptr 0x10eaaa28 has slot +0x14 at 0x10eaaa3c = f_1027834c, subtracting 8 then branching f_10278280. Slot +0x18 at 0x10eaaa40 = f_1067ab54 forwards to source slot +0x14. f_10278280 calls f_10277d6c with full-state flag 1 for nonnull first writer (0x102782d8), flag 0 for nonnull second writer (0x102782f0), under engine+0x170 lock. This resolves the service-specific event payload producer, independently of name similarity. Raw table words are 0x10eaaa3c=0x1027834c and 0x10eaaa40=0x1067ab54. Constructor 0x102761d4 (0x3969008c) forms source vptr 0x10eaaa28 from primary 0x10eaa99c; 0x1027620c (0x917d0008) installs it at engine+8. Generic handler 0x1067ab64 (0x81280014) loads this source slot +0x14, not a LastChange-specific renderer. The renderer, not shared sender dispatch, establishes direct properties.

Full-state branch 0x1027807c..0x10278238 emits seven direct e:property entries: TimeZone (effective rule engine+0x232, f_10c3ce18 gives 28 lowercase hex digits), TimeServer (source+8 string), TimeGeneration (source+4 unsigned), AlarmListVersion (engine+0x7ec0 identity, colon, unsigned revision +0x7edc), TimeFormat (+0x2dc), DateFormat (+0x2e0), DailyIndexRefreshTime (empty if flag +0x7ee8 is zero, otherwise f_10c3d264 formats +0x7ee9). Writers f_1067693c/f_10676968 bracket the propertyset; f_10676994/f_10676a44 bracket each property. No LastChange wrapper is used. Incremental branch checks dirty bytes +0x21d, +0x245, +0x244, +0x7ee0, +0x2e4, +0x7ef8; no dirty bytes means no document. TimeFormat and DateFormat share +0x2e4. It clears all six dirty bytes at 0x10277fa4..0x10277fbc after incremental emission; full-state branch bypasses that clearing. AlarmListVersion emission also calls f_102779a8 at 0x10277f18/0x10278198.

Concrete timezone-refresh producer compares raw rules, and only on change writes dirty byte engine+0x21d = 1 and calls f_1067c6ec(engine+8). This tails to f_1067c46c(source,0,0), which sets source pending +0x110 at 0x1067c4c8 and, if a live sender exists, calls f_10678c50 at 0x1067c5c8. Sender wake sets sender+0x10e = 1 at 0x10678c80 and signals its condition at 0x10678c88; missing sender takes diagnostic/return path. Thus mutation schedules asynchronous eventing, not synchronous guaranteed delivery. The installed source payload callbacks are identified separately; this evidence does not claim a socket send occurs within the setter.

Alarm version producer constructs identity:unsigned-revision from engine+0x7ec0/+0x7edc and passes the resulting string payload with topic index 6 to f_10677ccc at 0x10277b9c. f_10677ccc -> f_10677b94 -> f_10677970 at 0x10677bd4; f_10677970 maps the supplied index through f_109e1038 at 0x10677a88. f_109e1038 indexes 20-byte registry records at 0x110b8ce8. f_10098d34 builds index 5 alarmClock (literal 0x10f96140, record ID 20, tag 64) and index 6 alarmVersionChange (literal 0x10f9614c, record ID 24, tag 1). f_10677b94 invokes observer delivery f_1067b3a8 at 0x10677bf8, which iterates registered observers under the shared lock and invokes observer slot +8 at 0x1067b4b8. This establishes the topic-6 publisher; the concrete observer registration and transport continuation are traced separately below.

f_1067c46c calls f_10678c50 to mark sender pending and signal its condition. Consumer f_10679b14 walks registered sources and calls f_10683da0 at 0x10679e54. f_10683da0 checks source/group eligibility, clears source pending at 0x10683fdc, skips empty subscription groups (0x10683ff8..0x10684004), and dispatches source slot +0x18 at 0x1068406c. AlarmClock slot points to f_1067ab54, forwarding to the already-bound +0x14 producer. ZGT instead overrides +0x18 with f_1012abe0. Thus the concrete producers, not the SOAP snapshot workers, feed the sender. After property/subscription preparation f_106845b4 at 0x106841d8, the sender enters f_1068108c at 0x106841f0. No eligible group means no corresponding outgoing notification.

GENA branch calls header formatter f_10677350 at 0x106835f4. Formatter uses literal 0x10f00628 and __snprintf_chk at 0x1067740c: NOTIFY %s HTTP/1.1, HOST: %s:%d, CONNECTION: close, CONTENT-TYPE: text/xml, CONTENT-LENGTH: %d, NT: upnp:event, NTS: upnp:propchange, SID: %s, SEQ: %d, X-SONOS-SERVICETYPE: %s, CRLF-separated with a final blank line. f_10677478 is called at 0x10683650 and writes remaining buffered bytes: plain write at 0x106774e4, secure connection selection f_1056c6ac followed by f_1056c650/f_1056d9dc and mbedtls_ssl_write at 0x10677538. Positive full-length completion sets the completion byte at 0x106774fc; short/error results do not. Further sender branches call mbedtls_ssl_write at 0x10683768 and write at 0x10683900. This is actual socket output, unlike the property XML helpers.

Separate Muse fanout within the shared sender checks the subscription flags at 0x10682758..0x10682778, loads the source topic from source+0xc0 at 0x10682768, constructs the topic/payload handoff and calls f_10677b94 at 0x10682810. Consequently installed AlarmClock index 5 and ZGT index 72 reach the same registry/observer path as explicit topic-6 and topic-4 publications. f_10677b94 -> f_10677970 maps registry metadata through f_109e1038 and invokes f_1067b3a8. The latter first obtains matching event data through f_109e31b4 (0x1067b3f4); no match/empty result exits before observer dispatch.

Concrete WebSocket observer identity: f_106260c0 calls f_10625b7c, which allocates the connection and invokes f_106c3664 at 0x10625c34. Constructor calls f_10689000 then installs primary vptr 0x10f071e4 at 0x106c36d0 and observer vptr 0x10f07238 at connection+0xc4 (0x106c36d4). On successful f_10689310 setup, 0x106261b0..0x106261c4 registers connection+0xc4 with f_1067b318. That function links the object into global observer chain 0x11097824. f_1067b3a8 reads that chain at 0x1067b45c and calls observer slot +8 at 0x1067b4b8. Raw table 0x10f07240 contains f_106c2c18, which subtracts 0xc4 and branches f_106c2af4. This resolves the object identity, not merely a nearby WebSocket implementation.

Observer f_106c2af4 submits the supplied event vector to f_109e2064(connection+0xe8). f_109e2064 checks subscribed-event state through f_109e1e8c at 0x109e2100, queues eligible entries via f_109decc8 at 0x109e2114, and returns zero for an empty/no-eligible vector. Nonzero scheduled count wakes connection I/O through f_100ad260. Primary table 0x10f071e4 slot +0x14 contains drain f_106c2e1c. It uses the same context connection+0xe8 and callback vptr 0x10f071c4 (0x106c2e88..0x106c2ea0) with connection stored as callback+0x10 at 0x106c2e70. Drain calls f_109e3a1c -> f_109e36d8/f_109e296c; the latter invokes callback slot +0x14 at 0x109e2b38. Raw table 0x10f071d8 contains f_106c2818. This is the queue-to-serialization continuation for the registered observer. The drain dispatch is concrete: successful protocol upgrade installs f_10688fb4 as the connection callback through f_100ad234 at 0x10689650 (callback formed at 0x10689644). f_10688fb4 reads the supplied connection vtable slot +0x14 at 0x10688fc4 and invokes it at 0x10688fec, selecting installed f_106c2e1c rather than the base no-op f_10688fa4.

f_106c2818 constructs a buffered Muse writer through f_109f6a48 using callback+0x10 as sink, then serializes the event through f_109e98c4 at 0x106c2888. f_109e98c4 selects f_109f6fb0 or f_109f6d7c according to event state. f_109f6fb0 -> f_109f6f0c emits the version-dependent header and payload callback, then flushes at 0x109f6f90 via f_109cdd28. Shared header producer f_109f6bc4 contains namespace, name, type and apiVersion keys; header selection depends on the writer mode rather than an AlarmClock-specific SOAP envelope. Writer constructor f_109cdc30 stores the connection sink at writer+0x2c (0x109cdc50). Flush loads that exact sink and calls its slot +0x0c at 0x109cdd7c. Primary connection table 0x10f071f0 contains f_10689924. Therefore event serialization reaches the concrete connection writer, not an unbound abstract sink.

Connection writer requires state byte connection+0xbd == 1 at 0x1068996c; otherwise it returns false. Open-connection path calls frame writer f_106897a8 at 0x10689a00. f_106897a8 writes opcode, then RFC6455 unmasked server length encoding: inline lengths through 125; marker 126 plus big-endian u16 through 65535; otherwise marker 127 plus high zero word and u32 length (0x10689808..0x106898d0), then payload at 0x10689910. It buffers via f_100acdf0/f_100accb0 and flushes via f_100acc2c at 0x106898e8. Plain flush -> f_100a791c -> write at 0x100a79cc; TLS flush -> f_100b333c -> mbedtls_ssl_write at 0x100b3380. Failure returns false and the caller logs Write to websocket failed. Empty payload writes only framing before flush. These are static eligible/open-connection paths, not a claim that every scheduled update was sent or acknowledged. Final-fragment path sets FIN with ori r30,r30,0x80 at 0x10689a50; intermediate fragments retain the continuation state.

The channel map is parsed by f_1053c234/f_1053e0c4: entries are separated by ';', each entry is a 24-character player UUID followed by ':' and its channel token (f_1053d8a4), at most 16 entries are kept, duplicate UUIDs are rejected with the log 'Duplicate entry: %s at index %zu and %zu' (category chanmapset), and the parse result records whether the local UUID (impl+0x25c) is present and at which index. AddBondedZones.notes: On this build, even a valid existing bonded map cannot bypass the constant-401 apply helper at f_1035c738; the nonempty HT-map branch returns 402 before reaching it.
AddBondedZones.implementation_notes: Runtime object: the DeviceProperties implementation constructed by f_10351904 (called only from f_103fa434 at 0x103fc274), which installs vtable 0x10ebc630 at 0x10351bf4 over the base vtable 0x10ebd214 installed by f_1035e5ac. 0x10ebd214 is the base vtable only; the slots used by the bonding actions are overridden in 0x10ebc630. Slot +0x18 of the base vtable 0x10ebd214 is f_1035a390, a stub returning 401, which is why reading the base vtable makes this action look unimplemented; the runtime object dispatches to f_1035560c instead. f_1035560c passes zero for the worker's fifth to eighth arguments, so the SOAP path never supplies the optional trigger, bond-duration or Muse-API arguments that f_103548f4 also accepts.

AddHTSatellite.description: Attaches a home-theater satellite. The wrapper parses HTSatChanMapSet (cap 640) and calls slot +0x48 of runtime vtable 0x10ebc630, f_1034f670, a thunk that calls f_1034f5b0 with two zero arguments. f_1034f5b0 asks f_1065a73c about the zone-player context at impl+0x25c: when it answers nonzero this player acts as the primary and the work is done by f_1034ec5c; otherwise f_1065a6cc validates the map for the satellite role, returning 402 when it refuses, and f_1034cf38 stages the satellite map. The result is then banded: 1032 and 1035 pass through unchanged, any other value in 1000..9999 becomes 800, and values outside that band are returned as they are. When the result is 1032 the wrapper commits success and afterwards calls slot +0x74 (f_1034c82c, which forwards to slot +0x80, f_1034cabc). The runtime follow-up calls f_1034c850 from 0x1034ccd4 to consume the pending map, update primary UUID/network settings and take the applicable restart path.

It returns 402 for a map that does not parse or has at most one entry, and 1034 when this player is not the map's primary or a joinZone send failed (the failed satellite is rolled back through f_1034d858). Options.description: Mode options string (cap 128), forwarded unchanged to the selected mode entry and to satellites. For Mode 'room_calibration-calibrate' the entry f_10364360 parses it as a structured object (f_10c3b6c4). The string field 'mode' defaults to 'spectral' (selector 1); 'plug-in spectral' selects 2. Any other value stores selector 0 and continues processing. 'ver' and 'tone' are validated by f_10364284 through f_1035b170, which accepts only a nonempty string other than '..' made of letters, digits and '-', '_' or '.'; anything else fails with 402 and the log 'invalid input parameters v:%s t:%s'. They are then used as path parts by f_103639d0, which loads tone files from https://sonar.ws.sonos.com as '%s/%s/%s/%s-%s' and keeps their eTags. 'force' removes the cached Trueplay asset directory through f_1035d8bc and reloads the tones ('force ' in the eTag reload log). The integer fields 'polarity', 'volume' (clipped, 'Sonar cal volume - using clipped volume %d instead of requested %d') and 'tone_duration' configure the calibration tone, which is played as x-rincon-configmode:sonar-calibrate-tone. Mode 'trueroom' uses f_10362190 instead: it parses at 0x10362204/0x1036229c, reads volume, tone and force at 0x103622b4/0x103622d4/0x103622f0, and can return 800 for invalid options. button-notify and speaker-detect do not read Options. Value handling: 'volume' defaults to 50 when absent and is clamped to 35..70 (isel at 0x103646e0 and 0x103646f0, logged when clipped). 'polarity' is true only when it equals 1; that boolean goes to the impl+0x1a8c audio object through f_102a5124 -> f_107f6c24 -> f_10d8e348, and internal event 4 is then posted to impl+0x11c through f_105d24f8. 'tone_duration' is in seconds and defaults to 90 when absent or 0. f_1035d7e8 first selects x-rincon-configmode:sonar-calibrate-tone through the AVTransport object's slot +0x08, then passes the duration unchanged to f_102b4638, then starts playback through slot +0x44 and sets mode 'NORMAL' through slot +0x40. f_102b4638 stores the duration at AVTransport+0xaa74. The URI-specific reader at 0x102cfd34 uses f_10c3d118 to break the unsigned value into hour, minute and second bytes. When AVTransport+0x4654 is neither 1 nor 2, f_102b4c1c converts those bytes back to seconds and adds the result to the seconds word returned by sonosClockGetTime to set the sleep timer deadline. The parser path has no explicit range check; the conversion stores only the low byte of the computed hour count.

State.format: zero to four records concatenated directly with no inter-record delimiter; each record is NAME:PRESS_COUNT:AGE_SECONDS
State.unit: PRESS_COUNT is a 16-bit event count; AGE_SECONDS is monotonic seconds since the most recent press
State.accepted_values: NAME is selected from the event enum accepted by the recorder: AMP, LEDS, IR, HEADPHONE, SUBWOOFER, ORIENTATION, BUTTON_PLAYPAUSE, BUTTON_VOL_UP, BUTTON_VOL_DN, BUTTON_JOIN, BUTTON_MODE, BUTTON_POWER, BUTTON_MICMUTE, BUTTON_PAIRING, CAPZONEA, CAPZONEB, CAPZONEC, CAPZONEM. Empty string is valid when observation mode is active but no records are occupied.

SetZoneAttributes.description: Sets the zone name, icon, configuration and target room name. The wrapper parses the four strings (caps 1024, 1024, 16 and 65) and calls slot +0x08 of runtime vtable 0x10ebc630, which the most-derived class overrides with 0x10356df4. That override parses the bonded channel map stored at impl+0xe60 and, when this player is entry 0 (the primary) of that map, first forwards a SetZoneAttributes request carrying DesiredZoneName, DesiredIcon, DesiredConfiguration and an empty DesiredTargetRoomName to other bonded members through f_10359898, skipping any member whose URI lookup fails. It then applies the values locally with the base worker f_105b4574 and returns that worker's result; the forwarding result is discarded. Afterwards, when f_104d82ac reports the sonar flag of the object at impl+0x1368 and f_1075c4d0 identifies the local UUID as a secondary in a valid channel-map roster through the topology object at impl+0x968 (call 0x10356f3c), it calls f_10356c14 to clear sonar configuration. Mere presence of the UUID is insufficient: f_1075c4d0 returns false for the primary at roster index 0, and true for a valid nonzero local index. The worker calls the configuration object at 0x10356cfc and 0x10356d18, updates the +0xa54 flag at 0x10356d38, clears the sonar flag at 0x10356dd8 and requests event processing at 0x10356de0.

AddMember.description: Adds a player as a group member. The handler 0x10738654 reads MemberID as type-tag 7 text with capacity 0x19 and BootSeq as an integer. Request validation that returns 0 faults 402 at 0x10738898. The worker is f_10394d10, slot +0x08 of the static vtable 0x10ec2bc0. f_103938f0 stores that vtable at the gm_impl object at 0x10393bbc. A zero return writes the five outputs and commits. A nonzero return is the SOAP fault code.

implementation.description: The vtable is the static table stored by the constructor. It is not injected at runtime. f_10394d10 returns 807 when the byte at impl+0xda4 is 0. It returns 402 when MemberID is null or its first byte is 0, and logs 'Adding member failed - invalid argument'. It returns 808 when f_10759850 returns nonzero, logging 'Rejecting AddMember: GC or new member is an ungroupable player'. It returns 804 when f_1075d770 returns nonzero, logging 'Adding member to satellite is not supported'. It returns 800 when the compatibility lookup fails, and also when the string at impl+0x210 does not match the string at impl+0x120. It returns 806 when that compatibility byte is 0, logging 'Adding member %s failed - incompatible member'. It returns 803 when BootSeq is nonzero and f_10123d80 reports the out-of-sync byte, logging 'Adding member %s with bootseq %u failed - out-of-sync GM'. It returns 801 when MemberID matches the string at impl+0x210. It returns 802 when none of the 32 member slots is free. A matching slot logs 'Adding member %s that already exists' and still refreshes the outputs when f_103929e0 returns 0. Success copies the member id into the slot, fills the five output buffers, calls f_10391dd8(impl, 1), and returns 0.
implementation.notes: Return register is r31 at 0x10394de0. The handler passes BootSeq when the parser byte at +0x31 is nonzero and passes 0 when that byte is 0.

RemoveMember.description: Removes one exact MemberID from the coordinator's GroupManagement member table. The direct SOAP path enters gm_impl through vtable slot +0x0c (f_10395b0c -> f_10395854), rejects an empty ID with 402, then case-sensitively scans up to 32 fixed 25-byte member records at gm_impl+0x288. A match is removed from the membership and dependent topology structures, group-size-dependent state is recomputed, a GroupResize notification is published with reason 'Remove', related VLI linkage is cleared when it refers to the removed ID, and the active AVTransport URI path is reset with empty URI/metadata. A non-member ID returns 800.

CommitLearnedIRCodes.description: Writes the learned VolUp, VolDown, and VolMute codes to g_pszJFFSRoot/irconfig.txt under the supplied name. The wrapper 0x10739968 reads Name as a type-tag 7 string with capacity 0x20. Validation returning 0 is fault 402. f_10242380 returns 402 when the first byte is 0. A nonempty name tail-calls f_1024aeb8 on the decoder. That function returns 803 (0x323) unless the length bytes of all three slots are nonzero: VolUp at decoder+0x54c8c, VolDown at +0x54cd8, and VolMute at +0x54d24. The failure log prints those three lengths. On success it strlcpy's Name into decoder+0x54c44 with capacity 0x20, calls decoder virtual +0x10, then f_10249004. f_10249004 installs the three code pointers at the name record +0x20, +0x6c, and +0xb8 through f_10248930 with indexes 0, 1, and 2, then calls f_102457b8. The writer opens the JFFS irconfig path with mode w and, if that fopen succeeds, sets the configured byte and writes the sections :repeat_codes:, :vol_up_codes:, :vol_down_codes:, :vol_mute_codes:, and :input_codes:. A failed fopen logs 'Could not write ir configuration!' and does not set the byte. f_1024acc0 then runs. Its 0 return becomes SOAP 801 and the log 'Timeout during commit of learned IR code'. A nonzero return becomes SOAP success, after which the worker copies 0x150 zeroed bytes back over the learned-code area.

IdentifyIRRemote.description: Waits for one infrared button press and tries to match it to a stored remote. The wrapper 0x10241f24 reads Timeout through TRequest virtual +0x1c and f_105614e0 (type tag 4). Validation returning 0 is fault 402. Otherwise f_10242dfc compares the parsed word unsigned with 0xea60 (60000). A greater value returns 402. A value of 0 through 60000 calls f_10249cc8 on the decoder at impl+0x218, passing the timeout and the TRequest. f_10246ff4 clears the done byte at decoder+0x54d94 and the result word at decoder+0x54d98, sets the mode word at decoder+0x498 to 5, and arms a deadline with timevalAddMs. Timeout 0 adds 10000 milliseconds. Any other accepted timeout adds that many milliseconds. The wait calls f_10246f2c, which returns nonzero while sonosClockGetTime is still before that deadline, and sleeps one second between polls. It also stops when decoder+0x498 is 0, when the done byte becomes nonzero, or when the result word becomes nonzero. Each poll calls TRequest virtual +0x44. On this build that slot is f_10731660, which returns 1, so the compare against 0 never ends the wait. After the wait, a nonzero done byte returns 0. A zero done byte with a zero result word returns 802 and logs that the one-button code was not found. A zero done byte with a nonzero result word returns 801 and logs a timeout. A database match in f_1024b464 sets the done byte, logs the remote id, and calls f_10249004, which copies three code records and calls f_102457b8 to rewrite g_pszJFFSRoot/irconfig.txt.

LearnIRCode.description: Captures one infrared code for a named target. The wrapper 0x10242008 reads IRCode as a type-tag 7 string with capacity 0x20 and Timeout as a type-tag 4 integer. Validation returning 0 is fault 402. f_10242e20 rejects a timeout unsigned-greater than 60000 with 402, and rejects an empty IRCode (first byte 0) with 402. The deadline rule matches Identify: 0 means 10000 milliseconds, otherwise the timeout value is the millisecond count. Mode word decoder+0x498 is set to 1. The loop polls f_10246f2c, calls TRequest virtual +0x44 (constant 1, so it does not stop the loop), and sleeps one second. SetIRRepeaterState.description: Changes the infrared repeater between On and Off. The wrapper 0x10739878 fetches DesiredIRRepeaterState (TRequest virtual +0x1c), configures it as a type-tag 7 string with f_1056157c capacity 9, and validates with TRequest virtual +0x08. Validation 0 is fault 402. Otherwise it calls impl virtual +0x0c, f_102424d8. That worker accepts only the exact strings On (0x10fe55b8) and Off (0x10e739b8); every other string, including Disabled, returns 402 (0x192) with no store. If the current impl+0x1ec text is Disabled, the worker unlocks and returns 401 (0x191) without applying the request. Otherwise it sets a 4-byte flag to 1 for On and 0 for Off (cntlzw/rlwinm of the second On compare), takes a file descriptor from f_102a5160(impl+0x148), and calls ioctl(fd, 0x8004fc1a, &flag). f_102a5160 returns the word at *(impl+0x148)+0x34+0xe4. ioctl returning -1 yields SOAP 501 (0x1f5). Any other ioctl result copies the new text into impl+0x1ec with capacity 9, calls the settings object at impl+0x144 virtual +0x14 with the key IRRepeater and that string, sets the event dirty byte impl+0x1e4 to 1, signals the event source at impl+8 through f_1067c6ec, unlocks, and returns 0. A nonzero worker result is passed unchanged to TRequest virtual +0x14. Zero commits success and this action has no output record.

implementation.description: f_102424d8 is the only setter reached by the SOAP wrapper. The settings fan-out f_101bc458 also tail-calls f_10242d00 for the key IRRepeater when its object pointer at +0x4c is nonzero. f_10242d00 ioctls the same command and copies the supplied text, but it does not reject Disabled, does not check the ioctl result, and does not set the dirty byte.

A nonzero argument saves impl+0x1ec at impl+0x1f5, writes Disabled, ioctls flag 0, and signals the event source. A zero argument ioctls flag 1 and, when impl+0x1f5 is nonempty, copies that saved text back. The ioctl flag on the restore path is 1 even if the restored text is Off.

events.mechanism: GENA SUBSCRIBE is accepted at /HTControl/Event. Property text is produced by f_10243170, reached from event-source virtual +0x14. f_1024340c adjusts this by -8 and branches to f_102432dc, which calls f_10243170 at 0x10243338 and 0x10243350 for non-null property buffers, because the source object is the embedded object at impl+8, and slot +0x18 (f_1067ab54) tail-calls slot +0x14 with the same r3, r4, and r5. The renderer emits TOSLinkConnected from the byte at impl+0x1e5 and IRRepeaterState from the string at impl+0x1ec. It does not emit LEDFeedbackState or RemoteConfigured. Registration: f_101981f0 calls f_10189a10 at 0x1019826c. In f_10189a10, r31 is the zone player and r29 is r31+0x40000. The load at 0x10189cc4 reads the htc impl from r29-0x2af8, which is zone-player+0x3d508. The addi at 0x10189ccc forms impl+8. The isel at 0x10189cd4 keeps that pointer when the impl is non-null and substitutes 0 when the impl is null, then 0x10189cd8 calls f_106795b4 with the sender loaded from zone-player+0x5744. f_106795b4 appends its r4 argument to the vector at sender+0x110 when the byte at sender+0x10d is 0. The sender constructor f_106782b4 stores 0 at that byte (0x10678388). The other store of that byte is f_10678ab8, which stores 1, and f_101981f0 does not call f_10678ab8. Signal: SetIRRepeaterState calls f_1067c6ec, which calls f_1067c46c with null buffers, so that call does not enter f_10243170. f_1067c46c calls f_10678c50 on the sender at source+0xb4. That sets sender+0x10e and signals the condition at sender+0xb8. The consumer f_10679b14 scans a snapshot of active sender+0x110, skips sources found in pending-removal sender+0x128, and applies readiness and timing checks before calling f_10683da0 at 0x10679e54. The slot +0x08 comparison at 0x10679d44-0x10679d4c is a getter fast path, not a universal eligibility gate: equality with f_100c9bac loads source+0xbc directly, while inequality calls the getter virtually at 0x10679fc4 and rejoins at 0x10679d54. The HTControl source vtable 0x10ea628c has f_100c9bac at +0x08, f_1024340c at +0x14, and f_1067ab54 at +0x18. In f_10683da0, frame+0x50 is initially zero at 0x10683e0c, but is also the linked-node head at table+8 for the table rooted at frame+0x48. At 0x10683e4c the code passes &frame[0x48] to f_10684d00, called at 0x10683e50 for a name group rooted at source+0xa0 before its subscriber eligibility loop. A missing key allocates a node at 0x10684dac-0x10684de8 and calls f_10684ac8 at 0x10684dfc with r4=table and r7=new node. When insertion finds an empty destination bucket, 0x10684c98-0x10684ca0 links the old head into the new node and stores the new node at table+8: stw r26,8(r30) at 0x10684ca0 therefore writes the caller's frame+0x50. This happens on first insertion into the initially empty table. An existing key returns its value without this insertion; insertion into an already populated bucket uses 0x10684b48-0x10684b58 instead. A second lookup/insertion at 0x10683fa8 uses the same table when frame+0x54 is zero and source+0xf0 is zero (0x10683f68-0x10683f7c). Thus frame+0x50 is not invariant zero, and the collector is conditionally reachable. The real gates remain: a nonzero head at 0x10683fe0-0x10683fe8 and a nonempty group vector at 0x10683ff8-0x10684004. Eligible subscriber entries are added after f_10686038 returns nonzero at 0x10683e78-0x10683eb4; creating a name group alone does not establish a nonempty vector. For a populated batch, 0x10684060 loads source+0x18 and 0x1068406c calls it with the global object's property buffers at +0x90/+0x94, reaching the HTControl renderer chain above. In plain English, the sender builds groups before generating the properties for groups that have work; a helper can populate the apparently zero local head through its containing table. This establishes static reachability, not a live subscription or successful wire delivery. f_1067b214 instead walks the separate global list at 0x11097824, with insert sites 0x1059bf34 and 0x106261c4. Unknown: the complete binding from an accepted /HTControl/Event subscription to an eligible source+0xa0 record and successful callback delivery remains untraced. Next: follow the SUBSCRIBE handler's insertion into source+0xa0, trace its f_10686038 eligibility result and group-vector population, then follow the populated batch to its notification callback.

/MediaRenderer/AVTransport/Control.name: AVTransport
/MediaRenderer/AVTransport/Control.description: UPnP AVTransport service. Its wrapper delegates to the engine at wrapper+4, which has a base vtable (0x10eaf2ec) and a group-capable derived vtable (0x10edfbb8). For SOAP slots the derived table overrides SetAVTransportURI and the three Become*Coordinator* methods. Many transport actions serialize at impl+0x458, and use impl+0x4654 to select indexed (2), streamer (1), or default/source-specific paths.

availability.notes: The ZonePlayer constructor initializes the wrapper unconditionally; the router's availability byte comes separately from ctx+0x571c XOR 1. Engine A is the base vtable, and the group-capable derived constructor replaces it with B. The presence of B is not itself a test for the zone's current topology; B's overrides make those tests per call. At activation, the zone binds its allocated derived engine to wrapper+4 and its lifetime controller to wrapper+8. A null candidate in the binding call leaves this wrapper unchanged. Rebinding can release the previous engine reference. Destruction replaces the wrapper vptr and releases its controller; it does not clear the engine pointer as a separate step.

Normal ZonePlayer construction passes the embedded SOAP aggregate as the sixth argument of the engine constructor chain (from 0x1018ef1c via stack +0xfc and r8). AVTransport is constructed at aggregate+0x0c at 0x1018fb70.

The 0xae38-byte allocation on the engine-creation path is passed to the derived AVTransport constructor. The result is kept in the owner at +0x1934 and its lifetime controller at +0x1938 (0x103fb680/0x103fb678). No base-only allocation or current group membership test selects the constructor at this site.
The activation routine passes obj+0x1934 as r6, and loads r3 from obj+0x220, the SOAP aggregate pointer saved by the owning constructor at 0x103fa75c.

Copies the object from r6[0] to aggregate+0x10 (AVTransport wrapper+4). The lifetime controller is stored at aggregate+0x14 at 0x104d4ba4. If r6[0] is null, the binder skips this service; a raw nonnull pointer with no controller takes the 0x104d5830 store.

The ZonePlayer destructor computes r30=this+0x40000 at 0x10192450. It replaces the AVTransport member vptr at this+0x3fa38 with 0x10e978e8 and calls f_100c5050 on the nonnull controller loaded from member+8. The sequence does not zero member+4.

The first two slots point to f_102fc9e4 and f_102fcae8. Both restore the base vptr and release a nonnull wrapper+8 controller; decrementing the strong count from one invokes controller slot +8 and then drops the weak count. A final weak release invokes +0xc. The second destructor also deallocates the 12-byte wrapper.

When a bind supplies a different controller, it retains the incoming one and drops the previous one's strong count before storing the replacement at aggregate+0x14. A null engine skips the bind entirely at 0x104d4b10, so this binder is not an unbind operation.

Void commit token mismatch can abort without a SOAP failure. Matching Spotify routing may initialize/start a client or set count to 1 instead of local entry writing. Preparation can power the amplifier and schedule cleanup; this path does not perform deletion actions' alarm-deadline clear.

evidence.notes: Derived AVTransport constructor f_10511f34 installs vtable 0x10edfbb8 at 0x105123c0 after base f_102c05d8; factory invokes derived at 0x103fb5d8. f_102b7000 returns 402 for NumberOfURIs=0 at 0x102b706c; its strlen bounds are 10249/40969, already enforced by public buffer truncation. f_102b6d28 tokenizes URI list using ASCII space 0x20, not semicolon, with 1024-byte item limit and 10250-byte destination. BackupQueue.notes: BackupQueue uses the shared SavedQueues XML/compression serializer with its own explicit trackqueue.rsq filename and fixed queue-backed flags. This does not make SaveQueue/CreateSavedQueue/AddURIToSavedQueue/ReorderTracksInSavedQueue error ladders reachable. Cleanup registration is conditional and its callback uses a stat timestamp comparison; do not describe this action as guaranteed permanent persistence or guaranteed deletion exactly five minutes later.

BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup.description: Makes this player the coordinator of a standalone group and returns its newly generated local group ID. It also returns the replacement coordinator for the old group if delegation succeeds. The group-aware engine can reject the action before standalone setup.

If identical, returns zero and sets the byte only when the URI is empty. resolved_findings: Home-theater and VLI classification are separate tests. The early restore checks saved and current URI equality; a changed URI tries to reload immediately, and the fallback flag blocks a second saved-source reload.

f_1090ad44 returns the local product information at 0x110c8150. f_109089f0 reads product code +0xcc. The 0x04020041 mask applies to codes 29 through 55 and selects 29, 35, 46 and 55; the separate comparison accepts 59. The model tables at 0x10f7c1f4 and 0x10f7c2f0 identify those codes as S27/Roam, S35/Roam SL, S44/Move 2, S54/Roam 2 and S58/Mojave. This is a hardware test, not a membership query.

The fallback acquires the live topology holder from impl+0x44c and looks up the local ID passed from impl+0x3dc. f_10765a00 requires record+0x10 to match the ID by strcmp and device state (*(record+0x2568))+0x710 to equal 1. f_10762df8 additionally requires record bytes +0x1f18 and +0x1f4b to be nonzero. It then uses the roster at record+0x1c88: f_1053ce34 reads its first byte and f_1053c370 returns whether its word +0x288 is zero. The fallback returns 1 only when the first byte is nonzero and that word is nonzero, the active secondary case. evidence.notes: A_ARG_TYPE_SourceState (string): advertised argument | file:artifacts/downloads/rootfs-86.10-80260-1-9/opt/htdocs/xml
Registers CurrentSourceState at the request's +0x1c slot and attaches a 165-byte type 7 caller buffer using f_1056157c. The bounded materializer reserves one byte for NUL.
The base engine calls the adapter's +8 materializer with output storage. A materialization failure goes through engine cleanup before the outer wrapper reports it.

Attempts source-state restoration using f_1032d7f8; the false result can clear the local restore decision. Then f_1025c30c receives the accepted descriptor, current URI and snapshot-related input record.

Rejects a retained strlen other than 164. At 0x1032d8dc scans the fixed-width header using %04hX%08X%08X%08X%04hX%02hhX%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%02X and tests for 15 conversions. At 0x1032d91c copies exactly 64 bytes from input+0x64, NUL-terminates them and trims whitespace before passing the tail to f_1045fbac.

The second header value is the source kind stored in the nested descriptor at snapshot+0xf0 (the parser starts at snapshot+0xf0 and writes this value to its +0). Other confirmed destinations include header values 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 at snapshot+0xea, +0x138, +0x13c, +0x140 and +0x154. The final conversion is passed to the nested descriptor unless it exceeds 0x11, in which case zero is passed.

The nested parser f_10803f38 requires a colon at tail+2 and parses a two-wide hex flag word no greater than 3. Bit 0 selects three conversions %08X:%08X:%016llX: starting at tail+3 (advances the next section to tail+38). Bit 1 selects eight two-wide hex conversions followed by two four-wide hex conversions separated by colons, starting at the current offset. The code tests conversion counts, not complete-string consumption.

f_1045fbac installs the source-kind word and auxiliary descriptor values only if the nested tail parser succeeds; failure clears the local nested descriptor and returns zero. f_1032d7f8 returns that result. The handoff worker gates f_1025c30c on it and compares the installed kind with 5 and 8 for the early playback request (0x102df924 to 0x102df934). Kind 5 with no live source byte at +0x518 is changed to kind 1 at 0x102dfdf0 before restoration.

Header value 6 at snapshot+0x154 gates a playback-control callback with the word at +0x13c and halfword at +0x140. Values at +0x14c and +0x150 are copied to indexed manager+0x35184 and +0x35188. The helper selects a source handler using CurrentURI, installs the descriptor as the state goal at indexed manager+0x3280c, and treats snapshot+0x138 equal to 1 as true at indexed manager+0x35180.

ResumePlayback.description: Requests indexed playback after source-state restore. A false value suppresses the later request, but source types 5 and 8 can request playback earlier without it, and sink reset can force a false value to true. Requesting playback is not confirmation that audio has started.
ResumePlayback.format: Case-insensitive text for 1, true or yes; other present text decodes as false.
ResumePlayback.accepted_values: Any present value at boolean materialization; only 1, true and yes map to true.
ResumePlayback.range: At most 23 bytes are retained for conversion; the result is one byte, 0 or 1.
ResumePlayback.special_values: An empty value decodes as false; a missing required value fails materialization.
ResumePlayback.validation: A type 1 descriptor materializes the required value by name. Other text is false, not a boolean-format fault. An absent value causes 402 from the adapter.

evidence.notes: A_ARG_TYPE_ResumePlayback (boolean): advertised argument | file:artifacts/downloads/rootfs-86.10-80260-1-9/opt/htdocs/xml
Looks up ResumePlayback in the engine-driven request adapter.
The base engine calls the adapter's +8 materializer with output storage. A materialization failure goes through engine cleanup before the outer wrapper reports it.
Registers ResumePlayback using the type 1 descriptor helper f_10561444. The whole adapter returns 402 on request materialization failure at 0x102fa134.
Supplies sp+0x5f as the boolean destination. The worker loads the byte at 0x102dfb58 and only takes the later submit arm on nonzero when the source-state restore branch flag is set.
For restored source record type 5 and zero state-source byte +0x518, the logged resetting-sinks branch overwrites ResumePlayback with 1 and changes the restored record type to 1.

TRequest slot +0x1c allocates a record and forwards the argument name in r4 to record slot +8. The record vtable at 0x10eebf40 binds that slot to f_1055eb4c, which stores the name at record+0x34. At 0x10730480 materialization retrieves it via record slot +0xc (f_1055eb5c) and passes it into parsed-body lookup at 0x10730490.

If lookup does not produce a value, finalization is skipped. A record not marked finalized at +0x31 and not marked optional at +0x30 makes materialization return zero. The input-record constructor zeros both bytes.

Type 1 ends at a NUL (input retained to 23 bytes) and performs strcasecmp against 1, true, and yes. It stores one on those matches and zero otherwise, including an empty string; it does not reject a present nonmatching value.

Selector 5 invokes f_10256604 under the session lock. The state-name table at 0x10ea8534 identifies 5 as PLAYING, 6 as PLAYING_START, and 7 as TRAN_PLAYING. The worker returns success directly for current state 5 or 6; otherwise an accepted transition can write 7 at 0x102568dc and wake the state processing path.

The worker passes sp+0x18bb8 in the argument slot consumed by the AlarmState type 7 registration at 0x102fa020. The alarm import at 0x102dfaa8 reads this same buffer; both playback submit branches test the first byte of this AlarmState string, not a byte from the decoded source-state record.

The late selector-5 call requires ResumePlayback (or its sink-reset override) and the source-restore branch. If AlarmState is nonempty, it passes the nonzero playback byte and 0 in r6/r7. If AlarmState is empty, both auxiliary arguments are the URI classifier f_10148308. The earlier call at 0x102dfe30 is independent of ResumePlayback for restored record kinds 5 and 8 and uses 1/0 with nonempty AlarmState or two classifier values otherwise. Both calls discard the selector return.

The auxiliary URI classifier is true for the exact, case-sensitive prefixes x-sonosapi-stream:, x-sonosapi-hls:, hls-aac://, hls-radio:// and x-rincon-mp3radio://, the middle HLS family via f_101475dc.

The selector wrapper forwards the auxiliary arguments into r9/r10 of f_10256604. The first becomes the indexed manager byte +0x327c9; runQueue checks it at 0x1026cafc and publishes a decimal value from +0x327cc through the in-process event helper f_10272030 when set. The second goes to f_1032db8c, which clears subobject+0x296d and writes subobject+0x296e. The frame callback may promote the latter to the former via f_1032dbd4 at 0x1026a67c; the source-state snapshot reader tests +0x296d at 0x1032ded0 and 0x1032e070.

The indexed playback loop calls runQueue (f_1026badc). One branch switches state 7 (TRAN_PLAYING) to 5 at 0x1026dd80, while another switches it to 6 (PLAYING_START) at 0x1026ceb8. The frame callback switches 6 to 5 at 0x1026afd4; the loop can instead move to 9 (TRAN_PAUSED) when the PlayTTL check is nonzero at 0x1026cf00. Thus merely reaching the selector does not report playback completion.

return_behavior.description: The group-aware override returns 1023 before reading the SOAP arguments only when the hardware code does not bypass the check and the local topology marks the player as an active secondary. The base engine returns 800 for nonzero engine mode without x-sonos-clone-gc, 718 for nonzero parsed InstanceID, and 402 for missing required arguments or invalid OtherMembers framing. Faults pass through the wrapper unchanged, including when standalone setup runs as a fallback.

The adapter calls request +8 after registering all argument records, including separate required type-8 records for SharedQueueTrackList and PrivateQueueTrackList. It returns 402 on zero at 0x102fa134.

TRequest +8 materializes each record by its registered name via parsed-body slot +8 at 0x10730490. A lookup miss leaves the finalized byte +0x31 clear and the required record (optional byte +0x30 clear) makes materialization fail. A present value runs f_10560a58, which sets finalized at 0x10560a74 before type-specific work; neither conversion results nor the type-8 destination callback result are tested as parse success.
After successful materialization and the zero-InstanceID check, a zero return from f_102ab92c on the OtherMembers text sets the worker result to 402.

The base worker returns r25. The adapter status enters r25 at 0x102df684, and the only action-local 402 assignment to it is the OtherMembers failure at 0x102df848. Standalone fallback at 0x102df6f4 does not overwrite it; neither source-state decode nor indexed resume submits a later SOAP 402.

The +0xd4 override bypasses the secondary check on a nonzero f_109089f0 result. Otherwise it calls f_1075c4d0 at 0x1051351c and maps only its nonzero return to 1023. Both permitted paths branch to f_102df410 with the original arguments at 0x10513510.

f_1090ad44 returns the local product information at 0x110c8150. f_109089f0 reads product code +0xcc. The 0x04020041 mask applies to codes 29 through 55 and selects 29, 35, 46 and 55; the separate comparison accepts 59. The model tables at 0x10f7c1f4 and 0x10f7c2f0 identify those codes as S27/Roam, S35/Roam SL, S44/Move 2, S54/Roam 2 and S58/Mojave. This is a hardware test, not a membership query.

The fallback acquires the live topology holder from impl+0x44c and looks up the local ID passed from impl+0x3dc. f_10765a00 requires record+0x10 to match the ID by strcmp and device state (*(record+0x2568))+0x710 to equal 1. f_10762df8 additionally requires record bytes +0x1f18 and +0x1f4b to be nonzero. It then uses the roster at record+0x1c88: f_1053ce34 reads its first byte and f_1053c370 returns whether its word +0x288 is zero. The fallback returns 1 only when the first byte is nonzero and that word is nonzero, the active secondary case. Missing or expired topology, no matching valid record, an inactive roster or a zero roster word returns 0.

The tokenizer walks seven descriptors with successive strtok_r delimiter sets ':', ',', ':', ':', ':', ',' and empty. Value types are IPv4 via inet_pton(AF_INET), decimal helper with a halfword store, IPv4, three more halfword stores, then a 25-byte strlcpy of the remaining token. All seven tokens must be present. Input is copied to a 129-byte buffer first.

If token parsing is unsuccessful, leaves the default record untouched. Otherwise the first IPv4 becomes record+0, the four parsed halfwords in token order become +8, +4, +6 and +0xa, the second IPv4 becomes a dotted string at +0xc, and the trailing token goes to +0x1c (max 24 bytes plus NUL).

The tokenizer walks seven descriptors with successive strtok_r delimiter sets ':', ',', ':', ':', ':', ',' and empty. Mode 1 omits baseline Stop for a valid x-sonos-htastream: URI. f_102931f0 forwards to f_10293014; the prefix comparison is case-insensitive, followed by 24 bytes, a colon, and an exact suffix of spdif, v-spdif, vli, chsnk or test. A nonzero provider mask can still contribute Stop.

The byte that suppresses the entire action list is source entry+0x82c. f_10741b4c writes it after a successful name lookup only if f_10762df8 succeeds or the alternate +0x1f18, f_1053ce34 and f_1053c370 gates pass; otherwise the caller's initialized zero survives.

Indexed capabilities start from word +0x26e4 of the source held at session+0x326c8. The initial masked copy also drops Next (0x00020000) if the source has bit 0x00080000 and session+0x32800 is outside 5..8. Selector 3 applies track overrides: f_1014a190 returns a 16-byte record, then the worker clears bits from its first word and sets bits from its second word. It ignores bit 0x8 in both override words (0x10258968/0x10258974).

On the nonzero input+0x86 branch, f_10255af0 initializes the source word to 0x1173e4a8 if the supplied category matches audiobook (case-insensitive with end of string or a dot boundary), otherwise 0x1173eca8. It then applies (word & ~input[+0x8c]) | input[+0x90] through f_10145dc0. At 0x102576c8 the same helper clears bit 0x400 for a noncurrent source that had it; at 0x1026bdc0/0x1026cdcc it replaces bit 0x40000000 according to whether the preceding callback returned 1.

f_1014a190 zeroes all four override words and fetches the selected track reference. If source bit 0x2000 is clear and the URI passes f_101477e4 it calls f_1045f890 directly. That helper extracts the URI's flags field using f_1071af38, which passes base 10 and a null end pointer to strtol. If the field is found, both override words receive the mapped 0x02000000 bit, if any (rotate left 11 and retain that bit); flags bit 0x8000 additionally puts X_DLNA_SeekTime in the clear word. A missing field leaves both words zero. On the other branch f_10146a38 supplies an optional string to f_10424870, whose callback table 0x10eccbc0 includes f_104257e4; it copies two supplied words to the override when the callback context byte +5 and output pointer +0x170 are nonzero.

With no entries (source halfword +0x26c8 is zero), mask 0xfe8c7fff clears all published indexed actions before the outer Set bit is applied. It re-adds original X_DLNA_SeekTrackNr only if source bit 0x400 is set, and original Play only if either source bit 0x400 or 0x1000 is set. f_10148044 and f_10148058 extract those two flags respectively.

With entries present, f_10149d80 and f_10149ff0 test for alternate track indices. Failure from f_10149d80 clears Next unless source bit 0x1000 is set, or bit 0x400 is set and session byte +0x4b3f is zero. Failure from f_10149ff0 clears Previous unless bit 0x400 is set and session byte +0x4b3e is zero. These branches do not add a missing Next or Previous bit.

The two +0x2c calls are sequential, not alternatives. The first queries the active record's +4 control object for another interface; the second calls that interface for the capability word and stores it at 0x106a7ccc. Missing active record, control object or returned interface gives false without writing a word.

Spotify registers streamer source type 2 through f_106a76b8: r5 is the Spotify VLI control object adjusted by +8 and r6 is the SpotifyAudioInput object. The registration helper writes these at record+4 and +8 in the first free 12-byte entry of the nine-entry table at streamer+0x2e8. f_106a8b08 selects by type and installs the record at streamer+0x354 (0x106a8df4); a failing selection callback clears it at 0x106a8e34.

Spotify finishes wiring the controller with f_1022c7d4(control, spotify+4), which stores this interface pointer at control+0x188. The controller constructor installs address point 0x10ea53a8 at control+8 (0x1022d94c). Its +0x2c entry at 0x10ea53d4 adjusts back by 8 and calls f_1022add4, which returns that stored pointer. The Spotify constructor installs address point 0x10ea2210 at spotify+4 (0x102198d4).

The Spotify interface at 0x10ea2210 uses +0x2c thunk f_10212b54. f_10212ae4 calls VLI control slot +0x10 (f_1022ac04, reading byte +0x18c); when zero it returns 0x01018000 (Stop, Pause, Play). Otherwise control slot +0x4c (f_1022b450) returns Play if byte +0x18d is zero, or reads the SpotifyAudioInput bits through f_104dce44 and adds X_DLNA_SeekTrackNr if control+0x380 equals 3.

The streamer constructor zeros all nine registration entries. The only direct branch to f_106a76b8 in .text is the Spotify type 2 registration at 0x10219cf0; there is no aligned absolute function pointer to f_106a76b8 in the image. The source-selection path uses the active record at +0x354.

f_104dce44 locks the audio input and computes capabilities from its +0x4e58 restriction record. f_104da720 starts at 0x01338007. It clears Pause if restriction word +0 is nonzero ignoring bit 0, Play if +4 is nonzero, and SeekTime, Previous and Next if +8, +0x14 and +0x18 respectively are nonzero ignoring bit 0x80. The respective mask sites are 0x104daaac, 0x104daa84, 0x104daa3c, 0x104da96c and 0x104da924. Nonzero words +0xc and +0x10 can log a restriction but do not change the mask. The outer mode 1 baseline includes Play even when the provider clears it.

The Spotify provider clears the low Shuffle, Repeat All and Repeat One bits for nonzero restrictions at +0x24, +0x1c and +0x20 respectively (0x104da8dc, 0x104da894, 0x104da84c). The GetCurrentTransportActions formatter does not publish those three bits.

One source-entry updater copies input byte +4 to entry +0x82c when the prior byte differs. Another updater rewrites bits 7 and 6 of the same byte from input word +0x22e8 bits 15 and 14 at 0x10767428 and 0x1076743c while preserving the low six bits. The action tests the resulting byte as a whole, not an individual bit.

Reads the word at +4 of the streamer state object: 0 -> PLAYING, 1 -> PAUSED_PLAYBACK, everything else -> empty string.
Reads source+0x28b0 under its lock: 3, 5, 7 or 9 -> PLAYING, 1 -> STOPPED, all other values -> TRANSITIONING.

Request +0x40 fills an initially zeroed 8-byte descriptor. After a true return, byte +1 below 0x16 enables the override; byte +1 equal to 0x16 enables it only if byte +2 is zero and the unsigned word at +4 is <= 0xf653. Otherwise there is no override. When enabled, only TRANSITIONING is rewritten to PLAYING (0x102fbd7c).

state_transitions.description: Both kind-4 workers clear the selected queue. Only clearing the active queue resets current index/descriptor, clears source identity and notifies the track-play monitor. Active running clear marks source change; the main controller requests resync, sees count 0 and enters completion rather than restarting a remaining source. Empty-queue progression writes TRAN_STOPPED, later STOPPED and stopRoutine. Paused handling likewise leaves the empty queue in TRAN_STOPPED before outer stop handling. CurrentTrack and TransportState are timed source snapshots, so SOAP success does not wait for the final STOPPED/current-index-0 event. Inactive clearing leaves active-source state alone. Mode 1 external-source AVTransport snapshots remain source-dependent rather than unconditionally mirroring queue-controller state.
