Relative running table 0x10ea8468 entry 4 targets 0x10265d6c; stopped table 0x10ea84d0 entry 4 targets 0x1026863c. Selector indexes session+0x326a0 scaled by 4, and both handlers call f_10262a98 (0x10265d84/0x10268654). That helper clears the selected queue and returns whether it was active, not whether clearing succeeded. Both handlers report true completion: running 0x10265d90 or active 0x102665d0; stopped 0x10268344 or 0x102687b4. Active running clear flags source change and notifies monitor at 0x102665b8; inactive clear does not. Active stopped clear resets descriptor, marks metadata changed and notifies monitor at 0x10268660..0x102687c0.

Clear helper locks through f_1014aee8, calls f_10145b98 then invokes f_1014d738 whenever queue name +0x4c is nonempty, with no old-count guard; finally unlocks via f_1014af64. f_10145b98 writes count +0x26c8=0 at 0x10145bb4, clears words +0x26d4/+0x26ec and other bookkeeping, resets optional +0x2700 block and invokes backing object +0x48 slot +0xc if present. It logically clears membership rather than compacting each removed track. Named queue version +0x70 increments once and dirty +0x74 is set by f_1014d738, which posts through queue+0x18 at 0x1014d820. Clearing an already-empty named queue therefore still advances revision and posts the update.

Compares selected queue with active pointer session+0x326c8, calls f_1014da34 at 0x10262af0 regardless of active status, and only when equal resets current index +0x326cc using f_10146924 (empty count yields 0), resets +0x326ce and calls f_10261b38. That clears source pair +0x35184/+0x35188 and +0x327c8, resets descriptor and invokes f_10261a44. Active running output reaches the common main-loop source-change branch and completion path because count is zero; paused empty-queue handling sets internal state 2 at 0x10269330. Queue-end empty branch writes state 2 at 0x1026e758; outer loop later switches state 2 to state 1 and stopRoutine at 0x1026f4e8/0x1026f4f0. This is not a synchronous SOAP STOPPED guarantee, and inactive queue clearing does not stop an unrelated source.

Session state/metadata publishing records a timed source node through f_103420a4 at 0x1026470c, then obtains the transport weak owner at 0x10264784. Nonzero live owner and transport pointer gate f_1067c6ec at 0x102648c4. Stopped active-clear postprocessing reaches f_102642d4 at 0x10267e2c; running clear reaches it through later controller state changes, not a per-track notify loop. Shared AVTransport source snapshot/latches determine emitted fields; external mode 1 source snapshots need not mirror queue-controller state.

Raw word 0x554807fb at 0x10266fa4 has SH=0, MB=31, ME=29, Rc=1: wraparound mask 0xfffffffd of state minus 2. BO=13, BI=2 at 0x10266fa8 uses CR0 equality, meaning state 2 or 4, not a shift or missing comparison. These later controller gates do not make SOAP completion wait for STOPPED.

RemoveTrackFromQueue.description: Removes the entry selected by ObjectID from queue selector 1 through implementation f_102aa770. Base constructor f_102c05d8 installs vtable 0x10eaf2ec; derived AVTransport implementation constructor f_10511f34, called by the factory at 0x103fb5d8, replaces it with live vtable 0x10edfbb8. Both tables have f_102aa770 at slot +0x70. InstanceID must be zero. A nonzero UpdateID must match the current queue version. Modes 1 and 2 permit the operation. A kind-3 request is submitted to the session worker and the caller waits for its completion byte; success is not merely submission acceptance. The worker deletes the entry and updates queue bookkeeping. The alarm buzzer-fallback deadline clear, ContentDirectory observer chain, Queue notification readiness and snapshot construction, and source bookkeeping are traced below. Conditional current/last-position selection, packet-history reconciliation, empty-queue stop progression and AVTransport snapshots are detailed below. Success alone does not identify a unique playback-state snapshot.

events_triggered.description: Named queue deletion increments its version, sets queue+0x74 dirty, and posts CdNotifyUpdateId through queue+0x18 using f_10117654. The registered ContentDirectory observer f_10304808 increments its SystemUpdateID, coalesces the container/version in its changed map, and schedules eventing. ContentDirectory f_103035c4 emits SystemUpdateID and comma-separated ContainerUpdateIDs; incremental emission is gated by pending state and elapsed whole seconds greater than one, with a Q:0 map entry bypassing the delay. Otherwise it schedules the previous timestamp plus two seconds. SystemUpdateID and the container map have separate pending/timing state. Queue service has a separate LastChange builder f_10465b54: Queue-namespace XML carries QueueID from snapshot+0 and UpdateID from snapshot+0x14. f_10465e28 obtains snapshots through f_102b0908 and f_1025bfd4; f_10146cc0 copies queue+0x5c, so version and dirty byte become snapshot+0x14/+0x18. Incremental Queue output requires a changed snapshot; consuming snapshots clears copied dirty flags. Queue and AVTransport use the same notification sender supplied by the factory. A transport notification wakes that sender, not a direct Queue forwarding callback. The sender tests every registered source with f_1067d028; Queue slot +0x1c reaches f_10465aa4, which takes a nonconsuming snapshot and returns its changed flag. Thus dirty queue snapshots make Queue ready even when its own pending byte is clear. For subscribed sources, the producer dispatch at 0x1068406c calls slot +0x18; Queue adapts this through f_1067ab54 to f_10465f74 and f_10465e28. AVTransport slot +0x18 instead reaches f_102e6400, f_102e6048 and f_102e43a0. Its full buffer bypasses the incremental latch gate; incremental output requires impl+0x7785, +0x7786 or one of +0xa094..+0xa09c. These producer gates do not imply that deletion changes every serialized transport property, or that a notification is sent without a subscription. The deletion source-list change reaches the grouped TransportState, NumberOfTracks, CurrentTrack, CurrentTrackURI and AVTransportURI block through the snapshot-version result and +0x7785 latch; these are not independent per-field comparisons. Conditional nonempty source selection and timed playback-state transitions are detailed in state_transitions. There is no direct network-event emission in f_102aa770.

Queue event extra string is empty, so its extra-string branch does not call f_1030470c.

ContentDirectory event builder, not Queue service: full buffer includes SystemUpdateID; ContainerUpdateIDs uses f_103034e8 comma-separated container/version map. Incremental SystemUpdateID pending flag +0x4e4 requires whole-seconds elapsed>1 or Q:0 in changed map (0x10303aa0..0x10303ac4), otherwise schedules prior timestamp+2 at 0x10303d4c; emission clears pending at 0x10303af8. Queue LastChange builder writes Queue namespace and QueueID %.20s from snapshot+0, UpdateID %u from +0x14. Nonempty snapshots only; incremental mode additionally requires f_1014d540(snapshot). Full includes Curated and QueueOwnerID; incremental includes these only for snapshot+0x52b/+0x119 respectively. f_10465e28 calls f_102b0908 and writes full buffer when supplied, incremental only if snapshot helper returns changed. Does not alone prove publisher scheduling.

f_102b0908 locks impl+0x458 and calls f_1025bfd4. Copies queue 0 at session+0x2d890 and queue 1 at +0x2ff98 via f_10146cc0, ORs f_1014d540(snapshot) into changed result. f_10146cc0 copies 0x2574 bytes from queue+0x5c; queue revision/dirty +0x70/+0x74 become snapshot+0x14/+0x18. consume=1 clears queue+0x6c/+0x74/+0x175/+0x587 after copying. Other records are initialized placeholders; consume also clears session+0x326c4. f_1014d540 tests snapshot dirty bytes +0x10/+0x18/+0x119/+0x52b.

Factory+0x1934 assigned impl at 0x103fb680; 0x103fbb78..0x103fbb98 forms weak pair with raw pointer impl+0x10. r6 is set at 0x103fbc1c before session ctor call 0x103fbc3c; the pair is copied to session+0x2578/+0x257c at 0x1025f53c..0x1025f54c. Running worker scheduling at 0x10265914..0x10265a08 requires change flags and live weak owner. f_1067c6ec delegates to f_1067c46c setting pending and checking notification sender. Actual AVTransport event callback is f_102e6400 -> f_102e6048 -> f_102e43a0, with full and incremental calls at 0x102e61d4/0x102e61f8. Thunk 0x102e4398 instead adjusts r4 and reaches property getter f_102e41a0; it is not the event callback.

Factory passes r25 common sender as r5 to derived transport constructor f_10511f34 at 0x103fb5d8 and as r4 to Queue constructor f_10465fac at 0x103fb6e4..0x103fb6e8. Transport base ctor calls f_1067aec4(impl+0x10, sender, AVTransport, 11, ...) at 0x102c06e4; Queue ctor calls it on Queue+8 at 0x1046607c. Generic source ctor stores sender weak pair in source+0xb4/+0xb8 at 0x1067af54..0x1067af64. f_1067c46c resolves the weak sender and calls f_10678c50 at 0x1067c5c8; that helper marks sender+0x10e and signals its condition variable. Derived transport ctor installs event-source vtable 0x10edfddc at impl+0x10 at 0x105123d0; slot +0x18 contains f_102e6400. Queue source vtable 0x10ed1c10 has readiness thunk f_10465b4c at +0x1c and producer adapter f_1067ab54 at +0x18.

Sender fireNotifications loop loads each source at 0x10679d10..0x10679d18 and calls f_1067d028 at 0x10679da8. A nonzero source+0x110 returns ready. Otherwise 0x1067d0bc..0x1067d1c8 invokes subclass slot +0x1c. Queue f_10465b4c adjusts this by -8 to f_10465aa4, which calls f_102b0908(engine, records, 6, 0) at 0x10465b0c and preserves the changed return through its epilogue. No consume means readiness polling does not clear dirty state. Ready-source dispatch reaches f_10683da0 at 0x10679e54 and source slot +0x18 at 0x10684060..0x1068406c. Queue adapter f_1067ab54 forwards to slot +0x14 = f_10465f74 -> f_10465e28. Thus there is no missing direct AVTransport-to-Queue producer call: the common sender polls Queue snapshot readiness. Actual delivery remains conditional on registered source/subscription state and sender operation.

f_102e6048 calls f_102e43a0 with r7=1 for supplied full buffer at 0x102e61d4, r7=0 for incremental at 0x102e61f8. At 0x102e46cc..0x102e46dc full mode or impl+0x7785 enters serialization; otherwise 0x102e54a8..0x102e551c tests +0x7786 then +0xa094..+0xa09c. r28 was reassigned impl+0x10000 at 0x102e465c. f_102b5658 updates latches before this gate: +0xa094/+0xa095 latch metadata flags +0x4251/+0x4252 at 0x102b56b4..0x102b56d8; +0xa096/+0xa097 latch capability changes masked by 0x01738000/0xf, with source/mode metadata flags as fallbacks at 0x102b5804..0x102b5828. These are generic gates; deletion-specific snapshot comparisons and their final emitted CurrentTrack/TransportState values remain residual.

The event builder first calls f_102b5a1c at 0x102e4698; its changed result r27 causes impl+0xa0a2=1 at 0x102e46ac..0x102e46b8 before f_102b5658 latches +0x7785. Mode-2 branch 0x102e55c0 returns to that test, with additional next-URI handling. f_102b5a1c mode2 calls session snapshot f_1026021c at 0x102b5d7c; that calls f_10341c74 at 0x102602fc. The latter compares source-list version +8 with consumed version +0xc at 0x10341cd0..0x10341cf4, returns changed, and consumes the version only when requested. Running deletion increments this version via f_103410c0 at 0x10265930 before notifying the transport at 0x10265a08. This is a version/snapshot gate, not a separate equality test for every XML property. f_102b5658 additionally consumes session metadata through f_1032dc18 at 0x102b59d4, storing its changed flag in +0x7786; that helper reads metadata+0x296b and clears it when consume is requested at 0x1032dda8..0x1032ddb0.

Full output or latched impl+0x7785 enters the common transport-property block at 0x102e47e4; otherwise 0x102e47e0 skips to 0x102e4d38. The block serializes TransportState at 0x102e47e8, NumberOfTracks at 0x102e4870, CurrentTrack at 0x102e489c, CurrentTrackURI at 0x102e48f4 and AVTransportURI at 0x102e4a50. These values can therefore be repeated unchanged when another source-list change makes the block eligible. f_1026021c puts the source-node +0x28c track number through output-record+4 at 0x10260300..0x1026030c; live active-queue count +0x26c8 goes through record+8 at 0x10260790/0x102603a4, subject to the start-window adjustment at 0x102606b4..0x102607b4. CurrentTrackURI is obtained by f_1014a28c from the selected queue entry at 0x10260470, after invalid indexes are reduced to zero and optional shuffle mapping at 0x102607b8. AVTransportURI is copied from impl+0x5dc at 0x102b5a28..0x102b5a80; deletion does not itself replace that selected source URI. f_10341c74 maps source-head state +0x288 through table 0x10eba220: 0 STOPPED, 1 TRANSITIONING, 2 PLAYING, 3 PAUSED_PLAYBACK. Snapshot timing, not the SOAP return alone, determines which of those values is observed.

state_transitions.description: Running active deletion uses f_10259f38 and f_103417dc. The latter computes the inclusive removal span, adjusts linked source indexes and shuffle mappings, detaches removed source nodes, returns their identity and flags removal of the list head. This flag is not merely a numeric CurrentTrack equality check. Head removal clears session+0x35184/+0x35188 and +0x327c8, marks changed and calls the track-play monitor with (1,0). Removing another identified source remaps the current index and invokes f_10259c1c; remapping failure sets +0x327d2. f_10259c1c resets saved identity words +0x327d8/+0x327dc to -1 and queries the NodeTX object at session+0x60. The factory passes a null override, so the session binds its embedded NodeTX at session+0x338, with vtable 0x10efb75c. Slot +0x38 is f_10636bc8, which scans packet/control-frame history for stream identity and returns packet/frame positions and identity through output pointers. Slot +0x40 is f_10270ce8, deriving the next packet identifier from NodeTX+0x120. Slot +0x48 is f_10636254, which reports crossfade state for a packet identifier. These methods do not directly assign TransportState. The deletion helper compares identities, saves the packet identifier at session+0x327d4, remaps queue indexes when needed, or saves the crossfade-state result at +0x327e0. Stopped active deletion uses f_1014ed90 with current-index and removed-current outputs. If removed-current is true, 0x10268e7c clears the same source pair and +0x327c8, resets the source descriptor and notifies the monitor. Successful stopped postprocessing clears playback bookkeeping through f_10261a44 when +0x327c8 is false, refreshes selected-track metadata through f_10267560 when the queue remains nonempty, and publishes session metadata through f_102642d4. The monitor callback is f_104bf2e4, not a direct STOPPED-state setter. For active running deletion, the main loop calls the worker at 0x1026cfd0 and tests its source-change flag at 0x1026cfd4. A changed source reaches NodeTX requestResync (slot +0x24, f_10637d2c) using the saved packet identifier, stream identity and crossfade flag, rather than a direct TransportState setter. If the queue remains nonempty and remapping has not failed, it switches to internal state 6 (PLAYING_START) and records a TRANSITIONING snapshot. Empty queue or failed remapping instead reenters completion handling. Once completion handling returns, the empty-queue branch sets internal state 2 (TRAN_STOPPED); after the queue routine returns, the outer controller switches to state 1 (STOPPED) and enters stopRoutine. Paused handling also sets state 2 when the stopped worker leaves the active queue empty. These are subsequent controller transitions, not a guarantee that SOAP success waits for a STOPPED snapshot. State recording f_102642d4 maps session states 1..8 through [0,1,1,1,2,1,1,3] and records state, current index and effective time in the source list. Snapshots prune consumed source nodes by time, then take CurrentTrack from head+0x28c and TransportState from head+0x288. NumberOfTracks is read separately from the active queue, so it need not wait for buffered playback state to settle. Deleting from an inactive queue has no corresponding active-source transition. Nonempty selection is conditional, not a promise to play the next numeric track. f_10149e68 retains a valid eligible selected index when queue+0x26dc bit0x4 is set; otherwise it tries the next-entry selector f_10149d80. Forward search f_10149bec respects shuffle ordering and URI eligibility; bit0x2 permits wrapping. Eligibility rejects URI flags bit0x10 and, when queue+0x26e4 mask0x40000000 is set, also rejects URI flags bit0x10000. Failed next-entry selection has a separate queue+0x26e4 bit0x10 gate and can retain the original index; exact branch conditions and current-index arithmetic are in the evidence. f_10259f38 sets +0x327d2 and restores the source-list index when normalization fails. For packet-history reconciliation, f_10259c1c uses crossfade state when the history query returns true, or returns false but reports the same identity. False with a differing identity instead saves the next packet ID and removed identity, optionally remaps the queue with f_1045f760, and clears the crossfade flag. These saved values feed requestResync. The selected index is distinct from the timed source-head CurrentTrack. Current/last-position deletion can restart a remaining source, or enter completion when normalization fails; the queue flags, entry flags, packet history and snapshot time determine the observed outcome.

evidence.notes: Running worker kind-3 table: base 0x10ea8468, entry +12 targets 0x10265d10. Queue selector from request+0xfc indexes the word array at session+0x326a0 with selector scaled by 4 (0x10265d20..0x10265d30 and 0x10268358..0x1026836c; constructor pointer stores at 0x1025fc1c/0x1025fc24); inactive queue uses f_1014ed90, active queue branches 0x102668e4 to f_10259f38. Stopped table base 0x10ea84d0 entry +12 targets 0x1026834c; active queue branch 0x10268ce4 uses f_1014ed90 with current-track out-parameters.

Deletion compacts entries at queue+0x26c0, adjusts optional shuffle map +0x26c4, decreases count +0x26c8, adjusts current-track index when supplied, sets +0x26e8, and calls f_1014d738 when queue name +0x4c is nonempty. f_1014d738 increments word +0x70 at 0x1014d7bc..0x1014d7c0, sets dirty byte +0x74 and posts an internal event through f_10117654 at 0x1014d820.
Calls f_103417dc before deleting through f_1014e9a8; paths call f_10259c1c, set session+0x327d2 or invoke session+0x2590 vtable slot +0x30.

Called at 0x10259fb8 with active queue, source identity, inclusive start/end, headRemoved/index/identity outputs. f_103410d8 prunes source list; inclusive span is uint16(end-start+1). Queue+0x26dc bit0 selects shuffle remapping. Adjusts source-node +0x28c/+0x28e indexes; detaches deleted nodes to secondary list at list+4 and returns identity +0x290/+0x294. Head-removed output set at 0x10341b18, not an unconditional CurrentTrack comparison. f_10259f38 head-removal branch 0x1025a09c clears source pair session+0x35184/+0x35188 and +0x327c8, marks changed and invokes monitor; other identified-source branch remaps with f_10149e68, sets +0x327d2 on failure, and calls f_10259c1c. Copies +0x326cc to +0x326fc on return.

Sets saved identity +0x327d8/+0x327dc=-1, queries session+0x60 slot+0x38 with identity and out-pointers. Compares returned identity; differing identity calls slot+0x40 (f_10270ce8 derives the next packet ID from object+0x120, with -1 yielding 1), stores packet ID at +0x327d4, remaps using f_10149e68 and f_1045f760. Alternate branch calls slot+0x48 at 0x10259d80 and stores crossfade-state byte +0x327e0. These are NodeTX packet-history methods, not transport-state setters.

Stopped active single deletion at 0x10268ce4 calls f_1014ed90 with current index &session+0x326cc and removed-current byte. True byte branches to 0x10268e7c: clear +0x35184/+0x35188, reset source descriptor through f_1045fd34, clear +0x327c8, call session+0x2590 slot+0x30(1,0), set +0x3c540=1 and timestamp +0x3c544. Successful stopped postprocessing 0x10267e00..0x10267ebc calls f_10261a44 when +0x327c8 false, f_10267560(0) if queue nonempty, then f_102642d4(1,sourceDescriptor). These operations do not by themselves identify final TransportState literals.

Track-play monitor ctor installs vtable 0x10ed8134; slot+0x30 points to f_104bf2e4. Factory constructs it at 0x103faf80 and stores factory+0x1904; session ctor r9 from that field is stored at session+0x2590 (0x1025f598). f_104bf2e4 submits monitor event kind3 through f_104c6264, not a direct AVTransport state assignment.

Session+0x60 is initialized by f_1066e7d4 at 0x1066e8ac from its r5, but that argument is NOT the session constructor's incoming r5. Session ctor loads incoming stack+0xc at 0x1025f1b8; nonnull passes that override as r5 at 0x1025f244, null branches to 0x1025ffa8 to pass session+0x338. Factory initializes r19=0 at 0x103fbbd4 and stores it in outgoing stack+0xc at 0x103fbc20 before actual ctor call 0x103fbc3c, selecting the embedded object. Session constructs that embedded NodeTX with f_106366c4 at 0x1025f510; NodeTX ctor installs vtable 0x10efb75c at 0x10636724. Its slots +0x38/+0x40/+0x48 contain f_10636bc8/f_10270ce8/f_10636254. This resolves the factory-created session's concrete binding without assuming a runtime-injected source.

NodeTX slot +0x38 scans packet records through f_10633e20 and control frames through f_1063311c. At 0x10636f50..0x10636f68 writes packet number, frame offset, frame payload word and stream identity to supplied outputs; analogous candidate outputs at 0x10636fc8..0x10636fec and 0x10636ffc..0x10637018. Invalid NodeTX packet bounds (+0x120/+0x11c == -1) branch to 0x106370dc and return false. Slot +0x48 f_10636254 looks up packet ID-1 at 0x10636274..0x10636294, parses control frames, returns false for absent/no control frames and tags 0xfa/0xfb (0x1063641c..0x10636460), true for other high-bit control tags (0x10636470..0x10636498). Diagnostic strings explicitly name crossfadeStateForPacketID. Slot +0x40 f_10270ce8 reads NodeTX+0x120, returning the next packet ID or 1 for -1.

Main queue routine invokes the running worker with source-change output &session+0x327c4 at 0x1026cfd0; true at 0x1026cfd4 branches to 0x1026ccfc. NodeTX slot+0x24 is f_10637d2c (word 0x10efb780); call 0x1026cd28 passes saved packet ID +0x327d4, identity +0x327d8 and crossfade byte +0x327e0. f_10637d2c logs requestResync and forms control type 0xfd for zero packet ID, otherwise chooses 0xfb/0xfe by crossfade flag. Back in the queue routine, 0x1026cd84..0x1026cd9c sends empty queues or remap failure to 0x1026d0ec; nonempty/no-failure calls switchState f_10264be8 with state6 at 0x1026cdb8. Worker signals request completion at 0x10265910 before returning to these controller branches, so SOAP completion does not wait for subsequent playback or network notification.

After completion handling f_10266c68, 0x1026f30c..0x1026f388 returns to queue-end state handling when there are no more tracks. 0x1026e724..0x1026e758 tests active queue count and sets session+0x32800=2 (TRAN_STOPPED) when empty; alternate queue-policy branch 0x1026ebfc..0x1026ec00 also reaches it on zero count. Paused routine f_102690f0 calls stopped worker at 0x102691cc; zero active count sets the same state2 at 0x10269330. Once f_1026badc returns at outer-loop call 0x1026f4c4, 0x1026f4c8..0x1026f4e8 selects state1 for state2 and calls f_10264be8, then stopRoutine f_102693cc at 0x1026f4f0. Raw isel 0x7c8ae71e at 0x1026f4e4 selects r10=3 on CR7 LT, else r28=1; state2 minus3 is unsigned greater than2, selecting1. This is a conditional later STOPPED transition, not an immediate literal assignment in the deletion implementation.

State recording maps internal states1..8 using words at 0x10ea8740: [0,1,1,1,2,1,1,3], with mapped-state1 (TRANSITIONING) fallback at 0x102644fc. It clamps an out-of-range selected index to0 at 0x102643a4..0x102643d0, passes mapped state/current index/effective time to f_103420a4 at 0x1026470c. That helper builds a timed source node through f_103404c8 at 0x1034221c, whose writes at 0x10340570..0x10340594 store state+0x288, current index+0x28c and effective time+0x290/+0x294. f_103420a4 inserts/replaces nodes in time order using f_105a8fd4 and increments list version at 0x10342440. Snapshot f_10341c74 first prunes timed source nodes through f_103410d8; f_1034071c reads head+0x28c at 0x103407d4 for CurrentTrack, while f_10341c74 reads state+0x288 at 0x10341d68 and table 0x10eba220 for STOPPED/TRANSITIONING/PLAYING/PAUSED_PLAYBACK. Session-mode snapshot f_1026021c reads queue count separately, so old buffered source state and reduced live count can coexist.

For selected index i, reads metadata through f_1014571c, using shuffle bit0x1 and queue+0x26c4 mapping. If bit0x4 of queue+0x26dc is set and f_10148230 accepts that metadata, retains i only for 1<=i<=count; invalid i returns false. Otherwise calls f_10149d80, which rejects i=0 or i>count, then searches f_10149bec(i,+1), writing zero-based result+1 on success. No forward match optionally wraps by searching from0 when queue+0x26dc bit0x2 is set. Search skips entries rejected by f_10148230. f_1014815c parses URI flags as decimal; f_10148230 rejects mask0x10, otherwise accepts unless queue+0x26e4 mask0x40000000 requires URI flag0x10000 to be clear. If f_10149d80 fails, queue+0x26e4 bit0x10 clear returns false; with that bit set, second search f_10149bec(i,+1) at 0x10149fcc retains original i and returns true only on result0xffff, otherwise returns false. This explicit fallback is not an unconditional next-track operation.

Current-index adjustment in f_1014e9a8 converts a supplied 1-based index to uint16(index-1), calls this helper with zero-based inclusive start a/end b and old count n, then converts0xffff to0 and other results to1-based. Let k=uint16(b-a+1), c be zero-based current. If k==n, writes0xffff. If c<a, retains c; if c>b, writes uint16(c-k). For c inside the span: if b==n-1, writes uint16(b+1-k); otherwise queue+0x26dc bit0x2 set selects0, clear selects uint16(a-1). Head-removal path f_10259f38 supplies this pointer at 0x1025a0b8. Identified non-head source path instead uses f_103417dc's index output, calls f_10149e68 after mutation at 0x1025a010, and on false sets session+0x327d2 and restores the source-list result at 0x1025a088; true clears +0x327c8. Both call packet reconciliation f_10259c1c and mark source change.

NodeTX history query true branches to crossfade query for saved packet at 0x10259d6c; false compares both returned identity words at 0x10259cb0/0x10259d5c and also takes crossfade query if equal. False/different identity saves next packet ID and input identity to +0x327d4/+0x327d8/+0x327dc, then calls f_10149e68 with current index and temporary output at 0x10259d18. True invokes f_1045f760(current,selected), false skips remapping; both clear crossfade byte +0x327e0. requestResync at 0x1026cd28 consumes these saved values. Source selection is therefore separate from the timed CurrentTrack/TransportState snapshot. Neither success nor deleting the final numeric position specifies a single immediate playback value.

return_behavior.description: No output arguments. Wrapper commits success on implementation result 0 and faults verbatim on nonzero result. Complete normal implementation result domain is {0,718,1028,800}: 718 for nonzero InstanceID, 1028 for version mismatch, 800 for disallowed mode or false worker completion. Request construction/tagging does not contribute a return code. Stack-check failure aborts rather than returning a SOAP code.

evidence.notes: Under impl+0x458 lock: InstanceID gate precedes current update-id fetch; nonzero UpdateID mismatch returns 1028; unsigned (mode-1)>1 returns 800; completed false request returns 800, true returns 0. Unlock result is discarded at 0x102aa7cc. Neither 1176 nor 1500 is assigned to r31 on a normal exit; the prior inferred return literals are unsupported.

Stores request at session+0x2594, signals session+0x2e8, unlocks session+0x208, tail-calls f_1032e658. That function waits for request+0xe0 and returns completion byte +0xe1. f_1032e6c0 writes result and done bytes then signals. This is a synchronous completion wait, not merely asynchronous acceptance.
Zero result branches to request slot +0x0c commit; nonzero invokes fault slot +0x14. Parse validation failure loads 402 at 0x102f9be0.

RemoveTrackRangeFromQueue.description: Removes an inclusive queue span through live derived AVTransport vtable 0x10edfbb8 slot+0x74, f_102acca8 -> f_102aca78. InstanceID must be 0. StartingIndex is 1-based; NumberOfTracks is a positive count, not a1-based index. Zero start/count returns 402. The common body resolves decimal queue ID0, checks optional UpdateID and computed endpoint, requires mode 1/2, submits kind 14 and waits. Success rereads queue revision into NewUpdateID. Endpoint arithmetic is uint32 without checked-add overflow, followed by uint16 worker endpoints.

Ordinary nonoverflowing valid range reduces count by NumberOfTracks. uint32 endpoint addition precedes uint16 worker truncation; no separately checked StartingIndex upper bound or overflow-safe sum.

Sets saved identity +0x327d8/+0x327dc=-1, queries session+0x60 slot+0x38 with identity and out-pointers. For selected index i, reads metadata through f_1014571c, using shuffle bit 0x1 and queue+0x26c4 mapping. If bit 0x4 of queue+0x26dc is set and f_10148230 accepts that metadata, retains i only for 1<=i<=count; invalid i returns false. Otherwise calls f_10149d80, which rejects i=0 or i>count, then searches f_10149bec(i,+1), writing zero-based result+1 on success. No forward match optionally wraps by searching from 0 when queue+0x26dc bit 0x2 is set. Search skips entries rejected by f_10148230. f_1014815c parses URI flags as decimal; f_10148230 rejects mask 0x10, otherwise accepts unless queue+0x26e4 mask 0x40000000 requires URI flag 0x10000 to be clear. If f_10149d80 fails, queue+0x26e4 bit 0x10 clear returns false; with that bit set, second search f_10149bec(i,+1) at 0x10149fcc retains original i and returns true only on result 0xffff, otherwise returns false. This explicit fallback is not an unconditional next-track operation.

NodeTX history query true branches to crossfade query for saved packet at 0x10259d6c; false compares both returned identity words at 0x10259cb0/0x10259d5c and also takes crossfade query if equal. False/different identity saves next packet ID and input identity to +0x327d4/+0x327d8/+0x327dc, then calls f_10149e68 with current index and temporary output at 0x10259d18. True invokes f_1045f760(current,selected), false skips remapping; both clear crossfade byte +0x327e0. requestResync at 0x1026cd28 consumes these saved values. Source selection is therefore separate from the timed CurrentTrack/TransportState snapshot. Neither success nor deleting the final numeric position specifies a single immediate playback value.

events_triggered.description: Named queue deletion increments its version, sets queue+0x74 dirty, and posts CdNotifyUpdateId through queue+0x18 using f_10117654. The registered ContentDirectory observer f_10304808 increments its SystemUpdateID, coalesces the container/version in its changed map, and schedules eventing. ContentDirectory f_103035c4 emits SystemUpdateID and comma-separated ContainerUpdateIDs; incremental emission is gated by pending state and elapsed whole seconds greater than one, with a Q:0 map entry bypassing the delay. Otherwise it schedules the previous timestamp plus two seconds. SystemUpdateID and the container map have separate pending/timing state. Queue service has a separate LastChange builder f_10465b54: Queue-namespace XML carries QueueID from snapshot+0 and UpdateID from snapshot+0x14. f_10465e28 obtains snapshots through f_102b0908 and f_1025bfd4; f_10146cc0 copies queue+0x5c, so version and dirty byte become snapshot+0x14/+0x18. Incremental Queue output requires a changed snapshot; consuming snapshots clears copied dirty flags. Queue and AVTransport use the same notification sender supplied by the factory. A transport notification wakes that sender, not a direct Queue forwarding callback. The sender tests every registered source with f_1067d028; Queue slot +0x1c reaches f_10465aa4, which takes a nonconsuming snapshot and returns its changed flag. Thus dirty queue snapshots make Queue ready even when its own pending byte is clear. For subscribed sources, the producer dispatch at 0x1068406c calls slot +0x18; Queue adapts this through f_1067ab54 to f_10465f74 and f_10465e28. AVTransport slot +0x18 instead reaches f_102e6400, f_102e6048 and f_102e43a0. Its full buffer bypasses the incremental latch gate; incremental output requires impl+0x7785, +0x7786 or one of +0xa094..+0xa09c. These producer gates do not imply that deletion changes every serialized transport property, or that a notification is sent without a subscription. The deletion source-list change reaches the grouped TransportState, NumberOfTracks, CurrentTrack, CurrentTrackURI and AVTransportURI block through the snapshot-version result and +0x7785 latch; these are not independent per-field comparisons. Conditional nonempty source selection and timed playback-state transitions are detailed in state_transitions. There is no direct network-event emission in f_102aca78. Kind14 uses the same named-queue version/dirty helper and shared sender. Active running success marks source-list change; active stopped success refreshes session metadata. Inactive edits need not change active transport properties.

The event builder first calls f_102b5a1c at 0x102e4698; its changed result r27 causes impl+0xa0a2=1 at 0x102e46ac..0x102e46b8 before f_102b5658 latches +0x7785. Full output or latched impl+0x7785 enters the common transport-property block at 0x102e47e4; otherwise 0x102e47e0 skips to 0x102e4d38. state_transitions.description: Active running kind 14 validates narrowed start/end and calls f_10259f38, the same inclusive source-aware helper used for single deletion. It adjusts/detaches timed source nodes via f_103417dc and reconciles packet identity/crossfade via f_10259c1c. Common main-loop handling requests NodeTX resync and can enter PLAYING_START/TRANSITIONING for a normalized remaining source, or completion for empty queue/failed normalization. Empty active queue later progresses TRAN_STOPPED -> STOPPED; SOAP completion does not wait for this snapshot. Active stopped kind 14 uses f_1014e9a8 current-index/removed-current outputs; removed-current clears source bookkeeping, resets descriptor and notifies monitor at 0x10268f38, then common postprocessing refreshes metadata. Timed source head supplies CurrentTrack/TransportState, live active count supplies NumberOfTracks. Selection depends on shuffle, queue policy, URI eligibility and packet history, not just the numeric successor. Inactive edits do not force the active source to stop.

Ordinary nonoverflowing valid range reduces count by NumberOfTracks. uint32 endpoint addition precedes uint16 worker truncation; no separately checked StartingIndex upper bound or overflow-safe sum.

Head-removed output set at 0x10341b18, not an unconditional CurrentTrack comparison. f_10259f38 head-removal branch 0x1025a09c clears source pair session+0x35184/+0x35188 and +0x327c8, marks changed and invokes monitor; other identified-source branch remaps with f_10149e68, sets +0x327d2 on failure, and calls f_10259c1c. Copies +0x326cc to +0x326fc on return.

Sets saved identity +0x327d8/+0x327dc=-1, queries session+0x60 slot+0x38 with identity and out-pointers. Compares returned identity; differing identity calls slot+0x40 (f_10270ce8 derives the next packet ID from object+0x120, with -1 yielding 1), stores packet ID at +0x327d4, remaps using f_10149e68 and f_1045f760. Alternate branch calls slot+0x48 at 0x10259d80 and stores crossfade-state byte +0x327e0. These are NodeTX packet-history methods, not transport-state setters.

Track-play monitor ctor installs vtable 0x10ed8134; slot+0x30 points to f_104bf2e4. Factory constructs it at 0x103faf80 and stores factory+0x1904; session ctor r9 from that field is stored at session+0x2590 (0x1025f598). f_104bf2e4 submits monitor event kind 3 through f_104c6264, not a direct AVTransport state assignment.

Session+0x60 is initialized by f_1066e7d4 at 0x1066e8ac from its r5, but that argument is NOT the session constructor's incoming r5. Session ctor loads incoming stack+0xc at 0x1025f1b8; nonnull passes that override as r5 at 0x1025f244, null branches to 0x1025ffa8 to pass session+0x338. Factory initializes r19=0 at 0x103fbbd4 and stores it in outgoing stack+0xc at 0x103fbc20 before actual ctor call 0x103fbc3c, selecting the embedded object. Session constructs that embedded NodeTX with f_106366c4 at 0x1025f510; NodeTX ctor installs vtable 0x10efb75c at 0x10636724. Its slots +0x38/+0x40/+0x48 contain f_10636bc8/f_10270ce8/f_10636254. This resolves the factory-created session's concrete binding without assuming a runtime-injected source.

NodeTX slot +0x38 scans packet records through f_10633e20 and control frames through f_1063311c. At 0x10636f50..0x10636f68 writes packet number, frame offset, frame payload word and stream identity to supplied outputs; analogous candidate outputs at 0x10636fc8..0x10636fec and 0x10636ffc..0x10637018. Invalid NodeTX packet bounds (+0x120/+0x11c == -1) branch to 0x106370dc and return false. Slot +0x48 f_10636254 looks up packet ID-1 at 0x10636274..0x10636294, parses control frames, returns false for absent/no control frames and tags 0xfa/0xfb (0x1063641c..0x10636460), true for other high-bit control tags (0x10636470..0x10636498). Diagnostic strings explicitly name crossfadeStateForPacketID. Slot +0x40 f_10270ce8 reads NodeTX+0x120, returning the next packet ID or 1 for -1.

Main queue routine invokes the running worker with source-change output &session+0x327c4 at 0x1026cfd0; true at 0x1026cfd4 branches to 0x1026ccfc. NodeTX slot+0x24 is f_10637d2c (word 0x10efb780); call 0x1026cd28 passes saved packet ID +0x327d4, identity +0x327d8 and crossfade byte +0x327e0. f_10637d2c logs requestResync and forms control type 0xfd for zero packet ID, otherwise chooses 0xfb/0xfe by crossfade flag. Back in the queue routine, 0x1026cd84..0x1026cd9c sends empty queues or remap failure to 0x1026d0ec; nonempty/no-failure calls switchState f_10264be8 with state 6 at 0x1026cdb8. Worker signals request completion at 0x10265910 before returning to these controller branches, so SOAP completion does not wait for subsequent playback or network notification.

After completion handling f_10266c68, 0x1026f30c..0x1026f388 returns to queue-end state handling when there are no more tracks. 0x1026e724..0x1026e758 tests active queue count and sets session+0x32800=2 (TRAN_STOPPED) when empty; alternate queue-policy branch 0x1026ebfc..0x1026ec00 also reaches it on zero count. Paused routine f_102690f0 calls stopped worker at 0x102691cc; zero active count sets the same state 2 at 0x10269330. Once f_1026badc returns at outer-loop call 0x1026f4c4, 0x1026f4c8..0x1026f4e8 selects state 1 for state 2 and calls f_10264be8, then stopRoutine f_102693cc at 0x1026f4f0. Raw isel 0x7c8ae71e at 0x1026f4e4 selects r10=3 on CR7 LT, else r28=1; state 2 minus3 is unsigned greater than2, selecting1. This is a conditional later STOPPED transition, not an immediate literal assignment in the deletion implementation.

State recording maps internal states1..8 using words at 0x10ea8740: [0,1,1,1,2,1,1,3], with mapped-state 1 (TRANSITIONING) fallback at 0x102644fc. It clamps an out-of-range selected index to0 at 0x102643a4..0x102643d0, passes mapped state/current index/effective time to f_103420a4 at 0x1026470c. That helper builds a timed source node through f_103404c8 at 0x1034221c, whose writes at 0x10340570..0x10340594 store state+0x288, current index+0x28c and effective time+0x290/+0x294. f_103420a4 inserts/replaces nodes in time order using f_105a8fd4 and increments list version at 0x10342440. Snapshot f_10341c74 first prunes timed source nodes through f_103410d8; f_1034071c reads head+0x28c at 0x103407d4 for CurrentTrack, while f_10341c74 reads state+0x288 at 0x10341d68 and table 0x10eba220 for STOPPED/TRANSITIONING/PLAYING/PAUSED_PLAYBACK. Session-mode snapshot f_1026021c reads queue count separately, so old buffered source state and reduced live count can coexist.

For selected index i, reads metadata through f_1014571c, using shuffle bit 0x1 and queue+0x26c4 mapping. If bit 0x4 of queue+0x26dc is set and f_10148230 accepts that metadata, retains i only for 1<=i<=count; invalid i returns false. Otherwise calls f_10149d80, which rejects i=0 or i>count, then searches f_10149bec(i,+1), writing zero-based result+1 on success. No forward match optionally wraps by searching from 0 when queue+0x26dc bit 0x2 is set. Search skips entries rejected by f_10148230. f_1014815c parses URI flags as decimal; f_10148230 rejects mask 0x10, otherwise accepts unless queue+0x26e4 mask 0x40000000 requires URI flag 0x10000 to be clear. If f_10149d80 fails, queue+0x26e4 bit 0x10 clear returns false; with that bit set, second search f_10149bec(i,+1) at 0x10149fcc retains original i and returns true only on result 0xffff, otherwise returns false. This explicit fallback is not an unconditional next-track operation.

Current-index adjustment in f_1014e9a8 converts a supplied 1-based index to uint16(index-1), calls this helper with zero-based inclusive start a/end b and old count n, then converts 0xffff to0 and other results to1-based. Let k=uint16(b-a+1), c be zero-based current. If k==n, writes 0xffff. If c<a, retains c; if c>b, writes uint16(c-k). For c inside the span: if b==n-1, writes uint16(b+1-k); otherwise queue+0x26dc bit 0x2 set selects0, clear selects uint16(a-1). Head-removal path f_10259f38 supplies this pointer at 0x1025a0b8. Identified non-head source path instead uses f_103417dc's index output, calls f_10149e68 after mutation at 0x1025a010, and on false sets session+0x327d2 and restores the source-list result at 0x1025a088; true clears +0x327c8. Both call packet reconciliation f_10259c1c and mark source change.

NodeTX history query true branches to crossfade query for saved packet at 0x10259d6c; false compares both returned identity words at 0x10259cb0/0x10259d5c and also takes crossfade query if equal. False/different identity saves next packet ID and input identity to +0x327d4/+0x327d8/+0x327dc, then calls f_10149e68 with current index and temporary output at 0x10259d18. True invokes f_1045f760(current,selected), false skips remapping; both clear crossfade byte +0x327e0. requestResync at 0x1026cd28 consumes these saved values. Source selection is therefore separate from the timed CurrentTrack/TransportState snapshot. Neither success nor deleting the final numeric position specifies a single immediate playback value.

state_transitions.description: No universal playback-state assignment. Inactive submitted rotation changes queue order only. Stopped/paused worker remaps current index only for the active queue, notifies track-play monitor and refreshes metadata, without itself starting playback. Active running f_1025a8e8 remaps timed source indices and reconciles buffered source continuity through f_103411b0; incompatible suffixes can require reselection and packet-history/crossfade reconciliation via f_10259c1c. The reported source-change flag feeds the main loop's NodeTX resync/transition path; eligibility and snapshot timing determine later state/current-track output. Ordinary rotation preserves count and does not inherently empty the queue or force STOPPED. No-op does not enter workers or a playback transition.

Active running helper first calls f_1014e794 with session+0x326cc current-index pointer at 0x1025a950, retaining its bool result. Seek.description: Repositions playback within the current transport source, dispatched to the zone-player engine as impl vfunc +0x34 -> f_102b95a8(engine,InstanceID,Unit,Target): queue/track ordinal seek (TRACK_NR) or time seek (REL_TIME absolute / TIME_DELTA relative).

InstanceID.description: Numeric transport-instance selector; the implementation accepts only 0 and rejects any other parsed value with error 718 before dispatching to the seek engine.
InstanceID.format: decimal integer parsed into a type-tag-4 argument record (helper 0x105614e0, 24-byte record)
InstanceID.range: 0 only; nonzero InstanceID rejected by impl +0x34 with 718

special_values.0: the only instance this zone player implements; anything else faults

InstanceID.validation: Request-layer validation faults 402 if absent/malformed (req vfunc +0x08 at 0x102f9408); implementation returns 718 when the parsed value is nonzero (0x102b9660-0x102b9668); on a successful engine call the value is stored into engine+0x6ed8 (0x102b96d4) but is not otherwise interpreted.

InstanceID.notes: The value is range-checked only; it is not forwarded as a seek operand.

Unit.description: Seek-mode token; the engine compares it with strcmp against a fixed set and interprets Target accordingly.
Unit.format: utf-8 text, buffer cap 1024 bytes (1023 chars + NUL)

special_values.TRACK_NR: target is a queue/track ordinal; only reached when engine mode field (this+0x4654) == 2 and capability bit 0x400000 is set, else 701
special_values.REL_TIME: target is an absolute time position (H:M:S); in stream mode always allowed, in indexed mode requires capability bit 0x200000; negative target rejected with 711 in indexed mode
special_values.TIME_DELTA: target is a relative time delta (H:M:S); same gating as REL_TIME; a zero delta is a no-op success in indexed mode

Unit.validation: strcmp chain in f_102b9088: indexed mode (engine+0x4654==2) accepts TRACK_NR/REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA (unknown -> 710 at 0x102b9320-0x102b9338); stream mode accepts only REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA (anything else -> 701 at 0x102b90e0-0x102b91b0). Missing or oversized argument faults 402 at the request layer.

Target.accepted_values: TRACK_NR: textual decimal whose strtol result lies in 1..65534. REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: three u8-wrapping decimal components; computed value = h*3600+m*60+s seconds.

special_values.TRACK_NR text beyond 1..65534 (incl. '0': rejected with 711: validation is (strtol_result - 1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned on the UNMASKED value; the u16 truncation (rlwinm r4,r30,0,16,31 at 0x102b938c) only sizes the record field and never rescues an out-of-range text - '65537' faults, it does not wrap to track 1
special_values.TRACK_NR with trailing junk, leading whi: accepted - strtol skips ws/sign and endptr is NULL so the tail is ignored
special_values.'--H:M:S' or signed components ('-5:00:0: accepted: the outer '-' is consumed manually, then each %hhu applies strtoul sign/wrap rules, so '--0:1:0' parses as negative-(251:00:00 wrapped) - a quirk of layering the manual sign over %hhu
special_values.'00:00:00' or '-00:00:00' (REL_TIME/TIME: zero magnitude -> success WITHOUT submitting any request (0x102b92d4-0x102b9318); '-00:00:00' under REL_TIME still faults 711 because the sign check precedes the zero check
special_values.'-H:M:S' (REL_TIME, indexed mode): rejected with 711 - sign flag byte nonzero and Unit != TIME_DELTA (0x102b9258-0x102b9270)
special_values.'-H:M:S' (TIME_DELTA, indexed mode): accepted; parser negates only the low seconds word (neg at 0x102ab920, hi word stays 0) plus a separate sign byte; submitted as a negative relative offset
special_values.'-H:M:S' (stream mode): not sign-checked at all - the negated seconds word *1000 yields a negative millisecond operand passed straight to the session vfunc; outcome is downstream-determined
special_values.'256:00:00' / '999:99:99' (either mode): accepted with u8 wraparound: 256->0, 999->231 etc.; there is no upper bound check on the total
special_values.'1 :2:3' (whitespace before a colon): rejected - the ':' literals in the scanf format must match immediately
special_values.'01:02:03junk': accepted - sscanf stops after the 3rd conversion and the tail is never inspected

Target.validation: TRACK_NR (indexed mode only): strtol result must satisfy (t-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned else 711; on success u16 field t&0xffff is recorded in the rchsrcreq tag-8 record (the truncation is field-width only; the range check ran on the raw strtol value, so no wrap-to-valid exists). REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: f_102ab830 failure -> 711 indexed / 701 stream; indexed-mode leading '-' under REL_TIME -> 711; indexed-mode zero magnitude -> silent success no-op; stream mode performs no sign or zero gating. Missing/unparsable at the request layer -> 402.

Mode 2 uses indexed seeks. With TRACK_NR, requires capability 0x00400000 at 0x102b91a8. REL_TIME and TIME_DELTA need 0x00200000 at 0x102b9214. Unknown unit in this mode returns 710. For other modes only REL_TIME and TIME_DELTA reach the streamer; no mask test occurs there.

Indexed time seeks parse with f_102ab830, reject a negative REL_TIME before submitting, and use f_1032e4dc with the time pair. A zero pair skips submission and succeeds. A failed boolean result maps to 701.
Track path calls strtol without an end pointer, then requires the full result in the range 1..65534; otherwise returns 711. A false indexed submission is also 711. True becomes zero.
Non-indexed paths pass milliseconds from the parsed seconds word to f_106a7930 and use its return only as a boolean. The action never exposes that return verbatim; false becomes 701.

Seek.events_triggered: No UPnP event is emitted synchronously by this path; the SOAP response is committed immediately after the engine accepts the request while the actual position/track change is applied asynchronously by the chsrc transaction or streamer session. Any LastChange/state-variable update therefore originates downstream of the async apply and is not statically proven in this path.
Seek.state_transitions: None synchronously. The accepted seek is queued/applied by the player engine after the call returns; decoder, position and track-index state change happen inside the async transaction/streamer path, not in this handler.
Seek.return_behavior: The impl returns an integer status. On 0 the wrapper commits an empty 200 OK via req vfunc +0x0c (0x102f9494). On nonzero the code is forwarded to the request fault path req vfunc +0x14 at 0x102f944c and surfaces as the UPnPError errorCode. Caveats: (1) the wrapper tests cr0 rather than r3 at 0x102f9440; impl epilogues' stack-canary xor. leaves cr0.eq=1 on normal return, so rc reaches the completion vfunc +0x0c with r4=rc which handles the status-bearing response - the +0x14 branch is effectively a fallback. (2) In stream mode rc==0 only proves a session object accepted the call; the session vfunc's byte result is captured to a flag that gates a log line (0x102b91d8) and is not reflected in the SOAP status - a rejected streamer seek still reports success. (3) In indexed mode rc==0 only proves the rchsrcreq was enqueued, not that the seek applied; a zero-magnitude time target returns 0 without enqueueing at all.

events_triggered.description: Both indexed consumers complete an unchanged active crossfade value without requesting its change notification. A changed value can schedule LastChange for the current state snapshot, which reads and publishes the new CurrentCrossfadeMode with the other common transport fields. The stopped or paused path records state before scheduling; a SOAP success is not a guarantee of a dedicated event. The stopped or paused update can wake the sender before its snapshot becomes current. A snapshot installed at the head advances the change generation immediately; one queued behind it advances the generation when collection moves past older snapshots.

evidence.notes: Record op 12: writes crossfade argument as halfword at +0xfc and 1 as halfword at +0xfe.
Submits the record to *(impl+0x580). A zero result gives 712; a nonzero result clears impl+0x6ed8 and returns zero to the wrapper.
Submission f_10255f64 stores the record at session+0x2594, signals session+0x2e8, then tail-calls this helper, which waits for request byte +0xe0 and returns byte +0xe1.

Both engine tables bind +0x200 to 0x102e6048 (table words 0x10eaf4ec and 0x10edfdb8). It locks impl+0x458 and calls f_102e43a0 at 0x102e61d4 and 0x102e61f8 for the two subscriber groups, with r7=1 and r7=0 respectively. The formatter opens LastChange for InstanceID 0 at 0x102e47b0.

The formatter's full transport block writes CurrentPlayMode from the collected string at stack +0x60de and CurrentCrossfadeMode from the collected boolean at stack +0x12522. The formatter calls f_102b5a1c at 0x102e4698 to collect the transport snapshot and can skip the block on a delta when impl+0x7785 is clear.
Indexed consumers fetch and clear the pending request pointer at session+0x2594. Their offset jump tables at 0x10ea8468 and 0x10ea84d0 select handlers by request+0xe4.

The LastChange collector calls f_102b5a1c and promotes its nonzero dirty result to impl+0xa0a2. f_102b5658 promotes that flag to the latched +0x7785 at 0x102b56ac and clears the source flag on a consuming pass at 0x102b57a0. The delta branch at 0x102e47d8 tests +0x7785 before emitting the common TransportState, CurrentPlayMode and CurrentCrossfadeMode block.

Op 12 calls f_10258130 from both handlers (second site 0x1026845c). It writes the 0x8 flag of the active track list's +0x26dc through f_10145e48 and also applies it to both alternate lists when the request's +0xfe flag is set. The active-list helper returns 0 for a change, 1 for an unchanged flag and 2 for a failed capability test.

The playing consumer sets its post-request notification condition only for a changed active-list bit. Both changed and unchanged complete successfully; return 2 goes to failed completion. A notification on the playing path uses the sender at session+0x2578 (call at 0x10265a08), if its listener reference and sender are nonnull.
The indexed snapshot reads active track-list flags and writes crossfade from bit 0x8 to the snapshot boolean. f_102e43a0 renders it as CurrentCrossfadeMode.

On the running path a changed op-12 result enters the refresh tail at 0x1026592c. f_103410c0 increments the generation at indexed session+0x327f8; a same-bit success does not enter that tail on its own. The consuming state getter f_10341c74 compares that generation with +0x327fc (0x10341cd0), copies the new generation into the baseline at 0x10341cf4 when consuming, and returns its change indication to f_1026021c. The running tail separately tests for a live listener and a nonnull sender before scheduling event work at 0x10265a08.

After returning request completion, the stopped/paused worker enters f_102642d4 only if its change flag is set; op 11 and op 12 set the flag on helper return 0 rather than on unchanged return 1. The worker records the current queue snapshot through f_103420a4 at 0x1026470c, and can schedule through the indexed sender at 0x102648c4 after checking the listener and sender. f_103420a4 can advance the state generation at 0x10342440 when recording the snapshot.

Stopped/paused common notification f_102642d4 passes the indexed timeline at session+0x327f0 to f_103420a4. The state word comes from session+0x32800: values 1 through 8 map through 0x10ea8740 to 0,1,1,1,2,1,1,3; other values pass 1. f_103404c8 writes this mapped state at snapshot+0x288, the supplied track/index halfword at +0x28c and the two-word effective time (first stack argument, local sp+0x5c at the caller) at +0x290/+0x294.

The indexed timeline is ordered by the snapshots' effective time. f_105a8fd4 returns true for existing time >= new time, so insertion at that point replaces the existing node and returns its suffix to the free list. If all existing nodes are earlier, the usual path appends. The tail coalesces when the +0x28c halfwords match and its state is 1: for unequal times, a new state of 1 replaces it using the old effective time; any other new state appends. The equal-time tail subbranch also replaces (it retains the old time for new state 1).

Replacing the head (or installing the first node) increments timeline generation +8, which is session+0x327f8. Inserting or replacing after the head does not increment it here. Before collection compares the generation to +0xc at 0x10341ce0, f_103410d8 advances the head to the last snapshot due by the requested time, incrementing +8 for each node retired at 0x10341184. With no other dirty source, a sender pass before a non-head record becomes due does not make the common transport block dirty solely from that record.

The stopped/paused function continues after the timeline write regardless of the replacement helper's result (which it saves separately for its own return). After promoting the listener reference, it wakes the AVTransport event source at 0x102648c4 if that reference and session+0x2578 are nonnull; f_1067c6ec separately checks the live source and its sender. Scheduling this pass is not itself a generation increment.

side_effects.description: A successful insert writes the next URI descriptor and inserts the prepared block at the saved position. The action then requests removal of any old entries after the block. Clearing an existing next URI requests removal from the saved position through the end, then clears the descriptor. Neither removal result changes the action result.

evidence.notes: Clears the next URI storage after submitting the removal range, regardless of response; sets +0x4252 at 0x102ae038.
Successful insertion changes the next URI descriptor and sets the dirty byte; a possible subsequent range request does not govern the result.

The commitAppend worker checks the transaction ID at 0x1014ddc0, grows the queue by the prepared count, can move the appended block to the chosen insertion position, and writes the post-commit total from list+0x26c8 at 0x1014df9c. The action checks that total for nonzero at 0x102ae148.

Op 14 selects its list and passes one-based first and last positions into f_1014e9a8 (direct calls 0x10266458 and 0x10268534, or current-list variants). The removal worker subtracts one from both positions, bounds-checks both against the list size, and removes the inclusive range.

After commit, requests the inclusive range from insertion position plus prepared count through post-commit total when that range is nonempty. Clear uses the saved insertion position through the current total instead: f_1025b35c returns position minus one, and f_1025b3e8 returns total minus position plus one. If the position is unset, they return total and zero, so clear submits an empty range. The action ignores trim and clear removal results.

events_triggered.description: A successful insert or clear of an existing next URI marks both next-URI fields dirty. The action and the LastChange collector hold the same engine lock. The action does not wake the notification sender directly; qualifying indexed queue changes wake the AVTransport source. If that wake is skipped, a later pass of the same sender can still collect the change from the registered source. Marking the descriptor dirty does not start a timer or guarantee a standalone notification. A delta reads the URI and metadata together at collection time.

evidence.notes: If both arguments are empty and a next URI is stored, submits a range request then clears impl+0x1a03, +0x1e04 and +0x2e05 and sets dirty byte +0x4252. This path ignores the submission return. If the next URI is already empty, returns zero without that request.
Successful insert stores the next URI descriptor at impl+0x1a03 using f_102ed638 and sets +0x4252=1. It may send a further range request at 0x102ae1d4; that result is ignored.

Both engine tables bind +0x200 to 0x102e6048 (table words 0x10eaf4ec and 0x10edfdb8). It locks impl+0x458 and calls f_102e43a0 at 0x102e61d4 and 0x102e61f8 for the two subscriber groups, with r7=1 and r7=0 respectively. The formatter opens LastChange for InstanceID 0 at 0x102e47b0.
Samples impl+0x4252 into pending event byte +0xa095 if not already pending. A consuming pass clears the source dirty byte at 0x102b57bc.
The delta branch checks +0xa095, then writes NextAVTransportURI from +0x1a03 and NextAVTransportURIMetaData from +0x1e04; full serialization can write the pair without this test.

The engine wrapper unlocks and returns without calling the sender. The indexed workers complete op 2 and op 14 before their notification checks; the running path tests its change flag and sender before 0x10265a08, and the stopped path calls f_102642d4 only when its change flag is set at 0x10267e04.

f_10255f64 posts the request and waits in f_1032e658 until request byte +0xe0 signals completion. The action then sets the descriptor dirty byte: after op 2 and before an optional trim, or after op 14 on clear. The consumer signals completion at 0x10265910 or 0x10267dfc before its explicit notification checks.

The running op-2 consumer directly commits a non-current list without setting the change flags initialized at 0x1026579c and 0x102657a8. For the current list it calls f_1025a350 and sets stack +0x38 at 0x10266980. The subsequent sender path also requires a live reference and nonnull sender at session+0x2578.

The running op-14 current-list path rejects a zero start or first > last, and leaves its change flags clear if f_10259f38 returns false. On success it sets stack +0x38 at 0x102666cc. The non-current-list path calls f_1014e9a8 without setting that change flag.

For stopped playback op 2 sets stack +0x2c after a current-list commit, but not after a non-current-list commit. The current-list op-14 handler sets the same flag at 0x10268d94 only if f_1014e9a8 returns true. The non-current-list branch does not set it. At 0x10267e04 the consumer requires that flag before entering the notification path.

The action acquires impl+0x458 before checking indexed mode and calling f_102af1c8/f_102adf20, and releases the lock at 0x102af2e4 after that worker returns. Both dirty writes occur inside the worker. Even if indexed request completion wakes the sender before the write, the same-engine collector f_102e6048 locks impl+0x458 at 0x102e6170 before invoking the formatter at 0x102e61d4 or 0x102e61f8.

The running indexed path's sender call reaches f_1067c46c and checks the live event sender at source+0xb4 before calling f_10678c50. This helper sets the sender's pending byte +0x10e and signals its condition at +0xb8; it does not serialize a delta on the indexed worker's stack.

When impl+0xa095 is set, the delta formatter reads the current URI at impl+0x1a03 and metadata at impl+0x1e04. The two tags are emitted together at 0x102e4d88 through 0x102e4ddc; this branch does not clear the pending byte.

ZonePlayer startup selects the AVTransport object at zone+0x1934 plus 0x10 when nonnull (isel r10,r0,r8,30, raw word 0x7d40479e), paired with its owner reference from zone+0x1938. It passes the pair at sp+0x128 in r6 at 0x103fbc3c. f_1025f19c keeps r6 in r24 and copies the pointer to indexed-session+0x2578 and the reference to +0x257c at 0x1025f540 and 0x1025f54c. This is the same AVTransport event-source subobject that the engine initializes with name AVTransport at 0x102c06e4 and that f_102e6048 accesses at 0x102e6190.

The active event-source tables at 0x10eaf510 and 0x10edfddc (stored at engine+0x10 at 0x102c0d40 and 0x105123d0) bind slot +0x1c to f_102e6974, which adjusts this and returns 1 through f_102e6964. Thus, on an AVTransport source scan, f_1067d028 returns ready whether source+0x110 is already pending or the override is called. The generic +0x170 and +0x18c/+0x190 subscription deadline walk at 0x1067d148 is for the base-slot implementation, not this override.

The sender clears its pending byte +0x10e before scanning its registered sources. If not pending, it waits on sender+0xb8 without a timeout when the accumulated deadline is zero (0x1067a118), otherwise it waits using the nonzero deadline (0x1067a17c through 0x1067a29c). Consequently a later independent wake or deadline-driven scan can consider AVTransport even when that source's own wake was skipped, but the next-URI dirty byte is not part of this wait decision.

The sender checks the ready source's last-dispatch time from slot +0x10 (f_1067ab74 returns source+0xc4) and its spacing interval from slot +0x0c (f_102aa368 returns the 64-bit value 250 ms). The spacing branch contributes a deferred deadline at 0x1067a0f8 rather than calling the collector yet. Otherwise f_10683da0 records the dispatch time at source+0xc4/+0xc8, clears source+0x110 at 0x10683fdc, and calls slot +0x18 at 0x1068406c for nonempty work batches. Checks current URI impl+0x5dc for a case-insensitive http:// or https:// prefix via f_1014743c. If neither is present, returns 701 before examining the requested next URI and metadata.

Nonempty NextURI must have a case-insensitive http:// or https:// prefix. Other nonempty schemes or an empty URI with nonempty metadata return 714. HTTP(S) URI length >1024 or metadata length >4096 (strlen, excluding NUL) returns 402.

If both arguments are empty and a next URI is stored, submits a range request then clears impl+0x1a03, +0x1e04 and +0x2e05 and sets dirty byte +0x4252. This path ignores the submission return. If the next URI is already empty, returns zero without that request.

Nonempty URI uses preliminary indexed requests. A false first or second submission yields 800. f_1014f6dc can return nonzero unchanged at 0x102ae0f8. On its success the insert at 0x102ae13c must return true with a nonzero result halfword, else returns 800.
Successful insert stores the next URI descriptor at impl+0x1a03 using f_102ed638 and sets +0x4252=1. It may send a further range request at 0x102ae1d4; that result is ignored.

Calls f_10564cb0 with a 0x1001-byte limit and replacement byte 0x20. Its loop at 0x10564cd0 copies through NUL and replaces each LF (0x0a) with a space (isel word 0x7d264f9e at 0x10564cd8). The resulting pointer is passed to preparation and stored with the next URI.

The op-1 consumers at 0x10266328 and 0x10268298 use list selector 0 and call f_1014b084 with an output transaction ID at request+0xe8. On preparation failure, op 19 passes that transaction ID to cancelAppend f_1014b1a8 from 0x10266504 or 0x10268888.

Op 2 for the indexed list embedded at session+0x2b188 uses its saved one-based insertion position at session+0x326ce, or sets it to list length plus one if zero or out of bounds. The stopped consumer uses the same rule at 0x10268cb0. The op forwards the append transaction, prepared count, insertion-position output, and total-length output to the commit worker.

The commitAppend worker checks the transaction ID at 0x1014ddc0, grows the queue by the prepared count, can move the appended block to the chosen insertion position, and writes the post-commit total from list+0x26c8 at 0x1014df9c. The action checks that total for nonzero at 0x102ae148.

Op 14 selects its list and passes one-based first and last positions into f_1014e9a8 (direct calls 0x10266458 and 0x10268534, or current-list variants). The removal worker subtracts one from both positions, bounds-checks both against the list size, and removes the inclusive range.

After commit, requests the inclusive range from insertion position plus prepared count through post-commit total when that range is nonempty. Clear uses the saved insertion position through the current total instead: f_1025b35c returns position minus one, and f_1025b3e8 returns total minus position plus one. If the position is unset, they return total and zero, so clear submits an empty range. The action ignores trim and clear removal results.

For a raw HTTP(S) URI that does not match the playlist loader predicates and whose metadata does not select f_10153fe0, f_1014b700 calls f_1014b624 with the original URI. If the parsed ID starts with SQ:, the alternate call at 0x1014b7ec passes the percent-decoded ID suffix after the last colon as an additional argument. A false result takes the 800/803 mapping at 0x1014f604.

The normal f_1014b3a8 branch hands the URI, descriptor, and metadata argument to slot +0x08 on the queue-entry subobject at list+0x04. Its table entry at 0x10e936b4 binds f_10149118, which tail-calls f_101489f0 after the capacity check. The same worker family binds the +0x14-adjusting entry thunk at 0x10e936cc.

The playlist classifier f_104605cc can accept HTTP(S) URLs from the ASX/WAX/WMX, M3U/M3U8, PLS, WPL and .rsq marker tests. The action chooses f_10146300 at 0x1014f5b4 for these matches. That helper supplies a deadline 15000 ms from the current clock and a callback table at 0x10e93668 to f_104634c4, which selects a loader for the recognized format. A false result maps to 803 if descriptor +0x12 is set and to 800 otherwise.

On the metadata-selected branch (f_1015367c returns nonzero), f_1014b700 invokes f_10153fe0 with the descriptor, its parsed ID, and the callback table at 0x10e93668. A result other than 800 is returned directly by f_1014f48c; 800 is checked against the queue/capacity flag at descriptor +0x12 and may become 803.

The queue-entry callback checks existing tracks plus descriptor +0x08 against capacity before appending. At capacity it sets descriptor byte +0x12 and returns zero; the entry allocator failure at 0x10149030 also sets that byte.

The entry callback calls f_10147da8 at 0x10148a60; a false playability result takes the branch at 0x10148a8c to the unplayable-track log and increments descriptor +0x14 before the later LF and append checks. Descriptor +0x08 increments at 0x10148db4 once an entry has been written. The preparation helper compares the counts at 0x1014f7c4, not a direct query for any playable entry.

f_1015379c parses the incoming metadata via f_102fd094 and f_10c3fc68 before the loader selector runs. It sets descriptor +0x661 only when f_101205fc succeeds and the follow-up f_10120904 returns a nonnull result, which it stores at +0x65c.

A nonzero descriptor byte +0x661 immediately selects the service loader. Otherwise f_1015367c parses descriptor +0x19 with f_1056fc20 and excludes packed types 7 and 8 (low seven bits). For SID other than 254, a URI that does not start with x-sonosapi-hls: returns the successful parse result unchanged at 0x10153744. If SID is 254 or the HLS prefix matches, the selector uses the x-sonosapi-rtrecent: comparison instead. An HTTP(S) URI therefore passes the fallback test for a successfully parsed descriptor of another SID and type, but not for SID 254.

The fallback descriptor parser matches SA_RINCON, parses a base-10 number, requires an underscore at the parse endpoint, and requires a nonzero packed value. It normalizes 1 or 2 to 0xca07, and 13 or 14 to 0xcb07. In either normalized case the low seven bits are 7, which the loader selector rejects; parsing a service descriptor alone is not sufficient to select service loading.

With descriptor +0x661 nonzero, f_10153fe0 selects f_10153ddc for +0x662 equal to 2 and f_10153d24 otherwise. Both pass a null flag output to f_10153a38. With +0x661 clear, the worker returns 800 for a missing lookup result or packed type 7 or 8; otherwise it enters f_10153e98. That path performs a SID lookup and, on success, passes a flag output to f_10153a38. If that call returns zero and sets the byte, f_10153e98 substitutes 802 at 0x10153fc8.

On the error-normalization branch, f_10153a38 preserves 801 when its input byte +0x1d is nonzero. Otherwise it calls f_10c3ba54 and maps statuses outside 1042 through 1045 to 800. The raw isel at 0x10153c1c chooses 800 when the predicate returns zero; this branch alone does not establish which values a callback can actually supply.

SetPlayMode.description: Requests a repeat/shuffle mode. The engine maps exact request strings to an enum and submits indexed op 11 or, for an eligible streamer URI, dispatches to the active streamer. The Spotify streamer queues the change without waiting for it to apply. NORMAL alone can fall back to success without submitting a change.

side_effects.description: Impl locks the engine mutex at impl+0x458 (f_10557cac/f_10557848) for the operation. Play-mode enum applied to the indexed engine or forwarded to the streamer as a mode command.

events_triggered.description: The indexed queue applies mode changes to the active track list and LastChange reads the resulting mode. An unchanged indexed mode does not schedule its own notification. A changed mode can wake the sender before a queued snapshot becomes current; the wake alone does not dirty the common delta block. For Spotify, shuffle and repeat requests are sent separately and successful command replies do not notify. Accepted device state can independently publish shuffle and repeat; the SDK skips notifications for values that equal its cache. The VLI notification reaches AVTransport through a registered listener and bounded worker admission. The running mode-change callback dirties the common block and schedules the sender. LastChange reads the active provider's mode, not the requested value or a mode in the event payload.
