Both engine tables bind +0x200 to 0x102e6048 (table words 0x10eaf4ec and 0x10edfdb8). It locks impl+0x458 and calls f_102e43a0 at 0x102e61d4 and 0x102e61f8 for the two subscriber groups, with r7=1 and r7=0 respectively. The formatter opens LastChange for InstanceID 0 at 0x102e47b0.

The formatter's full transport block writes CurrentPlayMode from the collected string at stack +0x60de and CurrentCrossfadeMode from the collected boolean at stack +0x12522. The formatter calls f_102b5a1c at 0x102e4698 to collect the transport snapshot and can skip the block on a delta when impl+0x7785 is clear.
Indexed consumers fetch and clear the pending request pointer at session+0x2594. Their offset jump tables at 0x10ea8468 and 0x10ea84d0 select handlers by request+0xe4.

The LastChange collector calls f_102b5a1c and promotes its nonzero dirty result to impl+0xa0a2. f_102b5658 promotes that flag to the latched +0x7785 at 0x102b56ac and clears the source flag on a consuming pass at 0x102b57a0. The delta branch at 0x102e47d8 tests +0x7785 before emitting the common TransportState, CurrentPlayMode and CurrentCrossfadeMode block.

The playing op-11 handler compares the requested enum with active-list +0x26dc masked to 7. Equality jumps to 0x10266618, succeeds without setting the change flag and does not call f_10259db0. The stopped/paused op-11 handler calls f_1014da80, which similarly returns 1 for equality, 0 for change and 2 for rejection.
The indexed snapshot obtains the mode name from f_10145f94 on the active track list. The event formatter uses its returned name at 0x102e4828.

After returning request completion, the stopped/paused worker enters f_102642d4 only if its change flag is set; op 11 and op 12 set the flag on helper return 0 rather than on unchanged return 1. The worker records the current queue snapshot through f_103420a4 at 0x1026470c, and can schedule through the indexed sender at 0x102648c4 after checking the listener and sender. f_103420a4 can advance the state generation at 0x10342440 when recording the snapshot.

In the running op-11 handler, f_10259db0 returning 0 sets the same generation-refresh flag as changed op 12. If the mode switch invalidates the running track position, f_10259db0 sets its optional position-rebuild byte at 0x10259f14; the worker tests this separately, without undoing the common changed-mode flag.

f_106a9e88 resolves the streamer+0x354 target through its contained object's slot +0x2c. A returned object gets slot +0x34 with the original four arguments; the wrapper ignores that virtual method's return and reports 1. A missing source or null result from +0x2c reports 0 instead.

Stopped/paused common notification f_102642d4 passes the indexed timeline at session+0x327f0 to f_103420a4. The state word comes from session+0x32800: values 1 through 8 map through 0x10ea8740 to 0,1,1,1,2,1,1,3; other values pass 1. f_103404c8 writes this mapped state at snapshot+0x288, the supplied track/index halfword at +0x28c and the two-word effective time (first stack argument, local sp+0x5c at the caller) at +0x290/+0x294.

The indexed timeline is ordered by the snapshots' effective time. f_105a8fd4 returns true for existing time >= new time, so insertion at that point replaces the existing node and returns its suffix to the free list. If all existing nodes are earlier, the usual path appends. The tail coalesces when the +0x28c halfwords match and its state is 1: for unequal times, a new state of 1 replaces it using the old effective time; any other new state appends. The equal-time tail subbranch also replaces (it retains the old time for new state 1).

Replacing the head (or installing the first node) increments timeline generation +8, which is session+0x327f8. Inserting or replacing after the head does not increment it here. Before collection compares the generation to +0xc at 0x10341ce0, f_103410d8 advances the head to the last snapshot due by the requested time, incrementing +8 for each node retired at 0x10341184. With no other dirty source, a sender pass before a non-head record becomes due does not make the common transport block dirty solely from that record.

The stopped/paused function continues after the timeline write regardless of the replacement helper's result (which it saves separately for its own return). After promoting the listener reference, it wakes the AVTransport event source at 0x102648c4 if that reference and session+0x2578 are nonnull; f_1067c6ec separately checks the live source and its sender. Scheduling this pass is not itself a generation increment.

Spotify registers streamer source type 2 through f_106a76b8: r5 is the Spotify VLI control object adjusted by +8 and r6 is the SpotifyAudioInput object. The registration helper writes these at record+4 and +8 in the first free 12-byte entry of the nine-entry table at streamer+0x2e8. f_106a8b08 selects by type and installs the record at streamer+0x354 (0x106a8df4); a failing selection callback clears it at 0x106a8e34.

Spotify finishes wiring the controller with f_1022c7d4(control, spotify+4), which stores this interface pointer at control+0x188. The controller constructor installs address point 0x10ea53a8 at control+8 (0x1022d94c). Its +0x2c entry at 0x10ea53d4 adjusts back by 8 and calls f_1022add4, which returns that stored pointer. The Spotify constructor installs address point 0x10ea2210 at spotify+4 (0x102198d4).

The Spotify interface's +0x34 entry f_10211bb0 adjusts this by -4 and enters f_10211b20. It calls f_102268a4 on the embedded Spotify thread at +0x7ae8. That helper writes pending byte +0xaec=1, stores the selector in byte +0xaed and the three halfwords in +0xaee/+0xaf0/+0xaf2. It does not check equality or call the AVTransport event sender there.

The Spotify thread consumes a pending selector-1 change in f_102269e0. It sends bit 0 of the requested mode to the shuffle setter; it sends repeat 2 when bit 2 is set, otherwise repeat takes bit 1. The worker tests the setter results separately, records failures through f_10225360 and clears pending at 0x10226a88. The SOAP success path does not wait for these results.

The shuffle setter f_10cfd2f4 submits SDK ring record 33 (INTERNAL_SHUFFLE); f_10cfd580 submits 34 (INTERNAL_REPEAT) at 0x10cfd6a0. f_10d09770 writes the selector and integer value to record+0/+4. These are different selectors from the incoming state updates 31/32. The SDK device-command handler f_10d1eb48 is installed at 0x10d21528, and its table at 0x10fd9918 sends these selectors to 0x10d1fbec and 0x10d1f7e4 respectively. These branches encode a shuffle boolean or the repeat integer and use the request builders for %s/devices/%s/set_shuffle or %s/devices/%s/set_repeat, then dispatch with separate response callbacks.

The command response callbacks f_10d17978 and f_10d17a48 return on a zero response status without sending a mode notification themselves. Separately, f_10d1c198 submits ring records 31 and 32 using device-state bytes at +0xcd04 (shuffle), +0xcd05 (repeat unless repeat-one is set), and +0xcd06 (when nonzero, use repeat value 2). The state publication at 0x10d199c0/0x10d199ec uses those same byte offsets and mapping.

The state descriptor at 0x10fdaac2 uses tag 5 to put a three-byte submessage at state+0x6014. f_10d28550 selects the nested descriptor through the table at 0x10fd9bac and recursively decodes at 0x10d294b0. The nested descriptor at 0x10fdacf2 maps tags 1, 2 and 3 to bytes +0, +1 and +2. In the installed snapshot based at device+0x6cf0, these are +0xcd04 through +0xcd06. The SDK publishes decoded state, not the values from the outgoing setter records.

f_10d1caa4 calls the state publisher f_10d1c198. Its call at 0x10d1d38c is from the successful StateConflictResponse path: the decoded entries are tried in order, a state-machine mismatch goes elsewhere, and the accepted final entry reaches this call after f_10d17308 copies scratch+0 to device+0x6c9c at 0x10d17368. The replace_state branch of f_10d1dc24 also calls f_10d1caa4 at 0x10d1e598 after decoding, matching the machine ID and pause byte, and successfully installing state through f_10d17308. f_10d1c198 itself requires a nonnull device+0x2d8 track after its selection/refresh before reaching the two ring submissions.

The separate successful StateResponse callback f_10d1d48c parses at 0x10d1d6f8 for the active-device branch and checks the state-machine and pause fields before copying decoded state from scratch to device+0x6cf0 at 0x10d1dacc. It installs the selected track at 0x10d1db30 when its index is in bounds. The final device+0x2d8 null check at 0x10d1d9f4 guards the call to f_10d1c198 with argument 1.

f_10d1dc24 matches observe_state at 0x10d1dd00 and stop_and_observe at 0x10d1dd18. After successful decoding, observe_state calls f_10d19704 with argument 3 at 0x10d1e67c. That publisher returns immediately for argument 3 when device+0xbde is set; the publishing observe_state path first copies decoded state at 0x10d1e5bc. The matching stop_and_observe path copies decoded state at 0x10d1e810 and calls f_10d19704 with argument 4 at 0x10d1e8a8. The publishing branch sends selector 31 then selector 32, independently of the setter acknowledgements.

The SDK update table at 0x10fd3fd4 sends selector 31 to 0x10cfa620 (shuffle) and 32 to 0x10cfa5d4 (repeat). Shuffle compares the update word to the cached byte at +0xb86; repeat compares to the cached word at +0xb88. Equality takes the zero-result branch without calling the notification helper. Unequal values update those fields and call f_10d3bb08 with IDs 5/6 for shuffle on/off or 7/8 for repeat on/off. The repeat getter f_10cfd29c reads +0xb8b, the low byte of that same big-endian word, so transitions between repeat values 1 and 2 update the getter and request notification ID 7 even though both are nonzero.

Spotify setup builds the playback callback record at stack+52 with f_10213a48 as its first word (0x10213f70), and registers it with f_10cf52e0 and the Spotify work-queue context. f_10cfc0f8 calls f_10d3a638, which stores the callback at 0x110bf65c and the context at 0x110bf668. f_10d3bb08 skips a null callback or invokes it with the notification ID and context. f_10213a48 saves the ID and Spotify receiver in its work item and queues the closure whose invoke function is f_10218574 (0x10213c68 through 0x10213c98).

f_10218574 dispatches the queued notification ID through f_10217d80; IDs 5 through 8 share the 0x10218150 entry. The worker selects the controller at Spotify+0x59f8 when its slot +0x10 test (f_1022ac04, controller byte +0x18c) is nonzero; otherwise it uses the embedded receiver at Spotify+0x5a00. It requires the selected receiver's slot +0x10 test to pass before dispatch. f_1022694c reads the current SDK getters, producing shuffle bit 0 only for shuffle value 1, repeat-all bit 1 for repeat value 1 and repeat-one bit 2 for repeat value 2 (verified against the f_10145f50 name table). The worker passes this mode to receiver slot +0x44. Controller table word 0x10ea532c selects f_1022d5e4, which stores the mode through f_104dc1e8 at audio-input+0x584c and then sends onVirtualLineInPlayModesChanged. The embedded fallback's +0x44 entry at 0x10ea44a4 is a no-op.

Controller byte +0x18c is read under the controller+0x50 lock. The source selection path sets it before invoking the activation callback through the interface at controller+0x3f4, keeps it set on success at 0x1022bd80, and clears it on callback failure at 0x1022be3c. The RSpotifyVLIControl deactivate path clears it at 0x1022c5f4, and the constructor initializes it to zero at 0x1022d9ac.

The controller forwards onVirtualLineInPlayModesChanged through the interface stored at controller+0x3f0. f_1021996c supplies streamer+0x120 to the controller constructor, and its +0x34 slot (0x10f046b8) thunk adjusts back to the streamer. f_106a6a8c forwards to the listener at streamer+0x2d0, slot +0x34. The listener's address point 0x10ecbe2c binds that slot to f_10416de4; it calls f_1041adb4 with the VliPropertiesChangedEvent mode flag set and the metadata flag clear.

f_1041adb4 takes the event-loop handle under lock and skips enqueueing when it is null (0x1041afb4, with the no-eventloop diagnostic at 0x1041b338). With a loop it assigns a cookie and calls f_100f14ec with the wrapper built by f_10419858. The wrapper's invoke function f_10418d10 reaches f_10418794, which walks the locked registry at 0x110a1948, skips listeners with byte +0x1c nonzero, and calls slot 0 of each enabled listener with the event payload at 0x10418c30.

The AVTransport listener setup f_102c1f2c inserts the interface at object+0x258 into the same registry (key at entry+0x10; owning handle at +0x14) if not already present. Slot 0 is f_102bf138 at table word 0x10eaf7b4 (also 0x10ee0080), which subtracts 0x258 and tail-calls f_102beca8. The constructor clears listener byte +0x1c at 0x102c09bc. Holding the registry lock, teardown f_102bfaf0 removes the listener immediately through f_102f1f4c at 0x102c040c if dispatch-active byte 0x11096cc8 is clear, otherwise marks it for removal by setting listener+0x1c at 0x102bfe84. The dispatcher skips set bytes, clears the dispatch-active byte at 0x10418980, then clears each marked listener byte at 0x104189f8 as part of unlinking the node at 0x10418a78.

The AVTransport VliPropertiesChangedEvent receiver f_102beca8 copies the metadata and mode flags and submits the callback f_102afb40 via f_102eff8c. That submission builds the work record and calls f_102ef534 at 0x102f0360. Its f_1099bd70 test with selector zero atomically increments the count and succeeds only if the previous count was below the limit stored at counter object+8; otherwise it rolls back the increment. The accepted path calls executor slot +0x10 at 0x102efdc0. With the mode flag set, the running callback enters f_102afa40, which sets impl+0x4658 and calls f_1067c6ec on the event source at impl+0x10. f_102b5658 tests the flag at 0x102b582c, promotes it to the common LastChange dirty latch at impl+0x7785, and clears the source flag at 0x102b57a4 on a consuming pass.

Startup f_100c1478 saves the f_1099c76c pool at 0x1109bc38. The startup call at 0x100c1af4 passes that pointer at stack+0x18, and f_1018d27c saves it at owner+0x57f8 (0x1018df8c). events.mechanism: UPnP GENA NOTIFY. A separate event sender collects eligible batches from the registered AVTransport event source. LastChange carries a snapshot or a delta selected from dirty and pending state; the SOAP return does not deliver the event.

evidence.notes: AVT event template with ~30 variables + 8 constant fields
propertyset wrapper

The LastChange collector calls f_102b5a1c and promotes its nonzero dirty result to impl+0xa0a2. f_102b5658 promotes that flag to the latched +0x7785 at 0x102b56ac and clears the source flag on a consuming pass at 0x102b57a0. The delta branch at 0x102e47d8 tests +0x7785 before emitting the common TransportState, CurrentPlayMode and CurrentCrossfadeMode block.
AVTransport engine slot +0x200 enters f_102e6048, collects under the engine mutex, and calls f_102e43a0 for two subscriber groups where present, passing r7=1 and 0 respectively.

ZonePlayer startup f_103f8924 pairs the nonnull AVTransport object at zone+0x1934 plus 0x10 with the owner at zone+0x1938. It passes this pair with the event wrapper at zone+0x228 to f_104017c8. That wrapper loads the sender at +4 and calls f_1067938c, which appends the raw source to the sender vector at +0x110 and retains the owning pair in the vector at +0x11c. The +0x128 vector is different: f_103f6a48 passes that same AVTransport source to f_106794f0 at 0x103f6ad0 to queue its removal. f_10679678 removes matches from the scan vector, and the scan itself skips pending-removal matches at 0x10679cf0 through 0x10679cfc.

The sender checks pending byte +0x10e at 0x10679bbc. A pending wake clears it and enters the scan. Otherwise it waits on sender+0xb8, with a timed wait only when it has a nonzero deadline; either wake path then copies the +0x110 vector. The scan tests readiness through f_1067d028 and reads the source's previous dispatch time through slot +0x10. A zero timestamp bypasses spacing; otherwise AVTransport's slot +0x0c supplies 250 ms (f_102aa368 -> f_102aa354). The elapsed-time test can contribute an earlier retry time at 0x1067a0f8 instead of dispatching. This is minimum spacing, not a fixed 250 ms poll.

f_10683da0 updates source+0xc4/+0xc8, scans subscription groups from source+0xa0 and clears source+0x110. f_10684d00 takes the batch table at sp+0x48 and reaches f_10684ac8, which can populate the group-list head at sp+0x50 indirectly. The selector at 0x10683fe0 requires a group; 0x10683ff8 through 0x10684004 require its vector to be nonempty before calling source slot +0x18. The base and derived AVTransport event-source address points 0x10eaf510 and 0x10edfddc bind it to f_102e6400, which adjusts this by -0x10 and reaches f_102e6048.

Builds the /MediaRenderer/AVTransport/Control entry, sets the capability mask 0x2000 at 0x1019553c and stores the enable byte ctx[0x571c] XOR 1 at 0x10195684.
Zoneplayer composite init calls the AVTransport wrapper constructor (f_102fc9c0). That constructor stores 0x10eb300c at wrapper+0 and clears wrapper+4 and +8 before the engine is bound.
Base engine construction installs 0x10eaf2ec through an address formed at 0x102c0cd8.
The derived constructor calls f_102c05d8 at 0x1051218c then installs 0x10edfbb8 into the same object's vptr. The derived constructor is called at 0x103fb5d8.
The engine is read via wrapper+4 at dispatch; a matching action with that pointer still null returns 401 instead of entering the action handler.

Normal ZonePlayer construction passes the embedded SOAP aggregate as the sixth argument of the engine constructor chain (from 0x1018ef1c via stack +0xfc and r8). AVTransport is constructed at aggregate+0x0c at 0x1018fb70.

The 0xae38-byte allocation on the engine-creation path is passed to the derived AVTransport constructor. The result is kept in the owner at +0x1934 and its lifetime controller at +0x1938 (0x103fb680/0x103fb678). No base-only allocation or current group membership test selects the constructor at this site.
The activation routine passes obj+0x1934 as r6, and loads r3 from obj+0x220, the SOAP aggregate pointer saved by the owning constructor at 0x103fa75c.

Copies the object from r6[0] to aggregate+0x10 (AVTransport wrapper+4). The lifetime controller is stored at aggregate+0x14 at 0x104d4ba4. If r6[0] is null, the binder skips this service; a raw nonnull pointer with no controller takes the 0x104d5830 store.

The ZonePlayer destructor computes r30=this+0x40000 at 0x10192450. It replaces the AVTransport member vptr at this+0x3fa38 with 0x10e978e8 and calls f_100c5050 on the nonnull controller loaded from member+8. The sequence does not zero member+4.

The first two slots point to f_102fc9e4 and f_102fcae8. Both restore the base vptr and release a nonnull wrapper+8 controller; decrementing the strong count from one invokes controller slot +8 and then drops the weak count. A final weak release invokes +0xc. The second destructor also deallocates the 12-byte wrapper.

When a bind supplies a different controller, it retains the incoming one and drops the previous one's strong count before storing the replacement at aggregate+0x14. A null engine skips the bind entirely at 0x104d4b10, so this binder is not an unbind operation.

notes: Engine impl object fields recovered: +0x458 command mutex; +0x3dc name string (nonzero gates scoped logging); +0x580 indexed/chsrc session manager (f_10255f64 submit, f_10256a84 ops); +0x5a0 streamer session object (vfuncs f_106a7880 pause, f_106a7a34 next, f_106a7930 seek, f_106a9e88 mode); +0x5dc source/URI control target (cap queries f_10147928/f_101471f0/f_101475dc/f_10148308/f_10688070, precondition f_102931f0); +0x5d4 default state source; +0x4654 transport-source mode enum {0,1,2} (2=indexed/queue); +0x6ed8 pending-op field cleared on successful track/mode ops; +0x7778 cleared by Stop; +0x1a03 shuffle-capable flag; +0x5a86/+0x5a7f/+0x7764/+0x7766/+0x776c chime-restore flags; +0xaaa0 member object touched by Stop. Engine vtables: A=0x10eaf2ec, B=0x10edfbb8 - identical for all actions except SetAVTransportURI and the three Become*Coordinator* ops (B overrides to 0x10513230/0x10513244/0x105133e4/0x105134a8, the group-aware class).

Two engine classes implement every action: standalone (vtable 0x10eaf2ec, ctor f_102cc070) and group-capable (vtable 0x10edfbb8, ctor f_104000c4). They share all 54 vfunc slots except ctor/dtor and the four coordinator-sensitive impls (+0x08 SetAVTransportURI, +0x54 BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup, +0xd0 BecomeGroupCoordinator, +0xd4 BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource). B impls gate on the zonegroup-topology singleton (global 0x110c8478 via f_1090ad44 + state predicate f_109089f0 on obj+0xcc); when ungrouped the B Become* impls tail-call the A impls verbatim.

In the per-entry callback f_105116e0 an empty ContainerURI (lbz job+0x18 == 0 at 0x1051171c) sends each entry to f_1014f808 at 0x10511750; a nonempty one sends it to f_1014fb34(job+0x18, job+0x419, ...) at 0x105117c4, i.e. the container URI and metadata travel with every entry insert.

Resolved: The container URI is checked and then stored as a pointer in the row template, not copied per track. f_1014fb34 returns 800 when it contains a newline (strchr at 0x1014fc10, 0x1014fc24) and passes it to f_1014b270, which stores it at row+0x770 (0x1014b340). Resolved: Position rule, from f_1014dc98: desired = min(Desired, old_length+1) (isel 0x7f8ae75e at 0x1014ddb0). In a queue without the order array (bit 0 of q+0x26dc clear), FirstTrackNumberEnqueued is old_length+1 (0x1014dfec). When 1 <= desired <= old_length, f_101463c8(q, desired-1, new_length-(desired-1), old_length-(desired-1)) rotates the new block to that position and FirstTrackNumberEnqueued becomes desired (0x1014e028). The direct-call closure of the mutation hook f_1014d738, four levels deep (239 functions, including the in-process dispatcher f_10117654), contains no call to f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700. The session consumer's mark-changed call targets AVTransport, and the subscription paths (f_1068faa4, f_1068e65c) only cover new subscribers. No data word in any non-.text section points at f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700, so these setters are reached only by direct calls. An indirect call from a Queue mutation would therefore have to land in one of their direct callers. No call to f_1067c6ec lies in the queue engine (0x10144000..0x10156000) or in the Queue manager (0x10460000..0x10468000). The session code calls it at 0x102648c4 and 0x10265a08 (AVTransport, per S01). The AVTransport implementation (0x102b0000..0x102f8000) calls it at 59 sites. 54 of them pass an object's +0x10 address, which is the AVTransport interface pattern that S01 traced at 0x103fbb78. The other 5 sites pass a saved register, and each register is also set to an object's +0x10 address: r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b7f84 (call 0x102b7fbc), r30 = r28+0x10 at 0x102bc3f0 (0x102bc484), r27 = r29+0x10 at 0x102c3548 (0x102c3588), r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b79b8 (0x102b7ab4) and r25 = r30+0x10 at 0x102e30f8 (0x102e32e8). At the last two sites the only later definitions are epilogue reloads (0x102b7a90, 0x102e3294) on paths that leave before the call (0x102b7aa0; 0x102e32b4, 0x102e32c8). This is a register-definition scan, not a full path proof. None of the 59 sites uses an object's +0x8 address, which is where the Queue interface sits in the Queue manager. Across the whole binary there are 213 calls to f_1067c6ec or f_1067c46c. 111 of them pass some object's +0x8 address, the same shape as the Queue interface at qm+8. None of those 111 calls is in a slot function of the Queue manager vtables 0x10ed1bcc or 0x10ed1c10. None of them loads the Queue manager pointer (main+0x193c) within 40 instructions before the call, or its holder (main+0x1940) earlier in the same function. This scan matches instruction patterns. It does not prove the base object of each +0x8 call, so whether a Queue mutation reaches the pending byte through some other path stays open. On timing: for each interface the eventing pass f_10679b14 ('runOnce starting') calls f_1067d028 (0x10679da8). f_1067d028 returns 1 at once when the pending byte +0x110 is set. Otherwise it walks the subscriber list (count +0xa0, list +0x1c) and checks each subscriber's byte +0x170 and times +0x18c/+0x190. For a due interface the pass reads the timeval that slot +0x10 returns (the Queue's slot is the shared base function f_1067ab74, which returns this+0xc4) and tests it with timevalIsZero (0x10679df0). A nonzero timeval branches to a separate path at 0x10679ffc. A zero timeval goes on to send through f_10683da0 (0x10679e54) and folds the 8-byte timeval at 0x1109b010 into the next wake time with timevalMinimize (0x10679e64). 0x1109b010 is in .bss and its address is taken in many functions (f_100c71d0, f_100e323c, f_100fd44c and others), so its value is set at runtime and the wake interval is not a constant in the image. For this action the commit f_1014dc98 calls f_1014d738 at 0x1014dfcc when the queue name byte q+0x4c is nonzero (0x1014dfbc).

Established (who calls the LastChange generator): the Queue manager is allocated in f_103fa434 (new(0x130) at 0x103fb6b4, constructor f_10465fac at 0x103fb6e8) and stored at main+0x193c, with its shared-pointer holder at main+0x1940 (0x103fb720). The constructor installs a second vtable 0x10ed1c10 at qm+8 (0x104660d8). In that vtable, slot +0x14 is f_10465f74, a this-8 thunk to f_10465e28 (Queue-manager slot +0x34, the only direct caller of f_10465e28 at 0x10465f78), and slot +0x18 is f_1067ab54, which tail-calls this->vtable+0x14. The upnpeventing loop f_10679b14 walks an array of 8-byte shared-pointer elements ending at registry+0x114, filled by f_1067938c (11 callers). For each interface it calls f_1067a9f0 (0x10679cec) to look it up in a separate vector at registry+0x128, and skips the interface when it is found there. Otherwise it calls f_1067d028 (0x10679da8), and when that returns nonzero and the interface's +0x10 timeval (this+0xc4, timevalIsZero at 0x10679df0) is nonzero, it calls f_10683da0 (0x10679e54). f_10683da0 calls interface->vtable+0x18 at 0x10684060, which for the Queue interface reaches f_1067ab54 -> f_10465f74 -> f_10465e28. f_103f6a48 adds qm+8 (0x103f6b18) to the registry+0x128 vector through f_106794f0 (0x103f6b24, push_back at 0x10679570), registry = *(*(main+0x228)+4), as one of 14 such calls. In plain terms: the Queue's LastChange text is built by the shared UPnP eventing thread, which asks each registered service interface for its event body, not by the Queue actions themselves.

Established (when the Queue interface is in the eventing loop): registering a MediaPlayer (f_1040fc34, log 'MediaPlayer [%s] registered. [%zu]', at 0x1040fdd4; also f_1040fffc at 0x10410d60) calls f_103fd65c, which calls f_103f8924 (0x103fdde4). At 0x103f8b60..0x103f8bb8, f_103f8924 builds a shared pointer {qm+8, holder main+0x1940} (isel at 0x103f8b78, reference count raised) and passes it to f_104017c8, which calls f_1067938c(registry = *(*(main+0x228)+4), &pointer) at 0x10401830. This adds the Queue interface to the array that f_10679b14 walks. Shutting down a MediaPlayer (f_1040e944, log 'Request to shutdown MediaPlayer [%s]', at 0x1040ea8c) calls f_103fe5c4, which calls f_103f6a48 (0x103fe918). That adds the same interfaces to the registry+0x128 vector through f_106794f0, and the loop skips every interface in that vector. Established (what gates each send): f_1067d028 (0x10679da8) atomically reads the interface's pending byte +0x110 and returns 1 when it is set. The evented-interface base constructor f_1067aec4, which the Queue manager constructor calls at 0x1046607c, sets +0x110 to 1 (0x1067b06c) and stamps sonosClockGetTime into +0xcc, so the first LastChange goes out after registration. The shared mark-changed function f_1067c6ec (232 callers) sets +0x110 again through f_1067c46c (0x1067c4c8), and f_10683da0 clears it after a send (0x10683fdc). Established (subscription trigger): the other caller of f_1067c46c is f_1067c700 (0x1067c860), whose callers are f_1068e65c and f_1068faa4. f_1068faa4 is the UPnP SUBSCRIBE handler, which logs 'UPnP Eventing denied. 403 Forbidden' on refusal. So an accepted subscription sets the service's pending byte +0x110, and the eventing loop sends a LastChange on its next pass that finds the byte set (when that pass runs depends on the loop timer, which is not traced). In plain terms: an accepted subscription queues a LastChange for the next eventing pass.

AttachQueue.description: Attach a controller to the session's default queue. The firmware compares QueueOwnerID with the owner ID stored in the session's default queue record q=s+0x2ff98 (s=*(engine+0x580)) and, on a match, returns that queue's ID and owner context; it changes no state. Chain: wrapper f_104647b8 parses QueueOwnerID (string, cap 0x100, f_1056157c at 0x10464804), then calls qm->v[+0xc](qm, owner, &QueueID, ctxbuf, 0x400) at 0x10464844 on the queue manager passed in r5 (mr r30,r5 at 0x104647c8); qm vtable 0x10ed1bcc slot +0xc is f_10465a54, which loads the engine *(qm+0x128) and tail-branches to f_102b2da4. f_102b2da4 takes a scoped lock on engine+0x458 (guard vptr 0x10eaea90, lock at 0x102b2e48, unlock in guard dtor f_100caad8 at 0x102b2e88) and calls f_102b2cbc (0x102b2e78). f_102b2cbc initialises a stack queue-record copy (f_1014ceec at 0x102b2d00) and fills it with f_10146cc0(the session's default queue record q=s+0x2ff98 (s=*(engine+0x580)), &rec, 0) (0x102b2d18), which is memcpy(rec, q+0x5c, 0x2574). The earlier statements that the action calls v[+0x1c] on a different r4 object and uses UpdateID were wrong: r4 is the request object and AttachQueue has no UpdateID argument.

Browse.description: Lists the tracks of a queue as DIDL-Lite. The queue is exposed as ContentDirectory object 'Q:<QueueID>' in the object tree held at qm+0x12c, and Browse is a BrowseDirectChildren on that object through the same browse engine ContentDirectory uses. Chain: wrapper f_10464200 calls req->v[+0x3c](req) at 0x10464228 (result discarded; r4 is preserved with SPE evstdd/evldd at 0x10464220/0x10464238) and tail-calls qm->v[+0x28](qm, req) at 0x10464250; qm vtable 0x10ed1bcc slot +0x28 is f_10466280. f_10466280 parses QueueID, StartingIndex and RequestedCount as u32 (f_105614e0 at 0x104662cc/0x104662f0/0x10466314), faults 402 if req->v[+0x8] reports a parse failure (0x104663e0), then calls f_104661fc(qm, QueueID) (0x104663a8), which formats the object ID 'Q:%u' (0x1046623c) and calls f_103042f0(*(qm+0x12c), 'Q:<QueueID>', 'BrowseDirectChildren') (0x10466250). f_103042f0 looks the object up with f_1034a224(cd+0x168, id) (0x10304314) and returns 701 when it does not exist (li r31,0x2bd at 0x1030430c), else 0. On 0 the four outputs are registered as lazy writers (f_10560608 at 0x10466488/0x104664ac/0x104664d0/0x104664f4) over a stack context (vptr 0x10ed1bb8) holding qm, QueueID, StartingIndex and RequestedCount, and the response is committed with req->v[+0x10](req, strbuf) at 0x1046650c. Resolved (lazy browse chain): the action handler f_10466280 only checks that the object exists. f_104661fc formats 'Q:%u' (fmt 0x10e94018) and calls f_103042f0, which looks the id up with f_1034a224 -> f_10349d00 ('Q:' prefix -> container node tree+0x354, 0x10349dbc) -> f_10349640. CreateQueue.description: Requests ownership of the session's default queue for QueueOwnerID with QueueOwnerContext and a policy flag word, and returns that queue's ID. The session thread applies the f_1032e56c request (op 15) in f_10262670 (cases 0x10266488 and 0x10268564, which report ok=1 unconditionally): under the s+0x208 lock it calls f_1014d8c4(s+0x2ff98, 1, owner, ctx, flags). f_1014d8c4 empties the default queue (f_10145b98 at 0x1014d900), releases q+0x48, stores the policy word at q+0x26e4 (0x1014d930) and clears the low 3 bits of q+0x26dc. When the queue name buffer q+0x4c ('Q:%u') is nonempty it renumbers the queue (0x1014d9b8..0x1014da2c): n = strtol(q+0x4e, 10) + 1, with isel at 0x1014d9d8 turning a wrap to 0 into 1, writes 'Q:%u' (0x10e94018) to q+0x4c, copies the digits into the QueueID string q+0x5c, and resets the UpdateID q+0x70 to 0. It then copies QueueOwnerID to q+0x75 (256 bytes, 0x1014d958), sets q+0x175 to 1, copies QueueOwnerContext to q+0x186 (1024 bytes, 0x1014d970), clears the UUID at q+0x176 (sonos_uuid_clear, 0x1014d978) and, when q+0x4c is nonempty, calls f_1014d738, which bumps the UpdateID to 1 and posts the in-process queue event. If the default queue is the playing queue, f_10262670 also resets s+0x326cc and s+0x326ce and calls f_10261b38. Because the submit is synchronous (f_1032e658 waits for the consumer), f_102c3694 reads the ID afterwards: *out = strtol(s+0x2fff4, 0, 10) at 0x102c3750. In plain terms: CreateQueue empties the session's default queue, gives it a new QueueID one higher than the old one, records the owner, context and policy on it, and returns the new ID.

QueuePolicy.notes: Empty keeps the default policy flag word 0x0173c02e. Otherwise it is parsed into policy flags, and text that cannot be parsed returns 402.
resolved_findings: Resolved: post-parse handling of `QueuePolicy` = verbatim forward to impl vfunc +20 (obj r5-in, call site 0x10464ccc); the handler segment contains no compare/convert call on the parsed value, so no impl-layer rejection exists - validation is the request parse (402) plus delegate internals.

Resolved (flag mapping): an empty policy keeps the default flag word 0x0173c02e (0x102dfff4). A nonempty policy is fed to the parser built by f_10463c88/f_10464198 (f_10c3fc68 at 0x102e008c and a final flush at 0x102e009c); a parse failure or an unset parser-ok byte (sp+0x24) logs 'bad policy input' (0x102e00d4) and returns 402 (0x102e00f0). Otherwise eight parsed booleans at sp+0x1c..0x23 edit the defaults: +0x1c sets 0x1, +0x1d clears 0x2 when false, +0x1e clears 0x20 when false, +0x1f sets 0x40, +0x20 sets 0x100, +0x21 sets 0x200, +0x22 sets or clears 0x80, +0x23 sets or clears 0x10 (isel chain 0x102e0118..0x102e018c). The result is passed as r6 into f_102c3694 and from there into f_1032e56c.

Established (policy grammar): the parser object built by f_10463c88 (vptr 0x10ed1914) registers the SAX callbacks f_10464168 -> f_10463f34 (start element) and f_10463c68 -> f_10463be8 (end element) with f_10c3fcd4. Both callbacks return at once when the stop byte +0x10 is set. The constructor's defaults are +8 = 0, +9 = 1, +0xa = 1 and +0xb..+0xf = 0. f_10463f34 tracks the element depth. At depth 0 the element must be 'PlaybackPolicy' (strcmp 0x10463f6c, name 0x10ed1920), which sets +0x11. At depth 1, with +0x11 set, the child element name picks a boolean: allowShuffle -> +0x8 (0x104640ec), allowRepeat -> +0x9 (0x104640f8), cacheOnPause -> +0xa (0x104640c8), stopOnError -> +0xc (0x10464104), clearOnEnd -> +0xd (0x10464110), pauseAtEnd -> +0xe (0x10464120), repeatLastTrack -> +0xf (0x104640a0). Any other name, and any deeper element, is ignored (0x10463f80). Each value comes from the element's 'value' attribute (name 0x10f84bc8) through f_10463d2c. cacheOnPause goes through f_10463df8 instead, which also reads a 'fullTrackOnly' attribute (0x10ed1930) into +0xb (0x10463ea0). A value the boolean parser rejects sets the stop byte +0x10 (0x104640bc, 0x104640e0, 0x10464140). The boolean parser f_10c397cc lower-cases the first character and calls strncasecmp against a literal loaded through its PIC base 0x11095ccc: 'false' (0x10f0df68, 5 characters) and 'no' (0x10ecd564, 2) store 0, 'true' (0x10f0df88, 4) and 'yes' (0x10e71a70, 3) store 1 (0x10c398b4). Because only the literal's length is compared, a value that merely starts with one of these words is also accepted. A first character below 'f' is accepted only as exactly '0' or '1' with nothing after it, and stores 1 for '1' (0x10c39904..0x10c3992c). The direct-call closure of the mutation hook f_1014d738, four levels deep (239 functions, including the in-process dispatcher f_10117654), contains no call to f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700. The session consumer's mark-changed call targets AVTransport, and the subscription paths (f_1068faa4, f_1068e65c) only cover new subscribers. No data word in any non-.text section points at f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700, so these setters are reached only by direct calls. An indirect call from a Queue mutation would therefore have to land in one of their direct callers. No call to f_1067c6ec lies in the queue engine (0x10144000..0x10156000) or in the Queue manager (0x10460000..0x10468000). The session code calls it at 0x102648c4 and 0x10265a08 (AVTransport, per S01). The AVTransport implementation (0x102b0000..0x102f8000) calls it at 59 sites. 54 of them pass an object's +0x10 address, which is the AVTransport interface pattern that S01 traced at 0x103fbb78. The other 5 sites pass a saved register, and each register is also set to an object's +0x10 address: r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b7f84 (call 0x102b7fbc), r30 = r28+0x10 at 0x102bc3f0 (0x102bc484), r27 = r29+0x10 at 0x102c3548 (0x102c3588), r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b79b8 (0x102b7ab4) and r25 = r30+0x10 at 0x102e30f8 (0x102e32e8). At the last two sites the only later definitions are epilogue reloads (0x102b7a90, 0x102e3294) on paths that leave before the call (0x102b7aa0; 0x102e32b4, 0x102e32c8). This is a register-definition scan, not a full path proof. None of the 59 sites uses an object's +0x8 address, which is where the Queue interface sits in the Queue manager. Across the whole binary there are 213 calls to f_1067c6ec or f_1067c46c. 111 of them pass some object's +0x8 address, the same shape as the Queue interface at qm+8. None of those 111 calls is in a slot function of the Queue manager vtables 0x10ed1bcc or 0x10ed1c10. None of them loads the Queue manager pointer (main+0x193c) within 40 instructions before the call, or its holder (main+0x1940) earlier in the same function. This scan matches instruction patterns. It does not prove the base object of each +0x8 call, so whether a Queue mutation reaches the pending byte through some other path stays open. For a due interface the pass reads the timeval that slot +0x10 returns (the Queue's slot is the shared base function f_1067ab74, which returns this+0xc4) and tests it with timevalIsZero (0x10679df0). A nonzero timeval branches to a separate path at 0x10679ffc. [%zu]', at 0x1040fdd4; also f_1040fffc at 0x10410d60) calls f_103fd65c, which calls f_103f8924 (0x103fdde4). Established (what gates each send): f_1067d028 (0x10679da8) atomically reads the interface's pending byte +0x110 and returns 1 when it is set. Established (subscription trigger): the other caller of f_1067c46c is f_1067c700 (0x1067c860), whose callers are f_1068e65c and f_1068faa4. f_1068faa4 is the UPnP SUBSCRIBE handler, which logs 'UPnP Eventing denied. 403 Forbidden' on refusal. Residual: no call that sets the Queue interface's pending byte (qm+8+0x110) after a Queue mutation has been found. The direct-call closure of the mutation hook f_1014d738, four levels deep (239 functions, including the in-process dispatcher f_10117654), contains no call to f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700. The session consumer's mark-changed call targets AVTransport, and the subscription paths (f_1068faa4, f_1068e65c) only cover new subscribers. No data word in any non-.text section points at f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700, so these setters are reached only by direct calls. An indirect call from a Queue mutation would therefore have to land in one of their direct callers. No call to f_1067c6ec lies in the queue engine (0x10144000..0x10156000) or in the Queue manager (0x10460000..0x10468000). The session code calls it at 0x102648c4 and 0x10265a08 (AVTransport, per S01). The AVTransport implementation (0x102b0000..0x102f8000) calls it at 59 sites. 54 of them pass an object's +0x10 address, which is the AVTransport interface pattern that S01 traced at 0x103fbb78. The other 5 sites pass a saved register, and each register is also set to an object's +0x10 address: r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b7f84 (call 0x102b7fbc), r30 = r28+0x10 at 0x102bc3f0 (0x102bc484), r27 = r29+0x10 at 0x102c3548 (0x102c3588), r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b79b8 (0x102b7ab4) and r25 = r30+0x10 at 0x102e30f8 (0x102e32e8). At the last two sites the only later definitions are epilogue reloads (0x102b7a90, 0x102e3294) on paths that leave before the call (0x102b7aa0; 0x102e32b4, 0x102e32c8). This is a register-definition scan, not a full path proof. None of the 59 sites uses an object's +0x8 address, which is where the Queue interface sits in the Queue manager. Across the whole binary there are 213 calls to f_1067c6ec or f_1067c46c. 111 of them pass some object's +0x8 address, the same shape as the Queue interface at qm+8. None of those 111 calls is in a slot function of the Queue manager vtables 0x10ed1bcc or 0x10ed1c10. None of them loads the Queue manager pointer (main+0x193c) within 40 instructions before the call, or its holder (main+0x1940) earlier in the same function. This scan matches instruction patterns. It does not prove the base object of each +0x8 call, so whether a Queue mutation reaches the pending byte through some other path stays open. On timing: for each interface the eventing pass f_10679b14 ('runOnce starting') calls f_1067d028 (0x10679da8). f_1067d028 returns 1 at once when the pending byte +0x110 is set. Otherwise it walks the subscriber list (count +0xa0, list +0x1c) and checks each subscriber's byte +0x170 and times +0x18c/+0x190. When byte *r26 or sp+0x38 is set (0x10265914..0x10265928) it also bumps the counter at s+0x27f0+8 (f_103410c0) and, through the weak reference at s+0x257c, calls notifyClients on the event source s+0x2578 (f_1067c6ec -> f_1067c46c 'upnpeventing', 0x10265a08). Established (validation, f_102f7bd0 0x102f7ea0..0x102f7f08): f_10c39f14 splits the argument into tokens of up to 0x20 bytes at sp+0x349c. When job+0x1468 is zero each token is converted with strtol(token, NULL, 10) and rejected when it is negative (0x102f7f04) or greater than the inserted count u16 job+0x1478 (0x102f7ec8). In plain terms: each listed index must lie between 0 and the number of tracks added, otherwise the action returns 402, and the values themselves never reach the queue commit. The number of entries in the list does matter: the pre-commit trim f_102f7798 keeps that many existing tracks starting at CurrentTrackIndex (see side_effects).

EnqueuedURIsAndMetaData.notes: Streamed into the track-list parser, which runs the insert once per URI and metadata pair. The first failing entry's code is returned, or 1000 when the list itself cannot be parsed. Format: <URIs><URI uri="track URI"><DIDL-Lite>track metadata</DIDL-Lite></URI>...</URIs>. URIs over 1024 bytes and metadata over 4096 bytes are cut; newlines in metadata become spaces; an XML parse failure gives 1000.
resolved_findings: Resolved: post-parse handling of `EnqueuedURIsAndMetaData` = verbatim forward to impl vfunc +48 (obj r5-in, call site 0x104650f4); the handler segment contains no compare/convert call on the parsed value, so no impl-layer rejection exists - validation is the request parse (402) plus delegate internals.

Resolved (binding): bound as a streaming sink by f_105615a8 (parse site 0x10465510) feeding the f_1014ce8c parser (init at 0x102f7c40), which calls the job callback f_102f7a50 (job vtable 0x10eb2fd0 slot +8) per entry; the parser error is the u16 read at 0x102f7c8c.

Established (track-list grammar): the value is an XML document read by a SAX parser. f_1014ce8c tail-calls f_1037045c(parser+0x10, handler parser+4), which registers the callbacks with f_10c3ffa8: start element f_1037043c -> f_10370058, end element f_103706e0 -> f_10370564, character data f_1036fd7c -> f_1036fc90. Each callback returns at once when the stop byte reader+0xc is set. The start handler keeps the element depth at reader+0x1414. Until a <URIs> element is seen (strcmp at 0x103700bc, depth stored at reader+0x1418) every element is ignored. Inside <URIs>, a <URI> element (strcmp at 0x10370320) starts an entry, its depth is stored at reader+0x141c, and its attribute named uri (strcmp at 0x10370354) is copied with the bounded copy f_10906304(reader+0xd, value, 0x401) at 0x10370390, so at most 1024 bytes of the URI are kept. Inside a <URI>, a <DIDL-Lite> element (strcmp at 0x10370404) starts the metadata: it and every element, attribute and text node below it are written back out as XML text into reader+0x40e by f_1036fd9c ('<', ' ', '="', '"', '>', '</'), with namespace declarations handled in f_1036fc90 (' xmlns', ':'). f_1036fd9c stops at reader+0x140f, so metadata beyond 4096 bytes is silently cut, and it replaces each newline byte 0x0a with a space (isel at 0x1036fde0). Other elements directly inside <URI> are ignored (0x1037040c). At </URI> (strcmp at 0x1037069c) the end handler calls the handler's slot +8 with (reader+0xd URI, reader+0x40e metadata) at 0x103706cc; f_101446ac -> f_10144650 passes the pair to the owner callback and records the first nonzero result at parser+0xc (0x1014468c). A nonzero result sets the stop byte (0x103706d8), so the remaining entries are skipped. </DIDL-Lite> and </URIs> clear their depth fields (0x1037061c, 0x10370688). f_10144c50 runs the parse (f_10c3fc68 -> f_10c3f440) and records 1000 at parser+0xc when the XML fails to parse and no entry error was recorded first (0x10144cc0). In plain terms: the argument must look like <URIs><URI uri="..."><DIDL-Lite ...>...</DIDL-Lite></URI>...</URIs>. Each <URI> element is one track, its uri attribute is the track URI and its DIDL-Lite child is the track metadata.

Residual: no call that sets the Queue interface's pending byte (qm+8+0x110) after a Queue mutation has been found. The direct-call closure of the mutation hook f_1014d738, four levels deep (239 functions, including the in-process dispatcher f_10117654), contains no call to f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700. The session consumer's mark-changed call targets AVTransport, and the subscription paths (f_1068faa4, f_1068e65c) only cover new subscribers. No data word in any non-.text section points at f_1067c6ec, f_1067c46c or f_1067c700, so these setters are reached only by direct calls. An indirect call from a Queue mutation would therefore have to land in one of their direct callers. No call to f_1067c6ec lies in the queue engine (0x10144000..0x10156000) or in the Queue manager (0x10460000..0x10468000). The session code calls it at 0x102648c4 and 0x10265a08 (AVTransport, per S01). The AVTransport implementation (0x102b0000..0x102f8000) calls it at 59 sites. 54 of them pass an object's +0x10 address, which is the AVTransport interface pattern that S01 traced at 0x103fbb78. The other 5 sites pass a saved register, and each register is also set to an object's +0x10 address: r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b7f84 (call 0x102b7fbc), r30 = r28+0x10 at 0x102bc3f0 (0x102bc484), r27 = r29+0x10 at 0x102c3548 (0x102c3588), r29 = r30+0x10 at 0x102b79b8 (0x102b7ab4) and r25 = r30+0x10 at 0x102e30f8 (0x102e32e8). At the last two sites the only later definitions are epilogue reloads (0x102b7a90, 0x102e3294) on paths that leave before the call (0x102b7aa0; 0x102e32b4, 0x102e32c8). This is a register-definition scan, not a full path proof. None of the 59 sites uses an object's +0x8 address, which is where the Queue interface sits in the Queue manager. Across the whole binary there are 213 calls to f_1067c6ec or f_1067c46c. 111 of them pass some object's +0x8 address, the same shape as the Queue interface at qm+8. None of those 111 calls is in a slot function of the Queue manager vtables 0x10ed1bcc or 0x10ed1c10. None of them loads the Queue manager pointer (main+0x193c) within 40 instructions before the call, or its holder (main+0x1940) earlier in the same function. This scan matches instruction patterns. It does not prove the base object of each +0x8 call, so whether a Queue mutation reaches the pending byte through some other path stays open. On timing: for each interface the eventing pass f_10679b14 ('runOnce starting') calls f_1067d028 (0x10679da8). f_1067d028 returns 1 at once when the pending byte +0x110 is set. Otherwise it walks the subscriber list (count +0xa0, list +0x1c) and checks each subscriber's byte +0x170 and times +0x18c/+0x190. For a due interface the pass reads the timeval that slot +0x10 returns (the Queue's slot is the shared base function f_1067ab74, which returns this+0xc4) and tests it with timevalIsZero (0x10679df0). A nonzero timeval branches to a separate path at 0x10679ffc. A zero timeval goes on to send through f_10683da0 (0x10679e54) and folds the 8-byte timeval at 0x1109b010 into the next wake time with timevalMinimize (0x10679e64). 0x1109b010 is in .bss and its address is taken in many functions (f_100c71d0, f_100e323c, f_100fd44c and others), so its value is set at runtime and the wake interval is not a constant in the image. Which value it holds is not established.

In that vtable, slot +0x14 is f_10465f74, a this-8 thunk to f_10465e28 (Queue-manager slot +0x34, the only direct caller of f_10465e28 at 0x10465f78), and slot +0x18 is f_1067ab54, which tail-calls this->vtable+0x14. The upnpeventing loop f_10679b14 walks an array of 8-byte shared-pointer elements ending at registry+0x114, filled by f_1067938c (11 callers). For each interface it calls f_1067a9f0 (0x10679cec) to look it up in a separate vector at registry+0x128, and skips the interface when it is found there. Otherwise it calls f_1067d028 (0x10679da8), and when that returns nonzero and the interface's +0x10 timeval (this+0xc4, timevalIsZero at 0x10679df0) is nonzero, it calls f_10683da0 (0x10679e54). f_10683da0 calls interface->vtable+0x18 at 0x10684060, which for the Queue interface reaches f_1067ab54 -> f_10465f74 -> f_10465e28. f_103f6a48 adds qm+8 (0x103f6b18) to the registry+0x128 vector through f_106794f0 (0x103f6b24, push_back at 0x10679570), registry = *(*(main+0x228)+4), as one of 14 such calls. Established (when the Queue interface is in the eventing loop): registering a MediaPlayer (f_1040fc34, log 'MediaPlayer [%s] registered. [%zu]', at 0x1040fdd4; also f_1040fffc at 0x10410d60) calls f_103fd65c, which calls f_103f8924 (0x103fdde4). Shutting down a MediaPlayer (f_1040e944, log 'Request to shutdown MediaPlayer [%s]', at 0x1040ea8c) calls f_103fe5c4, which calls f_103f6a48 (0x103fe918). That adds the same interfaces to the registry+0x128 vector through f_106794f0, and the loop skips every interface in that vector. Established (what gates each send): f_1067d028 (0x10679da8) atomically reads the interface's pending byte +0x110 and returns 1 when it is set. The evented-interface base constructor f_1067aec4, which the Queue manager constructor calls at 0x1046607c, sets +0x110 to 1 (0x1067b06c) and stamps sonosClockGetTime into +0xcc, so the first LastChange goes out after registration. The shared mark-changed function f_1067c6ec (232 callers) sets +0x110 again through f_1067c46c (0x1067c4c8), and f_10683da0 clears it after a send (0x10683fdc). In plain terms: an event is sent when an interface's pending flag is set, and the flag is set at startup and by explicit mark-changed calls.

Established (subscription trigger): the other caller of f_1067c46c is f_1067c700 (0x1067c860), whose callers are f_1068e65c and f_1068faa4. f_1068faa4 is the UPnP SUBSCRIBE handler, which logs 'UPnP Eventing denied. 403 Forbidden' on refusal. So an accepted subscription sets the service's pending byte +0x110, and the eventing loop sends a LastChange on its next pass that finds the byte set (when that pass runs depends on the loop timer, which is not traced). In plain terms: an accepted subscription queues a LastChange for the next eventing pass.

resolved_findings: Resolved at ladder granularity: the upstream worker 0x10ed2edc emits constant set {no code constants found} (extracted from the worker body). The shared atomic-save rung semantics, decoded on the 0x10283998 exemplar: low 0x1f5-range = tmp-open/prep failure, 0x320-range = write/serialize failure, +1 = flush/sync failure, +2 = rename/commit failure. Constants outside the wire-code domain are data values (sizes/masks); rung-level attribution beyond the shared shape is bounded by the worker's own branch structure.

Established (f_104794d4 and f_1047ee0c): f_104794d4 builds the save context at sp+0x24, with the queue at ctx+0x5c (sp+0x80) and kind ctx+0x3c = 1 (0x104796d4). Before saving it walks every queue track (0x10479734..0x1047978c): f_10146a1c reads the track, and f_1014815c returns the integer 'flags' query parameter of its URI (f_10c3b830 with key 0x10eeead8, paranoid_atoi). A track counts in ctx+0x40e0 when flags & 0x1000 (f_101482c0). When byte ctx+0x59 is clear, a track whose URI host starts with 'mobile-' and ends with '.x-udn' (f_10475f00, 0x10475f6c..0x10475fa0) counts in ctx+0x40de (0x1047985c). Both counters are skipped-track counts. f_1047ee0c then returns: 501 when the '.tmp' file cannot be opened (f_103d1ca8 with 0x241, 0x1047f31c), when loading the existing file fails (f_1047ec6c: open or XML parse failure, 0x1047ecc4, 0x1047ede8) or when rename fails (0x1047f2e8); the u16 code a parse callback stored at ctx+6 (0x1047f27c, 0x1047ee00); 701 when the requested index ctx+0x40 is 0 or more and byte ctx+0x6f is clear (0x1047f288..0x1047f2a0); 802 or 501 when f_103d1b24 returns 0 (802 only with byte ctx+0x40d1 set and ctx+0x40d0 clear, 0x1047f1d0..0x1047f1f8). When every track was skipped (queue length == ctx+0x40de + ctx+0x40e0, 0x1047f2c4), it returns 804 if all were mobile tracks, 805 if all had flag 0x1000, 806 for a mix (0x1047f464..0x1047f47c). After a successful rename: 0 with no skipped tracks, 807 when only flag-0x1000 tracks were skipped (isel 0x1047f314), 803 when only mobile tracks were skipped, 808 when both were (isel 0x1047f52c). The kind-specific codes 810, 811, 812 (kinds 6, 2, 8 at 0x1047f2c8..0x1047f2e0) cannot occur for kind 1. 813, 850 and 899 are in f_10477fe8, which f_1047ee0c does not call, and 814 is a logged result of f_1047db08 that f_1047e16c discards (0x1047e6a4). In plain terms: the save succeeds with 803, 807 or 808 when some tracks could not be stored in the playlist, and fails with 804, 805 or 806 when none could.

Established (computed ctx+6 values): the stores at 0x1047df10 and 0x1047e024 both write the nonzero result of f_10476cb8 (called at 0x1047de70 and 0x1047df98, each followed by cmpwi r3,0). f_10476cb8(p) returns the pending halfword p+0x44 when it is nonzero. Otherwise, when p+0xc is not below p+0x8, it returns 899 (0x383, 0x10476cd8). When p+0xc is below p+0x8, it decrements the per-level counter at p+0x48+idx*6 (idx = p+0xc), returns 899 when that counter is already 0, and advances idx when it reaches 0 (0x10476ce4..0x10476d18). The store at 0x1047dc98 writes r30, which f_1047db08 sets only to 0 (0x1047db4c), 1 (0x1047db90) or 805 (0x325, 0x1047dbe8). In plain terms: the computed codes are a parser error carried in the context, 899 when the parser runs past the end of its nesting levels, or 805.

Established (the p+0x44 halfword): it is zeroed by f_10476720 (0x10476778). It is set only from the nonzero result of f_104783b8 (0x10478500, 0x1047de1c, 0x1047dfe4); the setter f_10476b70 has no direct callers. f_104783b8 returns 899 (0x383) when the level halfwords at p+0xc46 and p+0x46 differ, and otherwise returns any nonzero result of f_10477fe8 (0x10478428, 0x10478448). f_10477fe8 loads only 0, 1, 812 (0x32c) and 899 as result constants. In plain terms: the parser error carried in the context is 899 or 812, or a value f_10477fe8 passes up from its callees.

resolved_findings: Resolved: the impl chain is fully static. wrapper f_104643c0 parses QueueID as u32 (0x10464408), Title (cap 0x400, 0x10464430) and ObjectID (cap 0x400, 0x10464458), faults 402 on parse failure (0x104644ec) and calls qm->v[+0x24](qm, QueueID, Title, ObjectID, out, 0x400) at 0x1046449c; nonzero rc faults through req->v[+0x14] (0x104644b8), 0 emits AssignedObjectID from the out buffer (0x104644fc/0x1046451c). qm vtable 0x10ed1bcc slot +0x24 is f_10465f7c: QueueID != 0 returns 800 (0x10465f88); QueueID 0 tail-calls engine->v[+0x7c] on *(qm+0x128) (0x10465fa8), which in AVTransport impl vtable 0x10edfbb8 is f_102aa8b4. f_102aa8b4 locks engine+0x458 (0x102aa908); a nonzero QueueID would return 718 (0x102aa910, unreachable from this service); it returns 800 unless engine mode engine+0x4654 is 1 or 2 (0x102aa968..0x102aa974); it copies Title into a 0x400 buffer (f_10906304, 0x102aa988), trims it with sonosTrimWhitespace (0x102aa990), returns 402 if the result is empty (0x102aa99c) or contains CR or LF (strpbrk at 0x102aa9ac); otherwise it returns f_10146e94(s+0x2d890, title, ObjectID, out, cap, 0, 0, 0) (0x102aa9e0), s=*(engine+0x580). f_10146e94 forwards to f_104794d4 with this = *(0x11096770) (0x10146ecc). f_104794d4 logs 'pszObjectId is NULL' for a NULL ObjectID; an empty ObjectID selects index -1 (new playlist); a nonempty ObjectID must parse with sscanf 'SQ:%d' or it returns 801 (0x104798d4), and a parsed index selects replace mode (0x104796cc). Under the lock at this+0x28 (f_10988558/f_10988984) it walks tracks 1..u16 q+0x26c8 with f_10146a1c (0x10479744), saves through f_1047ee0c (0x10479794) to the 'savedqueues.rsq' store, and when that returns 0 or 803 it increments this+0xec, calls f_1047cd90(this, *(this+0xc8), count) (0x1047988c) and writes 'SQ:%d' with the saved index into the output buffer (0x104798b0) before returning the f_1047ee0c code. In plain terms: SaveAsSonosPlaylist only works with QueueID 0, needs a nonblank single-line title and transport mode 1 or 2, always saves the session queue s+0x2d890 (not a queue selected by ID), and returns the saved playlist's 'SQ:<n>' ID. A save that returns 803 still updates the counter and writes the ID internally but is reported to the client as fault 803.

Established (listener installation): at startup f_101981f0 copies the shared pointer at main+0x2900c (r28 = main+0x30000 at 0x10198214, copied by f_101a22c4 into sp+0xe4 at 0x10198fa8) and passes it to f_104791b0 at 0x10198fdc. f_104791b0 moves it into store+0xc0/+0xc4 (0x104791f4..0x1047920c, the source is nulled). The store notifies this listener through its slot +0x14 from f_104786a4 (0x104788ac), f_104791b0 (0x10479314), f_10479930 (0x10479b08, 0x10479e50), f_1047a918 (0x1047abe0), f_1047ac60 (0x1047ae7c) and f_1047cd90 (0x1047cdc4). In plain terms: a single listener object, created at startup, is told every time the saved-queue store changes.

Router f_101953c8 builds the RC record at stack+0xa4: path +0xa8, name +0xac, cap_flags 0x1000 at +0xb0 and enabled byte literal 1 at +0xb4 (0x1019558c). RestoreVolumePriorToRamp.description: Proven primary +0x70 -> f_104712ec obtains the topology snapshot through f_10759984. When snapshot/gating helpers f_1053ce34/f_1053c370 permit forwarding, it allocates at most 32 session records and enumerates remote entries from index 1. Filter f_10472690 returns true; capture f_1046b664 copies the InstanceID/Channel pair and f_1046aef4 writes those original arguments to the request. A zero endpoint-preparation result at 0x10471658 skips that recipient. Prepared requests are queued through f_106fcf50, waited via f_106fb998 against a two-second deadline and inspected at session+0x2722. The last nonzero status is retained and skips local restore. Earlier peer work is not undone. f_104726a0 manages capture pointers; session vptr 0x10ed26e0 begins with destructors, not the operation implementation. Local f_100dba7c locks +0x938 and returns 702 for nonzero InstanceID, 402 for any Channel except exact Master, and 800 when restore flag +0x3d4 is zero. With a pending restore it copies saved volume +0x3d6 into both target +0x3c8 and cached Master +0x7da before calling f_100d7f34. It marks +0x7f0 and requests f_1067c6ec(this+8)/f_100d993c regardless of the apply result. Raw 0x7fe9df9e at 0x100dbb60 is isel r31,r9,r27,30: after comparing the apply result with zero, r9=501 and r27=0 select status 501 for apply-zero, otherwise success. However, f_100d7f34 returns one on every traced normal-return path, so the late local apply-zero 501 is unreachable. The path does not clear restore flag +0x3d4, revalidate saved volume, apply a fixed-mode guard or signal condition +0x358. Repeated calls can repeat restoration. Setting both cached Master and target equal is not proof of cancel/join or completed device application; the separate f_100da4cc ramp loop observes its fields when it next runs. SOAP freshly tests status at 0x1073aaa4: nonzero faults through request+0x14 at 0x1073aab8, zero commits an empty response via request+0x0c. There are no outputs. On normal return f_100d7f34 yields one: absent/unready audio takes the explicit r28=1 path at 0x100d7fd0; ready audio converts the return from f_102a54ec using cntlzw/shift at 0x100d8110/14, and its concrete f_107f700c always returns zero at 0x107f7078 after DSP dispatch. The optional LED call does not change retained r28. Raw 0x547cd97e at 0x100d8114 is SH=27, MB=5, ME=31, making the zero-return test, not a field extraction. Consequently the local apply-zero 501 select exists but is unreachable on this traced normal-return implementation; it cannot report a DSP/hardware failure. Successful RestoreVolumePriorToRamp still does not acknowledge physical audio completion.

SetChannelMap.description: Primary slot +0x50 -> f_100db9a8 checks InstanceID before parsing the map. Nonzero selects diagnostic status 702 and skips map work, but all normal paths converge on 0x100db9f0, which explicitly returns r3=0. Zero InstanceID parses ChannelMap; parse failure selects diagnostic 402 and skips application, also returning 0. Successful parse calls f_100d96e0 -> f_100d9628 under mutex +0x938, storing all three words at +0x81c/+0x820/+0x824 before calling f_102a56c8. The worker result selects diagnostic 0/402, not SOAP status. There is no forwarding proxy, +0x7ff guard, derived-table detection, or CR0-input dispatch on this bound slot. f_1053d5b0 fills a three-word map using f_10c39fb0 comma tokenization with backslash escapes and a five-byte token buffer. Names are exact case-sensitive table indices 0..17: LF, RF, CC, SW, LR, RR, LS, RS, LTF, RTF, LTR, RTR, LW, RW, LTM, RTM, AX1, AX2. An unrecognized first token fails; later unrecognized tokens become -1. Tokenization ending or failing after at least one accepted token pads remaining words with -1 and succeeds. After three tokens it returns success without checking remaining text. Empty input or failure on the first token does not apply a map. This permissive implementation grammar is distinct from required-string request parsing. f_102a56c8 loads device+0x34 and tail-calls f_107ea854 on object+0xd0. That bridge calls f_10d93f34(trueplay manager at +0x2cb8, count 3, map), then f_107f5628 on object+0x10 if the first result is true. f_107f5628 is a literal true stub. f_10d93f34 translates every word through f_10d96d18, appends three translated IDs to a descriptor through f_10ddcee8, copies it under manager mutex +0x118 via f_10dddb60/f_10ddcfac into manager+8, calls f_10dda628(manager+0x1a8), and returns true for this in-range count regardless of that follow-up result. Words 0..9 map to 1..10, 10/11 map to 14/15, 12/13 map to 11/12; -1 and 14..17 take the unknown-channel diagnostic path and map to 0. f_10dda628 calls f_10dda4b8 and conditionally f_10dd8168/f_10dd8214 according to bytes +0x17b8/+0x17b9. None of those results reaches the SOAP status.

side_effects.description: After the ID/descriptor/interface gates, calls the selected provider action interface +0x18 at 0x106a6e0c. The manager does not itself update playback/group counters or wait for a controller completion boolean. Concrete provider effects are not yet established. For recovered Spotify ID 2, f_102132e0 updates audio-input accounting through f_104ddcf4, creates a RSpotifyPlaybackSkipToNext request, and submits/waits through f_10226c6c. An occupied request or shutdown can prevent submission without changing the SOAP success path. f_10cf5754 is the SpPlaybackSkipToNext wrapper. It calls f_10cfc65c; nonzero validation status returns directly. Validation checks the SDK context, readiness and current-playback data, permission helper f_10d077e0(4), cached playback flags and request-rate state. In its accepted branch it calls f_10d09770(0x18,0,0), then f_10d09770(0x16,0,1), but does not test their return values, and returns zero. The queue helper writes event type and arguments at the selected queue entry and advances its write index. Its full-queue path includes assertions/logging and can return -2 if control returns; that return is not checked by this caller. After zero validation status, f_10cf5754 calls f_10cfbdb0, which invokes f_10d08534 then unconditionally returns zero, ignoring the pump result. The pump checks the SDK module-manager context and recursive-call flag, processes queued records by calling each registered module callback at entry+0x10 with the event record, and clears the processing flag when drained. An empty queue invokes no module callback; a recursive pump request is ignored, and a missing context has a -1 return that this wrapper discards. Therefore zero SDK/request status does not prove the skip event was accepted by a module or produced a new audible track. Before submission f_104ddcf4 locks audio-input+0x28, calls f_104dc4a4 and copies +0x100 to +0x104. f_104dc4a4 exits without work when +0xcc/+0xd0 are both zero. Otherwise it obtains a snapshot via audio-input+0xb8 virtual +0x0c, initializes baseline +0xd4/+0xd8 and zeroes +0xdc..+0xe8 when the baseline is empty. StartTransmission.description: Adds the selected virtual line-in source coordinator through f_106a87c8/f_106a8614, returns transport settings, and requests source-manager thread state 3. side_effects.description: f_106a7450 copies a new coordinator and increments total/remote counts. Its group-added thunk f_106a6f5c calls f_106a6e60, enabling concrete transport configuration and setting +0x388. Existing identical coordinator skips adding/count increments. After settings serialization, f_106a81d4 requests thread state 3 and may wait for it; this is not a direct call to controller Play. Configuration(true) only copies the pointer value at transport+0x1b0 into embedded NodeTX+0xfc. State-3 entry resets transport counters and resyncs/ends the prior NodeTX transmission before configuring the source and passing it a shared transport reference. The accepted StartTransmission requests state 3; this NodeTX cleanup is reached on exit from that worker, not synchronously as a successful start acknowledgement. Existing f_106a95e8 cleanup reaches f_106c9e38, which invokes embedded NodeTX +0x24 with three zero arguments at 0x106c9e80 and then +0x28 at 0x106c9e94. The raw table 0x10efb75c maps these to f_10637d2c and f_10637f48 respectively. Neither result is tested before transport+0x70 and +0x79c are cleared. The reached null-argument branch of f_10637d2c sets pending packet marker NodeTX+0x534 to 0xffff and pending byte count +0x536 to zero at 0x10637f04/0x10637f08. It constructs a zero-valued three-word payload through f_106334a4, whose return is 12, and invokes NodeTX +0x14 -> f_10637a44 with control type 0xfd at 0x10637e4c. Only a zero control result calls f_10637ca8(1); a nonzero result returns without that flush. f_10637f48 similarly attempts control 0xff and only on zero tail-calls f_10637ca8(0). f_10637a44 constructs the control header through f_10633348, sends/appends its 16 bytes through f_1063777c and, only after a zero header result, processes the optional payload. f_1063777c manages pending buffer +0x134/count +0x536 and invokes f_106374cc to transmit a filled/flushed packet. f_10637ca8 returns zero when pending count is zero; otherwise it zero-pads the remainder, calls f_106374cc and resets marker/count even when that call fails. f_106374cc obtains a packet through f_10634188 or f_10637314, constructs/registers it through f_106337e4/f_10633edc, conditionally calls f_106690c0 and f_10634454, and can invoke optional NodeTX+0x53c listener slots +8/+0xc. These are packet construction/queue/listener boundaries, not a recovered receiver acknowledgement or VLI subscription bridge.

Browse.description: Browses metadata or direct children using bound cd_impl, with a preflight and a separate deferred Result executor. The top-level ObjectID resolver recognizes 0, A:, S:, Q:, R:, AI:, SQ: and FV:, not an arbitrary URI. The root enumeration and outer paging/response machinery are traced; detailed per-container enumeration and item serialization remain explicitly scoped below. R/FV node browsing is traced through its concrete SAX callbacks: Filter and SortCriteria are ignored, eligible entries retain stored order and paging does not impose an independent maximum. Q children use queue order and unsigned paging, with no independent request cap or SortCriteria validation; the native 16-bit queue length is a storage bound, not a paging clamp. SetBrowseable.description: Unsupported setter in this firmware: a present Browseable argument reaches cd_impl primary slot +0x40 = f_10302488 and always faults with 800, without changing browseability. A missing required argument faults with 402 first. The wrapper parses a signed decimal word using permissive strtol, not the boolean true/false parser. Browseable.description: Required named text converted to a signed 32-bit word, then normalized to false for zero and true for nonzero before the unsupported setter.
Browseable.format: strtol(text,NULL,10); accepts a decimal prefix, whitespace and sign
Browseable.accepted_values: Any present text reaches the setter. Empty and nonnumeric text convert to zero; trailing nonnumeric text is ignored. Only missing required input causes request-validation 402.
Browseable.range: At most first 23 text bytes are retained before NUL termination; converted word uses 32-bit strtol result. No explicit 0/1 or range check.
Browseable.special_values: 0, empty text and text such as true convert to false; nonzero numeric prefixes convert to true. All present forms still receive fault 800.
Browseable.validation: Presence/parsed flag is checked, not complete lexical validity. No conversion end-pointer or errno is inspected.

/MusicServices/Control.name: MusicServices
/MusicServices/Control.description: Music-service catalog and account-session service. Concrete catalog implementation is embedded at ctx+0x292b8; service at ctx+0x3d010 binds its primary and secondary interfaces during construction. GetSessionId can authenticate remotely; ListAvailableServices reads catalog state; UpdateAvailableServices refreshes it. Catalog file musicservices.xml is local; UpdateAvailableServices downloads it synchronously while a separate timed job can call the same worker. Native event is ServiceListVersion=device:counter, not LastChange.

availability.notes: Service object constructed at zone-player init; always registered in this build - no feature-gate found at the registration site

GetSessionId.description: Looks up a catalog service and a stored account by ServiceId and exact Username, then obtains SessionId synchronously from that provider through SMAPI, or through a configured MusicServices proxy. This is not a cached-token-only getter. ServiceId is not limited to0..255 by the wrapper.

ListAvailableServices.notes: No network/device experiment. Catalog membership and endpoint strings are runtime data, not a hardcoded provider enumeration.
ListAvailableServices.implementation_notes: Local-file SAX rewrite and synchronous callback output order traced; old-client branches are not assumed reachable on ordinary SOAP. XML SchemaVersion1 is distinct from AvailableServiceListVersion. CSV cap2048 is not an XML cap. Wrapper 0x1073a424 calls request +0x3c then +8. Branch 0x409e001c at 0x1073a46c dispatches when the validation result is nonzero. Zero returns at 0x1073a484 without local fault emission. Success tail-calls the object directly stored at service+8, slot +8; there is no extra pointer dereference through the stack. Static catalog secondary vtable 0x10e76900 contains thunk 0x100c6948, which adjusts this by -4 and branches to serializer 0x100c6314. Zone initialization proves service+8 is primary+4: r19=r29-0x6d48 at 0x1018e5bc, while r5=r29-0x6d44 at 0x1018f48c. The second delegate is therefore statically bound to this secondary interface.

UpdateAvailableServices.description: Synchronously refreshes the installed music-service catalog from the configured service-catalog endpoint, using conditional ETag download when available. Parses/rewrites a temporary local catalog, installs it by rename, advances its device:counter version and requests native ServiceListVersion notification only when a new catalog is accepted. Not an asynchronous enqueue-only action.

/QPlay/Control.description: QPlay (QQ Music) authentication service; QPlayAuth dispatch is statically bound (strcmp-matcher 0x1073a4f0, exec 0x1073a5d0) and the request/response grammar and the Seed->Code transform are fully decoded.

QPlayAuth.description: QPlay authentication handshake: dispatcher f_1073a4f0 strcmp-matches QPlayAuth -> exec f_1073a5d0. Exec calls req->v[+0x1c] to fetch arg Seed (0x10f11d64), parses via f_1056157c into a stack buffer capped at 0x80, gates on req->v[+0x08] parse-ok -> emits 402 (0x192) Invalid Args on failure, the dispatcher independently emits 401 (0x191) for any other action name. On success it calls impl->v[+0x08](impl, seedBuf, codeOut, 0x80, midOut, 0x15, didOut, 0x15) where impl = the service object's member at +0x04. IMPL PROVEN STATIC: the impl object is constructed by f_10466750 (vptr 0x10ed1d18, installed at ctor site 0x1018f280) and its v[+0x08] = f_104666b4. f_104666b4 computes Code via f_1064548c(codeOut,0x80,seed) -> f_106453bc: ZZ0062 digest-init type 2 (proven MD5 - libsonoscrypto ZZ0062 dispatches type1=SHA-256, type2=MD5, type3=SHA-1 at 0x6b60-0x6b78), ZZ0064 update with seed bytes, ZZ0064 update with a 16-byte static key at 0x10efc7ac (53 6f 6e 6f 73 03 11 19 88 09 10 17 1e 22 ff ff = "Sonos"+11 bytes, preceded by literal 62800021), ZZ0061 finish, then RserializeData(digest,0x10,out,cap) serializes the 16-byte MD5 into codeOut. So Code = serialize(MD5(Seed || key16)). MID = "62800021" - f_106453a8 returns that literal (0x10efc7a0), copied via strlcpy f_10906304 cap 0x15; DID = snprintf "%u" of singleton 0x110b8150 member +0xcc (f_106454a8 -> getInstance f_1090ad44 -> f_10908350 reads +0xcc). Outputs emitted individually via req->v[+0x24] with names Code(0x10eb95c4)/MID(0x10f11d6c)/DID(0x10f11d70), response committed via req->v[+0x0c]. Correction: an earlier note claiming f_104666b4 was a MuseDebugInfo formatter and a wrong attribution is itself wrong - the impl vtable at 0x10ed1d18 statically binds it as v[+0x08]; the nearby MuseDebugInfo literals belong to a different function.

state_transitions.description: TuneIn changes visibility settings only. Ordinary core constructs a new record; a strict matching nonzero serial/UUID/cloud-clock lineage is reused, otherwise serial is taken from NextSerialNum. Household clock advances from store version+1. Main save advances store version/LUD/counter only on success and keeps preferred serial. Cache rebuilding, selected work and pending cloud pushes have their own gates and can later change further account state.

return_behavior.description: On success returns AccountUDN and commits. Complete synchronous code domain is 0, 402, 802, 803, 809, 810. No output is committed on nonzero status. TuneIn maps any settings setter failure to 802; ordinary manifest/insertion failure is 802, a conflicting family account under single-account policy is 803, failed main account save is 809 and failed snapshot is 810. No missing-account 806 arm exists in this core.

AddOAuthAccountX.description: Adds or rebuilds an OAuth account through delegate 0x104b052c and core 0x1028a224. Nonempty token takes precedence; otherwise a nonempty authorization code is exchanged, and both empty invoke preinstalled-service credential acquisition. All eight fields must materialize and every string has an explicit length limit, even when its selected route ignores the value.

implementation.description: Concrete delegate +0x1c routes to 0x1028b2e4, 0x1028b440 or 0x1028ad54; all can reach OAuth core 0x1028a224.

evidence.notes: SystemProperties constructor installs delegate vtable 0x10ed75c4, whose slot +0x1c is 0x104b052c. Handler constructor 0x10732e94 installs 0x10f110a8 and retains this delegate at +4; handler 0x10732454 calls delegate +0x1c at 0x1073272c. Concrete store constructor 0x10285224 installs 0x10eabc6c in account manager +0x118.

Nonempty AccountToken selects 0x1028b2e4, irrespective of AuthorizationCode. Otherwise nonempty AuthorizationCode selects 0x1028b440; both empty selects 0x1028ad54 preinstalled-service acquisition. Token route passes input Key, OAuthDeviceID, Hash and min(AccountTier,65535), but an empty nickname and false guest flag. Raw 0x7d49ef5e at 0x104b0648 is isel r10,r9,r29,29 following unsigned comparison with 65535, not a shift. Code route passes OAuthDeviceID, AuthorizationCode and RedirectURI; input Key/Hash/Tier are ignored. Preinstall passes OAuthDeviceID and false guest flag; input Key/Hash/Tier/RedirectURI are ignored. Unlike AddAccountX, no exact-65031 TuneIn visibility branch exists here.
