AccountNickname.validation: Response writer emits initialized output buffers only after successful delegate return.

validation.description: Missing required materialization or any string above its explicit byte limit produces 402 before delegate dispatch. Present empty strings pass this layer. Numeric text uses unchecked decimal conversion; route/core/service validation is separate.

evidence.notes: All eight arguments register required materialization through request +0x1c/+0x20, both concrete 0x1073017c in request vtable 0x10f10f20. AccountType/AccountTier use tag 4 with 24-byte buffers. The six tag-7 strings use capacities 2050,2050,66,1026,8194,26 respectively. After validation through 0x10730414, strlen checks at 0x1073262c..0x107326d4 independently reject Token/Key >2048, OAuthDeviceID >64, AuthorizationCode >1024, RedirectURI >8192 and UserIdHashCode >24 bytes with 402. These limits apply even to fields unused by the selected delegate route. Unlike AddAccountX, each string buffer holds limit+1 payload bytes, permitting rejection rather than acceptance of overlong text. Missing materialization faults at 0x107327c8; excess length or delegate status faults at 0x10732650.

Validation checks required materialization, not numeric grammar or nonempty strings. Concrete request vtable 0x10f10f20 has both +0x1c and +0x20 bound to 0x1073017c; neither makes these descriptors optional. Tag 4 at 0x10560b50 calls strtoul(text,NULL,10), ignoring errno/end pointer; numeric copy retains at most 23 payload bytes. Leading whitespace/sign and decimal prefixes are accepted; suffixes are ignored and 32-bit overflow produces ULONG_MAX. String copy 0x10560708/0x10560a58 retains capacity minus one bytes, NUL terminates, accepts empty text, truncates without UTF-8 validation.

Nonempty AccountToken selects 0x1028b2e4, irrespective of AuthorizationCode. Otherwise nonempty AuthorizationCode selects 0x1028b440; both empty selects 0x1028ad54 preinstalled-service acquisition. Token route passes input Key, OAuthDeviceID, Hash and min(AccountTier,65535), but an empty nickname and false guest flag. Raw 0x7d49ef5e at 0x104b0648 is isel r10,r9,r29,29 following unsigned comparison with 65535, not a shift. Code route passes OAuthDeviceID, AuthorizationCode and RedirectURI; input Key/Hash/Tier are ignored. Preinstall passes OAuthDeviceID and false guest flag; input Key/Hash/Tier/RedirectURI are ignored. Unlike AddAccountX, no exact-65031 TuneIn visibility branch exists here.
Complete handler control flow, local strlen checks,402 fault and delegate call.

requirements.description: All eight fields must materialize and pass byte limits. Direct-token route needs nonempty Token/OAuthDeviceID at core; code route additionally needs successful service exchange. Both-empty route requires a supported OAuth descriptor and service credential acquisition rather than rejecting the request for missing token/code. Store read, family policy, capacity and persistence apply after credentials are obtained.

Token route calls required-manifest helper 0x10287238 and returns its nonzero 802 result, otherwise invokes OAuth core 0x1028a224 directly with supplied token/key/device/hash/tier and empty nickname. No token-exchange call precedes this core on that route. This does not prove the credentials work remotely.

Any nonzero exchange result is returned unchanged; zero invokes 0x1028a224 using returned Token/Key, Hash, nickname and Tier, not request Key/Hash/Tier. All three SOAP routes pass false guest flag to the core.

Both-empty route first obtains descriptor for type>>8: absent descriptor returns 802; unsupported descriptor or credential-type mapping other than 2 returns 401. Required-manifest helper precedes further work. Empty supplied OAuthDeviceID is generated through 0x1071e120/0x105ad854/0x10570128. Nonempty supplied ID can load an existing record through 0x1028903c/0x105714d8 and copy cached Token/Key. The needs_reauth prefix, caller false flag and cached credentials influence downstream service-household/auth acquisition. 0x104b8d0c failure becomes 1015 internally; auth/setup failures reaching 0x1028b03c map to 802. Successful 0x1072a2a4 obtains credentials/userInfo before OAuth core 0x1028a224. This is not a missing-token no-op or request-layer 402. Complete setup/metrics leaves remain to be traced.

Core requires nonempty Token and OAuthDeviceID (802 if absent), then extracts a device UID through 0x1056ffb0 (4001 on false). Length <=32 accepts arbitrary device text with UID zero. Longer text requires underscore at byte index 32; suffix at index 33 uses strtoul(base16,endptr) and must end at NUL. No errno or no-digits check: empty suffix is accepted as zero, signs/leading whitespace/0x prefixes work when consumed, trailing text/whitespace fails and overflow can produce ULONG_MAX. 0x1056fdec formats account ID X_#Svc%u-%x-Token from original requested full type and UID. Distinct device IDs can therefore select the same computed account ID. Account UDN formatter 0x1056f254 wraps this as SA_RINCON%u_%s; serial and UUID are not UDN components.

Under store mutex +0x20, reads snapshot with 0x102887e0 (810 on failure), builds fresh 0x250-byte record via 0x1056fb1c, constructs computed ID and sets supplied/returned OAuth credentials. Record offsets: ID +8, MD +0x89, PW +0x10a, NN +0x14b, OAuthDeviceID +0x18c, Hash +0x1cd, Tier +0x1e8, dynamic Token/Key +0x1ec/+0x1f0, Flags +0x1f4, household/cloud clocks +0x1fc/+0x220, UUID +0x240. Strict normalized-type/computed-ID lookup uses 0x10570e34; matching record can retain serial, UUID, cloud lineage and prior nickname. New or serial-zero records take NextSerialNum and increment it. Family policy can reject another account with 803. Nickname helpers 0x102871a8/0x102854ac can generate or update account nicknames; 0x1057082c insertion capacity failure gives 802.

Normal insertion/update and guest upgrade persist through 0x10289258; false save maps to 809 on SOAP guest-flag-false paths. Uses shared accounts.xml writer 0x102890b0 -> 0x10508988, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml under configured roots. Escaped XML contains live/deleted arrays, Token/Key and vector-clock/version/serial metadata. fflush/fsync results are ignored; failure can perform root-only fallback rewrite, so 809 does not guarantee unchanged disk contents. Successful save advances local version/LUD, caches counters and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. Writer scheduling is separately gated by 0x10285878, including store+0x14d.

Delayed push requires a nonzero registration-state result from global context +0x90 getter/receiver +0x14, a nonzero zone implementation +0xc4 predicate result, and store+0x14d push-request flag. The flag is zero at construction, set from caller boolean for replication operation 1 at 0x102877b8 (which queues 0x100ba320), and cleared after successful push at 0x102917fc. Writer schedules clock+3 only for a true predicate: 0x10289244 compares result with zero and BO13/BI30 skips on equality. Cloud request 0x10506e3c uses concrete 0x10eded98/+8; embedded HTTP client constructor 0x105cc984 installs 0x10ef4aa4, +0x60=0x105cc4dc POST. Endpoint /music-account/v0/accounts, application/xml, ten-second deadline; transport error or non-200 HTTP response returns false. 0x10505ccc emits MuseHouseholdId and optional full-sync header. Successful response is parsed by 0x10506c70 and merged by 0x10285e18; exact conflict and maintenance leaves remain under investigation.

Known local statuses are 401 unsupported preinstall descriptor, 802 manifest/setup/core-token/device/capacity failure, 803 duplicate/family conflict, 809 save failure, 810 snapshot failure and 4001 invalid device UID suffix. Code-exchange SMAPI statuses propagate rather than being mapped to this local vocabulary; complete fault/transport mapping remains below. Token-route success is not proof of remote authentication.

evidence.notes: All eight arguments register required materialization through request +0x1c/+0x20, both concrete 0x1073017c in request vtable 0x10f10f20. AccountType/AccountTier use tag 4 with 24-byte buffers. The six tag-7 strings use capacities 2050,2050,66,1026,8194,26 respectively. After validation through 0x10730414, strlen checks at 0x1073262c..0x107326d4 independently reject Token/Key >2048, OAuthDeviceID >64, AuthorizationCode >1024, RedirectURI >8192 and UserIdHashCode >24 bytes with 402. These limits apply even to fields unused by the selected delegate route. Unlike AddAccountX, each string buffer holds limit+1 payload bytes, permitting rejection rather than acceptance of overlong text. Missing materialization faults at 0x107327c8; excess length or delegate status faults at 0x10732650.

Token route calls required-manifest helper 0x10287238 and returns its nonzero 802 result, otherwise invokes OAuth core 0x1028a224 directly with supplied token/key/device/hash/tier and empty nickname. No token-exchange call precedes this core on that route. This does not prove the credentials work remotely.

Authorization-code route calls 0x10287238, then 0x10286e44 with supplied code, redirect URI and OAuthDeviceID, two 2049-byte output credential buffers and a user-info structure. Any nonzero exchange result is returned unchanged; zero invokes 0x1028a224 using returned Token/Key, Hash, nickname and Tier, not request Key/Hash/Tier. All three SOAP routes pass false guest flag to the core.

getDeviceAuthToken requires descriptor credential-type mapping 2, otherwise 1000. It builds Services/1.1 credentials through 0x1071f0c0, propagating its status, then getDeviceAuthToken with householdId and optional linkCode/callbackPath/linkDeviceId. It uses the descriptor service URL and request constructor 0x106fe328 with 20000/10000 ms timing arguments. Response descriptors parse authToken, privateKey and userInfo. userInfo +0x18 callback 0x1071a3cc forwards userIdHashCode/nickname/accountTier through 0x1071a2d0 to the supplied structure; nickname copy capacity is 65. RPC executor 0x106ff03c propagates its fault/transport result. Credential helper returns 1045 when descriptor flag 0x20000 is set, a certificate buffer and manager exist, and manager +8 returns 1; other certificate paths can fall back to deviceId/deviceProvider. Code-path status is not restricted to the local account-store vocabulary.

Both-empty route first obtains descriptor for type>>8: absent descriptor returns 802; unsupported descriptor or credential-type mapping other than 2 returns 401. Required-manifest helper precedes further work. Empty supplied OAuthDeviceID is generated through 0x1071e120/0x105ad854/0x10570128. Nonempty supplied ID can load an existing record through 0x1028903c/0x105714d8 and copy cached Token/Key. The needs_reauth prefix, caller false flag and cached credentials influence downstream service-household/auth acquisition. 0x104b8d0c failure becomes 1015 internally; auth/setup failures reaching 0x1028b03c map to 802. Successful 0x1072a2a4 obtains credentials/userInfo before OAuth core 0x1028a224. This is not a missing-token no-op or request-layer 402. Complete setup/metrics leaves remain to be traced.

Core requires nonempty Token and OAuthDeviceID (802 if absent), then extracts a device UID through 0x1056ffb0 (4001 on false). Length <=32 accepts arbitrary device text with UID zero. Longer text requires underscore at byte index 32; suffix at index 33 uses strtoul(base16,endptr) and must end at NUL. No errno or no-digits check: empty suffix is accepted as zero, signs/leading whitespace/0x prefixes work when consumed, trailing text/whitespace fails and overflow can produce ULONG_MAX. 0x1056fdec formats account ID X_#Svc%u-%x-Token from original requested full type and UID. Distinct device IDs can therefore select the same computed account ID. Account UDN formatter 0x1056f254 wraps this as SA_RINCON%u_%s; serial and UUID are not UDN components.

Under store mutex +0x20, reads snapshot with 0x102887e0 (810 on failure), builds fresh 0x250-byte record via 0x1056fb1c, constructs computed ID and sets supplied/returned OAuth credentials. Record offsets: ID +8, MD +0x89, PW +0x10a, NN +0x14b, OAuthDeviceID +0x18c, Hash +0x1cd, Tier +0x1e8, dynamic Token/Key +0x1ec/+0x1f0, Flags +0x1f4, household/cloud clocks +0x1fc/+0x220, UUID +0x240. Strict normalized-type/computed-ID lookup uses 0x10570e34; matching record can retain serial, UUID, cloud lineage and prior nickname. New or serial-zero records take NextSerialNum and increment it. Family policy can reject another account with 803. Nickname helpers 0x102871a8/0x102854ac can generate or update account nicknames; 0x1057082c insertion capacity failure gives 802.

Nonempty Hash can select an existing normalized-family account through 0x105714c8 -> 0x10571338; Hash and OAuthDeviceID comparisons are case-sensitive. With SOAP guest flag false, a normal hash match requires a matching Hash/OAuthDeviceID pair, otherwise 803. Matching guest upgrade rejects an already selected OAuthDeviceID with 803; otherwise 0x1028686c clears Flags bit 0, updates ID/device/credentials/Tier while retaining serial, and updates household clock. Guest migration can return 802 when another same-Type/different-serial record has equal Hash or computed ID. Flags bit 0 is distinct from the deleted-account array. Branch 0x1028ab24 that ignores guest-update save status requires guest flag true and is not an immediate SOAP path of this wrapper.

Normal insertion/update and guest upgrade persist through 0x10289258; false save maps to 809 on SOAP guest-flag-false paths. Uses shared accounts.xml writer 0x102890b0 -> 0x10508988, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml under configured roots. Escaped XML contains live/deleted arrays, Token/Key and vector-clock/version/serial metadata. fflush/fsync results are ignored; failure can perform root-only fallback rewrite, so 809 does not guarantee unchanged disk contents. Successful save advances local version/LUD, caches counters and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. Writer scheduling is separately gated by 0x10285878, including store+0x14d.

After zero core result, formats computed account UDN through 0x1056f254 into wrapper 144-byte buffer. AccountNickname output is copied only when core nickname input is nonempty (0x1028a4b8..0x1028a5e4), into 64-byte output buffer. Token route supplies empty nickname, leaving output empty even when stored nickname exists or is generated. Code/preinstall route can return service-provided nickname rather than a retained/generated stored nickname. Handler initializes outputs, emits AccountUDN and AccountNickname through request +0x28 and value-writer +0x10 at 0x10732754/0x10732784, then commits through +0xc at 0x107327ac. No output is emitted on nonzero status.
Direct handler success/fault control flow.

EditAccountMd.description: Replaces the metadata payload on an existing live service account. Handler 0x10732310 dispatches via concrete SystemProperties delegate vtable 0x10ed75c4 slot +0x30 to 0x104b06d0, then 0x1028b760. The worker selects by normalized AccountType and exact AccountID, stores a leading ASCII 1 plus the retained NewAccountMd bytes, stamps the household clock, and conditionally persists accounts.xml. Empty input stores MD="1" rather than removing MD. It does not change the password, nickname or OAuth credentials, authenticate a login or create an account. Returns no output arguments.

AccountType.description: Requested account type for the metadata target, compared through strict normalized-type lookup.
AccountType.format: Base-10 prefix conversion of at most 23 retained bytes.
AccountType.accepted_values: Any present text. Leading libc whitespace and optional sign are accepted; a decimal prefix is converted and suffix ignored. Empty or no-digit text converts to zero.
AccountType.range: 32-bit conversion result 0..4294967295; in-range negative magnitude wraps modulo 2^32, overflow gives ULONG_MAX.
AccountType.special_values: Lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32 on input and stored type. It does not require an enumerated service type or rewrite the stored type.
AccountType.validation: Required tag 4 materialization. Numeric lexical errors do not cause 402; an unmatched normalized type plus ID causes 806 after snapshot reading.

AccountID.description: Existing account ID whose metadata is to be edited.

NewAccountMd.description: Opaque replacement metadata payload, stored after a leading ASCII 1 format marker.
NewAccountMd.format: At most 127 retained bytes in the 128-byte request buffer.
NewAccountMd.accepted_values: Any present text; no metadata grammar, boolean parsing, whitespace trimming or remote-service validation. Overlong values truncate rather than reject.

NewAccountMd.default: None; absent input faults 402, distinct from present empty metadata.
NewAccountMd.validation: Required tag 7 materialization, then bounded payload copy with capacity 128 at record+0x8a and unconditional marker write at +0x89.

side_effects.description: Writes ASCII 1 plus NewAccountMd into a copied existing record and stamps its household vector clock. Does not clear password, Token, Key, nickname, OAuth device ID or flags. A true array update rewrites escaped Accounts XML at the configured accounts.xml path (default /opt/settings/accounts.xml), with the full marker-prefixed string as MD. Main serialization/close failure can replace the file with a root-only fallback yet return 809; ignored fflush/fsync failures do not independently cause that fault. Save success advertises replication and refreshes account caches; callback-enabled failure can still schedule delayed synchronization work.

side_effects.description: Copies the supplied password into the selected account while preserving ID, metadata, nickname, OAuth device ID, Token, Key, flags, serial and UUID. Stamps the household clock with local version+1 and submits the copied record by serial. A true array-update result rewrites the entire escaped Accounts XML, including other live and deleted entries, at the configured accounts.xml path (default /opt/settings/accounts.xml). Nonempty password is a PW attribute; empty password removes that attribute. A false update result returns success without invoking the writer. Failed main serialization/close may still replace the file with a root-only fallback and return 809; fflush/fsync failures are ignored. Successful save updates cached LUD/version, advertises selector 11 to replication and invokes account-cache refresh. A callback-enabled failed save can still queue the clock+3-second job. It does not synchronously test the new password against the music service.

evidence.notes: Loads delegate+0x26c, adds 0x118 for the embedded account store, moves NewAccountPassword from r6 to r7, passes NULL new ID/metadata/nickname/OADevID/Token/Key and zero flag masks to 0x1028b760. Returns the worker status. This is not the no-op 0x1019d288.

Under store mutex +0x20, reads live/deleted arrays through 0x102887e0. False read returns initial 810. Missing strict match returns 806 at 0x1028ba14. Copies the existing 0x250-byte record; NULL new ID reuses the current ID. Copies password to temporary record+0x10a with capacity 65. NULL nickname bypasses the duplicate-nickname ladder and sets status zero at 0x1028bb68. Other credential fields and flag masks are unchanged.

0x1056ecb4 builds the local household vector-clock value from store version+1 while preserving cloud clock. 0x105709c0 updates by existing serial. If that helper returns false, worker exits with zero and skips persistence; if true, it calls 0x10289258. Same supplied password alone does not establish no change because the vector clock is also compared.

0x1056efb0 compares serial/type/flags, account data, household/cloud clocks and UUID. Equal records return false without replacement. Guest-upgrade limit requires clearing flags bit 0, which these zero-mask copied-record edits cannot do. The token-identity guard 0x1057007c rejects new-invalid/old-valid identity; password-only editing preserves the identity fields. Helper return is not propagated as a wire fault.

Resolves accounts.xml through 0x102856a8/0x1068ab6c, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots. Reader 0x10506b0c clears destination arrays, opens the file, streams chunks into XML parser 0x10c3fc68, and returns false for failed open or invalid reader/parser state. Live and deleted record arrays are separate; these edits search live records only.

0x10289258 forwards to 0x102890b0 with callback enable=1. Writer resolves accounts.xml, serializes via 0x10508988 and returns boolean. False maps to 809 at 0x1028bb24. Success invokes store vtable +0x34 at 0x1028bb44, concretely 0x102850c4, then returns zero. No service-manifest acquisition or TuneIn R_HideTuneIn setter occurs in this delegate.

For live entries, nonempty record+0x10a is written as escaped PW attribute; an empty password omits PW. XML writer 0x105084e0 also serializes other live fields and Token/Key elements and preserves the separate deleted array. These calls do not encrypt the PW attribute.

Writes escaped Accounts XML to %s.tmp; successful main serialization/close returns rename success. 0x1054f0e8 ignores fflush/fsync results but reports fclose status. Main serialization/close failure can reopen the temporary file, write a root-only fallback with reset metadata, attempt rename with ignored result, and still return false. Temporary open or main rename failure also returns false. An 809 does not guarantee the original file survives.

Requires initialized receiver+0x3b0 and registered selector 11. return_behavior.description: Normal wire domain is success 0, or faults 402/806/809/810. 402: a required input did not materialize. 810: account snapshot reader returned false. 806: strict normalized-type/exact-ID lookup found no live record. 809: true array update followed by false account XML writer result. Zero: matched record and either false array-update result (no save), or successful save followed by refresh; no output arguments are emitted. Nickname duplicate 802 and new-ID collision branches in the shared core are bypassed because this delegate passes NULL for both updates. Callback return values do not become SOAP faults.

GetRDM.description: Reads SystemSettings R_RDM through a15-byte bounded value buffer and returns0/1 according to a strict unsigned decimal parser. Missing backend/key, failed lookup or rejected numeric text yields0 without a SOAP fault.

RDMValue.description: Boolean interpretation of the bounded, strictly parsed stored R_RDM unsigned integer, serialized as0 or1.
RDMValue.accepted_values: 0 when backend/key unavailable, lookup fails, numeric parse fails or parsed integer is0;1 for a successful parse of1..4294967295. Lookup retains at most15 payload bytes before parsing.
RDMValue.special_values: 0 conflates stored zero with unavailable/rejected data. Leading libc whitespace and optional+ are accepted; trailing whitespace, suffixes, any minus (even -0), hex notation, empty/sign-only text and overflow are rejected. Leading zeroes remain decimal.
RDMValue.default: 0; output byte initialized before backend lookup
RDMValue.validation: paranoid_atoui requires complete nonempty base10 conversion, errno0 and a32-bit unsigned result. Rejects instead of clamping. Value is first truncated to15 bytes by strlcpy, so truncation can remove a suffix or leave a shorter valid decimal prefix. If a value was found before later XML parse failure, that saved lookup result can still be used.

side_effects.description: Nonempty token/key replace stored fields; empty preserves them. Conditional persistence advances Version/LUD and refreshes account caches. Every zero worker result then updates all matching clients, even if no save occurred; cached empty strings can diverge from preserved stored strings. No new serial is allocated.

evidence.notes: Delegate vtable 0x10ed75c4 slot +0x2c = 0x104b0510. Handler passes AccountType, AccountUID, AccountToken, AccountKey in r4..r7; 0x104b0510 loads member +0x26c and tail-dispatches its vfunc +0x18, not an unresolved arbitrary implementation.

AccountType, AccountToken and AccountKey are required. AccountUID is explicitly optional: local default zero at 0x10732888 and descriptor byte +0x30 set to 1 at 0x107328b0. Numeric buffers capacity 24 use unchecked decimal strtoul after 23-byte truncation. Token/Key tag-7 buffers capacity 2050 retain 2049 bytes, but explicit strlen checks at 0x107328d8/0x107328ec reject lengths greater than 2048. Empty strings pass. Missing materialization faults at 0x10732958; length/delegate faults at 0x10732904. Zero delegate result commits without outputs at 0x107329a0.

Zone object constructs manager at 0x1018e5d4 and stores shared pointer at +0xaa48. Delegate setup 0x104b10c4 takes that shared pointer (caller 0x101982fc). Constructor installs concrete primary vtable 0x10e9af38 at 0x101b63f0 and constructs embedded store +0x118 at 0x101b6440. Slot +0x18 at 0x10e9af50 is 0x101b54d0. Secondary manager tables do not supply this primary-member call. Initialization 0x10199844/0x10199858 also stores this manager into global 0x1109791c.

Calls 0x1028bc8c on embedded store +0x118 with type/UID/token/key. Any nonzero status is returned unchanged. On zero, including the shared core false-update/no-save success, calls 0x10724740(global 0x110a9ca0,type>>8,original UID,token,key); its result is ignored. Raw 0x57c4c23e at 0x101b5574 is a rotate/mask equivalent to unsigned shift by 8, not low-byte masking.

Nonzero UID formats X_#Svc%u-%x-Token using full requested type and lowercase hexadecimal UID via 0x1056fdec. UID zero calls global 0x1109791c primary +8 = 0x101b69e0 -> 0x101b6934 under cache mutex, then 0x105710c0(cache +0x290,type,serial0,strict0). It selects the last matching unflagged OAuth-like UID-zero entry if any, otherwise lowest unsigned serial among matching unflagged normalized-type entries. Success copies its actual ID; no selection formats the UID-zero token ID. Store mutation still uses a fresh snapshot and strict lookup, so cached selection need not exist there.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Calls 0x1028b760 with selected ID, NULL new-ID/password/metadata/nickname/OAuthDeviceID, supplied Token/Key, and zero flag masks. False snapshot read returns 810; no strict normalized-type/exact-ID match returns 806. Nickname duplicate/new-ID collision branches are bypassed. Token/key pointers reach 0x1056f10c -> 0x1056ebb0: each nonempty string replaces its allocated field (+0x1ec/+0x1f0); NULL or empty does NOT clear an existing field. Other record fields remain copied unchanged except household clock Version+1.

Existing-serial update 0x105709c0 false returns zero without saving; true invokes 0x10289258. False writer maps to 809. Main success updates Version/LUD and calls store +0x34 cache refresh after unlocking. Serial/NextSerialNum/preferred serial unchanged. No remote OAuth exchange or direct account-operation publication occurs in this core.

Under global list mutex +8, traverses all clients via +0x1410, matching service ID +0x13c8 and ORIGINAL supplied UID +0x1284. Locks each client +0x1418 and calls 0x107240f4(client+0x18,token,key). No client match is silent. Original UID zero is not replaced by the UID of a cache-selected stored account, so record and client selection can differ.

Compares token at object+0x124 and key +0x925. Changed token copies up to 2048 bytes, calls token-map erase 0x107235d4 and token-map populate 0x10722c14; changed key copies up to 2048 bytes and calls 0x1071dc10(object,1), marking byte +1 valid without authentication. Unlike stored-field helper, these strlcpy calls can clear cached strings on empty input. Token-map populate can hash/cryptographically transform token through ZZ0058 and global 0x1109792c +0x14 before Base64 insertion. These cache-helper results do not become SOAP faults.

Callback-enabled 0x10289258 saves accounts.xml, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots, via 0x10508988. Main success increments Version +0xd4, updates cached LUD +0xb8 and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10efcf88/+0x14 = 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. NextSerialNum is supplied unchanged by these actions. Writer tests 0x10285878 and can queue 0x10285338 -> 0x100ba320 even on failure. Serialization/close failure may attempt root-only fallback replacement and still return failure; fflush/fsync results are ignored.

Resolves accounts.xml through 0x102856a8/0x1068ab6c, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots. Reader 0x10506b0c clears destination arrays, opens the file, streams chunks into XML parser 0x10c3fc68, and returns false for failed open or invalid reader/parser state. Live and deleted record arrays are separate; these edits search live records only.

Writes escaped Accounts XML to %s.tmp; successful main serialization/close returns rename success. 0x1054f0e8 ignores fflush/fsync results but reports fclose status. Main serialization/close failure can reopen the temporary file, write a root-only fallback with reset metadata, attempt rename with ignored result, and still return false. Temporary open or main rename failure also returns false. An 809 does not guarantee the original file survives.

Queues MusicAccountChangedEvent. Incoming r4 is unused; this event has no password/account payload. Constructs empty payload text, dispatches monitoring paths 0x10bbca78 and 0x10bbd280, and queues an event-loop callable via 0x100f14ec. Source ptr/length comes from emitter+4/+8, not the account. No-event-loop branch reports the event through 0x10bbd098 instead of scheduling that callable.

After cache/event processing, when manager+0x5134 count and +0x1a864 halfword are both zero, 0x101b7620 can rebuild the selected service-account collection through 0x101b6fdc; true schedules 0x100bbc80. Writer job 0x10285338 separately schedules 0x100ba320 at clock+3 seconds, reaching 0x101b6eac -> 0x10290df4 after its feature predicate. These downstream branches remain distinguished from the SOAP status.

Requires initialized receiver+0x3b0 and registered selector 11. Under receiver mutex +0x320, reads prior table entry with 0x10660af0 and compares using 0x10660e58: incoming version other than UINT_MAX wins if unsigned-greater, or if equal and incoming LUD sorts lexicographically smaller. Only acceptance updates table via 0x10660a7c, copies 0x254-byte LUD/version table with 0x106608d0/memcpy and appends caller flag false, then 0x10654800 queues in-process ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent. Unchanged/rejected advertisement does not enqueue. Queue failure is logged and not returned as SOAP fault. The payload is replication-version metadata, not PW, MD, Token or Key; remote transfer/delivery is not a synchronous save result.

state_transitions.description: Missing required input or oversize credential fails before delegate. Identity selection precedes fresh snapshot lookup. Store false update returns zero without save; successful save refreshes caches. Both zero cases subsequently update service-client caches using original UID. Nonzero worker status bypasses that client-cache update.

RemoveAccount.description: Removes a live stored service account selected by account type and ID, with an OAuth identity-selection branch. Exact type 65031 instead hides TuneIn through SystemSettings and does not delete an account record. Ordinary removal conditionally retains a deleted-account tombstone, rewrites accounts.xml and refreshes account caches. No output arguments; success does not establish remote credential revocation.

AccountType.description: Unsigned account type for removal, or exact TuneIn visibility selector 65031.
AccountType.format: Decimal-prefix conversion after at most 23 payload bytes.
AccountType.accepted_values: Present text, including empty: leading libc whitespace/sign and decimal prefix accepted; suffix ignored; no digits gives zero.
AccountType.range: 0..4294967295; negative in-range magnitude wraps; overflow yields ULONG_MAX.
AccountType.special_values: 65031 hides TuneIn. Ordinary lookup normalizes type but actual removal uses exact full requested type.
AccountType.validation: Tag 4 unchecked strtoul, followed by concrete delegate selection and account removal.

evidence.notes: AccountType tag 4 capacity 24 and AccountID tag 7 capacity 128 are required. Request validation 0x10732138 precedes delegate +0x20; missing input or nonzero delegate result faults at 0x10732178. Zero commits without outputs at 0x107321c0. Delegate constructor installs 0x10ed75c4, whose +0x20 is 0x104b0918; not the unrelated secondary manager vtable.

Request vtable 0x10f10f20 slots +0x1c and +0x20 both reach 0x1073017c; neither makes these descriptors optional. Validator rejects missing materialization, not malformed present text. Tag 4 uses strtoul(text,NULL,10), ignoring endpoint and errno, after truncation to 23 payload bytes. Tag 7 retains capacity minus one bytes, accepts empty text, does not trim or validate UTF-8, and truncates rather than rejecting overlength text (0x10560708/0x10560a58).

Only exact type 0xfe07 (65031) takes the TuneIn branch: secondary SystemSettings setter writes R_HideTuneIn="true", ignoring AccountID after required parsing. Setter zero maps to success; every nonzero result maps to 809, not the AddAccountX 802 mapping. Other types use member +0x26c, embedded store +0x118, worker 0x1028c5f4.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Copies selected record with 0x1056f854, then 0x10570cdc removes exact full requested Type and case-sensitive selected ID, with flag 1 allowing flagged entries. Unlike lookup, deletion does not normalize Type: a normalized alias can find a record yet fail removal with 809. False removal returns 809. True removal clears PreferredSerialNum +0xdc if it equals the copied serial, before persistence; optional removed-record output is copied and preset selection status returned. Nonzero preset status prevents save even after this local work.

resolved_findings: Concrete delegate 0x104b0918 separates exact TuneIn visibility from account removal; normalized lookup does not guarantee exact-type removal succeeds.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Locks store +0x20, calls 0x1028c3b8(type,ID,1), unlocks, and only for result zero calls store +0x34 = 0x102850c4. Core 0x1028c3b8 returns 809 on false 0x102887e0 snapshot read, unlike modification core 810; nonzero 0x102863a8 prevents save. Successful mutation calls 0x10289258 with unchanged NextSerialNum; false save maps to 809.

If first exact-type live record has Token pointer or ID longer than three bytes starting X_#, 0x105716a0 selects the OAuth-family path. Parse UID from supplied ID with 0x1056fe5c (hex conversion after first hyphen, zero if absent), format X_#Svc%u-%x-Token with requested type at 0x1056fdec, and try strict computed-ID lookup. If missing, try original ID; missing returns 806. For original-ID fallback, 0x1057007c invalid identity keeps original ID and preset zero; valid identity selects computed ID and preset 806 before continuing mutation. Raw isel words 0x7f9cdf9e/0x7f60df9e at 0x102865e8/0x102865f0 select on CR7 EQ. Non-OAuth-family selection is strict normalized-type/exact-ID lookup directly.

Copies selected record with 0x1056f854, then 0x10570cdc removes exact full requested Type and case-sensitive selected ID, with flag 1 allowing flagged entries. Unlike lookup, deletion does not normalize Type: a normalized alias can find a record yet fail removal with 809. False removal returns 809. True removal clears PreferredSerialNum +0xdc if it equals the copied serial, before persistence; optional removed-record output is copied and preset selection status returned. Nonzero preset status prevents save even after this local work.

0x10285818 requires a separate deleted record when Token pointer/nontrivial X_# ID predicate is true, or the service descriptor credential byte +0x12c equals 2. Copy is stamped with local household clock Version+1 and added by 0x1057082c (return ignored). When deleted count exceeds 7, first deleted record is removed and store household clock +0xe4 reset via 0x1056eea0 before insertion. Tombstones are not Flags bit 0. 0x1056f854 copies credentials in memory; it does not securely erase them.

Deleted XML entries carry Type, SerialNum, Flags, Deleted="1", UUID and nonempty household/cloud clocks, and UN if nonempty. Deleted flag skips NN/PW/MD/OADevID/Hash/Tier serialization. 0x105084e0 deleted loop calls this header with flag 1 then closes Account without live Token/Key child serialization. Thus serialized tombstones omit credentials, despite in-memory copying.

Callback-enabled 0x10289258 saves accounts.xml, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots, via 0x10508988. Serialization/close failure may attempt root-only fallback replacement and still return failure; fflush/fsync results are ignored.

Tombstones are not Flags bit 0. 0x1056f854 copies credentials in memory; it does not securely erase them.

Deleted XML entries carry Type, SerialNum, Flags, Deleted="1", UUID and nonempty household/cloud clocks, and UN if nonempty. Deleted flag skips NN/PW/MD/OADevID/Hash/Tier serialization. 0x105084e0 deleted loop calls this header with flag 1 then closes Account without live Token/Key child serialization. Thus serialized tombstones omit credentials, despite in-memory copying.

Callback-enabled 0x10289258 saves accounts.xml, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots, via 0x10508988. Main success increments Version +0xd4, updates cached LUD +0xb8 and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10efcf88/+0x14 = 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. NextSerialNum is supplied unchanged by these actions. Writer tests 0x10285878 and can queue 0x10285338 -> 0x100ba320 even on failure. Serialization/close failure may attempt root-only fallback replacement and still return failure; fflush/fsync results are ignored.

After successful save, store +0x2c descriptor lookup for type>>8, descriptor flags 0x00400000 and absence of a remaining account through 0x10570e34(NULL ID,strict=0) gate 0x100c6d14 -> 0x1011b310 removeManifest. Then store +0x28 = 0x10284950 publishes operation "del" with copied removed record; wrapper invokes +0x34 refresh after unlocking. Callback results do not alter selected SOAP result. Raw 0x57dcc23e at 0x1028c540 is rotate/mask equivalent to unsigned type>>8.

Resolves accounts.xml through 0x102856a8/0x1068ab6c, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots. Reader 0x10506b0c clears destination arrays, opens the file, streams chunks into XML parser 0x10c3fc68, and returns false for failed open or invalid reader/parser state. Live and deleted record arrays are separate; these edits search live records only.

Writes escaped Accounts XML to %s.tmp; successful main serialization/close returns rename success. 0x1054f0e8 ignores fflush/fsync results but reports fclose status. Main serialization/close failure can reopen the temporary file, write a root-only fallback with reset metadata, attempt rename with ignored result, and still return false. Temporary open or main rename failure also returns false. An 809 does not guarantee the original file survives.

Queues MusicAccountChangedEvent. Incoming r4 is unused; this event has no password/account payload. Constructs empty payload text, dispatches monitoring paths 0x10bbca78 and 0x10bbd280, and queues an event-loop callable via 0x100f14ec. Source ptr/length comes from emitter+4/+8, not the account. No-event-loop branch reports the event through 0x10bbd098 instead of scheduling that callable.

After cache/event processing, when manager+0x5134 count and +0x1a864 halfword are both zero, 0x101b7620 can rebuild the selected service-account collection through 0x101b6fdc; true schedules 0x100bbc80. Writer job 0x10285338 separately schedules 0x100ba320 at clock+3 seconds, reaching 0x101b6eac -> 0x10290df4 after its feature predicate. These downstream branches remain distinguished from the SOAP status.

Requires initialized receiver+0x3b0 and registered selector 11. Under receiver mutex +0x320, reads prior table entry with 0x10660af0 and compares using 0x10660e58: incoming version other than UINT_MAX wins if unsigned-greater, or if equal and incoming LUD sorts lexicographically smaller. return_behavior.description: Normal synchronous domain is 0/402/806/809, with no outputs. 402 is missing required materialization. 806 is missing account or the selected OAuth fallback error state. 809 is ordinary snapshot/removal/save failure, or any nonzero TuneIn setter result. Main success and callbacks return zero; there is no immediate remote credential-revocation result. In particular snapshot failure here is 809, not modification-core 810.

evidence.notes: AccountType tag 4 capacity 24 and AccountID tag 7 capacity 128 are required. Request vtable 0x10f10f20 slots +0x1c and +0x20 both reach 0x1073017c; neither makes these descriptors optional. Validator rejects missing materialization, not malformed present text. evidence.notes: Only AccountUDN remains required. Five credential descriptors explicitly get optional byte +0x30=1 after setup at 0x10732a44/74/aa4/ad4/b04. Unlike Refresh numeric UID, their stack buffers are NOT initialized: only NewAccountUDN output gets memset at 0x107329ec. 0x1056157c merely registers buffer pointers. Validator 0x10730414 skips copy/finalization for absent arguments and accepts +0x30 nonzero. Thus omitted optional strings remain indeterminate, yet unconditional strlen checks at 0x10732b84/b94/ba4/bb4/bc4 read them. Empty materialized strings are safe; omission is not a defined empty-string default.

Explicit maximum payload lengths are AccountUDN144, NewAccountID128, NewAccountPassword64, AccountToken2048, AccountKey2048, OAuthDeviceID64. Each tag-7 buffer is max+2, so overlength materialization retains enough to reject at max+1 instead of accepting truncation. All six strlen checks precede delegate, even for unused branch inputs. Missing required UDN faults at 0x10732c74; lengths and propagated statuses at 0x10732b48. Zero emits NewAccountUDN then commits at 0x10732c58. Unsigned strlen comparison; over-limit goes to literal402 fault path.

0x1056fc20 requires case-sensitive SA_RINCON prefix, unchecked decimal strtoul with endpoint underscore and nonzero remapped type; types1/2 map51719,13/14 map51975, arbitrary retained suffix including empty is allowed. Copies at most128 ID bytes. Bad grammar returns806. Numeric signs/whitespace and unchecked overflow follow strtoul, not a stricter UDN grammar. Raw isel 0x7c634f5e at 0x1056fc94 is conditional selection, not a shift.

Let C(t)=((t & 0x7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo2^32. Only C(type)==7 tries store +0x2c descriptor lookup(service=type>>8). If lookup succeeds, raw credential byte +0x12c <=4 and mapping [3,3,1,2,2] at 0x10eaba54 equals2 (raw byte3/4), OAuth branch is taken; every other case takes ID/password branch. Raw words 0x56e907fe and 0x56ea067e at 0x1028c178/17c are masks; 0x56e4c23e at 0x1028c2d0 is unsigned type>>8; 0x5529103a at 0x1028c2fc multiplies index by4.

ID/password branch requires both NewAccountID and NewAccountPassword nonempty, else402. Discards supplied Token/Key/OAuthDeviceID after handler checks by setting their update pointers NULL. Calls 0x1028b760 with parsed old type/ID, NewID/PW and NULL metadata/nickname, flag masks0. Stored token/key/OAuth device ID are preserved, not wholesale replaced. Present empty password is rejected here, unlike EditAccountPasswordX.

OAuth branch requires nonempty Token and OAuthDeviceID, else402. NewID/PW ignored after handler length checks; key may be empty. 0x1056ffb0 derives UID: any device string <=32 bytes gives UID0; longer requires underscore at index32 and fully consumed hexadecimal suffix, ignoring errno/no-digit conversion. Empty suffix accepted as0, trailing text rejected. Failure returns402 without modification (unlike AddOAuthAccountX core4001). Success computes X_#Svc%u-%x-Token with full parsed type and UID, supplies this as new ID, an EMPTY non-NULL password (clears PW), and supplied OAuthDeviceID/Token/Key. Nonempty token replaces stored Token; empty Key preserves stored Key through 0x1056ebb0.

Raw words 0x56e907fe and 0x56ea067e at 0x1028c178/17c are masks; 0x56e4c23e at 0x1028c2d0 is unsigned type>>8; 0x5529103a at 0x1028c2fc multiplies index by4.

ID/password branch requires both NewAccountID and NewAccountPassword nonempty, else402. Discards supplied Token/Key/OAuthDeviceID after handler checks by setting their update pointers NULL. Calls 0x1028b760 with parsed old type/ID, NewID/PW and NULL metadata/nickname, flag masks0. Stored token/key/OAuth device ID are preserved, not wholesale replaced. Present empty password is rejected here, unlike EditAccountPasswordX.

OAuth branch requires nonempty Token and OAuthDeviceID, else402. NewID/PW ignored after handler length checks; key may be empty. 0x1056ffb0 derives UID: any device string <=32 bytes gives UID0; longer requires underscore at index32 and fully consumed hexadecimal suffix, ignoring errno/no-digit conversion. Empty suffix accepted as0, trailing text rejected. Failure returns402 without modification (unlike AddOAuthAccountX core4001). Success computes X_#Svc%u-%x-Token with full parsed type and UID, supplies this as new ID, an EMPTY non-NULL password (clears PW), and supplied OAuthDeviceID/Token/Key. Nonempty token replaces stored Token; empty Key preserves stored Key through 0x1056ebb0.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Shared modify 0x1028b760 reads snapshot (false810), strict normalized-type/exact-old-ID lookup (missing806), checks changed-ID collision (another match806), copies existing serial/flags/nickname/metadata/tier/clocks/UUID, applies selected new fields and stamps household Version+1. No nickname duplicate802 branch because nickname pointerNULL. False array update returns0 without save; true update calls callback-enabled accounts writer (false809). NextSerialNum/preferred serial unchanged.

Callback-enabled 0x10289258 saves accounts.xml, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots, via 0x10508988. Main success increments Version +0xd4, updates cached LUD +0xb8 and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10efcf88/+0x14 = 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. NextSerialNum is supplied unchanged by these actions. Writer tests 0x10285878 and can queue 0x10285338 -> 0x100ba320 even on failure. Serialization/close failure may attempt root-only fallback replacement and still return failure; fflush/fsync results are ignored.

After zero modification, changed ID calls 0x104b16b4(store member+0x18,type,newID). True result calls 0x1028bdc0 -> 0x1028b760 with set-Flags mask2 (Pending report), potentially a second save/cache refresh. Nested result is ignored before constructing output. No new account-operation add/del publication in this immediate core. Remote registration/reporting leaves remain shared residuals.

Constructs a fresh temporary identity with new ID and canonical type, then 0x1056f2ac -> 0x1056f254 formats SA_RINCON%u_ID into caller capacity144. Zero after false/no-save array update still constructs new UDN and invokes outer reference updates.

Every zero core result calls member+0x278 0x1027cbf8(oldUDN,newUDN), then member+0x280 0x1037f5b8(oldUDN,newUDN), ignoring both results. First takes mutex+0x170, passes old/new strings to 0x10283998, and only on its zero return runs 0x10279c0c, updates cached LUD+0x7f10/version+0x7f2c and advertises receiver selector5. Second takes mutex+0x30, runs 0x10384490 with operation6 and old/new pointers, and on zero calls 0x1037e554("2",0). These are subsequent local reference-store paths, not part of accounts.xml atomicity; their deeper persistence/event leaves remain identified residuals.

Resolves accounts.xml through 0x102856a8/0x1068ab6c, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots. Reader 0x10506b0c clears destination arrays, opens the file, streams chunks into XML parser 0x10c3fc68, and returns false for failed open or invalid reader/parser state. Writes escaped Accounts XML to %s.tmp; successful main serialization/close returns rename success. 0x1054f0e8 ignores fflush/fsync results but reports fclose status. Queues MusicAccountChangedEvent. Incoming r4 is unused; this event has no password/account payload. After cache/event processing, when manager+0x5134 count and +0x1a864 halfword are both zero, 0x101b7620 can rebuild the selected service-account collection through 0x101b6fdc; true schedules 0x100bbc80. These downstream branches remain distinguished from the SOAP status.

Requires initialized receiver+0x3b0 and registered selector 11. Omitted optional strings leave uninitialized buffers consumed by strlen; neither deterministic SOAP status nor memory-safe completion can be promised for that path.

SetAccountNicknameX.description: Changes the stored nickname of an existing account selected by an account UDN, not a device UDN. Both arguments are required. It parses the UDN, applies normalized-type/exact-ID lookup, checks nickname conflicts, copies the supplied nickname and conditionally persists accounts.xml. It does not change credentials or test service login. No output arguments.

AccountUDN.description: Account identity in SA_RINCON<decimal type>_<ID> form, not a speaker UUID.
AccountUDN.format: Case-sensitive SA_RINCON prefix, decimal conversion, underscore and account ID.
AccountUDN.accepted_values: Any materialized text reaches the concrete UDN parser; accepted forms must meet its prefix/nonzero type/underscore checks.
AccountUDN.range: 143 retained request payload bytes; parsed ID retains at most 128 bytes.
AccountUDN.special_values: Types 1/2 map to 51719; 13/14 map to 51975. Empty ID after underscore is syntactically valid; empty UDN is not.
AccountUDN.validation: Tag 7 truncation, then 0x1056fc20 grammar. Numeric substring accepts leading whitespace/sign and unchecked overflow if its endpoint is underscore. Bad UDN or no matching live account produces 806, not 402.

evidence.notes: Both AccountUDN (tag 7, capacity 144) and AccountNickname (tag 7, capacity 64) are required, despite +0x20 request lookup. Validation at 0x10731d70 precedes delegate +0x28. Missing materialization or nonzero worker result faults at 0x10731db0; zero commits with no outputs at 0x10731df8. Delegate vtable 0x10ed75c4 slot +0x28 is 0x104b071c.

Request vtable 0x10f10f20 slots +0x1c and +0x20 both reach 0x1073017c; neither makes these descriptors optional. Validator rejects missing materialization, not malformed present text. Tag 4 uses strtoul(text,NULL,10), ignoring endpoint and errno, after truncation to 23 payload bytes. Tag 7 retains capacity minus one bytes, accepts empty text, does not trim or validate UTF-8, and truncates rather than rejecting overlength text (0x10560708/0x10560a58).

Loads member +0x26c, adds embedded store +0x118 and calls 0x1028bb74 with AccountUDN and only the nickname update pointer. New-ID/password/metadata/OADevID/Token/Key pointers and both flag masks are zero. Wrapper 0x1028bb74 parses UDN using 0x1056fc20; false returns 806 before account-store access, true calls 0x1028b760 with parsed type/ID and nickname.

Case-sensitive prefix SA_RINCON (9 bytes), then strtoul(base10,endptr). Remaps 1/2 to 0xca07 and 13/14 to 0xcb07, requires converted/remapped nonzero type and underscore at endpoint, and copies remainder to ID with capacity 129 (128 payload bytes). Empty remainder is valid. No errno/overflow/sign check: libc whitespace/sign and ULONG_MAX conversion can be accepted if followed immediately by underscore. No digit-consumption requirement independent of nonzero test. Raw 0x7c634f5e at 0x1056fc94 is isel r3,r3,r9,29, not a shift.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Request vtable 0x10f10f20 slots +0x1c and +0x20 both reach 0x1073017c; neither makes these descriptors optional. Validator rejects missing materialization, not malformed present text. Tag 4 uses strtoul(text,NULL,10), ignoring endpoint and errno, after truncation to 23 payload bytes. Tag 7 retains capacity minus one bytes, accepts empty text, does not trim or validate UTF-8, and truncates rather than rejecting overlength text (0x10560708/0x10560a58).

Loads member +0x26c, adds embedded store +0x118 and calls 0x1028bb74 with AccountUDN and only the nickname update pointer. New-ID/password/metadata/OADevID/Token/Key pointers and both flag masks are zero. Wrapper 0x1028bb74 parses UDN using 0x1056fc20; false returns 806 before account-store access, true calls 0x1028b760 with parsed type/ID and nickname.

Case-sensitive prefix SA_RINCON (9 bytes), then strtoul(base10,endptr). Remaps 1/2 to 0xca07 and 13/14 to 0xcb07, requires converted/remapped nonzero type and underscore at endpoint, and copies remainder to ID with capacity 129 (128 payload bytes). Empty remainder is valid. No errno/overflow/sign check: libc whitespace/sign and ULONG_MAX conversion can be accepted if followed immediately by underscore. No digit-consumption requirement independent of nonzero test. Raw 0x7c634f5e at 0x1056fc94 is isel r3,r3,r9,29, not a shift.

Strict lookup compares N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f)-((t & 1)^1)) modulo 2^32, then case-sensitive AccountID; empty ID matches only empty stored ID. Raw 0x548907fe retains bit 0; 0x5495066e clears 0x80, not a shift. Strict flag 1 disables fallback selection.

Under store mutex +0x20, false 0x102887e0 snapshot read returns initial 810; missing strict normalized-type/exact-ID lookup returns 806. Copies existing record, then nickname to +0x14b with capacity 65 (at most 63 supplied by SOAP). No immediate generation occurs; empty nickname clears the field. Before copying, scans other serials with exact same stored Type and Flags bit 0 clear: strcmp-equal nickname sets 802, including empty nickname. Same serial, flagged records and different full types do not conflict. Raw isel 0x7fa8ef9e at 0x1028b9f0 selects 802 on CR7 EQ, preserving previous status otherwise. Nickname copy and later status check0x1028bad0 precede table update/commit. Duplicate802 aborts before table update.

Sets copied household clock from Version+1, preserving cloud clock and serial. Zero flag masks preserve flags. Existing password, ID, metadata, OAuthDeviceID, Hash, Tier, Token and Key remain unchanged by the synchronous edit. PreferredSerialNum and NextSerialNum are unchanged. A false 0x105709c0 array update exits with zero and no save; true update invokes 0x10289258. False save maps to 809; main success unlocks and calls store +0x34 = 0x102850c4, then returns zero. No account-operation publisher, manifest acquisition, credential authentication or TuneIn visibility setter is called by this immediate delegate.

Callback-enabled 0x10289258 saves accounts.xml, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots, via 0x10508988. Main success increments Version +0xd4, updates cached LUD +0xb8 and advertises selector 11 through receiver 0x10efcf88/+0x14 = 0x10652074 with false advertisement flag. NextSerialNum is supplied unchanged by these actions. Writer tests 0x10285878 and can queue 0x10285338 -> 0x100ba320 even on failure. Serialization/close failure may attempt root-only fallback replacement and still return failure; fflush/fsync results are ignored.

Resolves accounts.xml through 0x102856a8/0x1068ab6c, default /opt/settings/accounts.xml with configured roots. Requires initialized receiver+0x3b0 and registered selector 11. BeginSoftwareUpdate.description: Submits a software-update handoff through statically bound topology worker f_107413c8. Requires UpdateURL and Flags; ExtraOptions is optional. calls.arg4: UpdateURL; r5 normalized u32 Flags; r6 optional ExtraOptions

UpdateURL.description: Required update location with a permissive four-byte http prefix gate.
UpdateURL.format: bounded text, not fully validated URI
UpdateURL.accepted_values: Any text starting case-insensitively with http
UpdateURL.range: 1024 bytes plus NUL before further percent-encoding into another 1025-byte buffer
UpdateURL.special_values: Empty faults 402; https and httpfoo both pass prefix gate. Escaping expansion may truncate without fault.
UpdateURL.validation: No complete URL/scheme/host parser in submission path.

evidence.notes: UpdateURL registration f_1056157c at 0x1073319c uses capacity 1025. Flags tag-4 registration at 0x107331c0. ExtraOptions text capacity 128 at 0x107331ec, initially empty at 0x1073317c; optional byte argument+0x30 set at 0x107331f4. Validation +8 at 0x10733208 false selects 402 at 0x1073320c and shared fault call 0x10733228. Request +0x40 at 0x10733284 supplies controller-version tuple, not implementation dispatch. Actual worker arguments r4 URL, r5 normalized Flags, r6 ExtraOptions. Nonzero worker return faults verbatim at 0x10733228; zero commits empty response at 0x107332d4. No named outputs.

Type-7 copies bounded text and NUL-terminates; excess text truncates, present empty is accepted. Type-4 Flags uses strtoul(text,NULL,10) at 0x10560b50, stores u32 at 0x10560b54, with no end-pointer/errno/range validation. Its text staging capacity is 24 including NUL. Empty/nonnumeric text becomes zero and numeric prefixes are accepted. Validator f_10730414 checks parsed byte +0x31 or optional byte +0x30 at 0x107304b4..0x107304c8; missing required URL or Flags fails, missing optional ExtraOptions retains empty buffer.

Only case-insensitive first-four-byte comparison against http, literal 0x10e77b84. Nonmatch, including empty, returns 402 and local detail Update URL is malformed. Any matching prefix (http, https, httpfoo) reaches f_1073f1c8 by tail call 0x107413c4; no full scheme/host syntax validation here. f_1073f1c8 calls f_10c3a0f4 at 0x1073f24c to encode URL into capacity 1025: alphanumeric and :/.-_ copied, other bytes encoded with %%%02x literal 0x10fb1318 (percent plus two lowercase hex digits). Output stops when another encoded/copied character will not fit. This is escaping, not invalid-character rejection; truncation does not fault.

Flags.description: Required unsigned decimal bitmask normalized using controller-version context.
Flags.format: strtoul base 10, no end-pointer or errno checks
Flags.accepted_values: Any present decimal-prefix text, including empty/nonnumeric -> 0
Flags.range: u32 result; input staging capacity 24 including NUL
Flags.special_values: Bits 0x10/0x20 always cleared. Bit 4 forced for absent/newer-than-17.5.49009 controller version. Simultaneous bits 2 and 0x40 fault 402.
Flags.validation: No numeric lexical/range rejection beyond required presence; normalized conflict check in launcher.

ExtraOptions.description: Optional comma-separated options providing system_version and updateID.
ExtraOptions.format: case-sensitive key=value tokens, backslash escaping supported
ExtraOptions.accepted_values: Any text; recognized values trimmed then validated as alphanumeric plus .-_ or +-_/ respectively
ExtraOptions.range: 127 bytes plus NUL; extracted values at most 64 bytes plus NUL
ExtraOptions.special_values: Missing/empty options or absent keys yield empty metadata. Invalid recognized value is cleared entirely without fault; unknown keys ignored.
ExtraOptions.validation: No options SOAP fault; whole-value character validation, not truncation at invalid character.

Reads customer provider topology+0x58c R_CustomerID (type 7 controller instead uses POS), local household through f_105ad854 and current software via f_1090b078. Alphanumeric validation clears invalid customer ID; household additionally permits underscore. Missing/empty/exactly 0 customer ID becomes empty. Legacy flag field Ignore=1 only if normalized Flags lacks 4 and topology+0xa36 is nonzero. Builds /var/run/upgradeinfo and opens with fopen64(w) at 0x1073f388/0x1073f638. fprintf literal 0x10f12868 writes Progress, Ignore, Report=1, SonosID, HouseholdID, CurrentVersion, SystemVersion, UpdateID, Timestamp, URL, OriginClient, Offline and SWGenDowngrade. Progress uses normalized Flags retained in r31 at 0x1073f240. At 0x1073f3b4 raw word 0x73ea0002 tests Flags&0x02 in CR0; 0x1073f3b8 loads r6=1 and bne at 0x1073f3bc (0x40820008) skips the rotate when that bit is set. Otherwise 0x1073f3c0 (0x57e6dfbc, rlwinm r6,r31,27,30,30) yields (Flags&0x40)>>5, either 0 or 2. r6 reaches __fprintf_chk at 0x1073f430 as the first variadic argument, matching Progress: [%d] at 0x10f12868. Thus normalized Flags 0x04/0x06/0x44 write Progress 0/1/2 respectively. The wrapper normalization at 0x10733294..0x10733298 sets 0x04 and clears only 0x30 for older controllers, preserving 0x02/0x40. Value 2 is reachable: the launcher rejects only the simultaneous 0x02+0x40 combination at 0x1073f1d4..0x1073f228 (402 at 0x1073f57c), not 0x40 alone. Timestamp is empty unless f_1076ba0c deadline exceeds monotonic current seconds, then decimal milliseconds. OriginClient uses f_10674040 result+0x70 then +0xe4, or unknown. Current-version read failure logs but continues. Null fopen unlinks target and returns 501 at 0x1073f71c. Negative fprintf closes and returns 501 at 0x1073f6f0; fclose status is ignored. This is a runtime handoff file, not an alarm/settings definition or availability-property save.

After file write, optionally marks Wi-Fi idle-manager client 5 active via f_106b0538, then calls coordinator topology+0xec8. Under coordinator mutex, +0x90 already set returns 806 at 0x106b2e80 without callback. Launcher explicitly maps 806 to zero at 0x1073f724, leaves handoff file and does NOT fault. New start stores +0x90=1, option bytes +0x49d/+0x49e, calls functor +0x4ac at 0x106b2f38 with pointer to coordinator+0x9c, and on callback failure resets +0x90 and returns failure. On zero callback status queues f_105e80fc via scheduler slot +8 at 0x106b2f94, returns zero without awaiting completion.

BeginSoftwareUpdate.notes: Submission only, not installation confirmation. Corrected inherited required ExtraOptions, option truncation, URL-option attribution, opaque numeric type and unbounded runtime delegate claims. No synchronous exec call; deferred work requests shutdown after handoff.

CheckForUpdate.description: Checks software update metadata through concrete topology slot +8. CachedOnly selects cached Software metadata or a fresh network discovery. The Version input is required but ignored; UpdateType is checked only on the cached branch.

calls.arg4: UpdateType; r5 CachedOnly; r6 Version (ignored); r7 output; r8 3072

UpdateType.description: Required text checked against Software only when CachedOnly is true.
UpdateType.accepted_values: CachedOnly true: Software; CachedOnly false: any present text
UpdateType.special_values: Empty is accepted by parser; cached branch faults 402, online branch ignores it.
UpdateType.validation: f_10752bf0 strcmp at 0x10752c80 is reached only for CachedOnly nonzero.

Nonzero return faults at sole call 0x107333e8; zero serializes UpdateItem at 0x10733478 and commits at 0x1073348c.

Boolean input text buffer capacity is 24. Missing required records make canonical validator f_10730414 return false, unlike permissive text conversion.

Version argument r6 is never consumed on either branch.

UpdateItem.description: Self-closing Software UpdateItem XML from cache or the fresh discovery result.
UpdateItem.format: <UpdateItem xmlns="urn:schemas-rinconnetworks-com:update-1-0" Type="Software" Version="..." UpdateURL="..." DownloadSize="..." ManifestURL="..." Swgen="..." LatestSwgen="..." ManifestRevision="..."/>
UpdateItem.accepted_values: Serialized Software metadata with nonempty Version
UpdateItem.range: 3072-byte output buffer including NUL; writer overflow is not faulted
UpdateItem.special_values: Missing/empty Version faults 801 rather than a successful empty UpdateItem. Output overflow can leave an incomplete XML prefix without changing success.
UpdateItem.validation: Worker nonzero prevents output commit; writer overflow flag is not checked.

evidence.notes: Registers required UpdateType text capacity 128 at 0x10733368, CachedOnly tag-1 boolean at 0x1073338c, Version text capacity 65 at 0x107333b4. Validation +8 at 0x107333c8 false loads 402 at 0x107333cc. Worker receives UpdateType r4, CachedOnly byte r5, Version r6, output r7 and capacity 0xc00 r8. Nonzero return faults at sole call 0x107333e8; zero serializes UpdateItem at 0x10733478 and commits at 0x1073348c.

CachedOnly zero forwards only output pointer/capacity to f_10752adc; it does not compare UpdateType. CachedOnly nonzero locks topology+0x318 and compares UpdateType case-sensitively with Software at 0x10752c80; mismatch returns 402. On match, topology+0x5f4 zero returns 801; this is the first Version byte of cached item at +0x5ec, not a feature/busy flag. Nonempty cached version serializes item and returns zero. Version argument r6 is never consumed on either branch.

Builds temporary update-item collection then calls f_10752420 with collection and zero final option. Nonzero helper return propagates. On success selects type 1 (Software) via f_10574a08; missing item or empty item Version at item+8 returns 801 at 0x10752bbc. Otherwise serializes the freshly fetched item, not cached topology+0x5ec, and returns zero. It never launches installation or uses the caller Version.

Nonempty item Version at +8 produces self-closing UpdateItem XML through f_10578490/f_105782a0. Attribute list: xmlns=urn:schemas-rinconnetworks-com:update-1-0, Type=Software, Version, UpdateURL (+0x49), DownloadSize (u32 +0x88c, decimal %u), ManifestURL (+0x44a), Swgen (u16 +4, decimal), LatestSwgen (u16 +6, decimal), ManifestRevision (+0x84b). Empty version emits nothing, but action guards reject it with 801. Writer f_10578764 initializes a 3072-byte response buffer. Raw append f_10577ea8 requires room for NUL, sets sticky overflow byte +0x14 and skips failing/subsequent fragments. No caller tests that byte or converts overflow to a SOAP fault. Attribute text uses writer slot +0x0c -> f_10577c40 -> escaping writer.

validation.description: All three inputs must be present. Text/boolean parsing is permissive. CachedOnly true additionally requires exact Software and a cached nonempty version. Online discovery ignores caller UpdateType and Version; its own returned Software record must have a nonempty Version.

Cached request needs exact Software and cached version; online request needs a constructible discovery endpoint, successful fetch, usable manifest and a Software version.

Separate system-property observer f_1073f8f8 (adjustor f_1073fd38 subtracts 0x2d8) reads R_AvailableSoftwareUpdate at 0x1073faf8/0x1073fc04, parses through f_105746bc and requires Software type at 0x1073fc30. It locks +0x318, compares old/new item and copies into cache +0x5ec at 0x1073fd0c. side_effects.description: Cached branch only locks and formats. Online branch performs HTTP discovery with redirect/header handling, parses temporary manifest state and, for changed nonempty Software metadata, attempts to save R_AvailableSoftwareUpdate. Save failure is diagnostic only. Does not download/install a firmware image, launch updater or change grouping.

events_triggered.description: No direct event-scheduler call in the action worker. A changed online result attempts a system-property update; when its observer processes changed Software metadata and topology eventing is enabled (+0x5a4), it updates cache, sets +0xe7c and calls f_1067c6ec(topology+8). Cache-only, unchanged records, save failure or disabled observer eventing do not unconditionally schedule an event. This is availability notification, not firmware-install progress.

return_behavior.description: Wrapper faults 402 for missing required records. Cached worker returns {0,402,801}; online path returns {0,800,801,899}. Zero commits UpdateItem; nonzero faults verbatim at 0x107333e8. 800 maps HTTP-open failure; 801 covers endpoint construction or absent/empty Software version; 899 covers unusable manifest. Availability-property save and XML-writer overflow do not replace successful status. No 792 path is reachable.

Looks up target under topology+0x318 in topology+0x5a8, copies endpoint via f_10762bac, then issues f_106e9814 to that endpoint with DeviceUUID equal to the target UUID and DesiredAction=Remove. The remote-player VerifyThenRemoveSystemwide branch reaches this helper at 0x10748040. Raw addis 0x3f6010e9 at 0x107476ac and addi 0x3b7bbcf8 at 0x107476b8 form 0x10e8bcf8, whose literal words 0x52656d6f/0x76650000 encode Remove followed by NUL. At 0x107476cc (0x7f65db78) r5 receives this pointer, r4 receives the target UUID at 0x107476d0, and bl at 0x107476d8 (0x4bfa213d) calls f_106e9814. The client saves r5 in r27 at 0x106e9858 (0x7cbb2b78); after selecting parameter name DesiredAction at 0x106e9934 (literal 0x10f0931c), it copies that same value to r4 at 0x106e9940 (0x7f64db78) and writes through parameter slot +0x10 at 0x106e9950. DeviceUUID is written from the saved r4 at 0x106e9918..0x106e9928. This verification request is distinct from the separately accepted TopologyMonitorProbe operation selected at 0x10747d00..0x10747d04 (literal 0x10e8bf80); it is not a TopologyMonitorProbe SOAP request. Terminates retries on 0,402,800,804,805 or after five attempts; waits to maintain roughly two-second spacing. Lookup failure reaches 0x1074779c from missing member (0x10747684 -> 0x1074774c) or failed endpoint copy (0x107476a0 -> 0x10747754), regardless of logging at 0x1074776c. It does not unconditionally select 805. At 0x1074779c topology+0x580 supplies the provider; 0x107477a0 seeds r31=805, 0x107477a8 calls f_1057d9f0, and 0x107477ac sets r9=0. Compare 0x107477b0 (raw 0x2f830000) writes CR7.EQ (BI=30); 0x107477b4 (raw 0x7fff4f9e) is isel r31,r31,r9,30, selecting 805 when that bit is set (provider helper returned zero), otherwise 0. f_1057d9f0 locks provider+0x90, reads provider+0x150 at 0x1057da20 (raw 0x807f0150), returns zero for null, otherwise calls f_105841c4 at 0x1057da30 to read byte +0x128 (0x105841c8, raw 0x88630128). Thus this is provider state, not the endpoint-lookup result; setter f_105841d4 writes that byte to 1 at 0x105841dc, so the helper is not a constant-zero stub. No runtime provider value is assumed. Cleanup preserves r31 and returns it via r3 at 0x107477ec. Caller compares helper status with 800 at 0x10748044 and 805 at 0x10748050 (raw 0x2b830325); equality branches to 0x10748074, selecting 800 at 0x10748080 (raw 0x3b200320). Helper zero instead proceeds to broadcast and local removal through 0x10748058..0x10748070. Therefore a failed lookup can permit removal rather than faulting; internal 805 is normalized to SOAP-domain 800. Elapsed time stored through caller pointer. f_106e9814 at 0x106e98b8 explicitly builds ZoneGroupTopology ReportUnresponsiveDevice SOAP with DeviceUUID/DesiredAction. f_1074791c enumerates up to 114 members through f_10744d1c, excludes target, resolves each endpoint and sends DesiredAction=Remove via the same client; increments count of attempted sends, does not forward peer errors. Its return is used for telemetry and overwritten by successful local removal.

Player removal calls installed primary slot +0x118 (entry 0x10e8b13c -> f_10128e08) at 0x10747c90 with defunct record {UUID, zero source flags, DesiredAction reason}. f_10128e08 checks discovery-origin flags, updates local designation via f_1074700c -> f_10746e74, invokes f_10750cb8, and informs AlarmClock helper f_102766c8. f_10750cb8 removes active-list entry (0x10750e0c), conditionally transitions it to vanished list, marks topology data via f_10766064 and schedules topology+8 with f_1067c6ec at 0x10750ebc; follow-on f_10741960 processes topology changes. No guaranteed playback stop or device shutdown follows from the action name. Non-player removal f_1011e11c locks +0x318, removes media-server entry from +0x11b8 via f_10765118, and only if changed calls f_10760d48 and f_1067c6ec(topology+8) at 0x1011e1b4. No action-specific registration or alarm-definition persistence.

side_effects.description: May probe a peer, broadcast Remove to other members, remove a cached media server or transition an active player into vanished state, update designation/group bookkeeping and inform AlarmClock of topology changes. Optional logging/telemetry. Self-probe, rejected and drop-as-success paths do not perform removal. No clock setting or alarm-definition save.

evidence.notes: Non-RINCON branch compares exact VerifyThenRemoveSystemwide and Remove; other DesiredAction values return 402. Remove calls f_1011e11c then returns 0. Verify first calls f_101205fc for media-server URI lookup. Lookup false calls f_1074791c then removes locally with zero return. Lookup true builds f_106fb1c4 request and calls f_106f2750; zero result returns 800 at 0x10121440, nonzero result proceeds to broadcast/local removal and returns 0. No worker status from removal is propagated.

RINCON branch recognizes exact Remove, TopologyMonitorProbe, VerifyThenRemoveSystemwide; other strings return 402. f_1075df68(topology+0x310,UUID) distinguishes local target. Remove of a remote target proceeds to local defunct handling; Remove of self returns 800 unless byte +0xed8 is nonzero, in which case it is dropped with success. Probe of a remote target returns 804 at 0x10747fac; probe of self returns 800 unless +0xed8 permits drop-as-success. Verify of self follows the same 800/drop gate. Verify of remote calls f_10747624; probe result 800 or 805 prevents removal and yields 800, otherwise calls f_1074791c then local removal. Unknown actions do not remove a device. Common exit 0x10747e30 returns r25; successful local removal unconditionally resets r25=0 (0x10747cf0 or 0x10747f74), so boolean/removal-count/peer statuses are not exposed as SOAP faults. Optional telemetry records action, probe error/result, hardware and elapsed time through f_10747820.

Looks up target under topology+0x318 in topology+0x5a8, copies endpoint via f_10762bac, then issues f_106e9814 to that endpoint with DeviceUUID equal to the target UUID and DesiredAction=Remove. The remote-player VerifyThenRemoveSystemwide branch reaches this helper at 0x10748040. Raw addis 0x3f6010e9 at 0x107476ac and addi 0x3b7bbcf8 at 0x107476b8 form 0x10e8bcf8, whose literal words 0x52656d6f/0x76650000 encode Remove followed by NUL. At 0x107476cc (0x7f65db78) r5 receives this pointer, r4 receives the target UUID at 0x107476d0, and bl at 0x107476d8 (0x4bfa213d) calls f_106e9814. The client saves r5 in r27 at 0x106e9858 (0x7cbb2b78); after selecting parameter name DesiredAction at 0x106e9934 (literal 0x10f0931c), it copies that same value to r4 at 0x106e9940 (0x7f64db78) and writes through parameter slot +0x10 at 0x106e9950. DeviceUUID is written from the saved r4 at 0x106e9918..0x106e9928. This verification request is distinct from the separately accepted TopologyMonitorProbe operation selected at 0x10747d00..0x10747d04 (literal 0x10e8bf80); it is not a TopologyMonitorProbe SOAP request. Terminates retries on 0,402,800,804,805 or after five attempts; waits to maintain roughly two-second spacing. Lookup failure reaches 0x1074779c from missing member (0x10747684 -> 0x1074774c) or failed endpoint copy (0x107476a0 -> 0x10747754), regardless of logging at 0x1074776c. It does not unconditionally select 805. At 0x1074779c topology+0x580 supplies the provider; 0x107477a0 seeds r31=805, 0x107477a8 calls f_1057d9f0, and 0x107477ac sets r9=0. Compare 0x107477b0 (raw 0x2f830000) writes CR7.EQ (BI=30); 0x107477b4 (raw 0x7fff4f9e) is isel r31,r31,r9,30, selecting 805 when that bit is set (provider helper returned zero), otherwise 0. f_1057d9f0 locks provider+0x90, reads provider+0x150 at 0x1057da20 (raw 0x807f0150), returns zero for null, otherwise calls f_105841c4 at 0x1057da30 to read byte +0x128 (0x105841c8, raw 0x88630128). Thus this is provider state, not the endpoint-lookup result; setter f_105841d4 writes that byte to 1 at 0x105841dc, so the helper is not a constant-zero stub. No runtime provider value is assumed. Cleanup preserves r31 and returns it via r3 at 0x107477ec. Caller compares helper status with 800 at 0x10748044 and 805 at 0x10748050 (raw 0x2b830325); equality branches to 0x10748074, selecting 800 at 0x10748080 (raw 0x3b200320). Helper zero instead proceeds to broadcast and local removal through 0x10748058..0x10748070. Therefore a failed lookup can permit removal rather than faulting; internal 805 is normalized to SOAP-domain 800. Elapsed time stored through caller pointer. f_106e9814 at 0x106e98b8 explicitly builds ZoneGroupTopology ReportUnresponsiveDevice SOAP with DeviceUUID/DesiredAction. f_1074791c enumerates up to 114 members through f_10744d1c, excludes target, resolves each endpoint and sends DesiredAction=Remove via the same client; increments count of attempted sends, does not forward peer errors. Its return is used for telemetry and overwritten by successful local removal.

Player removal calls installed primary slot +0x118 (entry 0x10e8b13c -> f_10128e08) at 0x10747c90 with defunct record {UUID, zero source flags, DesiredAction reason}. f_10128e08 checks discovery-origin flags, updates local designation via f_1074700c -> f_10746e74, invokes f_10750cb8, and informs AlarmClock helper f_102766c8. f_10750cb8 removes active-list entry (0x10750e0c), conditionally transitions it to vanished list, marks topology data via f_10766064 and schedules topology+8 with f_1067c6ec at 0x10750ebc; follow-on f_10741960 processes topology changes. No guaranteed playback stop or device shutdown follows from the action name. Non-player removal f_1011e11c locks +0x318, removes media-server entry from +0x11b8 via f_10765118, and only if changed calls f_10760d48 and f_1067c6ec(topology+8) at 0x1011e1b4. No action-specific registration or alarm-definition persistence.

events_triggered.description: Conditional topology-source scheduling, not unconditional notification: local media-server removal schedules only when its map changed; player defunct handling marks cached topology and schedules source +8. Rejected, probe-only and dropped requests need not emit. Peer SOAP Remove is distinct from outgoing event notification.

state_transitions.description: Remove can evict a media server or move a player from active to vanished; verification can prevent removal. Repeating a report need not find an active entry. Self-target safety gate can reject or silently drop. No alarm-running state is set by this report.
