return_behavior.description: Normal installed-worker domain {0,402,800,804}. Zero yields an empty success response, not proof of peer removal or network delivery. 402 is missing required input or unknown action for the selected target class; 800 is protected self-target or verification refusing/failing removal; 804 is player probe addressed to a nonlocal UUID. Internal 805 and arbitrary peer/probe errors are not directly propagated.

evidence.notes: Wrapper registers required DeviceUUID (0x107334e0, text capacity 1024) and DesiredAction (0x10733508, capacity 128). f_1056157c tag 7 copies bounded text and NUL-terminates; long values truncate, present empty text passes. Request +8 validation at 0x10733528 false selects 402. Worker nonzero is faulted verbatim at 0x1073359c; zero commits empty success at 0x10733580. TopologyMonitorProbe bypasses peer logging; other actions can fetch request-server +0x34 for logging before the identical worker call.

SubmitDiagnostics.description: Coordinates diagnostic ticket allocation, local/peer collection and optional controller uploads, waits for reported results and returns a numeric DiagnosticID when at least one submission succeeds. Both inputs are optional. It is not an unconditional enqueue-and-return operation.

After local/peer/controller requests, waits for progress with f_106b7f50(coordinator+0x368, 60000+1000*requested-player-count). f_106b7f50 counts pending status-0 entries via f_106b7e54 at 0x106b7f94 and waits on progress condition +0xd50 when any remain. It is a device-model capability byte, not a per-request computed predicate.

resolved_findings: Established: zp+0x5704 is a ctor-arg-derived config byte propagated into the SOAP per-request record. Still unknown: which config dimension it encodes (the +0x56fc..+0x5702 cluster suggests device/capability id fields). Next step: trace the ctor-arg source word (callers of f_1018d27c, arg slot 0xc4) to name the flag.

Named: zp+0x5704 is the device's audio-input-present capability. The producer chain: product-descriptor singleton 0x110b8150 flag word +0xd0 -> low byte +0xd3 -> booleanized by f_10908540 (returns byte!=0) -> caller f_100c1478 supplies it as the first stack arg -> zp-aa ctor f_1018d27c stores it at zp+0x5704 (0x1018dc70) -> SOAP router copies it into each request record at 0x101955b0.

Feature gated: in the UPnP service-registration builder (0x10433xxx), the same f_10908540 result at 0x10433318 selects the registration branch that emits '/AudioIn/Control' + 'urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:AudioIn:1' (target 0x10433a70). Nonzero byte -> AudioIn service exists; zero -> it is never registered. This matches the record's affected_services=[AudioIn].

Flag-word structure: +0xd0/+0xd4/+0xd8 are a 3-word capability bitfield on the MDP-populated product descriptor (product names {S43,ZP120,ZP90,BR200,S1,Sub,S3}, model codes A100/A200/A101/A102/B100/D100/C201/C100/X999/C200). Enumerated accessors: +0xd0 bit16 (andis.0x1 gate in f_109085a8 -> +0xd8 bit3), bits18/19 (f_109085fc/f_10908610), bits8-15 nonzero test (f_1090855c), bits16-31 nonzero test (f_10908578), bit16 as 0 or 1 (f_10908594: low bit of the big-endian high halfword); +0xd4 bits 2/4/13/21; +0xd8 bits 3/11/23. No accessor inspects individual bits of the low byte: it is only booleanized, so zp+0x5704 carries a unit flag.

Byte encoding resolved for S9: the model ctor f_10908f38 match-else ladder writes +0xd0=0x00008000 for ZPS9/Playbar (addis/ori constants at 0x10909184-0x10909190), so the flag word low byte +0xd3 = 0x00 and byte +0xd1 = 0x80. Two accessors partition the word: f_10908540 reads lbz +0xd3 and returns (byte != 0) - this is what zp+0x5704 caches; f_1090855c reads lwz +0xd0 and masks 0xff00 (the +0xd1/+0xd2 byte pair). Since +0xd3 = 0 on S9, the AudioIn/Control service registration gate evaluates false on Playbar - consistent with Playbar having no analog line-in jack (its only input is the TOSLink TV path, handled through the +0xd1 flag byte instead). The low byte is therefore a per-model analog-input-present byte written as a constant per product id, not a runtime bitmask.

0x1011ad40.description: f_1011ad40 creates a .tmp path and opens it using f_1054f088. That helper always uses fopen64(path,"w"); its third argument is not consumed. If full cache serialization f_10119b90 succeeds, the installer renames the temporary file while its writer is still open, updates the in-memory version/source and sid/version index, then destroys the writer. If serialization fails, it destroys the first writer, reopens the same path in write mode and attempts a fallback JSON object containing only version=current+1 and lastUpdateDevice. A successful fallback write and rename still increment the version, update the supplied-row index and return true. Thus save success need not mean that the manifests array reached disk. Fallback rename failure unlinks the candidate. Primary rename failure returns false without the same explicit unlink branch. The writer destructor f_1054f15c delegates to f_1054f0e8 when open. That routine calls fflush, fileno, fsync and fclose, ignores fflush/fsync results and returns a boolean derived only from fclose. f_1011ad40 does not test that close result. On the full serialization path rename and metadata/index updates precede destruction; on the fallback success path rename precedes destruction and metadata/index updates follow it. These are static call-order facts, not a runtime durability test.
0x1011ad40.why_external: Defines what manifest persistence success means and when a successful update can omit the manifest array.

evidence.notes: Entire save worker through 0x1011afb0; full and fallback paths.

0x10553994.description: f_10553994 packs a non-null input string into a 64-byte descriptor URL field. In order, strncasecmp tests https://www. (12 bytes, marker 1), http://www. (11, marker 2), https:// (8, marker 3) and http:// (7, marker 4). The first matching prefix is removed and replaced by its marker byte; the remaining suffix must have strlen<=62, followed by a terminator. If no prefix matches, strlen<=63 is copied as a plain string. An overlong matched suffix or plain string returns false without writing the destination; it does not try another encoding or truncate. Empty plain input is accepted. These are byte-count limits, not a complete URL syntax validator. Case-insensitive prefix matching followed by expansion through lowercase literals normalizes the prefix case while preserving the suffix.
0x10553994.why_external: Determines accepted descriptor URL lengths and whether a failed update changes stored URI bytes.

0x1023a214.description: Binder f_1023a214 installs schemaVersion at field index 1 as type 4 (fixed character buffer), target model+0, capacity 17 and flags byte 1. Binding capacities and per-field truncation flags are proven; aggregate acceptance of oversized values still needs tracing through the enclosing parser and callback checks.

0x1011c34c.description: Endpoint resolver f_1011c34c takes (view, endpointType, destination, capacity). It returns false for an invalid view, requested type zero, zero stored endpoint count or no matching row. It scans all stored endpoint rows in order and compares type exactly. If destination is null or capacity is zero, it skips URL writing but still returns true when a matching type is present, even if that row URI is empty. With output enabled it processes every matching row rather than returning at the first; later matches overwrite earlier output unless an earlier relative-join failure has already returned false. No-match/invalid exits do not clear the destination. A true result therefore establishes neither a nonempty URL nor lossless output. For a matching URI whose first byte is slash and a nonempty view base, the resolver copies the entire base with strlcpy and requires capacity>returned source length. It removes exactly one trailing slash from the copied base, then appends the endpoint URI verbatim with strlcat and again requires capacity>attempted length. This joins strings against descriptor SecureUri; it does not resolve a leading slash against just the URI origin or discard an existing base path. For example, base https://host/service and endpoint /report produce https://host/service/report/ after the final slash step. It then appends a trailing slash if the resulting nonempty output lacks one. A leading-slash endpoint with an empty base takes the direct-copy path instead. Non-leading-slash URIs are copied directly without scheme or absolute-URI validation by this resolver. The relative base-copy and endpoint-append length failures return false after possibly writing a truncated or partial destination. In contrast, the direct strlcpy return is ignored. Its output can be truncated and still reach success. The final trailing-slash strlcat result is checked only to decide whether to emit the Added trailing slash diagnostic: capacity>attempted length logs, while insufficient room still continues with success. Empty copied output skips slash insertion and also continues with success. Thus complete relative joining, direct copying and final slash insertion have different success criteria. The resolver makes no network request.
0x1011c34c.why_external: Determines selected service endpoint URL text, output truncation behavior and presence-query status.

evidence.notes: Instruction-level endpoint/view/caller trace; see music_service_manifest and svc_manifest.details.

0x10483e28.description: Shared version parser f_10483e28 takes a begin/end text span and an output structure. It requires decimal major, a literal dot and decimal minor, with an optional dot plus decimal patch. f_10483c1c first requires an ASCII digit, then clears errno and calls strtoul(base10) with an end pointer; errno 22 or 34 rejects. Leading zeroes are not rejected. Whitespace/sign prefixes are rejected by the first-byte guard. Patch is written only when present; the caller must initialize it otherwise. After the numeric components, either span end must be reached or a hyphen/pre-release and/or plus/build suffix is processed. Each suffix must start with isalnum, but subsequent bytes are copied without per-byte validation. Pre-release ends at the first plus or span end; build metadata consumes the remaining span. Each stored suffix is truncated to 32 bytes plus terminator while the cursor advances across the full suffix. Success requires cursor==span end. This is the implemented grammar, not complete enforcement of Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. Exact libc locale/overflow ABI and reads at malformed span boundaries still need verification.

0x10483cf0.description: Cloud-queue version extractor f_10483cf0 lazily compiles the literal regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$) with flags 1, parses the URI into components using f_10c3a920 and runs regexec from the path pointer. It uses the first regex match, starts the selected version span two bytes after the match start (after /v), and normally ends at the URI path end. If the final byte of the match is slash, it ends the span at that slash instead. There is no independent check that this slash is the last path separator. Consequently a matching version segment followed by more path can supply the accepted version, despite the error text saying the path must end with a version. An earlier matching version segment is chosen before a later one. No match returns 1; regex compilation failure returns 2. Candidate suffix syntax is narrower than the shared parser because the regex permits only letters in pre-release and letters/dots in build metadata.

0x1011a650.description: Manifest lookup f_1011a650 takes this, service ID and a nonnull output row. It formats service ID with %u and searches the three-entry memory cache by key length plus memcmp under mutex this+0x1f8. A hit refreshes entry+4 with the current clock word, copies the entire row from entry+0x20 through f_10118f64, unlocks and returns true. It does not compare a requested manifest version, cached row version, public SID/version index or cache entry+0 time word before returning a hit. There is no requested-version argument in this lookup. A cache miss unlocks, loads svcmanifests.json into a fresh 34-row scratch table through f_1011a5d0, finds the requested sid by exact word equality and copies it to output. Load failure or absent SID returns false. A successful file load can still update stored source/version/index even when the requested SID is absent. This lookup performs no HTTP download. The memory cache is separate from the 34-row persisted table. Constructor f_10119a2c sets its capacity to three; entries have stride0x51c and contain a time-derived word at +0, last-access word at +4, string key object at +8 and full manifest row at +0x20. f_1011be38 and the miss-fill code inside f_1011a650 replace an existing equal key if found; otherwise they choose the entry with the smallest unsigned last-access word. The comparison uses strict LT, so ties keep the earliest selected entry, initially index zero. There is no separate empty-entry priority beyond zero-valued initial timestamps. Both insertion paths stamp last access with the clock word. Lookup fill stores clock+1 at entry+0; f_1011be38 stores clock+its fourth argument there, and the download worker passes one. The inspected hit path does not consume this word as an expiration gate. Unsigned timestamp ordering has no wrap compensation in these selection loops.

0x1011a650.todo: Established: Manifest lookup f_1011a650 takes this, service ID and a nonnull output row. It formats service ID with %u and searches the three-entry memory cache by key length plus memcmp under mutex this+0x1f8. A hit refreshes entry+4 with the current clock word, copies the entire row from entry+0x20 through f_10118f64, unlocks and returns true. It does not compare a requested manifest version, cached row version, public SID/version index or cache entry+0 time word before returning a hit. There is no requested-version argument in this lookup. A cache miss unlocks, loads svcmanifests.json into a fresh 34-row scratch table through f_1011a5d0, finds the requested sid by exact word equality and copies it to output. Load failure or absent SID returns false. A successful file load can still update stored source/version/index even when the requested SID is absent. This lookup performs no HTTP download. The memory cache is separate from the 34-row persisted table. Constructor f_10119a2c sets its capacity to three; entries have stride0x51c and contain a time-derived word at +0, last-access word at +4, string key object at +8 and full manifest row at +0x20. f_1011be38 and the miss-fill code inside f_1011a650 replace an existing equal key if found; otherwise they choose the entry with the smallest unsigned last-access word. The comparison uses strict LT, so ties keep the earliest selected entry, initially index zero. There is no separate empty-entry priority beyond zero-valued initial timestamps. Both insertion paths stamp last access with the clock word. Lookup fill stores clock+1 at entry+0; f_1011be38 stores clock+its fourth argument there, and the download worker passes one. The inspected hit path does not consume this word as an expiration gate. Unsigned timestamp ordering has no wrap compensation in these selection loops. Remaining: Audit all callers, clock wrap/replacement, file/cache races, malformed/null and exception contracts.

0x1011a204.description: Manifest replication worker f_1011a204 holds the file mutex, applies revision comparator f_10660e58 to current stored source/revision and incoming source/revision supplied in r6/r7, opens the incoming path supplied in r8 and parses it into a fresh scratch row table. Failed revision acceptance, open, parse or rename returns false. After rename succeeds it copies the caller-supplied source (capacity25) and revision into object state, rebuilds the SID/version index from parsed rows, clears all three cache keys/time words, invokes observer slot+0x14 with (kind13, stored source, stored revision, zero), and returns true. It does not compare parsed file version/lastUpdateDevice to the caller-supplied source/revision before committing those supplied values. Its post-rename kind13 call has no new-version-nonzero guard, unlike the local save wrapper. The normal parser permits header-only input; no independent manifests-presence guard is added here. Sender binding, fetch transport and observer delivery remain open.

0x1011b310.description: Local deletion f_1011b310 initializes a fresh table and output revision zero, acquires the file mutex and loads the current file through f_1011a4bc. On load failure it returns false. Compactor f_101195ac removes every row whose SID equals the requested SID, copies survivors forward in order and stores the survivor count; it returns whether any match was removed. No match returns false without saving. A removal calls f_1011ad40; only a true save result leads to matching-key cache invalidation and true return. The save worker header-only fallback is shared here, so true deletion is not proof that all surviving rows were persisted. An observer kind13 call is made only when the output revision is nonzero. Loading can already change stored metadata/index before a later no-match or save-failure false result, and no rollback is performed for those earlier load effects.

resolved_findings: f_10292f78 is a boolean classifier, not a selector parser. At 0x10292f98 it calls strncasecmp@plt (0x11098068) on the input and the 16-byte prefix x-rincon-stream: at 0x10eacf20. A mismatch returns 0 at 0x10292fd4. On a match, 0x10292fa4 restores the ORIGINAL input pointer before strlen@plt (0x11098920) at 0x10292fa8. The unsigned comparison with 42 at 0x10292fb0 and isel at 0x10292fc0 return 1 for total strlen <=42, including equality, and 0 for a longer URI. No selector split, colon search or call to f_10292040 occurs in this body (0x10292f78-0x10292fe4). The BecomeGroupCoordinator worker calls this classifier at 0x102deb2c, falling back to f_10688070 at 0x102deee0 before rejecting with 402 at 0x102deeec; its separate call at 0x102deef8 rejects a false result through 0x102deb20. A prefix match alone therefore does not imply coordinator eligibility, and printf/glob literals do not enumerate a complete accepted grammar.
x-rincon-stream.grammar_detail: The classifier f_10292f78 accepts a case-insensitive 16-byte x-rincon-stream: prefix only when strlen of the whole original URI is <=42 bytes, excluding the terminating NUL. It does not validate a room-id grammar or split an optional selector. The bare prefix itself passes this predicate; a longer URI fails even if its prefix matches. The separate helper f_10292040 compares an entire incoming string against a literal table using strcmp at 0x1029207c; it is not called by this classifier. The x-rincon-stream:%s and x-rincon-stream:%s:%s literals are producer forms, while the *:*:* strings are service-description patterns, not proof of parser acceptance.

x-sonos-misc.htastream_validation: f_102931f0 zeroes optional output arguments and tail-calls f_10293014. At 0x10293058 the parser calls strncasecmp(input, x-sonos-htastream:, 18), using literal 0x10e99698. It finds the first colon after that prefix (0x10293070), requires exactly 24 bytes before it (0x10293090-0x10293094), and requires a nonempty suffix accepted by f_10292040. That helper uses case-sensitive strcmp against spdif, v-spdif, vli, chsnk and test; this is not hex decoding. Failure returns 0, success returns 1. A nonnull output buffer is filled with the 24-byte source plus NUL only when its size argument is exactly 25; a nonnull suffix output receives the pointer after the colon. SonosSeekTime.description: Sonos time-position operand produced by f_102ab830: an optional leading '-' sets a separate sign flag, then sscanf('%hhu:%hhu:%hhu') must convert exactly three decimal fields. Each %hhu applies strtoul semantics per component - leading whitespace skipped, own optional +/- sign allowed, result truncated to u8 so >255 wraps mod 256. The ':' separators match literally (no whitespace before them); trailing characters after the third field are ignored. Output is a {seconds_word, fraction_word=0} pair (printed as '%lld.%06lld') plus the sign byte; a leading '-' negates only the seconds word. Total range 0..934575 s (255:255:255); there is no upper-bound check.
SonosSeekTime.format: [-]H:M:S where each component is a scanf %hhu (u8, mod-256 wrap); exactly three required; trailing junk ignored
used_by: AVTransport.Seek (Target for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA, both indexed and stream modes)

evidence.notes: sign skip via cmplwi '-' + r3+=cr4.eq; sscanf fmt at 0x10eafc7c; secs=(h*60+m)*60+s; neg on cr4.eq; stw {secs,0} pair + sign byte

SonosSeekTime.notes: Action-specific restrictions layer on top: e.g. Seek indexed mode rejects a set sign flag unless Unit==TIME_DELTA, and treats a zero-magnitude pair as a silent no-op success. Stream mode performs no sign or zero gating.

SonosTrackOrdinal.description: Sonos track-ordinal operand: strtol(text,NULL,10) on the raw string - base 10, leading whitespace and +/- accepted, endptr NULL so trailing junk is silently ignored ('5junk' -> 5), saturates at LONG_MIN/MAX. Acceptance range is validated on the UNMASKED strtol result as (value-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned, i.e. exactly 1..65534; a separate u16 truncation (value & 0xffff) sizes the downstream record field and cannot wrap an out-of-range input into validity.
SonosTrackOrdinal.format: decimal integer, strtol base 10; accepted lexical range 1..65534

fields.meaning: Track ordinal in the metadata playlist/shuffle order. Playing producer reads metadata-history+0x28e; stopped fallback is1 if current playlist has any tracks, otherwise0; paused uses CHSRC+0x326cc. Zero is an empty/default ordinal; normal ordinals are one-based.
Stream byte offset from nodetx getLocationAtTime frame-header source offset; same value as resume-state getter0x1045fcd4. Separate from transmitter packet cursor and HLS segment sequence.
Source-state snapshot. Normal worker writes1=STOPPED,5=PLAYING,8=PAUSED. Full source-state names0..9 are given below; parser does not restrict state values.
Transmitter packet number from nodetx getLocationAtTime. If no suitable data, next packet number is last_packet+1, with last_packet=0xffffffff producing1. It is not a queue-track index.
Byte offset within the1024-byte transmitter packet; nodetx location walker produces offsets below0x400. Empty/no-data snapshot uses0. Parser does not enforce that bound.

Preserve transmitter cursor flag: restore skips nodetx reset when nonzero. Clone helper sets1 and converts source states5..9 to8; fresh snapshot initializes0. Raw parser retains the byte, with no boolean normalization.
Frame playback timestamp seconds from the nodetx frame header on the synchronized playback timeline;0 in no-data paths. Not UTC wall-clock time or track elapsed seconds.
Frame playback timestamp microseconds; pairs with field7.
Track-relative elapsed seconds derived by metadata-history0x1034071c from stored elapsed time and current playback timestamp. Invalid/negative stored elapsed values normalize to0 before capture.
Track-relative elapsed microseconds; playing history adds timestamp delta and normalizes >=1000000 to seconds.

Pending seek/start-position seconds copied from CHSRC+0x35184. Setter0x1025d04c computes absolute/relative target, clips negatives to0 and caps at known track duration. Playing snapshot clears this goal pair.
Pending seek/start-position microseconds from CHSRC+0x35188; pairs with field11.

Required group capabilities for the current stream, copied via CHSRC+0x3cc84. Restored by0x1025c30c; cleared on fresh construction and the explicit Resetting required group caps path0x10268e48. Distinct from the available group-capability mask.

Framer identifier from metadata-history+0x34c, carried with AFC. Normal domain0..17; unknown parsed values>17 become0. Source recovery specifically uses AFC/latest-context fallback for IDs7,12,16. This is not a window-duration or time field.

sonos_iv_token.description: The IV attribute of the HLS '#EXT-X-KEY' playlist tag, parsed inside the 'hlsaudio' key-extraction worker f_103c0364. Grammar: literal 'IV=' (strstr), mandatory '0x' prefix (strncmp at 0x103c0584), then a byte-wise loop sscanf'ing '%02hhX' (0x10ec6414) until ',' or NUL - exactly one conversion required per byte. sonos_hex_blob_line.description: Audio-framer context (AFC) bookmark serialization used for playback-position recovery. It is not the X-Sonos-Latency HTTP header. Canonical text is a two-digit hexadecimal presence mask followed by optional framer position and opaque context-discriminator sections. HLS gives the first section concrete semantics: bitrate, stream index, and media-segment sequence number. Channel-source and segmented-audio code carry this bookmark with a separately stored stream byte offset.

resolved_findings: Mask prefix %02X: at0x10f2c884. If bit0 set, append %08X:%08X:%016llX: (0x10f2c88c); if bit1 set, append %02X repeated8 then :%04X:%04X (0x10f2c8a0). Canonical text lengths for masks0/1/2/3 are3/38/29/64 characters. Serializer0x10803dac returns1 only if each snprintf result is positive and strictly smaller than remaining capacity; maximum canonical capacity is65 including NUL. The u64 is a scalar hex conversion, not bytewise network layout. Calls use0x41-byte buffers; the full mask3 string is exactly64 printable bytes.

0x10803f38 requires non-null text, strlen>2 and text[2]==colon. It sscanf-parses prefix with conversion count1, rejects raw prefix value>3, stores valid mask BEFORE parsing sections. Bit0 parses three conversions from text+3; bit1 parses ten conversions from text+3 when bit0 absent, otherwise from fixed text+0x26. Identity octets and u16s are truncated when stored. Each width is sscanf maximum width, not an exact lexical-length requirement; no end-of-input check exists, so trailing text and variable-width forms can be accepted. Mask0 accepts any suffix after the valid prefix. There is no58-character length check. Early null/short/colon rejection leaves destination unchanged; failed prefix conversion/out-of-range mask clears only mask; later section failure can leave a valid mask and partially updated payload. Caller should use returned boolean. Resume wrapper0x1045fbac clears mask and validity on failure but does not erase old context bytes.

Initializer0x108039cc zeroes all32 payload bytes and mask. Copy/assignment0x10803a60/0x10803b7c copy mask and all32 bytes;0x10803c98 copies payload only and leaves the destination mask untouched. Clear0x108042d4 clears mask only. Empty test0x108042b4 is mask==0. Primary presence0x10804120 raw0x546307fe is rlwinm SH0 MB31 ME31 (=mask&1), although the local decoder prints srwi; secondary presence0x10804134 is(mask>>1)&1. Setter0x1080422c ORs bit0 and writes words/u64 from r4/r5/r7/r8. Getter0x10804148 checks bit0 and non-null first/u64 output pointers, then copies (second output pointer is not separately checked). Secondary setter0x10804254/getter0x108041a4 write/read8 bytes and two u16s under bit1; neither has direct/tail callers, loadable pointer words, or lis/low references in this image. Secondary tuple is an opaque received compatibility discriminator, with no in-image node-ID/timing interpretation. Equality0x108042e8 compares masks then all32 payload bytes via0x10804300, including absent-section and non-wire bytes. Stale bytes can make cleared contexts unequal.

HLS consumer0x103b9328 logs starting at bitrate %u stream %u segment %llu after primary getter; its context delegate0x103bd4d0 tail-branches at0x103bd4e0 to setter0x1080422c and forwards arguments. HLS playlist path0x103beff4 extracts segment sequence, and0x103bd1f4 selects bitrate/stream with an index-bound check. Segmented-audio producer0x1047f850 attaches a new context to notifyFrame when its pending byte+0x15 is set, then clears the byte. Ogg fallback0x1045a2f4 and generic segmented fallback0x104833ac seed primary wordA from stream state, wordB=0 and position=0. CHSRC0x10256f3c asks frame-history0x10315f48 for the bookmark corresponding to a timestamp and wraps it with byte offset via0x1045fb18. Seven formatter callers include CHSRC recovery/flush, frame-history add/pop/flush, and packed playback-token serializer0x1032d59c. That serializer pads AFC text with spaces into its final64-byte field; paired parser0x1032d7f8 trims and passes it through0x1045fbac->0x10804114, whose branch0x1080411c is a semantic tail call to0x10803f38. No clock or latency producer supplies these fields.

Adjacent function0x1080396c independently retrieves X-Sonos-Latency by name through0x10551344 and tail-branches at0x108039a8 to paranoid_atoui. Adjacency of that header literal to AFC format strings does not bind the two formats.

ns2_setup_reauthorize.description: Netstart2 SETUP_REAUTHORIZE opcode18 carries a contactless-reauthorization flags word and optional idle-timeout cap in seconds. This format describes the byte contract and its established local consumer; message admission and state-specific reachability remain in the subsystem record.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.format: Opcode0x12, followed by tagged fields with one-byte tag and BEu16 length. Required tag2 is exactly4bytes, u32BE flags. Optional tag27(0x1b) is exactly1byte, unsigned timeout seconds. Normal serializer order is flags then optional timeout. With flags1 and timeout15 the12-byte plaintext is12 02 00 04 00 00 00 01 1b 00 01 0f; with omitted timeout it is8bytes12 02 00 04 00 00 00 01. Both fields may appear in either order on input. No text, hex encoding, checksum or embedded signature in this message body; DTLS is the enclosing transport.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.value_domains: Parser accepts every u32 flags value and timeout byte0..255. In this daemon only flags bit0 is tested, at0x1001f304 and0x1001c584; other bits are stored/logged but do not affect these consumers. Bit0 requests the contactless branch. Timeout0 or absent means no extra shortening, not immediate expiration. Nonzero cap is min(base60seconds,byte), so1..59 shorten the REAUTH_PENDING idle period and60..255 retain60seconds. Repeated admitted messages can refresh the deadline; it is an idle cap rather than a fixed duration measured from the original request.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.parser: 0x1002cdd4(buffer,length,flags_out,optional_timeout_out) uses two8-byte descriptors at0x10036304:{tag2,required1},{tag27,required0}. It requires opcode18, then uses u32 getter0x1002e0c0 for tag2 and byte getter0x1002df08 for tag27. Wrong widths invalidate the cursor. Missing required flags, duplicate known fields and wrong opcode fail. Unknown well-framed tags are skipped; tags>39 are skipped by header reader. Optional timeout outputNULL skips that field without width decoding, but supplied output enforces width1. Successful finalizer0x1002db94 zeros a supplied timeout output when its optional field never occurred, via descriptor runtime+0x10 at0x1002dc30. Flags output may already have been changed when a later field causes failure; no output rollback. As in ACK, malformed trailing bytes can terminate iteration without invalidating cursor after the required field was read, and finalizer does not require full byte consumption. It can therefore accept a valid flags field plus malformed trailing framing.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.serializer: 0x1002ccc0(buffer,capacity_inout,flags,timeout_word) initializes opcode18 and the same two descriptors, always writes tag2/u32BE through0x1002ea08, and emits tag27 through0x1002e8b8 only when the full timeout_word!=0. Byte writer truncates the emitted value to low8bits; thus timeout_word256 emits an explicit zero byte while word0 omits the field. No range check rejects larger words. It returns common finalizer success0/1; successful finalization stores actual8or12byte size through capacity_inout. Insufficient capacity invalidates the writer and returns0; it does not make a transactional unchanged-buffer guarantee. Direct branch-call census found no serializer callsite in this netstartd executable; its implementation is present but not a proven local outbound trigger.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.local_consumer: 0x1001f2d4 parses flags directly into session+0xa5c and timeout into stack byte+0x28. Parse failure returns from the message handler without rollback of already-written flags. Success clears cap session+0xa60. Reauthorization starts only if flags bit0 set, setup-context contactless budget+0x2f8!=0 (predicate0x10024078), and config callback+0x68 nonnull. It invokes that callback(cookie+0x34), ignores its return, copies nonzero timeout byte to cap, and enters REAUTH_PENDING14 through state setter0x1001c220. Otherwise it clears the entire flags word and serializes SETUP_STATUS with status8 via0x1002b470; serialization success submits through0x10026798, whose result is ignored. This response branch does not perform the REAUTH_PENDING transition. Main binds callback+0x68 to0x1000ac44, which calls mode-notification0x10008298(8,0,0), selecting local command43, and returns1 regardless of notification result. The external notification receiver remains outside this lane.
ns2_setup_reauthorize.related_consumers: REAUTH_PENDING button handler0x1001c544 examines the same bit0 and contactless-budget predicate, chooses status7or8, clears flags+0xa5c, and returns to START2 before optional followup callback. Its full callback/state effects remain subsystem work. Common reset0x1001cbac clears the stored flags. Admission allows REAUTHORIZE18 only for factory-fallback source1 in the ordinary table, and rejects it under the deactivation restriction; successful wire parsing alone does not prove that admission or state-specific processing accepted the message.
used_by: netstartd serializer0x1002ccc0 (no direct local callsite found)

ns2_setup_begin.description: SETUP_BEGIN opcode 7 supplies the requested setup method, encrypted setup seed, optional encrypted client PIN, discovery/waiting idle limits and discovery volume ramp. Wire parsing, the local START handler, preparation gates and local discovery notification are established here. Detailed chirp construction and subsequent interaction states remain separately unresolved.
ns2_setup_begin.format: One-byte opcode 7, then fields {u8 tag, BEu16 length, bytes}. Descriptor table 0x10036244 has seven {tag,required} rows: {11,1},{12,1},{14,0},{27,0},{28,0},{29,0},{30,0}. Tag 11 is exactly one byte, method 1..8; zero and 9..255 fail. Names: 1 NFC, 2 CHIRP, 3 MANUAL_PIN, 4 CLIENT_PIN, 5 CHIRP_WITH_BUTTON, 6 QR_CODE, 7 QR_CODE_WITH_BUTTON, 8 QR_CODE_WITH_REMOTE. Tag 12 is a required arbitrary-length encrypted setup envelope; framing permits length zero, but seed parsing/decryption subsequently fails. Tag 14 is an optional arbitrary-length encrypted client-PIN blob. Tags 27/28/29/30 are optional one-byte discovery timeout seconds / waiting timeout seconds / discovery starting volume / ending volume. Input tag order is unrestricted. A framing-only minimum example is 07 0b 00 01 02 0c 00 00; its empty seed prevents an actual setup transition.
ns2_setup_begin.parser_api: 0x1002ac28(buffer,length,mode_out,seed_buffer,seed_capacity_inout,pin_buffer,pin_capacity_inout,discovery_timeout_out,waiting_timeout_out,start_volume_out,end_volume_out). Runtime descriptors point tag 14 +8 to pin_capacity_inout, and each byte tag +0x10 to its output. Absent optional PIN resets its supplied length to zero while leaving buffer bytes untouched; absent optional byte fields write zero. Required seed copies raw bytes through 0x1002e2c8, requiring actual length <= caller capacity and updating capacity_inout to actual length. It adds no NUL terminator. Optional PIN is decoded only when pin_capacity_inout is nonnull and its current capacity is nonzero; otherwise it is skipped without copying or width restrictions. Byte fields with null output pointers are likewise skipped without checking their one-byte width. The actual daemon supplies all four byte outputs, seed capacity 512 and, when enabled, PIN capacity 36.
ns2_setup_begin.parser_failures: Wrong opcode, missing required tags, duplicate known tags, bad method byte, wrong decoded byte widths and oversized copied blobs fail. Well-framed unknown tags are skipped. As in ACK/REAUTHORIZE, malformed trailing framing after both required fields can stop iteration without invalidating the cursor; finalization checks required-field presence, not complete input consumption. Parsing is not transactional: mode and copied seed/PIN bytes can change before later failure, and absent optional outputs are reset only by successful finalization. A present tag skipped due to null output still counts as seen, so duplicate detection remains active.
ns2_setup_begin.serializer: 0x1002aa24 uses the same descriptor table, initializes opcode 7, always writes tag 11 as low eight bits of the supplied method word and tag 12 as a blob. It does not enforce parser method domain 1..8. Optional tag 14 is emitted only when supplied PIN length is nonzero. Tag 27 uses a full-word nonzero test and writes its low byte, so 256 emits explicit zero. Tags 28/29/30 are byte arguments and emitted only when those bytes are nonzero. Normal order is 11,12,14,27,28,29,30. Size is 8 + seed_length + (3 + PIN_length if nonzero) + 4 per emitted byte field. Blob writer 0x1002eb84 returns zero for lengths >65535 without invalidating an otherwise valid cursor; skipped oversized required seed makes finalization fail, but an oversized optional PIN can be silently omitted because this serializer ignores individual writer returns. Capacity failures in header writer invalidate the cursor. Finalizer returns 1 and updates capacity_inout only on success; failure is not transactional. Direct PPC branch census, including non-linking tail branches, finds no local serializer caller in this executable.
ns2_setup_begin.local_reachability_and_inputs: State table 0x1004f4ac assigns 0x1001f138 as START state 2 message handler; its opcode-7 branch begins at 0x1001f354. Normal admission additionally requires active authentication source 1, the factory fallback. DEACTIVATED handler 0x1001f6a8 delegates only opcode 2 CLIENT_HELLO to 0x1001f138 and delegates other opcodes to the default handler, so reuse of that function does not admit BEGIN in DEACTIVATED. BEGIN passes mode output directly to session+0x29c and seed buffer session+0x2b0. Setup-context byte+0 must be zero for optional PIN input to be enabled (predicate 0x10023fa0); then input capacity is 36 and destination session+0x4b0. Otherwise PIN output is disabled with null buffer and capacity zero. Parse failure returns without resetting any already-written mode/seed or initiating discovery.
ns2_setup_begin.seed_and_method_preparation: After parse success, handler clears discovery/wait caps session+0xa61/+0xa62, then calls 0x100233b0(setup_context,method,seed,actual_seed_length). That function stores requested method +0x2f4 and clears the nine-byte PIN buffer +0x2f9..+0x301 BEFORE envelope validation. It parses ZZ0056 then decrypts ZZ0051 into secret pointer/length +0x304/+0x308, with manufacturing private-key provider described in encrypted_setup_envelope_selection and setup_envelope_cipher_contract. Successful decrypt is followed by method-specific gates: method 2 requires remaining contactless budget +0x2f8 !=0, decrements it before PIN generation, then calls random-PIN helper 0x10022724; method 5 calls that helper without this budget decrement; method 4 returns setup-context byte+0 XOR 1; method 3 logs Invalid PIN and returns 0; other methods log Unknown setup mode and return 0. Thus accepted wire method values are broader than methods this particular BEGIN preparation can execute. Envelope failure logs Unable to decrypt seed and returns 0. PIN generation failure does not refund an already-decremented contactless attempt.
ns2_setup_begin.client_pin_and_chirp: Method 4 additionally calls 0x10023570 with parsed optional PIN and length. It requires setup-context byte+0==0, requested method 4 and nonempty decrypted seed. Helper 0x10027854 derives 16 bytes from that seed with ZZ0215 label setup_pin and no context, using the already established HMAC-SHA256 counter derivation. ZZ0043 selector 2 decrypts the PIN blob, with null additional data/options 0, to an eight-byte output; selected cipher is AES-128-GCM with 12-byte IV and 16-byte tag. Decryption must return 0 and actual plaintext length must equal 8. On success those eight bytes go to PIN +0x2f9..+0x300, with trailing zero +0x301. Derived key is wiped; output scratch is also wiped on wrong plaintext length. No digit-only check occurs here. Methods 2/5 instead call chirp builder 0x1002384c with 64-byte capacity; failure logs and enters shared failure cleanup. Full chirp field encoding/authentication remains open.
ns2_setup_begin.idle_limits_and_volume: Successful preparation copies nonzero discovery tag 27 to cap +0xa61 and waiting tag 28 to cap +0xa62. State-table timer uses min(60 seconds, nonzero cap), so zero/absence preserves 60, 1..59 shortens it and 60..255 cannot extend it. Discovery callback receives raw nonzero tag 27, or 60 if zero; a value above 60 is therefore forwarded even though the NS2 idle deadline remains capped at 60. Tag 29 zero/absent gives starting volume 30. Tag 30 zero/absent gives ending volume 60; explicit nonzero end is clamped to 20..65. Start is then clamped to 20..effective_end. These are numeric discovery-volume parameters, not claimed physical sound levels or percentages. Waiting zero/absence is logged as 60. Caps are installed before transition to DISCOVERY 3 through 0x1001c220.
ns2_setup_begin.discovery_notification: Main binds config+0x5c to 0x1000a9f8 at 0x10002f0c. After entering DISCOVERY, handler invokes it with (cookie,method,start_volume,end_volume,discovery_seconds,chirp_buffer,chirp_length), ignoring its return. Main maps methods 1..8 through u32 table 0x10030bcc to local modes {6,5,4,3,9,10,11,11}. It zeroes an 84-byte payload: u32 mapped mode +0, start +4, end +8, seconds +12, parameter bytes +16 with capacity 64, u32 parameter length +80. Rejects mode outside 1..8, mapped mode 0 or parameter length >64. Chirp methods 2/5 supply 64 bytes; client-PIN method 4 supplies length zero. Mapped modes 3..11 submit mode notification 0x10008298, selecting outgoing command 41 with 84-byte payload through semantic tail sender 0x10006b2c, then return 1 irrespective of send result. Mapped modes <=2 take the payloadless mode helper instead, but none of these table rows maps there. Local enqueue/write does not establish discovery execution by the external receiver, which remains excluded.
ns2_setup_begin.failure_cleanup: Preparation, client-PIN decode or chirp failure leads to 0x1001f5e0. Requested methods 2/6/8 first invoke contactless-termination helper 0x1001eed8 with max attempts reached; all failures common-reset 0x1001c984 with bad SETUP_BEGIN, then close DTLS through 0x100265a0(transport,1). It does not emit a SETUP_STATUS success/failure response in this branch. Message parse failure is different: it returns without that reset/close sequence. The later discovery callback can fail or be absent while state has already become DISCOVERY, and no rollback follows its result.
ns2_setup_begin.todo: Residual: the 64-byte chirp field encoding and authentication at builder 0x1002384c remain unresolved, along with complete producer error propagation and downstream consumers after the DISCOVERY_INTERACTION and PIN_EXCHANGED transitions. The local DISCOVERY table is separate from the peer notification receiver, and submission does not prove a physical discovery action.

evidence.notes: Seven descriptors establish required method/seed and five optional fields.

The setup handler sets a 64-byte output capacity at 0x1001f5b0 and calls chirp builder f_1002384c. The subsequent discovery continuation evidence does not describe the builder's field encoding or authentication.
Raw isel 0x7f893e9e selects default discovery seconds 60 on zero.

State transitions to DISCOVERY before calling discovery callback.

Notification is a semantic tail call into local IPC sender.

One successfully parsed continuation branch clears the discovery cap at 0x1001db48, calls the configured hook only if present at 0x1001db64, and enters state 5 at 0x1001db70 even when there was no hook. The timeout handler in the same row (f_1001d110) tail-calls reset instead.

music_service_catalog.name: Normalized music-service catalog XML
music_service_catalog.description: The player converts the downloaded catalog to a local XML document before attempting installation. The local revision is identified by source text and a numeric version; shipped fallback data, the downloaded representation and SOAP descriptor projections are related representations whose exact parser/projection differences must be traced separately.
music_service_catalog.root: Services with LastUpdateDevice, Version, SchemaVersion=5 and optional nonempty ETag. f_100cc4f4 writes these from its local context; it does not copy the remote root verbatim.

service_children.Presentation: Optional wrapper for Strings and PresentationMap when not suppressed by the manifest capability.
service_children.Manifest: Version and Uri attributes; separate from Presentation.

music_service_catalog.built_in_service: BuiltInService with Type and Name attributes; separate from ordinary Service rows.
music_service_catalog.overrides: The normalized catalog suppresses downloaded Service entries whose numeric ID matches any supplied local descriptor row. Callback f_100cb88c marks that row skipped through byte +0x1025, including nested elements and the closing Service. After the remote stream completes, f_100cc4f4 appends supplied local rows only when both name and expanded secure URI are nonempty. Therefore a matching empty local row can suppress the downloaded entry without appending a replacement. Local row identity overrides the remote row before validating whether the local replacement is usable.
music_service_catalog.manifest_projection: Capability bit 0x400000 controls presentation suppression in the normalized catalog emitter: its extraction at 0x100cb784 stores per-service byte +0x1434, which gates Presentation, Strings and PresentationMap callbacks. The separate Manifest callback remains available when a manifest URI is present. Nested URI elements are serialized as Version/Uri attributes by f_100c757c; this helper performs no network fetch. Policy carries Auth and PollInterval.
music_service_catalog.trial_list: The normalized BuiltInService callback emits Type and Name. It appends a type to the available-trials comma list when (type &0x81)==0x80 and type!=0x84. These are literal mask/equality tests; no named enum assignment is inferred here. The accumulated list has its final comma removed before successful return and is later passed to the R_AvailableSvcTrials update helper.
music_service_catalog.limits: The network response must first have a usable advertised total below 131072 bytes. The separate temporary writer admits normalized output up to and including 131072 bytes. Parsing is fed chunks of at most 4096 bytes. These are distinct input and output limits.

input_rules.catalog_header: Start handler f_10552c20 matches the literal Services and recognizes LastUpdateDevice, Version, SchemaVersion and ETag with strcmp. Version and SchemaVersion use strtoul(base=10,endptr=NULL). Both default to zero; source and ETag default to null. The unsigned SchemaVersion must be <=5 to set the valid/root-seen bytes. Larger values leave the validity byte clear. The callback still receives parsed header values; acceptance also depends on the XML parser completion state.
input_rules.service_row: The parser recognizes Id, Name, SecureUri, Version, ContainerType and Capabilities. Id starts at 0xffffffff; unsigned values above 0x00ffffff skip the row. Name, SecureUri and Version pointers must be present, but these tests do not themselves reject empty name/endpoint strings. Version must pass f_10552b38. ContainerType defaults to MService; Capabilities defaults to zero. Id and Capabilities use decimal strtoul with a null end pointer. Invalid row guards return without setting the active-Service byte; they do not directly invalidate the complete catalog.
input_rules.service_version: f_10552b38 scans the supplied version with sscanf("%d.%d") and requires two conversions. It compares the unsigned major/minor pair with the compiled pair 1.2: greater major rejects, smaller major accepts, equal major requires minor<=2. It does not check an end pointer or require the version string to end after the pair. The raw isel instructions preserve a true result only when the conversion-count and comparison conditions hold.
input_rules.policy: Auth defaults to UserId and PollInterval defaults to 30 in the XML start handler. PollInterval and child Version attributes use f_105527f8: decimal strtoul, return low 16 bits for values <=65534, otherwise return 65535 with a diagnostic. The descriptor-storage policy setter subsequently keeps 1 through 29 and maps other values to 30. XML numeric conversion and stored polling normalization are separate steps.
input_rules.manifest_uri_gate: When the global option query f_1054bdc8(key=7) is false, Manifest Uri must pass strncmp(uri,"https",5)==0 before the callback runs. A true query bypasses this prefix test. This guard checks a literal prefix, not a complete URI scheme; later URI/storage helpers may impose additional constraints. Missing Uri skips the callback. The check alone does not prove that every accepted manifest uses HTTPS.
input_rules.completion_and_skips: The converter needs successful XML feed/completion plus its valid-catalog byte and no explicit processor error. Individual malformed or unsupported Service rows can be skipped while the document remains acceptable. The state adapter recognizes descendants through flags rather than validating a complete catalog schema. Processor-specific return handling and shared XML-engine lexical/error behavior require separate analysis.
input_rules.ratings: With an active Service, the literal Ratings sets parser byte +0x12 and invokes processor slot +0x2c. While Ratings is active, Rating sets byte +0x13, recognizes Id, StringId, AutoSkip and OnSuccessStringId, and invokes slot +0x30 with (ratingId, StringId, AutoSkip, OnSuccessStringId). The three string arguments default to null on each Rating start. AutoSkip is forwarded as text, with no boolean conversion in this adapter. Id is converted with f_105527f8, then stored as a halfword at parser+0x14. That halfword is initialized to zero only by construction and is not reset at Rating, Ratings or Service boundaries: a Rating without Id retains the last parsed Id, including across services in the same parser instance. Downstream processors may impose separate validation.
input_rules.rating_icons: While Rating is active, the literal Icon recognizes Controller, LastModified and Uri; each defaults to null for that Icon. Processor slot +0x34 receives (stored ratingId, Controller, LastModified, Uri). This adapter forwards attribute text without interpreting the controller, timestamp or URI. Icon has no separate active-state byte or closing callback here. End Rating clears byte +0x13 and invokes slot +0x38; end Ratings clears byte +0x12 and invokes slot +0x3c.
input_rules.ratings_projection: Normalizer processor vtable 0x10e767a8 uses the empty void functions f_10552784 at slots +0x2c, +0x38 and +0x3c, and f_1055276c at slots +0x30 and +0x34. It therefore does not emit Ratings, Rating or Icon data into normalized catalog XML. These void callbacks do not return a success boolean. Generic parser recognition does not establish that another descriptor projection preserves the fields.
input_rules.state_dispatch: The start/end adapter uses active-state bytes, not an element-depth stack. Its constructor clears valid/catalog/Service/Policy/Presentation/Manifest/Ratings/Rating/BuiltInService flags at +0x0c..+0x13 and +0x16. Start recognition uses literal case-sensitive strcmp and current flags. End handler f_10552938 checks active Policy first, then Presentation, Manifest, Rating, Ratings, Service, BuiltInService and Services. Once it finds an active branch it compares only that branch name and returns even if the closing name differs. A matching close clears that flag. Thus this adapter is not an independent strict parent/child grammar validator. Unknown elements do not create a subtree-skip depth in this adapter; recognized descendants can still reach its handlers while the corresponding flags remain active. The underlying XML parser still enforces XML well-formedness.
input_rules.namespace_setup: Catalog parser constructor f_105528ac installs start/end thunks f_10554c70/f_10554c64. f_10c3fcd4 passes namespace option zero to f_10c3f81c, which selects f_10c4a8cc. That constructor passes a null namespace-separator pointer to f_10c4a530, leaving the namespace-processing byte +0xe8 clear. The alternative non-null path sets that byte and installs the separator. f_10c3f27c installs the catalog callbacks directly through f_10c4b220, which stores them at XML-parser offsets +0x34/+0x38. The thunks perform no name transformation. The catalog handler compares literal names rather than namespace URIs or local-name suffixes; a prefixed callback name does not match Services or Service. Namespace-expansion and colon-resolution paths in the XML engine are gated by +0xe8, including f_10c45190. Full DTD/entity/encoding behavior remains a shared XML-engine investigation.
input_rules.uri_storage: Descriptor URL storage is secure URI at +0x20, strings URI at +0x60, presentation-map URI at +0xa0 and manifest URI at +0xe0, each 0x40 bytes. f_10553f1c sets secure URI through the packer. f_105540f4/f_1055410c/f_10554124 first store the supplied version halfword at descriptor+0x124/+0x126/+0x128, respectively, then call the packer for strings/presentation-map/manifest URI and return its boolean. Consequently a failed URI update can leave the new version paired with the previous URI; callers must handle the result. This is independent of the earlier SAX prefix and version gates. f_10553994 packs a non-null input string into a 64-byte descriptor URL field. In order, strncasecmp tests https://www. (12 bytes, marker 1), http://www. (11, marker 2), https:// (8, marker 3) and http:// (7, marker 4). The first matching prefix is removed and replaced by its marker byte; the remaining suffix must have strlen<=62, followed by a terminator. If no prefix matches, strlen<=63 is copied as a plain string. An overlong matched suffix or plain string returns false without writing the destination; it does not try another encoding or truncate. Empty plain input is accepted. These are byte-count limits, not a complete URL syntax validator. Case-insensitive prefix matching followed by expansion through lowercase literals normalizes the prefix case while preserving the suffix.
input_rules.manifest_uri_expansion: f_105543d0 reads descriptor+0xe0 through f_10553ab0 into a 128-byte stack buffer, finds the first literal {device} with strstr and replaces only that occurrence with the two bytes zp. For expanded source length L, replacement requires unsigned destination capacity >=L-5, which fits the new L-6 bytes plus terminator. On insufficient capacity it copies the original unexpanded string with strlcpy and may log Service manifest URI truncated; the fallback can therefore leave {device} intact, and the diagnostic does not itself establish actual truncation. Without a placeholder it also uses strlcpy. The function returns the destination pointer and does not report truncation or placeholder substitution as a separate status. Other placeholders and subsequent occurrences are unchanged by this helper.

music_service_manifest_cache.name: Persisted music-service manifest cache JSON
music_service_manifest_cache.description: The persisted svcmanifests.json root contains numeric version, string lastUpdateDevice and a manifests array. Each row is emitted with numeric sid, numeric version, string uri and object manifest. f_10119034 emits sid from row+0, version from the low halfword at row+6, uri from row+8 and the nested manifest from row+0x40c. f_10119b90 emits store version+1 and the local source, then f_10119720 emits the array. This schema is proven by emitters and distinct static parser-definition tables; it is not the catalog XML descriptor grammar.

schema.version: number emitted from current store version plus one

row_schema.version: numeric row version emitted from its low 16 bits
row_schema.uri: manifest source URI stored in a 1025-byte row buffer

music_service_manifest_cache.capacity: Manifest row upsert f_10119434 replaces an existing row with the same sid. For a new sid it permits append while count<=33, reaching a maximum of 34 rows; a full 34-row table rejects a new sid. Existing rows can still be replaced at capacity. Constructor f_101191c8 initializes exactly 34 row objects at stride 0x4fc.

music_service_manifest_cache.todo: Established: persisted grammar and selected acceptance paths, partial-load/upsert behavior, header-only reload, SID-only memory cache, replacement/invalidation, receiver/deletion worker ordering and full-word versus persisted-halfword versions are decoded. Remaining: finish nested/null/type/numeric/exception and absent-manifest round trips; audit malformed-tail effects, all callers/cache writers, clock wrap, concurrency and replication transport/observer/reconciliation consumers.
music_service_manifest_cache.save_fallback: The ordinary emitter writes version, lastUpdateDevice and manifests. A separate persistence fallback can write only version and lastUpdateDevice after full serialization fails, then rename and report success. This header-only fallback is a real emitted representation; header_only_reload documents its accepted root grammar and its effect on fresh versus reused row tables.
music_service_manifest_cache.input_bindings: Cache-file binder f_10119fe8 requires root version (numeric target at parser+0x1304) and lastUpdateDevice (fixed character buffer at +0x12e8, capacity 25). It leaves the manifests array optional. Row binder f_10119ec8 requires sid and version numeric fields and uri as a fixed buffer of capacity 1025; the nested manifest object binding has no required flag, although schemaVersion is required when that object is parsed. Required presence is checked separately from empty-text validity and numeric conversion. The row version is parsed into a 32-bit word at row+4, but saved through the halfword at row+6; round-trip emission therefore keeps only its low 16 bits.
music_service_manifest_cache.header_only_reload: A syntactically valid header-only object containing version and lastUpdateDevice can pass cache parsing because manifests is optional. f_1011991c returns success when f_1011987c reports zero; the latter checks top-level binding status bit 0x2 but does not require an array. f_1011a4bc then copies source/version and rebuilds the public SID/version index from the supplied row table. If the caller supplied a fresh zero-row table, as the download worker does after f_101191c8 at 0x1011b7c4, the index is empty until later upserts. Parsing a header-only object does not itself clear an arbitrary already-populated supplied table. This closes the missing-array grammar question for the save fallback; it does not establish complete cache freshness/reconciliation behavior.
music_service_manifest_cache.incremental_load: Cache-file parsing mutates the supplied row table as each row object closes. Callback f_10119568 checks token kind 1 and field index 4, then f_101194cc calls f_10119434 directly on the supplied table and discards its boolean result before resetting scratch row data. Therefore a new SID beyond 34 stored rows can be silently skipped while the file parse succeeds; existing SIDs can still replace rows at capacity. Duplicate SIDs resolve through replacement in arrival order for admitted rows. A later syntax/required-field failure does not roll back earlier inserted/replaced rows. f_1011a4bc updates stored source/version/index only after overall parse success, but its caller-supplied table may already contain a parsed prefix after failure. The download worker warns on load failure and proceeds with this table to insert the newly downloaded row and save. Whole-file acceptance, complete row retention and unchanged output on failure are three different properties here.
music_service_manifest_cache.post_parse_checks: Cache wrapper f_1011987c scans its five top-level runtime field descriptors after parser result zero. A descriptor with a seen/default marker and bit 0x2 yields internal error 7. It does not recursively scan every nested field status there. The streaming downloaded-manifest wrapper f_1011aabc instead checks its outer root descriptor. Conversion status bits in deeper bindings therefore require a concrete propagation trace; a converter result or a status bit alone must not be promoted to a whole-file rejection claim.
music_service_manifest_cache.memory_lookup: Manifest lookup f_1011a650 takes this, service ID and a nonnull output row. It formats service ID with %u and searches the three-entry memory cache by key length plus memcmp under mutex this+0x1f8. A hit refreshes entry+4 with the current clock word, copies the entire row from entry+0x20 through f_10118f64, unlocks and returns true. It does not compare a requested manifest version, cached row version, public SID/version index or cache entry+0 time word before returning a hit. There is no requested-version argument in this lookup. A cache miss unlocks, loads svcmanifests.json into a fresh 34-row scratch table through f_1011a5d0, finds the requested sid by exact word equality and copies it to output. Load failure or absent SID returns false. A successful file load can still update stored source/version/index even when the requested SID is absent. This lookup performs no HTTP download.
music_service_manifest_cache.memory_cache_policy: The memory cache is separate from the 34-row persisted table. Constructor f_10119a2c sets its capacity to three; entries have stride0x51c and contain a time-derived word at +0, last-access word at +4, string key object at +8 and full manifest row at +0x20. f_1011be38 and the miss-fill code inside f_1011a650 replace an existing equal key if found; otherwise they choose the entry with the smallest unsigned last-access word. The comparison uses strict LT, so ties keep the earliest selected entry, initially index zero. There is no separate empty-entry priority beyond zero-valued initial timestamps. Both insertion paths stamp last access with the clock word. Lookup fill stores clock+1 at entry+0; f_1011be38 stores clock+its fourth argument there, and the download worker passes one. The inspected hit path does not consume this word as an expiration gate. Unsigned timestamp ordering has no wrap compensation in these selection loops.
music_service_manifest_cache.cache_invalidation: Local download success inserts/replaces its decimal-SID entry through f_1011be38; it does not invalidate unrelated cached SIDs. Accepted replication f_1011a204 clears every cache key and both time words after the incoming file is renamed into place. Successful local deletion f_1011b310 clears only the matching decimal-SID key and its two time words after the save worker succeeds. Clearing these paths does not overwrite the old row model stored at entry+0x20; subsequent keyed lookup cannot match an empty cleared key. A cache hit otherwise has no file modification check, so out-of-band file changes are not revalidated by that hit path. Disk reload and cache invalidation must not be treated as the same operation.
music_service_manifest_cache.replication_acceptance: Manifest replication worker f_1011a204 holds the file mutex, applies revision comparator f_10660e58 to current stored source/revision and incoming source/revision supplied in r6/r7, opens the incoming path supplied in r8 and parses it into a fresh scratch row table. Failed revision acceptance, open, parse or rename returns false. After rename succeeds it copies the caller-supplied source (capacity25) and revision into object state, rebuilds the SID/version index from parsed rows, clears all three cache keys/time words, invokes observer slot+0x14 with (kind13, stored source, stored revision, zero), and returns true. It does not compare parsed file version/lastUpdateDevice to the caller-supplied source/revision before committing those supplied values. Its post-rename kind13 call has no new-version-nonzero guard, unlike the local save wrapper. The normal parser permits header-only input; no independent manifests-presence guard is added here. Sender binding, fetch transport and observer delivery remain open.
music_service_manifest_cache.deletion: Local deletion f_1011b310 initializes a fresh table and output revision zero, acquires the file mutex and loads the current file through f_1011a4bc. On load failure it returns false. Compactor f_101195ac removes every row whose SID equals the requested SID, copies survivors forward in order and stores the survivor count; it returns whether any match was removed. No match returns false without saving. A removal calls f_1011ad40; only a true save result leads to matching-key cache invalidation and true return. The save worker header-only fallback is shared here, so true deletion is not proof that all surviving rows were persisted. An observer kind13 call is made only when the output revision is nonzero. Loading can already change stored metadata/index before a later no-match or save-failure false result, and no rollback is performed for those earlier load effects.
music_service_manifest_cache.version_widths: Full row copies f_10118f64 preserve the 32-bit version at row+4. Memory cache hits can therefore retain a full version word written by the download worker. The file emitter writes only its low16 bits, and the public index stores a halfword. A later file reload can return the saved low-halfword version while an uninvalidated in-memory row can retain its earlier full word. No version reconciliation check occurs on a hit; each representation and update path has its own width.

music_service_manifest.name: Nested music-service manifest JSON
music_service_manifest.description: The nested manifest parser table at 0x10ea5bec declares schemaVersion, presentationMap, strings, endpoints, apiKey, accountTiers and advertising. f_10239dc0 emits presentationMap/strings only when their stored URI string length is nonzero; it always emits the endpoints array and apiKey object, conditionally emits accountTiers when its count is nonzero, and emits advertising.headers. The nested field schemaVersion is emitted only when its stored string is nonempty. Unknown or absent fields and required-field policy still require analysis of the JSON framework.

schema.schemaVersion: schema version string checked against supported 1.0 when the schema callback handles it
schema.endpoints: array of objects with type and uri

music_service_manifest.endpoints: Manifest endpoints contain type and uri. The type vocabulary table maps radio=1, reporting=2, audiobook=3 and browse=4. The emitter omits endpoint rows whose stored type is zero or URI length is zero. The in-memory manifest has three 0x1c-byte endpoint slots; accepting an array longer than three depends on the still-untraced collection parser. Endpoint lookup/URI resolution must be traced separately from schema recognition.
music_service_manifest.account_tiers: The accountTiers vocabulary is none=1, free=2, paidLimited=3 and paidPremium=4, with zero as the unnamed enum entry. The emitter skips enum zero. The model stores four tier values plus a count; exact oversized-array and unknown-value behavior remains a parser-framework question.
music_service_manifest.version_gate: Schema callback f_10118580 processes a string token (token kind 3) when its callback field metadata +8 equals 1. It parses the compiled supported string 1.0 and incoming schema string with f_10483e28; malformed input yields internal parse code 16. f_104840f8 compares the supported major/minor pair against the incoming pair. It accepts an incoming pair no greater than 1.0 under unsigned comparison and returns internal code 16 for a greater pair. These are JSON parser results, not independently established SOAP fault codes. The manifest binder requires schemaVersion; see music_service_manifest.required_fields. Shared lexical grammar is documented in music_service_version_string; libc/span boundaries and null/type/error aggregation remain to be traced.
