vli_transport_detail.impl: Virtual line-in control and source/sink transport integration: media_player_vli_ctrl.cxx, avt_impl.cxx and vli_source_manager.cxx. The local VLI action channel is distinct from an HLS status endpoint and from the AvtHaltAction channel.
vli_transport_detail.event_payload: VliTransportActionEvent is an in-process typed event, not an arbitrary action-name string plus unconstrained arguments. Its copied payload is two 32-bit words: VLI type at +0 and action ordinal at +4. f_1013f0f4 is the producer/queueing wrapper, not the consuming VLI controller: it copies these words into the queued closure, chooses the current event-loop subscriber set and returns whether work was queued. No subscriber/usable loop can return false. Its Queued log names the event; names in logs are obtained from the numeric enum.
vli_transport_detail.action_enum: f_106a5fd4 uses the bounded table at 0x10f044bc: 0 START_SESSION, 1 END_SESSION, 2 SUSPEND_SESSION, 3 JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, 4 START_AUDIO_STREAMING, 5 PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, 6 BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, 7 UNKNOWN. Out-of-range values also format as UNKNOWN. The table at 0x10f0403c instead formats the separate AvtHaltAction enum: AHA_STOP, AHA_RESTORE, AHA_END_VLI_SESSION, AHA_SUSPEND_VLI_SESSION and AHA_PAUSE_VLI_SESSION; f_106a3420 bounds it at 4 and otherwise returns AHA_NOT_VALID. The neighboring RCA/TV/VLI table is not the VLI type enum. Neither int_updateCurrentVLISource nor vliCommand is an additional VliTransportAction ordinal.
vli_transport_detail.dispatch_and_completion: The actual AVTransport consumer is f_102be7e4, referenced by event-interface/vtable entries at 0x10eaf3ac and 0x10edfc78. It logs action through f_106a5fd4, copies both words and schedules asynchronous work through f_102eff8c. It installs completion callback f_102dd020 and distinct stopped/scheduler-failed callbacks f_102aac00/f_102aac68. Completion dispatch treats ordinal 3 as group-join follow-up (f_102dceac), 6 as standalone follow-up (f_102d56b8) and 4 as conditional streaming startup (f_102d0280), then publishes type, action and success through f_102f44dc. A queued event is therefore not proof of completed streaming or successful grouping.
vli_transport_detail.controller_paths: f_10415854 handles a StartSession request using the concrete VLI type, with a bounded type dispatch and an unusable/unknown-type diagnostic leading to RabortIfUnlocked. On its event-driven grouping path it emits ordinal 3, not START_SESSION solely because the entrypoint is named StartSession. f_1041616c emits ordinal 4 for audio streaming on its corresponding branch. Topology and group-update callers also emit ordinal 3 with explicit type/action words. f_102b2118 deactivates the local VLI session through state-dependent branches and returns success/failure. Completion waits in f_10413184 use pending flags and a signal wait with a timeout diagnostic; event submission alone does not guarantee completion.
vli_transport_detail.sntp_and_settings: VLI transmission settings carry a 16-bit SNTP port at structure offset +0xa. The local source-settings accessor f_106aa13c delegates to its transport provider virtual slot +0x64. ChangeCoordinator f_102af490 copies returned settings and reads that exact halfword for the sntp port diagnostic. The settings formatter f_1066e5e0 returns an empty string when the validity/name byte at +0x1c is zero; otherwise it passes address, port and auxiliary fields, including +0xa, to f_1066e57c. That formatter renders %d.%d.%d.%d:%d,%s:%d:%d:%d,%s, with SNTP as the last colon-separated number before the final comma. The field is transport metadata, not evidence that this event channel sends SNTP packets or that synchronization succeeded.
vli_transport_detail.group_constraints: The BecomeGroupCoordinator path f_102ce068 can obtain local VLI settings and propagates them through group setup. It compares the low-16-bit off-box-member count from f_106aa688 with the CHSRC capacity from f_1066eea8. A count above capacity reaches the diagnostic and RabortIfUnlocked at 0x102ceafc-0x102ceb30; equality is allowed. State and local/remote-source branches make this conditional, not a universal fixed group-size limit.

evidence.notes: Event-loop/subscriber lookup, queue log, exact two-word payload copy, queued-work closure and boolean return. Corrects prior misidentification of producer as consumer and string payload.

Direct unsigned bounds checks and indexed name loads distinguish eight VLI ordinal names from five halt actions and the separate RCA/TV/VLI table. No AHA names or command strings occur in the actual VLI action table.

Reachable consumer copies type/action into async callback context, installs stopped/failed handlers and schedules the operation. Completion switches on ordinals 3/6/4 and reports action/success. Consumer pointers at 0x10eaf3ac and 0x10edfc78.

Concrete producer calls f_1013f0f4 with type and action=3 or 4, distinct from entrypoint names; invalid-type gate and RabortIfUnlocked, pending completion wait and timeout. Other topology/group producers also use ordinal 3.
State-dependent local deactivation with returned success, and completion event queueing with type/action/result; diagnostic and queued event do not guarantee remote completion.

Local transport-provider accessor, copied tx settings and SNTP halfword at +0xa. Empty-setting gate and concrete formatter argument flow establish the port in serialized settings rather than inferring it from a log string.
Local VLI transport-settings branch, masked unsigned member/capacity comparison and over-capacity error/abort path; equality is not rejected.
Allocation, concrete VirtualLineIn registration, vptr install and zp+0x19a0 ownership. Concrete Play slot points to 0x106a60d4.
Caller passes VLI shared-pointer pair from zp+0x19a0; callee stores its implementation at +0x58, separately from AVT/GRC/RC.
Play SOAP action dispatches impl+0x14; constructed primary vtable resolves it to a logging-only method returning401, not the local event producer.

vli_transport_detail.soap_binding: The SOAP VirtualLineIn implementation is a separate object from media_player_vli_ctrl and the local VliTransportActionEvent queue. Startup f_103fa434 allocates 0x1510 bytes, calls f_106aae20 at 0x103fbe30 and stores that object at zp+0x19a0. Its constructor registers VirtualLineIn and installs primary vptr 0x10f045c4. The service binding routine f_104d49e8, called at 0x103fdd60 in f_103fd65c, binds this object through its +0x58 field at 0x104d4f64. The nearby stores 0x104d4b50, 0x104d4cf0 and 0x104d4dc0 bind AVTransport, GroupRenderingControl and RenderingControl at +0x10/+0x28/+0x34 respectively; these addresses are binding instructions, not implementation entrypoints.
vli_transport_detail.soap_play: The VirtualLineIn Play action entry at 0x10f11ef8 selects SOAP handler f_1073d2dc, which parses InstanceID and Speed and dispatches the implementation virtual slot +0x14. For the constructed object, 0x10f045c4+0x14 points to f_106a60d4. That method optionally logs Play and unconditionally returns 401 at 0x106a6128, without submitting a VliTransportActionEvent. The handler forwards a nonzero implementation result as a SOAP fault at 0x1073d3a0; malformed required arguments have a separate 402 path. Dispatcher-level unknown/unavailable action handling at 0x1073cd64 also produces 401, but it is not the evidence for the implementation stub. Thus local session/group event functionality does not establish that SOAP Play starts VLI playback.

usage_data_sharing.semantics: A mutex-protected, three-state usage-consent cache supplies separate strict upload and permissive collection predicates.
usage_data_sharing.description: Controls collection and upload of player-activity records through ordinary reporting channels. Playback records can include the station identifier, audio format, success or failure, error details and timing. While the local usage-sharing cache is unread, permitted event collectors can retain records in their buffers, but ordinary upload routines hold those batches until the cache says allow. An exact UMTracking value of NoReport selects refusal; any other successfully read value, including an empty value, selects allow. Initialization with no settings interface also selects allow, so this is a local policy state rather than proof of an explicit user opt-in. Separate reporting exceptions mean it does not stop every diagnostic submission.
usage_data_sharing.key_surface: UMTracking is read through the replicated-settings interface at vtable+0xc into a 32-byte buffer. RUsageDataSharing is the mutex name, not a second property read in this module. share_usage is unrelated SMB text and is not this consent key.
usage_data_sharing.state_layout: Singleton 0x10577408 constructs object 0x110a5710 with vptr 0x10eeec5c, signed state +4=-1 (uninitialized), initialization marker +8=0, cached string +9 empty, word +0x2c=2, mutex +0x30. States: -1 unread, 0 permitted, 1 explicitly refused. Destructor tail-calls mutex destruction; deleting destructor tail-calls sized delete (0xc0).
usage_data_sharing.initialization: 0x10577520 returns +8 immediately when nonzero. Otherwise a successful UMTracking read, or a null settings interface, copies the initially empty/read buffer and sets +4=(strcmp(value,NoReport)==0), under the mutex and a second +8 check. +8 becomes (cached string is nonempty). A failed getter copies the empty buffer without changing +4. Thus empty successful values permit sharing but remain retryable; failure preserves the previous state.
usage_data_sharing.writers: 0x10577664 stores callerConsent XOR 1 under the mutex, without changing string or marker. Reporting facade 0x105591b0 tail-calls that setter. This API expects a Boolean caller value; the setter itself does not normalize or validate it. Refresh 0x10577870 ignores null interfaces and failed reads, otherwise copies the string and stores the comparison result under the mutex, returning whether the numeric state changed. It does not set +8 or publish an event. Usagemetrics 0x10707cd4 consumes that change result only for logging.
usage_data_sharing.predicates: Strict 0x105776d8 returns state==0. Permissive 0x10577748 returns unsigned(state+1)<2, accepting -1 and 0. Invalid caller-written values outside {-1,0,1} fail both predicates unless their arithmetic wraps to those accepted states. Both predicates lock +0x30. Helpers 0x105777c4 and 0x1057783c perform mutex ownership assertions and return zero, not additional consent states.

misc_health.arpchecker: ARPC checker decoded (arpchecker.cxx, tag 'arpchecker', selthrd callbacks {reset,data,except,timeout}): at init it resolves the local interface and tunes kernel ARP neighbor params via /proc/sys/net/ipv4/neigh/<iface>/{retrans_time_ms,retrans_time,mcast_solicit} ('failed to open proc fs for retrans'/'...mcast'). Job model: playStream/playDeferredStream enqueue bounded job lists ('playStream too many jobs!','too many deferred jobs! [%u]'), exclusivity gate drops competing streams ('skipping stream due to exclusivity'), deferred queue drains when current job ends. Per-job: decoder lookup, illegal-sample-frequency reject, channel-count cap, volume override [%i,%i-%i over %ums], play status events via ExtAudioPlayStateChangedEvent.

Overflow policy proven in playDeferredStream (f_10377bcc): there is NO eviction - when the job count at obj+0x224 exceeds the bound (flag-mode andi 0x2 gates: <=1 -> free-slot path, >5 -> reject path, else -> 'too many jobs!' log and return 0), the NEW job is refused outright. Job slots are 0x40-byte records at obj+0x228; removal memcpys the record out and memsets the slot.

Deferred-job FSM decoded at 0x10377d18: mode-arg flag bits select policy, not bound. mode&0x2 = multi-job mode (queue up to the 5-job bound; when count>=5 or slot-capacity>=4 the NEW job is rejected with too many jobs! and return 0). mode&0x2 CLEAR = single-job mode: overflow path pops the head job record at +0x228 (memcpy out + memset) and replaces it. mode&0x4 = allow enqueue when the job list is empty (count==0 && !(mode&0x4) -> return 0). Fields: +0x224 live job count, +0x228 0x40-stride job records, +0x268 slot capacity counter, +0x26c/+0x27c playid list (16-byte entries), +0x2ac list bound.

ota_upgrade.retry: The scheduler counter at +0x64 is reset to zero for a new update at 0x102aa268. f_102a9654 increments it before launching the manager. In f_102a9764, unsigned values 0-4 enter the retry-launch branch, whose log prints count+1 out of 5; larger values give up. Thus the normal zero-initialized flow permits five launch attempts including the initial one, not five additional retries. f_102a9654 schedules now+600 seconds after a launch failure; after a successful launch it stores the start time, changes state and schedules a now+900-second status check. Completion/failure exits clear the counter. This is scheduler launch/status behavior, not an exponential network-download backoff.

ota_upgrade.handshake: anacapad f_102a7c90 performs manifest work and passes upgrade_mgr_report.json to its report path. f_10675a5c invokes the local-device BeginSoftwareUpdate operation and spawns /bin/upgrade_mgr through f_1076a8ec. The manager is a TCP controller, not the demonstrated parent of /bin/upgrade: its per-device connection uses port 4444 and sends HELLO, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, PING and REBOOT commands. The installer server listens on 4444 and dispatches those commands with phase/state gates. Independently, etc/runanacapa lines 7-16 starts /bin/upgrade when /var/run/upgradeinfo exists, captures/logs its exit status, removes that file and returns the same status. The installer main reads upgradeinfo for its configuration and client/server mode. Report-file polling by anacapad and the live manager/device TCP protocol are separate coordination mechanisms; neither file-only IPC nor a direct upgrade_mgr exec of upgrade is supported.

evidence.notes: Addresses are offsets into the gzip-decompressed U-Boot payload, not ELF VAs. 0x20004d26 dispatches file position through MTD+0x194; partition wrapper adjusts offset; VNB callback installation points to vnb_set_last_block (name at decompressed+0x289eb0), which stores last-block offset and write metadata compares it. 0x20004d20 follows generic dispatcher default -25 ENOTTY. ota_upgrade.protocol_contract: upgrade_mgr f_10001c8c opens a nonblocking AF_INET/SOCK_STREAM connection to the per-device address on TCP 4444; immediate success or EINPROGRESS is accepted. f_10001424 sends newline-terminated commands and handles partial sends. f_10001684/f_10001728 collect replies and parse HELLO, STATUS, COMPLETE and ERROR, including phase and percent-complete. ERROR parses phase, error-code, internal-data and extra-data, stores the result at device +0x270 and returns -3; receive/protocol failures use internal error 1012. f_1000331c propagates per-device COMPLETE or ERROR with phase/error-code to its controlling client. In upgrade, f_1000924c starts the server with port 4444 through f_10008270; f_100085dc accepts a connection and the poll loop invokes f_10009024. Its vtable dispatch runs HELLO f_10008090, DOWNLOAD f_10008ef0, FLASHWRITE f_10008f8c and REBOOT f_100095ec; PING reports progress and QUIT terminates the connection. f_10007a94 gates operations: HELLO requires initial state 0, DOWNLOAD state 2 or 4 and a zero previous result, FLASHWRITE state 4 and zero result, REBOOT state 6 and zero result. Completion f_10007bb4 moves the corresponding in-progress states 1/3/5/7 to 2/4/6/8 and stores the result. Invalid transitions do not blindly advance: they produce error replies. f_10008d18/f_10008e30 emit COMPLETE?phase=... on success or ERROR?phase=...;error-code=...;internal-data=...;extra-data=... on failure. Download and flash workers reach f_100052bc and f_100065d8 respectively; an installer flash error is propagated as a phase failure.
ota_upgrade.signature_acceptance: The section-dispatch table routes type 0x11 to f_10004db4. It counts encountered signatures separately from successfully accepted signatures (context +0x220 and +0x224). Parsing through ZZ0121 must consume the supplied signature payload exactly. The verifier receives the accumulated SHA-256 image digest, a required digest identifier of 1 and 32-byte length, and signer-policy context byte 1. Only verification success increments +0x224. A failed signature can be logged without immediately aborting that handler, but final package validation in f_100052bc explicitly rejects accepted-count zero with No valid signature and result 6 at 0x10005950-0x10005968. It also checks payload presence and required sections. The section reader permits only further signature sections after the first signature; another section fails as Extra section after signature. Signature sections themselves are excluded from the accumulated image digest. This is section parsing/decryption followed by final package acceptance, not a claim that every input is verified before any decryption.
ota_upgrade.signer_selection: In libsonoscrypto.so.3, ZZ0124 delegates to ZZ0125, which selects a signer through the supplied lookup callback and checks digest type/length. Signed attributes, when present, must contain the matching supplied image digest and are themselves hashed for signature verification; otherwise the supplied digest is verified directly. The upgrade callback ZZ0039 matches a kind-3, 20-byte signer identifier against two embedded root entries at library table 0x1fd80, rejecting an unknown identifier. Its first root is revoked when policy mask 0x1 is set; upgrade sets that mask, so this call path cannot accept that root. An accepted root is loaded through ZZ0101. ZZ0110 delegates to ZZ0109, which requires the signature length to match the RSA modulus size (at most 512 bytes) and calls mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_verify. The upgrade path supplies SHA-256, rather than choosing an algorithm solely from a diagnostic or from the other hash algorithms supported elsewhere in the library. No private key or recovered secret bytes are reproduced here.
ota_upgrade.key_and_cipher_selection: upgrade main constructs its configuration with a null private-key slot at +0xbc. Before processing encrypted sections, it derives DRBG input from flash MDP/MDP2 fields, optionally mixes a word read through /dev/chk ioctl 0x4004f301, generates an IV, a 16-byte symmetric key and a non-NUL/non-newline password, and decrypts the embedded 0x540-byte blob at 0x10021cf8 using library cipher id 1. ZZ0183 parses the decrypted, password-protected RSA private key into configuration +0xbc; temporary plaintext is wiped and freed. Failure leaves encrypted-section processing without a key. f_10004998 decrypts only sections with flag 0x4 and rejects an encrypted signature section (flag 0x1). f_100045c8 parses the envelope with ZZ0053, initializes with ZZ0052 and the configured private key, streams through ZZ0050 and finalizes with ZZ0047. Missing key gives error 48; malformed sizes/headers and decrypt init/update/final failures are rejected, not treated as plaintext. The UBI_RED_KEY_WITH_NONCE text at 0x10040124 has no direct code/address-pointer reference found by the xref scans; its presence is not evidence that it selects the active cipher. The positively traced key path is the configuration slot populated above.
ota_upgrade.envelope_contract: libsonoscrypto ZZ0053 checks envelope magic 0x779b99ca/version 1, bounds its certificate/recipient data, accepts one or two recipient records and at most 512 bytes of wrapped key, and validates wrapping and content algorithm identifiers. ZZ0052 uses the key lookup callback; upgrade supplies ZZ0070, which returns the configured private key rather than looking up a different key for each recipient identifier. The library unwraps the content-encryption key through ZZ0075 and mbedtls_rsa_pkcs1_decrypt: wrapping id 1 uses PKCS#1 v1.5 and id 2 selects OAEP. It checks the content-key length and wipes the temporary unwrapped-key buffer. Content validation ZZ0054 accepts only ids 1, 2, 5 and 6 (the PPC mask clears bit 0x4 before the unsigned range check), even though the generic cipher registry supports seven ids. These map respectively to AES-128-CBC, AES-128-GCM, AES-256-CBC and AES-256-GCM. The mapping is verified against libmbedcrypto.so.16 cipher definitions, not assumed from upstream enum numbering. The streaming wrapper handles the IV/nonce and trailing authentication data; finalization reaches mbedtls_cipher_finish and, for the authenticated mode, mbedtls_cipher_check_tag. Invalid final padding/tag produces failure. Which allowed cipher and signer a particular downloaded package actually uses depends on its bytes, not on strings in the executable.
ota_upgrade.flash_contract: upgrade f_100065d8 checks the optional M4/bootsound partition product flags, reads the partition table, current boot section and generation through libflash, and runs /var/upgradescript before calling hal_flash_reprogram_flash. Nonzero flash results are logged and mapped to installer result 4; success can proceed to the separate application-install path. In libflash.so.1, hal_flash_reprogram_flash at 0x373c scans ten partition-table entries. For type 0x10 (kernel), 0x11 (root filesystem) and 3 (FPGA), current boot-section selector 0 chooses the second matching entry and selector 1 the first: the opposite member of the paired layout. Missing types are skipped. It programs kernel, then root filesystem, then FPGA through f_34c0/hal_upgrade_write_partition_platform, not by rewriting the partition table or explicitly setting a bootsection flag. hal_flash_get_bootsection and hal_flash_get_bootgeneration parse the corresponding /proc/sys/kernel files. This proves target selection in userspace, not the bootloader policy after restart.
ota_upgrade.erase_write_verify: hal_upgrade_write_partition_platform (libflash 0x3214) opens/programs the raw flash device through its caller f_34c0, checks capacity, seeks to the partition end minus one and issues ioctl 0x20004d26, then seeks to the partition start. It erases each block with MEMERASE (0x80084d02), writes a full block and requires an exact-length write. The final partial block is zero-padded in scratch memory and issues the last-block ioctl again before writing. Seek, erase, allocation, ioctl and short-write failures return errors; there is no userspace readback/compare verification pass in this helper. The packaged kernel implements ioctl 0x20004d26 by dispatching the current file offset to the MTD +0x194 callback; its VNB implementation vnb_set_last_block records that offset, and the write path compares it when constructing per-block metadata. Thus this ioctl is last-block metadata, not evidence of a readback verification command. For a redundant rootfs layout the library additionally opens /dev/mtd/(selected-index+1) and issues ioctl 0x20004d20 before writing; an ioctl failure returns 15. In the included kernel generic MTD ioctl dispatcher, that request falls through to -ENOTTY, whereas 0x20004d26 is implemented. This conditional branch is not proof that an observed device actually uses that layout or successfully completes it. No unconditional erase/verify/boot-slot commit guarantee is inferred from API names.

timedjobs.scheduling: timedjob.cxx uses the timedjobmanager tag and channels timedjobmgr, timedjobmgr_ac and timedjobmgr_btn. Jobs bind to registered endpoints; f_105726a8 rejects a missing endpoint. f_10571fac stores absolute next-fire time at job +0, marks scheduling with flag 0x4 at +0x14 and wakes the manager. It distinguishes boot and monotonic time (log markers B/M), converting monotonic to boot time for the default conversion implementation when the job's 0x2 flag is set. Removal cancels pending additions or queues removal and may wait on a condition variable for outstanding work. In f_1057318c, IP deferral applies only to jobs with flag 0x20 when manager +0x1c4 is zero; recovery-AP deferral compares the state helper result with job flag 0x200. Thus these are conditional eligibility checks, not a universal retry policy. In-memory containers are visible, but absence of persistence strings alone does not prove reboot behavior.
resolved_findings: Slow runs are elapsed seconds >= the byte threshold. The consecutive counter increments; logging uses level 4 when log_every is 1 or count modulo log_every is 1, otherwise level 6. A normal run resets the slow counter, logging recovery when the old count exceeded the cadence. These are diagnostics, not automatic exponential retry/backoff.

timedjobs.callback_contract: Registration f_10572dbc accepts (manager, name, callback, context, initial_time, slow_seconds, log_every, flags). It keys entries by callback/context, rejects duplicate active or pending entries and strips internal bits 0xc4 from initial flags. Pending entries are copied into the active tree by f_10573104; f_105721a8 erases entries marked for removal (0x40). In f_1057318c the active entry holds callback +0x10, context +0x14, next time +0x18, slow threshold byte +0x1c, name +0x20, logging cadence +0x24, slow count +0x28 and flags +0x2c. Before calling, the manager copies next time to a stack word, clears explicit-schedule flag 0x4 and sets running flag 0x80. At 0x10573544-0x10573558 it releases the manager lock and calls callback(context, &next_time). The integer return is ignored: the pointed-to absolute time is the rescheduling output. It reacquires the lock, clears running and signals removal waiters when needed. If another thread called the scheduling API during the callback, flag 0x4 makes that explicit stored next time win over the callback output; the flag is then cleared. Otherwise the callback output becomes next time. A callback leaving its already-due time unchanged remains eligible, so a recurring callback must supply its own future time or disable itself.
timedjobs.rescheduling: The disabled sentinel is signed INT_MAX (0x7fffffff), tested without clock conversion and omitted from future-wake calculation. f_10571fac takes a boolean mode: zero replaces the stored time; nonzero keeps the earlier of existing and requested signed times. Requesting INT_MAX stores the disabled time and clears 0x4. Ordinary changed times set 0x4 and signal the manager condition. Flag 0x2 selects the conversion branch through the manager virtual conversion slot +0x10 (default f_10571d8c calls sonosConvertMonotonicTimeToBootTime); callback-produced nonsentinel times in that mode receive the sampled-time offset at 0x10573650-0x1057366c before storage. The run loop samples time before scanning, runs eligible due entries, and accumulates the minimum positive future delay in milliseconds, selecting zero for an already-due result. A changed next time causes another full scan before sleeping. Empty lists and disabled-only lists use INT_MAX milliseconds. The first wait uses zero milliseconds. f_10987584/f_10987204 implement a relative-millisecond pthread_cond_timedwait using clock_gettime(1); explicit schedules, removal, pending-queue integration and stop signal the condition. The starting log s/n/b prints scheduled time and the two sampled times, not a retry-backoff value. Network-ineligible entries are skipped until a subsequent wake; they are not assigned an invented fixed retry interval.
timedjobs.persistence: The scheduler has no internal durable job-state contract. f_10571de0 constructs empty active/pending trees, zero counts, synchronization/thread objects and cleared runtime flags; it does not restore a queue. f_10573104 allocates/copies pending nodes into the active tree, and f_105721a8 frees removed nodes. The destructor f_100c5854 (deleting variant f_100c58b4) destroys thread/condition/mutex and frees both trees, without serializing them. f_10571eec sets the stop byte, signals and joins the worker. Owner initialization builds fresh registrations in code: f_100c1478 allocates the generic manager and registers jobs (including renewSubs with now+2 and advertise disabled), then starts it at 0x100c29e8; f_10276048 constructs the alarm manager and f_10276bb0 registers syncInternetTime and dailyIndex before starting it; f_103c4e64 constructs/registers the button manager and f_103c556c starts it. f_101981f0 calls the latter two startup paths at 0x1019a428/0x1019a440. Thus manager queue nodes and next-fire fields are process-lifetime state recreated at startup, not saved scheduler records. An owner may independently persist its own application data; this statement does not deny saved alarm/timer databases.

The persistent path is constructed from debug/devmode.bin under the persistent root. The runtime output is/tmp/devmode.tmp.bin. Resolved: devmode.bin load path (f_1054c0c0 region, devmode.cxx strings @0x10ee9744+) reads the statement file and passes it to libsonoscrypto import ZZ0137 before "Loaded persistent statement." - the blob is crypto-verified at load, and on failure or when the statement carries R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL the persistent statement is removed ("Removing persistent statement with R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL"). Paths: {debug/devmode.bin source, /devmode.bin active, /tmp/devmode.tmp.bin staging}. The R_* name family is a project-wide result/reason enum vocabulary (~350 names spanning service errors, LED states, stream ops, play ops, SSL errors), not exclusively devmode capabilities.

ZZ0137 is the outer binary-statement parser, with magic/model/constraint-range/length-prefixed identifier and payload guards. It verifies through a signature-envelope delegate. The trust callback loads an embedded2048-bit RSA key and matches its20-byte SHA1 identifier; it does not pass a verifying-key filename to ZZ0064. Detailed joins are in statement_outer_format/statement_key_source.

statement_outer_format.parser: ZZ0137 at libsonoscrypto.so.3:0xca14(size604) parses an unaligned byte buffer(r3) and byte length(r4). Words are copied bytewise to a stack word before comparison, giving big-endian fields on this PPC target. It returns0 on any local rejection and delegates cryptographic acceptance to ZZ0121 -> ZZ0123 -> ZZ0126 -> ZZ0125. No NUL-terminated capability scan occurs in this outer parser.
statement_outer_format.header: Bytes0..3 must be0x28721e71, proven xoris0x2872 plus positive cmpwi0x1e71. Word+4 must equal caller r5; anacapad passes device-info MODEL from manager+498 (constructor0x1054bc74/0x1054bc78 calls getter0x10909550). Bytes+8..17 are part of the signed prefix but have no individual outer-parser guard. Word+18 is an inclusive lower bound and word+1c inclusive upper bound on constraint c=((r8<<16)&0xffff0000)|r9. Callsites supply manager bytes+49d/+49e. Constructor0x1054bbfc..0x1054bc08 writes major86/minor10 into these bytes, so the value is firmware version86.10 packed as0x0056000a. This is an inclusive firmware-compatibility interval, not a timestamp interval.
statement_outer_format.identity_and_payload: Byte+20 is identifier length n. It must exactly equal caller r7; n bytes at+21 must memcmp-equal caller identifier r6. The two callers pass manager string+414 and length+494. Constructor0x1054bc58 fills that string with0x1054c850 then strlen-caches its length. This helper reaches cached manufacturing bytes through0x10909630 and formats six bytes as exactly12 uppercase hexadecimal characters with no separator or serial check suffix; see identifier_contract. Byte at+21+n is payload length k; payload starts+22+n and ends+22+n+k. The parser bounds-checks each required area against total length. Remaining bytes after that end are passed as a signature envelope to ZZ0121. The prefix from byte0 through the payload end is the signed-data input passed through ZZ0123; trailing signature metadata is separate.
statement_outer_format.outputs: Optional lower/upper-bound outputs are written when those fields have passed their local range checks. Payload length and byte offset are written only when both supplied outputs are nonnull, before signature-envelope parse/verification. These output writes can occur before a later rejection; callers must require the final success return before treating them as accepted grants. The parser does not allocate a new payload string or insert a terminator.
statement_outer_format.callsites: anacapad load0x1054c2ec and submission-validation0x1054c4f4 pass the same model, identifier and two-byte constraint. The loader reads at most1024 bytes from constructJFFSRootPath(debug/devmode.bin) via0x1054c8d0. That helper retries EINTR and accumulates partial reads, requires the stat size fit caller capacity, and distinguishes complete read from failure; it does not itself verify signatures.

statement_key_source.binding: ZZ0137 GOT reconstruction uses LR anchor0xca20 and .rela.dyn joins: r4=ZZ0063, r5=ZZ0110, r6=local callback0xc938, r8=ZZ0078. ZZ0064 at0x6c08 is a hash-update wrapper, not a key-file loader. The previous proposed ZZ0064->ZZ0053 verifying-file chain does not describe this call path.
statement_key_source.embedded_key: Callback0xc938 requires key-identifier algorithm3 and length20, calls ZZ0080, then ZZ0072 to obtain20 fingerprint bytes and memcmp-compares them with the envelope key ID. A mismatch frees the loaded key and returnsnull. ZZ0080 at0xcd58 loads294 DER bytes from library rodata0xdc9c and tail-branches to ZZ0101. Independent OpenSSL DER decoding confirms a2048-bit RSA public key with exponent65537. SHA256 of that DER blob is16aa1397c35465e50e06eb947964218dd94823b0d2d64e0345da1522240a86f5. There is no verifying-key filename parameter in this callback.
statement_key_source.algorithm_and_lifetime: ZZ0072 serializes the key to public DER and hashes it with SHA1 selector3. The signature pipeline separately uses SHA256: ZZ0063 requires selector1, ZZ0118 requires1, ZZ0110 tail-branches to RSA verifier ZZ0109 and ZZ0120 requires RSA selector1. The exact direct/metadata signing layouts and candidate/error behavior are in signature_envelope_contract. ZZ0078 releases loaded trust keys. The SHA1 key identifier is not the algorithm used to sign the statement.

evidence.notes: Raw XOR/compare yields outer statement magic0x28721e71.
Inclusive lower/upper constraint guards use packed caller bytes, not current time.
Length-prefixed identifier exact match; no outer NUL capability scan.
Remaining bytes go to signature-envelope parser; full prefix separately passed as signed data.
Trust callback loads embedded key and compares20-byte fingerprint.
Key loader tail branch passes294 DER bytes at0xdc9c, no filename.
Expected outer word+4 comes from device MODEL getter.
Persistent-file callsite supplies manager identity/model/constraint bytes and out-params.
Persistent reader accumulates partial reads and retries EINTR.
Raw XOR/signed-compare equation yields envelope magic0x621da74d.
Primary metadata count<=8; secondary count<=8 at0xa03c.
Unsigned count-1 guard accepts exactly one or two signatures.
Digest selector validator accepts only1; unused alternative size arms cannot widen acceptance.
Duplicate normalized metadata types across primary/secondary lists reject.
Secondary digest reference must equal SHA256 of outer statement prefix.
Tail delegate hashes secondary list bytes when present, otherwise outer supplied data.
Callback reaches RSA signature verification; any accepted candidate can succeed.
Consumed size is bounded by declared size, not required equal.
Matching-key signature failure exits via0xa438; only unmatched-key lookup advances candidates.
Manager firmware major86/minor10 constants produce statement compatibility value0x0056000a.
Identifier comes from cached six manufacturing bytes, not a file-selected identifier.
Six uppercase hexadecimal components; devmode mode has empty separator and suffix.
Specialized type5 marker compare uses31 complemented constant bytes.
Format selector validator accepts exactly1..3.
32-bit stride/count calculation has no independent count/overflow rejection.
Successful type5 parse advances cursor and stores pointer descriptor, without per-element interpretation.
Payload index maps from end of bitmap; no capability-string parser.
Persistent SSH bit47 removes the statement even when bit0 is set.
Submission rejects combined developer/SSH grant via clear, status1.
Final file opened write/create/truncate directly, no atomic rename.
Partial-write accumulation and EINTR retry.
Clear callback ordering continues after failure; submission differs.
Longer new payload arm copies old payload then reads beyond its bitmap span in common loop.
Callback+4a8 points to secondary interface of IPC object configured for/tmp/netstartd.ipc.
Second callback installed as owner+c8c; concrete table not yet bound.
Shipped IPC callback slot+8 points to thunk105d3070.
Tail branch subtracts secondary-interface offset and reaches command13 method.
Zero-payload control frame is u32[12,1,4,13].
Partial-write loop returns transport completion, with no negative/EINTR retry.
Type5 getter delegates to generic metadata retrieval with tag5 and internal length40.
Hash delegate chooses outer prefix or encoded secondary list; primary/header metadata excluded.
Metadata digest retrieval checks type2, not array entries.
Grant application reads separate payload offset/length for bitmap query.
Matching control command13 is silently ignored; sending it does not cause grant reload in this daemon build.

signature_envelope_contract.header: ZZ0121 at libsonoscrypto0x9e14 parses a big-endian envelope into a zeroed0x22c0-byte context. Header: u32 magic0x621da74d at+0, u32 declared size at+4, u16 format version1 at+8, u16 field at+a copied without a local value predicate, u32 primary-metadata count at+c. Magic derives from raw xoris0x9de2 and signed cmpwi0xffffa74d. Provided bytes must cover declared size. Parsing ultimately requires consumed bytes<=declared size rather than exact equality, so unconsumed declared padding and extra provided trailing bytes are not rejected by this parser alone.
signature_envelope_contract.metadata_lists: After the16-byte header come0..8 primary entries, then a u32 secondary count and0..8 secondary entries. ZZ0026 parses entries into0x108-byte slots. Ordinary entry layout is u32 type,u32 value length and value bytes (length<=256). Type identity is low31 bits; high bit supplies required/optional treatment for unrecognized types. ZZ0057 at0x3b1c rejects duplicate normalized types within either list and across both lists. Known ordinary shapes: type1 arbitrary bytes;type2 digest descriptor;type3 four bytes;type4 one byte;type6 four bytes. Type5 follows the fixed-marker/format/count/array delegate ZZ0179, described in type5_metadata_contract. The digest descriptor(type2) must carry byte1 followed by32 SHA256 bytes, since its validator ZZ0118 only accepts selector1; alternative digest-size arms in ZZ0026 cannot pass that validator.
signature_envelope_contract.signature_records: A one-byte signature count follows the lists and must be1 or2, proven unsigned(count-1)<=1 at0xa0d4/0xa0e0. Each record is u32 key-ID length(max2047),u8 key-ID algorithm(valid1..5 via ZZ0119),key-ID bytes,u8 digest algorithm(required1 via ZZ0118),u32 signature algorithm(required1 via ZZ0120),u32 signature length(max256),signature bytes. Parser checks every segment against provided end. The developer trust callback further requires key-ID algorithm3 and length20 matching the embedded key SHA1 fingerprint. The embedded RSA key is2048 bits, so verifier ZZ0109 additionally requires signature length256 exactly.
signature_envelope_contract.signed_data_choice: ZZ0126 computes a32-byte SHA256 digest of the outer statement prefix through ZZ0063; this callback rejects any requested digest selector other than1. ZZ0125 then iterates signature records and reloads a matching trust key for each candidate. If the secondary list is empty, ZZ0117/0x906c uses the supplied outer-prefix bytes as the final hash input. If the secondary list is nonempty, it requires secondary type2 digest descriptor, checks its selector1 and compares its32-byte digest against the already-computed prefix digest. The final hash input instead becomes the contiguous secondary u32 count plus encoded entries, tracked at context+1094/+1098. Thus the outer data is bound directly in the first layout and through its checked digest in the second.
signature_envelope_contract.acceptance_and_cleanup: Final verification reaches ZZ0110 -> ZZ0109 -> mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_verify with SHA256 and RSA selector1. A successful candidate returns1. A null trust-key result advances to the next candidate, but after a key matches, a digest/integrity/signature failure branches directly to cleanup/return0 at0xa438. The second candidate is not tried after such a failure. Exhausting unmatched candidates returns0. Loaded keys are released through ZZ0078; the preliminary key lookup in the two-signature path is also released before the second-stage verification reloads candidates. Metadata retrieval/digest-length/digest-selector/signature verification failures reject. ZZ0123 passes optional expected metadata counter0 for this developer-mode path, so the generic nonzero-counter comparison branch does not impose an additional developer counter requirement.
signature_envelope_contract.limits: Structural parse success is distinct from cryptographic success. Parser validates framing, selector domains and duplicate metadata types before the verifier validates trust binding and digest/signature relationships. It does not itself interpret developer capabilities. The copied u16+a field, type5 array meaning/consumers and unused primary metadata meanings still require consumer joins. No HTTP request-object or service-dispatch records were needed for these library contracts.

identifier_contract.source: 0x1054c850 creates a temporary formatted identity via0x10564b18, strlcpy-copies it with caller capacity128, calls no-op cleanup0x10564bdc and returns1. The intermediate helper calls device singleton0x1090ad44 then getter0x10909630, which returns device-info+118: its cached MDP1+104 plus identity offset14. It copies exactly six manufacturing identity bytes before formatting.
identifier_contract.encoding: 0x10564b18 calls0x1055e59c with capacity20, suffix-enabled flag0 and separator0. Raw isel0x7cc04f9e at0x10564b8c selects separator0 when the flag is0. Formatter0x1055e67c writes an empty suffix; isprint(0) selects an empty separator. Format0x10eebb64 emits six%02X components, yielding12 uppercase hex digits andNUL. The same formatter has other suffix/separator modes, but this devmode call uses neither. No modulo17 character from the displayed SERIAL is appended. Constructor caches strlen12 at+494; the outer statement compares identifier length and these ASCII bytes exactly.
identifier_contract.limitations: The identity wrapper always returns1 after its copy; it does not report a missing/invalid manufacturing identity or destination truncation. A matching statement identifier therefore means equality with the cached formatted bytes used here, not an additional hardware identity validation.

firmware_compatibility_contract.producer: Manager constructor0x1054bbb4 first advances r3 to manager+4b0. It stores0x56 at offset-13(absolute+49d) at0x1054bc00 and0x0a at-12(+49e) at0x1054bc08. Load and submission callsites read those bytes and pass them as r8/r9 to ZZ0137.
firmware_compatibility_contract.predicate: ZZ0137 packs major<<16 | minor. Word+18 must be<=that value and word+1c must be>=it, using unsigned comparisons. For this build the tested value is0x0056000a(86.10). Equality to either endpoint passes that range gate. Capability grant/expiry decisions elsewhere remain separate and are not inferred from these firmware bounds.

type5_metadata_contract.delegate_and_marker: ZZ0026 recognizes normalized type5 and treats its next word as a copied metadata word, then tail-branches to ZZ0179 at0x3d24 with cursor immediately after that word. This is a specialized representation, not the ordinary length-prefixed TLV value. ZZ0179 requires31 marker bytes equal56ea9f16215431a5ba0f50abf164fa176dabb010c4b5719e333159c682ba4c. The library reconstructs them by complementing31 rodata bytes at0xcefc; the initial first byte is hard-coded0xa9 before the complement loop.
type5_metadata_contract.wire_fields: Following that31-byte marker is u8 format at+1f, then u32BE entry count at+20 and the array at+24. Validator ZZ0181(0x9050) accepts formats1..3 by unsigned(format-1)<=2. Format1 computes8 bytes per entry,format2 computes6,format3 computes16. Count0 is locally accepted. The routine checks header availability and array-end against the supplied end pointer, copies a40-byte internal descriptor containing marker/format/count and array pointer into entry+8, advances the caller cursor to the computed array end and returns1. Marker/format/bounds failures return0. It does not copy or inspect individual array contents.
type5_metadata_contract.arithmetic_quirk: The array-span operations at0x3f80,0x3fb4..0x3fbc and0x3fc4 use32-bit shifts/subtraction. There is no independent upper bound on entry count and no overflow check. Computed span is stride*count modulo2^32. For example format1 count2^29,format2 count2^31 andformat3 count2^28 each compute span0. A large count can therefore satisfy this local byte-span gate with fewer array bytes than its unbounded mathematical size. This is a static instruction/boundary audit, not a live-device exploit or observation.
type5_metadata_contract.semantic_boundary: The parse establishes marker, three format selectors, count, strides and pointer descriptor. It supplies no names for array element roles and performs no per-element validation. Its developer-mode consumers and any meaning attached to those formats remain to be joined; no IPv4/IPv6/MAC element interpretation is asserted from stride alone.

grant_bitmap_contract.representation: The outer length-prefixed payload is a byte bitmap. libsonoscrypto ZZ0018 at0xcc70 takes payload pointer,length,bit index and returns0 when index>=8*length; otherwise it reads payload[length-1-(index>>3)], shifts by index&7 and returns its low bit. It allocates nothing and does not scan strings. For outer payload length<=255, bit domain is0..2039. Bit0 is the least significant bit of the final byte. RDevMode manager0x1054bd60 invokes it on statement+404 offset and+408 length under the manager-lock assertion, then converts exact result1 to true.
grant_bitmap_contract.known_capabilities: Load/submission paths query index0 for developer-mode permission and index0x2f(47) for R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL. Evidence includes0x1054c36c/0x1054c54c and the matching removal/retention diagnostic strings. Thus01 is a minimal bit0 payload;800000000000 is a six-byte bit47-only payload;800000000001 sets both. These are byte-encoding examples, not signed usable grant files. Other capability-index consumers remain to be joined; the R_* string vocabulary is not a textual grant-payload grammar.
grant_bitmap_contract.startup: 0x1054c220 reads the persistent file, validates the statement and installs parser outputs directly into the manager. Failed verification clears/deletes through0x1054c048. A verified statement without bit0 also clears/deletes. When bit0 is present, bit47 causes the Removing persistent statement with R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL path and clears/deletes. Only bit0 present plus bit47 absent reaches Loaded persistent statement and retains the statement. Startup does not accept an SSH-only file as a persistent grant.
grant_bitmap_contract.submission: 0x1054c424 rejects length>1024 or verifier failure with return0 before replacing manager data. After verification it computes a notification byte array, clears the1024-byte statement buffer, copies the supplied statement and stores size/payload offset/length/compatibility bounds. If bit47 and bit0 are both set, it calls clear0x1054c048 and returns1. Otherwise bit0 requests a persistent write; bit0 absent removes the old persistent file. Both accepted cases then write the runtime file and notify configured callbacks. Full accepted completion returns2; save/notification failures return0. These are manager method statuses, not HTTP status codes. State replacement precedes writing/notification and has no rollback on later failure.

statement_file_contract.persistent_path: Writer0x1054ca58 with mode nonzero constructs persistent-root/debug, mkdirs it with mode0777(accepting EEXIST), appends/devmode.bin, then opens that final path directly with flags0x241(write/create/truncate) and mode0600. It is not a temporary-file-plus-rename commit. No rename/fsync occurs in this writer.
statement_file_contract.runtime_path: The same writer with mode0 directly writes/tmp/devmode.tmp.bin with the same flags/mode. This file is a separate runtime statement output, not a staging file renamed over the persistent one. Submission writes persistence first when required, then runtime output. File paths under the persistent root are bounded to1024 bytes; path overflow rejects.
statement_file_contract.io: Writes accumulate partial positive returns, retry write-1 with errno4(EINTR), fail on other-1/zero/nonpositive results and close on all opened paths. Return1 means requested bytes were written,0 means failure. Close result is ignored. A failed direct overwrite can leave truncated/partial data. Unlink helper0x1054cbe8 selects persistent path for mode1 or runtime path for0 and returns whether unlink succeeds. Clear/submission paths do not make those unlink results a rollback gate.
statement_file_contract.clear: 0x1054c048 computes a removal notification payload, clears statement bytes and fields+400/+404/+408/+40c/+410, attempts to unlink both persistent and runtime files, then invokes each nonnull manager callback at+4a8 and+4ac via vtable slot+8 with byte buffer and length. It logs callback-1 failures and continues, including trying the second callback after the first fails. Submission instead stops on first callback-1 and returns0 without calling the second.

grant_notification_bytes.mechanism: 0x1054beb0 clears the caller output buffer using its supplied capacity. New payload length0 copies the old bitmap and reports its length, supplying removal bytes. Equal old/new lengths with equal bytes reports length0. Otherwise it reports max(old_length,new_length), zeroes a255-byte stack workspace, then XORs that workspace with bytes read from the old manager payload. The callback interpretation of this byte array remains untraced.
grant_notification_bytes.alignment_and_quirk: When old length>=new length, it right-aligns the new payload in the zeroed workspace then XORs all old bytes, producing a big-endian-aligned difference. When old length<new length,0x1054bfe8 instead copies the old payload into the right-aligned workspace, then the common loop at0x1054bf90 still reads max-length bytes from the old manager payload. It does not read the supplied new payload in this arm and can read into the following statement bytes. This asymmetry is established from the copy and loop arguments; do not describe this helper as an always-correct old-XOR-new delta. Both outer payload lengths are byte-sized, keeping the workspace span<=255 in these callers.

notification_ipc_contract.installation: Owner initialization0x101998d8..0x101998f8 installs manager callback+4a8=owner+8d4 and callback+4ac=owner+c8c. The first pointer is the+14 secondary interface of the IPC object at owner+8c0, configured immediately beforehand by0x105d364c with endpoint/tmp/netstartd.ipc. Callback setters0x1054c738/0x1054c748 only store the object pointers, with no retain operation or null check in these setters.
notification_ipc_contract.shipped_interface_method: The concrete shipped IPC secondary table0x10ef5f64 has slot+8=0x105d3070, a thunk that subtracts0x14 from this and tail-branches to0x105d304c. The method ignores the change-buffer arguments and sets command13,payload pointer0,payload length0, then tail-dispatches primary slot+34. For the corresponding primary table0x10ef5f10, that slot is0x105d3c7c, which locks IPC+88 and delegates to0x105d3b10. The full main-owner installation of this concrete primary/secondary table pair still needs joining before treating the installed callback as proved to take this exact implementation.
notification_ipc_contract.frame: For command13 with zero payload,0x105d3b10 emits exactly16 bytes with four u32 words [12,1,4,13], in the native big-endian representation of this PPC build. The fields are built at0x105d3c44..0x105d3c60. No capability bitmap bytes follow them. It sends a control-IPC command; this is distinct from the NS2 over-the-air opcode13(GET_PSK). The shipped netstartd control table maps13 directly to its common return: it performs no statement reload or state effect. See bin_netstartd.control_ipc_command_13 for receiver bounds/table evidence.
notification_ipc_contract.transport_result: The send helper rejects fd+18c<0 and payload lengths beyond the virtual limit(default2048). A zero-payload frame uses the common write loop. It accumulates partial positive writes until all16 bytes are sent, returns0 on that completion and-1 for zero/negative write or unusable connection. Unlike the statement-file writer, this loop has no EINTR retry. The return proves transport write completion, not daemon acknowledgement, statement reload or grant application. The manager treats-1 as notification failure.
notification_ipc_contract.second_callback_boundary: The second installed pointer(owner+c8c) and its invocation slot+8 are proved, but its concrete table/receiver still needs tracing. The developer-mode event-generator label alone is insufficient to assign it that role. Existing state clear/submission callback ordering remains as documented; no delivery/event effect is inferred from the label.

metadata_use_in_developer_grants.decoded_array_scope: Type5 parser creates a pointer/count descriptor. Getter ZZ0180 at0xa864 requests normalized type5 and internal descriptor length40 via tail branch to0x9d78. A direct branch audit found no call to this getter in libsonoscrypto, and no import in the checked shipped executable directories bin,sbin,opt/bin,wifi. This audit does not prove absence of every indirect/external caller. In the traced ZZ0137 verification chain, ZZ0126/ZZ0125 invoke the trust/hash/RSA callbacks and retrieve type2 digest metadata; they do not call the type5 getter or read individual array entries. The manager later queries only the separately located capability bitmap.
metadata_use_in_developer_grants.primary_metadata: Primary entries are structurally parsed, type-checked and included in the normalized duplicate-type rejection. The developer verifier does not use their values as capabilities or compatibility bounds. Generic expected metadata-counter handling is disabled because ZZ0123 passes0 for that argument. The copied u16+a envelope field likewise has no local predicate or value-dependent branch in this traced grant path. These fields cannot be assigned a developer-mode permission meaning from their presence.
metadata_use_in_developer_grants.signature_coverage: The signed outer statement prefix ends before the envelope. Direct layout hashes that prefix, not the envelope header/primary list. Metadata layout first checks the outer-prefix digest, then hashes the secondary count and encoded secondary entries; it still does not include the envelope header or primary list in that hash input. Thus valid primary metadata can affect framing/duplicate rejection without being part of the RSA-protected data in either traced layout. A secondary type5 entry is covered as encoded bytes by the metadata signature, even though grant application does not interpret its array contents.
metadata_use_in_developer_grants.scope_limit: This establishes concrete use and nonuse inside developer-grant verification/application. It does not name the generic type5 formats from their strides, or establish their use in another application. The unavailable concrete notification-object installation chain remains explicit because continuing into shared implementation initialization would enter the other agent's protected lane.

mod_zp.shutdown: ordered teardown: modZPShutdown_{HttpClient, ZonePlayer, AsyncMuseThreadPool, InternalEventDispatcher, resetZone, DropoutEventHandler, deleteTimedJobManager, AsyncThreadPool, finalSection{,End}} via lmodZPShutdownWrapper

trackplaymonitor.semantics: Per-track playback accounting with sampled stream segments, in-progress/final reports and asynchronous reporting work. This is not evidence of a universal CurrentTrackPlayed event or a server-side billing contract.
trackplaymonitor.consumer: The monitor calls the notifier at object +0xa8, virtual slot +8, with a temporary report, track metadata and stream entry at 0x104c1e68-0x104c1e84. Its return controls follow-up recorder ACK processing; a successful callback on a non-final entry produces operation 4 via f_104c6264. The RPlayReportSubmitter notify implementation is f_104caf08 (vtable pointer at 0x10ed8fac), which distinguishes final/non-final entries and routes service-specific reporting. CurrentTrackPlayed at 0x10ea1608 is a Spotify state-name table entry at 0x10ea1480, adjacent to AwaitingCurrentTrackAck and AwaitingNextTrackAck. String adjacency does not establish that the monitor emits an event by that name, nor that Spotify and VLIPlaybackTracker are the same consumer. The previous universal Spotify/VLI/session-channel/billing claim is unsupported and is not part of this contract.
trackplaymonitor.record_shape: Track records retain URI/station identity and reporting metadata; the label table at 0x10ed83c8-0x10ed8460 names Track Or Station URI, Extra Md, Context URI, CQ Auth Token, SMAPI Device Id, CloudQueueVersion, CQ Context Version, CQ Playback Id, API Key and Framer Name. f_104c19e8 constructs a temporary report from the selected entry, computes duration through f_104c3808 and passes it to the notifier. Diagnostic output includes play seconds, timestamp, packet id, action, offset, error count and URI. In progress and Final are selected by the report-final flag, with a separate LSE annotation. These are diagnostic/report fields, not a wire schema guaranteed for every service.
trackplaymonitor.stream_accounting: f_104c6264 is the recorder operation dispatcher: an unsigned operation >10 returns through the default path, otherwise a relative jump table selects SAMPLE, OPEN, CLOSE, INTERRUPT, ACK, ERROR, IMMED_RESYNC, SCHED_RESYNC, BOUNDARY, ORIGIN_TIME_SELECTED or QUALITY_SELECTED processing. The latter two were missing from the previous inventory. Samples publish playback segments keyed by timestamps and packet ids; close, interrupt, error, resynchronization and boundaries are distinct inputs, not all treated as normal completion. The recorder retains segment collections and cancellation state; full-container paths can overwrite a segment or drop a report, so accounting is not lossless under all memory/error conditions.
trackplaymonitor.report_job: f_104c48d4 serializes scheduling under the recorder lock. Byte +0xb39 suppresses another kick while reporting work is already pending; a new kick sets it and submits callback f_100be4b8 with the owner identifier through the generic job interface. That adapter calls f_10188298, which finds the owner through f_1040edf4 and, only if found, calls f_103f76d0. The latter loads the monitor at owner +0x1904 and reaches f_104c25e8, which flushes work through f_104c228c and f_104c1f60. A missing owner safely skips dispatch. A kick therefore means queued work, not proof of a successful cloud upload. RPlayReportSubmitter separately prepares service/report data; f_104cbf1c contains submission and failure-dependent paths. Backend acceptance, service billing and the meaning assigned to listen data by a remote server are not recoverable from these local calls.
trackplaymonitor.bounds_and_failure: f_104c15a0 startup processing uses a bounded track-entry pool; exhaustion at 0x104c1738 logs Resetting due to no free RTrackLogEntries and calls f_104c0728 to reset before retrying the entry path. f_104bf7c8 diagnoses a too-small string pool. f_104c265c handles memory pressure by flushing with f_104c1f60 and recovering through f_104c228c. Recorder diagnostics and branches include cancellation of zero-sample streams, full segment containers and report dropping. No unconditional guarantee that every loaded track generates a completed, delivered report follows from this implementation.

evidence.notes: Three absolute string pointers name AwaitingCurrentTrackAck, AwaitingNextTrackAck and CurrentTrackPlayed. This establishes names, not a monitor event dispatch or a VLI consumer alias.

Report construction, duration and diagnostic fields; virtual notifier call at 0x104c1e84, success/non-final ACK follow-up. Submitter notify handles final/non-final and service-dependent paths. Metadata label table in 0x10ed83c8-0x10ed8460 is vocabulary, not a universal serialized schema.
Unsigned operation range <=10, relative dispatch table and operation-specific branches. ORIGIN_TIME_SELECTED and QUALITY_SELECTED are additional inputs; resync/error/close are distinct from samples.
Pending-byte scheduling guard, report callback and owner lookup/null handling, then monitor flush. Proves reachable reporting work, not successful remote delivery.

ir_remote.impl: irdecoder.cxx: RIRDecoder capture, decode, learn, code matching and local controls, with HTTP database support. IR learning is not restricted to retail demo mode.
ir_remote.reader_and_decode: The select-thread data callback f_1024dee0 reaches f_1024dd38, which calls hal_ir_read with a bounded capture buffer. HAL errors, zero/oversized data and captures of two bytes or fewer do not enter the decoder. Accepted captures call f_1024cd1c. That routine checks capture size, derives pulse histograms/thresholds and has separate biphase, pulse-width and pulse-distance decoding branches. Missing peaks, a missing required second peak, an excessive biphase pulse or too many raw bits reach rejection paths. Successful decoded captures feed matching/learning; the diagnostic recognized count alone is not a universal successful button action.
ir_remote.code_lists: There are five independently bounded installed lists: repeat, volume up, volume down, input and mute, not three volume lists plus a fixed input code. The insertion routines at f_10247f28 through f_1024836c refuse a list already containing 10 entries. Installation also rejects null codes, excessive code length, unknown target and unknown pattern. The repeat list is decoding/repeat metadata, not a fifth user action. Factory initialization supplies brand-specific remotes and example code bytes; these are defaults, not a remotely fetched complete model catalog.
ir_remote.persistence: f_102451a4 chooses the factory file /opt/ir/irconfig.txt when its factory-mode argument is set; otherwise it obtains irconfig.txt through the configuration-store interface. It parses repeat_codes, vol_up_codes, vol_down_codes, vol_mute_codes and input_codes sections. The writer around 0x102457ac obtains the configured filename, opens it for writing and emits all five sections, with an explicit open/write failure diagnostic. The three volume lists are additionally serialized for settings/reporting by f_1024a108. The local reader/writer does not itself hard-code /jffs/irconfig.txt, so that previously asserted physical overlay path is not a portable storage guarantee.
ir_remote.learning: f_1024b714 handles capture/repeat learning with state and timeout checks, rejects overly long captures, compares repeated captures, tracks short/long alternatives and can fall back to a non-repeat classification after its bounded capture count. f_1024967c summarizes multiple passes: it compares the first and third short-code lengths and bytes, checks repeat/alternate redundancy, and distinguishes repeating, alternating and non-repeating results. This is not a universal two-pass algorithm. One-button recognition f_1024b464 first compares local candidate hashes, lengths and bytes, then tries the local database lookup f_1024b3d8 when needed. A timeout or database miss reaches explicit failure handling in f_10249cb4; ordinary learned codes are not required to have a successful cloud lookup before local use.
ir_remote.actions_and_debounce: f_1024bd80 uses current/previous action, repeat state and timestamps to debounce local controls. The recent comparison uses a 350-ms increment and volume repeat accounting uses 100-ms steps; mute and input have separate conditions from repeated volume steps. The local-control interface receives volume/mute calls, and input processing uses play state and autoplay paths. The IR Volume Up/Down/Mute/Input strings in f_1024c810 are testpoint press-action labels, not proof that every physical capture publishes an in-process event with those names. A rejected, disabled, repeated or unrecognized capture need not produce a control action.
ir_remote.database_http: The default URL is http://ir.ws.sonos.com/IRCode/, obtained through override selector 0x1d (O_IR_DB_WS_IRCODE_URL). f_1024a700 renders GET requests; f_1024a8b0 renders POST with Content-Type application/xml. f_1024aae0 submits IRCode containing code, value and guid. The GUID is generated locally from a 16-byte /dev/urandom read by f_1024a584 and formatted before submission, not returned by the server. Submission f_1024a3dc accepts HTTP 201; lookup f_1024b048 uses a 5000-ms deadline and handles 200, 404, transport errors and response parsing separately. Commit f_1024ae38 installs/saves learned state and schedules the submission path, with a completion-timeout branch; local learning and remote database population are distinct operations. These binaries cannot establish current server availability or the contents of its live model database.
ir_remote.soap_vocabulary: The DeviceProperties action-name table includes CommitLearnedIRCodes, IdentifyIRRemote, IsRemoteConfigured and LearnIRCode. The local learn implementation has a specific one-button-code-not-found result as well as timeout, unknown target and unknown pattern failures; remote learning is not equivalent to accepting any raw capture.

evidence.notes: HAL read return/size gating and reachable decoder call at 0x1024ded4; decoder histogram and separate coding branches, peak/pulse/raw-bit rejection paths. Does not infer an action from a recognized log alone.

circuitbreaker.semantics: Shared circuit breaker for the UCS and Thor outbound clients: stop new attempts after six failures in two minutes, reopen after 30 seconds, and let a successful result clear the failure history.
circuitbreaker.state_machine: State +0x1c: OPEN=0, SEMI_OPEN=1, CLOSED=2; ctor initializes CLOSED. 0x109d91ec locks mutex +0x90 and reports an outcome. Nonzero success calls 0x109d90cc: clear +0x18, add its previous value to +0x130, empty timestamp history via 0x109bc8a4, account interval via 0x109d9670 if previously non-CLOSED, then CLOSED. Zero failure appends monotonic timestamp to six-slot circular history (+0x48 control,+0x60..0x8f storage), increments +0x130. In CLOSED with +0x38 !=0, remove oldest timestamps only while age > window_ms(+0x40/+0x44)*1000000. Equality remains in window. Normal trip predicate is history_count >= threshold(+0x20), unsigned compare at 0x109d92b0/0x109d92b4. In SEMI_OPEN, increment failed-retry count +0x18; counts below +0x24 bypass normal trip check; once count >= +0x24, evaluate normal history threshold. Thus +0x24 counts failures, not concurrent requests or an admission quota. OPEN reports can still append failures and rearm the deadline if caller submits them. Trip writes OPEN and deadline(+0x30/+0x34)=now_ns+hold_ms(+0x28/+0x2c)*1000000, increments open counter +0x120, saves interval start +0x140/+0x144. 0x109d9470 lazily transitions OPEN to SEMI_OPEN when now >= deadline, folds failed-retry count into +0x130, resets +0x18, increments +0x134; no background timer is armed. Public locked gate 0x109d957c returns state==OPEN (1 means BLOCKED), not an allow flag. Success clears the retained pre-trip history; opening and half-opening do not.

Both pass threshold=6, failed-retry threshold=2, signed i64 hold_ms=30000, sliding_enabled=1, signed i64 window_ms=120000. 0x1008e190 sets r28=1 before stb r28 at 0x1008e3bc. Durations convert milliseconds to nanoseconds: 0x1086d504 uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC, converts seconds to chrono nanoseconds via 0x1086d12c->0x1086d220->0x1086d174 and adds tv_nsec via 0x1086d2a8/0x1086d358. 0xf4240 is the ms-to-ns multiplier, not a fixed OPEN timeout.

UCS outcome at 0x104d0f8c is HTTP response code >0, so an HTTP error response can count as a successful connection. Thor reports at 0x105fc7a4 and 0x105ff0bc likewise use response status >0; applicability is additionally conditioned on the request bookkeeping check at 0x105fc33c. Gate callers 0x104cf450 and 0x105fcb90 treat returned 1 as OPEN/blocked. This primitive has no SOAP fault number or wire parser; callers choose their own failure mapping.

0x109d95f4 copies the 0x28-byte telemetry record starting +0x120; in OPEN/SEMI_OPEN it first calls 0x109d9670. That helper accumulates now minus interval-start into +0x128/+0x12c and clears +0x140/+0x144, so snapshotting is a state mutation. It is not an epoch notifier. No callback or vtable controls the breaker states. Publisher resets only its snapshot with0x109d9704, not the breaker counters.

noncehandler.semantics: Muse peer-address-bound,one-use authentication challenges with300-second expiry and a three-address cache;separate MAC/SHA-1/RSA signing-envelope helper. JSON/base64 input contracts,clock/mode policy,key provenance and concrete consumption behavior are bound.
noncehandler.lifecycle: The two previously combined pipelines are distinct. HTTP signing helper0x105ccad4 formats six device-MAC bytes,an embedded16-byte salt and the caller credential C string,hashes them with SHA-1,and RSA-PKCS1-v1.5-signs the20-byte digest. Its nonce output is the base64 signature;0x105cccbc inserts that into credentials/nonce/keyType JSON and base64-encodes the JSON. There is no entropy draw at0x1090ad44/0x10909630; those obtain the static device-info singleton and its MAC field. Muse nonce creation is0x10b99b38: it calls ZZ0154 to produce16 characters from the62-character alphabet0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ and records per-binding expiry/context. Muse validation0x10b996b4 base64-decodes and parses credentials/nonce,checks current credentials,then looks up and consumes the matching cached nonce through0x10b995a8. Record flags+0x18 and+0x28 are optional-value presence flags,not valid-slot/consumed flags. Consumption is hash-node erasure,not a byte written to+0x28.
resolved_findings: The Muse delegate is concrete: player+0x56c0 -> initialization argument7 -> host+0xb8 -> handler+0xac -> vtable0x10f986e8. Creation0x10b99b38 supplies16 alphanumeric characters and300-second deadlines.
Nonce record+0x18/+0x28 are optional deadline/snapshot presence bytes. Invalid predicate0x10b9917c chooses optional provider-time expiry or snapshot fallback; they are not consumed-state flags.
An exact binding+nonce match is erased at0x10b99684 before the accepted or stale result is returned. Capacity is three distinct bindings with stale pruning; accepted result is3 at0x109f98a4.

concrete_provider.producer_chain: Player owner constructor0x10691e00 stores provider vtable0x10f986e8 at owner+0x5318 at0x10692960. With owner=player+0x3a8,this is player+0x56c0. Live Muse initialization0x1019ab7c computes this provider and0x1019abb4 passes it as argument7 to0x109f7d30. That function retains it at host+0xb8 and passes it to nonce handler host+0xd0 via0x10b98fb8 at0x109f7dcc. Setter0x10b98fec stores the exact provider at handler+0xac under the handler mutex. The delegate is therefore statically bound; the previous claim that its expiry was unrecoverable was incorrect.
concrete_provider.slots: Concrete provider vtable0x10f986e8 has slot+8=0x109eec0c (optional signed64-bit time),+0xc=0x109ef8b8 (optional current context string),+0x10=0x109ef028 (optional context-string/monotonic-time snapshot),+0x20=0x109ef26c (snapshot-invalid predicate),+0x24=0x109eec8c (time-expired predicate). These last two predicates return an optional boolean whose true value means invalid/expired,not accepted.
concrete_provider.current_time: Live provider setter0x1019aa24 passes singleton0x110977d0 to0x109ef480;0x109ef50c writes provider+0xc. Static initialization0x10090d18 installs vtable0x11089e6c in that singleton. Its slot+8=0x1098b430 calls gettimeofday at0x1098b478 and returns the seconds word; slot+c=0x1098b418 is a semantic tail wrapper to gettimeofday.0x109eec0c sign-extends this32-bit seconds result into an optional64-bit value. This is wall-clock epoch time,not a trusted-time availability check and not the explicit clock-id1 monotonic time used by snapshot expiry. The seconds getter does not inspect gettimeofday's status before returning the seconds word.
concrete_provider.snapshot: Provider context is the current BootSequenceManager value formatted as unsigned decimal,not an arbitrary security-settings string. Player construction0x1018ddbc creates BootSequenceManager through0x1058a574 and0x1018ddec retains it at player+0x5730/control+0x5734.0x1019aa28 supplies that shared-reference pair to0x109ef480,which stores weak object/control pointers at provider+4/+8. Context getter0x109ef8b8 locks that weak reference into a temporary strong reference,returns absent when unavailable,and uses the concrete slot+c formatter0x10582890. The optimized path0x109ef994 invokes boot-sequence slot+8 then formats %u at0x109ef9b8. Concrete vtable0x10ef09f8 has slot+8=0x1058a2bc,which reads BootSequenceManager+0xd8 under mutex+0x48. Snapshot getter0x109ef028 obtains this decimal string and clock-id1 seconds; snapshot invalidation requires the current decimal boot-sequence string to match and current monotonic seconds<=saved deadline. A changed boot sequence invalidates it early.

expiry_policy.generation: 0x10b99b38 receives a caller binding string and the RDM-or-MTM household flag. For other households,it requires provider time slot+8 to have a value,then adds300 to the64-bit time using raw addic0x3129012c at0x10b99d48 and addze0x7d4a0194 at0x10b99d4c. RDM/MTM households skip this optional wall-clock deadline. Both modes require snapshot slot+0x10 to succeed and add300 to its monotonic-seconds word at0x10b99dc8 (raw0x3929012c). Missing required provider data returns an absent challenge; the random-string draw alone is not successful creation.
expiry_policy.value_layout: Hash-node value begins at node+0x20. Relative to that value: nonce std::string at+0,optional time-deadline presence byte+0x18,64-bit deadline words+0x20/+0x24,optional snapshot presence byte+0x28,snapshot object+0x2c containing context string pointer+0x34/length+0x38 and monotonic deadline+0x4c. Node hash is at node+0x70. Presence writers are visible in0x10b99978..0x10b99ab4 and the producer at0x10b99b38; neither flag is a replay-consumed marker.
expiry_policy.validation_order: 0x10b9917c locks the handler. If the time deadline is present,it calls provider slot+0x24. A present predicate result is returned directly; an absent provider result falls back to the snapshot. Without a time deadline,it directly uses that snapshot fallback. Missing snapshot or an unavailable/unequal current context returns invalid. Snapshot predicate false means usable,true means stale. There is no unconditional requirement that+0x18 be set or+0x28 be clear.
expiry_policy.time_boundary: 0x109eec8c compares signed high time words then unsigned low words. It returns expired for current>=deadline and unexpired for current<deadline. Equality is expired on this time-source path. Snapshot path0x109ef26c uses strict currentSeconds>savedSeconds,so equality is still valid there. Raw branch words0x409c0018/0x409efff0/0x40bcffe4 and CR extraction0x5529f7fe were inspected; these two boundaries must not be described as identical.

replay_and_capacity.lookup_and_consume: 0x10b995a8 looks up the caller peer-address string in handler map+0x90 via0x10b9a48c,then checks nonce byte length and memcmp equality against the supplied nonce. Missing binding or wrong nonce returns1 and leaves any existing entry in place. On an exact match,it computes the invalid predicate through0x10b9917c,then unconditionally erases the node via0x10b9a1ac at0x10b99684 before returning1 if stale or3 if usable. Thus both a successful use and a matched expired/stale attempt consume the record. Eraser unlinks the node,frees both stored strings/snapshot storage and decrements count+0x9c at0x10b9a29c.
replay_and_capacity.credential_gate: Wrapper0x10b996b4 returns4 if base64 decoding or credentials/nonce parsing fails. It compares parsed credentials through0x10b994ec against the currently configured optional credential value from0x109ecf0c(kind8); inequality returns2 before nonce lookup. Matching current credentials enter binding lookup/consumption. Result3 is the accepted path at live Muse consumer0x109f98a4; other results do not take that path.
replay_and_capacity.capacity: Store0x10b997e4 permits insertion while count+0x9c<=2,so at most three distinct peer-address strings are retained. At count>2,an existing address can still be updated. A new address causes the store to walk current nodes and erase those whose invalid predicate is nonzero; it inserts only if that reduces count to<=2. Otherwise it returns5 at0x10b99930 and creator returns an absent challenge. No fixed eviction of an arbitrary valid entry occurs in this branch. Store/lookup/consume are protected by the same handler mutex.
replay_and_capacity.clear: 0x10b99028 clears provider+0xac,walks and frees every current node including optional snapshot storage,zeros hash buckets and resets count/list under the mutex. No persisted nonce-store writer is present in this recovered lifecycle; no on-disk replay list is asserted.
