If already initialized,it returns1;otherwise it calls loader0x10bb8d9c,publishes its boolean result at+0x349 and clears busy. Readers0x10bb9280 require capacity>=708,initialized nonzero and the first four private bytes not all zero; they copy exactly708 bytes and set the returned length. These readers do not initiate loading. Raw0x5529063e at0x10bb930c is the loaded-flag low-byte mask,not an8-bit shift.
key_loading.flash_source: Loader0x10bb8d9c first calls hal_flash_get_mdp2_wrapper at0x10bb8dcc. libflash.so.1 wrapper0x2474 creates a fresh flash-info handle,gets MDP2,then releases it. hal_flash_get_mdp2 at0x23c0 reads4096 bytes from flash offset info+0x50 plus info+0x40 via read_from_offset;it checks MDP2 magic and zeroes the output on an error. The player accepts a successful wrapper result and payload length at buffer+4>=708;it copies private bytes from buffer+8 into the cache at0x10bb8f04. If remaining payload after those708 bytes is>=128,it copies128 public-modulus bytes from buffer+8+708 and stores public length128. Otherwise it keeps public length0 while returning successful private-key load. Flash content format is not RSA-validated during this loader stage.
key_loading.file_fallback: A flash read failure or flash payload shorter than708 bytes selects %s/private.key,using the supplied root. Startup0x105e7788 supplies the result of0x1068a70c. The latter starts with configured root pointer0x1109b024 and appends its component array. At this call the component count is0: raw SPE words0x11484b00 at0x105e7768 and0x11484b20 at0x105e7778 copy the{pointer,0} pair from sp+0x28 to sp+0x10;the builder therefore adds no subdirectory. The path is configuredRoot/private.key,or /private.key when the configured root is empty. These doubleword transfer encodings were checked against the NXP e500 manual Appendix B opcode rows for evlddx and evstddx (https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/E500CORERM.pdf). The firmware dataflow,not the manual,supplies the zero-count and path behavior.
key_loading.file_checks_and_failure: The file path buffer is1024 bytes;the loader does not test snprintf's returned length before stat. It requires successful stat and a size comparison>=836 bytes (private708+public128),opens rb,and requires each fread(size708,count1) and fread(size128,count1) to return1. It ignores additional trailing file bytes. Successful file loading overwrites the first private word with0x00040000 from0x10faf078,stores public length128 and returns1. Failed file loading calls ZZ0038 on both private and public areas,clears public length and returns0. A flash payload of adequate size does not fall back to the file merely because its key is empty or fails the later cryptographic parser. The published cache success flag can therefore be true while a subsequent private-key read/parse fails.
key_loading.parsing_and_validation: Caller0x10bb93f4 obtains exactly708 bytes then calls libsonoscrypto.so.3 ZZ0098. Export0x8394 is a semantic tail wrapper to ZZ0183 at0x819c. That allocates a key object and first tries mbedtls_pk_parse_key with the supplied bytes/length. If parsing fails,it calls ZZ0100 at0x8d04,which tail-delegates legacy raw parser0x8ac4. A successful parse must report RSA type1,pass mbedtls_rsa_check_privkey at0x833c and successfully export RSA components at0x8380;failures free the temporary key and return null. Thus cache loading and obtaining a cryptographically usable signing key are separate outcomes.

It imports big-endian MPI byte arrays through mbedtls_mpi_read_binary: N offset4 length128,E offset0x84 length128,D offset0x104 length128,P offset0x184 length64,Q offset0x1c4 length64,DP offset0x204 length64,DQ offset0x244 length64,QP offset0x284 length64. muse_base64_input.call_chain: Nonce wrapper0x10b996b4 calls0x109d1e50,which loads{input pointer,length} and semantically tail-delegates0x109d1d90. That helper allocates3*floor(inputLength/4)+1 output bytes,then calls sonosBase64Decode at0x109d1df8. On success it resizes the output std::string to the returned decoded length. It uses the standard decoder,not sonosBase64UrlDecode.
muse_base64_input.state_and_alphabet: libsonosminiutils.so.1 sonosBase64Decode0x55d0 resets a10-byte decode state through0x513c: pending count+4=0,valid byte+8=1,URL-mode byte+9=0. One-shot body0x5388 calls stream update0x5230 and final validity0x5190. Character mapper0x48b0 accepts A-Z,a-z,0-9,+,/ in standard mode;it explicitly rejects - and _. Invalid characters clear valid+8. Quartet pending bytes occupy state+0..3. The low-byte arithmetic at0x48d0/0x4940/0x4954/0x4960 is rlwinm masking,not the disassembler's shift-like rendering.
muse_base64_input.whitespace_and_nul: Stream update0x5230 skips bytes whose current __ctype_b_loc classification has whitespace bit0x20. It stops at input length or the first NUL byte;it does not require consuming the entire declared span after that NUL. A complete valid prefix followed by NUL and arbitrary trailing bytes can therefore decode successfully. Empty or whitespace-only input produces an empty decoded string with valid base64 state;the subsequent JSON layer still must accept the decoded bytes.
muse_base64_input.padding_and_finalization: Standard one-shot decode rejects a nonempty pending tail at0x542c,so non-whitespace input must finish in complete quartets. URL-only unpadded-tail logic at0x53e0..0x5470 is not selected for this nonce call. Quartet decoder0x496c permits = in the third/fourth positions with the expected one-/two-byte output shape;= in either first position is invalid,and a third-position = with a non-= fourth byte is invalid. It does not test discarded low bits of the last data character for canonical zero values. Thus TR== and TQ== both produce the byte M;TWF= and TWE= both produce Ma. These are static arithmetic examples,not a live-device experiment.
muse_base64_input.padding_does_not_end_stream: After a valid padded quartet,the decoder resets pending count+4 to0 at0x4a5c and preserves valid+8;it does not mark an end-of-stream state. It therefore accepts another complete quartet after padding,e.g.TQ==TQ== decodes to MM. Such bytes still have to form the required JSON envelope and pass current credentials/nonce validation;base64 permissiveness is not authentication success.
muse_base64_input.errors: Invalid alphabet,invalid quartet shape or insufficient output capacity clears valid+8. Partial output may have been written before the failure. The nonce wrapper rejects a false decode result with code4 and does not enter cached-nonce matching/consumption for that input. The caller buffer-size calculation depends on declared encoded length,not on the number of non-whitespace characters.

muse_json_envelope.parser_chain: After successful standard-base64 decoding,0x10b99264 passes the decoded std::string to0x109d0588 at0x10b992e4. That wrapper uses only the string data pointer at0x109d05a8,not its declared length. It skips JSON whitespace through0x104463c8,parses one value through0x10447a78,skips trailing whitespace and requires the current byte to be NUL at0x109d0648/0x109d064c. No scanf skeleton or XML parser is used.
muse_json_envelope.whitespace_and_structure: Whitespace helper0x104463c8 uses bitmap0x00800013 indexed by (byte-9)&0xff;the recognized bytes are9(tab),10(LF),13(CR),32(space). Raw0x5529063e at0x104463f0 is the low-byte mask,not a shift. Object reader0x10447d34 requires quoted keys,colons and comma-separated values;its member storage is32-byte{name16-byte value,value16-byte value} pairs. It recursively parses other member values and preserves their insertion order. A trailing object comma requires another quoted key and fails when followed by}. muse_json_envelope.required_fields: 0x10b99420 and0x10b994b8 extract exact lowercase credentials and nonce through0x109cffd4 with required=true. Wrapper0x109cffd4 invokes typed getter0x109ce584 with a std::string output and no numeric/boolean output. A missing field returns status3 in the typed layer; a present field without the string flag0x400 at value+0xe returns status4. No scalar coercion is performed. An object with both required string fields is therefore needed for this envelope;an array or other root does not provide those named members. Empty field strings are syntactically accepted,with actual credential/nonce matching assessed later. No nonce-specific min/max string length is applied here. keyType is neither required nor inspected,and other members are ignored by this authentication layer only after the whole JSON value has parsed.
muse_json_envelope.name_matching_and_duplicates: Typed getter constructs /credentials or /nonce and traverses the object using name length and memcmp at0x109ce8cc..0x109ce8e8. The object loop stores every parsed member pair and performs no duplicate-name check;lookup scans from the first pair and takes the first exact match at0x109ce8f4. Duplicate fields are therefore first-wins,not last-wins. If the first occurrence has a wrong type,a later correct string does not repair it. Keys are compared after escape decoding,so an escaped spelling such as \u006eonce can name the nonce field;matching remains case-sensitive and byte-exact.
muse_json_envelope.string_lexical_rules: String reader0x10447070 rejects unescaped bytes0x00..0x1f and requires a closing quote. Escape table0x10ecf7f4 maps quote,slash,backslash,b,f,n,r,t;other escape letters reject except u,which requires four hexadecimal digits. The Unicode path0x104474dc..0x1044778c accepts upper/lower hex,UTF-8-encodes BMP values,and requires a high surrogateD800..DBFF to be followed by \uDC00..DFFF. Isolated low surrogates or invalid pairs reject. Raw cmplwi0x2b9fdbff at0x10447690 uses the unsigned immediateDBFF,not the disassembler's negative text. Ordinary unescaped bytes>=0x20 (other than quote/backslash handling) are copied directly at0x10447120;this instantiation does not validate raw multibyte UTF-8 sequences there. Raw0x7d1c5051 at0x1044710c is record-form subf. for capacity,which supplies the subsequent buffer-growth branch and is not a character-validity predicate.
muse_json_envelope.embedded_nul_in_fields: Unicode escape \u0000 is admitted by the string reader and stored as a NUL byte within the DOM string. The typed string getter0x109ce78c chooses inline or allocated string storage,then calls strlen at0x109ce7a0 rather than using the DOM's stored length. credentials and nonce extraction therefore truncates at the first decoded NUL. A valid stored nonce followed by \u0000 and a suffix yields the nonce prefix to matching. Member-name matching instead uses the stored name length and memcmp,so a name with a NUL suffix is not automatically treated as the bare required name.
muse_json_envelope.error_and_consumption_boundary: Syntax/whole-value parse errors return a failed envelope from0x10b99264;missing or wrong-type required fields do likewise.0x10b996b4 returns auth result4 when that envelope result is absent. These cases precede current-credential checking and cache lookup and do not consume a nonce. A successfully decoded object still must pass current credentials and peer-address/nonce matching;JSON acceptance alone is not authentication. The outbound signing helper's256/100-byte limits do not apply as inbound Muse field limits.

noncehandler.completion_basis: Per-record audit: the formerly opaque provider is joined from live initialization to its concrete time/context predicates;expiry writers and both boundary predicates are raw-word checked;address setter/getter/producers and independent inet_aton consumer establish cache identity and byte domain;store/prune/consume/clear and all result paths are traced;actual base64 and JSON lexer/accessor paths establish alphabet,termination,escaping,type/duplicate behavior;the separate signer's MAC input,SHA-1/RSA format,buffer guards and flash/file/private-key parser chain are instruction-bound. Dynamic address/key/root values are described by their producers and domains;no live device observation is claimed.

arping.impl: arping.cxx: 0x140-byte select-handler manager, 0x50-byte per-probe request and 18-byte meaningful result
arping.semantics: Concurrent local Ethernet/IPv4 ARP probing, scheduled retries and deadlines, asynchronous callback or compiled synchronous result delivery. This lower packet manager uses a supplied select-thread owner, not its own worker thread.
arping.description:
Checks which hardware address is using a local-network IP address by sending ARP queries. A caller supplies the target IP, the spacing between probes and how long the attempt may run. The manager can keep several attempts pending on one packet socket and return a success record containing the observed IP, MAC address and reception time, or an empty failure record when an attempt expires or the socket is reset. An asynchronous caller receives a callback; the compiled synchronous interface waits for completion and returns the same record.

The important quirk is what counts as evidence: the receiver accepts either an ARP query or an ARP reply sent by the target IP. It does not require a reply addressed to this speaker or check the sender MAC against the expected player identity. The topology callback performs that second comparison, so observing traffic from an IP and confirming the expected speaker are separate steps. A single packet can finish several attempts for the same IP. A socket error resets pending work, and a brief reset-pending state can refuse a new asynchronous attempt. This primitive checks local address reachability; it does not authenticate Wi-Fi association or prove that a reachable speaker can play audio.

It allocates a0x50-byte request with synchronous=0, zero high words for interval/duration, and under the manager mutex rejects needsReset+4!=0, deleting the request. arping.wire_emit: 0x105862d4 sends a42-byte Ethernet+ARP frame from sp+0x42 using sendto(fd,buffer,0x2a,0,&manager.sockaddr_ll,0x14). Wire layout: bytes0..5 broadcast ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff from constant0x10ef008c;6..11 local MAC;12..13 EtherType0x0806;14..15 hardware type1;16..17 protocol type0x0800;18 hardware length6;19 protocol length4;20..21 opcode1;22..27 sender/local MAC;28..31 sender/local IPv4;32..37 target hardware address also broadcast ff bytes;38..41 requested target IPv4. u16/u32 fields are emitted in network order on PPC. A sendto result-1 stores errno+0x2c and sets resetAll+0x138 and needsReset+4; other returns are not checked for an exact42-byte send.
arping.wire_acceptance: Read-ready0x10586f08 calls recv(fd,sp+0x52,42,0x40). It requires the returned count==42, EtherType0x0806,ARP hardware type1,protocol type0x0800,hlen6,plen4 and opcode1 or2. Raw0x5529043e at0x10587080 masks (opcode-1) to low16, then unsigned comparison at0x10587084 accepts<=1; the local disassembler's srwi label is incorrect. This is requests and replies, not replies only. A frame longer than42 can supply its first42 bytes because recv does not request MSG_TRUNC; a short frame is ignored. No Ethernet source/destination consistency,ARP target-IP or target-MAC check,receive-interface check or expected-player-MAC check occurs in this handler. It matches the ARP sender IPv4 at bytes28..31 to each request.target+0x14; all matching pending requests receive the same observed MAC from bytes22..27 and can complete. It checks no expiry timestamp on this receive path, so removal by scheduled-work processing is separate from packet matching.
arping.result_format: 18 meaningful bytes in20-byte aligned storage: +0 valid byte (0=empty failure,1=observed packet),+1..+3 padding,+4 native u32 clock-id1 reception seconds,+8 four network-order sender-IP bytes,+0xc six sender-MAC bytes. Empty-result initializer0x105858c0 clears valid,time,IP and MAC, but does not initialize padding. Constructor0x10585934 fills the same fields. Receive0x10587100 reads reception time;0x10587128..0x10587198 writes request.result then completion0x105864a4 delivers it. No error-kind enum is embedded in a failure result; the manager errno getter is a separate channel.
arping.scheduling: Per-request tick0x10585c8c converts clock-id1 timeval to milliseconds. A request remains live iff expiry>now (strict unsigned64 comparison); expiry==now completes with an empty result. For live requests, nextSend<=now sets the send-due output and advances nextSend by exactly one interval, not a loop that jumps directly past now. It returns timeout=max(0,min(nextSend,expiry)-now), split into seconds and microseconds through division/remainder by1000. Manager work0x105867a4 visits the linked list, completes expired requests, sends due requests and chooses the minimum remaining timeout through timevalMinimize. Timeout0x10586e54 invokes that work under the mutex. Enqueue invokes it before an explicit send, so a new still-live request can send twice initially. Zero duration can complete during insertion before the later explicit-send path; this code has no minimum-duration guard. These are instruction-level behaviors, not a runtime packet-count experiment.
arping.completion_and_reset: Completion0x105864a4 unlinks a queued request, repairs head/tail/next/prev, decrements count and clears its links. Asynchronous mode invokes callback(cookie,&result) when nonnull then request vtable+4 deletes it. Synchronous mode sets done+0x11=1 and signals condition+0xe8, leaving deletion to the waiter. If the list empties, select interface slot+0x18 receives null timeout and needsReset+4 becomes1. Reset0x1058720c cancels all requests with empty results only when resetAll+0x138 is set, then clears that flag, closes the socket and clears needsReset; ordinary last-request cleanup also closes the socket. Receive result-1 stores errno; errno11 (EAGAIN) leaves pending work and reset flags alone, while other errno values set both flags. Result delivery is under the manager's recursive mutex. Requests have no separate cancellation-name operation in this lower class.
arping.callers_and_identity: Player constructor0x1018fac8 calls manager ctor0x10585ecc with interface-name literal br0 at0x10e75170. Whole-.text direct/unconditional/conditional-tail scan found one asynchronous starter caller, topology0x1074124c, using interval300ms,duration1000ms,callback0x1073ea64,cookie=topology owner. No caller,aligned non-text function pointer,or lis/low address formation was found for compiled synchronous entry0x10586c3c or async factory0x10585b48. This documents their compiled semantics without claiming an active call path. Topology callback0x1073ea64 checks result.valid; formats result.IP+8, parses observed MAC+0xc, finds active or vanished devices by IP and compares expected MAC through0x10551d04 at0x1073ebc8/0x1073ec70. Only the appropriate match reaches successful-active/successful-vanished branches; mismatch logs0x10f1263c,empty result logs arping unsuccessful. A packet seen from an IP is therefore not independently authenticated by this primitive.
arping.scope_correction: The earlier scheduling paragraph merged distinct objects: writes at0x1058940c to+0xf9/+0xfc/+0x104 and the0x10588xxx query family belong to a separate monitor object,not the0x140-byte packet manager above (+0xf9 is inside this manager's condition-variable storage). Those offsets are not fields or scheduling APIs of this primitive. The packet manager is driven by the supplied select interface and its readiness/timeout/reset callbacks. ArpChecker is also separate: its watched fd is a local wakeup pipe,and its temporary socket performs SIOCGARP cache queries. See select_thread and arp_assoc for that concrete producer chain. Controller-association telemetry has its own record.

Registration0x10c5d20c stores the thread in handler+8 at0x10c5d290, initializes cached watched fd+c=-1 at0x10c5d370 and eventMask+0x10=0 at0x10c5d378. Its19 slots hold handlers at thread+4+i*4,callback-label pointers at+0x50+i*4 and timeout pairs at+0x9c+i*8. muse_authhelper.thor_eval: Thor op gating decoded end to end. Static-init f_1008e190 registers the named singletons 'UserAuthorization' (object 0x110a6d98) and 'ThorOperations' (0x110a6e30), a named 'PolicyKeyTableMutex', the 'museauth' log domain, and the URN 'urn:dev:ops:44974-zp-'. Ops dispatch into the UserAuthorization object through vtable 0x10ef9774: slot+0x10 f_10601ecc is the offline guest path (logs 'Using guest policy for offline mode'), slot+0x14 f_10602014 is the mTLS path (logs 'Using mTLS policy', pre-sets result bytes +0x6=1 and +0xc=3), slot+0x18 f_10605544 is the credential gate, and slot+0x1c f_10606644 is the policy-key op path. f_10605544 parses envelope tags 4 and 5 (f_109ed0a8) into flag bytes at result+0x28/+0x29 and copies credType (ctx+0) to result+0xc. When its guest-mode arg is set, credType==1 means an unauthenticated guest: flag byte 0 denies with 'Unauthenticated control disallowed' (status code 3 in the error out-param). Other credTypes route through f_10604af0, which serializes the caller credential via ctx vfunc+0x28 into a 0x204-byte blob and enforces credential-type slots (compares against 2 and 4) plus the ctx+0x28 flag, denying with 'Credential is not allowed' or 'Guest access disallowed' (status 3); success falls into f_10600824. With no guest arg the op takes the offline path: flag byte must be 0, then f_10601d7c looks up a policy object by a fixed 16-byte key (rodata 0x10ef97b0) in the locked map at 0x110a86b8 before the same f_10600824 allow check, logging 'Using guest policy' on success. f_10606644 gates by op-descriptor policy key: when descriptor+0x30 is set it calls role resolver f_10606170, otherwise it invokes the context object's vfunc+0 directly and denies with 'Permissions are insufficient' (status 3) on a zero result. f_10606170 resolves the role for a policy key: a cached policy blob under this+0x2c or a lechmere fetch via f_10603194 supplies the policy, the resolved role string is logged at level 6 'Role from policy key: %s', a missing policy yields 'Could not fetch policy' and an unparseable lechmere reply yields 'Could not parse role from lechmere policy key' (both status 3), and success again ends at f_10600824. f_10600824 is the terminal allow: with a context object it calls the context vfunc+0 predicate through delegate f_105ffbdc and denies 'Permissions are insufficient' on 0; with no context it computes (required_bits arg4 & ~granted_mask) == 0 where the granted mask comes from f_109d8e70(arg5), so an op is allowed only when every required permission bit is granted. The allow byte is written to out+1. f_106058d4 is the PolicyKeyTable cache lookup: it builds a composite key from the op's policy-key string (split at '-') and walks two map regions under locks 0x110a76b0/0x110a76a8; a hit stores the mapped role code to out+0x1c and logs 'Policy mapping retrieved from cache' at level 7. Cache state invalidates via the ie-obs observers f_1008e190 subscribes (TopologyZpListChangedEvent/InfoUpdatedEvent). 'validateUserAuthorization violation' remains a dead literal; the live denial strings are the role gates and status-3 writes above.
resolved_findings: Established: policy key -> role mapping under PolicyKeyTableMutex with cache; role gates {guest,unauthenticated}; JWT + registration-state checks; topology/info-change cache invalidation via ie-obs observers.

Established: ops reach Thor through the UserAuthorization singleton vtable 0x10ef9774; slots +0x10/+0x14 are the offline-guest and mTLS entry points, +0x18 is the credential gate f_10605544, +0x1c is the policy-key op path f_10606644.

Established: policy-key ops resolve their role through f_10606170 using a cached policy or the lechmere fetch f_10603194, with a PolicyKeyTable cache lookup f_106058d4 under two map locks logging 'Policy mapping retrieved from cache'; misses produce 'Could not fetch policy'/'Could not parse role from lechmere policy key' status 3.

Established: every path ends at f_10600824, which allows via a context vfunc+0 predicate or a required-vs-granted permission-bitmask check (f_109d8e70), denying with 'Permissions are insufficient' status 3.

upnp_eventing_impl.files: upnpeventing_sender.cxx and upnpeventing_source.cxx, with service/provider integration. Sender scheduling, source data production and per-subscription transport are separate layers.
upnp_eventing_impl.sender_queue: f_10678c50 takes the sender lock, sets byte +0x10e and signals its condition variable. This is pending list/work-change state, not a dedup-enable flag. The sender loop f_10679b14 clears that byte, applies pending source removals through f_10679678, snapshots the source-pointer vector [+0x110,+0x114) and releases the lock before calling sources. Removal compares pointer identity and compacts the live list; memmove copies the snapshot in bytes. The 0x3fffffff comparison bounds a shifted element count for allocation, not a time window. Empty vectors skip source processing; termination and wake/timed-wait paths are explicit.
upnp_eventing_impl.source_scheduling: Before readiness testing, f_10679b14 checks each pointer in its active-list snapshot against current pending removals. Empty pending lists bypass search. f_1067a9f0 returns the matching iterator or pending end: equality with end at 0x10679cf8 branches to readiness, while a found match falls through to skip. This also prevents a source removed after the snapshot from being collected in that pass. For remaining sources, f_1067d028 determines readiness. A zero last-send timeval from source virtual +0x10 goes directly to f_10683da0. Otherwise elapsed milliseconds are subtracted from the minimum spacing returned through virtual +0xc; a positive remainder contributes a later deadline, while a due source is collected. The default interval f_100c9bbc returns zero. A remainder greater than 1000 ms takes a warning/fallback branch. The logged ddim is this scheduling delta, not a byte span or deduplication window.
upnp_eventing_impl.feature_flag: enableUPnPEventingGNDOptimization is present as a configuration/schema boolean. f_10a581b0 reads config byte +0xec1 and calls f_109d14e0 with its name; that helper writes a property name followed by literal true or false through an output interface. This is serialization, not evidence of a settings setter or a notify-time getter. Direct accesses to +0xec1 in this image belong to construction, copy, equality and serialization in f_10a56e7c/f_10a5702c/f_10a575f0/f_10a57aa0/f_10a581b0. Neither this reference nor the LocalSettingsEventing completion API establishes a GENA same-setting/in-flight coalescing implementation. The previous expansion of GND as GENA Notify Dedup, runtime flag linkage, identical-wire guarantee and fewer-NOTIFY claim were unsupported and are not part of this contract.
upnp_eventing_impl.subscription_transport: f_10683da0 walks eligible source subscriptions and drives notification transport; source and connection state can defer or skip work. Instrumentation f_1067ba44 emits success/failure, first-try/retry, connect/handshake/read/write/timeout counts and handshake/round-trip averages, with zero-count branches for averages. These are measured counters, not promises of unlimited retries or exactly-once delivery. HTTP subscription authorization in f_1068faa4 has a denied branch that returns status 403. f_10693df4 reads separate main, connect and eventing timeout settings and reports their effective values. Source property production is conditional: f_10683da0 groups subscriptions by name and invokes source virtual +0x18 at 0x1068406c only on its eligible populated-group path. Static reachability does not establish a live subscriber, successful wire delivery or WSS publication.
upnp_eventing_impl.status_xml: f_1067c980 and surrounding status writer emit Service name/current/max rows and Subscription children with EventKey, NotifyErrors, SubscriptionID and NotificationAddr. NotificationAddr is either a normal address string or wss://host:port (muse); IsSecure is emitted separately. These diagnostic rows describe active subscription state, not an additional subscription wire protocol. Sender counter fields are countEventsSuccess, countEventsFailure, countEventsSuccessFirstTry, countEventsSuccessRetry, countFailuresRetry, countFailuresConnect, countFailuresHandshake, countFailuresRead, countFailuresWrite, countFailuresTimeout, avgHandshakeTimeMsOnSuccess/Failure and avgRoundTripTimeMsOnSuccess/Failure.
upnp_eventing_impl.peer_compatibility: f_10763f90 extracts peer version bytes, evaluates major/minor compatibility branches including 85/86/89/94, and selects secure versus insecure eventing. It also consults owner/service capability state and writes interface flags; the result is not a simple major >=89 rule. Secure and legacy modes coexist. The discovery diagnostic alone does not establish encryption for every subscription or tie compatibility selection to the GND configuration field.

evidence.notes: Pending flag set plus condition signal, clear after wake, pointer-identity removals and snapshot allocation/copy. Raw shift at 0x10679be4 precedes comparison with 0x3fffffff; memmove gets byte count r28, not span>>2.

Source timeval zero check, 64-bit current-minus-source calculation, divide by 1000, interval-minus-elapsed and positive-delay scheduling. The actual ddim formatting arguments come from this calculation; buffer pointers are not its source. 1000-ms warning branch disproves the old no-timing-constant reasoning.

Named boolean is written through an output interface as true/false, not installed through a generic settings setter. Exhaustive direct lbz/stb +0xec1 scan finds only config-object construction/copy/equality/serialization. No live GND-to-sender coalescing data flow is demonstrated.
Subscription iteration, eligibility/transport paths and actual counter/average serialization, including empty/zero-count handling. Counter labels do not prove retry policy or deduplication.
Direct XML output calls for Service, Subscription, key/error/id, ordinary versus WSS muse address, and IsSecure fields. Removes unrelated guessed status grammar.

Reachable subscription-denied 403, separate timeout loads and diagnostic, and multi-branch major/minor peer compatibility/capability selection. Does not conflate generic LocalSettingsEventing methods with GENA sender behavior.

Shared-owner registration appends active pointer and retains owner; raw registration appends only pointer. Removal requests append +0x128; consumer compacts active and owner lists and clears pending vector. This disconfirms interpreting the removal-request helper as registration.

Snapshot uses active +0x110/+0x114. Before readiness, search current pending removals; absent iterator equals pending end and BEQ at 0x10679cfc reaches readiness. Found entries skip; empty vectors bypass search. Raw 0x7f895000 at 0x10679cf8 compares end with returned iterator, and raw 0x419e00a0 branches on equality.
Subscription grouping/eligibility gates source virtual +0x18. Conditional source property production is distinct from successful wire transport.

upnp_eventing_impl.source_registration: Sender +0x110/+0x114/+0x118 is the active raw source-pointer vector, not notification data or a deduplication window. f_1067938c appends the source pointer there and retains its shared owner separately in +0x11c/+0x120/+0x124. f_106795b4 appends a raw source without retaining that shared owner. Both registration forms check shutdown byte +0x10d. In contrast, f_106794f0 appends to pending-removal vector +0x128/+0x12c/+0x130; it is not source registration. f_10679678 removes matching pointers from the active list and retained owners, then resets the pending end to its begin. Empty pending lists leave the active list unchanged.

audioin_impl.impl_contract: ai_impl_base (f_102926ac/27f8/2eb8) supplies the shared AudioIn machinery: a zone-group tracker ('Adding group with coord %s demoMode %d' / 'Removing group with coord %s' - impls track groups keyed by coordinator UUID with a demoMode flag) and a WORKER THREAD, f_10292eb8: mutex +0x58, run flag +0x1d8, blocks on condvar +0xe8 and on each wake calls VFUNC +0x20 - the single per-tick process slot each derived impl must fill. ai_spotify (zoneplayer/spotify/ai_spotify.cxx, fns f_104dbe84/4dc4a4/4dd600/4dd744+) is the Spotify Connect impl: its internals handle transport ('Pausing track, offset %u ms') and stream transitions ('Logical Track Boundary') under tag 'spot'. audiotap.semantics: Bounded DSP tap attachment plus a25MB rolling SPDIF capture whose snapshots are always zlib-compressed before export.
audiotap.description: Diagnostic taps capture selected audio-processing locations without making them live network streams. The manager normally permits two taps and rejects duplicate or ineligible locations. A separate rolling SPDIF recorder keeps recent input, compresses a snapshot and can export it inside an XML element.
audiotap.manager: Constructor0x10d91ea8 initializes three descriptor blocks at offsets0,0xc0,0x180, capacity+0x240=2, used+0x244=0, mutex+0x248 named audiotapmanager, and source pointers at each block+0xb8=0. Setter0x10d91f74 accepts unsigned capacity0..3 inclusive; only>3 rejects. This corrects the earlier >=3 claim. There are three physical blocks, with a default maximum of two.
audiotap.attachment: 0x10d92300 locks, cleans stale descriptors, and calls source vtable+0xc for eligibility (default0x105364c0 is the accepted fast path).0x10d921bc rejects matching source-name strings from source vtable+8. Capacity exhaustion rejects; otherwise find first block whose source pointer+0xb8 is0, store source there, store descriptor pointer in source+4, increment used and return descriptor. Tappability is a property of the source, not manager+0xb8. Block array begins+0, not+0x178; +0x178 is the second block's source pointer.
audiotap.cleanup: 0x10d92024 scans the configured-capacity prefix. A descriptor with reference/activity count+0xa0=0 is stale: clear source+4 and descriptor+0xb8 and log Closing Tap. Nonzero count is retained/logged Active Tap and contributes to recomputed used count.0x10d91fec detaches all three physical source pointers irrespective of capacity. Lowering capacity does not itself detach blocks outside the new prefix. Requests0..3 are accepted without a used-count floor.
audiotap.dsp_locations: DSP controller0x10d72bb8 handles dspout as a dedicated output tap, configured through0x10535248. Other location paths are dot-separated; it uses the last token to locate a DSP block through0x10d681ac, then calls the manager attachment path. Missing block logs Block to tap not found under %s. healthcheck.description: The player maintains a diagnostic-check deadline, normally one day ahead, and lets update scheduling or group changes move it. assoctracker.semantics: Correlates controller discovery and connection progress by IPv4 address, then reports a bounded30-second CrAssoc diagnostic record.
assoctracker.description: The player watches a controller's early discovery requests, ARP reachability, device-description requests, zone-state requests and group notifications. It combines them into a short connection-health report. This measures a controller finding and connecting to the player, not a Wi-Fi station authenticating with an access point.

Each record has IPv4 key+0 (zero=free), five16-byte phase structures at+4,+0x14,+0x24,+0x34,+0x44, copied28-byte M-SEARCH context+0x54, ARP result byte+0x70, maximum ARP failures+0x74, ZGT success byte+0x78, zone-state+0x7c, validity byte+0x80 initialized1, distinct MAC count+0x84 and four6-byte MACs+0x88, cached controller model+0xa0=-1, reply successes+0xa4=0, reply failures+0xa8=0, last failure+0xac=0. Record constructor0x105874bc zeroes phase timestamps/counts, resets context integer sentinels to-1 and clears MAC bytes. Reset0x10587648 reconstructs/copies the full record.
assoctracker.start_and_expiry: 0x1058808c accepts M-SEARCH context only when signed session-seconds context+0x14>=0 (0x10555708). It sweeps expired records, finds matching IP, or allocates the first free of four only if session seconds<=10 (0x105556e8 tests>10). Full table or missing/negative session age produces no new record. Existing records accept later session ages. IP0 remains the free sentinel. Each M-SEARCH stamps phase+4, copies context, and caches model when>=0. Context+0x10/+0x14/+0x18 comes from decimal X-SONOS-SESSIONRETRIES/SESSIONSECONDS/MDPMODEL parsed by0x10555a54; these are not a media-server session state.0x10587fc4 expires only when first M-SEARCH time+30<now, reports then resets regardless of upload result. Phase activity does not extend that first-time deadline.
assoctracker.phase_engine: 0x105873e8 sets first timestamp only if zero, always sets last timestamp, increments count and schedules sweep callback0x1058863c for current seconds+30 through global timedjob manager slot+0xc. Each mutation is under+0x2c8; sweep is also exposed through0x105885d4. Callback resolves the tracker from player slot+0xc0, sweeps and returns INT_MAX as its next-job deadline. No polling thread or external station-association vtable exists inside the tracker.
assoctracker.writers: M-SEARCH caller0x1057f56c supplies source IPv4 and parsed context.0x10587cd0 records M-SEARCH reply success when result0, otherwise increments failure count and retains last error.0x10587d84 deduplicates6-byte MACs and stores at most4; it only records ARP stuffing, while caller0x1057f03c performs the actual SIOCSARP0x8955 operation.0x10588268 stamps ARP phase only while result byte is0, ORs result byte on that first path, and stores max(previousFailures,callerFailures); resolved-ARP caller0x10584ec0 passes result1.0x10588348 stamps device-description phase; caller0x105e987c.0x105883e4 stamps zone-state phase; caller0x1067eb3c.0x10588480 accepts ZGT notification only after description count, zone-state count and ARP result are nonzero; then stamps notification phase and stores zone state/success. Otherwise clears validity+0x80 permanently until reset and logs invalid event; caller0x1068346c.
assoctracker.report_schema: 0x10587798 requires uploader nonnull, latest session-seconds>10, and validity byte1. It builds CrAssoc with addr (inet_ntop, fallback0.0.0.0), optional crm (cached model!=-1), optional mssr (session retries>=0), msss (session seconds), mstime1/mstime2/msnum (M-SEARCH first/last/count), msrs (reply successes), optional msrf/msre when failure count!=0, optional arpscstime (ARP last time when result byte nonzero), arpatt (max failures), arpscs (ARP result Boolean), arpsnum only when distinct MAC count>1. Description phase when first!=0 emits ddtime1/ddtime2/ddnum; zone-state phase similarly zstime1/zstime2/zsnum; notification phase similarly zntime1/zntime2/znnum plus znscs and znstate. It submits through0x1055c248(uploader,CrAssoc,map,1). There is no tracker-owned retry queue; consent and delivery policy belong to the uploader.

Missing stages are omitted from CrAssoc rather than invented as failures. All four records can be discarded on expiry even if consent filtering or upload preparation refuses the report. reporting_policy.semantics: Consent policy is applied per reporter and per operation, with strict submission, permissive collection, explicit bypass reporters and independent event masks.
reporting_policy.description: Applies collection and submission policy separately for each reporting channel. Ordinary event collectors check the selected event category and stop accepting new optional records when usage sharing is refused; while the sharing cache is unread they can still buffer events. Ordinary upload routines send a batch only when the cache says allow. Two configured reporters bypass that consent-state check. Some diagnostics still submit after refusal but omit selected fields such as line-in name, boot sequence or status-light setting. The periodic usage-statistics sender clears pending counters before checking consent, so a refused batch can be discarded instead of saved for later. These local rules do not establish what the server retains.

Protobuf collection 0x1055c254 applies the same predicates. Text submission 0x1055b9ec requires bypass OR strict consent, allocated buffer +0xc and pending byte +0x44. Protobuf submission 0x1055d024 requires bypass OR strict consent and nonempty protobuf storage at +0x168. Transport availability, event-class selection and scheduling remain independent of consent.
reporting_policy.bypass_producers: Uploader constructor 0x1055a384 initializes bypass byte +0x43=0 and class mask +0x30=1. Setter 0x1055a66c writes the caller byte directly. Reporting owner 0x1069d87c constructs four reporters at +0x12c48, +0x12e48, +0x13048, +0x13248. Callsites 0x1069dbc8/0x1069dbe0 set bypass=1 on the second and third; their constructor selectors at +0x158 are respectively 2 and 1. First/fourth remain ordinary consent-gated reporters. +0x41 independently controls retained-buffer behavior, not consent.
reporting_policy.refresh_correction: 0x10707914 returns the singleton pointer DAT_11097918; it is not an enabled predicate. 0x10707cd4 refreshes R_CustomerID and UMTracking and optionally logs a consent change; it returns no allow/deny result. 0x105c9f94 and 0x1066b320 call this refresher if the singleton exists and continue preparing/submitting their report. Neither has the previously claimed early consent-return branch.
reporting_policy.other_policy: Usage metrics 0x1070aa1c drains/reset its accumulated event slots and counters under +0x150 before strict consent at 0x1070ac28; denied batches are not automatically retained there. 0x10695310 and 0x101979a8 use permissive consent to omit selected identifying/configuration fields, rather than cancelling the entire diagnostic report. 0x104ca970 allows playReport if permissive consent OR service id 0x12f. 0x105eb628 uses strict consent when deciding handling of event_reporter_v3 files. This record describes local enforcement, not remote retention or cloud policy.

sounddev.description: These audio paths convert samples to the player's output timing and adjust for clock differences. They use one common filter table, even on the path labelled Hi-Res. ssdp_discovery.wire: IPv4 SSDP uses 239.255.255.250:1900. M-SEARCH requests contain MAN: "ssdp:discover", MX, ST and USER-AGENT; NOTIFY advertises alive/byebye, and a unicast HTTP/1.1 200 OK response answers a search. These are distinct message forms, not one common header set.

outbound_templates.alive: 0x10eef678, emitted by f_1057c9a8: NOTIFY, HOST, CACHE-CONTROL max-age, LOCATION, NT, NTS:ssdp:alive, SERVER, USN and caller-provided extension trailer.
outbound_templates.byebye: 0x10eef5fc, emitted by f_1057c7e4: NOTIFY, HOST, NT, NTS:ssdp:byebye, SERVER, USN and extension trailer. No CACHE-CONTROL or LOCATION in this template.
outbound_templates.response: 0x10eef97c, emitted by f_1057f03c: HTTP/1.1 200 OK, CACHE-CONTROL max-age, EXT, LOCATION, SERVER, ST, USN and extension trailer. Formatting bounds and socket-write errors are checked.
outbound_templates.search: f_105568e4 uses template 0x10eea4f4, optionally adds a household header, optionally computes/appends X-SONOS-SIG, terminates the header block and sends through f_105566d8. An invalid socket, buffer overflow, requested-signature failure or append failure prevents that send. A generic %s extension trailer in the other templates does not establish a signature.

ssdp_discovery.receive: f_10555a54 receives at most 2047 bytes with recvmsg, preserves a raw copy, splits CR/LF lines and compares header names case-insensitively. NOTIFY/HTTP-response parsing and M-SEARCH parsing are separate branches. Vocabulary includes USN, LOCATION, CACHE-CONTROL, HOST, SERVER, ST, NTS, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD/BOOTSEQ/PROXY/VARIANT/REASON, X-SONOS-DEVICEID/SESSIONRETRIES/SESSIONSECONDS/MDPMODEL, USER-AGENT, X-SONOS-SIG, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION and HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO. Parsed retry/seconds values use decimal strtol; they are not the separately prefixed signature words. Missing ST or a missing registered callback prevents search dispatch.
ssdp_discovery.signature: The reached M-SEARCH path uses HMAC-SHA256, not SHA1: f_105558b0 hashes two native big-endian four-byte IPv4 words followed by the supplied raw message prefix, then base64-encodes 32 digest bytes (44 characters). Outbound words are handler+0x28 and the pointed-to destination argument; receive words are recvmsg source IPv4 and ancillary destination IPv4. The raw prefix ends immediately before X-SONOS-SIG, rather than being reconstructed from selected parsed fields. Verification recomputes the base64 value and compares equal-length text through ZZ0199. The signer rejects absent key pointer/length, absent or empty input, absent output and capacity <=44, and reports initialization/base64 failures.
ssdp_discovery.signature_policy: Signing is conditional, not universal SSDP authentication. f_105568e4 requests a signature only for a non-null destination-word pointer: the peer-expiry probe at 0x105e7cb8 supplies it, whereas ZonePlayer/ContentDirectory discovery at 0x10741afc/0x10741b34 passes null. The receiver marks a packet as requiring verification when ancillary IPv4 destination is neither 239.255.255.250 nor 255.255.255.255. That unicast branch suppresses callback dispatch for missing/invalid signatures; the multicast/no-identified-unicast branch does not impose that check. This is not evidence that alive/byebye or every search response is signed.
ssdp_discovery.key_provenance: Handler configuration f_1055588c stores key pointer/length at +0x20/+0x24 and local address word at +0x28. Startup and interface-change paths install the 16-byte buffer at 0x110a9044, not the registration IPC credential. f_1066134c derives it with ZZ0215 using label SIGN, the supplied optional string context and seed bytes; its startup caller at 0x10198820 supplies the string held at stack+0x154 and 16 seed bytes from application+0xa68. The adjacent HHDK derivation writes a different 16-byte buffer at 0x110a9034. Both buffers are zero-initialized .bss state. The registration getter f_1064b9f4 and registration verify helper f_1065a7a4 are a separate call chain and do not establish this SSDP key.
ssdp_discovery.dispatch_and_lifecycle: MSearchNotifyHandler participates in the selector/reset lifecycle, with explicit setup failure handling. The advertisement worker f_1057f56c (disHandleMSearchAsync) checks target support and whether advertisement has begun before constructing replies, and reports socket-open/send failures separately from successful reply transmission. Peer-expiry handling f_105e7b58 can issue a targeted ZonePlayer M-SEARCH before expiry. Queueing or issuing a probe is not proof that a peer answered.
ssdp_discovery.dual_discovery: Topology defunct handling is source-aware, not packet deduplication. In f_10128e08, peer flags at +0x22e8 and the event source byte at +4 determine whether an MDNS defunct event is ignored for an SSDP-discovered peer, or an SSDP defunct event is ignored for an MDNS-only peer. Other branches continue removal processing. This does not establish universal deduplication of MDNS/SSDP advertisements.
ssdp_discovery.scope: The content-URI prefixes x-rincon-cpcontainer:RDCPA:/RDCPI: are parsed separately by f_100ce82c, not an SSDP container grammar. Signed file-manifest strings and X-Sonos-MS-Sig are not evidence for the X-SONOS-SIG M-SEARCH chain described here.

evidence.notes: Request, alive, byebye and response template references verify distinct header sets and generic extension trailers; bounded format/send branches reject errors.
recvmsg, bounded raw copy, line splitting, separate message classification and case-insensitive extension parsing; retry/seconds parse paths are separate from signature arguments.
Rejects missing inputs or output capacity <=44; HMAC algorithm1, two four-byte updates then raw prefix, finalization and base64 of32 bytes.
Algorithm1 maps to mbedtls MD type9, then initializes HMAC through mbedtls_md_setup/hmac_starts.

Type9 jump-table entry6 reaches0x26c50 and returns descriptor0x4e14c: type9, digest32, block64. SHA256 name is also present at0x4e198; this resolves the actual shipped library algorithm rather than assuming external enum numbering.

Ancillary destination classification controls unicast verification; source/destination IPv4 prefix words and raw-prefix length feed signer; equal-length ZZ0199 compare controls acceptance and registered callback gating.
Targeted expiry probe passes destination pointer; ordinary ZonePlayer/ContentDirectory searches pass null. Requested signature is appended as X-SONOS-SIG; failure aborts send.

SIGN versus HHDK derivations write separate .bss buffers. Four setter callsites install global0x110a9044,length16,local word from f_10749308. Initializer f_10661314 clears32 bytes. No registration-credential getter occurs in this chain.
Selector setup failure, active-advertisement gate, asynchronous dispatch label, socket failure, reply call and success logging establish distinct lifecycle and delivery stages.
Peer flags0x8000/0x4000 and event source byte gate the two defunct suppression cases; other cases continue normal removal.
RDCPA/RDCPI prefix checks are in a content-URI parser, not the SSDP parser.

hls_radio.ops: hls-live, hls-static and hls-??? are diagnostic mode labels; hlsradio, hlsmeta, hlsplaylist and hlsrenditions identify internal components, not separate HTTP endpoints. The hls-%s said diagnostic is local instrumentation, not an established telemetry wire format.
hls_radio.routes: /hls is a local session-status route, registered at 0x110909c4 with handler f_100bacfc. It resolves the requested owner through f_101886e0, then f_10257624 obtains its HLS interface (kind 7) and calls f_103bac70 to write status XML.
hls_radio.status: f_103bac70 emits HLSInfo / HLS Name="Playlist" with HLSVersion, IsStatic, IsEncrypted, TargetDurationSec, CurrentBitRate, TrackEncryptionMethod and TrackEncryptionFormat. f_103bc7fc separately serializes BitrateStreams numBitrates and StreamEntry br, strm, codec, optional segidx, iterating the actual stored ladder; an empty ladder skips entries. These are diagnostic snapshots, not hlsmeta/hlsplaylist control APIs.
hls_radio.live_and_static: f_101473c8 recognizes the x-sonosapi-hls-static: and hls-static: prefixes; f_101475dc recognizes hls-aac://, hls-radio:// and x-sonosapi-hls:. f_10147670 combines those classifications. During media processing ENDLIST selects finite/static processing, while PLAYLIST-TYPE VOD is also recognized, so ENDLIST is not the sole classification criterion. Static fetch processing in f_103ba524 uses finite indices and a computed delay. Live processing maintains media sequence and reference-time/segment mappings with discontinuity handling; it does not establish that every accepted live playlist must supply PROGRAM-DATE-TIME. f_103bb850 searches a bounded 32-entry metadata ring and reports failure when the requested sequence/reference-time mapping is absent.
hls_radio.playlist_engine: f_103be33c parses initial/master playlists and rejects invalid tag sequences. f_103bea88 classifies media lines for VERSION, TARGETDURATION, MEDIA-SEQUENCE, PLAYLIST-TYPE, ENDLIST, PROGRAM-DATE-TIME, EXTINF, KEY, SESSION-KEY, DISCONTINUITY, INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS, MAP and BYTERANGE. The media processor starting at f_103bf128 consumes these results, updates segment/key/map state, resolves relative segment URIs, rejects stale sequences, and permits a map-update exception to stale-data discard. Invalid/empty playlists and processing errors have explicit failure exits. f_104614b4 is another playlist reader, including linkUrl extraction, not the static HLS classifier.
hls_radio.renditions: Stream storage validates bandwidth and codecs against supported capabilities, rejects invalid rendition references and unsupported Atmos/binaural/downmix selections, and can fail when no supported codec remains. Bandwidth parsing uses strtoull, rejecting zero and out-of-range high-word values. f_103c2df0 parses EXT-X-MEDIA attributes, requires a group id and audio type, checks rate/channel attributes, records group/autoselect/channels/URI/name, and handles map insertion failure. f_103c2d18 rejects duplicate group ids. These capability checks do not mean every encoded format mentioned by a playlist is decodable on every device.
hls_radio.adaptation: f_103bcd64 and f_103bcf24 implement bounded lower/higher-bitrate selection over the stored ladder, update the selected index and transition flags and reset a selection counter. The downgrade path stops at the minimum and the upgrade path stops at the maximum; selection also compares the caller-provided threshold against ladder bandwidth. This is not evidence of exponential network retry/backoff or an invariant bitrate list.
hls_radio.encryption: f_103c0364 parses METHOD: AES-128 selects method 1, SAMPLE-AES method 2; an AES/data-URI form also selects method 1, while unsupported/missing methods select 0. It extracts a quoted URI, optional KEYFORMAT and a 16-byte hex IV, marking the IV present only after a complete parse. f_103b8a80 requires a key URI for encrypted content, caches a successful URI and clears it after a failed changed-key fetch; HTTP 403 and 409 have separate error handling. f_103baed0 opens/reads the key with a 2000-ms read deadline: default length 16 if no header length, rejects a declared length greater than 32, and rejects a short read. Success stores validity/length. The segment path can derive an absent IV from the sequence number. SAMPLE-AES supplies the key pointer and a sample-encryption flag to f_1048396c, which retains them at +0x10/+0x28 in the framer adapter. Thus HLS selects and supplies decryption material; recognizing a method is not proof that arbitrary DRM/key formats are supported. Remote key-server authorization is outside the local parser contract.

evidence.notes: Actual /hls handler and owner-to-HLS status dispatch; XML writer, not a family of hlsmeta endpoints.
Status ladder traversal including zero-count skip, StreamEntry attributes; exact static/live URI prefixes.

Tag dispatch, ENDLIST and VOD handling, stale sequence/map exceptions, invalid/empty/error exits and finite-fetch delays. Metadata ring index is masked to 31; missing sequence mapping is an error, not universal PDT enforcement.

Initial playlist tag validation; bandwidth strtoull and invalid/unsupported rendition/codec exits; rendition prefix, group id, audio type and attribute checks. Duplicate group-id and failed insertion paths verified.
Bounded bitrate-index updates and caller-threshold comparisons, minimum/maximum exits, reset counter and transition flags. No retry timing claim follows from these selectors.

METHOD/URI/KEYFORMAT/IV parser, changed-key cache and fetch failure mapping, key length/deadline/short-read checks, Sample-AES material passed to and retained by the framer adapter. Separates HLS material selection from general DRM support.

todo: Established: HDMI ops behind a registered ioctl-callback driver interface; hdmi.log diagnostics; no sysfs/i2c literals.
Residual: which ioctl command numbers and CEC frame content - driver-call boundary, kernel module side
hdmi.hal_boundary: The HDMI hardware boundary is now pinned: hal_detect_open, hal_detect_close and hal_detect_get_cable_states resolve to .dynstr IMPORTS (0x1006216f/21eb/2223), i.e. anacapa calls an external HAL shared library for cable detection - the .text never builds CEC frames or EDID transactions itself (no 'cec'/CEC_* opcode literals exist in the binary). The SMAPI routes v1/players/{playerId}/hdmi/{status,edid,powercycle} (+household variants) therefore terminate in thin wrappers: status -> hal_detect_get_cable_states, edid -> the 'edidStatus' property surface (0x10f97a08), powercycle -> a HAL call. The only in-binary HDMI driver evidence is DDPI user-space completion plumbing ('ddpi_udc_timeslicecomplete returned %d'), i.e. anacapa waits on the display-driver's timeslice completions while the actual CEC/EDID I2C traffic is generated inside the HAL lib/DDPI driver stack. So: CEC commands ARE sent for powercycle, but from the external HAL, not from anacapa code.
resolved_findings: Resolved: all three ops terminate in imported hal_detect_* dynsyms - CEC/EDID generation lives in the external HAL lib + DDPI driver; anacapa only polls cable states, surfaces edidStatus, and waits on ddpi timeslice completions. No CEC frame construction exists in-binary.

Resolved (partial): HDMI surface = ARC/eARC audio-in (HDMI_ARC/HDMI_EARC modes) + status telemetry {edidStatus, stateCEC, tvCECStatus, deviceCEC} + capability bit HdmiCecAvailable emitted in status XML (' HdmiCecAvailable='). Cloud API exposes v1 hdmi endpoints {status, edid, powercycle} per player and household. CEC command sending is conditional - 'target does not support HDMI CEC' reject path exists; powercycle IS an exposed cloud action. EDID is read and reported via the edid endpoint. Product log /opt/log/anacapa.hdmi.log.

Resolved (partial): no sysfs/i2c device path literals exist for HDMI - the only /sys path in the image is /sys/class/net/eth0 (ethernet stats). HDMI edid read and powercycle ride the generic driver dispatch: literal "ioctl_func -> %d" / "ioctl callback returned error %d" (0x10f7eee2/0x10f7eef4) show a registered ioctl-callback interface, plus hdmi.log diagnostics output. So the mechanism is a driver ioctl callback, not userspace i2c/sysfs.

mdp_flash.semantics: Factory manufacturing data:512-byte MDP1 identity/configuration and4096-byte MDP2 key/certification data. The original page reader normalizes optional/versioned fields;read success is distinct from CRC or cryptographic validation. See bin_mdputil for field/edit mappings and noncehandler for the separate MDP2 signing-key consumer.

read_contract.physical_sizes_and_headers: libflash.so.1 hal_flash_get_mdp0x2120 reads512 bytes;hal_flash_get_mdp2 at0x23c0 reads4096 bytes. The first magic is0xce10e47d. Raw xoris at0x21bc XORs high0x31ef;cmpwi at0x21c0 compares against sign-extended0xffffe47d,so solving the comparison gives high0xce10,not0x31ef. The default mdputil template also starts0xce10e47d. MDP2 accepts0xca989b4a or0xfa87b921,not the XOR operand fragments. Reads use flash-info-derived offsets;MDP1 offset info+0x50,and MDP2 offset info+0x50+info+0x40.
read_contract.io_and_status: read_from_offset at libflash0x1f78 opens read-only,checks the64-bit seek result when offset is nonzero,and accumulates partial reads until the requested count is reached. It retries read errno4(EINTR). Return0 means the full requested read;1=open failure,2=seek mismatch,3=short/failed read. MDP readers add9=null flash context and12=bad page magic. MDP1 failure clears its512-byte output then supplies Vendor1,Region1 and the library's current-model value;the original error is still returned. MDP2 failure clears4096 bytes. mdputil does not treat these library fallback values as proof that a valid stored page exists.
read_contract.normalization: For valid MDP1 magic,FLAGS&4 absent clears HWFEATURES+0x68. FLAGS&0x10 absent clears+0x70/+74/+78/+7c/+80. The reader then computes a version for normalization:old+70 when old<=5; for old>5, nonzero new+84 or old. Version<=1 clears+84/+88/+8c;<=2 clears+90..+97;<=3 clears SERIES_ID+98..+9b. For later versions it retains SERIES_ID only if first byte isA-Z and the next three are digits. Version<=5 clears+a0 and then+a4..+ab/+ac;version6 clears+a4..+ab/+ac;version7 clears+ac;later versions retain those tail areas. This is in-memory normalization,not a flash write. Unprinted tail fields still need semantic consumer joins.
read_contract.checksum_limitation: hal_flash_get_mdp invokes crc32(seed0,buffer,508) at0x2298 but neither compares its result with stored+0x1fc nor stores it;the result is discarded before returning the read status. The underlying read_from_offset does not validate CRC either. In contrast,mdputil preparation helper0x10002bf8 stores computed CRC at+0x1fc at0x10002c7c and its alternate branches. Basic read success therefore establishes length/magic and normalization,not CRC/signature acceptance.
read_contract.printing: COPYRIGHT is forcibly terminated at+0x63. Effective MDPVERSION selection is old+70 unless old>5 and new+84 is nonzero. WIFITYPE=N is a literal output line,not a radio-type probe. Invalid DATECODE values are zeroed only in the display buffer. VARIANT,SERIALSIG,UNITSIG,FSN and NANDID are derived helper results and are not interchangeable with fixed MDP1 byte fields.

application_flag_consumer.source: anacapad getter0x10909620 loads cached device-info+0x168,which is its MDP buffer+0x104 plus FLAGS offset0x64. It is an MDP flags word,not a capability word.
application_flag_consumer.predicate: Cleanup0x105e64fc proceeds only when cached(flags&0x20)==0 and cached(flags&3)!=0,proven by0x105e6524/0x105e6528 and0x105e6564/0x105e6568. The earlier documentation reversed both gates.
application_flag_consumer.effect: It reads current MDP1 from flash and optional MDP2,then computes newFlags=(flashFlags&0xfffffffc)|0x20 at0x105e65f8/0x105e65fc and writes via0x10d54658. This clears named numeric bits0x1(printk) and0x2(console) and sets a cleanup marker0x20. A set cached marker skips this path. The record does not claim a refresh of the cached flags after writing or an upgrade-only trigger.

evidence.notes: Separate512-byte MDP1 and4096-byte MDP2 buffers and template.
XOR/signed-compare equation yields0xce10e47d.
Flags/version normalization before return.
CRC return is discarded;no stored-CRC comparison.
Read-only open,64-bit seek,partial-read loop and EINTR retry.
Cached marker must be clear to reach debug-flag cleanup.
Cached printk/console low bits must be nonzero.
Clear numeric0x1/0x2,set0x20,persist new MDP flags.
Probe /dev/mtd8; copy size, erase/write geometry and type into flash context.
Open failure falls through uninitialized stack geometry path and returns0.
Second-page address is erase-block size plus write-page size.
Optional device ID assigned before subsequent serial retrieval/validation.
0xecaa requires55aa in one of four marker slots at returned buffer+0x800.
Length output set before complement verification; cannot imply success.
Bytewise XOR0xff complement validation and first-match copy.
0xec76 has its own8-byte one-pair retrieval sequence.
Raw unsigned high multiply and shifts implement last-four-byte n modulo17.
Bounded uppercase12-hex-plus-suffix serial formatter returns snprintf length.
Stored series checks only first byte and version, then copies four bytes plus terminator.
15-entry base-relative model table; revision/submodel branch thresholds preserved.
Setter stores exactly four checked prefix bytes without rejecting trailing input.
Manufacturing-reader outputs join optional NS2 tags32..36; zeros omit fields.
Setup public/private key and copied-signature consumer; no signature verification in extraction.

mdp_flash.signature_consumers: Standalone mdputil has two separately keyed MD5/RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 checks: original serial plus complement-validated hardware flash serial, signature MDP2+34c; and26-byte model/submodel/serial/color header plus260-byte payload, signature MDP2+3cc. See bin_mdputil.bundle_signature_contract for exact layout, key fingerprints, return domains and edit asymmetry. These checks are distinct from the basic read/CRC contract and from the signing-key consumer in noncehandler.

flash_geometry_contract.producer: libflash.so.1 SHA256454a6c5e2bde42f0f6fa64854dc738a3d1b4731a99f4af6c9272576ca2ff641d: hal_flash_info_init0x1ba8 takes an output-pointer address, sets it null, allocates a zeroed0x210-byte object and stores the geometry-device pathname at+208. PIC GOT reconstruction uses LR anchor0x1bb4, addend loaded at0x1ba4 and R_PPC_RELATIVE GOT addend0x3bec, which resolves /dev/mtd8. This is distinct from the /dev/mtd/0 used by page reads and mdputil writes.
flash_geometry_contract.geometry_fields: After opening /dev/mtd8 read-only, ioctl0x40244d01 receives a stack information structure at sp+18. Successful extraction maps info[0]=returned u32 at+8(total size), info+3c=returned+0c(erase-block size), info+40=returned+10(write-page size), info+50=erase-block size, info+48=0 and info+20c=returned type byte. The rest of the allocation stays zero. Exported get_pagesize0x1b00, get_blocksize0x1b2c and get_type0x1ad4 independently confirm the field roles. The leading type/size/erase/write layout agrees with Linux MTD ABI; the actual binary ioctl encodes36 bytes, so unspecified trailing ABI fields are not inferred.
flash_geometry_contract.manufacturing_layout: MDP1 reads512 bytes from /dev/mtd/0 at offset erase-block size, the start of the second erase block. MDP2 reads4096 bytes at erase-block size + write-page size, proven libflash0x23f4..0x240c. The CLI erase descriptor uses erase-block size as erase length and offset; its first-page write span is write-page size, except type3(NOR flash) forces512 in0x10002fe4..0x10003048. The MDP2 reader does not apply that NOR span override. These are geometry-derived positions, not a hard-coded512-byte separation for every flash type.
flash_geometry_contract.initialization_errors: Allocation failure returns7 with the output null. Negative ioctl result closes the file, frees the object and returns7. Open failure at0x1c1c instead branches directly to0x1c4c: it falls through the field-copy path, publishes the allocated object and returns0 although the stack information structure was never initialized by ioctl. Size remains the allocation zero, but type/erase/write/offset fields are loaded from uninitialized stack slots. Thus initializer success alone does not establish valid geometry. No null guard protects the output-pointer argument. info_exit0x1cc8 tail-branches to free.

flash_serial_reader.interface: libflash.so.1 hal_flash_read_fsn0x2d78 takes u32* length output(r3),serial-byte destination(r4),optional u32* device-ID output(r5). It opens /dev/mtd/0 read-only, gets device ID with ioctl0x40044d24, writes the optional ID immediately after a successful query, and issues serial command ioctl0x80244d23. Required length/destination pointers have no local null/capacity guard. Serial byte count is8 or16 depending on the device ID. This is the helper used for mdputil FSN/NANDID output, not the older in-executable helper used for SERIALSIG.
flash_serial_reader.parameter_layout: The ioctl receives a36-byte stack parameter block at sp+1c, initially zeroed: word+0=0x100;word+4 points to buffer sp+44;word+8 and bytes+c..f select a command sequence;word+14 specifies a per-family numeric parameter;word+18 is explicitly cleared through a variable-length memset in ordinary paths;byte+1c stays0;word+20 may be0xed. These field purposes below the kernel boundary remain untraced. The function reserves2048 returned-data bytes plus8 trailing bytes before its stack canary. Unlike the old utility checker, it also consumes returned marker bytes at buffer+0x800 for one family. Neither caller proves that the word0x100 is a transfer-byte count.

device_families.marker: Require55 aa in at least one of four two-byte positions at returned buffer+0x800,+0x802,+0x804,+0x806 before searching serial pairs.

flash_serial_reader.acceptance: For each candidate, compare serial bytes with the following equal-width complement bytes and require each XOR==0xff. A rejection advances the candidate start by twice the serial width. First complete match copies exactly8/16 serial bytes to the destination; no textual/hex conversion occurs here. For0xecaa, marker validation precedes serial-pair acceptance; it still permits up to8 serial/complement pairs. memcpy return is compared with the destination pointer; the alternate failure is defensive under the standard memcpy return contract.
flash_serial_reader.results_and_outputs: Return0=serial copied;1=device open failure or negative device-ID ioctl;7=unsupported device ID;15=negative serial ioctl, absent required0xecaa marker, or exhausted complement search. The FD closes on all paths after successful open. Optional device ID may be available even on later unsupported/retrieval failure. Length is assigned after successful serial ioctl but before complement search (and before the0xecaa marker check), so a nonzero length output is not proof of success. Serial destination is copied only on acceptance; it is not cleared on failure.
flash_serial_reader.cli_output: mdputil0x1000192c calls this helper with sp+18 length,sp+241c serial destination andsp+14 ID. Success prints NANDID=%04x then FSN= followed by exactly length bytes using%02x, lowercase hexadecimal without separators. identity_format_contract.serial_formatter: sonosMdpSerialToString at libsonos-mdp0xbdc takes six-byte identity pointer(r3),destination(r4),capacity(r5). It assembles source bytes2..5 into unsigned32-bit big-endian n. Raw mulhwu at0xc18 uses0xf0f0f0f1; shift-right4 of the high product yields floor(n/17). The code subtracts17*quotient and renders remainder0..9 as0..9,10..16 asA..G. Format string at0x1084 is %02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%c, giving12 uppercase hexadecimal digits plus one derived suffix. The first two source bytes are printed but do not contribute to the suffix. This formatter performs no serial validity check.
identity_format_contract.serial_output_contract: Formatter calls __snprintf_chk with caller capacity,flag1 and object-size sentinel-1, returning its result unchanged. A complete output needs14 bytes including NUL; smaller capacities truncate according to snprintf while reporting the would-be13-character length. It still reads all six identity bytes. mdputil0x100016c0 supplies capacity32 and prints SERIAL from that output. Its-s edit does not consume/check this suffix as a separate validation character. The boot script consumes only the initial12 hexadecimal characters for the hostname.
identity_format_contract.stored_series: sonosGetSeriesID0xcb0 takes destination(r3),capacity(r4),MDP1(r5). If effective version>=4 and byte+98 is nonzero, it copies bytes+98..9b to a five-byte temporary with trailingNUL, strlcpy-copies to the destination and returns1. It only tests the first stored byte here; no four-character lexical validation occurs inside this getter. EmbeddedNULs can shorten the copied text. Read-time normalization and the setter have separate lexical checks. Return1 describes the chosen stored source even if capacity truncates the output.
identity_format_contract.derived_series: When stored data is ineligible/empty, the getter dispatches MODEL8..22 through15-entry base-relative table0x10a0 (PIC GOT0x27ef0-0x7fd8). Other models, including unsigned underflow below8, use X999. The selected static string is copied with strlcpy and return0 identifies derivation, not failure. The getter does not reject X999 and does not return a copied-length result.

identity_format_contract.series_setter: sonosSetSeriesID0xe64 takes input(r3),MDP1(r4). It checks first byteA-Z then next three bytes0-9. Invalid prefix returns-1 without storing the four-byte field. A valid prefix stores exactly four bytes at+98..9b and returns0; no input-length/end-of-string check follows, so a longer argument with a valid prefix is accepted. No version/flag is changed. There are no local pointer guards. A stored edit may therefore remain ineligible until write preparation sets a sufficiently new version.
identity_format_contract.caller_behavior: mdputil0x10001690 requests a five-byte series string. Return0 causes the literal (dynamic) annotation; return1 uses no annotation. The utility therefore marks X999 as dynamic too. It does not imply that every fallback was a recognized factory series or that a stored series is cross-checked against model/submodel/revision.

Constructor0x100228dc stores these in setup-context+138..+148; server serializer emits them as u32BE tags32..36 only when nonzero. MDP2-read failure produces color0, and the color decoder has a null status output here, so omission of tag35 cannot prove whether color0 was valid or color retrieval failed. soap_param_redaction.semantics: params (passwords, tokens, account data) flagged to be excluded from SOAP request logging; 'Invalid secure param' when a redacted param is malformed
todo: Established: per-param redaction flags at request-param +0x48/+0x4c; tier-2 literal REDACTED substitution sites; arg-record +0x31 proven to be a zero-initialized runtime flag, not the redact marker.
Residual: the complete param-name list that arrives flagged - driven by action metadata tables, partially observable per action
soap_param_redaction.flag_location: Two-tier model decoded. TIER 1 - log suppression (f_1056026c, tag 'reporter'): each request param record carries flag word +0x48 and flag byte +0x4c; when +0x48 is set the param is dropped from logs entirely ('not logging %s, sensitive'), otherwise the four-flag diagnostic 'not logging %s, secure %d, prevent %d, sensitive %d, trackIDing %d' prints the param name (vfunc +0xc) with {secure=+0x48, sensitive=+0x4c, prevent=f_1055fde8(), trackIDing=f_10560138()} - so 'secure'/'sensitive' are stored flags while 'prevent'/'trackIDing' are computed predicates. TIER 2 - value substitution: the 'REDACTED' literal replaces flagged values inside serialized dumps rather than dropping the field - e.g. the wifi settings serializer f_101d0d1c emits 'ssid' and 'frequency' plainly but substitutes 'REDACTED' for the credential-bearing members at +0x24/+0x28/+0x2c; ~10 substitution sites spread across the anacapa (0x101d0d1c) and muse (0x109f-0x10a7) serializer families. DEFAULTS: flags come from the action/dispatch metadata - credential params (psk, passwords, keys, device secrets) are the flagged class; 'trackIDing' marks params that can identify what a user played.
resolved_findings: Resolved: flags live at param +0x48 (secure=suppress) and +0x4c (sensitive), with prevent/trackIDing computed; tier-2 substitutes 'REDACTED' inside dumps - credential params are the flagged class.

Resolved (partial): one redaction mechanism is hardcoded substitution - the credential-response serializer writes literal 'REDACTED' for fields {clientId, authFlow, refreshToken, accessToken} unconditionally (sites 0x10ba6450..0x10ba64b8 via f_109d1924 doc-setter), independent of any flag. Separately, each parsed request-arg record carries a flag byte at +0x31 (zeroed by the f_105614xx/f_105615xx parse ctors alongside type tag at +0x4 and value ptr at +0x8/+0xc) - candidate carrier for a per-param redact marker.

Resolved: the +0x31 flag byte is NOT the redaction carrier - the arg-record ctor family f_10561414..f_105616xx (per-type ctors storing type tags {1,2,3,...} at +0x4, value ptr +0x8, vec {base+0xc,len+0x10,cap+0x14}) unconditionally ZEROES +0x30/+0x31/+0x32 for every type. +0x31 is a runtime-mutated per-arg flag (dirty/consumed class) set post-parse; redaction itself rides the request-param record flags at +0x48 (secure=suppress) and +0x4c (sensitive) as established.
