csrf_protection.name: CSRF tokens on browser-facing POST endpoints
csrf_protection.description: Browser-facing forms use a hidden csrfToken field. The shared generation, validation and reset helpers and all their direct callsites are mapped below. Most diagnostic forms share the application holder; SSH/developer-mode forms use the holder returned by the developer-mode manager. Consumption and HTTP failure behavior are handler-specific. This is not a universal browser-POST policy.

evidence.notes: Setstring form template containing csrfToken.
SSH form template containing action="/ssh/authorized_keys".
Capacity >32; 24-byte ZZ0071 input, guarded base64 encoding, timestamp store and copy. No session identifier argument.
Signed cmpwi 299 expiry guard, null check and strcmp. Reset separately clears +0x24 and byte +0. Raw branch 0x10540854 uses bo=13,bi=29 (greater-than rejection).
Render loads *(0x11097680)+0x810; generation failure 500. POST content-type and field checks return 400. Validation followed unconditionally by reset. Field parser here is f_10c3b72c, not f_10c3b73c.

Holder expression *(0x11095f88)+0xbb8 aliases *(0x11097680)+0x810: initialization stores the root and root+0x3a8 at 0x100c1bcc/0x100c1be0. This handler deliberately responds Success after body/token failure as well as after the valid action.

Logger emits hidden-field template at 0x10f15228, validates without immediate reset. 0x1068de90 is a parsing path, with f_10c3b73c call at 0x1068dea8, validation at 0x1068decc and resets on failure/success.
Root/interface global assignment proves +0xbb8 == +0x3a8+0x810. Developer-mode getter returns its manager+0x4b0. Generation does not include route/session identity.

evidence.function: HTTP route table / f_100d4060 / f_100d3d44 / f_10549cf8
evidence.notes: Route/function pairs, tools form generation, ping/traceroute shared parser, nslookup holder forwarding and host/token guards. Nslookup validates/resets only encountered token fields, returning 400 on missing/false token. Direct branch/call scan covers 11 generation, 13 validation and 15 reset sites in .text; every site is assigned to the endpoint contracts, including thunks and the registered developer hook.

mDNS read/token failures reset and give 400; operation errors log but converge on 200/reset. Spotify form generation on spotdbg; reset action intentionally returns 200/reset even for missing/false token or read failure, but does not execute the action.

Custom service permission/method dispatch, generation and reset paths; advconfig and directsubmit render, false/missing-token guards and encountered-field consumption. Read failure in customsd returns before the reset path.

Logger aliases receive the application holder and reject missing/false token with 401; no reset call anywhere in that handler. Reboot/reset generation, read/missing/false-token reset and valid-token consumption before reboot are distinct paths.

SSH and developer-mode forms obtain manager+0x4b0; permission/method gates, generation failure 500, missing/false-token 400, encountered-token reset. Developer parser/generator pair also registered in the generic HTTP-hook slots; no direct helper callsite remains unmapped.

Disproved old fcs/testenv shared-token inventory: dispatch and complete form-field loops have permission and application-setting calls but no shared token generator/validator/reset. fcs recognizes overrideconfig/button, testenv recognizes url/env/button/reset. Do not assign them another handler's CSRF policy.

csrf_protection.token_model: Holder-relative layout: token string at +0, issue time at +0x24, guard at +0x28. f_105406d8 rejects unsigned output capacity <=32 and entropy-helper failure without replacing the previous token; otherwise ZZ0071 supplies 24 bytes, f_1053c0c0 base64-encodes into a 33-byte slot under the guard, records sonosClockGetTime(1), and copies the token out. Each successful generation replaces that holder's previous token. f_105407bc locks the holder, rejects a zero issue time, uses a signed comparison of current seconds minus issue seconds against 299 (reject >299), rejects a null candidate, then returns whether strcmp matches exactly. The helper itself does not consume the token. f_1054066c zeroes the issue time and first token byte under the guard. Validation and reset acquire separate locks, not one atomic consume operation; universal single-use or per-session binding must not be inferred.
csrf_protection.holder_ownership: f_100c1478 stores the application root in 0x11095f88 at 0x100c1bcc and its embedded interface at root+0x3a8 in 0x11097680 at 0x100c1bd4-0x100c1be0 (null root produces null interface). Therefore interface+0x810 and root+0xbb8 are exactly the same holder. The null-root branch at 0x100c2ad8 rejoins the same assignment. The second expression used by SSH and developer-mode functions is f_1054c758(*(0x11097374)), which returns that manager+0x4b0. Rendered tokens contain no session or route identifier; generating another form on a shared holder invalidates its predecessor.
endpoint_contracts: /setstring and /removestring: f_100b7cb4/f_100b79e0 render and generate on GET (0x100b7d9c/0x100b7ac0), failing with 500. POST requires exact case-insensitive application/x-www-form-urlencoded, a successfully read body and expected form fields; unknown/missing required fields or false validation yield 400. Each encountered csrfToken is validated and immediately resets the application holder on either result (0x100b7ea4/0x100b7eb8 and 0x100b7ba8/0x100b7bbc). A request rejected before reaching a token field does not automatically reset. Unsupported methods produce 405.

/tools and /tools.htm: f_100d4060 generates the application token at 0x100d40fc and emits forms for /ping, /traceroute, /nslookup and /mdnsannounce; generation failure is 500. The submit-only endpoints do not generate their own tokens. /ping and /traceroute wrappers f_100d3f88/f_100d3ff4 enter f_100d3d44: POST-only, strict form content-type, read/host/token failure 400, unsupported method 405, each encountered token validate/reset at 0x100d3ec8/0x100d3edc. Permission rejection occurs in the wrappers before parsing.

/nslookup: route f_100b96d0 checks permission then passes the application holder to f_10549cf8. Null holder gives 500, non-POST 405, content-type/read failure 400. It accepts host and csrfToken fields, rejects unknown fields with 400, validates at 0x10549e78 and resets at 0x10549e88 on either result. Missing/false token or empty/invalid host gives 400; only after these guards does DNS/mDNS/NetBIOS resolution execute. It never generates a token itself; the form is on /tools.

/mdnsannounce: f_100c1230 is POST-only with strict form content-type. Body-read failure, missing token or false token reset the application holder at 0x100c131c and return 400; success performs the operation then resets at 0x100c141c and responds 200 Success, even when the resend operation returned an error that was logged. Bad content-type returns 400 before reset; other methods give 405. Validation is at 0x100c135c. Generation is on /tools.

/spotdbg renders a token at 0x100b81f8 after its permission check (403 on denial, 500 generation failure, 405 non-GET). It supplies the form for /spotresetnts. That POST-only handler f_100b7fd8 returns 400 for bad content-type but deliberately resets and returns 200 Success on body-read failure, missing token and false validation as well as on success (0x100b80d0, 0x100b8120). Only a true validation executes f_1020d4d0. A Success response is not evidence that the operation ran.

/advconfig and /advconfig.htm: f_105e8444 renders/generates at 0x105e875c (500 on failure); POST enforces strict form content-type and a successful read, parses its settings, validates and resets each token field at 0x105e880c/0x105e8820. Missing/false token or invalid settings gives 400, without an invented reset on paths that never encountered the token. Permission checks precede processing.

/support/directsubmit: f_105e9b30 renders/generates at 0x105e9c0c (500 on failure), POST requires strict form content-type/read success and valid token. Each encountered token is validated/reset at 0x105e9e28/0x105e9e3c. Missing/false token or malformed form yields 400. Unsupported methods give 405. Only a validated form reaches diagnostic submission; its later outcome is independent of the token check.

/customsd and /customsd.htm: route f_103429f4 gates permissions, GET calls f_10342824 (generation 0x10342858, failure 500), POST checks content-type in f_10342988 then calls f_10342590. Body-read failure returns 400 before reset; missing/false token returns 400 through reset 0x1034267c, validation is 0x10342698. The successful operation and downstream operation errors also pass through reset. The route propagates returned error status; other methods give 405.

/logger, /diaglevel and /diagmsg: route-table aliases to f_105e93d8 pass the application holder into f_1076c8d0. GET generates at 0x1076cb6c (500 on failure). POST parses fields and validates at 0x1076e198; a missing/false token produces 401 via 0x1076d620-0x1076d62c before settings are applied. There is no reset call in this handler, on success or validation failure: reuse is possible until replacement or expiry. Other methods produce 405. Permission denial happens in the wrapper before generation/validation.

/reboot and /reset: wrappers f_105e92e0/f_105e935c enter f_1068dcdc with mode 0/1 and the application interface. GET generates at 0x1068ddc4 (500 on failure). POST requires strict form content-type; read failure, missing token and invalid token reset at 0x1068de84/0x1068deb8 and return 400. Valid token at 0x1068decc is reset at 0x1068dedc before the response and reboot/reset. Bad content-type returns 400 before reset; unsupported method gives 405. Wrapper permission checks still apply.

/ssh/authorized_keys: route thunk f_105e9594 enters f_10670168, which requires the developer-mode manager and permission 0x2f (500/403 respectively), obtains manager+0x4b0 and dispatches GET/POST. f_1066fbe4 generates at 0x1066fc0c (500 on failure). f_1066fda4 parses the form, validates/resets each token at 0x10670004/0x10670014. Missing/false token yields 400 before writing/removing keys; read status propagates. Bad content-type gives 400 and other methods 405. This is the developer-mode holder, not the application-holder expression.

/devmode: f_105e8d90 tail-calls f_1076f6bc. GET wrapper f_1076f238 calls f_1076f108, generation 0x1076f18c; missing manager or generation failure gives 500. POST wrapper f_1076f590 reads the strict form and calls f_1076f2ec: validation/reset at 0x1076f4bc/0x1076f4cc uses manager+0x4b0, missing/false token returns 400, invalid statement/action has its own returned status. The same generation/parser pair is registered as an indirect HTTP hook at 0x105e77c4/0x100ab708 and dispatched through f_1076f794, so those callsites are not unassigned route evidence. Unsupported methods give 405 in the normal route wrapper.

/fcs and /testenv were incorrectly included as users of these shared CSRF helpers. /fcs routes through f_105eba60 -> f_106ba5b0: permission 0x18 gates GET/form/JSON/DELETE, and the form parser f_106b9fac recognizes overrideconfig/button without generating, validating or resetting this token. /testenv routes through f_105eb9dc -> f_10776c14 and parsers f_10776574/f_10776970; it gates permission 0x25 and parses url/env/button/reset rather than csrfToken. Neither path has a shared-token consume policy. This finding does not claim those endpoints lack all access controls.
resolved_findings: Resolved the apparent two-global ambiguity: they point to the application root and its +0x3a8 embedded interface, so their token-holder expressions alias. Mapped all 39 direct helper callsites. Most diagnostic forms share this holder, but developer-mode/SSH callers obtain their holder from another getter; there is no universal device-wide or atomic single-use token contract.
Corrected the alleged form-emission site 0x1068de90: it parses csrfToken, not emits it. The /logger hidden-field emitter is at 0x1076cecc-0x1076cedc and references template 0x10f15228.

device_description_variants.selection_rule: Selection logic decoded at f_1035b128: the description endpoint mutex-reads flag byte +0xa56 on the device object (f_105b5edc) - the bonded-satellite flag - and returns '/xml/satellite_device.xml' when set, else '/xml/device_description.xml'. So: a satellite (stereo-pair second / surround / bonded sub member) advertises the reduced satellite description while the coordinator/standalone serves the full description. '/xml/group_description.xml' is a separate dedicated handler (f_100bdedc) - the group-coordinator description for zone-group discovery, not a flag variant. '/xml/device_description_no_ai.xml' has NO code references anywhere in .text (even the '_no_ai.xml' suffix is unreferenced): it is served purely request-side - the file ships in the image and is delivered verbatim when a client asks for it, i.e. the no_ai variant is client-selected (controllers that must not see the AudioIn service section fetch it explicitly), not something anacapa substitutes.

gena_internals.notes: AVT envelopes carry the r: extension namespace for Sonos fields; Queue events live in a Sonos-private namespace (schemas-sonos-com, not rinconnetworks): clients parsing LastChange must handle all three namespaces; val="" attribute form used throughout
gena_internals.delivery: Delivery runs on worker threads keyed by (event-name, event-id): 'Beginning delivery of %s(%u) event on thread %zu' -> per-subscriber 'Delivering %s(%u) event to "%s"' -> 'Completed delivery' / 'Delivery ... cancelled'.
gena_internals.retry: Send retries are counted per-subscriber: 'Success sending event to %s:%d after %u retry(s)', '%d failure(s) sending event to %s:%d. (id=%s, state=%d, errno=0x%x) Now %ld...' (logs subscription state), batch backoff '%s: Failure (%u events, %zu bytes, attempt %u, retrying in %u seconds)', metric 'countEventsSuccessRetry'.
gena_internals.persistence: Pending events are persisted across reboot: preserveEvents writes 'Preserved %zu bytes' to a file; restoreEvents validates on read (length checks 'Length %zu too short'/'does not match recorded length' + 'SHA256 hash check failure') then 'Restored %zu bytes'. Parallel preserveProtoEvents/restoreProtoEvents pair handles protobuf-serialized events.
gena_internals.sid_management: Client-side (outbound) subscriptions distinguish the client-assigned Logical SID from the server-assigned SID: 'Subscribe %s; Logical SID: %s; Port: %u; Secure Eventing: %d (srRet=%d)' -> 'Successfully subscribed %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s, UDN %s'. Renew: 'Successfully renewed %s; SID/logical SID', 'Failed to renew ... HTTP Result: %d; SR: %08x', 'Unsubscribe in renew %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s (oos:%d seq:%d)' - an out-of-sync flag and sequence counter ride the renew. Dedup: 'register skipped for non-empty SID: %s'. 'Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u' moves subscriptions between server sids; 'setting token key to %s for sid: %u' binds an eventing auth token.
resolved_findings: Resolved: threaded per-(name,id) delivery, per-subscriber retry counts+backoff, persisted event queue (file, length+SHA256 verified, xml+proto variants), logical-vs-server SID split, secure-eventing flag, oos+seq on renew, register dedup, SID migration, per-sid token.
Established: the subscription machinery vocabulary, the three event namespaces, and the per-service LastChange schemas are documented.
Established: notify-delivery internals reach the injected-delegate boundary - documented.

icy_metadata.icy_fields: Full client grammar decoded (the 'shoutcastradio' module, 0x10ed45f0-0x10ed47d0). REQUEST: 'GET %s HTTP/1.1' + 'ACCEPT: */*' + 'HOST: %s%s' + a spoofed UA 'User-Agent: %s Nullsoft Winamp3 version 3.0 (compatible)' + 'Icy-MetaData: 1' - the player masquerades as Winamp3 and opts into in-band metadata. RESPONSE: accepts 'ICY 200', 'HTTP/1.1 200', 'HTTP/1.0 200' and 30x redirects ('redirect to %s', plus the audio/x-mpegurl playlist hop 'Redirect audio/x-mpegurl to %s'). HEADER SET parsed: '@icy-metaint:' (the metadata interval that paces in-band blocks), 'icy-name:' (station name), 'location:', 'CONTENT-TYPE:', 'server:'; generic 'add header [%s : %s]' collects the rest. METADATA FIELD SET: exactly one in-band field is extracted - 'StreamTitle' - from each metadata block; the block framing is the standard icy-metaint byte-counted segments between audio. EVENTING PATH: StreamTitle feeds the current-track metadata surface (radio title in AVTransport track info / LastChange) - the stream's title line is what appears as the now-playing metadata for shoutcast-style radio.
resolved_findings: Resolved: request spoofs Winamp3 UA + Icy-MetaData:1; accepts ICY/HTTP 200 + redirects + m3u hops; header set {@icy-metaint, icy-name, location, content-type, server}; the only in-band field extracted is StreamTitle -> current-track metadata.
Established: ICY in-band metadata via the @icy-metaint interval header is documented for mp3radio streams.
Established: ICY field set + eventing path reach the stream-metadata extractor boundary - documented.

alert_engine.duck_policy: Duck engine fully decoded (duck.cxx, SMAPI routes v1/players/{id}/playerVolume/{duck,unduck}). POLICY TABLE: five named policies - 'always-apply', 'always-ignore', 'ignore-if-mic-present', 'ignore-if-tv-playing', 'ignore-if-mic-present-or-tv-playing' - stored per source as a bitmask ('muse ducking policy: %x -> %x', 'initial muse policy %x'). EVALUATION ORDER: (1) global switch - 'ducking globally enabled/disabled' honor-or-drop; (2) device-class gate - 'voice enabled device, dropping muse duck request' (mic-present devices refuse); (3) activity gate - 'playing tv, drop duck req'; (4) acquisition fallback - 'failed to acquire gc/avt, honoring duck req' (when group-coordinator or AVTransport state can't be read the duck is honored anyway - fail-open); (5) flag set + distribute. MECHANISM: ducks are 64-bit 'ducking bits' (0x%016llx) queued per source under duck_tracker_mtx ('Queueing ducking bit from %s', 'too many pending ducking bits', 'Dequeueing ducking bit', 'Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'); the coordinator fans them out to 'all secondaries'/'bonded peer' ('Forward %s %d to %s %s', 'failed to forward duck command'), 'zone %d received ducking bit' on receipt. LIFECYCLE: 'expireRemoteDuckingFlags' sweeps stale bits and 'WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout' auto-releases a stuck local duck - so a crashed source can't hold the group ducked. 'RecordDuckingActionEvent' telemeters each transition; 'runDuckingHeartbeat'/'FV:GC-HB' keep the group state fresh. 'fastvolduck'/'duckOrUnduck'/'clearMuseFlag' name the op helpers.
resolved_findings: Resolved: five-name policy table (always-apply/always-ignore/ignore-if-mic/-tv/-either) evaluated global->device-class->activity->acquisition-fallback(fail-open)->distribute; ducks are 64-bit bits fanned out by the GC with expiry sweeps + local timeout auto-release.

token_refresh_state_machine.name: music-account OAuth token refresh lifecycle
token_refresh_state_machine.description: Per-account token refresh FSM ('token refresh state for acct. sn. %u action %d', transition log lines, tokencache file) feeding outbound /auth/oauth/v2/validate and /product/v2/households/.../players?action=complete&token= calls: the layer SystemProperties account actions write into.

token_refresh_state_machine.transitions: Transition vocabulary recovered; the FSM runs INSIDE the per-account request transaction (f_1038e82c is the cloud-queue response handler, tag 'cqatrs_tx'), driven by the request's result code not a standalone thread. Recovered transition semantics: IDLE->refresh ('%s requesting token refresh sync for acct. sn. %u %d -> %d' and '%s requesting new token refresh sync' - a sync request moves the action state); WAIT ('%s need to wait for token refresh for acct. sn. %u; %d' + 'waiting for token refresh completion' + 'waiting for refresh tx complete; current state %d' -> 'wait finished; new state %d' - callers block on the transaction); REFRESH ('Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d)' - hrs/te are the hours-since and token-expiry counters); SUCCESS ('Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry.' - the original request is retried automatically); FAIL ('Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d', 'Could not find SD, sid=%u', 'Could not find account, sn=%u'); CACHE ('%s using token from file' / 'last refresh token for load timed out' / 'no last refresh token time' / 'trying to load token' / 'failed to load token' - the tokencache file read path with timeout checks); UNKNOWN ('unexpected token action %d' - the default arm). The '%d -> %d' transition numbers are the action-state codes inside the transaction; the upstream driver is the request result (HTTP/UPnP status codes 0x191/401-class token-expired results trigger the refresh arm).
resolved_findings: Resolved: FSM vocabulary = IDLE->sync-request, WAIT-on-tx, REFRESH(hrs,te), SUCCESS->auto-retry, FAIL(upnp-result/no-SD/no-acct), CACHE-load(file,timeout), unexpected-default; embedded in the per-account transaction driven by request result codes.
Established: the per-account token refresh FSM, tokencache file, and the outbound validate/complete calls it feeds are documented.

enum_tables.name: Static enum name->integer registration tables
enum_tables.note: The 0x10fac7d4-0x10faddxx block plus .data.rel.ro arrays hold the binary's enum registration tables, giving proven integer values for the name vocabularies elsewhere catalogued as unordered literals (muse roles/auth-types/playModes, SMAPI capability bitmask, CHSRC source classes, alarm/timer/power/replication FSM states, remote buttons, speaker orientation, netmodes, trueroom data types, content-object classes, ratings, update-FSM results, vanish reasons). Values are sequential (enum) or power-of-two (bitmask) as marked.

r_led_mask.provenance: per-use extraction: applyLEDMode f_10c918a0 bit-test chain: each R_LED_* name logs its tested mask bit as (hi<<32)|lo constants; PROVEN from code, not registration table

names.R_LED_PLAYING: 0x0 (else/default case: mask with no bit set)

r_led_mask.note: 64-bit LED-state mask; !R_LED_HHID logs the same 0x2 bit inverted (set vs clear both logged)

r_play_op.provenance: jump-table dispatch in f_104c9270: cmplwi bound 6 + PIC offset table @0x10ed8640; each case logs its R_PLAY_OP name: PROVEN

names.0: (no R_ log in case: likely NONE/nop)
names.4: shared case: R_PLAY_OP_RESYNC (sched), R_PLAY_OP_CHANGE_SRC, R_PLAY_OP_SAMPLE all logged here

r_stream_op.provenance: jump-table dispatch in f_104c6264 (stream op handler); case->log-name bucketing: PROVEN

muse_result_codes.provenance: direct-indexed char* table @0x10f94d14; consumer f_109e0d14 does cmplwi 106 bound-check + table[code] name lookup; f_109e0e10 the reverse (name->code). PROVEN: index IS the wire result code
muse_result_codes.note: the muse/lechmere result-code enum (systemResult/result fields, cmd responses). 0-51 domain errors, 52-56 success (OK/CREATED/ACCEPTED/NO_CONTENT/NOT_MODIFIED mirroring HTTP 200/201/202/204/304), 57-106 protocol/request errors. Out-of-range renders UNKNOWN

media_service_errors.note: legacy media/service playback error enum: generic transport errors 0-17, then per-service ranges (RHAP 18-23, AUDIBLE 24-26, WMP 27-28, SIRIUS 29-37, PAND 38-44, SONOS 45-47, LASTFM 48-51,55, DOCK 52, SONOS extras 53-54,56-59, CLOUD_QUEUE 60-64, CERT 65-66, tail 67-70)

r_client_keycert_id.provenance: selector f_1057ac60 returns id in r3; each arm loads its R_CLIENT_KEYCERT_ID_* log string then returns 0-3: PROVEN name->id
r_client_keycert_id.note: selection driven by flag bits at cert-ctx+0x0c (bit0/bit2) plus a predicate call; consumer f_1057ade8 (cert path builder) feeds id into f_1056c738 which indexes bss tables 0x110a5670/0x110a56d8 (runtime-populated cert objects). chirp_sdk.note: Asynchronous Inc's Chirp SDK v4.2.3: ultrasonic data-over-audio for device setup (sonos-cdma profile). Error vocabulary recovered: profile/channel validation, modulation-scheme mismatches, payload decode failures ('payload contains unknown symbols', 'Couldn't decode the payload'), gain-level errors, muted-device guard. Source paths leak the SDK layout: /code/src/chirp-sdk/chirp_sdk_process.c, chirp_sdk_states.c, /code/chirp-core/source/utils/src/utils/helpers.c; internal funcs chirp_sdk_process_shorts_{input,output}, chirp_sdk_send, chirp_levenshtein.
chirp_sdk.payload_format: The ultrasonic payload is chirp_payload_t: a message payload plus a SEPARATE parity payload ('Chirp message payload has already been allocated' / 'Chirp parity payload has already been allocated') - the parity is forward-error-correction symbols. Protocol constraints on the payload: alphabet_bits (symbol alphabet size, bounds-checked 'Alphabet bits is not within acceptable range'), min/max message length ('Min/Max message length cannot be less than 1 byte', 'Max ... cannot be less than min'), polyphony ('Polyphony is outside valid range'), and the sonos-cdma profile is FIXED-LENGTH ('Chirp protocol must be fixed length for CDMA'). Encode chain: raw bytes -> chirp_payload_t (payload.c) -> chirp_encode -> symbols -> chirp_cdma_encoder (CDMA) or FSK (decoders_fsk family) -> wavetable+biquad synthesis ('Chirping raw array of length = %d') -> PCM shorts. Decode chain: shorts input -> block_buffer -> chirp_fft -> chirp_cdma_decoder_process_frame (score-based decoding, 'Call to add_score failed') -> chirp_levenshtein correction -> payload bytes. Test hooks: chirp_sdk_random_payload, 'Generated random chirp with identifier: %s', chirp_protocol_corrupt_random_symbols. The zp-facing dispatcher rejects unknown payload types with 'Chirp payload %s not supported.'
chirp_sdk.sonos_cdma_profile: The concrete 'sonos-cdma' protocol profile is a compile-time struct in .data at 0x11094630 (not runtime JSON): sample_rate 44100 (0xac44), timing floats {0.05, 0.004, 0.035}s, level ramps {0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.53}, and an ultrasonic carrier plan {17000->0, 18000->12, 19000->24, 20000->36} = four 1kHz-spaced carriers in the 17-20kHz band with cumulative symbol-index offsets 0/12/24/36 into a 48-symbol codebook (codebook.c). Companion fields: 0x80000 flag word, '1' format tag, internal table ptrs 0x110bb7xx. The protocol constraints validated at new_chirp_protocol: alphabet_bits range, min/max message length >=1 byte, polyphony range - errors are literal 'chirp_protocol_t: <field> is not within acceptable range'. The profile is instantiated via new_chirp_protocol_from_json_value so the same struct shape can be reconfigured by JSON, but this build's compiled-in default is the sonos-cdma values above.
resolved_findings: Established: concrete sonos-cdma profile - 44100Hz, 17-20kHz carriers {17k:0,18k:12,19k:24,20k:36}, timings {50ms,4ms,35ms}, levels {0.2..0.8,0.53}; protocol built from JSON-configurable struct.

Resolved (partial): payload pipeline proven from linked chirp-core symbols: chirp_payload_t + chirp_payload_randomise, RS coding (reed-solomon.c), CRC (crc.c), bitstring encoding, codebook CDMA (chirp_codebook_t), and decode chain {peaks,scorer,voter,weighting,rms,note_estimate,cdma_match} with chirp_decode_metrics_t metrics. Data traversing the ultrasonic channel = payload bytes RS+CRC protected, CDMA/codebook modulated per chirp_protocol_t config (protocol.c/protocol-acoustic.c/protocol-encoding.c).

Resolved: channel payload content decoded from call sites - the chirp carries a small opaque payload = the device's unique identifier value ('Start chirping with unique device value:%d'; 'Generated random chirp with identifier: %s'). Payload typed by name ('Chirp payload %s not supported.'). Three uses: SETUP_CHIRP (device discovery during app setup), EXT_CHIRP (external audio source trigger), ROOM_DETECTION_CHIRP (Trueplay room detection via cloud API v1/.../roomDetection/chirp{,/{playId}}). Wire form = chirp_payload_t bytes, Reed-Solomon + CRC protected, CDMA codebook-modulated (chirp_protocol_t: fixed-length for CDMA - 'Chirp protocol must be fixed length for CDMA'), alphabet-bits/min-max length/polyphony constrained by protocol config. chirp-core 4.2.1_7265.

Resolved: the complete protocol-profile list is literal @0x10fd04c8+ = {audible, sonos-cdma, sonos_secure_setup, ultrasonic, new_chirp_protocol} (5 profiles). The per-profile parameter dump format is proven: {Frequency base %.1fHz, Frequency interval %.1fHz, Channels %d, Channel interval %.1fHz, Note duration header %.3f, Note duration body %.3f, Envelope duration attack %.3f, ...} (0x10fd0578+) - confirming the profile struct carries {freq_base, freq_interval, channels, channel_interval, note_durations, envelope_durations} numeric fields defined in /code/chirp-core/source/core/src/profile/protocol.c.

Resolved: the embedded SDK is chirp-core 4.2.1_7265 (literal version string 0x10fd3454) with the complete source module map recoverable from assert paths (0x10fce74-0x10fd38c6): chirp_sdk.{c,process.c,states.c}; chirp-private {chirp_private.c, _cdma.c, _fsk.c}; core/common {chirp.c, crc.c, payload.c, reed-solomon.c, template.c, utils.c, bitstring.c, filter.c, multitone.c}; core/profile {profile.c, protocol.c, protocol-acoustic.c, protocol-encoding.c, config.c, config-voter-config.c}; core/cdma {cdma_decoder.c, cdma_encoder.c, codebook.c}; decoder {decoder.c, peaks.c, scorer.c, voter.c, weighting.c, rms.c}; encoder {encoder.c, wavetable.c, decorator.c}; dsp {blockbuffer.c, fft.c, reverb.c}; maths float32 fft init/deinit. The sonos-cdma protocol is selected via chirp_builtin_profile/chirp_profile/chirp_protocol with config objects chirp_default_config + chirp_default_voter_configs. Profile validation gates are literal: "Alphabet bits is not within acceptable range", "Min/Max message length cannot be less than 1 byte", "Max message length cannot be less than min message length", "Polyphony is outside valid range" - so the sonos-cdma profile declares {alphabet bits, min/max message length, polyphony} fields. FEC = reed-solomon (chirp_rs_*). Decoder pipeline = fft -> peaks -> scorer -> voter (chirp_voter_set_state, weighting) -> rms. Symbols: chirp_get_symbols, chirp_levenshtein (symbol-distance metric), chirp_decode_metrics_t metrics struct.

Resolved: the compiled protocol-profile table is literal at 0x11094600+ (records ~0x1b0 stride, each with a vptr cluster {0x110bb7xx} + name + flags + float arrays). sonos-cdma profile (0x11094630): flags 0x80000; 5-float threshold run {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.53}; a 7-entry sub-table pointer list (0x11094768+) indexing 8-float rows - five identical tone maps {17000Hz:0, 18000Hz:12, 19000Hz:24, 20000Hz:36} (the 4-tone alphabet spanning 17-20kHz), a correction row {17000:17.248, 18000:34.405, 19200:34.238, 19400:0}, and a weight row {17000:8, 18000:6, 19000:4, 20000:0}; trailing params {500,100}, packed fields 0x4030a0a/0x20a0a00, carrier-ish float 19000.0, 60.0, and small-float set {0.12,0.06,0.01,0.01,0.03,0.015}. Second protocol sonos_secure_setup (0x110947ec): same flags 0x80000, threshold run {0.97 x5, 0.99, 0.97}, packed 0x30206/0x8000000, same {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.53} tail - sharing the alphabet but with a much stricter voter threshold (0.97/0.99 vs 0.2-0.8).

Profile record tail decoded (sonos-cdma @0x11094630, stride 0x1c0): the 7 sub-table blocks split as {5 identical alphabet pair-blocks {17000:0,18000:12,19000:24,20000:36} at +0x28..+0xdf (only 2 are referenced), 1 correction block {17000:17.2,18000:34.4,19200:34.24,19400:0} at +0xf0, 1 weighting block {17000:8,18000:6,19000:4,20000:0} at +0x110}; 4 row pointers at +0x144..+0x150 bind exactly the last 4 blocks. Tail fields: +0x154 packed u32 0x4030a0a (bytes {4,3,10,10}), +0x158 packed u32 0x20a0a00 (bytes {2,10,10,0}), +0x15c base freq 19000.0, +0x160 60.0, +0x164 bitfield 0x1000000, +0x16c param floats {0.12,0.06,0.01,0.01,0,0.03,0.015}, +0x194 bitfield 0x80070000, +0x198 sample rate 44100 (0xac44), +0x19c bitfield 0x8000100, +0x1a0 fn/row ptr cluster ending with next-profile name ptr.

Resolved: the two packed u32s in each profile tail are the protocol-encoding field block. The protocol-encoding JSON keys are literal in the image at 0x10fd0af4+ = {alphabet_bits, crc_length, message_length_max, message_length_min, polyphony, rs_length_max, rs_length_min} (parsed by new_chirp_protocol_from_json_value; 'Invalid key in encoding: %s'), seven u8 fields packed as two words plus a zero pad. Byte order inside each word is MSB-first (the min<=max constraint fails under reverse order). Decoded per profile: audible {alphabet_bits=8, polyphony=1, message_length_min=1, message_length_max=32} / {crc_length=2, rs_length_min=8, rs_length_max=16}; sonos-cdma {4, 3, 10, 10} / {2, 10, 10, 0}; sonos_secure_setup {5, 3, 1, 192} / {1, 8, 56, 0}. sonos-cdma is the only fully fixed-length encoding (message_length_min==max==10, rs_length_min==max==10) which matches the literal 'Chirp protocol must be fixed length for CDMA' constraint; sonos_secure_setup carries the largest payload (1..192-byte message with 8..56 RS parity symbols, block max 248 <= 255) consistent with credential transfer, and audible is the only monophonic profile (polyphony=1).

tsclient.name: tsclient: MPEG transport-stream demuxer client

evidence.notes: payload-type dispatcher

ES PID bytes are combined before type dispatch. Raw575a04fe: op21 SH0 MB19 ME31 Rc0, mask00001fff; timed-ID3 registration stores that masked value atthis+0x30. Record-form andis.752a0020 provides CR0 for the following beq; masking is not a shift or a new comparison.

r16 holds Unsupported stream type format; bne after andi.0x3c18 reaches that diagnostic, disproving the former acceptance-set claim. andis.0x20 selects metadata type21; subsequent andi.0x8000 selects audio type15. PID stores at+0x30/+0x10 are separately gated.

tsclient.note: CORRECTED: 'ts' is transport-stream (MPEG-TS), not track-service. f_104cd500 is a TS packet parser: it reads the 4-byte TS header ({sync, PID[12:0], adaptation control, continuity counter} via the +0x28..+0x2b bytes) and dispatches by PID. Registered PIDs live on the client object: audio PID at this+0x10, timed-ID3 PID at this+0x30. Rejects log 'non-audio and non-timed_id3 PID 0x%x (%d)'; accepts log 'PID: 0x%x (a=%d, p=%d)' (a=audio-flag, p=PCR-flag). PSI handling: PAT on PID 0 ('found PAT PID'), PMT discovery ('found PMT PID 0x%x'), then full section walk 'sectlen: %x' / 'desclen: %x' / 'eslen: %x' with per-ES stream_type dispatch ('stype: %x', 'Unsupported stream type: %x'). Adaptation field parsed ('afelen=%x'). In-band metadata: detects ID3v2 byte-magic inline ('detected ID3v2 tag' after matching 0x44='D',0x33='3' header bytes; 'ID3v2 tag is malformed' on bad tags). 'silen: %zu' logs silence/stuffing runs. Outer pump f_104cdff0 batches packets under a deadline (sonosClockGetTime+timevalGt each iteration); this+0x54==1 is a flush-only path; the globals at this+0x87b0/0x87b4/0x87b8 are cleared after processing and a byte flag at this+0x87c8 gates a fast path. Feeds f_104cd1bc (payload accept), f_104cd0e0 (PID-filter predicate), f_104cccd8 (free), f_104cd2f4 (ID3 tag handler).

payload_types.PID_based: dispatch is by 13-bit TS PID, not a 0/1 type enum: PAT PID 0, discovered PMT PID, registered audio PID (this+0x10), registered timed-ID3 PID (this+0x30), everything else rejected
payload_types.stream_types: PMT registration recognizes audio stream_type0x0f and timed metadata0x15. The0x3c18 mask is a rejection set for0x03/0x04/0x0a/0x0b/0x0c/0x0d; other types skip registration rather than universally logging unsupported.
payload_types.id3: in-band ID3v2 tags detected on 49 44 33 magic inside PES payloads

resolved_findings: Resolved: tsclient is an MPEG-TS demuxer - 4-byte header parse, PID dispatch (PAT 0 / PMT / audio this+0x10 / timed-ID3 this+0x30), PSI section+descriptor+ES walk, stream_type dispatch, adaptation-field handling, in-band ID3v2, deadline-bounded batch pump.

The PMT stream-type branch has a rejection mask, not an audio acceptance set. At0x104cdb20 types above0x15 skip registration. For smaller types, nonzero (1<<stype)&0x3c18 branches to the Unsupported stream type diagnostic at0x104cdb48 (format held in r16 from0x104cd580): types0x03,0x04,0x0a,0x0b,0x0c,0x0d are rejected here. Otherwise bit0x00200000 selects type0x15 metadata-in-PES and stores its timed-ID3 PID atthis+0x30; bit0x00008000 selects type0x0f AAC/ADTS and stores its audio PID atthis+0x10 via0x104cda10. Other types do not register either PID on this branch. Raw0x575a04fe at0x104cdb38 is rlwinm r26,r26,0,19,31 (clrlwi19): the stored timed-ID3 PID is the low13 bits of the ES PID field, not a right13 shift. Rc=0 leaves the preceding andis. stream-type test in CR0 for the beq at0x104cdb3c.

netstart_ipc.name: netstartd IPC event dispatcher

protocol.message_id: big-endian u32 at msg+12..15; dispatched as id-31 -> PIC jump table 0x10f01d6c, 61 entries (ids 31..91); unhandled ids -> shared default case f_10691188-region

cases.48: WiFi connected -> posts muse event wifiConnected {eventType, hardware:wifi}
cases.53: Received set Muse HHID -> calls f_109c??? muse HHID setter then f_109dbe58 f_10652d88
cases.91: recovery AP connection: %02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X + set recovery AP state (else "unable to set recovery AP state")
cases.conn-type names: sub-case maps conn type int -> {WiFi, Ethernet, Ethernet (WiFi Disabled), SonosNet (wireless), SonosNet (Ethernet), Home Theater, Home Theater (Ethernet), Home Theater 2.0, Unknown} via offset-table name jump (b 0x1057f8a0 epilogue)

netstart_ipc.wire_format: PROVEN via f_105d3980 (the select-loop reader): stream = [12-byte header][payload]. ReadIPCHeader (libsonos, .plt 0x11098588) consumes the 12 bytes; the u32 at header+8 is the declared payload length N (accepted range 4 <= N <= 0x804, 'len-4 <= 0x800'); payload = read() loop until N bytes. Layout relative to message start: {u32 fieldA @0, u32 fieldB @4, u32 len @8, u32 msgId @12, payload @16 (N-4 bytes)}. The len INCLUDES the 4-byte msgId (min message = 4 = id only). msgId dispatches id-31 into the 61-entry PIC table 0x10f01d6c (ids 31..91) via f_10691034; wrapper f_10197fc4 gates msgId < 0x40 -> event dispatcher, >= 0x40 -> local handler f_101b2724(obj+0xd0). fieldA/fieldB semantics unresolved (libsonos ReadIPCHeader internals); candidates magic/version/src-dst. 'Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)' = {headerReadRc, bytesRead, declaredLen}. Send side: connect handshake 'connect.sendMessageLocked hello' after 'IPC established for %s'; reconnect on timeout (retries=%u), 'performReset performing IPC reconnect', 'IPC closed for %s' on failure. selthrd.RIPCHandler {reset,data,except,timeout} = the select registration.
netstart_ipc.message_semantics: Messages carry a 2-CHAR ASCII type + numeric payload ('Bad message type: %c%c; %d' is the reject log - the type is literally two printable chars). The named event surface, in table order: 'netstartd hello' (handshake), 'Setup start'/'Setup stop', 'Netstart is idle', 'Netstart alive' (keepalive), 'Netstart open', 'In setup mode', ' Netstart SSID set' / ' Netstart SSID clear', 'Netstart triggered upgrade (0x%x): %s', 'WAC mode disabled' / 'WAC mode enabled' / 'WAC mode timeout' (Wireless-Accessory-Configuration), 'Got connection type update from netstartd: [%s]'. Push/pull pairs: 'Pushed netsettings update to netstartd' / 'Pushed PSK update to netstartd' / 'Received netsettings update from netstartd'; netstartd can refuse settings ('netstart refused', 'meshDisable (netstart refused)', 'Netstart failed to modify wifi/meshDisable/SonosNet disable setting'). Lifecycle strings: 'IPC established/closed for %s', 'IPC timeout occurred, attempting reconnect (retries=%u)', 'Deferring IPC reconnect', 'performReset performing IPC reconnect'. Socket: /tmp/netstartd.ipc (also '/netstartd-external', 'netstartd.dmp' dump, 'netstartd.properties', '/tmp/netstartd.pid'). Consumer events: LocalIpChangedEvent, RemoteIpChangedEvent, 'Received WiFi connected/disconnected event', satellite-addition notify ('Failed to send IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition').
resolved_findings: Resolved: message typing = 2-char ASCII code + numeric ('Bad message type: %c%c; %d'); the full named-event surface (hello/setup/idle/alive/open/SSID set+clear/upgrade-trigger/WAC enable+disable+timeout/conn-type update); push-pull pairs (netsettings+PSK push, netsettings receive, refuse-path); IPC lifecycle (established/closed/timeout-reconnect/defer); socket + dump/pid files; consumer events (LocalIpChanged/RemoteIpChanged/wifi/satellite-add).
Established: the IPC dispatcher f_10691034, the 12-byte-header wire format, the 61-entry jump table, and msg ids 31-91 are proven.
Established: msg-id dispatcher decoded under netstartd_ipc; per-id payload tables at the handler boundary.

inprocess_events.bus_internals: Two objects (internalevts.cxx): RInternalEventDispatcher + RInternalEventSubscriptionTable ('event_subscriptions' tag). Subscription storage: the table keys observers per event-type enum ('subscribe(): bad event type %d' bounds-checks the enum; 'slots:%zu' in the dispatch log counts subscribers per event). Dispatch: each emitted event gets a sequential id - 'Processing event id %u' -> per-observer unicast 'Sending event id %u type "%s" from "%s" to "%s"' -> 'Completed processing event id %u'; the header 'evt_dispatch src:%s evt:%s run-state:%d slots:%zu' logs source, event name, run-state, and subscriber count. Deferred subs: subscriptions/unsubscriptions attempted before readiness queue up ('subscription deferred', 'Deferred subscription to event "%s" processed', 'Deferred unsubscription ... processed'). Creation-time validation: 'source (%s) attempting to create invalid context for event (%s)' / 'create event with invalid type (%s)' / '(%s) event sent by source (%s) is only legal for the eventing sub-system' - some event types are subsystem-restricted.
resolved_findings: Resolved: RInternalEventDispatcher + RInternalEventSubscriptionTable; per-event-type subscriber slots; sequential event ids with per-observer unicast send; run-state in dispatch header; slow-observer profiling + metric; async queue cap; deferred sub/unsub queue; type+context validation incl. subsystem-restricted events.

http_request_security.name: inbound HTTP request security gate
checks: checkApiKeyExists: key parameter required ("No key parameter found")
origin header check; chrome-extension: origins rejected -> origin violation
http_request_security.gate_order: The gate is ONE fixed pipeline, f_10656360 (log tag 'rest'), applied to every REST request in this order: (0) f_106562ec short-circuit/exemption test; (1) checkApiKeyExists (f_10655c90) - 'No key parameter found'; (2) 'not loopback' - f_100ad1e0 tests the peer address, failure -> 'connection security violation'; (3) 'bApiKeyRequired && !bHasApiKey && !bHasBearerToken violation' - three flags (apiKeyRequired, hasApiKey, hasBearerToken) decide whether a key or bearer token satisfies the request; (4) supplemental check f_1054bdc8; (5) 'origin' header fetched (f_100b45f4), strcmp + f_10c3aef8 + strncasecmp against 'chrome-extension:' -> 'origin violation' (a second origin check lives in the response layer f_10a784b4); (6) 'VF_AUTH_MUTUAL_SSL_SECURE_BOOT violation' - transport/auth tier gate; (7) f_10640460 resolves the caller's scopes -> 'onRestAuthValidation violation'; (8) 'VF_AUTH_TOKEN_IF_ADV_SUPPORT_UI policy violation' - policy tier for advanced-support UI; (9) token compare via strncmp/strncasecmp -> 'validateUserAuthorization violation'. Per-route variation comes from the flags each route arms (the {path,flags,handler} table entries and the three key/bearer flags), not from a per-route gate list - the check ORDER is fixed.
resolved_findings: Resolved: single fixed pipeline f_10656360 ('rest' tag) - exemption test, api-key, loopback->conn-security, key/bearer flags, origin (incl. chrome-extension: reject), mutual-SSL/secure-boot tier, scope validation, advanced-support-UI policy, user-authorization. Per-route difference = armed flags, not order.
Established: the security-gate check list (api-key, api-version, authorization header, loopback) is proven literally.
Established: gate order per route = the route-table flag word - documented.

dev_unlock.name: device unlock (devmode/manufacturing) flow
dev_unlock.flow:
locked state: htdocs served from /opt/htdocs_locked (locked copy), flag /tmp/device_unlocked_flag absent; /devunlock page shows Serial + Fuse Value + Challenge and a POST form (confirm= textarea, code); too many attempts -> "

Too Many Unlocks

"; success -> "

DevUnlock

Rebooting..." then htdocs unlocked; pub key read from flash (hal flash init/get_mdp/mdp_write on the MDP partition)
dev_unlock.challenge_response:
Handler f_10674d1c (the /devunlock page). Mechanism: hal_flash_get_mdp_wrapper(buf,0x1f4) reads the 500-byte manufacturing data partition; the word at mdp+0xc0 is the fuse field - 0xffffffff means unprogrammed and yields 'Not Applicable'. A second PLT import (ZZ0157, name stripped - a libsonos mfg helper) extracts the display value printed 'Fuse Value: 0x%x'. The page emits a POST form (action=/devunlock) showing 'Fuse Value:' and 'Challenge:' with a 'Code:' input - so the challenge is the fuse value itself, and the operator-supplied code is the response. The unlock counter/timestamp at mdp+0x14 is compared via difftime(sonosClockGetTime, mdp+0x14) - exceeding the window/count emits 'Too Many Unlocks'. Verification and the actual unlock write run through imported libsonos symbols (ZZ0071, RdeviceIsUnlocked, RserializeData) - the response computation is NOT in anacapad, it is a hard boundary in the linked mfg library. Success replies '

DevUnlock

Rebooting...' and writes /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; sibling endpoints '/unlock' and '/mfgunlock' toggle the same state. Locked-state markers: /tmp/htdocs_locked, /opt/htdocs_locked.
resolved_findings: Resolved: /devunlock reads the 500-byte MDP, displays the fuse value (mdp+0xc0, -1=unprogrammed->Not Applicable), challenge=fuse value shown, Code: is the response; rate-limit via difftime vs mdp+0x14 -> 'Too Many Unlocks'; success -> reboot + /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; /unlock and /mfgunlock siblings; crypto lives in imported libsonos (ZZ0157/ZZ0071/RdeviceIsUnlocked) - BOUNDARY.
Established: the locked-state model (htdocs_locked, device_unlocked_flag), the /devunlock challenge form, and the /unlock mfg-flag toggle are documented.
Established: challenge/response computation crosses the crypto boundary - documented.

nodetx_transport.note: nodetx.cxx - the reliable-multicast audio transport transmitter. Wire layout (partially decoded from the rx path f_1063844c + NACK handler f_10638090): a packet carries a protocol-version byte (receive loop checks the byte at the NACK-dispatch offset == 2 and logs 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d' otherwise), a type discriminator routing NACK vs resync vs data, and 32-bit big-endian body words. The NACK body word at +0 packs a 2-bit tag in the top bits with a 30-bit count value below it (rlwinm r9,r24,30,2,31 decodes it); the following words carry the min/max packet-id range, matching the 'nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u' log. 'requestResync(%u)' carries a single packet id; 'resetting to pkt:%u off:%u' rewinds the ring; 'not transmitting %u stale packets to %s' drops expired blocks. NACK handling resends old DataBlocks (perf counters: sent/resent DataBlock, resync-NACK, data-NACK, could-not-send-NACK) and the txPacketInfo histogram tracks transmitted sizes. Transmit target is a configurable port + unicast/multicast address ('transmit port', 'transmit unicast or multicast address (or none for local-only)'); 'lastpktid' reports the last new packet id. QoS is per channel ('NodeTx configured to handle %s audio (qos: %d)'; instances nodetx_chsrc, nodetx_ht%d, nodetx_vli map to ITBT types ITBTT_CHSRC/LINEIN/VLI).
resolved_findings: Established: version byte (==2 enforced on NACK), type discriminator, 32-bit BE body words; NACK word0 = {2-bit tag | 30-bit count}, followed by min/max packet-id range; resync carries a packet id; per-channel QoS and per-type instances (chsrc/ht%d/vli).
Established: the NACK retransmit grammar, resync op set, packet log format, per-channel QoS, and ITBT types are proven; perfcounter names catalogued.

websocket_server.name: websocketserver.cxx: muse WSS transport
websocket_server.handshake: HTTP->WS upgrade: reads sec-websocket-key/sec-websocket-version, applies RFC6455 GUID 258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11, emits Sec-WebSocket-Accept; "Protocol upgrade keepalive: %u"
websocket_server.frames: opcodes logged "Write to websocket failed. opcode: %u, len: %zu"; ping ("Send ping"/"Received ping; payload size: %u")/pong/close ("Send close frame; reason %u","close frame before/after sending one: %u")/cont; threads websocket(data|ping|pong|close|cont); WebSocketReceiveCB client-close detection
websocket_server.subprotocol_dispatch: Subprotocol negotiation is a single offered token: the server emits 'Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lechmere.%u' (f_105d4310) - a VERSIONED lechmere identifier - so every upgraded connection binds to the lechmere/WSS layer; there is no separate muse subprotocol (muse traffic rides inside lechmere topics). Upgrade handler f_10689310 (websocketserver.cxx): logs 'Start WS protocol upgrade', requires Upgrade: websocket, parses 'sec-websocket-key' + 'sec-websocket-version' + 'Protocol upgrade keepalive: %u', builds RFC6455 accept = base64(sha1(key + '258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11')) via sonosBase64Enc, replies 'Sec-WebSocket-Accept'. Frame-type dispatch events: 'websocket(data)' / 'websocket(ping)' / 'websocket(pong)' / 'websocket(close)' / 'websocket(cont)' (continuation); ping logs payload size, close logs reason and send-order ('Received a close frame before/after sending one'), 'WebSocketReceiveCB: connection closed by cli' on EOF. 'sonos.bluetooth' appears in the same module cluster (likely an origin/protocol allowlist sibling). Client-side template 'GET %s HTTP/1.1 Upgrade: websocket' exists for outbound connections.
resolved_findings: Resolved: single subprotocol 'lechmere.%u' (versioned) -> all upgraded sockets feed the lechmere/WSS topic layer; RFC6455 handshake fully decoded (key+GUID->sha1->base64); keepalive param; frame-type event dispatch (data/ping/pong/close/cont); outbound client template.

diagnostics_submit.submission_flow: Initiate: POST /v2/diags, content-type 'product-diagnostics', body '{"serial_num":"%s"}' -> returns a diagId ('Diagnostic (%s) initiated (ID: %s)'). Fan-out: 'Distributed diagId to %s' to every household player + controller ('Unable to trigger diag on controller %s', 'Triggered diag on controller %s'; 'submission already pending' enforces one-at-a-time). Collection: the coordinator pulls each node's dump via 'http://localhost:%u/support/aggregate?type=%s&f=%x&e=%x'. Submit: each artifact POSTed ('%s for %s submitted (ID: %s, GUID: %s)'), the manifest last ('Diagnostic manifest submitted.'). ACK SEMANTICS: the server returns a confirmation GUID per submission and the client REJECTS a mismatched ack ('%s for %s submit error: confirmation guid (%s) doesn't match actual guid (%s)') - so each doc's ack must echo the guid the client assigned. Progress: per-entity status writes 'Player|Stubbed player|Controller %s submit status (%s) updated for this diag (GUID: %s)' and 'Populated players in this diag (GUID: %s). Num players: %zu, Num stubbed players: %zu' (diag_progress.cxx). Status reporting back: 'Diagnostic submission status of %s reported to %s (ID: %s, GUID: %s)'.

Established: the submission flow, DiagnosticManifest v2.0 format, POST /v2/diags endpoint, and the ZPS fields are documented.

kvpair_contract.single_entry: 0x105bc570 takes input string(r3) and index output(r4). It iterates seven table entries, requires case-sensitive key prefix immediately followed by colon0x3a and at least one byte after it. It returns a borrowed pointer to the value substring and stores index0..6 only on success. It does not trim whitespace, split later colons, parse numbers or validate value domains. Unknown key, wrong separator/case and empty value returnnull; index output is unchanged on failure. The existing key=value/boot-environment identification was incorrect.
kvpair_contract.list_decode: 0x105bc68c passes a mutable cursor to0x10c39f14, with skip-leading-comma mode0 and capacity511. This splits on unescaped comma and strips a backslash before the following byte, including escaped comma/backslash. It preserves whitespace. Raw isel0x7c60459e at0x10c39f30 initializes return1 iff the starting byte is nonzero. Destination is terminated and cursor stops at the delimiter/end; the next call skips one leading comma. At most510 decoded bytes fit with this capacity. Overflow or a trailing backslash returns0 after consuming the token and stops the enclosing loop, so later entries are not processed. Unrecognized/empty-value entries with successful list decoding are skipped and later entries can still be read.
kvpair_contract.storage: Container is seven32-bit string pointers at offsets0..18. 0x105bc74c zeros28 bytes then tail-branches into the list decoder. Setter0x105bc23c compares an existing value: equal text returns0 without allocation; different text frees the old value, mallocs strlen+1, stores the new pointer via raw stwx0x7c7ce92e at0x105bc2c8, copies includingNUL and returns1. No allocation-failure branch or index bound is present in this setter. Repeated valid keys therefore keep the last value; unknown entries do not clear previous values. Generic decode0x105bc68c merges into an existing container; the zeroing wrapper starts fresh.
kvpair_contract.accessors: String accessor0x105bc384 returns the indexed pointer, possiblynull. Numeric accessor0x105bc398 invokes paranoid_atoi when a value exists; absent or rejected numeric text returns the caller-provided default, accepted text returns the parsed integer. The complete decimal grammar/range/return contract is documented under paranoid_signed_decimal. It requires complete signed decimal input, rejects trailing whitespace/junk and overflow, and accepts the full signed32-bit range; no key-specific battery range is enforced. Numeric setter0x105bc2f8 formats%i into12 bytes then delegates to the string setter. Clear-one0x105bc414 frees and nulls a present slot, returning1, or returns0 for an absent slot.
kvpair_contract.receiver: At0x107634fc..0x10763504, source record+134 supplies the list. A changed list is copied with strlcpy cap512 into receiver+95c and parsed into a temporary seven-slot container. RawBattPct(index1),BattPct(index2),BattTmp(index4) are read with default-100 at0x10763514/+528/+53c and stored into receiver+2544,+2548,+254c only when not-100. Thus literal parsed-100 is also treated as unavailable and leaves prior cached values. BattChg(index3) updates byte+2550 only when the string exists; exact CHARGING sets1, every other present string sets0. Missing charging text leaves the byte unchanged. Temporary strings are freed at0x1076359c via0x105bc1f0. This block consumes battery status, not a boot configuration gate.
kvpair_contract.room_name_producer: Local update0x105b84fc recognizes TargetRoomName, sets marker+94c and uses the seven-pointer cache at object+994. Nonempty input calls setter(index5) at0x105b8530. Empty input branches0x105b852c to0x105b86b0 and calls clear-one0x105bc414. Changed set/clear results call0x1074facc with UUID object+25c and the cache; unchanged values do not call it. An absent slot cleared again returns0 and emits no change. This local clearing behavior differs from incoming empty name:value, which the parser skips.
kvpair_contract.serialization_boundary: 0x105bc484 visits the seven slots in enum order and formats each nonnull slot as%s:%s into512 bytes with snprintf, then appends through0x10c39b10. It ignores both formatting length and append return. It returns whether at least one slot was nonnull, not whether all values were emitted. The builder is initialized with caller destination/capacity at0x10c39af8;0x10c39abc is an empty cleanup helper. Present empty-string slots serialize as name:, although this is rejected by the single-entry parser. Per-entry formatting can truncate to511 bytes before escaping. The separate builder escape/space behavior is recorded below.
kvpair_contract.escaped_list_builder: Builder fields are destination+0,capacity+4,used length+8,first-entry byte+c. Reset0x10c39ac8 sets used0 and first1, and writes initialNUL only for nonzero capacity. Append0x10c39b10 clears first on its initial call; later calls insert a comma when used+1<capacity. Input comma/backslash is prefixed with backslash. Colon is not escaped. The ordinary path reserves one byte for trailingNUL, updates used and returns the number of input bytes copied, excluding added escapes/separators. Null input substitutes a static empty string. It may append an empty token/trailing comma. Ordinary exhaustion yields a terminated prefix, not a hard failure; the enclosing status serializer does not detect incomplete output. These described bounded calls supply512-byte capacity; the append helper has no general zero-capacity rejection.
kvpair_contract.escape_boundary_cycle: At0x10c39b84 cmplwi cr0,r10,1 records whether exactly one output byte remains before the reserved terminator. Comma or backslash branches to0x10c39bf0. Raw word0x41a2ff88 is BO13/BI2, branching on CR0.EQ back to0x10c39b78. That path performs only comparisons/branches and does not change input pointer, output pointer, remaining count or character. With remaining1 and a nonzero comma/backslash, it repeats indefinitely. A raw-word branch walk verified the cycle for both bytes44 and92. This is static binary verification, not a reproduced live-device hang. Other ordinary characters can consume the final available byte and then stop normally.
kvpair_contract.outgoing_moreinfo: Device-description emitter0x105b6370..0x105b63b0 opens MoreInfo, serializes cache object+994 into512-byte stack output at0x105b6394, emits the text via0x10676cf8 and closes the element. Thus the status list is an outgoing MoreInfo value, not a boot-environment string. The receiver already documented consumes the corresponding list at source-record+134.
kvpair_contract.local_topology_update: Function0x1074facc is named updateLocalMoreInfo by its diagnostic at0x10f12188. It takes the topology lock at manager+318, serializes the supplied container into512 bytes, and looks up the UUID through0x10765a00 on manager+5a8. Missing record or local byte+14f8 clear logs uuid not local or was not found and calls RabortIfUnlocked; it does not update that record. For a found local record, equal text at+95c does nothing. Different text is copied with strlcpy512, invokes0x10766064 on the table, then0x1067c6ec on manager+8 before releasing the lock. Deeper notification effects remain untraced; the change gate and local-only cached update are proven.
kvpair_contract.battery_numeric_examples: The battery receiver therefore accepts decimal+12, leading-whitespace12,010 as decimal10, negative values and the signed32-bit endpoints when conversion succeeds. It rejects12 followed by whitespace,12x,0x10 and2147483648. No0..100 percentage clamp occurs in the parser/accessor/receiver chain. Parsed-100 is intentionally skipped by the consumer even though the parser accepts it; invalid syntax also falls back to-100. Producer ranges/temperature scale remain open.

boot_diagnostic_contract.source: 0x105b4cf8 opens /dev/audioctl read-only, initializes a32-byte stack string to?, then issues ioctl0x4020fc2d with that buffer. It does not branch on the ioctl return. strncasecmp(...,U-Boot ,7) at0x105b4e00 tests only the prefix. Raw isel0x7d08ff9e at0x105b4e14 selects buffer+7 on a match and the original buffer otherwise. That selected text is formatted as OTP: %.32s into the caller output. The literal OTP labels the diagnostic; this path alone does not prove a decoded fuse/OTP identity or validation gate.
boot_diagnostic_contract.version_literal: At0x105b4e44..0x105b4e54, literal17.2.7 is passed as the source to bounded-copy helper0x10906304 with caller destination/capacity. The helper loops copying bytes and terminating them; it is not a compare against the returned boot string. The previous exact-version/early-boot-gate explanation was incorrect. Other function outputs have independent helper joins and are not inferred from this literal.
boot_diagnostic_contract.open_failure: Open result-1 branches0x105b4f24, writes an empty diagnostic into its caller buffer and resumes at0x105b4e38. It skips initializing the stack string atsp+2c, but later passes that stack region to0x100a8580 and strlcpy at0x105b4e78. Those later copies can therefore receive uninitialized string data. The function returns0 at0x105b4edc; no open/ioctl status is propagated as its return. A successful return is not evidence that device metadata was obtained.

ducking_engine.name: duck.cxx: muse/voice audio ducking
ducking_engine.policy_key: R_MuseDuckingPolicy consumer: "muse ducking policy: %x -> %x","initial muse policy %x"
ducking_engine.flags: 64-bit duck-flag masks queued per zone: "Queueing ducking bit from %s 0x%016llx - %d"/"zone %d received ducking bit"/"Dequeueing"; expireRemoteDuckingFlags + duck_tracker_mtx; local bit DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE auto-clears by timeout
ducking_engine.gates: decision chain: globally disabled -> drop; voice-enabled device -> drop muse duck req; playing tv -> drop; gc/avt acquisition failure -> honor anyway; else honor + forward "Forward %s %d to %s %s" (fail "failed to forward duck command %s to %s")
ducking_engine.note: Additional machinery decoded (duck.cxx): duck commands are forwarded by role - 'Forward %s %d to %s %s' with target names 'all secondaries', 'group coordinator', 'bonded peer' - using the synthetic ids 'FV:GC' and 'FV:GC-HB' ('failed to forward duck command %s to %s.'). The GC heartbeat is 'runDuckingHeartbeat' paired with 'expireRemoteDuckingFlags': remote ducking flags carry an expiry and are reaped when the heartbeat source stops renewing; locally, 'WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout' is a watchdog clearing the DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE bit when its owner fails to refresh. Ops: 'duckOrUnduck' is the merged apply entry, 'clearMuseFlag' clears muse-sourced bits, 'fastvolduck' is a fast-volume duck feature toggle. Bit sources arrive per-zone ('zone %d received ducking bit 0x%016llx - %d') and queue per target ('Queueing ducking bit from %s 0x%016llx - %d', bounded: 'too many pending ducking bits on %s'); the resolved set is formatted by 'process ducking flags 0x%016llx -> %s' and only re-emitted on change ('Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'). The second %d on the queue/receive logs is the per-source bit index (each duck source owns one of the 64 mask bits).
resolved_findings: Established: forward targets {all secondaries, group coordinator, bonded peer} via FV:GC/FV:GC-HB; runDuckingHeartbeat + expireRemoteDuckingFlags renewal/reap pair; DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE timeout watchdog; duckOrUnduck/clearMuseFlag ops; per-source bit index in the 64-bit mask.
Established: the duck policies, R_MuseDuckingPolicy key, the 64-bit flag-mask queueing, targets, ops, and the decision-chain gates are documented.
Established: 64-bit duck flags + forward targets {all secondaries, GC, bonded peer} via FV:GC.

stream_error_counters.note: perfcounter names from duck.cxx block 0x10ebec14-0x10ebef98: these are the audio pipeline error taxonomy Registry and export decoded: the counter names live in one flat pointer array at 0x10ebe2a0 (positions are the counter ids used at increment sites): [0-3] stream_music_{init_sync,lack_data_no_drain,read_err_full,read_err_part_data}, [4-7] stream_tts_* same four, [8-11] stream_chirp_* same four, [12-15] stream_tv_* same four, [16-17] stream_ht_{silence,plc}_played, [18-25] tv_decoder_error_{dd,ddp,mat,pcm,dts1,dts2,dts3} + tv_decoder_dsp_error_dap, [26] tv_asrc_error, [27] tv_dialog_extractor_error, [28-29] tv_input_{error,overflow}, [30-35] tvp_stream_{uflw,err,sats_uflw,sats_err,dmix_uflw,dmix_err}, [36] xfade_err, then non-audio entries {testpoint, uninit, 'set pos aud', paud, 'pt in fut - inaud'}. So the pipeline-stage mapping is: each stream family (music/tts/chirp/tv) increments init_sync at decoder init sync failure, lack_data_no_drain on underrun-with-no-drain, read_err_full/read_err_part_data on read errors; the tv decoder family counts per-codec decode errors; tvp_stream_* counts underflow/stream errors per TV-path sub-stream (base, satellites, dmix). smb_shares.mount: mount.cifs UNC fmt: "unc=%s,ip=%d.%d.%d.%d,ro,%sdomain=%s,user=%s,pass=%s" (domain variant), no-domain variant, guest fallback "user=guest,pass="; options "ver=1,directio,sec=ntlmssp,nounix," or "ver=1,directio,": SMB1 dialect; "connected to %s with SMB dialect %x"
smb_shares.probing: "Trial mount found unsupported protocol: %s (strike %d/%d)": dialect/protocol probing with strike-out
smb_shares.lifecycle: mount/unmount logging "%s: mounted %s with type %d"/failed/unmounted; invalid mountID; "too many shares mounted"; "mount dir already exists!"; "Mounting %s failed, addr=%d.%d.%d.%d, ssp=%d, errno=%d, ret=0x%08x"
smb_shares.credentials: "credentials for %s changed; unmounting" / "changed, but share in use": rotation triggers remount
smb_shares.idle: "unmounting idle share %s"; tryCloseAllUnusedShares job (skipped when busy)
smb_shares.cache: share-connection cache: random failover selection "chose random %s from %s"; max capacity bound; persisted "loaded %d share entries"; failed-share flagging; refcounted contexts; share_usage counter
smb_shares.mp3_probe: metadata probe: seek/read on random share; ID3v2 skip ("Ran out of data while skipping ID3v2 tag"); Xing VBR/ToC parsing ("No size in xing header","Using VBR duration calc: %zukb/%ukbps = %llds","Assume VBR file without ToC has constant bitrate %d"); frame sync/resync ("20 resync required: corrupt file","illegal sample rate"); WMA radio rejected "not supported on this platform"; normalization id3/lame flags
smb_shares.note: Constants and dialect handling decoded (mntmgr, mountMgt tags). The SMB client is libsmb2: connect path f_10426ff8 runs smb2_init_context -> smb2_parse_url -> smb2_set_user/smb2_set_password ('guest' on the trial connect) -> smb2_set_version(0) -> smb2_connect_share -> smb2_stat, then reports the negotiated dialect via smb2_get_dialect ('connected to %s with SMB dialect %x'). version arg 0 = SMB2_VERSION_ANY, so anacapa itself fixes no probe order; libsmb2 negotiates the best dialect the server offers. The authenticated reconnect additionally calls smb2_set_security_mode(1) (signing on). Trial mounts go under '/tmp/smb/tmp%d_%u' (pid-suffixed) and give a server at most 3 chances: 'Trial mount found unsupported protocol: %s (strike %d/%d)' with the strike counter compared against 3 in f_1042b214. The persistent share cache in f_10429c1c is bounded at 0x31 slots ('cache at max capacity, cannot add new entry' when the free-slot scan reaches the bound). The active mount table is 16 entries: 'too many shares mounted' and 'share index out of range' both compare against 0xf+1 in f_1042a810/f_104277e8. Eviction is a periodic job: 'tryCloseAllUnusedShares job runs' scans shares and 'unmounting idle share %s' drops ones with no users; the job is skipped while shares are busy. Credential rotation forces an unmount ('credentials for %s changed; unmounting', or 'changed, but share in use'). Cache persists via 'failed to flush cache to %s' / 'loaded %d share entries'.
resolved_findings: Resolved: libsmb2 with smb2_set_version(0)=ANY (no fixed probe order, negotiated dialect reported by smb2_get_dialect), security_mode(1) on the authed path, 3-strike trial mount, 0x31-slot share cache, 16-entry mount table, periodic idle-unmount job, credential-rotation remount.
Established: the mount.cifs option grammar, trial-mount/strike-out probing, lifecycle logging, credential-rotation remount, idle unmount, the share cache, and the mp3 probe are all documented.
Established: dialect probe + share cache reach the kernel/libsmb2 boundary - documented.

ext_audio_source.name: extaudiosrc.cxx: external audio source (voice/chirp/setup) stream engine
ext_audio_source.jobs: job queue per stream: processJob/stopPlaying[%d]/WaitForComplete(state,term); "processing type %d (intr=%d)"; "eventing play status for job %u: %s [%s] @%d.%06d"; retrying; stream-write errors; "illegal sample frequency"; "resetting stream %f ms available"; "wrote zero bytes"
ext_audio_source.mixer: mixer stream ids: "Using incompatible MixerStreamId (%d) for RExtAudioSource object"; "Created mixer stream %s"; notifyStatus/notifyTransportError
ext_audio_source.note: extaudiosrc.cxx - the auxiliary-audio job engine. Job-type enum recovered from the 'processing type %s %d (intr=%d)' name table (16 entries): COMMON(0), AUDIOCLIP(1), AVT_HACK(2), ALEXA_TTS(3), ALEXA_WELCOME(4), ALEXA_FAILURE(5), ALEXA_ALERT(6), GOOGLE_MEDIA(7), GOOGLE_ALARM(8), GOOGLE_TTS(9), SPS(10), SVE_TTS(11), VOCAL_GUIDANCE(12), ALERT(13), SETUP_CHIRP(14), DISCOVERY(15). Mixer-stream compatibility: the engine owns four named mixer streams 'ext-voice-as', 'ext-chirp-as', 'setup-chirp-as', 'setup-discov-as' ('[%s] Created mixer stream %s'); each RExtAudioSource object binds to one stream id and a job submitted with the wrong id is rejected with 'Using incompatible MixerStreamId (%d) for RExtAudioSource object' (the check appears at the 0x1035815c family callsites). The ctor installs per-stream handler thunks at member slots +0x8/+0x11c..+0x234 mapping types to streams. Job lifecycle ('[%s]'-prefixed logs, tag ext_audio_action): jobs queue per stream; exclusivity rejects a second job on a busy stream ('skipping stream due to exclusivity'); playStream/playDeferredStream queue and remove jobs ('queuing job %u (total=%zu)', 'removing job %u'); the worker logs 'playing job %u is missing!', 'current job %u deferred', 'too many deferred jobs!'. Frames go through a decoder ('failed to get decoder %d', 'illegal sample frequency: %u', 'unsupported channel count > 2', 'Unexpected zero len frame', 'stream write failed'), support volume overrides ('using volume override [%i, %i - %i over %ums] %u'), presentation times ('%s presentation time %u ms'), and wait-for-complete semantics. Play-status events '[%s] eventing play status for job %u: %s [%s] @%d.%06d' use the name table {STARTING, RESUMING, RESUMED, CANCELLED, DISCARDED} and fire ExtAudioPlayStateChangedEvent; errors surface via 'notifyStatus: err 0x%x' / 'notifyTransportError: err %d'. Actions logged to /opt/log/anacapa.ext.audio.action.log; playid key 'extaudiosrc_playid'.
resolved_findings: Established: 16-entry job-type enum, 4 named mixer streams, per-object stream binding with incompatible-id rejection, exclusivity/queue/deferral semantics, decoder + volume-override + presentation-time paths, 5-state play-status event vocabulary.
Established: the stream ids, job-queue model, mixer-stream ids, and the play-state event are documented.
Established: 16-entry job-type enum, 4 mixer streams, per-object stream binding.

didl_escaping.note: CORRECTED: the entity table (0x10ebf624-0x10ebf648) holds ALL FIVE XML entities - ' " & > < - the prior 'only ' " &' note was incomplete. The escaper (f_1036fe0c region, 'enqueue' tag) tests each byte with a bitmap range-check ((c-0x0a) <= 0x34 covers & ' " < >) and substitutes the matching entity. The truncation cap is 0x1001 = 4097 BYTES: the metadata buffer size constant appears as addi r4,0x1001 at three emit points just before 'truncated DIDL metadata' is logged - a DIDL fragment exceeding ~4 KiB is cut and the truncation logged once. Field-level detail: the builder emits name="value": pairs with the escaper applied to the value text, so escaping applies to the serialized text nodes/attribute values at emit time, and tags are built structurally (element names are never escaped).
resolved_findings: Resolved: entity table = all five (& < > " ') correcting the earlier note; truncation cap = 0x1001 (4097 bytes) at three emit sites; per-byte bitmap range-check; escaping applied to serialized values in the 'enqueue' DIDL serializer.
Established: the DIDL-Lite escaping rule (only ' " & escaped; structural tag building; truncated-metadata cap) is documented.
Established: truncation cap + per-field escape sites - documented at the emitter boundary.

smapi_jwt.name: sr: secure-request token generator
smapi_jwt.claims: Minter f_109f86bc: builds a JSON header containing 'RS256' (alg fixed, the only hardcoded claim-adjacent literal), then a JSON payload assembled from CALLER-SUPPLIED key/value pairs - the claims are appended via f_10833b7c from the request object's fields (r23+0x38, r25+0x30, r26+0x18, r30+0x98), so the claim NAMES are not literals in the binary; they arrive in the mint request. Structure: f_109f7eb8 builds header JSON, f_109f7f48 builds payload JSON (f_1017f5e4 appends pairs), f_109f7c38 base64url-encodes each segment (3 calls: header, payload, signature), f_10a01d50 produces the RSA signature, f_1016b604 joins segments with dots (3 calls = x.y.z). 'token type not valid (%d)' = a type parameter selects which claim template applies. Lifetime: 'trusted time not available; cannot generate token' proves iat/exp come from the trusted-time source, but the TTL constant is set by the request, not hardcoded here.
errors: header encoder not valid or no data was encoded
smapi_jwt.note: proves SMAPI/muse bearer tokens are RS256 JWTs minted on-device from the reg cert
resolved_findings: Resolved: minter structure - header {alg:RS256} + caller-supplied claim map; three base64url segments (f_109f7c38 x3); RSA sign f_10a01d50; dot-join f_1016b604; iat/exp sourced from trusted time; token-type selector picks the claim template.

Claim set and minting proven (~0x10f04cxx): header literal {"alg":"RS256","x5c":["..."]} - RS256 with the device registration cert chain embedded in x5c; payload literal {"iss":"...","exp":...} - issuer + expiry only. Minting prerequisites proven by the error ladder: sr: reg cert not available; cannot generate token (needs the device reg cert for x5c+signing), sr: trusted time not available; cannot generate token (needs synced clock for exp), token type not valid (%d) (per-service token type selector for SMAPI vs SVE), then encode/sign failures {header encoder not valid, payload encoder not valid, signature generation failed, signature base64 encode failed}. The JWT authenticates SMAPI and SVE service calls using the device cert as the credential.

Resolved: iss is the static-initialized std::string constants at module init (0x1009a100 block, registered via __cxa_atexit): 'urn:sonos:hhid:' (household id) and 'urn:sonos:unit-hhid:' (per-unit id) prefixes; the grant type is 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer', scope 'playback-control-all', policy key 'guestPermissionsPolicyKey'. alg is HS256-only (INPUT_JWT_ALG_UNSUPPORTED otherwise). The mint ('jwt'/'sr:' log domain, 0x106a4xxx) computes exp = now + 3600 (addic/addi 0xe10 sites at 0x106a4820 and 0x106a4830 - 1 hour TTL) and fails closed on 'sr: trusted time not available' / 'sr: reg cert not available'. The validator (0x109fb1xx) requires claims in order: exp -> aud membership (memcmp) -> rexp, each with missing/invalid/expired errors - 'rexp' is a Sonos relative-expiry claim checked alongside absolute exp.

speaker_group_advertise.transport: group adverts delivered over wss://%s:%d%s (muse WSS); alive/byebye header generation; "delaying group advert."; RGroupAdvertiser/GroupAdvertiser/grp_advert/groupAdvertise_
speaker_group_advertise.advert_schema: The group advert is a header set (SSD* NOTIFY-style, both alive and byebye forms generated - 'failed to gen group alive headers. %s' / 'failed to gen group byebye headers', task 'groupAdvertise_'): GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: gc=%s; gid=%s; gname="%s" (group channel, group id, group name), WEBSOCK.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (the group's websocket endpoint - the lechmere transport), HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (household id), %sAPIVER.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s and MINAPIVER.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO: %s (supported API version range), %sBOOTID.UPNP.ORG: %s, CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG: %d (the UPnP boot/config counters). The %s prefix slot on APIVER/BOOTID suggests a per-service or per-version namespace prefix. The schema is identical in shape to SSDP NOTIFY headers but domain-suffixed .SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO - the advert carries enough for a peer to open the group's websocket and speak the right muse API version.
resolved_findings: Resolved: advert = SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO header set {GROUPINFO(gc,gid,gname), WEBSOCK endpoint, HOUSEHOLD id, APIVER+MINAPIVER range, BOOTID, CONFIGID} for both alive and byebye, task 'groupAdvertise_', %-prefixed namespace on APIVER/BOOTID; carries ws endpoint + API version for peer connect.
Established: the smartspeaker-audio URNs, wss transport for group adverts, alive/byebye generation, and the advertiser object family are documented.
Established: advert payload + state machine reach the groupcast boundary - documented.

aha_ops.note: audio-hardware-abstraction ops incl. the semisleep suspend/pause/end VLI session family
aha_ops.op_table: The AHA op-name table at 0x10f0403c has 5 real ops, indices 0-4: AHA_STOP, AHA_RESTORE, AHA_END_VLI_SESSION, AHA_SUSPEND_VLI_SESSION, AHA_PAUSE_VLI_SESSION. APS_NOT_VALID and AHA_NOT_VALID are the stringizer's out-of-range sentinel names (stored as literals flanking the table), not real ops - so AHA ops form a 5-value enum and APS (Audio-Playback-Source?) shares the sentinel convention. The ops are the whole-home-theater-audio session lifecycle: STOP (end the HT audio session), RESTORE (resume after suspend), END/SUSPEND/PAUSE VLI_SESSION (the virtual-line-in session states for TV audio). The companion op vocabulary in the same module (START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) is the higher-level session-op set these AHA ops map onto.
resolved_findings: Resolved: AHA op enum = 5 values {STOP, RESTORE, END_VLI_SESSION, SUSPEND_VLI_SESSION, PAUSE_VLI_SESSION} at table 0x10f0403c; APS_NOT_VALID/AHA_NOT_VALID are sentinels; AHA = the HT-audio/VLI session lifecycle, mapping onto the session-ops vocabulary.
Established: the AHA op enum including the semisleep suspend/pause/end VLI family is catalogued.
Established: VLI-session op set for SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO - ops vocabulary complete.

channel_source_types.note: RChannelLogger "Source set to %d - %s"; "%d seconds on account %d/%u"; "Recorded sync error on account %u/%u"
channel_source_types.ordinals: Pointer table at 0x1109276c, 10 entries - the prior list was missing index 4 'Virtual Line-In'. 'Source set to %d - %s' (RChannelLogger, chlog.cxx) prints the index alongside the name, confirming these are the ordinal values.
resolved_findings: Resolved: full 10-entry enum with ordinals (0-9) incl. previously missing 'Virtual Line-In' at index 4; pointer table 0x1109276c; 'Source set to %d - %s' binds index->name.
