txst_enum.transitions: Six members (TXST_UNKNOW was missing). Transitions are op-driven, not a free FSM: the companion op table in the same cluster (START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) names the triggers. Mapping: a channel-source stream start -> TXST_CHSRC; line-in streaming -> TXST_LINE_IN; home-theater satellite mesh -> TXST_HTA_MESH; virtual-line-in session (JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE) -> TXST_VLI; PAUSE/SUSPEND/BECOME_STANDALONE -> TXST_NONE (not transmitting); TXST_UNKNOW = the never-set/default state. So TXST records WHICH transmit path owns the stream: CHSRC = SonosNet channel-source, LINE_IN = wired input re-broadcast, HTA_MESH = the satellite TV-audio mesh, VLI = virtual line-in, NONE = idle, UNKNOW = uninitialized.
resolved_findings: Resolved: 6-member enum incl. missing TXST_UNKNOW (default); transitions driven by the session-ops {START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START/PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE} - TXST names the owning transmit path (chsrc/line-in/hta-mesh/vli/none/unknow).
Established: the transmission-source state enum is catalogued.
Established: TXST_* enum complete; transition rules at the session-FSM boundary.

telemetry_endpoints.writer: zonereportmgr "wrote %zu bytes"/"open or response to %s failed with %x"
telemetry_endpoints.payload_format: Two uploader clients (zonereportmgr.cxx). eventUploaderClient POSTs '/data/submit.aspx' with headers 'POST %s HTTP/1.1'/'HOST: %s:%u'/'CONNECTION: close'/'USER-AGENT: %s'/'CONTENT-TYPE: text/xml'/'CONTENT-ENCODING: gzip'/'TRANSFER-ENCODING: chunked'/'X-Sonos-SWGen: %u' - the event payload is a gzipped XML stream uploaded chunked ('Sending Report Header' then 'Sending Report Data' phases). protoEventUploaderClient POSTs '/binary' with 'CONTENT-TYPE: application/octet-stream', 'CONTENT-LENGTH: %zu', 'X-Sonos-MessageType: product-data-telemetry' - the protobuf event serialization uploaded as one binary body. 'triecatstore' is the on-device categorized event store (trie-organized categories) that both readers drain; 'wrote %zu bytes'/'write error' are its persistence logs. So schema = XML event documents for the legacy channel and protobuf event records for the binary channel; the X-Sonos-SWGen header tags the software generation on every upload.
resolved_findings: Resolved: two clients - eventUploaderClient (XML, gzip, chunked, submit.aspx, X-Sonos-SWGen) and protoEventUploaderClient (protobuf, octet-stream, /binary, X-Sonos-MessageType: product-data-telemetry); triecatstore is the categorized trie store; write logging.
Established: the /binary + /data/submit.aspx paths, the triecatstore event store, the uploader clients, and the writer logs are catalogued.
Established: payload format + store schema reach the transport boundary - documented.

wifi_idle_roles.note: RZPWifiIdleMgr: idle-scan mgmt "Device set to %08x with primary chan %d code 0x%x cnt %u retry %u"; WifiFuncsSetIdleScan fronthaul; WiFiIdleScanUpdateRetry; "client %s is %s with primary chan %d" Role vocabulary decoded from wifi_idle_mgr.cxx: the role byte indexes an 8-entry name table - AUDIO_OUT(0), AUDIO_IN(1), LOCAL_SONOSNET(2), NO_SONOSNET_PEERS(3), NO_PRIMARY(4), UPGRADING(5), HT_SWAP(6), UNKNOWN_ID(7). f_106b0330 resolves a client's role to its name for the 'client %s is %s with primary chan %d' log. The roles read as reasons a client is (dis)qualified as the idle-scan radio: a client carrying audio out/in traffic or in UPGRADING/HT_SWAP transitions is treated differently than an idle LOCAL_SONOSNET or peerless one. The manager f_106addb8 ('Device set to %08x with primary chan %d code 0x%x cnt %u retry %u') then programs the pick into the fronthaul via WifiFuncsSetIdleScan with {primary channel, code, count, retry} parameters, logging 'Set WifiFuncsSetIdleScan fronthaul result %d attempt %d' (WiFiIdleScanUpdateRetry retries).
resolved_findings: Established: 8-role name table (AUDIO_OUT/AUDIO_IN/LOCAL_SONOSNET/NO_SONOSNET_PEERS/NO_PRIMARY/UPGRADING/HT_SWAP/UNKNOWN_ID) resolved per client; chosen device programmed via WifiFuncsSetIdleScan {chan,code,cnt,retry} with update-retry loop.
Established: the idle-role enum and the RZPWifiIdleMgr idle-scan machinery are catalogued.
Established: 8-role table {AUDIO_OUT, AUDIO_IN, LOCAL_SONOSNET, NO_SONOSNET_PEERS, ...} decoded.

wakelock_guard.note: modifyPreventIdleLockForOperationTimeout / modifyWakeLockForOperationTimeout must be guard-acquired or ERROR Guard mechanics decoded: two manager singletons, 'powPrvntIdlM' (prevent-idle-lock) at f_106a4f78 and 'powWakLkMgr' (wake-lock) at f_106ad594, expose a modify*LockForOperationTimeout(op:int, timeout:longlong) entry. Each modify call verifies the calling object's vtable slot (powPrvntIdlM checks vfunc+0xa4 identity against guard type f_106a4de8; powWakLkMgr checks +0xa8 against f_106ad3d4) and refuses with 'ERROR: modify*LockForOperationTimeout(%d, %lld) not acquired by guard' (return 0x80000038) unless the caller is the RAII guard class. Guard ctors f_106ad4ac/f_106ad760 take (manager, op id, timeout) and perform the acquire; scope exit releases. Observed holds: f_1061a4c8 acquires op 0x1e via the guard then modifies op 0 with timeout 0xb4 (180, units not printed) and registers op 0x36; f_1065b8a4 (customer-account path, near 'R_CustomerID' reads) guards op 0x1e and registers op 0x1e0. So the guard enumerates operations by small integer ids and each acquire specifies its own timeout; the lock is per-operation, not global.
resolved_findings: Established: two managers (powPrvntIdlM / powWakLkMgr); modify*LockForOperationTimeout refuses non-guard callers (vtable-identity check, 0x80000038); RAII guard ctors f_106ad4ac/f_106ad760; observed op ids 0, 0x1e, 0x36, 0x1e0 and a 180-unit timeout.
Established: the guard-acquire requirement on modifyPreventIdleLock/modifyWakeLock timeout calls is documented.
Established: two managers {powPrvntIdlM, powWakLkMgr} + modify*LockForOperationTimeout refs.

rincon_uuid.derivation: The UDN is 'uuid:RINCON_' + <12-hex-MAC> + '01400' - proven by the update-path format 'RINCON_%s01400 updated to %s' (f_102a8100, the %s is the pre-rendered identity/MAC string and 01400 is a fixed suffix appended to every UDN), the literal 'RINCON_000E58VLIDID01400' (000E58 = the Sonos MAC OUI, VLIDID = the template slot where the runtime value lands), and the all-F's test literal 'RINCON_FFFFFFFFFFFF99999'. So the identity field is the device's MAC rendered as 12 hex digits and 01400 is a constant trailer (present on every unit's UDN, not a per-model value). Eight sites format with the 'RINCON_' prefix directly (f_1011d6ac, f_10121494, f_1035c43c, f_104bf82c, f_10551ec4, f_106beae8, f_1073f730, f_10764520) - the MAC string is composed once and reused; the separate '%08X%08X%04hX%08X...' printf is a different identifier rendering (grouped hex for diagnostics), not the UDN.
resolved_findings: Resolved: UDN = 'uuid:RINCON_' + 12-hex-MAC + '01400' fixed trailer; MAC carries the 000E58 Sonos OUI; 'VLIDID' literal is the template slot; 8 prefix-formatting sites enumerated; the multi-field %08X printf is a separate diagnostic id, not the UDN.
Established: the RINCON_ UUID printf format (8+8+4+8x7 hex) is documented.
Established: identity derivation reaches the device-cert boundary - documented.

mdns_stack.name: mdns_{device_service,discovery,listener} + mdns_spotify_service
mdns_stack.txt: TXT record diffs applied keywise: update/duplicate-ignore/replace/remove; version gate "Sonos mDNS TXT record for %s is older version or missing keys"; household filter "%s is not in our household: discovered:%s - ours:%s"; payload "Notify topology of %s at %s; bootseq=%u; ports={%u-%u}; mdnssequence={old %u new %u}": TXT carries bootseq + port range + sequence counter
mdns_stack.lifecycle: discovered/bye-bye: "Unknown player %s went bye-bye" + reason ("QRCB: Update bye-bye reason to %s","BRCB: Notify topology %s went bye-bye; reason: %s"); "Re-discovered a player"; "%s is local; ignoring"; stub URI stub://stub:%u
mdns_stack.dnsservice: DNSService{CreateConnection,Browse,Resolve,QueryRecord} on br0, domain local.; mDNS Listener thread + poll loop; error-restart "Attempt # %zu"; callback table reallocated; "Ignoring startBrowse during shutdown"
mdns_stack.announce: addService %s | %s on port %u; updateTxtRecord; SvcRegRecord Reply: /mdnsannounce ResendTriggers this
mdns_stack.note: The _sonos._tcp. publisher has17 TXT keys including optional/incremental keys (see mdns_device). Counter+0x360 is an explicitly incremented u16, while TXT upserts/removals/replacements do not bump it. Peer0x106beae8 logs and stores received sequence without a monotonic-order check. Its key ladder parses attributes; it does not define local bump exemptions. Controller updates suppress exact duplicate values/maps and commit only after DNS success.
resolved_findings: Initial builder0x105e3538 publishes14 keys: info=prefix+UUID+/info; vers=literal5 at0x10fe4b00; protovers; minApiVersion; bootseq from+0x200 provider; hhid from player household helper; location from0x105aa108; mhhid from+0x1f8 provider slot+0x10; sslport; hhsslport; uuid; variant; mdnssequence from controller slot+0x20; wss=/websocket/api. locationid is optional when its provider string is nonempty. infohash is optional when weak provider locks successfully and0x10a062b0 supplies a value. byebyereason is an incremental update key, not in initial map. Thus the publisher vocabulary has17 keys including optional/incremental keys, not9. Controller builder0x106bc370 walks map entries, calling TXTRecordSetValue(key,u8 length,value) using the low byte of stored string length; no extra length rejection is in that adapter. DNS-SD library builds the TXT wire records and0x106c258c calls DNSServiceUpdateRecord with TXTRecordGetLength/GetBytesPtr. Scalar TXT values are decimal strings, not packed endian integers.

Controller vptr0x10f066dc: +8=register0x106bca9c,+0xc=update0x106bcf7c,+0x10=unregister0x106bc898,+0x14=start discovery0x106bc5a0,+0x18=shutdown-discovery adapter0x106bc360 (adjusts this+0x278 and tail-branches at0x106bc36c to0x106bf878; stops browse/resolve tokens and clears discovered-peer state),+0x1c=increment0x106bc2f4,+0x20=sequence getter0x106bc2e4,+0x24=TXT population0x106bc370.0x106bcf7c locks controller+0x20, looks up registered key, clones current map and implements modes0=upsert,1=remove specified keys,2=replace full map. Exact duplicate values or maps skip DNS update; removal of absent keys is ignored. On a real change populate TXT, call adapter slot+0x10, and commit the new map only on DNS success. Unknown service, TXT population failure, or DNS update failure returns0/logs; unchanged valid updates return1. None of these modes modifies the sequence counter or inserts a new mdnssequence key automatically.

Peer TXT parser0x106beae8 enumerates keys via TXTRecordGetItemAtIndex; vers must be>=3, bootseq must parse/present, hhid/location/UUID must be nonempty and mdnssequence conversion must succeed. Missing UUID can be recovered by extracting RINCON_ up to slash from location. bootseq uses strtoul base10; sslport/hhsslport use strtol then low16 mask; sequence uses paranoid_atoi then low16 retention. Household mismatch produces a defunct-device notification unless0x1075df68 identifies that UUID as the local player: it finds a valid topology record and returns its is-local byte+0x14f8. Constructor0x10762464 initializes that byte0; local-player record update0x1074dfec sets1 at0x1074e3fc. Consumer0x10749e64 explicitly logs isLocalZPIdle: uuid not local or was not found when+0x14f8 is0. This exception is local-player identity, not a generic trusted-device or cross-household permission flag. New bye-bye reason is stored at peer+0x44 and suppresses regular topology announce in that callback; the next callback without a bye-bye reason clears it. Otherwise topology notification is built with location, bootseq and stub://stub:port URIs through0x1054a688/0x105a51d8. Incoming sequence is logged beside old peer+0x5c then assigned to+0x5c at0x106bf244. There is NO old<new or equality gate on this sequence. The key ladder parses named attributes; it is not an exemption policy controlling local counter bumps.

Controller ctor0x106bc75c initializes u16+0x360=0 at0x106bc820/0x106bc85c. Getter0x106bc2e4 loads it; increment0x106bc2f4 locks controller+0x20, adds1 and sth at0x106bc32c, wrapping65535->0. The upstream receiver is now concrete: RZonePlayer ctor0x1018d27c calls embedded zoneImpl ctor0x10691e00 with this+0x3a8 at0x1018da0c. That ctor installs the MdnsController pointer at embedded+0x938; therefore outer player+0xce0 is the same pointer. Address-notification worker0x101931a8 loads outer+0xce0 at0x1019348c, loads controller vptr+0x1c at0x10193494, and bctrl at0x1019349c invokes0x106bc2f4. This is the increment, not publisher rename. The input-this adapter0x101935f0 subtracts0x3a8 then tail-branches at0x101935f4 to that worker.

0x101931a8 first compares new address string against stored outer+0x4b0. Its update flag is0 if addresses are equal, OR if stored address is not0.0.0.0 and ContinueAfterIPChange is false. Flag is1 for a changed address when old address is0.0.0.0 or ContinueAfterIPChange is true. The controller increment occurs ONLY in update==0 branch at0x10193484..0x1019349c; update==1 takes the full rebind/report path without increment. Thus an unchanged-address notification increments sequence, while initial address acquisition and permitted full rebinding do not. Config getter0x105e7370 reads BSS byte0x110a6a95, initially0. Setter0x105e7384 writes it; option callback0x100bdc08 recognizes ContinueAfterIPChange and sets true only when strcasecmp(value,true)==0 (call0x100bdd24). The address worker always calls0x10690d44: equal-address notification logs same addr; changed address rebinds when old is0.0.0.0 or option true, otherwise follows the shutdown-for-new-IP path. A rejected rebind can therefore increment before deferred shutdown; do not simplify the predicate to any address change.

After either address branch,0x101931a8 calls0x10690298 on the embedded zoneImpl. It shuts down discovery via controller+0x18, calls the derived zoneImpl+0x48 refresh hook, then restarts discovery via controller+0x14. RZonePlayer installs derived vptr0x10e98278 at0x1018dbd0; slot+0x48 is0x1017fa90, whose adjusted-this tail branch0x1017fa94 reaches0x1017fa08. That hook visits media players through0x1040e4cc with functor0x1018038c. Functor invokes stop0x103f7688 then start0x103f766c. Those tail bctr sites0x103f76a0/0x103f7684 use player+0x1a2c, the MdnsDeviceService installed by ctor chain0x103fc938->0x105e083c, dispatching slots+0x14/+0x10 to0x105e25c0/0x105e42cc. Stop clears registration key; start rebuilds the initial TXT map if normal name/UUID/enable gates pass.0x105e3538 then reads controller+0x20 at0x105e3ad0 and renders the new sequence as decimal. settings_xml.paths: SystemSettings constructor f_1066a514 selects syssettings.xml and root SystemSettings; SecureSettings f_1066a4bc selects securesettings.xml and root SecureSettings. Shared path resolution f_1068ab6c combines the configured settings directory and relative filename, preserving absolute paths. Defaults at f_10092268 use /opt and settings, yielding /opt/settings/syssettings.xml; this is not proof of a /jffs mount. mobiledevsettings.xml is a separate settings filename, not an assertion that all three stores use identical policy.
settings_xml.named_entries: The named store writes <Setting Name="..." Value="..."/> within a root carrying LastUpdateDevice and Version. Both names and values are XML-escaped, including quotes, apostrophes, ampersands and angle brackets. Names are supplied by callers, not constrained to a fixed enum in the writer. Empty values are not the same operation as a null replacement value; the update loop skips null values rather than serializing them as text.
settings_xml.replication_entries: <Setting idx="%u" lud="%s" version="%u" /> is an indexed replication/version inventory format, not the Name/Value format of syssettings.xml. LUD means last-update device identifier here, not a date.
settings_xml.factory_seed: SystemSettings factory content returned by f_106696e4 at 0x10efeaa0 contains R_CustomerID=0 and R_HideTuneIn=true. Startup f_1066bbc8 can use this backend+0x28 seed when explicitly creating a file. The transaction writer f_106c6118 never dispatches that slot: its missing-root fallback emits only a root header and requested nonnull values, not those factory entries. These two defaults are a seed, not a complete vocabulary of possible named settings.
settings_xml.writer: f_106c6118 first opens the existing source; open failure returns false before creating a temporary file. Otherwise it constructs <path>.tmp, writes the root and retained/updated named entries, appends the closing root and checks the final ftell result: -1 or a signed size greater than 32768 is failure. Missing recognized root reaches 0x106c643c -> f_106c5f24 -> f_106c5e04 to emit only the new root and requested nonnull values, despite the factory-default log message. A parse error after a recognized root may retain already parsed unaffected entries; parse-valid state controls secondary recovery, not primary output success. Entry/root write failures set the writer error flag. It checks close success before rename; close failure or an accumulated writer error removes the temporary file. Rename failure is recorded as failure and also cleans up the temporary file. A successfully replaced file is not proof of durable storage: f_1054f0e8 calls fflush and fsync but ignores their return values; only fclose determines that helper's success.
settings_xml.mutation_and_recovery: f_1066bee0 performs a local named update with next version and local device ID. Primary writer failure returns800. On successful output from an invalid source, it attempts f_1066ba04 to add FileRecoverVersion and repair CustomerID; the second write result is not propagated before the successful update continues. Startup f_1066bbc8 separately checks/parses the existing file, unlinks invalid content and follows the factory-creation path; creation uses write/fsync/close without turning their individual results into a durability guarantee.
settings_xml.replication_binding: Backend+0xec is statically bound, not an opaque runtime repair interface. Startup at 0x1019911c passes the application receiver at application+0x2900c into f_1066bbc8. Receiver constructor f_10650660 installs vptr0x10efcf88 at 0x106507d8; slot+0x14 is f_10652074 (informLocalReplicatedSettingVersion). Successful writes update saved LUD at backend+0xc4 and version at +0xe0, and inform this receiver. Backend+0xe8 points to the local device ID; it is not saved LUD.
settings_xml.read_failure: f_1066c24c records read failure with backend+0xe4 and advertises version0 to the bound replication receiver once. It does not directly rewrite the file or call f_1066ba04. f_10652074 compares cached version/LUD, updates them for an accepted change and conditionally queues ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent through f_10654800. That asynchronous notification is not synchronous XML repair or proof that replication has completed.

watchdog_crash.note: Watchdog internals decoded (sonos-watchdog-1.0/sonos-watchdog/src/watchdog.cxx): it is a client-registration watchdog, not a process monitor - subsystems register named clients each supplying a health check callback ('Watchdog client must have a name', 'Watchdog health check callback must be non-null', 'Watchdog clients:', 'Unregistered watchdog client %s', 'Watchdog client %s not found'). One watchdog thread polls on a per-build frequency ('Watchdog constructed with %u seconds frequency', validated by 'Invalid watchdog health check frequency') running 'In watchdog thread, performing health check' then 'Waiting for next health check' ('watchdog.poll' thread). Lifecycle: 'Creating watchdog' / 'Watchdog already created' / 'Destroying watchdog' / 'End of watchdog destructor'; the zoneplayer eventloop cancels it on shutdown ('Eventloop shutdown. Cancelling watchdog.'). A helper socket endpoint exists ('watchdoghelper', 'Unable to start watchdog helper on port %hu', routes '/watchdog', '/watchdog-legacy', '/watchdogs', '/watchdogcrash'). uri_service_map.resolution: Prefix matching is a static ordered cascade, not a longest-match table: the classifiers (f_1014f48c family and the per-prefix predicate thunks like f_101471f0) run strncmp against literal prefixes in fixed source order and the first hit wins. Specific stems are checked before generic ones by authorial order (e.g. 'x-rincon-playlist:' -> 'x-sonosapi-stream:' -> 'x-rincon-mp3radio://' -> sub-predicate families -> 'x-rincon-cpcontainer:' -> 'x-rincon-buzzer:' -> 'x-rincon-configmode:' in f_1014f48c). Collisions are resolved by including the ':'/'://' terminator in each literal, so 'x-sonos-http:' and 'x-sonosprog-http:' are distinct atoms rather than prefix/substring matches. Openers cascade too: 'Failed to open %s (%d) Trying MMS,RTSP next' shows http->mms->rtsp fallback when the first transport fails. No dynamic registration: every comparison is a literal in .rodata reached by generated predicate functions; nothing walks a writable registry.
resolved_findings: Resolved: first-match ordered strncmp cascade; ':'/'://' terminators make overlapping stems disjoint; transport fallback http->mms->rtsp on open failure; no dynamic registration (all literals).
Established: the URI-prefix -> service-impl map is catalogued.
Established: resolution precedence at the resolver-table boundary - documented.

action_dispatch_records.description: Per-service action dispatch tables are sorted name-keyed records of stride 12 consumed by a binary-search dispatcher (e.g. f_10307608 ContentDirectory, f_10733b44 AlarmClock). Two record layouts exist: DIRECT {name_ptr, fn_ptr, 0} - used by AVTransport, ContentDirectory, ConnectionManager? no; used by AVTransport, ContentDirectory, DeviceProperties, GroupManagement, GroupRenderingControl, Queue, RenderingControl, VirtualLineIn - the middle word is the handler. VIRTUAL {name_ptr, pmf_voff|1, delta=0} - used by AlarmClock, HTControl, ConnectionManager (both URNs), MusicServices, SystemProperties, ZoneGroupTopology - the middle word is a pointer-to-member-function encoding (low bit set = virtual dispatch at impl-vtable byte offset value&~1, third word is the 'this' delta). paranoid_signed_decimal.name: Checked signed decimal conversion
paranoid_signed_decimal.scope: libsonosminiutils.so.1 decimal wrappers paranoid_atoi0x7288 and paranoid_strtoll0x7298, plus their signed conversion helpers0x71ec/0x70fc. This record covers the decimal wrappers and helper control flow, not the separate unsigned/floating parsers.
paranoid_signed_decimal.call_and_output: Inputs are NUL-terminated string pointer(r3) and output-word pointer(r4). paranoid_atoi writes a signed32-bit result; paranoid_strtoll writes signed64-bit big-endian high/low words. Return1 means accepted and stored;0 means rejected and output remains0. The parser is not atoi-style value-as-return. Required pointer arguments have no local null checks. Output is cleared before conversion, so callers must retain the boolean to distinguish valid0 from failure.
paranoid_signed_decimal.delegation_and_grammar: Both public decimal wrappers set r5=10 then tail-branch through the PLT into their _ex helper. paranoid_strtoll_ex0x70fc clears errno, invokes libc strtoll(input,&end,base), then requires errno==0,input[0]!=NUL and*end==NUL. Its _ex base parameter is forwarded without additional base validation. For decimal wrappers this accepts libc decimal lexical forms, including leading whitespace and optional sign, while rejecting any unconsumed trailing byte. All-whitespace, sign-only, empty and numeric-prefix-plus-junk inputs reject. Leading zeros remain decimal;0x prefixes are not enabled by base10. EmbeddedNUL defines the end of the supplied C string. It does not normalize/trim/copy input.
paranoid_signed_decimal.range: strtoll helper accepts the libc signed64-bit range only if conversion raises no errno, storing the returned r3/r4 pair on success. paranoid_atoi_ex additionally requires the signed64-bit result to fit[-2147483648,2147483647]. At0x7234 raw0x7d2a4814 is addc(low,0x80000000), and0x723c raw0x7d290194 is addze(high). Acceptance requires that high+carry modulo2^32 equals0. This admits signed32-bit endpoints and rejects larger positive/negative values without truncating. A boundary audit checked both endpoints, adjacent failures,-100,0 and the64-bit endpoints.
paranoid_signed_decimal.error_and_ownership: Failure does not allocate or mutate the input. errno is reset to0 before libc conversion and is not restored afterward. A libc range failure can leave errno nonzero; the extra32-bit-fit rejection itself sets no errno. No logging, exception or external side effect occurs in these helpers beyond errno and output storage. SPE words0x10a10b21/0x10a10b01 at0x7150/0x7168 save and restore the base register across __errno_location, so base10 survives the call. Stack-canary checks guard normal returns.
paranoid_signed_decimal.concrete_consumer: anacapad0x105bc398 supplies a temporary output word to paranoid_atoi and returns a caller-provided default on false. Battery consumer0x10763514/0x10763528/0x1076353c passes default-100 for RawBattPct/BattPct/BattTmp. It then skips cached-field updates when the returned value equals-100. Thus valid parsed-100 and invalid/missing input produce the same skip behavior, while valid0 updates the cached field. These proven consumer semantics are separate from untraced producer ranges.

evidence.notes: Decimal wrapper tail branch is a semantic call to paranoid_atoi_ex after setting base10.
Clear errno then call strtoll, preserving forwarded base with SPE save/restore.
Error, nonempty input and end-at-NUL predicates control acceptance.
Raw addc/addze pair verifies signed32-bit range; no low-word truncation acceptance.
Failed checked conversion returns caller default instead of zero output.
Battery receiver skips value-100, including a valid literal-100.

counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.name: Counter-based HMAC-SHA256 key derivation
counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.library: libsonoscrypto.so.3 ZZ0215 at0x7144,size464; internal vector-HMAC0x6f68. The record covers this byte-level primitive, not the protocol-specific source of its secret.
counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.inputs_and_formula: Arguments are secret pointer/length,label NUL-terminated string,context pointer/length,output pointer,requested output bytes. It concatenates HMAC-SHA256 blocks using LE16(counter)||label[0:strlen]||context||LE16(requested_bytes*8), counter starts1. The four vector segments have lengths2,label_length,context_length,2. Neither the label terminator nor an additional delimiter byte is hashed. Full32-byte blocks copy directly; a final short block is computed into a32-byte scratch buffer then copies only remaining bytes. Requested size0 returns success0 without producing a block.
counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.limits: There is no separate output-capacity check: requested byte count is the write extent. Encoded output-bit length is the low16 bits of requested_bytes*8; the counter wraps modulo65536. Large requests can therefore wrap those encoded fields. The loop tracks actual output count separately and still writes the requested bytes. This is the literal primitive behavior, not a claim of compliance with a named KDF standard.
counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.algorithm_and_results: Vector-HMAC always selects library hash1. HMAC init maps it to mbedTLS type9; shipped digest table/name confirms SHA256. ZZ0215 returns0 for success,-1 on vector-HMAC initialization failure. Vector helper checks initialization but ignores individual update/finish return values. Successful completion wipes32-byte scratch. Failure returns before that successful cleanup and can leave already-written output blocks; no rollback/zeroing of caller output occurs. HMAC context setup failure has no cleanup call in this helper's failure path. Successful contexts finish and free via ZZ0066.
counter_hmac_sha256_kdf.consumer: netstartd0x10027734 derives32 bytes with label handshake_signature and empty context, then uses that key for a separate HMAC over session bytes. Its caller-supplied proof buffer must hold32 bytes. The proof comparison and mode predicates are documented in bin_netstartd.client_hello_verification_contract.

evidence.notes: Little-endian output-bit length; four-segment vector setup.
Counter increments/wraps16-bit; output writes track requested byte count.
Final short block computes to scratch then copies remaining prefix.
HMAC-SHA256 initialization is the checked failure boundary.

netstartd_local_ipc_send.name: Netstartd local IPC frame writer
netstartd_local_ipc_send.functions: 0x10006b2c(command,payload,payload_length), using IPC context0x10055808 and descriptor at context+0x70. Zero length ignores payload pointer and emits a header-only frame. No command-domain validation, string handling, authentication or checksum is performed. The caller owns pointer readability for the admitted length.

Raw payload follows at offset16; total write length16+payload_length. Nonzero payload copied into2048-byte stack area via __memcpy_chk. Native stw emits those header words in BE. Zero-payload branch writes extent4 and total16. Maximum total frame2064bytes. No payload conversion, encryption or escaping occurs.
netstartd_local_ipc_send.write_loop: Call write(fd,current_pointer,remaining). Positive result advances pointer and subtracts bytes; repeat until remaining0. Raw0x7fe3f851 at0x10006bc4 is subf. with Rc1, so the loop condition uses updated remaining count, not the earlier write result. Descriptor is reloaded from context+0x70 before each subsequent write. Full frame consumption returns0. No readiness registration, backoff, separate transmit queue or delivery acknowledgement is created here.

It unregisters the currently stored descriptor through0x10016ea8, calls imported CloseIPCContext(context), clears global0x100500d4 and returns-1. Cleanup results are ignored. Positive partial writes already accepted by the kernel are not undone before that close request, and no resend is queued. Pre-write validation failures return-1 without this connection teardown. Return0 means all frame bytes were accepted by write, not that the external peer parsed or executed the command. Shipped CloseIPCContext0x11e8 marksfd-1 and contextmode0 after its close request; mode1 also unlinks a nonempty listener pathname. It does not free the context. paranoid_atoui.name: Checked unsigned decimal conversion
paranoid_atoui.scope: Unsigned sibling of paranoid_signed_decimal. libsonosminiutils.so.1 exports paranoid_strtoull_ex at0x72a8, paranoid_atoui_ex at0x73a0, paranoid_atoui at0x7430 and paranoid_strtoull at0x7440. The public decimal wrappers set base10; _ex forwards the supplied base.
paranoid_atoui.contract: The input is a required nonnull NUL-terminated C string and output is a required pointer. Return1 means accepted;0 means rejected. Outputs are cleared before conversion: atoui writes32 bits; strtoull writes64 bits as big-endian high/low words. The helper first rejects ANY minus byte before the terminating NUL, including -0, before calling libc. It then clears errno, calls strtoull(input,&end,base), and accepts only errno==0, input[0]!=NUL and *end==NUL. Leading libc whitespace and an optional plus are accepted; trailing whitespace/junk, empty/sign-only/all-whitespace input and overflow reject. Embedded NUL terminates the supplied string. Decimal wrappers do not accept hex prefixes. There is no local pointer validation, trimming or canonicalization.
paranoid_atoui.range_and_errors: strtoull accepts the unsigned64-bit range when libc reports no error. atoui additionally requires the high word of the parsed64-bit value to be zero, accepting0..4294967295 without truncating larger values. Rejection leaves the output zero; valid zero requires retaining the boolean return to distinguish it from failure. Minus rejection precedes errno reset, while libc conversion resets errno and does not restore the previous value. The extra32-bit-fit check does not set errno.
paranoid_atoui.consumers: R_RDM handling at anacapad0x104b0c68 calls paranoid_atoui. AirplayIncludeLinked change notification at0x104b1ff4 also uses it, and only a successful conversion reaches the local Airplay event path. This differs from mutation validation0x1066a9d4 ->0x10c397cc, which accepts case-insensitive true/false/yes/no and0/1: stored textual booleans are not canonicalized and do not trigger that strict unsigned callback. R_ContentFiltering instead uses signed paranoid_atoi at0x1066a888 and unsigned-compares the result<=1, so accepted values are exactly0 and1, not arbitrary unsigned32-bit values.

audio_taps.file_format: The uncompressed SPDIF replay stream repeats [48-byte metadata][u16LE frame count * 8 audio bytes]. Metadata: byte 0 version 1; u32LE words at 1 and 5 from an eight-byte clock-provider result; u16LE frame count at 9; u32LE sample rate at 0x0b; cached 24-byte status block at 0x0f..0x26; byte 0x27 bit 0x80 signal loss. Remaining bytes are initially zero on the traced producer path; other semantics are not established. The writer reverses each 32-bit audio word for file output, and the reader reverses it back on the big-endian target. Zero-audio signal-loss packets contain metadata only. Validation retains a complete valid prefix and closes an invalid/empty first packet stream. Compression is a zlib wrapper around the stream; XML/base64 is a separate export envelope.

todo: Residual shared with audio_tap: identify the clock provider/domain for metadata u32 words at offsets 1 and 5, and decode the cached 24-byte status block at 0x0f..0x26 and any remaining flag semantics. Packet writer, sample-rate word, signal-loss producer, compression and framing are traced; the opaque metadata semantics are not fully resolved.
resolved_findings: Reader0x107e1264 reads48-byte metadata BEFORE each audio packet, not a single file trailer. Version byte0 must be1 during validation0x107e1e44. Byte reversal on this big-endian target decodes u32LE at1 and5, u16LE sample-frame count at9, u32LE at0xb; sample count*8 gives the following8-byte-frame audio size, stored reader+0x40. Signal-loss is byte0x27 bit0x80, not any nonzero flag value. Remaining metadata bytes are copied unchanged. Validation walks [48-byte metadata][count*8 audio] repeatedly and retains the valid prefix if at least one complete packet exists; it logs trailing audio/metadata truncation and rewinds to that valid size. Invalid first packet closes the file.

DSP manager and rolling snapshot mechanics, fixed zlib compression and consumptive XML/base64 export are fully documented under shared_primitives/audiotap. The16384-byte buffer in0x1034308c is a general file-reader buffer, not a metadata head section. The base64 stream contains the whole compressed snapshot.
DSP capacity is three physical descriptors with default capacity2 and setter domain0..3 inclusive. Tappability is source vtable+0xc; manager+0xb8 stores the source pointer.

Producer/consumer reconciliation with audio_tap: f_107d8624 initializes 48 zero bytes and version 1 at 0x107d8730-0x107d8740. Object +0x8d0 vtable +0x0c returns eight bytes at stack+0x2c, copied into metadata offsets 1/5 and the caller timestamp output at 0x107d8758-0x107d87a4. This proves common provenance but does not establish clock units or domain. Normal output sets frame count from (payload_bytes>>3)&0xffff and sample rate from processor+0xf1c at 0x107d89e0-0x107d8a20. Playback at 0x107d87f0-0x107d8858 compares metadata+0x0b against +0xf1c and logs TV input sample rate mismatch with audio tap, establishing the word meaning. f_107dede8 copies 24 cached bytes at processor+0x1a68 into metadata+0x0f. Error output ORs bit 0x80 into metadata+0x27 and calls f_107e1720 with null audio/zero size at 0x107d8bd8-0x107d8bf8. Therefore the writer is present in this ELF, not an unlocated external producer.

Writer f_107e1720 copies the 48-byte metadata, byte-reverses the packed scalar fields and emits it through object+0x678 sink virtual+8 at 0x107e1894-0x107e18ac. Non-null/nonzero audio is byte-reversed one word at a time and emitted through the same sink at 0x107e19c8-0x107e1a2c; null/zero skips the payload. Reader f_107e1264 returns 2 on short metadata fread, stores count*8 at +0x40, and returns 4 for byte 0x27 bit 0x80 while retaining the metadata copy. f_107e1a44 returns the cached metadata when a packet still has audio remaining, otherwise invokes f_107e1264. f_107e1a88 clamps requested audio to remaining packet/file bytes, reports short-read error 2 and converts word byte order at 0x107e1b6c-0x107e1b90. A zero-count metadata packet still advances validation by 48 bytes through f_107e1e44; zero count is not by itself an invalid-file rule. The status-byte interpretation is still unresolved, so neither record claims a complete semantic schema.

Bit-field audit agrees with audio_tap: GNU e500 and the fixed repository listing decode 0x107d89f0 as rlwinm r10,r5,29,16,31, computing (payload_bytes>>3)&0xffff. The paired byte stores at 0x107d8a18/0x107d8a1c prove a sixteen-bit count; the previous unqualified payload_bytes>>3 expression omitted that narrowing. Reader 0x107e1420 multiplies the reconstructed count by eight, and 0x107e147c tests status mask 0x80 with andi. This is not a second format or a right-shift-alias reinterpretation of the status byte.
audio_taps.file_format_correction: No XML queue or separate XML metadata header is written into the compressed snapshot. The XML wrapper is the export envelope only. Earlier claims of gzip, a trailing metadata block, big-endian packed fields, and a three-tap default are superseded by the concrete reader and compression paths.

Concrete window sizes recovered, disproving the no-image-constants residual: constructor f_1038d540 loads its itemId pointer into r27 at 0x1038d5a4, compares it to null into cr4 at 0x1038d5b4, and chooses the sizes at 0x1038d634-0x1038d654. GNU e500 decoding shows isel r29,r10,r9,18 after r9=10 and r10=20, then isel r31,0,r9,18 after r9=9. Therefore nonnull itemId selects previousWindowSize=9 and upcomingWindowSize=10; null itemId selects 0 and 20. The same r27 is emitted as itemId at 0x1038d6c0-0x1038d6d4, with null mapped to the empty string. Selection is pointer presence, not strlen, so a nonnull empty itemId still selects 9/10. f_10550c1c formats unsigned decimal using %u, and the two values are emitted at 0x1038d72c-0x1038d750. These are compiled request-policy values, not documented maximum response sizes or caller-supplied numeric windows.

updateToken premise corrected and residual closed: in version-request constructor f_1038d9d8 a caller boolean at incoming stack+0x77 is loaded/tested at 0x1038da64-0x1038da6c. False selects literal version? at 0x1038da74; true selects version?updateToken=true& at 0x1038db20-0x1038db30. It is a request flag, not a locally parsed opaque updateToken value whose TTL needs to be decoded. Both paths then append queueVersion and contextVersion strings at 0x1038daa8-0x1038dadc. The prior assertion that this literal proves an expiring optimistic-concurrency token or a server-side itemWindow cursor is withdrawn. No cloud credential lifetime or server rotation guarantee follows from this boolean builder.

Actual credential replacement is a separate response-header operation: f_1038c244 recognizes X-Updated-Authorization and X-Goog-Updated-Authorization case-insensitively at 0x1038c274/0x1038c298, sets the updated flag at 0x1038c2b4, skips whitespace, and strlcpy-copies the supplied header value with bound 0x1401 to owner+0x7210 at 0x1038c2d0-0x1038c2dc. The adjacent Retry-After header is separately parsed to an integer at 0x1038c30c-0x1038c334; it must not be interpreted as token TTL. These paths establish where an actual replacement credential enters without guessing its cloud-side expiry rules.

The cpcontainer path branch copies at most 256 bytes of the URI path, terminates it, passes identifier classification/validation through f_1071b3dc/f_1071b458 and canonicalizes it with f_1071d5c4/f_1071b5a0 into another 257-byte buffer. The other branch extracts/percent-decodes item path text through f_1071ac00, which recognizes x-sonos prefixes or x-rincon-cpcontainer and requires a nonempty parsed path. For x-sonos-http and x-sonosprog-http that helper strips the final dot/extension before decoding. The builder then percent-encodes the selected item text into a 257-byte scratch buffer with f_10c3a294, appends endpoint base + encoded text + slash using snprintf, and validates the resulting URL version with f_10338a34. Component truncation and formatter return values are ignored here; success is not a lossless-construction guarantee. Full identifier classification and decoder error/embedded-null behavior remain open.
cloud_queue.manifest_item_encoding: Percent-encoder wrapper f_10c3a294 passes the literal allow-list $-_.!*'(), to f_10c3a0f4. That helper copies isalnum bytes or allow-listed bytes and encodes every other byte through format %%%02x, using lowercase hexadecimal. Slash, colon, percent, query and fragment punctuation are therefore encoded unless already removed by earlier item parsing. A raw copied byte needs room for itself plus a terminator; an escape needs room for three bytes plus a terminator. If capacity cannot fit the next unit it stops, null-terminates and returns the number of bytes written, without a separate truncation error. f_1011c864 ignores that returned count. This encoder does not normalize already encoded percent sequences; a percent byte is encoded again.
cloud_queue.base_url_version_extraction: Cloud-queue version extractor f_10483cf0 lazily compiles the literal regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$) with flags 1, parses the URI into components using f_10c3a920 and runs regexec from the path pointer. It uses the first regex match, starts the selected version span two bytes after the match start (after /v), and normally ends at the URI path end. If the final byte of the match is slash, it ends the span at that slash instead. There is no independent check that this slash is the last path separator. Consequently a matching version segment followed by more path can supply the accepted version, despite the error text saying the path must end with a version. An earlier matching version segment is chosen before a later one. No match returns 1; regex compilation failure returns 2. Candidate suffix syntax is narrower than the shared parser because the regex permits only letters in pre-release and letters/dots in build metadata.
cloud_queue.base_url_version_gate: Cloud-queue version checker f_10338a34 first calls that extractor, then f_10483e28. It returns 2 only when parsing succeeds and the major word equals 2; other outcomes return zero. It does not compare minor or patch against a supported maximum. The optional diagnostic object receives code 0x48 and distinct text for missing version, malformed version or unsupported major when the relevant failure is recognized. Callers including f_1011c864 pass null for that diagnostic object and only test the numeric return as nonzero/zero. Diagnostics are therefore not proof that the stricter grammar described in their text is enforced.

dsp_ht_engine.todo: Established: complete selector map from 0x10fe8e8c, eight compiled constructors, two external-file branches and compiled Pinewood fallback are recovered. Unknown: constructor member semantics, ChProcConfig conversion/validation and end-to-end signal routing and numeric constraints. Next: trace member stores from constructors 0x10d75dac/0x10d76310/0x10d7686c/0x10d76dbc/0x10d77150/0x10d774b4/0x10d7778c/0x10d784dc into f_10d79a4c and block consumers; join the attachments at 0x10d810a0-0x10d81114 to actual processing calls and parameter guards.
resolved_findings: The claim that preset wiring is available only in absent XML/binpb files is false. f_10d7bebc subtracts ten from the model selector, bounds the resulting unsigned value by 0x25, then dispatches through relative table 0x10fe8e8c (0x10d7bec4-0x10d7bf20). Several arms directly call compiled configuration constructors at 0x10d7bfc8-0x10d7c004, including f_10d784dc/f_10d75dac/f_10d76310/f_10d7686c/f_10d76dbc/f_10d77150/f_10d774b4/f_10d7778c. Unhandled/out-of-range selectors reach f_10d7883c, which clears 0x5b0 bytes and seeds a Pinewood configuration from compiled data at 0x10d78844-0x10d788c4. The exact selector map is recovered below; constructor member meanings remain incompletely traced.

Two model arms use external ChProcConfig data: S41_fronts_chproc_config.binpb at 0x10d7bf24 and S39_fronts_chproc_config.binpb at 0x10d7c008. f_10d78ed4 constructs the writable app/debug/dsp directory, appends the supplied filename, and opens through the shared DSP file reader at 0x10d79048-0x10d79068. On open failure it clears the result presence byte and returns (0x10d79090-0x10d79114). On nonempty read it builds a nanopb stream and uses descriptor global 0x110954bc at 0x10d79198-0x10d791ac. Caller failure logs Could not load and parse satellite protobuf file then uses the compiled Pinewood fallback at 0x10d7bf40-0x10d7bf78. Successful load is separately converted by f_10d79a4c, with its own conversion-failure diagnostic at 0x10d7c014-0x10d7c080.

Artifact check included the recursive reference tree and the full shipped rootfs.squashfs inode list. Only S9_array.xml is shipped under /opt/dsp; no preset XML or .binpb files occur in either inventory. The S9 coefficient XML is not the external ChProcConfig schema. Missing files do not block reversal of compiled constructors or converter guards. They also do not prove which writable overrides a live device has installed.

Native block assembly is visible independently of preset filenames. At 0x10d810a0-0x10d81114, the ChannelProcessing constructor allocates InputGain through f_10d9bfb8 and ChProcInputMeter through f_10dd3408, assigns names through f_10d66b48 and attaches each child through f_10d67e10. This proves object construction/attachment, not by itself an end-to-end signal-flow order. The earlier claim that the complete sixty-block processing graph was closed from vocabulary alone is withdrawn. Named crossover/bass/filter blocks and DSP control routes remain useful surface vocabulary, not a substitute for those bindings.

Complete static selector map: table words at 0x10fe8e8c are signed offsets from that fixed base, not entry-relative offsets. Applying selector-10 and unsigned bound 37 at 0x10d7bec4-0x10d7bf20 yields direct constructors 10 -> 0x10d75dac, 13 -> 0x10d76310, 16 -> 0x10d7686c, 18 -> 0x10d76dbc, 21 -> 0x10d77150, 36 -> 0x10d774b4, 37 -> 0x10d7778c and 47 -> 0x10d784dc. Selector 41 reaches 0x10d7c008 and S39_fronts_chproc_config.binpb; selector 43 reaches 0x10d7bf24 and S41_fronts_chproc_config.binpb. Every other in-range row and every out-of-range selector reaches the fallback call at 0x10d7bf78 -> 0x10d7883c. Constructor call sites at 0x10d7bfc8-0x10d7c000 independently bind table targets to constructor addresses; table enumeration alone does not give member or signal-routing meanings.

resolved_findings: Resolved: entitlement schema = cloud-fetched entitlements doc over /entitlements/api with X-Sonos-User-Id header, etag+cache-control cached; internally savePendingEntitlementsLocked -> notifyClients -> version-changed muse event; gate call sites are the featureConfig*/entmt checks guarding cloud features; errors rc/http logged as cloud entitlements: rc %d, http %d.

Schema + gate points closed: cloud document fetched over /entitlements/api with X-Sonos-User-Id and ETag/cache-control caching through HTTPCacheManager (Corrupt Cache -> cloud refetch). Record schema literal: <Entitlements><Entitlement type="%s" isTrial="%s" sku="%s" startDate="%s" endDate="%s" codes="%s"/></Entitlements>; type vocabulary {SBiz,businessCore,sonosRadio,controlChannels,restrictedAccess} + fields {credentialTypeAllowed,allowGuestAccess,isTrial,startDate,endDate}. Muse surface locally served: getEntitlements/getUserEntitlements answered from cache; internalMuseSubscribeToEntitlements wires ENTITLEMENTS_CHANGED. Pipeline: fetch -> cache -> entitlements for "%s" changed -> savePendingEntitlementsLocked -> notifyClients -> version-changed muse event, with stash-compare diffing and staleness re-fetch. Gates: RRuntimeZPPolicy ctor requires [localSettingsMgr,entitlementsMgr]; SBiz presence gates Sonos Radio preinstall; BUSINESS usageContext supplies the CloudSettings gates.

Resolved: the entitlements fetch/cache pipeline is decoded (entitlementsmanager.cxx @0x10ebf908+): GET /entitlements/api on the cloud URL with X-Sonos-User-Id header; cached via HTTPCacheManager with eTag ("failed to get current eTag from cache") and Cache-Control:max-age=0 on explicit refresh; on ENTITLEMENTS_CHANGED (internal bus event type 6) old entitlements are stashed for compare, cache re-populates, and jobs are scheduled to reconsider Sonos Radio + Sonos Business MSP. XML cache schema: <Entitlements><Entitlement type="%s" isTrial="%s" sku="%s" startDate="%s" endDate="%s" codes="%s" /></Entitlements>. SBiz entitlement gates Sonos Radio preinstall: "no SBiz entitlement; preinstalling Sonos Radio" vs "found SBiz entitlement; blocking preinstall".

Shared name bindings were checked directly against business_msp: the nineteen named twelve-byte rows at 0x10f99838-0x10f99910 map SRADIO_NO_ADS/HD_CONTENT/SPECIAL_CONTENT/ONDEMAND_ARCHIVE/CAN_SKIP to 1..5, then SFB_BASIC_UI/COMMERCIAL_MSP/ESSENTIALS_MSP/PREMIUM_MSP/DASHBOARD_ACCESS/CNTRL_MEDIA_SRCS/CNTRL_THIRD_PARTY/RSTC_CONTENT_ACS/RSTC_SAVE_CONTENT_ACS/RSTC_SETTINGS_ACS/RSTC_ALARMS_ACS/RSTC_MESSAGING_ACS/RSTC_SAVE_GROUPS_ACS/SCHEDULES_ACCESS to 6..19. These values agree with the existing business_msp mapping. A preceding row at 0x10f9982c has an empty name, length zero and numeric value zero. The nineteen named values are ordinal IDs/indices, not literal powers-of-two masks; their downstream use as bit positions still requires the consumer binding.

Native lookup f_10a08744 starts from the preceding empty row, initializes a non-null output to zero, searches through index nineteen, requires an exact supplied length and then uses strncasecmp at 0x10a087ac-0x10a087c8. A match returns one and stores the row numeric ID at 0x10a087dc-0x10a087e4. A miss returns zero at 0x10a08810-0x10a08838. A zero-length name matches the empty row and yields zero. Null output is a special success path at 0x10a0883c rather than an error. Reverse helper f_10a08720 indexes twelve-byte rows by the incoming ID and loads the name pointer at 0x10a08720-0x10a08740; this helper itself has no range check. This establishes parser/reverse-name mechanics, not entitlement authorization.

The existing XML Entitlement format is diagnostic output, not proof of an input schema or an eligibility predicate. As recorded in business_msp, f_10372f48 emits type/trial/sku/date/code fields after a bounded five-record loop; the four category integers are emitted by f_10a4e0e4 through f_109d1570. A server-provided value can still have native acceptance and enforcement logic. Therefore server-defined semantics is not used as a reason to stop tracing: the actual input parser, time/trial predicates and category-to-feature consumers remain explicit work, consistently with business_msp.

factory_reset.mechanics: <PresetNameList val="FactoryDefaults"/> is the settings-side reset verb; after reset the device broadcasts its removal so peers drop it from 'vanished' lists; corrupt system settings auto-trigger a reset
resolved_findings: Resolved: wipe set = the CSRF-posted Factory Reset/Remote factory reset form creates /jffs/factoryReset.txt (marker consumed at boot by the reset path); sonosFactoryResetFull removes the zone from the household (device: %s %s removed from vanish..) and wipes the jffs settings tree; preserves hardware identity/certs (device cert and household key material survive, matching the cert subsystem); LED shows LED_MODE_FACTORY_RESET during wipe; reboot follows the marker-file commit.

Wipe model decoded: the reset handler ~0x105e8b44 (mod_zp log scope) has two paths. SOFT: joins app/run + factoryReset.txt via f_105e674c, ensures the directory via f_1068a70c, writes the literal SOFT into the marker with sonosFileCreate at 0x105e8bd8 (failure logs unable to create factory reset file.), then sync() at 0x105e8c84 - the actual file deletion runs at next boot from the marker, outside anacapad. HARD: calls the imported sonosFactoryResetFull at 0x110995d8 (0x105e8ce4), an extern syscall/IPC stub not contained in this image - the wipe-and-reboot executes in the sibling-daemon/HAL layer, consistent with the multi-daemon boundary (netstartd owns boot-time persistence). The in-binary wipe set is therefore exactly: the SOFT marker write plus the hard-reset IPC; which files survive is decided by the boot-time consumer of app/run/factoryReset.txt, not by anacapad. conf/rdmconfig and conf/rdmlocation literals sit in the same string region with bad rdm location / RDM Config watchdog triggering - the retail-demo config the reset also clears.

Resolved: the boot-time reset chain is fully proven - /sbin/frcheck reads /jffs/app/run/factoryReset.txt (SOFT marker) and polls hal_inputs_get_buttons_state (button-hold detection), returning {0=hard,1=normal,2=soft}; etc/Configure lines 41-51 dispatch: stat!=1 -> sonosledmgrd --fr (reset LED mode), stat==0 -> /wifi/netstartd --hard-reset, stat==2 -> /wifi/netstartd --soft-reset. netstartd exposes FOUR reset levels: {--hard-reset, --soft-reset, --qareset, --qareset-lite} and performs the wipe itself ("mt: factory reset - removing preference", "ssidmgr: factory reset", WIFI_RESET, NS2_STATE_RESET; while reset pending it blocks START_ISLAND/START_OPEN_AP). sonosFactoryResetFull is the anacapad-side import that writes the marker file.

Resolved: the wipe mechanism is partition-level, not a file list - netstartd links libflash.so.1 and the hard path resolves to hal_flash_secure_erase_jffs (flash_secure_erase_whole on the jffs mtd). The flag set is actually four: {--hard-reset,--soft-reset,--qareset,--qareset-lite} plus --preserve-system and the /var/run/stopnetstartd sentinel. netstartd's mode FSM is literal: {IDLE,CHECK_UPDATE,CHECK_UPDATE_PREDELAY,CHECK_UPDATE_DELAY,CHECK_UPDATE_DONE,BEGIN_SETUP,HH_ALIVE,HH_FORWARD,ALIVE,CONTACT,CONFIG_DELAY,COMPLETE_WAIT,CHECK_CONFIG,CHECK_CONFIG_DELAY,CHECK_CONFIG_DONE}. libflash also exports hal_flash_ptable_{read,write}, hal_flash_get_bootsection/bootgeneration, hal_flash_read_fsn, hal_upgrade_{write_partition_platform,compare_ptable,ptable_redundant_config,bytes_in_part,reprogram_flash} - the partition table + dual-boot generation machinery used by the upgrade path.

frcheck tri-state binding proven from shipped /etc/Configure: exit 0 -> netstartd --hard-reset (plus sonosledmgrd --fr LED pattern), exit 2 -> netstartd --soft-reset (plus --fr), exit 1 -> normal boot (no reset, no --fr LED). The boot LED flag /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led is touched before frcheck runs. /jffs/Configure replaces the stock Configure entirely when present (exec chain), and /jffs/system/Configure.dev runs additionally + marks the build dev-unlocked. Kernel modules loaded by Configure: sonos_device.ko, chk.ko, hwevent_queue.ko, audiodev.ko, conditional ir_rcvr.ko, then the Atheros wifi stack {adf,asf,ath_hal,dfs?,ath_driver} + bridge.ko. rmem_max is raised to 262143 and icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts set.

dirObjFavorites vtable mapped (ctor ~0x1037ca04, table base 0x10ec0b08, ~40 slots): +0x0 f_1037e030, +0x24 f_1037ea40 = userradio.d.xml persistence op, +0x30 f_1037f1ac = replication acceptance (deciding whether to accept replicated list / Rejected version %u, schema %u), +0x5c f_1037ee34 = replication receiver (replicating favorites from %s + userradio.xml), +0x2c f_1037b644 = the userradio load path. Retry/status arithmetic corrected against GNU e500 and the fixed repository disassembler. At 0x10355968-0x10355974 the retry branch tests (((status-0x409)&0xffff)<=1), not (status-0x409)>>16. The preceding band at 0x10355860-0x1035586c is (((status-1000)&0xffff)<=2). These accept low-sixteen-bit ranges, not broad upper-halfword classes; no upper-bit restriction is established at those tests. Other statuses reset this+0x1aec at 0x10355980; exact status 0x40b reaches the incompatible-partner diagnostic branch. The retry branch increments +0x1aec and sets the seconds word of the caller deadline to sonosClockGetTime(1)+10 at 0x10355904-0x10355924.

The ValidateBondedState call identity remains proven: 0x10355824-0x10355840 invokes topology object +0x1a80 through virtual slot +0x44 with debug-name argument 0x10e885b0. Its return is treated as a status code, not simply a boolean. The old claimed dynamic attempt bound ct<(derived>>4)*30 is withdrawn: 0x10355884 uses mulhwu with 0x88888889, shifts right four and reconstructs 30*floor(ct/30); comparison with ct selects log level 3 or 5 through isel at 0x103558a8. This detects every thirtieth retry for logging, not a retry-limit exit. The same arithmetic is repeated for the diagnostic at 0x103558c4-0x103558dc. Actual success/settle semantics and cancellation/termination must be traced in the concrete delegate and its callers.

Constructor 0x1035ea84 copies a shared object pointer/control pair into +0x1a80/+0x1a84. This proves construction provenance, not that the delegate is absent or impossible to resolve statically: the concrete constructor argument and vtable still require tracing in the shipped ELF. Runtime installation alone is not a reason to stop.

lechmere_wss.summary: Lechmere carries cloud traffic over a negotiated WebSocket connection, with policy-key authentication, application keepalive and explicit close reasons. Its reader consumes an eight-byte ASCII hexadecimal header, not AA-AK message identifiers. The shared Muse subscription layer has a compiled 73-row topic registry and separately serializes event metadata and bodies. Topic names, message-type names and payload schemas are different contracts; the complete per-topic body producer map remains unresolved.

frame_format.header: 8 ASCII bytes: version parsed at offset 0 with %02x, numeric type at offset 2 with %02x, extended-header length at offset 4 with %04x. Reader rejects parsed version<=6 and type>6; it does not test version==6. These are sscanf conversion checks, not proof of strict whole-field hexadecimal validation.
frame_format.msg_types: Numeric 0..6 in the frame-reader success path; 7..10 are additional reader result statuses, not extra AA-AK wire codes.

wss_topic_registry.lookup: f_109e10d8 walks 73 records and requires the signed subtype to match. A matching -1 subtype succeeds without a tag test; subtypes 0 and 1 also require namespace-tag equality. Unknown input returns 0x4a. The names below are not alphabetically ordered: tvAudioSignalStatus is row 1 and areasVersionChange is row 7.

resolved_findings: Header correction: f_105d52e0 requires the supplied buffer capacity to exceed 0xfffe at 0x105d52e8/0x105d533c, requests exactly eight header bytes at 0x105d53a8, and rejects short/nonpositive reads through distinct reader statuses. It parses version/type/extended length at offsets 0/2/4 with %02x/%02x/%04x. The branch at 0x105d54e4 is ble to the bad-version path: accepted parsed versions exceed 6. The type branch at 0x105d5558 is bgt to bad-type: accepted types are 0..6. No extended-length<=8 predicate exists here; eight is the fixed header size. Zero extended length copies an empty string; nonzero length requires an exact-length read before JSON extended-header parsing.

Registry reconstruction: constant evaluation of every store in initializer 0x10098d34-0x10099964, including mtctr/mfctr transfers, yields exactly 73 rows with ids 0..0x48. Earlier values above 0x48 were mistaken transient-register values, not actual topic ids. The secondary word is a Muse message-type id, resolved by 0x109ecb5c through the string-pointer table 0x10f97094, not an AA-AK ordinal. Examples: row 0 accessorySwapStatus -> id 3/accessorySwap; row 0x11 bluetoothConnectionStatus -> id 0x3c/bluetooth; row 0x3c settingsPlayerSettingsChanged -> id 0xfe/playerSettingsEvent; row 0x48 zoneGroupTopology -> id 0x142/upnpEvent.

Reachable subscription boundary: f_1068ec54 calls transport predicate f_109dd184 at 0x1068ed14 and rejects the non-WSS path with Invalid transport: WSS is required. It obtains a topic from f_109e10d8 at 0x1068ed3c/0x1068f044; sentinel 0x4a selects Invalid namespace: UPnP subscribe not supported. f_1068e65c similarly validates renewals at 0x1068e6e0 and rejects unsupported namespaces. Thus registry lookup has real WSS subscribe/renew consumers, but those consumers do not enumerate the event body members.

Event-output path: sender f_106c2818 invokes f_109e98c4 at 0x106c2888. That dispatcher selects f_109f6d7c when event+0xc is nonzero, otherwise f_109f6fb0 -> f_109f6f0c. The raw path copies event+8 bytes of length event+0xc without enumerating JSON members. A null raw pointer with nonzero length reaches the basic_string null-not-valid exception path. The typed path obtains a producer object at event+4 and calls its virtual slot +8 with the writer and writer+0x1040 flag; a null producer simply emits an empty object. The writer status, not merely a submitted event, determines the returned result.

Common envelope rather than per-topic schema: formats 4 and 5 invoke f_109f6d2c, which begins an array, emits a metadata object, then leaves the body serializer to emit its element and close the array. f_109f6bc4 emits namespace and additional addressed-header entries when the namespace resolver succeeds, optional apiVersion, response/success for response messages or registry-derived name for events, resolved type, optional cmdId and conditional async=true. This common envelope does not prove a field is present inside any particular topic body.

The old claim that body member sets are only an external subscriber contract is withdrawn. Raw-body storage and a concrete typed producer callback are present in the shipped image. Their callers and vtables must be joined to the corrected registry before claiming the 73 payload schemas are recovered; a code/name table alone does not establish them.

resolved_findings: Resolved: priority model decoded - each request carries LedPatternPriorityLevel; applyLEDMode compares it against m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and applies only on win; flash-mode stashes the active pattern for led_set_resumeDefaultLedPattern(Flash) restore; HAL path is led_get_hal_token + hal_led_{open,close,write,flash,brightness,diag}.

Arbitration model decoded: applyLEDModeLocked (f_10c8f06c, leds_zp log scope) is the single apply point. Its apply-time log names the full arbitration state: m_fLedBrightness, m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel (the queued request priority), m_lastClr, m_fade_effect, m_lLEDFlags, m_bIsInExclusiveBTMode, m_bIsBTConnected, m_bHasStatusLED, m_bHasMuteLED, useOnlyStatusLED. The eligibility gate f_10c8ee44 drops applies with two explicit reject reasons: not-ready/flag state (ignoring apply LED mode. m_bReady=%d, m_lLEDFlags=0x%llx) and the suspend bypass flag (ignoring apply LED mode due to suspend bypass flag). Pattern selection is therefore a request-with-priority model - setters queue {R_LED_code, priority} into m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and the locked apply reconciles against flags, BT exclusivity, and LED hardware presence. R_LED code to pattern binding runs through set_pattern_for_mode(LED_MODE_*) calls (modes: FACTORY_RESET, BOOTING, JOIN_HH, JOIN_HH_OPEN, BYPASS_BLOCKED, BYPASS, CLONE_CHECK_FAIL) plus applyLEDMode R_LED_* codes (WAITING_TO_PAUSE, PLAYING, WARN, DEMO_MODE, DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR, HHID, BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH).

Resolved: the R_LED_* priority ordering is the sequential test order in applyLEDMode (f_10c918a0) - first matching flag wins, so highest-to-lowest: DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR > UPGRADE > BROKEN_DEVICE > BEGIN_SETUP_MODE > JOIN_HH_OPEN > JOIN_HH > IN_SETUP_MODE > BREAK_POP > WAC > WAC_TIMEOUT > SHUTDOWN > !HHID (no-household pattern) > TRANSFER_REGISTRATION > CONTROL_FEEDBACK > IDENTIFY_PLAYER > AUDIO_OFF > MUTED > FAULT > WAITING_TO_PLAY > WAITING_TO_PAUSE > PLAYING > HHID (default). The restore path resumeDefaultLEDPattern re-applies the subset {BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH, BEGIN_SETUP_MODE, IN_SETUP_MODE, MUTED, AUDIO_OFF, PLAYING, HHID} in the same precedence; 'unknown restore pattern' is the fallthrough. User SetLEDState toggles ride a separate on/off flag outside this stack (applyLEDModeLocked logs m_lLEDFlags + m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel; 'ignoring apply LED mode' when !m_bReady).

resolved_findings: The previous uniform source-facet slot map is withdrawn: f_106a77d0 and f_106a7880 are directly called wrappers, not evidence that source vtable slots +0x40/+0x44 mean play/pause. AVTransport-side sites 0x102b00bc/0x102b00c0 and 0x102b0130/0x102b0134 load their object from +0x5a0 and call these wrappers directly. The wrappers take the selected entry at controller+0x354, then provider entry+4, call provider virtual +0x2c, and invoke returned-interface +8 or +0xc. Missing selected entry/provider/interface returns zero. These are distinct dispatch levels and their offsets must not be combined into one invented universal table.

The seek-related wrapper f_106a7930 uses the same selected-provider/+0x2c lookup. With r5 zero it calls returned-interface +0x10 at 0x106a79b4-0x106a79bc; the alternative path is separate. Meanwhile f_10258ab0 calls f_10257704 and f_102587b4 inside the chsrc capability path, not a universal source-vtable +0x68 entry. The source-module filename anchors alone do not establish common slot ordering.

Concrete static table counterexample: the VLI construction block installs 0x10f045c4 at object+0, 0x10f04644 at +8, 0x10f0466c at +0x11c, 0x10f04684 at +0x120 and 0x10f046c8 at +0x124 (0x106aaf30-0x106aaf6c). Those addresses contain executable method pointers; the same block names ai_vli at 0x106aafa0 and initializes its controller state. Therefore runtime selection does not mean the image lacks static vtables, and manager registration is not evidence of an external implementation.

Selected VLI provider mechanism: construction clears nine stride-12 entries beginning controller+0x2e8 and zeros controller+0x354. Selection scans nine keys at entry+0 and stores a matching entry address in +0x354 (0x106a8cac-0x106a8ccc/0x106a8df4). Entry+4 is the provider object. Selection calls provider virtual +0x10 (logged onSelect); deactivation calls provider virtual +0x14 and clears the selected pointer (0x106a9038-0x106a9064). Failed selection also clears it at 0x106a8e34. These local transitions explain why the control wrappers may return zero without reaching a provider.

Descriptor construction is distinct from the name arrays. f_10908f38 installs vtable 0x10f7c1d0 and delegates default setup to f_10908e70: name (Unknown), empty secondary names, +0xf4=-1, +0xec=425 and +0xf0=0, with memory/flash zero. f_10909058 recognizes S9 explicitly and writes S9/ZPS9/Playbar, flags +0xd0=0x8000, +0xd4=0x30206772, +0xd8=0x37008, and +0xf4=6. f_10909fcc constructs the fuller descriptor, reads HAL MDP/MDP2 data and branches on model/board values before assigning the scalar fields. The former claim that f_10908f38 itself executes the entire per-model strcmp ladder is withdrawn.

Tuple semantics recovered through actual consumers: +0xec is the amplifier power-on/startup time in milliseconds (getter f_10908d3c); +0xf0 is a signed 16-bit calibrated setup/chirp volume value (getter f_10908d4c uses lha, with zero meaning not yet calibrated at the audited callers); +0xf8 is the advertised memory scalar (getter f_10908ca8), and +0xfc the advertised flash scalar (getter f_10908cb8). Device-description replacement joins these getters to #AMP_ONTIME#, #MEMORY# and #FLASH#, and the shipped XML names ampOnTime/memory/flash. No memory/flash unit or exact volume scale is inferred solely from row magnitudes. These are not four hardware-generation/version classes.

Descriptor+0xf4, read by f_10908474, is formatted into #INT_SPEAKER_SIZE# and emitted as internalSpeakerSize. Consequently the S9 value 6 is not the ordinal used by the product-name arrays. The earlier Amp/Play/Soundbar/Portable labels assigned to +0x110 and S2-generation labels assigned to +0x10c are also withdrawn: f_10909fcc loads the HAL MDP block at +0x104 and uses +0x10c/+0x110 in model/board dispatch. Numeric comparisons alone do not establish those invented class names.

Big-endian capability extraction is numeric: f_10908540 tests byte +0xd3 nonzero (word low byte), f_1090855c tests word+0xd0 & 0xff00 (byte +0xd2 only, not both +0xd1/+0xd2), f_10908578 tests the high halfword, f_10908594 extracts word bit 16, f_109085fc bit 14, f_10908610 bit 13, and f_10908624 bit 20. The S9 mask 0x8000 is byte +0xd2 bit 7; the aggregate 0xff00 predicate alone does not name every bit or distinguish optical/ARC/eARC. Remaining per-bit names must be joined to actual consumers rather than inferred from product membership.

SKU document literals contain attributes sku/startDate/endDate/codes at 0x10ebfcb0. That separate SKU-document shape does not assign a meaning to the descriptor timing/volume/memory/flash fields or to every capability flag. The model-name vocabulary and the separate capability-name vocabulary must likewise not be mistaken for a verified per-model bit-to-name join.

multi_daemon_boundary.summary: The netstartd boundary uses a framed binary AF_UNIX stream, with direction-specific message dispatch and payload checks. The checked /anacapad-external, /netstartd-external and sibling path literals instead select outbound HTTPS crash-upload destinations; they do not establish local HTTP IPC handlers. Diagnostic uploads and netstartd control IPC must be mapped separately.

IPC framing decoded (ipc_msg.cxx, reader loop ~0x105d3954 under module ipc): the channel is a 3-field binary header read by ReadIPCHeader (0x11098588) followed by a bounded payload - the unsigned check (body_len-4)<=0x800 at0x105d39b8-0x105d39c0 accepts body_len4..0x804 inclusive, including the message-id word, and malformed frames log Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d) with the three header fields. Body is then read() and dispatched; the loop is lock-guarded (f_10988558/f_10988984 pair). Connection lifecycle literals: IPC established for %s, IPC closed for %s, IPC timeout occurred, attempting reconnect for %s (retries=%u), performReset performing IPC reconnect for %s, Deferring IPC reconnect for %s - the select-thread registers selthrd.RIPCHandler.reset/.data handler pair. netstartd message vocabulary visible in the same region: Disabling networking, Enabling networking, Signaling start/end of network connectivity test, and the outbound IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition. ReadIPCHeader is imported at0x11098588; its concrete shared-library implementation establishes the hdr_len/version/body_len semantics described below, not the earlier type/length/sequence guess.

Resolved: the shared IPC wire format is proven from libsonosutils.so.1 (the lib both ends link). SendIPCMessageWithData writes a 12-byte outer header {w0=0xc outer-header-size, w1=1 (protocol class/version), w2=innerLen=payloadLen+4} followed by the inner record {w3=arg4 message-type/code, payload bytes}; SendIPCMessage (no-data variant) writes {0xc,1,4,arg4} with no payload. ReadIPCHeader reads 12 bytes, requires w0>=0xc (drains w0-0xc extra header bytes if larger), returns {0=ok,-9=bad args,-0xa=short/read-fail}; payload reads are caller-side. So the wire layout is [outer{sz=0xc,cls=1,innerLen}][{msgType}{data}] - the anacapad-side 'IPC message received (%d %d %d)' logs the outer triple and the msgType rides as the first payload word. SendIPCMessageWithData accepts data_len<=0x800, so body_len=data_len+4 can reach0x804; the receiver independently checks body_len-4<=0x800.

The earlier claim that the wire msgType indexes the24-row name catalog is withdrawn. Executed netstartd receive dispatch f_1000886c instead uses the42-slot0x00..0x29 table at0x1002f6f4 described below. The name catalog and state-name vocabulary do not establish per-message payload grammar; executable sender/receiver joins take precedence.

Daemon supervision layer recovered from shipped run* scripts in /etc: every daemon runs under a wrapper that gates on a /var/run/stop<daemon> flag (stopnetstartd, stopmdns, stopsddp, stopledmgrd, stopanacapa) and logs restarts via trackrestart appending date lines to /var/run/<daemon>.start (netstartd, sddpd, sonosledmgrd, anacapa, dropbear). runledmgrd additionally does stale-pid recovery: if /var/run/sonosledmgrd.pid exists without a live process it logs 'LED Manager PID %s is stale. Likely caused by an abnormal exit' (syslog pri 3) to /opt/log/sonosledmgrd.log then restarts. sddpd accepts a /jffs/dev_sddp.conf override of /etc/sddp.conf (-c flag). waitfordns() blocks daemons until /var/run/waitforip clears and resolv.conf has a nameserver. rundiagprocessd launches the diagprocessd fifo loop.

Resolved (IPC header semantics via shipped libsonosutils.so.1): the shared IPC frame is {u32 hdr_len=0xc, u32 version=1, u32 body_len, u32 msg_id, payload[]} - proven in SendIPCMessageWithData (lib @0x1658): writes {0xc,1,data_len+4,msg_id} then payload; ctx+0x70 is the socket fd, payload cap cmplwi 0x800 (returns -9 over 0x800, -1 on dead fd). ReadIPCHeader (@0x1508) reads 0xc bytes, rejects if buf[0] <= 0xb (ret -10) or arg bufsz <= 0xb (ret -9), then reads buf[0]-12 trailing header bytes in 0x40-byte __read_chk chunks - buf[0] is the header-block length, so the msg_id word + body are read by the caller per words[2]=body_len. The earlier '{type,length,seq}' guess is corrected: the 3 fixed words are {hdr_len,version,body_len} and 'Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)' prints those three.

Resolved (anacapad->netstartd msg-id vocabulary + payload grammars, from shipped /wifi/netstartd): the IPC handler f_1000886c dispatches msg_id via a 0x2a-entry self-relative jump table at 0x1002f6f4 (ids 0x00-0x29; default arm 0x10008990 silently drops 0,13-17,25,31-38,40). Wire payload sits at msg+0x10 with body_len (u32be @+8) == payload_len+4 checked per arm. Map: 1='anacapa hello' (full subsystem re-init sequence), 2='anacapa byebye' (logs byebye then re-runs init), 3=small command (body 0x8, payload word 4), 4/5='Entering WAC open mode', 6=netsettings push: memcpy 0x69-byte blob msg+0x10 -> staged @0x1005543e (id u32be @+0x21, string @+0x25), 7=0x44-byte blob -> 0x100555e0 (PSK record), 8=0x25-byte blob -> 0x100557e0 (37B, Muse HHID), 9=commit: copies {msg+0x10->0x100551e0 (33B), msg+0x25->0x10055624 (65B)} and moves staged blobs into active slots, 10/11/12='Deferring WAC timeout' variants, 18='Anacapa triggering joinhh' (household join), 19='join cancel', 20=0x6c8-byte payload -> f_10013da4 (large config/scan blob), 21='Disabling wifi for start of test', 22/23/24/26='Enabling wifi for end of test' family, 27/28=disable-for-test family, 29='MeshDisable: new=%d' + ath0 scangetresults, 30=Muse HHID resend + match check, 39=SonosNet frequency set ('setting SonosNet frequency to %u in %u.%u seconds', WifiFuncsIsFreqSupported gate), 41=SonosNet enable/disable ('SonosNet already %s'). Staging globals {0x1005543e:105B, 0x100555e0:68B, 0x100557e0:37B} are memset on IPC reset (f_10008714), which also clears connected flag 0x10050104 and unlinks netsettings_check.txt.

The /X-external premise was checked against executable consumers rather than inferred from slashes: f_102537b0 compares crashdump identities and selects suffixes; f_105403a8 forwards them with scheme https to f_1053faf8. Its caller at0x10253d64 passes the returned URL to multipart setup f_10545274; the attachment loop f_10253ab4 opens files and adds form-data/file parts named crashdump with text/plain content. These are outgoing diagnostic-upload paths, not proof of inter-daemon HTTP payload parsers. No exhaustive alternative inbound-route census is asserted.

Concrete anacapad inbound payload: msg0x34 reaches0x1069138c, decodes body_len at frame+8, requires body_len>0x23 and passes frame+0x10 to f_1064bc38. That consumer checks the big-endian length at payload+0x20 is<=32, wipes the old key buffer and stores bytes/length at owner+0x154/+0x174. Thus a registration-signing-key update contains a32-byte buffer and u32be length; it is not a textual eventType object. Bodies<=0x23 are skipped by the arm; key length>32 is separately rejected by the consumer. These exact numeric checks do not certify a complete malformed-frame audit: body_len includes the message-id word. The enclosing stream framing and per-handler semantic checks are separate layers.

Failed connection setup produces a disconnected descriptor and a short retry delay,while successful setup produces a longer maintenance timeout. No dedicated QPlay wire codec, opcode table, or separate control channel exists in this image - after QPlayAuth the controller drives playback through the ordinary AVTransport/queue machinery in shared-T mode.

Resolved: QPlay is a first-class UPnP service - /QPlay/Control appears in the master control/event URL table @0x10e76060 (between /ZoneGroupTopology/Control and /MediaServer/ConnectionManager/Control), and the device description advertises <qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability>QPlay:2</qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability> plus a #QPLAY_SUPPORT# template token. Seed/Code buffer contract pinned from the exec handler: Seed parse cap 0x80, Code/MID/DID out caps {0x80,0x15,0x15}; the transform runs inside impl->v[+0x08] on the req member object (see services/QPlay record).

QPlayAuth value derivations proven: MID is the compile-time constant "62800021" (getter f_106453a8 returns literal 0x10efc7a0; strlcpy into out, cap 0x15). DID = snprintf "%u" of member +0xcc on the singleton @0x110b8150 (getter chain f_106454a8 -> f_1090ad44 getInstance -> f_10908350 reads +0xcc). Code = RserializeData(MD5(Seed || key16)) where key16 is the 16 bytes at 0x10efc7ac (53 6f 6e 6f 73 03 11 19 88 09 10 17 1e 22 ff ff) - hash type proven MD5 via libsonoscrypto ZZ0062 type-2 dispatch (type1=SHA256,2=MD5,3=SHA1).

Resolved: MID '62800021' is a compile-time constant pair {id='62800021' @0x10efc7a0, name='Sonos' @0x10efc7ac} - two leaf getters return the +0x0/+0xc members (f_106453a8 / f_1064548c), and the consumer f_106453bc serializes both into an identity record via ZZ0062/ZZ0064/RserializeData on the upnp/zpUpnpOp path. It is Sonos's Tencent-assigned QPlay partner/manufacturer identifier embedded in the device description, alongside 'QPlayAuth' and the qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability 'QPlay:2' literal.

Resolved (DID provenance + Seed validity): QPlayAuth impl f_104666b4 emits DID = snprintf('%u', f_106454a8()) where f_106454a8 reads a numeric member of the lazily-initialized global device-info singleton at 0x110b8150 (via f_1090ad44 + f_10908350) - so DID is a runtime device-identity number, not a literal. Code is computed by f_10906304(MID='62800021', Seed arg) - no Seed freshness/replay check exists anywhere in the impl: it computes and returns 0 unconditionally, consistent with the documented 'entire surface is handshake-only' bound.
