Resolved: the accept ordering in f_10660e58 is fully decoded - accept iff (incoming version > stored version at obj+0x1f0) OR (versions equal AND strcmp(incoming LastUpdateDevice, stored LUD) < 0, i.e. lexicographically smaller LUD wins the tie). version == 0xffffffff (-1 sentinel) skips the newer test and falls straight to the eq/tiebreak branch; eq with a non-smaller LUD rejects. Within this actual SNTP receiver, owner+0x18f0/+0x18f8 are64-bit floating-point state, not a shared_ptr pair. resolved_findings: Resolved: speaker-takeover = RSpotifyPlayback.BecomeActiveDevice triggers the generic coordinator-delegation sequence: delegate to %s builds the member list, logs delegating. / delegating. isPlaying set to %d, then delegation. Resetting track queue info on the target; guards are delegate to oneself (self-short-circuit) and delegation target %s not primary (rejects delegation to a non-primary member). The adaptive-bitrate variant logs delegation for adaptive bitrate stream.

Seamless-delegation sequence decoded: on takeover the receiver issues Seeking to %ims in support of seamless delegation (set seek time to %u ms, byte offset: %zu carries the ms+byte pair), then waits for the eSDK AudioStart callback - Timed out waiting for AudioStart from eSDK during seamless delegation is the budget-exceeded path, and %s failed to become active reports BecomeActiveDevice failure. Track identity is bound via spotify:track:/spotify:episode: URI prefixes (Bogus track URI: %s reject). Events fired: SpotifyDelegationNotification + GroupVolumeChangedEvent + SpotifyMDNSRequest; cert rotation re-publishes mDNS (new cert updating mDNS service [%s]). Layering: esdk_api over esdk_spi with the esdk pump thread (W esdk pump log), NTS callbacks including kSpConnectionNotifyTransmittingData, and R_ServiceBitrate settings {ulow,high} feeding %s changed from %d to %d bitrate transitions.

Context proven: this module is part of the vendored Spotify eSDK (source paths /var/lib/spotify/buildagent/teamcity/work/.../esdk/src/) - the client speaks Mercury/hermes (hermes record: methods {SEND, UNSUB, GETX}, vnd.spotify/mercury-mget-request, hwptp device topics) for Spotify Connect.

Resolved: the AudioStart wait is a poll loop in StreamStart (f_10211d7c): each iteration calls the stream object's v[+0x50] (AudioStart-arrived check), sleeps via f_1098a850 -> usleep(ms*1000) with arg 0xa = 10 ms, then tests the deadline via f_1098ca54 -> timevalGeq(deadline, sonosClockGetTime) where the deadline timeval rides in arg2 of StreamStart. On deadline the 'Timed out waiting for AudioStart from eSDK during seamless delegation' path returns without seeking; the seamless path also computes the seek offset as (stored_pos*1000us + (0x10624dd3 - ticks)) and calls v[+0x64] to seek. The absolute wait budget is the caller-filled deadline value - runtime data, not an in-image constant.

Resolved: the tuning-FSM state enum is bound at the 'trueplay tuning state changed to %d' handler (0x1035af1c): state 1 = apply calibration type 'spectral'; state 2 = apply calibration type 'spatial'; state 4 = 'clearing trueplay state' -> f_100e421c clear call; states {0,3,5+} hit 'unhandled state %d'. Both apply arms first fetch the calibration id via f_102a50ec(dp+0x1a8c, buf, 0x41) - return 2 = found ('found calibration %s' else 'no calibration ID found') - then vcall dp+0x1a80 vptr+0xa8 with {calibrationId=buf, name='dummy', type, 0}

Concrete legacy delay parsing in f_10ddaeb0 reaches paranoid_atoi at0x10ddb1dc, rejects conversion failure and negative values, then passes the nonnegative integer unchanged as r5 to f_10ddd5b0 with destination selected from receiver+0x78/+0x7c. This boundary does not establish seconds, samples or DSP ticks. The seven RoomCalDelay names form pointer table0x10fe9de8; co-location alone does not join that table to this parser.

Spatial loader entry f_10dd8abc constructs trueplay_spatial_tuning.bin, checks stat, reads up to0x2000 and calls pb_decode with descriptor0x11029c98. Return values are1 for successful decode,2 for missing file,3 for decode failure. Thus this persisted spatial asset is protobuf, not established as the keyed textual calibration grammar. f_10dd83ec constructs/logs channel delay records; logging the integer with %u is not unit evidence.

resolved_findings: Resolved: chsrc.cxx major routines are documented in the sub-blocks - frame production runs {chsrc state machine (TRAN_* states, ChsrcEvent), the itbt frame pump, op_enum dispatcher, chsnk_control_frame_dispatch}; chsnk side: noderx I/O + SNTP-gated sync + seamless handoff worker f_10308e48; nodetx carries the transport; each block names its routine set and role.

Bus message format decoded at dispatch level: the CHSNK request-frame dispatcher (f_1030c8xx-0x1030cd00, chsnk domain) cmpwi-chains frame types {0->payload {u16@+0x2a, u8@+0x39}, 1/2/8->generic control frame, 5->audio type changed, 0xc->{u16@+0x2a,ptr@+0x40}, 0x80000040->f_1030c338; r3==0->stop detected; flag byte @+0x38->underflow detected + LSE recovery; request frame pbe %X playback-boundary event; logical track boundary at %u; default->group coordinator uuid: %s, network I/O error 0x%x}. nodetx is NACK-based retransmit (nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u packet-id ranges, requestResync(%u), protocol-version reject) with rx bookkeeping {pid, ob, lr, lcg, lrx, slrx} + resendToLateJoiner. HT satellite control frame carries {ctrl 0x%x, unscV %d, curV %d, extV %d, extVM %d, B %d, T %d, led %d, SPL %d, SC %d} beside the pkt: %zu channels, %zu samples, payload:%zu audio frame.

Correction: the AFC diagnostic identifier is formatted as hexadecimal text by __snprintf_chk at 0x1032d6d4 using the literal format "%04hX%08X%08X%08X%04hX%02hhX%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%08X%02X" (0x10eb83d0, followed by "AFC truncated!"). Numeric formatting widths do not prove a fifty-byte binary wire header. The dump-order/object-offset map below describes this text identifier, not a separate transport serializer. The rchsrcreq command vocabulary is a 23-verb enum @0x10eb84b0+: {CHANGE_TRANSPORT_URI, BEGIN_ADD_URI_TO_QUEUE, COMMIT_ADD_URI_TO_QUEUE, REMOVE_TRACK_FROM_QUEUE, REMOVE_ALL_TRACKS_FROM_QUEUE, INVALIDATE_RADIO_TRACK_QUEUE, SEEK_TO_TRACK, SEEK_TO_TIME, SEEK_TO_TIME_WITH_ITEM_ID, SET_PLAY_MODE, SET_CROSSFADE_MODE, REORDER_TRACKS_IN_QUEUE, REMOVE_TRACK_RANGE_FROM_QUEUE, RESET_PRIVATE_QUEUE, COMMIT_REPLACE_QUEUE, SKIP_TO_ITEM, REFRESH_CLOUD_QUEUE, CANCEL_ADD_URI, SUSPEND, PREPARE_FOR_DELEGATION, RATE_ITEM, GET_RESUME_STATE, SET_FIRST_TRACK_MIME_TYPE}. A scheme:mime map table begins at 0x10eb8750 ("file:*:audio/mpegurl:*,x-file-cifs:*:*:*,x-rincon:*:*:*,...").

Resolved: AFC dump-order vs object-offset map proven at the snprintf emit site 0x1032d660-0x1032d6d4 (dest = record+0x155 name buf, maxlen 0xa5). Diagnostic format order -> object field: %04hX<-u16@+0xea; %08X<-u32@+0xf0; %08X<-u32@+0x138; %08X<-u32@+0x13c; %04hX<-u16@+0x140; %02hhX<-u8@+0x154; %08X<-u32@+0x144; %08X<-u32@+0x148; %08X%08X<-u64 pair via *@(r31+0x124); %08X<-u32@+0x14c; %08X<-u32@+0x150; %08X<-u32@+0x12c; %08X<-u32@+0x130; %02X<-u32@+0x120. The +0xf0..+0x130 block is a member sub-struct accessed via getter thunks f_1045fcd4/+0x00, fce4/+0x08, fcf4/+0x30, fd04/+0x34(ptr to u64), fd14/+0x3c, fd24/+0x40. A 0x40-byte tag string is memcpy-capped into +0x1b9 with "AFC truncated!" diagnostic and +0x1f9 terminator.

Shared noderx/nodetx header corrected consistently with chsnk and chsrc_chsnk. The ordinary serializer f_10633870 and override serializer f_1063391c emit wire {u32be packetId at 0, u8 version at 4, packed byte at 5, u16be first-frame offset at 6, 1024 payload bytes at 8}, total 0x408 bytes. The packed HIGH nibble becomes record+5, and LOW nibble becomes record+6, not the reverse: f_106339d0 shifts wire[5] right by four at 0x10633a24, stores that at record+5 at 0x10633a2c, masks the low four bits and stores record+6 at 0x10633a30. The override serializer takes high from r5 and low from r6 (0x10633928-0x10633934); ordinary serialization takes record+5/+6 at 0x106338b4-0x106338c8. f_106339d0 skips the payload copy when incoming r6 is nonzero and returns wire+8, so it also supports zero-copy receive. The caller-supplied r5 stored at record+0x40c is not a wire field.

HIGH nibble is the packet class, with operational producer meanings now bound rather than invented enum labels. Ordinary assembly f_1063777c calls packet producer f_106374cc with class=0 at 0x10637868-0x1063787c. Class=1 is explicitly used to flush a resynchronization-control packet: requestResync f_10637d2c appends a marker chosen from 0xfd/0xfb/0xfe, then calls f_10637ca8 with r4=1 at 0x10637eec-0x10637ef4; that routine pads the current packet and forwards the class to f_106374cc at 0x10637cec-0x10637d00. The producer places class in constructor r7 at 0x1063753c, and f_106337e4 stores it at record+5 at 0x10633838. Class=2 is a NACK request: f_1044ab7c builds it with r7=2 at 0x1044abc8 and emits via f_10633870 at 0x1044abe8. The nodetx NACK listener deserializes at 0x1063869c and accepts exactly record+5==2 at 0x106386a0-0x106386a8; the ordinary noderx path excludes that class at 0x1044ca68-0x1044ca74. Class mismatch is explicitly named by the logger at 0x1044d11c. These descriptions identify behavior, not canonical source enum spellings.

LOW nibble is the transmission/replay discriminator, independently of packet class. Initial packet production passes zero in constructor r8 at 0x10637554. NACK servicing f_10638090 reserializes cached packets with low=1 at 0x106381d8-0x106381e4, 0x1063826c-0x10638274 and 0x106383f8-0x10638400, preserving their high class. Receiver low==1 reaches the startup continuity gate at 0x1044ca94-0x1044cab0, whose logs explicitly say NACK resend at 0x1044d084 and 0x1044d378. Low=2 is cached replay to a late joiner: f_10636574 passes r6=2 at 0x106365c4-0x106365cc. The resendToLateJoiner loop calls sender virtual +0x1c at 0x106cb188-0x106cb1a0; sender vtable 0x10efb75c contains f_10636574 in that slot at 0x10efb778. Thus value two in the low nibble is not a NACK class. No additional meaning is assigned to unused nibble values 3..15.

Header u16 is a payload-relative first-full-frame offset, not a type code. The seamless sink reads it at 0x10309608, checks offset<=1023 and offset+16<=1024, then parses a subframe header at record+0xa+offset (0x10309614-0x103096c4). The normal receive path likewise tests <=0x3ef before reading sixteen bytes at 0x1044cba8-0x1044ce90. Offset above the payload range denotes no complete frame start in that packet. Both paths demonstrate the offset semantics independently of the diagnostic strings.

The prior nibble residual is closed by the complete observed operational split: high class {0 ordinary packet,1 resync-control flush,2 NACK request}, low discriminator {0 initial transmission,1 NACK resend,2 late-joiner replay}. Source-code enum spellings are not asserted. The four-bit fields still admit other numeric bit patterns; this is not evidence that values 3..15 are assigned a protocol meaning or must be rejected. Do not confuse these packet-level fields with the separate codec/control type in each sixteen-byte subframe header. The full per-subframe body grammar remains tracked in chsnk rather than being misrepresented as a nibble-name gap here.

Resolved: regState (obj+0x12c, mutex+0x88) uses the 5-state family {RESET=1, OFFLINE=2, INITIATING=3, ONLINE=4, ERROR=5} (0x10fad930), NOT the 6-state TERMINATING family - the transition helper at 0x1064c540+ writes only targets {1,3,4,5} and nothing in register.cxx ever writes or compares 6; target pick: settings-key present (f_105ad9cc!=0) -> 5(ERROR); else byte+0x128 set -> 4(ONLINE); else byte+0x141 or customerID strcmp mismatch -> 1(RESET, with 'Household customer ID [%s] in conflict with local device [%s]'); match -> 3(INITIATING). Deepened (setter callers enumerated): the regState setter f_1064c540 (logs 'regState changed %d -> %d', stores to obj+0x12c, then fires side-effects incl. xori-vs-3 ONLINE compare + informLocalSecureRegStateChange) has exactly 4 callers: 0x1064c7c4 passes literal 4 (ERROR), 0x1064cd34 passes literal 0 (RESET, inside the NewCertRegistrationEvent handler), 0x1064cd8c and 0x1064df94 pass a stack buffer filled by f_1064bb90 (event-struct carriers, state extracted inside the setter). The ordinary serializer f_10633870 and override serializer f_1063391c emit wire {u32be packetId at 0, u8 version at 4, packed byte at 5, u16be first-frame offset at 6, 1024 payload bytes at 8}, total 0x408 bytes. The packed HIGH nibble becomes record+5, and LOW nibble becomes record+6, not the reverse: f_106339d0 shifts wire[5] right by four at 0x10633a24, stores that at record+5 at 0x10633a2c, masks the low four bits and stores record+6 at 0x10633a30. The override serializer takes high from r5 and low from r6 (0x10633928-0x10633934); ordinary serialization takes record+5/+6 at 0x106338b4-0x106338c8. f_106339d0 skips the payload copy when incoming r6 is nonzero and returns wire+8, so it also supports zero-copy receive. The caller-supplied r5 stored at record+0x40c is not a wire field.

HIGH nibble is the packet class, with operational producer meanings now bound rather than invented enum labels. Ordinary assembly f_1063777c calls packet producer f_106374cc with class=0 at 0x10637868-0x1063787c. Class=1 is explicitly used to flush a resynchronization-control packet: requestResync f_10637d2c appends a marker chosen from 0xfd/0xfb/0xfe, then calls f_10637ca8 with r4=1 at 0x10637eec-0x10637ef4; that routine pads the current packet and forwards the class to f_106374cc at 0x10637cec-0x10637d00. The producer places class in constructor r7 at 0x1063753c, and f_106337e4 stores it at record+5 at 0x10633838. Class=2 is a NACK request: f_1044ab7c builds it with r7=2 at 0x1044abc8 and emits via f_10633870 at 0x1044abe8. The nodetx NACK listener deserializes at 0x1063869c and accepts exactly record+5==2 at 0x106386a0-0x106386a8; the ordinary noderx path excludes that class at 0x1044ca68-0x1044ca74. Class mismatch is explicitly named by the logger at 0x1044d11c. These descriptions identify behavior, not canonical source enum spellings.

LOW nibble is the transmission/replay discriminator, independently of packet class. Initial packet production passes zero in constructor r8 at 0x10637554. NACK servicing f_10638090 reserializes cached packets with low=1 at 0x106381d8-0x106381e4, 0x1063826c-0x10638274 and 0x106383f8-0x10638400, preserving their high class. Receiver low==1 reaches the startup continuity gate at 0x1044ca94-0x1044cab0, whose logs explicitly say NACK resend at 0x1044d084 and 0x1044d378. Low=2 is cached replay to a late joiner: f_10636574 passes r6=2 at 0x106365c4-0x106365cc. The resendToLateJoiner loop calls sender virtual +0x1c at 0x106cb188-0x106cb1a0; sender vtable 0x10efb75c contains f_10636574 in that slot at 0x10efb778. Thus value two in the low nibble is not a NACK class. No additional meaning is assigned to unused nibble values 3..15.

Header u16 is a payload-relative first-full-frame offset, not a type code. The seamless sink reads it at 0x10309608, checks offset<=1023 and offset+16<=1024, then parses a subframe header at record+0xa+offset (0x10309614-0x103096c4). The normal receive path likewise tests <=0x3ef before reading sixteen bytes at 0x1044cba8-0x1044ce90. Offset above the payload range denotes no complete frame start in that packet. Both paths demonstrate the offset semantics independently of the diagnostic strings.

Body framing traced beyond the old opaque-1024-byte claim: f_1063311c copies a sixteen-byte subframe header, while f_106331a8 extracts {u8 type at 0, u8 auxiliary at 1, u16be body length at 2, two u32be words at 4/8, u32be word at 12}; serializer f_10633280 emits the matching layout. Packet diagnostic walker f_10633a98 advances by 16+bodyLength at 0x10633b24-0x10633b40 and 0x10633cd8-0x10633ce8. Its six-way relative dispatch at 0x10efb528 maps 0xfa=boundaryX, 0xfb=schedResyncX, 0xfc=boundary, 0xfd=immedResync, 0xfe=schedResync, 0xff=endTX. Ordinary type names use a mask clearing bits 0x60, then table 0x10efb558: 0=mp3,1=wav,2=wma,3=mp4,4=flac,5=ogg,6=alac,7=sbc,9=opus,11=ec3,31=encrypted; the other table slots say unknown. These are names and dispatch, not a claim that each codec payload has the same body grammar. The live noderx control path f_10449e78 consumes the sixteen-byte header, forwards body+0x10 and its length to f_10633400, which extracts a first u32 and an optional following pair of u32 words; the resync producer f_106334a4 emits the corresponding words. Full per-type consumers remain the residual.

Local persistence is f_10289258 -> f_102890b0 -> f_10508988 (call at 0x10289174), not merely the cloud XML endpoint. f_10508988 serializes through f_105084e0 into a temporary file and replaces the destination through rename at 0x10508a7c after serialization and close succeed. The close helper f_1054f0e8 calls fflush, fileno, fsync and fclose at 0x1054f108-0x1054f11c but only tests fclose, so a true result does not prove a successful durable flush. Serialization failure can take a root-only fallback rewrite and still return false; failure does not guarantee unchanged storage. On a true writer result, 0x102891ec-0x10289230 copies the local device identifier, updates cached counter/version fields and invokes receiver virtual +0x14 with selector 11. When callbacks are enabled, the separate predicate f_10285878 can schedule f_10285338 even after a false writer result (0x10289198-0x1028919c and 0x1028923c-0x10289250).

MusicAccountChangedEvent is a local notification, not an account or password payload. f_102850c4 reaches f_101b8048 at 0x10285128 or 0x10285170. f_101b8048 rereads the account store at 0x101b8238, compares it with its cache at 0x101b8250 and calls f_101bb1d0 on the changed path at 0x101b8290. At both monitoring calls r5=&frame[0x5c] names this string object (0x101bb688 and 0x101bb6c0). The call at 0x101bb690 is f_10bbca78, and 0x101bb6c8 is f_10bbd280 with r6=1. Both pass the source string in r4 and event-name string in r5 to f_10bbb834, which constructs the monitoring key as source + '_' + event name (0x10bbb868-0x10bbb8b0); these arguments identify the monitored event, not an account payload. The emitter queues a callable through f_100f14ec at 0x101bb73c when an event loop is available. The callable's source string comes from emitter+4/+8 (0x101bb6dc-0x101bb6f4), not the incoming account argument. The no-event-loop path instead calls f_10bbd098 at 0x101bb9c0. This is separate from the generic UPnP event-source callback.

manifest_refresh_precondition.description: Account helper f_10287238 derives SID as unsigned accountType>>8 and obtains the catalog through zone slot+0x130, with a direct zone+0x11a4 getter fast path when the slot equals f_1012ba78. It calls conditional refresh f_100c7404. Zero returns zero; any nonzero result is logged when enabled and becomes account error802 (0x322), independent of logging. This collapses busy800 and download failure801 into802 rather than propagating them. A zero result also includes the conditional refresh no-op, so it does not prove an HTTP download occurred. The five direct call sites are user-credentials0x10289df0, preinstalled-service0x1028aec8, OAuth-token0x1028b36c, OAuth-code0x1028b4d0 and OAuth-direct-control0x1028b644. Each supplies a corresponding operation-name string for logging. User credentials performs refresh before taking its account mutex and loading tables; nonzero returns immediately. Token addition returns nonzero before tail-calling f_1028a224. Code and direct-control additions return nonzero before f_10286e44 credential acquisition and their later f_1028a224 calls. Preinstalled-service addition has earlier descriptor/authentication gates; refresh nonzero goes directly to cleanup. These observations establish the manifest precondition in these paths, not success of the remaining account operation.

account_family_lookup.description: f_10570e34 searches a table with count at+0 and records starting+4 with stride0x250. Record serial is+0, type+4, username+8 and flags+0x1f4. It compares normalized types N(t)=((t & 0xffffff7f) - (1 - (t & 1))) modulo2^32: bit0x80 is cleared and even values move to the preceding odd value. For example types7,8,0x87,0x88 match the same family; the mask retains upper bits, but subtraction can borrow into them when all low bits are zero. This is the implemented arithmetic even at that boundary. A non-null username requires an exact strcmp match (or an empty record username for an empty argument) and returns that record immediately, before the flags test. With a null username, records with flags&1 are skipped. Among remaining family matches it tracks the smallest unsigned serial, keeping the first on equal serial. The initial minimum is0xffffffff and replacement requires strict unsigned less-than, so serial0xffffffff never becomes this smallest-serial candidate. Separately it remembers the last matching record for which f_1056fd48 returns true and f_1056fe5c(username) returns zero. With selector argument6 zero, that special candidate is preferred, otherwise the smallest-serial candidate is returned; absence of either returns null. With nonzero selector, the explicit username-match fast return still works, but the null-username fallback returns null. f_1056fd48 is true for record+0x1ec nonzero or a username longer than3 beginning X_#. f_1056fe5c searches the first hyphen and parses its following bytes with strtoul(base16), returning zero if there is no hyphen. The selection is a type-family and flag policy, not a credential-validity check.

A non-null password pointer replaces its password text with capacity65; a non-null metadata pointer sets the metadata-present marker to ASCII1 and copies the text with capacity128. account_save_fallback.description: Writer f_10508988 uses <accounts path>.tmp. It attempts full serialization through f_105084e0 and a close/check helper. If both are true it renames the temporary file to the live path, returns whether rename succeeded and unlinks the temporary name. If full serialization or that close/check fails, it reopens the temporary file for replacement and constructs an Accounts header using f_105071e4. In this fallback parameter block, Version is0, NextSerialNum is1, PreferredSerialNum is0 and a fresh empty vector-clock object replaces the original clock; other copied header fields remain. It writes the closing Accounts tag without any account-row emission, writes/closes this buffer and can rename it over the live file. select_lifecycle.name: RIRDecoder
select_lifecycle.interface_slice: Primary decoder+8 has vptr0x10ea6458. Cache fields live at primary+0x10 owner,+0x14 watched fd,+0x18 event mask.
select_lifecycle.getter: slot+0xc=0x10244444 adjusts this-8 and tail-calls0x10244430,which loads primary+0x54e34. Constructor0x102473fc initializes fd=-1 at0x10247e04 and HAL handle+0x54e30=0 at0x10247e14.
select_lifecycle.socket_producer: It is a character-device fd,not a socket. Startup0x10248e08 calls hal_ir_open(&primary+0x54e30) then hal_ir_get_fd(handle,&primary+0x54e34). libsyslib_hal.so.1 hal_ir_open0xeec allocates16-byte handle,opens /dev/ir with flags0x80002 and ioctl0x4004f400 identifies the driver type. Path is proven by .rela.dyn R_PPC_RELATIVE addend0x227c at GOT entry0x1ff0c. hal_ir_get_fd0x106c requires nonnull handle,marker5 at handle+c and device type1 at handle+4,then copies handle.fd+0.
select_lifecycle.startup_failure: The primary initializes fd=-1. Open/get-fd errors are logged,and get-fd failure explicitly writes-1 at0x10248f30. The same select registration tail at0x10248edc executes after success or failure,so a registered IR handler is not proof of an open IR device.
select_lifecycle.registration: Live parent function0x1024369c passes decoder=parent+0x218 and its unchanged r4 select-interface argument to0x10248e08 at0x102436e0. Startup tail-calls that interface slot+8 with handler=primary+8; RSelectThread fills handler+8 (primary+0x10) with owner.
select_lifecycle.callbacks: data+0x18=0x1024deec adjusts-8 then tail-delegates0x1024dee0->0x1024dd38. Read builds a buffer at primary+0x56 and calls hal_ir_read with handle+0x54e30 at0x1024dd8c. timeout+0x1c=0x1024448c adjusts-8 and tail-calls0x10244468 to copy timevalInf. exception+0x20 is no-op0x10c5d11c; reset+0x28 is no-op0x10c5d148.
select_lifecycle.timeout_constant: Main .dynsym names0x1109b008 as timevalInf,size8,and .rela.dyn contains R_PPC_COPY(type19). The defining symbol in libsonos-time-c.so.1 at0x20018 holds{2147483647,0}. These are not uninitialized zero globals or a periodic IR polling interval.
select_lifecycle.close: Decoder destructor0x10244fd0 closes a nonnull HAL handle at0x10245028. HAL0x10b8 validates marker5,closes the fd,frees the16-byte handle and clears the caller pointer. The live parent stop and shared-reference disposal chains are bound in live_parent_lifetime; neither executes the compiled unregister helper. Joining the selector and closing the IR device are separate operations.

live_parent_lifetime.parent: The player owns IR/TV parent pointer at player+0x3d508 and shared-reference control at+0x3d50c. Allocation0x1018f5c4 reserves0x55118 bytes;0x1018f6b0 stores the parent pointer. Decoder primary is parent+0x218; its select slice is parent+0x220. Live start0x1019c2a0 loads this parent and0x1019c2a4 passes r21=player+0x4d8 to0x1024369c,which starts/registers the decoder at0x102436e0.
live_parent_lifetime.stop: Player stop0x10193860 loads the same parent and0x10193864 calls0x10243424. Its recovered body removes the TVSignalDetectedEvent observer from an in-process event registry; it does not access the embedded decoder,call0x10245170 or invoke the decoder's select owner. Player stop subsequently invokes selector.stop at0x10193884,whose started branch joins the event thread. This stops callback execution but leaves the IR registration/owner in the registry.
live_parent_lifetime.destruction: Player destructor0x101928a4 loads the parent shared-reference control and0x101928b0 releases it. Shared release0x100c5050 invokes control slot+8 on final strong release. Control vtable0x10e988e8 has slot+8=0x101b43ec; it loads parent at control+0x10 and reaches decoder destructor at0x101b443c. Direct parent destructors also call it at0x101b3ff8/0x101b40c4. Decoder destructor0x10244fd0 calls hal_ir_close at0x10245028 and contains no owner-unregister operation. The selector embedded in player+0x3a8 is destroyed later through0x10192dc8 ->0x10692d10 ->0x106930f8. Retaining another strong parent reference can defer parent/decoder destruction; release of the player's reference is not an unconditional immediate device close.
live_parent_lifetime.uncalled_helper: The compiled unregister helper0x10245170 loads decoder.primary+0x10 owner and tail-calls owner slot+c with primary+8. Whole-text direct,conditional and tail branch census found no caller. The exact function-address word has zero occurrences in the complete ELF,so no literal pointer table or GOT entry supplies an indirect caller either. The live parent stop and destructors were separately inspected to rule out treating that unused helper as their delegate.
live_parent_lifetime.contract: The recovered lifecycle does not automatically unregister IR before closing its device. The explicit player stop path joins the shared event thread; parent destruction closes the device on final reference disposal. Decoder destruction itself does not check whether the selector was already stopped. There is no claim that arbitrary destruction/restart ordering is safe,or that an external caller invokes the unused unregister helper. This is an established lack of enforced unregister-before-close behavior,not a missing per-class fd producer.

The multipart attachment construction is a separate path. The earlier description of /upload/{...} local submission endpoints is withdrawn; suffix adjacency does not establish local IPC.

Resolved: PlayReportSubmitter submits on 'playEntry is a final report' notify (f_104caf08) and on a periodic interval logged 'periodic report interval set to %lld seconds' - the interval is a runtime-set field (r29 from object state, gated by flag bit 0x4), not a literal. Report field set: {serviceType, activatedAccountCode, errorStatus, errorType, multiAccountId, codec, originDelay, outputDelay, endReason, skippedTrack}; playhead is omitted 'due to LSE'.

Resolved: periodic-interval seeding decoded at the setter 0x104cba10-0x104cbaa8. The interval arrives as a parsed message field (flag byte + value u32 pair in the inbound record at stack +0xd54/+0xd58, emitted under the cloudqueue log domain); when the flag is set the value is divided by 1000 (ms->s) via f_10982360 and stored as s64 at submitter+0x40/+0x44 with enable byte +0x50. When the field is absent or value==0 the code writes the literal default 10 (s64) to +0x40/+0x44 - the default periodic report interval is 10 seconds.

Adjacent evidence: a distinct named config surface exists - setter f_107740e8 maps key 'reportIntervalSec' -> strtoul -> obj+0x508 and key 'url' -> strlcpy -> obj+0x106 (0x401 cap). This is seconds-scale, not the ms field of the cloudqueue parse record, so the residual stands; the name documents the reporting config vocabulary.
Established: interval is a message-supplied ms field converted to s64 seconds; default 10s; stored at submitter+0x40/+0x44 with enable byte +0x50.

Periodic-interval field binding is recovered. f_1033dcf0 constructs the response at outer+8 through f_1051a450; that installs the generated configuration model at response+0x8c4 via f_10a9a3b8 and parser binding f_10a9abbc. In caller f_104cb240 the response starts at sp+0x480, so model+0x10/+0x14 equal sp+0xd54/+0xd58. Serializer f_10a9a748 names those exact offsets periodicIntervalMillis at0x10a9a7ec-0x10a9a7fc. This is a named compiled model field, not an unavailable server member name.

At0x104cba10-0x104cba20, periodicIntervalMillis is sign-extended from32 bits (raw0x7c83fe70, srawi r3,r4,31) and divided as signed64-bit by1000, truncating toward zero. The result is stored at submitter+0x40/+0x44. The explicit beq at0x104cba90 returns without clamping when that result is zero, including absent fields and subsecond magnitudes. Only nonzero values below10 seconds become10, including negative whole-second results; values>=10 remain unchanged. The former unconditional/default10 and zero-fallback claims are withdrawn. Nearby reportIntervalSec belongs to a different configuration surface.

sp+0xd5c/+0xd5d map instead to model+0x18/+0x19, named sendPlaybackActions at0x10a9a7d8. The presence test and isel at0x104cba2c-0x104cba38 choose false when absent and the supplied boolean when present, then store it at submitter+0x50. This byte is not proof that periodic reporting is enabled. The same model has sendUpdateAfterMillis at+8/+c; its distinct semantics must not be conflated with periodicIntervalMillis.
reporting.summary: Reporting combines separate crash-upload and play-report paths. The optional periodicIntervalMillis field in the compiled timePlayed response model is signed milliseconds converted to whole seconds. A zero-second result remains zero; nonzero results below10 seconds are clamped to10. sendPlaybackActions is a separate optional boolean, not the interval-enable flag. Crash suffixes are outbound URL components rather than local upload routes.
reporting.service_manifest_endpoint: The direct caller at 0x104c9ccc requests endpoint type 2, binding this resolver to the reporting vocabulary entry. Its enclosing f_104c9bd8 constructs the runtime view and first requires its separate provider gate f_104c9acc to succeed. After the resolver call it destroys the view and returns the original destination pointer from r30, without testing or returning the resolver boolean. If the gate fails it returns null. Therefore a nonnull result from this wrapper is not proof that a reporting endpoint was found or fitted; caller buffer initialization and subsequent request construction still need tracing.

evidence.notes: Concrete service-manifest endpoint consumer; remaining chain is documented in svc_manifest.details.endpoint_callers.

Response+8c4 contains generated config; +10 presence/+14 value are periodicIntervalMillis, +18/+19 are sendPlaybackActions. Caller responsebase sp480 yields d54/d58 and d5c/d5d exactly. Model serializer names fields; parser binder supplies matching ordinal/offset slots. f_104ca444 constructs timePlayed request through f_1038e10c, whose JSON includes items/durationPlayedMillis/timeSincePlaybackMillis.

Provider slot+0x1c nonempty-pointer early true at 0x104c9b0c..0x104c9b20; URI parse and endpointType2 presence query at 0x104c9b58..0x104c9bc4. f_1011c29c only checks validity and matching stored type.

Raw0x7c83fe70 sign-extends the input; raw0x7f404f9e chooses absent sendPlaybackActions=false. The result-zero branch0x104cba90 exits before minimum logic: absent/zero/subsecond results stay0, negative nonzero and1..9 seconds become10, >=10 remain unchanged. No upper cap claimed. Model field offsets and names are independently bound by constructor/parser/serializer.

reporting.manifest_reporting_gate: Reporting gate f_104c9acc first invokes provider slot +0x1c; a nonnull pointer with nonzero first byte immediately returns true. Otherwise an empty item URI returns false; a nonempty URI must pass f_101477e4 and service-ID extraction f_1071aeb0, after which it constructs a manifest view and queries endpoint type 2 through f_1011c29c. That presence helper compares stored type values without requiring nonempty URI or an output buffer. Consequently this gate is not a universal endpoint-URL validity check. The exact provider-slot string meaning and the full URI predicate/extraction grammar remain to be traced.

Persistence + action mapping proven: learned IR config lands in /jffs/irconfig.txt (bundled for diagnostics). The HTControl action set {LearnIRCode, CommitLearnedIRCodes, IdentifyIRRemote, IsRemoteConfigured, SetIRRepeaterState, GetIRRepeaterState, SetLEDFeedbackState, GetLEDFeedbackState} with state vars {DesiredIRRepeaterState, LEDFeedbackState, RemoteConfigured, CurrentIRRepeaterState} shows the flow: LearnIRCode captures codes, CommitLearnedIRCodes persists them to irconfig.txt, repeater state is a desired/current pair. Resolved: irconfig.txt grammar proven from the writer (0x102459a0 seq) + shipped file. File = colon-bracketed sections {:repeat_codes:, :vol_up_codes:, :vol_down_codes:, :vol_mute_codes:, :input_codes:}; writer fprintf's each header then serializes a per-section code array via f_102456b0 over 0x20-byte records: per line '<count>,<hex byte string>' (fprintf '%d,' of u32 at rec+0x18 = byte count, then f_102444c0 hex-formats rec code bytes space-separated, '%s\n'). Shipped /opt/ir/irconfig.txt matches: '2,25 01' = 2-byte code {0x25,0x01}. Section arrays live at irconfig-obj offsets {vol_up:+0x500..0x640, vol_down:+0x644..0x784, vol_mute:+0x788..0x8c8, input:+0x8cc..0xa0c} (0x140 bytes each, max 10 records x 0x20). Learned file path /jffs/irconfig.txt, factory defaults /opt/ir/irconfig.txt.

Resolved: the shipped seed remote DB is /opt/ir/irconfig.txt: :repeat_codes: {4f 13 05}, :vol_up_codes: {2,25 01}, :vol_down_codes: {2,27 01}, :vol_mute_codes: {2,29 01} - NEC-style (protocol, command, repeat-flag) triples that seed the persisted /jffs/irconfig.txt on first boot.

resolved_findings: Resolved: consolidated - ac_impl implements the action surface (CreateAlarm/UpdateAlarm/DestroyAlarm/ListAlarms/GetTimeNow/GetFormat/GetTimeZone/GetTimeZoneAndRule/GetTimeZoneRule/UpdateDailyIndexRefreshTime), the internals block holds the timer store (sqlite timers+paused_timers tables) and the scheduler (StartTime/Recurrence/RoomUUID/ProgramURI/ProgramMetaData fields); muse_validation is the household alarm-mirror path.

Timer-fire path consolidated (ac_impl.cxx literals 0x10eaacxx-0x10eab5xx): time authority is the {0,1,2,3}.sonostime.pool.ntp.org NTP pool plus NTPTimeOffset persisted in the sysclock_state file (Read "%s" from sysclock_state / corrupt / SYNCED/UNSYNCED / timeDiff: %ld with large-adjustment flag); UTC availability gates firing via UTCTimeAvailableEvent and AlarmClockTimeZoneChangedEvent. Scheduling is DailyIndexRefresh + recalculate alarms, num pa %zu over pending alarms (no pending alarm / skip triggered alarm), with jobs handed to timedjobmgr_ac (Alarm's TJM is not running / Failed to ensure alarm job is scheduled) whose persistence lands in the sqlite timers/paused_timers tables (embedded_sqlite record). Fire path: RunAlarm worker (f_102e17dc) reads the persisted zpAlarm keys {id,eventType,start,dur,mode,fb_buzz,vol,linked,sid} and installs the program URI via f_102da774 with buzzer fallback; ReportAlarmStartedRunning reports state to the GC (RACZonePlayer/acZonePlayer). Guards: Ignoring alarm %u for room %s while in Exclusive BT Mode. Migration: Rhapsody/non-OAuth alarm conversion with x-rincon-buzzer:0 fallback. Alarm XML grammar fields proven: StartTime, Recurrence, ProgramURI, ProgramMetaData, PlayMode, IncludeLinkedZones.

Decoded: Recurrence is a 4-value string enum {ONCE, DAILY, WEEKDAYS, WEEKENDS} - literals at 0x10eaaf70/0x10f084b0/0x10f084d0/0x10f084bc, bound into GOT2 slots 0x1108ddb4-0x1108ddc0 and rodata table 0x10fad484; parsed alongside StartTime/Duration in the alarm record reader (f_10282d20 family). Not an RRULE grammar and not a raw day bitmask on the wire.

Resolved: snooze/group arbitration proven - the coordinator suspends cloud-queue playback during both snooze and alarm windows ("suspending cloud queue during snooze" / "suspending cloud queue during alarm" / "suspending cloud queue" at 0x10eb14bc-0x10eb151c), i.e. the alarm/snooze owner preempts group CQ content on the same channel rather than mixing. The muse alarm-state vocabulary is literal: ALARM_{DISABLED,PENDING,SNOOZED,FIRING} (0x10fac86c+) plus outcome states {DISMISSED, INTERRUPTED} and context types {PLAYER_WITHIN_GROUP, BATTERY_SAVER}; button-event names {PLAY_PAUSE, DPAD_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/SELECT, LONG_PRESS} feed the snooze/dismiss path; event classes {PLAYBACK, HT_PLAYBACK, HT_POWER_STATE, AIRPLAY, AUDIO_CLIP, SPEAKER_DETECTION}.

Resolved: the snooze duration is NOT a firmware constant - the SnoozeAlarm handler (0x106ed1a0+) dispatches as 'SnoozeAlarm' on service urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:AVTransport:1 and pulls 'Duration' plus 'InstanceID' out of the request arguments, so the snooze length is a per-request caller parameter. The muse routes are v1/groups/{groupId}/alarms/snooze and v1/households/{householdId}/groups/{groupId}/alarms/snooze (spec groupId,alarms,snoozeAlarm). The state emit is <r:SnoozeRunning val="...">.
Established: coordinator suspends cloud queue during snooze/alarm; alarm FSM {DISABLED,PENDING,SNOOZED,FIRING} + outcomes {DISMISSED,INTERRUPTED} literal.

resolved_findings: Resolved: session lifecycle = ctrl (vliCommand {apiKey,operation,position,volume}) -> link establishment through the source-manager group hooks {[groupAdded] configureLocalTransport(VLI),[groupRemoved] configureLocalTransport(null),[startLocalPBAsGM],[stopLocalPBAsGM]} -> sink via the vli transport stream; VliSessionEndedEvt tears down.

Session lifecycle consolidated from the sub-block vocabularies: StartSession (ctrl callback) allocates the VLI group id and mints the x-sonos-vli:<id>:<ch>,<backing-source> URI; SessionStartInfoUpdated pushes metadata; the link worker processes the group info (Starting/Found Suspended Rooms/Finished Processing %s Group Info in %llu us) and links member players (Link player %s to %s group %s ret %d, too many members reject); vlintxsink begins NodeTX transmission (NodeTx configured to handle %s audio qos %d) with retransmit-aware frame scheduling; SuspendSession parks the session (Failed to suspend/resume source, Thread entering state %d desired=%d) while suspended rooms stay linked; StopSession deactivates (deactivating current VL). vli_source_manager registers sources (Error 0x%x registering vli source %d).

Session-op enum recovered (~0x10f044xx): TXST_* transmission-state {UNKNOW(typo in image), CHSRC, LINE_IN, HTA_MESH, VLI, NONE} identifies which transport owns the stream; session ops {START_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE} are the VLI lifecycle verbs - JOIN/BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE prove the session drives group membership transitions directly.

Resolved: the VLI source-manager thread state field is *(mgr+0x2e0) guarded by mutex +0x150 (vli_source_manager.cxx ~0x106a81d4). Valid stored states {1,2,3} (bound r9=cur-1<=2); requested transitions {2,3,4} (bound r31-2<=2). 'Thread entering state %d (desired=%d)' logs current vs requested; the setter returns (requested==stored). There is no state-name rodata table - the enum values map positionally to the source ops {activate=2, suspend=3, deactivate/stop=4} by call-site order rather than named literals.

Narrowed: the {1,2,3}/{2,3,4} VLI thread-state set plausibly indexes one of the proven RESET/OFFLINE/ONLINE FSM families in enum_tables (0x10fad874, 0x10fad8e8 or 0x10fad930) - the family binding is not statically referenced.

Resolved: VLI control is an event-driven FSM (media_player_vli_ctrl.cxx) - event vocabulary {VliVolumeProcessingCompleteEvent, VliSessionProcessingCompleteEvent, VliTransportAction, AvtHaltActionEvent, AvtVliActionEvent, VolumeSetActionEvent, GroupVolumeSetActionEvent} fired by name through a completion-signal mechanism (cookie + flags, "completion signal timed out"/"signaling completed rc:"); vliType names {AirPlay, bluetooth/Bluetooth, tvproxy/"TV Proxy"}; StartSession rejects unusable/unknown types; protocolInfo "x-sonos-vli:*:audio:*".

Resolved: the VLI source-manager thread state at mgr+0x2e0 is a 3-value lifecycle enum, NOT the RESET/OFFLINE/ONLINE FSM family - all writes decoded: 0x106a9c34 stores 1 under mutex+0x150 then signals (thread start); 0x106a8184 waits on condvar+0x1e0 while state==1 then stores 2 (thread exit/stopped); 0x106ab080 stores 0 (reset/idle) together with clearing +0x2dc/+0x2e4; +0x2e4 is a pending-request slot (stw r31 at 0x106a8248, drained to +0x2e0 at 0x106a852c). So {0=idle,1=running,2=stopped} - it never indexes the proven {RESET..ERROR} tables

VLI session-op vocabulary recovered at 0x10f044bc: {START_SESSION, END_SESSION, SUSPEND_SESSION, JOIN_GROUP_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, START_AUDIO_STREAMING, PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING, BECOME_STANDALONE_BASED_ON_VLI_STATE, UNKNOWN}; transport-state enum at 0x10f04458 {TXST_CHSRC, TXST_LINE_IN, TXST_HTA_MESH, TXST_VLI, TXST_NONE}.
vli.summary: Virtual Line-In session pipeline: ctrl layer receives muse/UPnP callbacks onVirtualLineIn{StartSession,StopSession,SuspendSession,SessionStartInfoUpdated,GetVolume,NameChanged,MetaDataChanged,PlayModesChanged}; the link layer expands the VLI group (Link player %s to %s group %s, x-sonos-vli:<16-hex-id>:<channel>,<source> URIs carrying {airplay:,bluetooth:,uri:,tvproxy:} sources, suspended-room tracking via Found Suspended Rooms While Processing %s Group Info); the sink layer (vlintxsink NodeTX) transmits audio frames to group members with qos negotiation, resend bookkeeping (delay sending new frames until resend finishes), and lTransmitOffBox unicast control; SuspendSession/ResumeSession preserve the session while members sleep

media_player_mgr.name: mpmgr: MediaPlayer actor registry
media_player_mgr.summary: MediaPlayer manager owns an in-process registry and constructs concrete local player objects. It validates {uuid,ix,port,ssl,mtls} keys, rejects overlapping registrations, resolves actor targets and backups, prepares per-player configuration, and removes/shuts down registered objects. Remote command encoding is not yet bound to the local objects; a spawned-player-only protocol is not established.

evidence.notes: media_player_mgr.cxx

Creation allocates 0x1a70 through f_10809f0c at 0x10410270 and calls local ctor f_103fa434 at 0x10410744. Ctor installs vptrs 0x10ecac9c/+0x20 at object+0/+4 at 0x103fa68c/0x103fa694. Manager later calls f_103fd65c and f_103f9010 before MediaPlayer-created diagnostic. This disproves the missing-spawned-binary premise without asserting the absence of later network operations.

Output handle is zeroed at 0x10410060/0x10410064. UUID byte tested at 0x10410068-0x10410074; u16 key+a,+6,+8 tested nonzero at 0x10410078-0x10410140. Equality of key+a and key+6 at 0x10410144/0x10410150 branches to comparison with key+8 at 0x104117a8; only equality there returns to invalid path, so not a pairwise-distinct rule. Diagnostic loads key+a,+8,+6,+4,+0 at 0x104101e4-0x104101fc with format at 0x10ecbaf0. Existing-entry walk begins at manager+a0 and key accessor f_103f7638 at 0x104101b4. Invalid branch calls RabortIfUnlocked at 0x104100bc.

Register: lock at 0x1040fc7c, lookup/insert at 0x1040fcb4, shared handle stores at 0x1040fcc4/0x1040fd38, unlock at 0x1040fd50. Shutdown: lookup at 0x1040e9fc, remove at 0x1040ea60, unlock at 0x1040ea78, local f_103fe5c4 at 0x1040ea8c. Resolution checks filter+b4 at 0x1040ef08/0x1040ef18, bounds type<=10 at 0x1040ef20/0x1040ef24 and dispatches via 0x10ecb7e8; local literal branch invokes filter+8 at 0x1040ef7c. No socket queue or per-op encoding follows solely from this registry.

Constant 1.1.0 at 0x10ecb328 is passed to f_103f685c while building a stack string at +0x1ac inside the constructor. This is not an observed wire write; previous protocol-envelope inference and spawned-player-only limitation are withdrawn.

todo: Established: local manager/player construction, static vtables, key layout and exact validation predicate, registry assignment/removal and shutdown call chain. Still unresolved: bind the concrete player control methods and any outbound request/response serializers to actor resolution and recover their actual operation/envelope fields. Start with primary vtable 0x10ecac9c (methods f_103f8030/f_103f812c), constructor f_103fa434, setup f_103fd65c and startup f_103f9010 (called at 0x10410d60/0x10410da8), then follow request submission and completion paths. Neither the old typed-op queue nor a spawned executable owning an out-of-image protocol is established; the present residual remains actionable static analysis, not a proven missing-binary limitation.
resolved_findings: The former actor-queue opcode list and assertion that actor messages must be socket IPC are withdrawn. A target tuple and config filenames do not prove a queue format or process boundary. f_1040fffc allocates a 0x1a70-byte local object at 0x10410240/0x10410270 and directly calls constructor f_103fa434 at 0x10410744. That constructor installs static primary vtable 0x10ecac9c at object+0 and secondary 0x10ecacbc at +4 (0x103fa670-0x103fa694). Thus the manager and concrete player implementation are present in anacapad, regardless of what networking those objects later perform.

Target-key layout is anchored by the diagnostic argument loads, not inferred from endpoint words: UUID pointer +0, index u8 +4, port u16 +6, ssl u16 +8, mtls u16 +0xa. Construction first zeros its output pair and rejects an empty UUID or any zero endpoint field. The additional predicate at 0x10410144-0x10410150 and 0x104117a8-0x104117b0 rejects when all three endpoint values are equal; it does not require pairwise distinct values. Invalid input logs and calls RabortIfUnlocked, then returns the empty output if that call returns. Existing objects are walked from manager+0xa0, with their key copied through f_103f7638; the overlap diagnostic uses the same five fields. The u16 ssl/mtls fields are not proven Boolean TLS-mode selectors.

Registry mutation is local: f_1040fc34 locks manager+8, looks up/inserts a UUID-indexed entry through f_104129b4 on manager+0x98, assigns the supplied two-word shared-object handle at entry+0/+4 with reference-count maintenance, unlocks, and performs subsequent player configuration callbacks. Shutdown f_1040e944 looks up the entry under the same lock, copies its player handle, removes it through f_104125bc, unlocks and calls f_103fe5c4 on the retained object. It is not a demonstrated wire shutdown opcode.

Actor resolution f_1040ee78 checks the configured actor filter at manager+0xb4. When present it dispatches target-ID types 0 through 10 through a branch table at 0x10ecb7e8; other values take a separate path. The local-target branch recognizes the local literal and calls filter virtual +8 at 0x1040ef7c. The found-actor, found-backup, resolved-target and no-actor diagnostics establish multiple resolution outcomes, not a fully recovered remote transport contract for every target type.

Per-player configuration and logger setup remain separate lifecycle work: f_1040d614 and f_1040dafc are reached before allocation (0x1041022c/0x1041023c), and the manager block contains anacapa_logger.toml, /localsettings.txt and Player%s plus creation/registration failure diagnostics. The configuration of a named player alone is not evidence that a separate executable was spawned.

The previous request-builder/protocol-version interpretation of f_103fa434 is withdrawn. It is the local constructor reached at 0x10410744. At 0x103fc834-0x103fc848 it constructs a string from 1.1.0 through f_103f685c, alongside other object setup. This does not demonstrate an emitted version field or join that token to /players/ on a socket. Absence of another player executable in opt/bin does not make per-operation encoding unrecoverable from the present implementation.

resolved_findings: Resolved: restore path = savedqueues.rsq documents load via the SavedQueue parser -> per-track <Track URI MD> re-enqueue through the queue engine; curated queues carry Curated="1" flag and are read-only via the playlist browse path.

Curated semantics + restore path decoded: Curated is a queue-level editorial flag surfaced in the Queue LastChange event (<Event xmlns="urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/"> alongside <QueueOwnerID val>, <QueueID val="%.20s">, <UpdateID val>, <Curated val="...">) and mirrored in the track queue as the curation/curationState fields of playmodelEvent (tqueue.cxx). In savedqueues.rsq it persists as the SavedQueue Curated= attribute; SavedQueue curation string: %s logs its value. Cross-device restore rides settings replication: the file arrives as application/gzip or text/xml, validates against Replicated SavedQueue file is not valid and the version/id rules, promotes through the .tmp rename to file:///jffs/settings/savedqueues.rsq with .d.rsq backup, and runs the SQ:%s object-id + service-id migration (Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u); the export fn at 0x10478f28 selects gzip vs xml on a flag.

Resolved: the SavedQueue parse ladder (f_1047d408) reads attrs positionally via extractor f_10577db8/f_10577c40: Id, Title, Version (strtol), Curated (extracted to a string, logged as 'SavedQueue curation string: %s'), NumTracks, then '>' close; no literal compare pins Curated to a fixed value in the parse path - the extracted string's predicate is inside a helper. Track lines are <Track URI=".." MD=".."/>.

Resolved: SavedQueue header attr ladder @0x1047c270 - strcmp ladder over {Title,Id,Version,NumTracks,Curated} collects value ptrs into r26/r25/r20/r21/r19; requires Title+Id non-null; Curated (r19) passes verbatim as arg8 into the record-build vfunc v[+0xc] of the factory at *(parser+8) (0x1047c368-0x1047c394). NumTracks goes through paranoid_atoi with "Number of tracks not valid %s" rejection; queue id allocation via f_101472a0 with "Next available queue ID not valid %s".

Resolved: the queue-metadata Event emitter (f_10465b80 loop, stride 0x2574 per queue record) writes <Event xmlns="urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/"> with <QueueID val="%.20s">, <UpdateID val="%u"/>, <Curated val="B"/> where the Curated value is a flag BYTE at queue+0x52a serialized via the bool formatter (f_10676cb0), then <QueueOwnerID val="%s"/>. So Curated is a boolean attribute, not a multi-value enum - the curation string parser maps it to {0,1}. Full .rsq grammar: <SavedQueues LastUpdateDevice Version Next> / <SavedQueue Id Curated NumTracks> / <Track URI MD> / playlistSummary, gzip-wrapped (application/gzip), files {savedqueues.rsq, savedqueues.rsq.tmp, savedqueues.d.rsq}.

Resolved (curation subtype provenance): the handler ~f_10144a90 parses an inbound muse event where eventType=='curation' carries a 'curationState' string field (default '0', compared against '1') and re-emits it as a 'playmodelEvent'. So the curation subtype is a muse-model state - richer values exist on the event channel (curationState is a string, not the .rsq bool); the wire .rsq grammar collapses it to the Curated bool byte at queue+0x52a.

resolved_findings: Resolved: mount protocol = kernel-cifs mount helper with options {ver=1,directio,sec=ntlmssp,nounix} (SMB1-only, NTLMSSP, direct I/O) plus unc= lines; the directory iterator is resilient (Reopened directory/resume, reattempt=%d on connect failure).

Client implementation proven via the import table: libsmb2.so.1 is linked and the smb2_* API family is imported (smb2_set_password, smb2_read, smb2_closedir, smb2_lazy_opendir, smb2_opendir, smb2_stat, smb2_get_timeout, smb2_destroy_context, smb2_destroy_url, smb2_disconnect_share, smb2_set_version, smb2_parse_url, smb2_connect_share, smb2_open, smb2_fstat, smb2_close, nterror_to_str) - a userspace libsmb2 client alongside the kernel-cifs path. Dialect names SMB2/SMB3 are literals in sharelist.cxx (0x10e89d38), which also emits the <Shares>/<Share><Path>/<Mount> XML and the shareProcStatus/slp/shareproc status fields; remoteSettingIsBetter drives share-list conflict resolution. The two stacks split by purpose: kernel mounts serve streamed playback (x-file-cifs:*:* in the protocolInfo caps); libsmb2 serves the indexer/sharelist enumeration where SMB2/3 dialect negotiation matters.
smb.summary: dual SMB client stack: kernel CIFS mounts (ver=1 SMB1, sec=ntlmssp, directio, guest fallback) under /tmp/smb for queue playback of x-file-cifs URIs, plus the libsmb2.so.1 userspace client (smb2_connect_share/opendir/read/stat/set_version family) used by sharelist.cxx for SMB2/SMB3 dialects; resilient directory iterator with reconnect + fast-forward resume

resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with abr_engine - DS-selection uses the streamer capability map {accepted_mimes codec ids, ABR ladder} to pick the fetch backend per URI scheme.

DS-selection predicate decoded (literal block 0x10ed3xxx-0x10ed4xxx): each data source is ranked by a happiness test - happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d compares measured fetch rate a against a threshold, with a saturated-buffer override happy (saturated): %d %d; hysteresis via was happy: %d / unhappy: %d counters plus Underruns %u accounting; rate update: a=1 (was %.2lf) resets the estimator. Bitrate switching logs New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d and persists Last estimated bitrate %u (Reset ABR state: start bitrate %u). The failure ladder per DS: fetch failed: 0x%08x (%ld buffer) -> Unable to select another DS, waiting to fetch new playlist -> playlist-level ladder (Timed out looking for playlist, Too many empty playlists, Switching source due to empty playlists rc=%d) -> track-level ladder (track failed 0x%08x, Unable to find playable track, Track failure with no time to recover, Unable to select another DS, fetching new playlist now, Attempting to switch source due to InitFramerForTrackList failure). Prebuffer gate: prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec; URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d paces the playlist refresh. Codec filtering uses the mp4a.40. prefix plus a URI version regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$). Resolved: the happy predicate implementation (0x10481b30, logs 'happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d' at 0x10482010 and 'happy (saturated)' sibling) - the estimator a is SPE double math (efdcfs int-to-double, efdmul, efdadd, efddiv around 0x10481f50-0x10481f88) and the threshold is loaded via evldd from the selector object (r31+0x40-class field), NOT a rodata literal - it is a runtime-initialized tunable field. resolved_findings: Resolved: message types from the rx parser = the device-discovery frame set; signing input = the household-PSK signed span documented under household_psk_vocabulary.

Discovery message grammar fully enumerated (ddthrd.cxx rx log literals): the RDevDiscThread (devdiscthr) accepts six message types - MSEARCH (rx MSEARCH %s from %s:%d), ALIVE (rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s), BYEBYE (rx %s BYEBYE %s), CDALIVE (rx CDALIVE %s %s %d - the Sonos change-detected-alive variant), CDBYEBYE, and QUARANTINE_RECHECK (rx QUARANTINE_RECHECK %s). Unknown types log ???? and are dropped (discarding %s type %d); zp byebye marks zone-player departure. Reliability telemetry: %s - %u SSDP messages lost is the drop counter, ddt hint:%d tags worker hints, Finished working on type %d closes each batch. Message-type id is the %d in the per-type logs.

Field sources proven from the outbound header templates: ALIVE packets carry LOCATION: %s, NT: %s, NTS: ssdp:alive, SERVER: %s, ST: %s, USN: %s, BOOTID.UPNP.ORG: %s (the boot sequence), CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG: %d, X-RINCON-VARIANT: %u, plus household tags HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO / GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO / SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG / X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION / X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD / X-SONOS-DEVICEID. The rx log %s - rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s therefore logs {interface-or-source, ALIVE-variant, location, usn-or-household, configid, bootseq, household-group string} - the numeric pair is configid (%d from CONFIGID.UPNP.ORG) and bootseq (%u from BOOTID.UPNP.ORG); the two %s strings are location and usn. CDALIVE %s %s %d is the slimmed customer-device announce {location, usn, configid}.

Resolved: rx ALIVE arg order at 0x105a54b4 - fmt '%s - rx %s ALIVE %s %s %d %u %s (%zd)' binds {a1: peer-name *(ctx+0x188), a2: transport tag ('SSDP' or 'mDNS' selected at 0x105a5450/54d0), a3: advert rec +0 inline 0x400-byte id string (canonical usn), a4: rec+0x408 = LOCATION: value, a5: rec+0x424 int, a6: rec+0x428 u32, a7: rec+0x420 str, a8: %zd size}. Header parse ladder (0x10555dc0..) maps by name length: USN:(4)->rec+0x404, LOCATION:(9)->+0x408, SERVER:(7)->+0x410, X-RINCON-VARIANT:(17)->strtoul->+0x414, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO:(29)->stack->+0x448, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG:(24)/X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION:(25)->+0x420 region, plus NOTIFY/HTTP//M-SEARCH first-line and NTS ssdp:alive/ssdp:byebye classification; M-SEARCH responses parse {ST:, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD:(19), X-SONOS-DEVICEID:(17)}.

Resolved: the SSDP advert parser is a strncasecmp ladder in f_10555a54 consuming {HTTP/, CACHE-CONTROL:, SERVER:, HOST:, X-RINCON-VARIANT:, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO:, X-RINCON-REASON:, SECURELOCATION.UPNP.ORG:, X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION:, X-SONOS-DEVICEID:, X-SONOS-SIG:}. Each value goes through extractor f_105551dc into stack slots sp+{0x2c..0x4c}; VARIANT, SERVER, HOUSEHOLD.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO take strtol (numeric), HHSECURELOCATION/SIG stay strings, X-RINCON-REASON pairs with an inet_ntop address log. The collected values then feed the advert-record ctor (rec+0x404.. block).

Resolved: the advert parser is index-keyed via f_105551dc(line, headerIdx) - proven bindings in the M-SEARCH/NOTIFY walk: idx3=ST->r20, idx0xe->r19, idx0xf->sp+0x30, idx0x10->sp+0x44, idx0x11=X-SONOS-DEVICEID->r15, idx0x13=X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD->r16/sp+0x2c, idx9->r17, idx0x19=X-SONOS-HHSECURELOCATION->sp+0x4c; collected set then feeds the record ctor (ssdp:alive/ssdp:byebye discriminated at 0x10556054-0x10556078; NTS checked vs "ssdp:alive"/"ssdp:byebye" before record build).

Flag bytes +0x401/+0x402 (USN-parsed ok) track arm state.

Resolved: the unicast-MSEARCH header ladder at 0x105562c8+ is fully decoded - strncasecmp ladder binds {'ST:'(3)->search-target slot r20; 'X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD:'(19)->0x2c(r1); 'X-SONOS-DEVICEID:'(17)->r16; 'X-SONOS-SESSIONRETRIES:'(23)->arm 0x105564a8; 'X-SONOS-SESSIONSECONDS:'(23)->arm 0x10556514; 'X-SONOS-MDPMODEL:'(17)->arm 0x1055656c; 'USER-AGENT:'(11)->arm 0x105565b0; 'X-SONOS-SIG:'(12)->arm 0x105565f0}. Three numeric fields init -1 (r17/r18/r19) = the session/retries/mdpmodel value defaults before header parse. The accept gate is 'Accepting %s unicast MSEARCH from %s' after an inet_ntop source render.

Resolved: the second-ladder arm destinations are bound - the M-SEARCH pass accumulates into registers then packs a 7-field request block at +0x7c(r1) for the notify-handler call: +0x7c=r20 (ST: search-target value), +0x80=[0x2c] (X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD value), +0x84=r16 (X-SONOS-DEVICEID value), +0x88=r15 (USER-AGENT value), +0x8c=r19 (SESSIONRETRIES, strtol base-10 errno-guarded via isel, default -1), +0x90=r18 (SESSIONSECONDS, same), +0x94=r17 (MDPMODEL, same). The numeric arms share one pattern: errno:=0, value:=f_105551dc(line+hdrlen), strtol(v,0,10), isel acc,result,acc,cr7.eq - the -1 default survives on parse failure. Dispatch is bctrl through global handler ptr *(0x11097388) with obj *(0x11097384), r4=&block, r5=r25 (peer addr) - the handler itself is runtime-installed. The X-SONOS-SIG arm (0x105565f0) does not store into the block: it clamps the wire sig span (isel r9,0,len,cr0lt; isel r5,maxlen,len,cr7gt), calls f_105558b0 to compute the expected signature into the +0x55c(r1) buffer, compares strlen/bytes against the wire value, and on match sets the sig-verified flag (r31=1) which gates the handler dispatch at the shared tail 0x10555f28 - unsigned or unverifiable requests skip the dispatch.

Corrected (the M-SEARCH notify delegate IS statically bound): setter f_105557ec stores {r3->0x11097388, r4->0x11097384}; its boot-time caller at 0x105e6e2c installs f_105e6844 as the handler (the other caller at 0x10193a88 NULLs the pair on teardown). f_105e6844 dispatches the parsed {st,household,deviceid,useragent,retries,seconds,mdpmodel} block: vfunc+0x84 gate, then a vfunc-identity check (slot +0x34 == f_105a594c selects the base impl path), then rec+4 selector: nonzero -> vfunc+0x64 + tail f_105a4f30; zero -> vfunc+0x4c(rec+0 st string) match gate before the same notify path. The block's rec+4 is the notify-type selector, rec+0 the ST string.

select_socket_transport.instances_and_slots: Two0x30-byte RMSearchNotifyHandler instances are embedded at player+0x9d04 and+0x9d34. Constructor0x10555720 initializes socket+0x14=-1,reset byte+4=0,owner+8=0,cached watch+c=-1,event mask+0x10=0,last-failure-log seconds+0x18=0 and stored errno+0x2c=0. Player construction0x1018e0dc/0x1018e0f8 installs vtables0x10eea178 (unicast) and0x10eea1b0 (multicast). Both use getter+c=0x10555094 (reads socket+0x14),label+8=0x105550a4 (table0x110925c8),data+0x18=0x10555a54,timeout+0x1c=0x10c5d128,exception predicate+0x24=0x10556b48 (stored errno+0x2c),reset+0x28=0x105550b8. Their setup slot+0x2c differs:0x10555278 versus0x105554dc.
select_socket_transport.unicast_producer: Setup0x10555278 opens socket(AF_INET=2,SOCK_DGRAM=2,protocol0) at0x105552ac and stores fd+0x14. It calls fcntl F_GETFL=3 then F_SETFL=4 with flags|0x800 for nonblocking I/O. bind0x10555314 uses16-byte sockaddr_in {family2,port0x076d=1901,address0},so it binds all local IPv4 addresses on port1901. It sets IP_MULTICAST_TTL (level0,option0x21) to one-byte4,then requires a firmware SOL_SOCKET option0x29 with four-byte value8 to succeed. Failure returns0; success returns1. No multicast-membership call occurs in this unicast setup.
select_socket_transport.multicast_producer: Setup0x105554dc opens the same socket family/type at0x10555510,sets nonblocking,reuse-address (level1,option2,value1) and IPv4 packet-info delivery (level0,option8,value1). bind0x105555c4 uses wildcard IPv4 port0x076c=1900. It requires the same SOL_SOCKET option0x29,value8,then invokes0x10555400 to join239.255.255.250 with interface address0 via IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP (level0,option0x23,8-byte ip_mreq). A successful join returns1. For a failed join whose errno is exactly0x62=98,the helper attempts IP_DROP_MEMBERSHIP (option0x24),ignores that result and retries ADD once; the retry result is converted to1 for nonnegative and0 for negative. Other join errors return0 directly. Option0x29 is documented numerically because its kernel-side interpretation has not been established here; its failure is a concrete setup rejection,not an optional optimization.
select_socket_transport.live_registration_and_stop: Live startup calls the unicast and multicast setups at0x10199864 and0x1019988c,then registers both at0x10199884 and0x101998b0 through0x10555824. r21 is player+0x4d8,established at0x101988b4 and retained through both calls. Register helper null-checks the supplied select interface and semantically tail-calls its slot+8 with watcher and null optional timeout. The startup block does not branch on either setup result. Live stop0x10193874/0x1019387c calls0x10555858 for each watcher; that helper uses retained owner+8 and tail-calls slot+0xc. The player then stops the select thread at0x10193884. Destruction0x10192c00/0x10192c14 closes retained sockets through0x10555770,whose close is also a semantic tail call.
select_socket_transport.reset_and_failures: Reset0x105550b8 closes old socket+0x14 when it is not-1,then calls the concrete setup slot+0x2c. It stores (setupResult^1)&0xff into reset byte+4; raw0x5463063e at0x10555104 is a low-byte mask,not an8-bit shift. On success,last-failure-log seconds+0x18 is cleared. On failure,the code compares lastLog+3600 against clock-id1 seconds and logs only if lastLog+3600<now; equality suppresses the log. This comparison throttles failure logs,not socket-retry scheduling. Independently of whether a log is emitted,a newly allocated failed fd is closed and+0x14 is set-1 at0x10555170..0x10555184. Direct setup calls return failure without doing this close themselves; their live startup callers still register the watcher.
select_socket_transport.read_and_timeout: Data callback0x10555a54 sets its optional timeout output to{INT_MAX,0},reads one datagram via recvmsg0x10555b4c with payload capacity0x7ff and24-byte ancillary-control capacity,then enters the discovery parser. Stored errno+0x2c is cleared before the read. A-1 socket getter sets it to9 at0x10556008; a negative recvmsg result stores actual errno at0x10556018. The timeout slot0x10c5d128 also returns{INT_MAX,0}; neither constant creates a periodic discovery-socket poll. The multicast socket requests IP_PKTINFO,which the data path identifies using cmsg level0,type8 and reads the destination IPv4 at cmsg+0x14. Parser/signing semantics are separate from this descriptor ownership trace.
select_socket_transport.meaning: Unicast discovery and multicast announcements are independent registered UDP inputs. Socket setup success,multicast subscription success and select-thread registration are distinct outcomes. Watch removal occurs before select-thread stop; connection reset and later object destruction own descriptor closure.

track_play_monitor.name: RTrackPlayMonitor/trackPlayRecorder: play-segment recording
track_play_monitor.summary: Processes playback-segment records on a one-second timer registered with the shared event thread. It owns no watched input socket: its descriptor getter returns-2 and data/reset callbacks are no-ops. Stream and playback events supply track identity,metadata,position and errors to bounded recording storage; the periodic worker obtains current playback information and updates entries. The live stop path stops the embedded recorder and unregisters the timer.

mpegts_id3.name: MPEG-TS demuxer + timed ID3 (HLS radio metadata)
mpegts_id3.summary: The HLS segment path configures a compiled TS/AAC reader. TS PMT stream type0x15 selects a timed-ID3 PID, separately from the AAC audio PID. Metadata is accumulated in a bounded 32768-byte buffer with ID3 header/footer length and overflow handling. This establishes a local extraction mechanism, not a named-service emission allowlist or a complete downstream metadata conversion contract.

Raw rlwinm r26,r26,0,19,31 at0x104cdb38 keeps low13 PID bits, no shift. Packet PID comparisons at0x104cd654-0x104cd668; metadata PID match0x104cdd10 sets kind1 at+8. Audio-kind0 branch at0x104ce0e0-0x104ce0e4 checks metadata completeness0x104ce238-0x104ce258 and timestamp state0x104ce2a0-0x104ce2c4/0x104ce30c-0x104ce338. It passes r4=r26 to f_104ccb98 at0x104ce2cc-0x104ce2e8; output pointer/count advance0x104ce28c-0x104ce294. This forwards ID3 bytes into the read output, without a direct generic-ID3-parser call.

The generic ID3 parser contains file priv data id does not match framer id at0x1051ffe4 and logs at0x1051fff0. This is evidence of a private-owner/framer comparison in that parser, not a music-service emission table or proof of a completed link from TS reader timed buffer.

todo: Established: HLS segment setup reaches the TS reader; PMT types0x15/0x0f select timed-ID3/AAC PIDs, with exact bounded tag accumulation and header/footer length handling. Complete eligible tags are copied into the same output stream as audio, rather than proving a separate service-specific metadata callback. Remaining: trace callers/configuration writers of f_103b89bc and reader setup f_104cc7e0 back to service/source/URI selection, then join consumers of reader virtual+8=f_104cdff0 to the generic ID3 parser f_1051da18 and private-owner consumers. Determine whether any compiled service-specific metadata selection exists before classifying named-service mapping as external-only; if none, distinguish compiled acceptance from provider emission observable only in manifests/segments. Complete conversion and malformed-frame grammar are not certified by frame-name literals. These are actionable static joins; the old fully-proven/external-configuration-only limitation is withdrawn.
resolved_findings: Reachable segment configuration: f_103b89bc calls f_104cc7e0 at 0x103b8a2c for its embedded reader at +0x18, supplying the segment string, source interface and configuration arguments. f_104cc7e0 obtains the segment extension via f_105a3bd4, compares ts/aac/mp3, selects TS mode0 or raw AAC mode1 in reader+0x54 for the first two, and explicitly rejects the recognized mp3 extension with status0x80000004. This checked layer chooses a container mode, not a named music-service ID. That does not prove upstream service-specific source/URI/configuration selection is absent.

Constructor f_104cc758 installs static reader vtable0x10ed9190; its +8 entry is f_104cdff0. That read method invokes packet parser f_104cd500 at 0x104ce1f8. PMT processing extracts stream type and 13-bit elementary PID; stream type0x15 stores the timed metadata PID at reader+0x30, while type0x0f stores AAC audio PID at +0x10. Later packets compare their PID with these separate slots; timed PID match sets payload-kind1 at reader+8. Other PIDs are skipped through the non-audio and non-timed_id3 path. These are stream-advertised PMT/PES conditions, not proof of which commercial provider emitted the data.

f_104cdff0 routes payload-kind1 to f_104cd1bc, which accumulates metadata at reader+0x1b0 and count+0x81b8; it then calls f_104cca78 to compute expected tag length at +0x81b0. With at most9 bytes available that helper returns without decoding. With at least10 it combines the low seven bits of header size bytes6..9 in shifts21/14/7/0, then adds10 for the header or20 when header flag0x10 indicates a footer. Expected total above0x8000 sets ignore byte+0x81c8 and logs Ignoring too large timed ID3 size; exactly0x8000 is not rejected by this comparison.

Two separate bounds guard the same buffer. Accumulation f_104cd1bc detects count+incoming>0x8000, logs reading ID3 would write OOB, resetting and clears accumulated/copied/expected counts, timestamp and ignore state. Copy-out f_104ccb98 checks copied+requested<=0x8000 before memcpy from buffer+copied, otherwise logs reading ID3 would read OOB and does not copy. The read loop also tests expected versus accumulated bytes and timestamp state before exposing metadata. Therefore merely recognizing an ID3 header does not prove complete metadata was returned.

The output mechanism is stream reinsertion, not a demonstrated separate track-metadata callback. f_104cdff0 saves the caller output pointer in r26 and requested length from *r5 in r27; payload-kind0 is the audio branch. If accumulated metadata reaches expected length, is not ignored and satisfies the timestamp gates, that branch calls f_104ccb98 with r4=r26 at 0x104ce2e8 to copy the ID3 bytes into the caller output, then advances output pointer/count before later audio copying. The generic ID3 parser is not directly called by this reader. Binding its caller chain remains necessary before claiming every timed payload reaches a particular track-metadata/private-owner consumer.

The prior assertion that the named-service residual is necessarily only external configuration is withdrawn: no service-name/ID predicate appears in the checked segment setup, PMT selector or timed-buffer routines, but the upstream configuration writers and downstream consumer binding have not been exhaustively joined. The generic ID3 frame vocabulary below is not itself proof that every TS metadata payload reaches that parser or that its PRIV owner string denotes a music service. Actual provider emission additionally depends on supplied manifests/segments; no named-service emission list is established here.

Independent generic ID3 parser vocabulary retained from the earlier trace: standard v2.3/v2.4 frames with v2.2 aliases {TPE1/TP1 artist, TCOM/TCM composer, TPE2/TP2 album-artist, TALB/TAL album, TIT2/TT2 title, TCON/TCO genre, TRCK/TRK track number, TPOS/TPA disc number}; artwork via APIC/PIC frames with format sniffing {JPG,PNG,GIF}; COM comment frames; vendor extensions MusicMatch_TrackArtist, Media Jukebox: Album Artist, iTunes TCMP/TCP compilation; WXXX user-URL frames carry remote artwork keys {artworkURL_, imageThumbnail, imageSmall, imageMedium} with WXXX=%s emit and skipping unsupported key=%s rejects. PRIV frames are framer-keyed: found PRIV frame id %s len %zu / file priv data id does not match framer id - the same private-data channel as logical track MD %s with %zu bytes of private data (PRIV data for %s is too big, only %zu bytes allowed). 'Diagnostic stub'/'Local diagnostic' mark stubbed players; diag_progress.cxx tracks per-player submit status with a timeout ('Timed out waiting for devices to report their submit status' / 'All devices reported'). File-table flags and manifest type text are separate data paths, not a proven runtime flag-to-symbolic-name join. Raw rows at 0x11090228 have sixteen-byte layout {path pointer, flags, zero/reserved word, name pointer}: /VERSION has flags 1, /etc/resolv.conf has 2, and /jffs/app/log/anacapa.log.backup has 0xe (0x11090228-0x11090254). Row-membership nicknames such as standard/wireless/verbose describe inferred groups, not recovered enum spellings or verified selection predicates.

The manifest writer f_106b4cd8 directly emits <DiagnosticManifest type=... version=2.0.0>: format at 0x10f05460, keys type/version at 0x106b4cf0-0x106b4d00, and type value taken from incoming record r4+0x5a at 0x106b4d30. It writes the header through f_105458e0, appends supplied serialized content through f_106b8688/f_106b8694, and writes the closing tag (0x106b4d44-0x106b4dd4). A failed write returns zero. Callers at 0x106b6534 and 0x106b6564 preserve this record argument rather than deriving a type name from the file-row mask.

The aggregate HTTP interface independently parses hexadecimal f and e through strtoul with base 16, restricts them to 0x23 and 0x13 respectively, then ORs each accepted value into its corresponding accumulator at 0x105ea20c-0x105ea24c. type is copied as text into a 32-byte buffer at 0x105ea1f8-0x105ea204, without a bit-to-name table. include_crs=no adds e bit 0x10 at 0x105ea0b8-0x105ea0ec. After output, f bit 0x20 reaches the cleanup branch at 0x105ea16c-0x105ea178. Thus f/e action/filter masks, file-row masks and manifest text must not be assumed to share symbolic names merely because their numeric bits overlap.

Loads snapshot via f_105c7c44, guards its result at 0x105c93b4, then category-2 userMetricsTracking comparison 0x105c946c and boolean-string getter 0x105c9490. f_105c6180 reads parsed snapshot+0x28 at 0x105c628c. f_105c92a8 emits false/true only on status 1 at 0x105c931c-0x105c934c.

Builds householdsettings.json filename from 0x10ef4498, resolves it with f_1068ab6c at 0x105c7d9c, and calls f_105c79c4 at 0x105c7ddc. resolved_findings: The legacy array formats are sscanf inputs at 0x105c72e0/0x105c730c, not current seed writers. The schema-2 writer f_105c6af0 emits restricted-admin/settings {explicitContentFiltering,recentlyPlayed,hhSwgenState,museHHName,userMetricsTracking} and restricted/settings {autoUpdatesEnabled}. Persistence calls it at 0x105c6dc4, creates a temporary file at 0x105c6dd8 and renames it at 0x105c6dec.

Protected and protected-admin are recognized category containers, but this file implementation has no supported stored members for them. They are not a missing replication-delivered member list: f_105c7714 constructs category parsers with ids restricted=1, restricted-admin=2, protected=3, protected-admin=4. Boolean and string setters reject ids 3 and 4 through f_105c5a44, which only logs the status-page exposure warning. Getters select only ids 1 and 2. The current serializer emits neither protected category. This is a limitation of this firmware's householdsettings.json implementation, not evidence that similarly named Muse settings objects elsewhere have no members.

Legacy UMTracking query consumer: f_104b1d90 forwards ordinary GetString keys to f_10669db4 at 0x104b1e00. That function strcmp-matches UMTracking and calls f_105c99c8 on its household-settings receiver at +0x168; only other keys dispatch the separate settings backend at +0x164. f_105c99c8 requests category 2/userMetricsTracking with an eight-byte text buffer and compares the returned text with exact lowercase true. True maps to Report; all other results map to NoReport. It logs the redirection and returns zero after bounded strlcpy, so query success alone is not evidence that the household file was read successfully or that the caller buffer held the complete label.

Concrete household reader binding: constructor f_105c96d8 installs vptr 0x10ef4918 at 0x105c976c; vtable+0xc contains f_105c94f0. That getter clears the output first, delegates category 0 to a separate backend, and sends nonzero categories to f_105c9358. Category 2/userMetricsTracking takes f_105c92a8 -> f_105c6180, reading the parsed boolean at snapshot+0x28 and emitting true/false. f_105c9358 first loads a snapshot through f_105c7c44, which resolves householdsettings.json and calls f_105c79c4 -> sonosFileReadWhole, then the household JSON parser. Failed snapshot reads leave the cleared query output empty and therefore yield NoReport, without falling through to the syssettings.xml backend. This is a read projection of the household setting, not XML recovery, migration completion, a write notification or proof that telemetry was transmitted.
