fdevent.summary: ops {removeFd,waitForEvent}; thread names fdevent.{signal.write,wait.poll,check.poll,reset.read}; EventSync %s; epoll_create1/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait error paths; fd capacity bound "%d already monitored"/"exceeded the fd capacity of %d"

evidence.notes: fdevent block
ctor stores r4 -> +0x90; slot array +0x98 memset 0x300 = 24x32B

resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with fd_event - the registrant list is the event-topic registry; capacity constant = the fd-event table size in the registry block.

epoll wrapper fully enumerated (literal block 0x10ef40xx): ops {addFd,removeFd,waitForEvent} over epoll_{create1,ctl,wait}; thread names fdevent.{signal.write,wait.poll,check.poll,reset.read} form a self-pipe poll loop; EventSync %s syncs state; error taxonomy covers %s epoll_create1 error errno %d, unsupported flags %u, trying to add fd %d, %d already monitored, exceeded the fd capacity of %d, adding fd %d 0x%08x, epoll_ctl error fd %d errno %d, trying to remove %d, removing %d 0x%08x, epoll_wait %d errno %d, epoll_wait error fd %d events 0x%04x but not in list, called with no events to wait on. This record duplicates fd_event - same machinery.

Established: the capacity bound is dual - the printed %d is the per-instance ctor arg stored at obj+0x90 (fdevent ctor f_105c4824 stores r4), but the hard ceiling is the fixed inline slot array: memset(obj+0x98,0,0x300) = 24 slots x 32B, initialized to -1 by a ctr=0x18 fill loop at 0x105c48a0, epoll fd at +0x398. Effective capacity = min(configured, 24).

Corrected (ctor arg identity): f_105c4824's r4 -> +0x90 is the instance NAME tag, not a capacity - it is printed verbatim by the 'EventSync %s' log immediately after the store, and call sites pass subsystem name strings (e.g. 'sntp_srv' at 0x104a90d8; two sites forward their own r4 name arg; one passes a config-object name field *(r28+0x7a60)). The fd-capacity bound itself is a pure literal: addFd walks the slot array with mtctr=0x18 (24) at 0x105c4a60-0x105c4aac, allocating per-slot {fd at +0x98+i*32, event bitmask slw 1<<slot at +0xa0, data at +0xa8, index at +0xb0}. Effective capacity is therefore exactly 24 - there is no configurable arg. The 'exceeded the fd capacity of %d' / '%d already monitored' strings at 0x10ef40f4/0x10ef4122 have zero references in .text or data pointer tables in this image - they belong to a second fdevent variant compiled for a different configuration (the visible addFd logs through 'fdevent'-gated f_109b6fe4 checks instead).

resolved_findings: Resolved: renew FSM = {subscribe -> sid issued -> renew -> expiry -> resubscribe}; upnpovertls channel = the WSS-transported event path behind the lechmere subscription surface.

SUBSCRIBE/renew FSM consolidated: Subscribe ... Port: %u; Secure Eventing: %d (srRet=%d) -> Successfully subscribed ... UDN %s -> renew loop {Successfully renewed / Failed to renew HTTP Result: %d; SR: %08x} with out-of-sequence tracking (Received OOS %u / %u for SID %s), deleted-client guard (Received SID %s for deleted client), graceful skips (Unsubscribe in renew ... oos:%d seq:%d, Not unsubscribing because bSendUnsubscribeRequest=false); /status/subrenew emits the live table <Outgoing>{<LogicalSID>,<UPnPSID>,<EventURI>,<FailureCount>,<NextRenew>,<ExpectedSeq>}. TLS tunnel mechanics proven: transport identifier upnpovertls wraps member-to-coordinator UPnP calls - tunneled requests log Tunneled UPnP call: %s:%s from/returned %d|200 to %s:%d over TRANSFER-ENCODING (chunked) with an explicit body-length field set LOBS = %d; the tunneled action vocabulary covers ConnectionManager {ConnectionIDs,GetProtocolInfo,GetCurrentConnectionInfo,RcsID,AVTransportID,PeerConnectionManager,PeerConnectionID} (the member AV-stream binding) and MusicServices {ListAvailableServices,GetSessionId,ServiceId,Username,SessionId}.

Renew-layer vocabulary (renew.cxx): subscription bookkeeping keys {subscriptionId, renew_failures, renew, failure_reason, subscribe, unsubscribe, active_record, network_safe, subrenew_del, subrenew_sub}; zpUpnpSub/upnpSub are the two subscription record types (zone-player vs generic). Renew FSM: Received HTTP_GONE, setting renew timeout to max (gone subs back off hard); Unsubscribe in renew %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s (oos:%d seq:%d) - unsub during renew is logged with out-of-sequence+seq counters; Unable to find record (%s, %s) on orphan renews.

Resolved: TLS-tunnel request framing decoded (f_105d4ff4 sender) - the tunneled request is a rewritten HTTP envelope carrying the original verb and target as headers "x-sonos-method: " + "x-sonos-uri: " plus preserved "SOAPACTION: " and "content-length: ", written over the websocket channel after a lechmere.%hhu protocol-version handshake; the wire has a binary extended header {version:%c%c, message-type:%c%c, ext-hdr-length:%c%c} (Bad protocol version / Bad message type / Bad extended header length / could not recv extended header errors) then the HTTP payload. Receiver logs "Tunneled UPnP call: %s:%s from %s:%d".
Resolved: LOBS is not tunnel framing - "set LOBS = %d" writes a process-global at 0x110927bc (upnp-domain); it is a last-observed-boot-seq state field consulted for event ordering.

Resolved: the counter transport is /proc files, not ioctl or sysfs - the literal proc set @0x10e75764+ is ath0: /proc/ath_rincon/{device,fullstatus,mibcc,nf,phyerr,roam,station,status} and ath1: /proc/ath_rincon_ath1/{device,dfs,fullstatus,mibcc,nf,phyerr,primary}, plus /proc/driver/accel; scan results come from shelling "athconfig scangetresults ath0". mibcc=MIB channel counters, nf=noise floor, phyerr=PHY errors - the radio-health counter sources are proc-files.

ws_client.summary: client handshake {Location,Upgrade: websocket,Connection: Upgrade,Sec-WebSocket-Accept,Sec-WebSocket-Extensions}; "failing connection due to unsolicited per msg deflate"; per-msg deflate only before open; openSession retry; nonce gen/encode; {"disconnectedReason":"%s"}; close codes on close frame; LoadBalancerHost/WebsocketServerHost; reasons {NEW_IP,BLUETOOTH,POWERED_OFF,UPGRADE,NEW_SSID,SLEEPING,RECONNECT}; threads wsc_mtx/wsc_smtx/wsc_cond

evidence.notes: websocketclient block

resolved_findings: Resolved: users = {lechmere, spotifyzc, WSS eventing}; reconnect policy = the transport {status,protocolVer,reason,retry,uptimeMs,closed,failed,opened} state machine with retry field.

Consumer census decoded: the WS client serves three endpoints - (1) Lechmere cloud channel lechmere.%s.ws.sonos.com with negotiated subprotocol lechmere.%u (the household event pipe); (2) the local WSS event socket advertised to controllers as <NotificationAddr>wss://%s:%u (muse)</NotificationAddr> inside Subscription records (with a plain <NotificationAddr>%s</NotificationAddr> fallback and <IsSecure>%d flag); (3) the group-advertised WSS endpoint in RGroupAdvertiser - wss://%s:%d%s is emitted beside the SSDP GROUPINFO.SMARTSPEAKER.AUDIO advert (delaying group advert is the backpressure path). The generic client frame uses wss:///ws:// scheme dispatch, Sec-WebSocket-Protocol negotiation, and scheduled ping/send cycles ([%u] scheduled event %s / [%u] send ping). Related non-WSS ws.sonos.com siblings: sonar.ws.sonos.com (tone/sonar service), ir.ws.sonos.com/IRCode (IR code submit), ws.sonos.com/oauth/v4/pdsw (OAuth device-cred exchange).

Resolved: the group-advertised wss endpoint IS the muse event surface - the advert literal "<NotificationAddr>wss://%s:%u (muse)</NotificationAddr>" @0x10f00cfb self-labels the channel, and the single WS server negotiates only the lechmere.%u subprotocol ("WebSocket-Protocol: lechmere.%u" @0x10ef64e4, response "lechmere-v1" @0x10ee7220, cloud host "lechmere.%s.ws.sonos.com") - there is no second subprotocol family, so the advert points at the same lechmere/muse listener.

Check-layer role proven: this is the update-check client that polls the upgrade server (Fetching %s / Failure fetching %s (0x%x) (%d)) and parses a manifest response - the server returns the latest build via the X-Sonos-LatestSWGen: %u response header and the payload location via Content-Location: %s, with redirect following (Redirect detected, final URI: %s). Checks run in two modes: scheduled auto-check (updateAutoCheckError field) and user-initiated (Check for online update (user)), logged as Check for updates %s (%u); useCachedOnly forces the cached manifest. The request carries device descriptor fields {dd_mhh, dd_sn, dd_md, dd_bld, dd_in_hh, dd_in_ver}. Results land in the R_AvailableSoftwareUpdate system property (error saving ... on failure) which drives the availableSoftwareUpdate lechmere topic; UPM Invalid and Unknown upgrade server state cover bad manifest responses. The SWGen downgrade policy {downgradeMinVersion,downgradeRestrictions} is enforced here before any download job is queued - the actual image fetch/flash is the bin_upgrade/bin_upgrade_mgr layer, not this record.

Resolved: manifest request grammar proven - GET '<base>update.upm?cmaj=%u&cmin=%u&cbld=%u&subm=%u&rev=%u&reg=%u&serial=%s' and image fetch '<base>%s-%u-%u-%u.upd?<same query>'. The manifest ('manifest: Setting base update url=%s') carries a base URL override plus per-device rows consumed as {udn, model, submodel, swgen, ver, URI, updateID} ('update check zp: udn %s, model %d, submodel %d, ver %s, URI %s, updateID %s'; 'not in manifest, skipping update: udn %s, model %d, submodel %d, swgen %d'; 'manual update required: below manifest's min auto-update version'). Resolved: the .upm consumer binary ships as /bin/upgrade (upgrade_lib embedded). Container integrity vocabulary proven from its 62-entry error string table at .rodata 0x10024788: idx0 success, 1 file-format unknown, 6 signature verification failed, 7 file type unknown, 0x22 corrupt data (MD5 signature mis-match), plus encrypted-upgrade stubs {0x2d encrypted upgrades currently unsupported on this product, 0x2e no encrypted upgrade key available, 0x2f error decrypting upgrade} and u-boot/FCB flash errors {no available slot, failure reading/erasing/writing the flash slot/FCB, unsupported partition, read-back comparison failed, bad fcbs, bad uboot}. Payload extraction runs /bin/tar into /jffs/app/install and executes /var/upgradescript via /bin/sh; per-component rcb bundles land at /jffs/sys/run/rcb/{upd_cert_bundle,%s-%s}.rcb verified via imported sonosRcbVerifySig (libsonoscrypto ZZ* family also imported).

Resolved: upgrade_mgr<->upgrade comm FSM and download URL from the shipped binary: state strings {HELLO, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, REBOOT, CONNECT, ERROR, FINISHED, *_DONE variants} with reportOpComplete state/upgradeResult reporting; control socket via /tmp/upgrade_mgr.pid presence; fetch URL templates "%supdate.upm?cmaj=%u&cmin=%u&cbld=%u&subm=%u&rev=%u&reg=%u&serial=%s" and "%s%s-%u-%u.upd?..." with optional "&au=1" and "&sonosid=%s&householdid=%s" suffixes; region names {any region, United States and Canada, Europe, China, Japan}; device-query report file /var/run/upgrade_report.txt and /var/run/stopupgrade cancel flag; upgradeinfo keys {sonosid, householdid, ver_from, ver_system, dnlspeed, dnlduration, serverip, requestpath, status, state}.

Resolved (.upm framing, from shipped /bin/upgrade): the per-section cursor is {+0: ctx, +4: section header}; header fields {+0x4: type (valid range 3..0x16/22, matches the .upd type vocabulary), +0xc: flags where bit 0x2 = optional/tolerated when the type is unknown, +0x10: payload offset}. Dispatch runs a stride-28 per-type handler table {+0x10: arg, +0x14: already-seen flag -> 'Multiple sections of type %u' dedup error, +0x28: flags where bit0 = 'Skipping checks for section %u'}. Section flag bit0x1 => 'encrypted signature section not supported', bit0x4 => unsupported-encryption reject. File body is mapped via mmap64 (anonymous/work buffer rounded to 0x200, then copied). The cert-bundle section is parsed by sonosRcbParseHeader(data,size,verifycb=sonosRcbVerifySig) and persisted to /jffs/sys/run/rcb/%s-%s.rcb via sonosFileCreate. Error names live in an enum-indexed string table at 0x10024788 (idx 0='success' ... 'upgrade file format unknown', 'MD5 signature mis-match', 'bad fcbs', 'bad uboot', 'lost client connection').

RCB header decoded from sonosRcbParseHeader @libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2:0xc64 - file layout {+0x00: 8-byte magic "rcbundle" (memcmp, fail->status 3); +0x08: u16 BE version, must be3 or4 ((version-3)&0xffff must be<=1, fail->status7); +0x0a: 64-byte bundle name string copied NUL-terminated into the out struct; +0x4a: 16-byte field A; +0x5a: 16-byte field B; +0x6a: u16 BE section count <=0x12c (300, fail->status 4); +0x6c: section directory begins}. Header consumed = 0x6c bytes; the0x78-byte output struct includes version at+0, a terminated name at+2 and identifier arrays at+0x43/+0x53, plus section metadata. The caller-supplied verification callback is argument3 (r5) whose status must be0 or9 to continue parsing; all bounds checks return status 8.

Both header16-byte fields are consumed together by the stash-name path. The old claim that field2 has no consumer is withdrawn. The &au=1 test at upgrade0x1000a4e4 reads stack+0x9b in a different function frame and does not establish a bundle-id bit test.

Independently checked sibling parser f_10003bc0 assigns UNDEFINED/CONNECT/HELLO/DOWNLOAD/FLASHWRITE/WAIT/REBOOT/ERROR/FINISHED values0..8. Update-result vocabulary at0x10fad0cc includes NO_DEVICES_NEED_UPDATE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, INFO_FILE_WRITE_FAILED, BSU_FAILED, UPGRADE_MGR_SPAWN_FAILED, MANIFEST_DOWNLOAD_FAILED, MANIFEST_PARSE_FAILED, UPDATE_NEVER_RUN and FINAL_RESULT_UNKNOWN. Encoding selection traced in f_102934f4: a null or empty encoding argument queries R_AudioInEncodeType through object +0x1e0 vtable +0x4c (including its specialized fast path) at 0x10293608-0x1029368c. Failed lookup falls back to the default path for a null argument; a non-null argument returns to string parsing. Otherwise it stores r5 into +0x838 and stores r4 into +0x834 only when r5 is zero. Thus AUTO/WAV/default preserve the previous +0x834 value rather than explicitly selecting a codec. The source URI and encoding vocabulary do not establish a capture driver, sample rate, bitrate, or ADC DSP chain. resolved_findings: SegmentTable growth policy corrected against GNU e500 and the fixed repository decoder: f_1029c56c doubles capacity with rlwinm 1,0,30 at 0x1029c848, stored at object+4; entries occupy 0xa8 bytes. The loop-count calculation at 0x1029c7f4-0x1029c810 first subtracts 168, shifts right by three at 0x1029c7f8, multiplies by 0x1cf3cf3d with mullw at 0x1029c804, masks with clrlwi 3 at 0x1029c808, then adds one. 0x1cf3cf3d is the multiplicative inverse of 21 modulo 2^29 (21*0x1cf3cf3d = 1 modulo 2^29, not modulo 2^32). For the exact 168-byte-multiple pointer difference this recovers the entry count; it is not a right shift by 29 after multiplication. The old srwi-29 description came from the shared decoder alias bug and is withdrawn. Growth logging independently prints the doubled capacity.

Resolved (SegmentTable growth policy, f_1029c56c realloc path at 0x1029c800-0x1029c884): the table doubles on each growth - new cap = old cap << 1 (slwi r9,r9,1 at 0x1029c848 stored back to obj+0x4), entries are fixed 0xa8 (168) bytes each and the realloc copies the last entry over the freed slot then compacts; the entry-count loop uses multiply-shift division by 0xa8 (ori 0xcf3d + mulli + srwi 29 at 0x1029c7f4-0x1029c80c). 'SegmentTable reallocated to %zu entries' prints the doubled capacity.

Initialization provenance resolved: 0x1025f6b4/0x1025f6f4 seeds the containing object buffer-size member +0x26f4 with 0x00300000 (3 MiB). Hardware-query branches at 0x1025fcc0-0x1025fcec and 0x1025fd74-0x1025fd88 can replace it with 0x00c00000 (12 MiB): the first checks f_10909730 and unsigned f_10909570 > 6; the second checks f_109096c4 and f_10909570 > 2. These helper names do not establish marketing model names. The size is passed as r5 at 0x1025fdc4 to constructor f_1029f07c; the constructor saves it in r28 and forwards it as r4 to f_1029af68 at 0x1029f25c. The caller r6 is a multithreading boolean derived from hardware queries, forwarded as init r5, not a rate-limit value from a settings pointer. Init masks the size with rlwinm 0,0,17 at 0x1029afa8, clearing the low 14 bits (16 KiB alignment), and stores size>>14 at +0x114. At 0x1029b024-0x1029b028 it unconditionally initializes +0x154 to 0x1770 = 6000 microseconds, the value printed as ratelimit. Thus both initial buffer capacities and the initial rate-limit value are compiled literals, contrary to the earlier runtime-settings claim. A zero size skips allocation; allocation failures clear the allocated-buffer state at 0x1029b0d0 onward. These are initialization defaults, not a claim that no later tuning occurs.

resolved_findings: Resolved: ST_SESSION_ACTIVE -> upgrade_mgr launch = the session-state transition hands off to the external upgrade_mgr with the manifest row; the window gate is the AutoUpdateWindow seconds-since-midnight range.

Window computation and launch proven (auto_update_scheduler.cxx, updateScheduler domain): the window is an HH:MM:SS range persisted via R_AutoUpdateWindowStart; shrinkWindow trims it (Trimming the window to (%d) seconds). ST_SESSION_ACTIVE gates on two blockers - Upcoming alarm is preventing update and Active device(s) preventing update (the <ActiveDeviceList> in UpdateInfo XML names them). Resolved: the device-wait retry loop (f_100d53a8) bounds attempts by a literal 5 - attempt counter at obj+0x30 increments each round and count>5 exits to 'We timed out on %zu devices after %u attempts'; each round does gettimeofday + a timed 'wake' wait before rechecking.

Member-side receiver op vocabulary recovered at 0x10eef2e0+0x28: {CONNECT, HELLO, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, WAIT, REBOOT, ERROR, FINISHED} - the controlUri opcodes the member answers, paired with the coordinator-side FSM states {INIT, HELLO, HELLO_DONE, DOWNLOAD, DOWNLOAD_DONE, FLASHWRITE, FLASHWRITE_DONE, REBOOT, REBOOTING_DONE, UNDEFINED} in the same table.
Member-side controlUri opcode ids bound (0x10fad660): CONNECT=2, HELLO=3, DOWNLOAD=4, FLASHWRITE=5, WAIT=6, REBOOT=7, ERROR=8, FINISHED=9 - the receiver op enum now carries numeric ids.

Coordinator/member selection residual resolved in the shipped /bin/upgrade_mgr, not inferred from scheduler strings: main f_10000d88 loads the supplied infofile through sonosSettingsFileLoad with parser f_10002a2c at 0x10000e60-0x10000e70, checks the parsed device count and calls f_10003818 at 0x10000f48. The parser appends each successfully constructed ZP to object+0x218+index*0x3c8 (0x10002dd0-0x10002e28), increments count +0x7b18 at 0x10002fd0, and rejects a new row when the prior count exceeds 31 at 0x10002cf0. The startup pass at 0x10003994-0x100039d0 iterates those rows in input-file order, calling f_100022fc on every row rather than choosing a best peer. f_100022fc sets state +0x260 to CONNECT=1 and schedules per-member timeout and connection-retry callbacks. It returns zero, so normal startup reaches every row. No serial/version/model-priority comparator participates in this startup path; the earlier pick-next-member/election premise is replaced by ordered registration and independent per-member progress. This establishes the launched daemon behavior, not an absence claim about every possible coordinator-selection mechanism elsewhere.

The cross-member decision is a reboot barrier, not a next-peer election. f_10003360 first scans the complete array and returns without starting reboot if any member state is >0 and <=4 (CONNECT, HELLO, DOWNLOAD or FLASHWRITE). If all rows pass, a second ascending-index pass invokes f_10002370 for every WAIT=5 member, not just the first. That callee changes WAIT to REBOOT=6, selects command index 4 and sends REBOOT?Delay=5 through f_10001424 (0x100023c0-0x100023d4, 0x10001564). UNDEFINED=0, ERROR=7 and FINISHED=8 do not block that barrier, while an empty array returns zero. The callback is reachable: parser f_10002a2c supplies f_1000346c as progress callback and f_100035f8 as completion callback to constructor f_10001f30, which stores them at member+0x258/+0x254. Progress callback f_1000346c falls through to f_10003478, which invokes the barrier for state WAIT=5; completion callback f_100035f8 falls through to f_10003604, which also invokes the barrier for an ERROR member while others remain. The normal COMPLETE/HELLO processing in f_10001684 increments per-member state/command, schedules WAIT retries, and invokes progress callback at 0x10001770-0x1000178c. Terminal/timeout paths invoke completion callback through +0x254 (0x10002228-0x10002244 and 0x10002188-0x100021ac). These call paths disprove the assumption that a ranking comparator must advance the next household device.

State and phase enums corrected from the actual /bin/upgrade_mgr tables: member state +0x260 uses 0:UNDEFINED,1:CONNECT,2:HELLO,3:DOWNLOAD,4:FLASHWRITE,5:WAIT,6:REBOOT,7:ERROR,8:FINISHED at 0x10005cbc. f_10003bc0 string parser confirms FLASHWRITE=4 and WAIT=5 at 0x10003d00-0x10003d20; the earlier swapped ids are withdrawn. The separate phase table at 0x10005c98 is INIT,HELLO,HELLO_DONE,DOWNLOAD,DOWNLOAD_DONE,FLASHWRITE,FLASHWRITE_DONE,REBOOT,REBOOTING_DONE. f_100031d8 counts FINISHED=8 rows for progress/final reporting; errors also feed the completion scan in f_10003604, which counts states >=7 for terminal completion. Empty parsed input takes the No devices to update report/exit-1 path at 0x10000e88, rather than trying to elect a device.

Protocol direction corrected while tracing the callbacks: /bin/upgrade_mgr member connections use nonblocking TCP to port 0x115c=4444 in f_10001c8c, not HTTP requests constructed from the command vocabulary. f_10001424 serializes a command as %s%s plus newline, using HELLO/DOWNLOAD/FLASHWRITE/PING/REBOOT table 0x10005228. Separately, f_1000245c formats status text and sends it through accepted status-client socket object+0x7c34; STATUS?phase, COMPLETE?phase and ERROR?phase report lines are built by callbacks f_10003478/f_10003604 and flow there. They are not proven NOTIFY bodies sent to a per-member controlUri. SSDP NOTIFY advertisement is a different path in f_10003058. The earlier conflation of report lines, HTTP member commands and SSDP is withdrawn. The anacapad receiver enum at 0x10fad660 is a separate binary-local enum, not these daemon state ids.

Secondary ZPs reject coordinator-only actions (AVTransportURI cannot be set to non-group URI on secondary ZPs, BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup improperly called on secondary ZP, BecomeGroupCoordinator improperly called, BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource improperly called) - role checks run before job entry. HT URIs route to the home-theater pipeline: x-sonos-htastream:%s opens the SPDIF/TV source rather than a network streamer; x-rincon-stream:%s is the line-in/network source; x-rincon-buzzer:1 is the custom alarm tone; the demo line-in URI plus Demo mode update available (%s) cover the retail path.

The dual URN set {urn:schemas-sonos-com:service:ContentDirectory:1, urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:ContentDirectory:1} serves both namespaces; zh-CN/ja-JP locale variants exist. Event vars {SystemUpdateID, ContainerUpdateIDs, ShareIndexInProgress, ShareIndexLastError, FavoritesUpdateID, RadioFavoritesUpdateID, RadioLocationUpdateID, SavedQueuesUpdateID, ShareListUpdateID, cdMediaServer} are the LastChange payload vocabulary. Resolved: the ContainerID prefix dispatch ladder is literal @0x10e77fc0+: RDCPA:ARTALBUM: -> explore:artist:mainreleases::art.%s; RDCPA:ARTCOMPILATIONS: -> explore:artist:compilations::art.%s; RDCPA:ARTSINGLESEPS: -> explore:artist:singlesandeps::art.%s; RDCPA:ARTTOPTRACKS: -> explore:artist:toptracks::art.%s; RDCPA:GLBALBUM: -> explore:album::alb.%s; RDCPA:GLBARTIST: -> explore:artist::art.%s; RDCPA:GLBPLAYLIST: -> explore:playlist::pp.%s; RDCPA:LIBPLAYLISTS: -> explore:playlist::mp.%s; RDCPA:LIBPLAYLISTS (no colon) -> mymusic:playlists; RDCPA:LIBALBUM: -> mymusic:album::alb.%s; RDCPI:ARTSTATION:/RDCPI:GLBSTATION:/RDCPI:GLBTRACK: are item-level URIs. So prefix rows ARE literal: RDCPA = container prefixes, RDCPI = item prefixes, each mapping to an explore:/mymusic: target template.

The RDCPA/RDCPI mapping is positively bound to a Rhapsody-ID converter, not proven as the entire ContentDirectory backend namespace registry. f_100ceb4c loads constant table 0x10e77464 at 0x100ceb68-0x100ceb70, compares each prefix with strncmp, advances by 0x18 per row and stops after index 12 at 0x100cebd0-0x100cebdc. A miss logs Unknown Rhapsody ID type and returns zero at 0x100cebe0-0x100cec18. The first row is RDCPI:GLBTRACK:, followed by the twelve RDCPA/RDCPI rows already enumerated. No runtime count, append operation or plugin callback is used by this thirteen-row search.

On a matching row, prefix-map consumers read an optional extraction marker at row+0x10 and a target/template at +0x14 (0x100cec6c-0x100cec94). A null marker copies the constant target directly at 0x100cecfc-0x100ced14; otherwise f_100ce8f0 extracts the identifier and snprintf formats the target at 0x100cec78-0x100cecb4. Failed extraction returns zero. Fields at +4,+8 and byte +0xc are forwarded to f_1071d758 before the result is copied to the caller. This is immutable per-row conversion data, not evidence that SMAPI plugins register new rows.

A distinct reverse-conversion path f_100ced24 starts with radea:Tra. and checks four fixed 0x20-byte rows, using offsets +0x138 through +0x154 relative to 0x10e77464 (0x100ced98-0x100cee58). Its existence further distinguishes these provider-specific conversion tables from a general-purpose ContentDirectory registration API. The earlier blanket attribution of this ladder to all ContainerID dispatch is withdrawn; the broader backend/plugin registration question still requires the Browse dispatch call chain.

evidence.notes: audio_stream/mixing blocks
Source category forwarded to DSP, guarded by null DSP pointer.
Matching-ID playback-category store and volume/DSP updates.
TV/TTS/FEEDBACK category-dependent gain-offset branches, not packed sample formats.
Sample-size tests 2/4; two-byte conversion at 0x107ecd18-0x107ecd2c and invalid-size abort at 0x107ecd88 disprove integer-only output.
Unsigned requested-channel bound reads +0x1c4, independently of sample-size member +0x1c0.
Capacity at +0x1c4 stores incoming r9 preserved in r25; +0x1c0 at 0x107ee52c stores incoming width r8 preserved in r24.
Literal width 4 reaches initializer call 0x10de08f8; the same literal occurs before calls 0x10de0a2c/0x10de1610. Generic callers 0x107fe268/0x107fe42c forward r18.
Vtables 0x10f299e0 and 0x10ff10c8 slot +0x48 select this provider; its empty-state branch clears output+4 and returns 2 at 0x107ed1e8-0x107ed200.

resolved_findings: Resolved: mixer loop = the E:%d,D:%d,B:%d,PR:%d stats line reports {encoded,decoded,buffered,pre-roll} per pass through the mixing algorithm - per-source ring buffers summed into the output stream at the device rate.

Mixing model proven: each input stream carries presentation time (pt); writes are fixed-stride interleaved frames (attempted to write %zu channels, max %zu channels; %zd samples > %zu stride; unexpected sample size %zu). Arbitration is pt-ordered initial sync: underflow during initial sync: diff %d | opt %d.%06d npt %d.%06d, perfect initial sync %d.%06d, @initial sync required %d, sutUsec %d >= diffUsec %d - streams align on the scheduled-uptime vs presentation-time delta; resyncStreamLocked re-anchors pt. The mixer stats E:%d, D:%d, B:%d, PR:%d count errors, drains, buffered, presentation-ready. Drain FSM: set for drain during write / changing drain flag %d->%d / calling drain on stream w/o pt / dont have enough data available, !draining, underflow [%u,%u]. Gain staging is fade-slot based: fade added: %i.%i sample_len(%u) current_gain(%f) target_gain(%f) rate(%.08f) - a bounded fade table applies per-sample linear ramps toward target gain (reached max/min fade gain, fade complete, no fade slots available: %s), with stream attenuation on reset (reset stream - contained %uus. reset attenuation %d, errPT %d.%06d). skipAheadLocked drops buffered audio: headPT=%d.%06d, delta=%u, %u usec buffered; skipping %u usec (%u samples), preserved %u usec, pt %d.%06d -> %d.%06d; cant skip ahead when delta exceeds buffered. discontinuity detected after schedule marks sync breaks.

Resolved: fade-slot capacity = 10 - the mixer init loop (0x107ef3b8-0x107ef418) does li r10,0xa / mtctr then writes 10 zeroed 0x28-byte slot records, and the allocator (0x107ef490+) wraps slot selection with the 0xcccccccd div-by-10 reciprocal. Slots live inline from mixer+0x0c; the used count is at +0x190, secondary index +0x194; the dump path logs each as '[%s%zu: %d.%d (%d)%s] ' under domain 'attenuation' and emits 'no fade slots available: %s' when all 10 are in use.

Resolved: mixer fade/gain math shares the 8169-entry float gain LUT at 0x10fc0218 (accessor f_10cad098, interpolator f_10cad0b4) - ramp curves index this table rather than computing coefficients inline.

Resolved (streamSampleType vocabulary): f_10d91e74 maps the type id via a 6-entry name table at 0x10feb654 - {0:NONE, 1:MUSIC, 2:TV, 3:FEEDBACK, 4:TTS, 5:CHIRP}, out-of-range prints 'UNKNOWN' (guard cmplwi 5). This is the enum the 'set streamSampleType to %s' / 'changed m_playbackStreamSampleType from %s to %s' logs index and matches the as-*-tv/-ext-voice/-ext-chirp stream-name suffixes - the mixer instantiates per-type DSP chain variants.

Physical write-path correction: f_107eca90 reads sample size from stream+0x1c0 and accepts 2 or 4 at 0x107ecb84-0x107ecb94; other sizes reach the unexpected sample size diagnostic and abort at 0x107ecd54-0x107ecd88. The two-byte arm uses signed halfword loads, efscfsi and efsmul, then four-byte floating-point stores (0x107ecd18-0x107ecd2c). The four-byte arm copies words at 0x107ecbc4-0x107ecbdc; a word copy alone does not establish an integer sample representation or interleaving. The old integer-only and channel-set {1,2,4} claims are withdrawn.

Channel capacity is a different member: the unsigned compare at 0x107ec2d0-0x107ec2d8 reads stream+0x1c4 and accepts requested channels no greater than that runtime maximum. It does not enumerate a compiled {1,2,4} channel set. Category names and the TV/source-category gain branches remain distinct from physical sample format.

The streamSampleType format-table premise is resolved by tracing the setters: this enum is a source/playback category, not a packed audio-format word. f_10801408 logs the category name with f_10d91e74, and, only if DSP object +0xa4 is non-null, forwards it to f_10d7e2b8 (0x10801484-0x10801494). That callee compares/stores the category at DSP +0x80 and runs gain-offset update f_10d7e1a0. f_10801b3c handles playback-category changes for the matching stream ID: a mismatched byte ID at +0x9c exits unchanged; a match stores the new category at +0xd8, updates volume through f_108017d8 and forwards it through f_10d7e32c when the DSP exists. f_10d7e32c compares/stores playback category at DSP +0x7c and invokes the same gain-offset update. No packed sample-format lookup occurs in either setter. The six-entry table 0x10feb654 is pointers to category names only, accessed by f_10d91e74, with UNKNOWN for unsigned values above five. Physical sample width, channel stride and rate belong to the audio-stream data path, not that name table. This replaces the earlier unsupported assertion that a missing format-word table must be external configuration.

Positive category consumer: f_10d7e1a0 tests playback +0x7c for TV=2 at 0x10d7e1b8. Only in that branch does it select source-category-specific gain offsets: TTS=4 and FEEDBACK=3 have byte +0x200-dependent branches using +0x204 and +0x208 respectively; the other TV source categories use +0x20c. Non-TV playback takes the shared identity/default offset path. Each path converges on storing gain offset at +0x210 and refreshing gain through f_10d7d830 and f_10d7dc9c. Thus category-specific policy really exists in compiled branches; lack of a six-row format table is not evidence of missing sample-format data. This finding concerns category/format separation, not a claim that all DSP behavior is controlled by these two setters.

Format/capacity writers are identified, not an open writer search: initializer f_107ee420 preserves incoming r8 in r24 at 0x107ee43c and r9 in r25 at 0x107ee444. It stores r25 to stream+0x1c4 at 0x107ee524 and r24 to stream+0x1c0 at 0x107ee52c. These are constructor arguments, not a compiled set of channel counts. Executable direct-call census finds five sites: 0x107fe268/0x107fe42c forward r18 as r8 and the preceding f_105369b8 return as r9; 0x10de08f8/0x10de0a2c/0x10de1610 instead supply literal r8=4 and the preceding return as r9. The literal width is established on those three paths, not universally. The caller and initializer store chain does not identify the four-byte sample value representation.

A concrete buffer-provider target is also identifiable: initializer f_107ee420 installs vtable 0x10f299e0, whose slot +0x48 points to f_107ed16c; the derived table 0x10ff10c8 installed after 0x10de08f8 has the same slot. f_107ed16c checks stream+0x1cc/+0x1d0 at 0x107ed1d0-0x107ed1e4 and, when both are zero, clears output+4 and returns 2. This is a reachable empty-provider path, not proof of a full buffer-layout or four-byte format contract; other derived providers and the successful buffer path still require tracing.
audio_stream_mixer.todo: Established: width/capacity stores in f_107ee420 at 0x107ee52c/0x107ee524 come from incoming r8/r9; three direct callers supply width 4, while two forward r18. Two-byte input conversion, separate channel bounds and category policy are traced. Unknown: upstream argument semantics/constraints, four-byte sample representation and complete buffer/channel/rate contract across concrete providers. Next: trace r18 and the f_105369b8 capacity source in f_107fe1a4 and the three 0x10de08f8/0x10de0a2c/0x10de1610 caller chains; follow f_107ed16c successful buffer output and derived slot +0x48/+0x4c implementations into the copy/conversion consumers at 0x107ecbc4/0x107ecd18 before assigning a universal format or layout.

resolved_findings: Resolved: volume pipeline = Channel arg (SonosRcChannel {Master,LF,RF}) -> audio-context object via *(impl+0x3c4)/+0x9c8 under +0x938 lock -> f_100da830 read path; writes mirror through the same lock with LastChange emission.
The channel-control, EQ, propagation and LED-feedback literals identify concrete tracing surfaces, not completion of the gain-table provenance question.

Raw words at0x10fc0218..0x10fc0237 are eight pointers:0x10fc8138,0x10fc8038,0x10fc7e38,0x10fc7a38,0x10fc7238,0x10fc6238,0x10fc4238,0x10fc0238. All point into rodata. f_10cad098 returns the selected word as a pointer; its caller0x10cabb98 dereferences the returned address in the subsequent inner loop. Reinterpreting these pointer bits and following data as8169 floats produced the old unsupported gain-range/count claim. This is not evidence for a single scalar dB-to-gain curve.

The concrete setup path f_10788928 calls f_10cad718 at0x1078899c and then f_10cab92c at0x107889b4. The latter takes its table pointer from *(receiver+4)+0x1c and does index*4 loads and arithmetic shifts by table+0xe48 plus1. Its static-pointer helper f_10cad098 is called at0x10cabb98/0x10cabc50/0x10cabe80/0x10cabee0. These are real compiled producer/consumer edges; neither integer-volume indexing nor Q28 gain interpolation follows from them alone. The previous volume-object, fractional-layout and adjacent-volume-entry interpretation is withdrawn pending a join to actual RCS paths.

f_10cadb70 sets +0xe48 to a boolean, not an arbitrary fractional-bit count. It reads table=receiver+0x1c and compares table word0 signed with64. When word0>64, a zero request stores0 and a nonzero request stores1. When word0<=64, a nonzero request returns-1 without storing; zero stores0. Successful paths return0. Raw isel0x7c80279e at0x10cadb90 selects literal0 versus1 using the saved zero comparison. Therefore the effective shifts at0x10caba48/50/58 are1 or2 on these setter paths, not proof of a Q-format or a runtime-generated volume curve.
Channel-pair enum at 0x10e8b6a0: {L+R, L, R, S} - the stereo-pair channel selector.
Volume-level enum at 0x10fad834: {OFF=1, LOW=2, DEFAULT=3, MAX=4}.

Coefficient-address correction from GNU e500 disassembly: 0x107fc508 materializes 0x10f2b918, not 0x10f2b8e8, because signed addi -18152 is added to lis 0x10f3. That literal is -1000.0, not 328.6074362. Likewise lis 0x10ec plus signed addi 0x9ee0 is 0x10eb9ee0 (1.0), not 0x10ec9ee0. Prior named gain attribution based on the linear listing is superseded by the explicit recurrence below. The 32000-rate branch writes gains 2e-8 and 1e-5 to globals 0x110927e8/+8, and bias multiplier 35 to 0x110b6830; other rates retain the global gains (image initializers 4e-8 and 0.0001) and set bias multiplier 30. This proves writable globals, not a user-facing tuning interface.

Initialization and mute-path scope corrected: constructor starts 0x107fb414, with 0x107fb418 only its stack setup. It stores r7 to +0x118/+0x120 but r8, not a copy from +0x118, to +0x128/+0x130 at 0x107fb4f4-0x107fb50c. f_107fc6b0 calls update f_107fc46c at 0x107fc6d0; non-32000 paths select the literal 1.016 (0x10f2b948) or 1.011 (0x10f2b950) depending on byte +0x170, before calling f_107fb8a4. The 32000 path loads 200.0 from 0x10f2b928 at 0x107fc870. Therefore 1.016/1.011 cannot be described as universal thresholds for every input rate. The counter +0x174 and latch +0x170 are updated at 0x107fc798-0x107fc7a8 on the out-of-bounds path. The earlier exact PI/member-binding interpretation is withdrawn; the telemetry names alone do not establish those equations.

Local SPE recurrence in f_107fc46c decoded with GNU objdump -WN -M e500, including branch polarity: let e be double +0x120, p previous e at +0x118, I prior +0x128, R double +0x10, and K1/K2 globals 0x110927e8/+8. Form q=(e>0 ? 1 : -1)*e*e. Bias b is 1000 if q>1000000, q/1000 if q<-1000000, otherwise -1000, as the actual loads and branches at 0x107fc4c0-0x107fc510, 0x107fc5e0 and 0x107fc69c specify. Compute u=clamp(e*e*e,-100,100), v=clamp(e-p,-200,200), store e to +0x118, then Inew=clamp(I+K1*u+K2*v,0.9746588693957114,1.026) and store +0x128. Store output +0x130=Inew+M*b/R, where M is 30 or 35 as above. These are equations from instructions, not a claim about physical units or intended control theory. The ordinary-input middle bias is explicitly negative, rather than silently substituting a conventional symmetric cubic law. The lower and upper I clamp paths and no-clamp path all store +0x128 before adding the bias.

Output-consumer check: f_107fc6b0 unconditionally invokes f_107fc46c at 0x107fc6d0; its normal return at 0x107fc710-0x107fc734 multiplies integer member +8 by double +0x130 and converts that double to single with efscfd. This establishes +0x130 as the multiplicative rate output, but does not itself establish the units or upstream definition of e. It also prevents describing +0x130 simply as the integrator: the bounded I term is +0x128 and output includes a separate bias. No error/null-input branch is implied for this object method; zero R would reach division without a guard here.

hal_amps_hipower(...,1), software latch writes 1 on both normal and logged-failure paths.
hal_amps_hipower(...,0), software latch cleared on normal and logged-failure paths.
Mode setter stores +0xf4 and clears latch only for new mode !=2.
Raw conditional branch 0x40beffe4 returns nonzero +0xe2 immediately in mode 2.

todo: Residual: trace all callers of f_10d565c8 to name modes 0, 1 and 2 and establish their policy semantics. Do not map manager+0xf4 to the unrelated AMP_HI_RAIL/AMP_LO_RAIL/AMP_OFF string order without a call-path binding. The +0xe2 software power latch is now traced through on/off writers; it is not a pending preemptive target.
resolved_findings: Rail transition order proven (ampManager.cxx, ampMgr tag): ampPowerOnLocked runs power -> unmute -> high-power-rail in sequence, each a separate amp command with per-step failures (failed to power on/unmute amps, failed to transition to high power rail) and unsupported-command ignores (ignored unsupported amp command: power/mute/hipower); ampPowerOffLocked runs the reverse mute -> power off -> low-power-rail (failed to mute/power off amps, failed to transition to low power rail, requested amp power off). Preemptive turn-on is zone-scoped (zone %zu preemptive turn on %d -> 0 / %d -> %d set-reset pair). Off is deferred (scheduling off in %d sec) gated on the condition bitmap roff:%d canoff:%d ofx:%d nzvplay:%d pre:%d unm:%d. Amp commands route to the amp driver via per-command support checks; fault recovery retries unmute (failed to unmute amps to clear fault). State machine emits ampState %d -> %d + notifyAmpState; notify hooks {notifyPlayState, notifyPlayingUnmuteableSource_p/_np, notifyOutputFixed, notifyPreemptiveTurnOn, resetPreemptiveTurnOn} feed the state inputs.

Flag names recovered via the debug printf 'roff:%d canoff:%d ofx:%d nzvplay:%d pre:%d unm:%d' (0x10d5574c, amp domain): args bind roff=+0xf0, ofx=+0xe0, unm=+0xe1 (object bytes); canoff=r28, nzvplay=r30, pre=r27 are computed locals - +0xdd nonzero forces pre=1 (and r28=0), +0xdc gates the nzvplay computation off +0xd8. So the armed-check flag chain {+0xdc,+0xdd,+0xe1,+0xe2} reads {nzvplay-gate, pre-gate, unm, +0xe2} - the veto semantics are now named. Amp command vocabulary from the same region: {hipower, power, mute} dispatch arms, 'scheduling off in %d sec', 'requested amp power off', 'ampPowerOffLocked', 'ampState %d -> %d'/'notifyAmpState' transitions, kernel-side audiodev.ko controls {amp_power, amp-mute, tas5708_*, limelight hiz/pdn/reset}.

Correction from writer tracing: +0xe2 is a software power-on latch, not preemptive-turn-on armed state. The power-on path calls hal_amps_hipower(handle,1) at 0x10d55498 then stores 1 to +0xe2 at 0x10d554b4. The logged failure path also stores 1 at 0x10d555b4, so this byte does not prove hardware success. The power-off path calls hal_amps_hipower(handle,0) at 0x10d55aac and clears +0xe2 at 0x10d55ac8, including the logged failure path at 0x10d55bc8. Initialization at 0x10d56194 clears it and initializes +0xf4 to 2. f_10d565c8 compares and updates +0xf4, logs ampState, and at 0x10d56684 skips clearing +0xe2 only when the new mode equals 2. f_10d552a0 returns 1 unconditionally when +0xf4 differs from 2; in mode 2 it uses the input flags and latch. At 0x10d55304 raw word 0x40beffe4 is BO=5, BI=30, branching when the preceding +0xe2 comparison is NOT equal to zero; it returns the nonzero latch immediately, not when the latch is zero. Thus earlier descriptions of this function as a veto chain or a pending-target query were incorrect. The hardware event name table is not sufficient evidence to assign these policy modes rail-state names. +0xe1 is the unm input in the local decision diagnostic, not a proven target rail enum.

evidence.notes: LLA

resolved_findings: Resolved: LLA device interface = the link-local audio device node; latency computation = measured frame latency through the tx pipeline minus the configured compensation.

Device interface decoded (liblla_input + output side): LLA is the low-latency audio device layer over the TDM driver - devices are named lla_in_%s / lla_hdmi with open returning an fd (id:%d, status:%s, fd:%d), polled via lla.in.poll (Select returned but LLA fd not set), and read through a buffer-info/copy/release cycle (could not get buffer information, pTmpFrame buffer is NULL, Failed to copy buffer contents, Trying to copy more bytes than expected...maxbytes is %d, could not release buffer after read). Latency computation: the RX path reads rx time in ticks plus input delay (Failed to get rx time in ticks, Could not get input delay, Could not get input time and delay); the TX path sets tx latency (Setting tx latency %u - rc %d, could not set tx latency rc %d try %u got %u) and queries output limits + combined time/output delay. Frame validation rejects invalid frame size, unsupported input rate, and bad sample counts; decoder_pcm reports <DEC_SampleRate>. Status codes {WOULD_BLOCK, UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW, NO_CSB, INVALID_DATA, SUSPENDED}.

Resolved (latency formula, f_10d591c0 + f_10d59300): ticks-to-time conversion is identical in the input-delay and play-time paths - a u64 tick count (built as a 64-bit SPE pair via evmergehi, spe22d) is multiplied by the device tick-period double at object +0x30 (evldd +0x30), the product truncated to whole seconds via efdctsiz, the remainder (t*p - sec) multiplied by the double 1000000.0 (constant at 0x10eb4858) and truncated to integer microseconds: {sec,usec} = split(ticks * tickPeriod_s). The 'sample unit time ticks' getter f_10d59230 reads rx ticks then subtracts member +0x14 (64-bit subfc/subfe pair at 0x10d5927c/0x10d59284) - the input delay is a tick-domain subtraction from the device clock, then the same 1e6 split renders play/write times for the '%s %s current time %d.%06d play time %d.%06d write at %d.%06d' diagnostics and the play-time-in-the-past guards.

Resolved: the +0x30 tick-period double is the constant 1.0 (rodata 0x10eb9ee0) - seeded in the ctor at 0x10d58fcc and re-written by the +0x2c-arming setter at 0x10d58828 (evstdd, stores 1.0 whenever a nonzero arg arrives). So anacapad never computes a sample-rate-derived period; the LLA device reports ticks in seconds-scale units natively, or a real period is installed by a runtime path not visible here.

Failure logs drc config is invalid and returns zero. This is a native DRC-record check, not proof of universal Dolby parameter units.

The /drc parse path is bound by f_10d5ee28 loading /drc at 0x10d5ee54. The encompassing f_10d5f1e4 constructs /staticparams and parses frontangle/heightangle/surrangle/rearsurrangle via f_109d024c into stack+0x19c/+0x1a0/+0x1a8/+0x1ac at 0x10d5f9a4-0x10d5fb30. Constructor f_10d5d6f4 initializes the object, attempts the constructed JFFS app/debug/dsp/dolby_config.json path, then /opt/dsp/dolby_config.json, then the fallback block at 0x10d5d858. The assertion that every numeric min/max is enforced server-side is not established by the UI. configDSP.js onSubmitValues (lines 504-546) reads input.value strings, builds block-specific XML and posts it to ../putDSP without a numeric range check in that submission function. Those labels/defaults define editing vocabulary, not native acceptance. No blanket frequency/Q/gain bounds are inferred from the form defaults.

The native request/apply chain is now bound: HTTP handler f_100bb63c checks request/configuration state, reads a text/xml body with a 0x7d0 argument at 0x100bb76c-0x100bb784, checks HTTP result 200, then invokes f_102a5188 at 0x100bb794-0x100bb7a0. That wrapper loads owner+0x34, adds 0xe0 and tail-calls f_107fa080. The latter gathers processor interfaces through virtual slots +0x98/+0x9c, constructs a temporary aggregate with f_10d64ad4, and passes the supplied arguments to f_10d65c40 at 0x107fa158-0x107fa174. Its returned status is converted to a boolean at 0x107fa178-0x107fa180. The child parser/setters beneath this aggregate, not the web labels, determine acceptance.

At least one related native numeric validator is explicit: Dolby DRC f_10d60f0c compares two doubles against inclusive zero/one bounds and requires both zero in mode one. This disproves the stronger implication that only external preset values could reveal all bounds. It does not establish IIR frequency/Q/gain limits, nor does it make DRC bounds apply to every DSP block. Remaining work is the block-specific parser/setter census.

nodetx.summary: TX half of the inter-player audio transport: sends fixed 8-byte headers plus 1024-byte payloads, keeps packets for retransmission, and handles version-checked NACK requests. Header byte 5 carries two packed caller-supplied nibbles; the serializer does not identify peer-only frames.
todo: Established: byte 5 packs high=(r5&15), low=(r6&15); all four direct TX callers emit low=1 or 2; deserialize maps high to record+5 and low to record+6; the local NACK receive gate tests high==2. Withdrawn: low-always-zero, peer-only origin, class-echo directionality and universal class-1 resend exclusion. Still unresolved: the full high-nibble class vocabulary, the semantic distinction between low values 1 and 2, and the per-record u16 at +8 beyond its byte layout. Trace the producers of stored record+5/+8 and both field consumers downstream of the other f_106339d0 callers at 0x10309500/0x103095bc/0x1030f2b4/0x1044ca64; do not infer those roles from the serializer or NACK log alone.
resolved_findings: The control-frame names and resend counters identify the transport vocabulary, not a complete semantic decode of the two header nibbles. Exact packing, direct sender arguments and the NACK receive predicate are documented below; remaining class/subtype meanings stay in the todo.

Consolidated with the chsrc_chsnk bus decode: nodetx is the TX half of the node transport - the control-frame type names {boundaryX, schedResyncX, immedResync, schedResync, endTX, ITBTT_UNKNOWN} mark the frame classes that ride beside audio frames; reliability is NACK-based retransmit (nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u covering packet-id ranges; requestResync(%u); protocol-version reject on NACKs) with late-joiner support (resendToLateJoiner: starting send at %u). noderx is the mirror RX half carrying bookkeeping {pid, ob, lr, lcg, lrx, slrx} plus skip-ahead entries and the rx histogram taxonomy; the frame-identity triple {id, class, offset} is shared between them. ops_counters track the resend/nack/drop tallies feeding the stats debug line // %3u %d.%06d %u:%s.

The NACK path logs count/min/max packet-ID statistics, checks the version byte at wire+4 and rejects incompatible packets. Its payload is passed to f_10638090 for cached-packet lookup and resend. The stale-packet diagnostic and transmit-thread nice value are separate transport controls; they do not identify the low nibble of wire byte 5.

Wire layout from f_1063391c/f_106339d0: an 8-byte header followed by a copied 0x400-byte payload, for 0x408 bytes sent by the recovered callers. Header bytes 0..3 are big-endian record+0, byte 4 is record+4, byte 5 holds high nibble -> record+5 and low nibble -> record+6, and bytes 6..7 hold the big-endian u16 at record+8. Deserialization copies the payload to record+0xa only when its r6 flag is nonzero; it also saves r5 at record+0x40c. The NACK receive path uses r6=0, then explicitly copies the payload through f_10633a7c. Version helper f_106339c0 reads wire+4, not +5.

Serializer f_1063391c(r3=record,r4=wire,r5=high,r6=low) stores wire[5]=((r5<<4)|(r6&15))&255. Raw 0x54c6073e at 0x1063392c has SH=0,MB=28,ME=31 and keeps the low four bits without shifting. The complete direct-branch census finds four callers: 0x106365cc uses high=stored record+5, low=2; 0x106381e4 uses high=1, low=1; 0x10638274 and 0x10638400 use high=stored record+5, low=1. These produce low nibble 2 or 1, not zero. A nonzero low nibble therefore cannot establish peer-only origin, and no request/response class-echo interpretation follows from the packing.

Deserializer f_106339d0 extracts wire[5]>>4 into record+5 at 0x10633a24/0x10633a2c and wire[5]&15 into record+6 at 0x10633a28/0x10633a30. NACK dispatch at 0x106386a0 loads stack+0x435 from record base stack+0x430, compares that record+5 byte with 2, and reaches f_10638090 only on equality. Thus the verified NACK predicate tests the HIGH nibble, not the low nibble. The low-nibble purpose and full class vocabulary are not established by this local receive predicate.

Cached resend f_10638090 separates class 1 from other stored high-nibble values: the first scan continues only for record+5==1 (0x106381cc-0x106381d4), serializes (1,1), and notifies callback +8 with r4=2. The second scan skips record+5==1 (0x10638260-0x10638268), serializes (stored class,1), and notifies with r4=3. A separate lookup branch serializes (stored class,1) at 0x10638400. Therefore class 1 is not universally excluded from resend. These branches do not by themselves prove a source-level control/data enum name.

evidence.notes: Raw objdump audit: 0x54a52036 at 0x10633928 is a genuine left shift 4; 0x54c6073e at 0x1063392c has SH=0,MB=28,ME=31,Rc=0, a low-nibble mask. OR at 0x10633934 and stb at 0x10633970 truncate to byte 5. Direct branches across .text identify exactly these four serializer callers. Their preceding assignments are r5=record+5/r6=2 at 0x106365c0/0x106365c4, r5=1/r6=1 at 0x106381dc/0x106381d8, r5=record+5/r6=1 at 0x10638260/0x1063826c and 0x106383f4/0x106383f8. No intervening instruction overwrites those arguments. Full nonzero-low-nibble counterexamples disprove peer-only origin.

Raw 0x552ae13e at 0x10633a24 shifts byte 5 right 4 (SH=28,MB=4,ME=31); 0x5529073e at 0x10633a28 retains low four bits. Stores at 0x10633a2c/0x10633a30 bind record+5 to high and +6 to low. NACK receive constructs record at sp+0x430 (0x10638694), invokes parser with r6=0, and loads sp+0x435 at 0x106386a0; cmpwi 2 at 0x106386a4 and bne at 0x106386a8 reject all other high classes. Payload copy f_10633a7c at 0x106386b4 precedes f_10638090 at 0x106386cc. High-class-1 resend scan uses bne at 0x106381d4, while the second scan uses beq at 0x10638268; the old blanket exclusion claim was false.

Serializer tail sets source record+0xa, destination wire+8 and length 0x400 at 0x106339a4-0x106339b8; resend send site 0x10638214 supplies length 0x408. Deserializer condition at 0x106339d8 controls memcpy at 0x10633a48-0x10633a54 and stores its r5 at record+0x40c at 0x10633a58. Header version is copied at 0x10633a18/0x10633a1c and read by helper at 0x106339c4. Direct parser branches also occur at 0x10309500/0x103095bc/0x1030f2b4/0x1044ca64: their semantic field contracts are not inferred from local nodetx handling.

Role split proven: anacapad does not drive the radio - netstartd owns wifi/satellite radio config (anacapad sends IPC to /tmp/netstartd.ipc: Failed to send IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition; wpa_supplicant is a separate daemon - wpa_supplicant.log/netstartd.log ship in diag bundles). What anacapad owns is the HT satellite topology layer: AddHTSatellite clears local sonar config on the SOURCE, applies satellite config overrides (Satellite config override: From: %s To: %s), pushes satellite state to the member (Push satellite state to UUID %s failed), and reports Add HT Sat. New map: %s before Start topology monitor; RemoveHTSatellite clears RoomCalibration on satellites and logs HT Sat %s removal (%u) via %s took %ld ms on %s with guards {secondary device %s not found, incompatible secondary device %s, RemoveHTSat: error %d sending to Sat %s}; reconnectHTSatellites runs the recovery FSM {reconnected Sat %s, Failed to reconnect with %s: %d, removing Sat %s, retry in 10 secs as topology hasnt settled yet, separating from HT primary %s} over map vocab {master, oldmap, failmap, recoverSat, recovery, satellite}. The assoc_tracker/idle_mgr/netif_poll sub-blocks are the local wifi-state feeds into this topology layer.

Resolved: the entire radio bring-up is /usr/sbin/netconfig.sh (invoked by netstartd). Mode verbs {sonosnet,station,satellite,sta_and_sat,open,credcheck,deauth,wacexit,island,up} + WAC wrappers {wacstart,wacapclose,wactimeout,waccredcheck,wacapopen,wacstation} mapping onto the base modes; arg2 = stp_disable|stp_enable. Reads /jffs/netsettings.txt keys {WEPKey,HouseholdID,Channel,PriorityBridge,BonjourName,PrimaryUUID,ForceMeshDisable} via keyval; credcheck substitutes /ramdisk/tmp/netsettings_check.txt. UseSSIDList from /jffs/net/settings/ssidlist.txt (recovery swaps in /var/run/softapssidlist.txt). open mode: ath0 = 10.69.69.1 on channel PARAM2 (default 2412MHz, /jffs/debug/openchannel override) after setmac -L. island = sonosnet mesh without eth. deauth = empty br0 with setmac -S. satellite/sta_and_sat build /var/run/htapsatwpa.conf {ssid,psk,scan_ssid=1,priority=4,bssid?} so the HT satellite STA-joins the primary's hidden AP; sta_and_sat appends the block to the running wpa conf. PrimaryUUID in netsettings => ISHTSATELLITE (athconfig setprimaryuuid+satenable). IS_HT_WIRELESS_PRIMARY arch attr in sonosnet|station mode turns ath1 into the HT AP (setuuid RINCON_<eth0mac>0<Port>, acs, acslmenable, wepkey, hhid). ForceMeshDisable => athconfig blockadvertisedpath 1. PriorityBridge=1 => brctl setbridgeprio 0x7000 else 0x9800; arg2 stp_disable turns STP off. Hostname = BonjourName else IS_BRIDGE?SonosZB:SonosZP. udhcpc is launched -f [-F -W 20 when island] -z (station/satellite/sta_and_sat) -s /etc/dhcp.script -i br0 -w ath0 -h <host> -d access.bestbuy.com; /jffs/debug/static_ipaddr bypasses DHCP; waits up to 60s for /tmp/udhcpc.pid; /jffs/debug/{testpoints.sh,wpa_supplicant.conf,wpa_supplicant,supplicant} debug hooks gated on /proc/sonos-lock/exec_enable.

Deepened (netstartd is shipped at wifi/netstartd): its WAC-mode event dispatcher is a 41-entry jump table at 0x10031770 (dispatch fn ~f_1000fce4, cmplwi bound 0x28). Opcode 0x28 shares the arm at 0x1000fd2c with 0x27 - a WAC stop/error event: it checks state flags globals+0x10/+0x2c; if in WAC-timeout it logs 'Ignore WAC Mode stop or error event while in WAC timeout'; if in station mode it logs 'Ignore WAC Mode stop or error event while in station mode'; otherwise in active WAC mode it runs the teardown pair f_1000d774(callback) + f_1000e3f4(state=1) then returns. Sibling arms in the same FSM: 'WAC Mode Credentials have been set', 'WAC provided credentials are bad, restart wacd' (also flushes + restarts), 'ASSERT: Open AP not up after WAC cred check, starting', 'Unexpected event %s in WAC Open state', and WifiFuncsSetStationEnabled/WifiFuncsGetOpenMode on 'ath0'.

Resolved (satellite-add channel): in netstartd's main IPC dispatch (jump table @0x1002f6f4, handler f_1000886c) msg id 0x28=40 maps to the DEFAULT arm 0x10008990 - ignored on /tmp/netstartd.ipc. netstartd opens a second socket /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc ('Failed to init WAC IPC'), so the anacapad satellite-add opcode 0x28 rides the WAC IPC channel whose event FSM jump table (@0x10031770) contains the decoded 0x28 arm shared with 0x27.

Netmode enum at 0x10f99f80 {NETMODE_SONOSNET_WIRED=1, SONOSNET_WIRELESS=2, WIRED=3, WIRED_NO_WIFI=4, STATION=5, SATELLITE_V1=6, ...} plus wifi-mode {SONOSNET,STATION,DISCONNECTED,STATION_SATELLITE}=1..4 at 0x10f9a0a4 and the wifi-enable FSM at 0x10fadd94 {INACTIVE=1, WIFI_ENABLING=2, ACK_AWAIT=3, WIFI_DISABLING=4, WIFI_DISABLED=5, ACK_NOT_RECEIVED=6}.

Resolved (satellite-add payload): the send site writes only the 4-byte opcode word 0x28 on /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc - there is no payload body; the notification is opcode-only and netstartd's WAC FSM treats 0x28 as a bare signal (shared arm with 0x27).

cert_layer.layout: On-disk cert store layout proven from f_106b268c (path builder): path = constructJFFSRootPath(buf, mgr, mgr->+0x10a4) + [/ + env] + / + file. mgr->+0x10a4 is the per-identity subdirectory, a ctor arg of f_106b20bc (the certManager store object, vtable 0x10f05130) - the only construction site found passes r4='regdevicecert' from f_105a7034, which f_10645bc8 supplies for the registration-device-cert manager (strings regcert/regdevicecert, callback f_106455e4). env is the deployment environment name resolved via f_10556e10 settings-table entry 0x25 with fallback 'prod' - certs are namespaced per environment so a staging device never loads production certs. Filename thunks: cert.xml via flag=0 (env-qualified), metadata.txt via flag=1 (unqualified) and a second metadata.txt via flag=0 (env-qualified). constructJFFSRootPath is a PLT import so the literal root prefix lives outside anacapad.
cert_layer.files_detail: cert.xml: device/client certificate+key store, loaded at startup ('loading %s (0x%x) took %ums', 0x%x byte size), bounds-checked ('Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate'), replaced atomically via tmpfile+rename on download ('failed to rename tmpfile', 'failed to load replacement (0x%x)'). metadata.txt: persisted cert download metadata (the DeviceCertInfo requestTimeMS/downloadStatusCode/httpResultCode/previousETag/reason fields) written after each fetch attempt. Root-of-trust chain: server/peer TLS certs are validated by the certval layer ('cert validation for %s (local port %u)', certvalStats) against bundles fetched from /certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb with ETag caching and failure backoff; client-auth uses cert.xml through the KEYCERT identity slots (R_CLIENT_KEYCERT_ID_SONOS, _SONOS_DEVICE, _SONOS_DEVICE_ACCEPT_LEGACY, _SONOS_REGISTERED_DEVICE). /regcert serves DeviceCertInfo XML, /root_cert_bundles serves the installed bundle set.

Peer TXT parser0x106beae8 enumerates keys via TXTRecordGetItemAtIndex; vers must be>=3, bootseq must parse/present, hhid/location/UUID must be nonempty and mdnssequence conversion must succeed. Missing UUID can be recovered by extracting RINCON_ up to slash from location. bootseq uses strtoul base10; sslport/hhsslport use strtol then low16 mask; sequence uses paranoid_atoi then low16 retention. This exception is local-player identity, not a generic trusted-device or cross-household permission flag. New bye-bye reason is stored at peer+0x44 and suppresses regular topology announce in that callback; the next callback without a bye-bye reason clears it. Incoming sequence is logged beside old peer+0x5c then assigned to+0x5c at0x106bf244. There is NO old<new or equality gate on this sequence. The key ladder parses named attributes; it is not an exemption policy controlling local counter bumps.

The earlier sequence monotonic-check, key-exclusion bump policy and MDP-field-change bump attribution are disproved by the actual producer/controller/parser instructions. Device-advertisement details and remaining upstream counter-caller work are maintained in mdns_device.

datatap.todo: Established: compressed snapshots contain forty-eight-byte little-endian packet headers followed by count*8 audio bytes; f_10343228 evicts a header and its associated audio, not a fixed file head/trailer. Unknown: timestamp units/clock domain and the semantic meanings of the 24 cached status bytes, consistently with audio_tap/audio_taps. Next: resolve the provider at owner+0x8d0 and its virtual slot +0xc called at 0x107d8754, following the returned eight-byte pair to metadata; enumerate writers/readers of the processor+0x1a68 block copied by f_107dede8 into metadata+0x0f and join each byte to its actual consumer.
resolved_findings: Snapshot and export boundaries corrected consistently with audio_tap/audio_taps. Snapshot f_10343368 reads the ring at owner+0x98 in chunks capped at 0x1000 (0x103433cc-0x103433dc), writes each chunk through f_103d16e0, consumes it only after a successful write via f_1053ed84, and counts consumed bytes (0x103433ec-0x1034342c). Write failure logs Datatap snapshot failed after the successfully written byte count and stops; an empty ring takes the finish path without emitting a data chunk. Compression setup f_103d1ca8 receives flags 0x241 and the staged filename, so raw ring bytes and the exported file must not be conflated.

The XML path f_1034308c emits <SPDIFTap>, opens the staged snapshot, constructs a generic file reader with buffer size 0x4000 at 0x103430fc-0x10343114, sets a ten-second read deadline, and streams file bytes through sonosBase64EncUpdate/Finalize. It then closes and unlinks the staged file before emitting </SPDIFTap> (0x10343160-0x103431a4). Open failure skips the streaming loop and still emits the closing tag. The 0x4000 is reader buffering, not an on-disk metadata head, and base64 wraps the snapshot file, not an assumed uncompressed PCM structure.

The forty-eight-byte item is a per-packet HEADER, not a big-endian EOF trailer. Space-making routine f_10343228 compares requested bytes with ring free space, rejects requests larger than capacity, then repeatedly reads 0x30 metadata bytes through f_10342f78 (0x103432e8-0x103432f8), decodes the little-endian u16 at metadata+9 and discards count*8 audio bytes (0x10343300-0x10343324). A short metadata read logs Error: failed to read metadata from buffer and fails. A zero count still consumes the header and continues. This matches audio_tap/audio_taps framing rather than the earlier {0x4000 head, PCM, 0x30 BE trailer} assertion.

Shared semantic provenance retained precisely: native producer f_107d8624 initializes version 1 in forty-eight bytes, obtains the eight-byte timestamp pair from clock-provider virtual +0xc, stores sample count and sample rate, and copies 24 cached status bytes from processor+0x1a68 through f_107dede8. Reader f_107e1264 reverses the scalar fields and handles metadata+0x27 bit 0x80 as signal loss; its fields agree with the ring eviction count. The reader/producer linkage resolves format and sample rate, but not clock units/domain or every cached status-byte meaning. Those are the same genuine semantic residuals retained in both audio tap records.

The clock provenance is an indirect call, not a unit conversion inferred from packet framing: 0x107d8738 loads owner+0x8d0, 0x107d874c selects virtual +0xc and 0x107d8754 invokes it with stack output storage. Subsequent byte copies preserve the returned pair. f_107dede8 requires a destination capacity greater than 23 before copying the cached block; neither copy names the provider clock domain or status semantics.

evidence.notes: Snapshot drains at most 4096 bytes per iteration, consuming only successful writes.
16384-byte argument is file-reader buffering, not a metadata head.
Ring eviction reads a 48-byte packet header before count*8 audio; not EOF trailer.
e500 scalar decode obtains little-endian sample count at packet metadata+9.
Indirect provider +0xc returns the timestamp pair; copying its output does not identify units/domain.
Capacity must exceed 23 for the cached 24-byte status copy; follow processor+0x1a68 writers/readers for meanings.

file_commit.description: f_1011ad40 creates a .tmp path and opens it using f_1054f088. That helper always uses fopen64(path,"w"); its third argument is not consumed. If full cache serialization f_10119b90 succeeds, the installer renames the temporary file while its writer is still open, updates the in-memory version/source and sid/version index, then destroys the writer. If serialization fails, it destroys the first writer, reopens the same path in write mode and attempts a fallback JSON object containing only version=current+1 and lastUpdateDevice. A successful fallback write and rename still increment the version, update the supplied-row index and return true. Thus save success need not mean that the manifests array reached disk. Fallback rename failure unlinks the candidate. Primary rename failure returns false without the same explicit unlink branch. The writer destructor f_1054f15c delegates to f_1054f0e8 when open. That routine calls fflush, fileno, fsync and fclose, ignores fflush/fsync results and returns a boolean derived only from fclose. f_1011ad40 does not test that close result. On the full serialization path rename and metadata/index updates precede destruction; on the fallback success path rename precedes destruction and metadata/index updates follow it. These are static call-order facts, not a runtime durability test.

Serializer false closes and reopens; fallback emits only version/source, renames at 0x1011af80 and joins metadata commit.
fopen64 uses constant w; input third argument is ignored.
fflush and fsync results ignored; fclose controls helper boolean; caller ignores destructor result.

Object-completion checker f_109c3070 tests bit 0 there and requires a seen/default marker from descriptor+0x21 &9. f_109c311c returns internal parser error 8 when a required field is absent. Thus an otherwise completed manifest object with no schemaVersion is rejected through this required-field path. Other named manifest fields are bound without this required flag. This establishes required presence separately from the schema callback version-pair check. A non-string/null/malformed schema value must also pass its token-type and schema callback paths; required presence alone does not prove validity. f_1023a214 binds presentationMap and strings through nested object definitions, whose URI uses a dynamic string binding limited by descriptor capacity 0x400 and whose version targets a 32-bit word. Endpoint object binding f_1023a13c uses a custom enum converter for type and the same 0x400 dynamic-string URI binding. apiKey.zp also uses that 0x400 string binding. Advertising headers binds type 6 directly to model+0xec as a byte boolean. The schemaVersion fixed buffer has capacity 17; f_109c1314 marks its descriptor flags with bit 1 (0x2) when the decoded copy length is >=capacity. Dynamic-string limit handling f_109c39bc also marks bit 1 when capacity is exceeded. Binding capacities and per-field truncation flags are proven; aggregate acceptance of oversized values still needs tracing through the enclosing parser and callback checks. The 12-byte JSON schema-definition entries contain name pointer, parent field index and token-kind tag. f_109c20f4 filters by the second word before exact strcmp name matching; the word is not a required-field boolean. Nested manifest entries 0..9 are: anonymous root object; schemaVersion; presentationMap; strings; endpoints array; anonymous endpoint object whose parent index is 4; apiKey; accountTiers array; anonymous tier string whose parent index is 7; advertising. Required policy lives separately in the runtime binding flags. Generic object/array starts f_109c29c4/f_109c2a64 reject a push when the incremented nesting count exceeds 15, setting internal parser status 1. That is a shared parser limit, distinct from endpoint/tier storage capacities.

evidence.notes: Manifest binder through 0x1023a53c. Raw 0x39000001 at 0x1023a21c sets schema flags=1; 0x38c00011 at 0x1023a224 sets fixed capacity=17. Other named fields use flags zero.
Generic field constructor stores source/destination, 16-bit capacity, array-count bytes, type tag and flags; flags argument r8 stored at +0x20.
Required-field scan tests descriptor+0x20 &1 and +0x21 &9. Missing field returns its descriptor; f_109c311c converts non-null result to parser error 8 at 0x109c3164.
Dynamic string append/capacity handling, including truncation/status branches; custom converter return3 sets flags0x5 at 0x109c3c4c.

json_collections.description: Endpoint collector f_10238144 handles object-end callback token kind 1 for field metadata index zero. With its target model installed, it copies the completed scratch endpoint to the next 0x1c-byte slot while count<=2, increments model+0xa0, and clears the scratch endpoint type/URI afterward. At count>2 it returns zero without appending or incrementing; the collector itself supplies no overflow error. This yields at most three stored endpoints even if further object callbacks arrive. accountTiers instead uses a generic array binding: f_1023a214 binds the count at model+0xe8 with maximum four and binds model+0xd8 as four 4-byte custom enum values. The generic array completion stores the smaller of parsed element count and the declared maximum. Exact overall acceptance and side effects for extra elements or repeated arrays still require the shared element cursor/error paths. Endpoint converter f_10238370 and account-tier converter f_10238250 clear their output enum word to zero, decode the JSON string into a 33-byte scratch buffer and require decoded length<=32. Longer text returns internal conversion code 16. They match a vocabulary entry only when length matches and memcmp matches all bytes, so names are case-sensitive. Unknown text returns internal conversion code 3 with output still zero. The generic custom-string binding f_109c1314 translates code 3 into descriptor status bits 0x5 (seen plus invalid-conversion bit 0x4), and code 16 into bits 0x3 (seen plus length/error bit 0x2), then returns the converter buffer. These conversion codes do not by themselves prove whole-document rejection; trace enclosing status aggregation before treating unknown enum strings as a download failure. Emitters separately omit unnamed enum zero.

evidence.notes: Endpoint object-end collector. Raw unsigned compare 0x2b890002 at 0x102381b4 and branch 0x41bdffc0 at 0x102381b8 bypass append when count>2; count increments before copy, scratch resets after admitted copy.
Raw 0x38e00004 declares accountTiers count max four; element binding at 0x1023a44c/0x1023a454 sets four elements with stride four.
Generic array-end updates bound count with min(element count, descriptor+0x1b), using unsigned compare and isel at 0x109c2588..0x109c2594.

Tier converter clears output, decodes with buffer size33, unsigned length<=32 guard and exact length/memcmp table search; unknown returns3, long returns16. Endpoint converter f_10238370 follows the same pattern.
Custom enum conversion codes map to descriptor seen/invalid/length status bits at 0x109c1430..0x109c1498. Fixed character copy flags bit0x2 for decoded length>=capacity at 0x109c13cc..0x109c13ec.

stream_parser.description: Download JSON reader f_1011aabc creates a fresh model, schema adapter and streaming parser, binds through f_1011bd2c, then requests chunks of up to 1024 bytes from input slot +8 using the supplied deadline. It feeds the reported byte count to f_109c4b34 without branching on that read call return register. Internal result 10 continues only while the last reported byte count is nonzero; a zero-length read with result 10 falls into the logged failure path. Parser result zero reaches root descriptor status checks: when the root has a seen/default marker, status bit 0x2 produces local internal error 7. Only after these checks does it postprocess a nonempty apiKey.zp and copy the scratch model to the caller with f_102399a4. Parse failure returns false without this final model copy. JSON framework error numbers here are not SOAP fault codes; the outer download worker maps this false result to 801. The manifest schema callback result 16 is mapped through f_109bf390 to shared parser result 12 because it exceeds the mapped-result range 0..15. The callback therefore has a different code domain from the parse result logged by f_1011aabc. Missing-required-field error 8 is set directly by f_109c311c. Both still reach outer download failure 801. Internal enum converter codes 3/16 are consumed by descriptor status-bit logic and must not be substituted for either callback or outer download result.

evidence.notes: Fresh model/binder construction; 1024-byte read/feed loop, status10/zero-length termination, root bit0x2 check, API-key extraction and final model copy only on accepted parse.

json_acceptance.description: The shared value path accepts some quoted representations in addition to native JSON tokens. For schema kind 3 (boolean), f_109c3c58 decodes the string and uses strcasecmp against true/false, writes the boolean through f_109c1288 and invokes the processor callback. Thus advertising.headers accepts quoted case variants such as "TRUE" and "False" in this path; other quoted text sets shared parser error 9. For schema kind 2 (numeric), the same string handler calls paranoid_atod and then f_109c1034; failed conversion sets error 9. Resource version fields therefore have a quoted-number conversion path. Exact floating-point-to-integer range, rounding and overflow behavior is not established by that call alone. Null handler f_109c2e64 resolves the field through f_109c2658, then for known schema kinds 0 (string) or 6 dispatches callback token kind 5 without marking the bound field seen. It does not call the string-value/schema-version callback path or write a boolean/numeric value. The manifest schema callback f_10118580 ignores tokens other than kind 3. For schemaVersion, a null therefore fails the required-field check at completed object close with internal parser error 8. The field reset happens before null processing, so a prior valid schemaVersion followed by a duplicate null does not retain the prior value/seen marker. Optional fields have separate reset/default effects according to their binding type; null is not a universal whole-document rejection. Field resolution f_109c2658 calls f_109c1514 for a recognized occurrence before assigning its value. That reset clears descriptor status +0x21 and resets the target by binding type: fixed strings and byte booleans start with zero, numeric words and array counts start with zero, dynamic strings are cleared, and custom converters receive their reset slot. Object bindings clear their member bindings through the installed adapter reset method. No duplicate-name rejection precedes this reset. Consequently repeated valid scalar members overwrite earlier values; repeated resource objects reset their nested URI/version members before processing the later object. A later invalid occurrence can still fail immediately or leave an invalid flag, so this is not a promise that every duplicate-bearing document succeeds. Unknown field names produce index -1 after parent/name lookup; in the manifest bindings, the unknown-field callback flag 0x8 is not enabled. Unmatched scalar fields take the no-assignment path. Unknown nested-object/array state and all type-mismatch combinations remain separate audit items. The endpoints array field itself has no count-target binding in f_1023a214; its anonymous object entry uses the collector target. Each completed endpoint object appends against model+0xa0, which is initialized by the fresh manifest model and incremented by f_10238144. Resolving a repeated endpoints array does not reset that model count through the array-count machinery. The collector therefore accumulates admitted object rows across repeated endpoints members up to the same three-row maximum. Other array bindings such as accountTiers explicitly bind and reset a count, so this collector behavior must not be generalized to all arrays.

evidence.notes: String-to-boolean path: decoded scratch string, strcasecmp(true/false), f_109c1288 byte assignment and callback; failed comparison enters shared error9. Quoted numeric path at 0x109c3f5c calls paranoid_atod then f_109c1034.

Null path calls field resolver/reset, emits kind5 callback for known string/null schema kinds and does not mark the string descriptor seen. Manifest schema callback at 0x101185a4 only processes kind3.
Resolver invokes f_109c1514 per recognized occurrence. Reset dispatch table 0x10f93ac4 maps fixed-string/boolean reset to 0x109c15c4, numeric/count to 0x109c15dc and dynamic-string to 0x109c164c.
Parent-index/name lookup returns -1 when unmatched; f_109c2658 preserves the unmatched state, and scalar paths skip assignment unless unknown callback flag0x8 is enabled.

No count binding installed for field4 endpoints; field5 binds reusable endpoint object and collector model/count target. Field7 accountTiers separately installs a count target. Collector at 0x10238144 owns model+0xa0 increment.
