cache_load.description: Cache-file binder f_10119fe8 requires root version (numeric target at parser+0x1304) and lastUpdateDevice (fixed character buffer at +0x12e8, capacity 25). It leaves the manifests array optional. Row binder f_10119ec8 requires sid and version numeric fields and uri as a fixed buffer of capacity 1025; the nested manifest object binding has no required flag, although schemaVersion is required when that object is parsed. Required presence is checked separately from empty-text validity and numeric conversion. The row version is parsed into a 32-bit word at row+4, but saved through the halfword at row+6; round-trip emission therefore keeps only its low 16 bits. A syntactically valid header-only object containing version and lastUpdateDevice can pass cache parsing because manifests is optional. f_1011991c returns success when f_1011987c reports zero; the latter checks top-level binding status bit 0x2 but does not require an array. f_1011a4bc then copies source/version and rebuilds the public SID/version index from the supplied row table. If the caller supplied a fresh zero-row table, as the download worker does after f_101191c8 at 0x1011b7c4, the index is empty until later upserts. Parsing a header-only object does not itself clear an arbitrary already-populated supplied table. This closes the missing-array grammar question for the save fallback; it does not establish complete cache freshness/reconciliation behavior. Cache-file parsing mutates the supplied row table as each row object closes. Callback f_10119568 checks token kind 1 and field index 4, then f_101194cc calls f_10119434 directly on the supplied table and discards its boolean result before resetting scratch row data. Therefore a new SID beyond 34 stored rows can be silently skipped while the file parse succeeds; existing SIDs can still replace rows at capacity. Duplicate SIDs resolve through replacement in arrival order for admitted rows. A later syntax/required-field failure does not roll back earlier inserted/replaced rows. f_1011a4bc updates stored source/version/index only after overall parse success, but its caller-supplied table may already contain a parsed prefix after failure. The download worker warns on load failure and proceeds with this table to insert the newly downloaded row and save. Whole-file acceptance, complete row retention and unchanged output on failure are three different properties here. Cache wrapper f_1011987c scans its five top-level runtime field descriptors after parser result zero. A descriptor with a seen/default marker and bit 0x2 yields internal error 7. It does not recursively scan every nested field status there. The streaming downloaded-manifest wrapper f_1011aabc instead checks its outer root descriptor. Conversion status bits in deeper bindings therefore require a concrete propagation trace; a converter result or a status bit alone must not be promoted to a whole-file rejection claim.

evidence.notes: Root required flags: version r5=1 at 0x1011a12c through helper f_1011bc84; lastUpdateDevice r8=1 at 0x1011a148 and capacity25 at 0x1011a150. Array field3 has no required binding.
Row sid/version flags1 at 0x10119efc/0x10119f3c; uri flags1 at 0x10119f54 and capacity1025 at 0x10119f68. Nested manifest flags0 at 0x10119f9c.
Zero parser result triggers five-descriptor status scan. f_1011991c treats zero as success without a separate manifests-presence check. Load metadata/index update at 0x1011a5a4..0x1011a5c4.
On row object end kind1 and index4, calls f_101194cc. Upsert result at 0x101194f8 is discarded while the scratch row is reset; callback returns0 at 0x1011959c.

Download worker uses the table initialized at 0x1011b7c4, warns on load failure, rejoins row insertion/save. File-loader metadata commits only after total success; no table rollback appears in f_1011991c or f_1011a4bc.

runtime_view.description: The runtime manifest view used by f_1011c34c is a separate object from a persisted cache row. Constructor f_1011c034 places a 1025-byte base-URI buffer at +0, the parsed manifest model at +0x404, valid byte at +0x4f4 and service ID word at +0x4f8; it starts invalid with an empty base. Catalog constructor f_1011c078 looks up a descriptor through catalog slot +0x20 and requires descriptor capability 0x400000. It expands descriptor SecureUri from descriptor+0x20 into the view base, not the descriptor Manifest URI. It then retrieves the manifest row by service ID through f_100c6b10 -> f_1011a650, copies row+0x40c model to view+0x404 and marks the view valid only on successful lookup. Failed construction leaves the initialized view invalid. Other constructors f_1011c19c/f_1011c1ec can construct a valid view directly from a model; the former leaves the base empty, while the latter expands a supplied descriptor SecureUri. Runtime resource readers use the same view validity byte. f_1011c570/f_1011c618 expose strings only when the stored signed 32-bit version is >0 and the URI first byte is nonzero; f_1011c6bc/f_1011c70c apply the same tests to presentationMap. Getter callbacks copy URI text with f_10906304 and store the version through a halfword output, so these getters expose low 16 bits even though the presence gate checks the full signed word. f_1011c5c0 reports valid view plus nonzero account-tier count. f_1011c5f0 returns advertising.headers only for a valid view. API-key getter f_1011c7e4 requires nonnull destination and nonzero capacity, clears destination first, and copies a nonempty stored key only for a valid view; it ignores the copy helper return. These accessors establish availability and output projection, not the downstream network or entitlement effects.

evidence.notes: Runtime view layout: f_10239628 at +0x404, base first byte and valid +0x4f4 cleared, serviceId +0x4f8 initialized. Constructors through f_1011c24c.

Descriptor slot+0x20 lookup, raw 0x752a0040 at 0x1011c13c tests cap0x400000. SecureUri expansion uses stack descriptor+0x20 at 0x1011c14c; row lookup via f_100c6b10 at 0x1011c168; row+0x40c copy and valid set at 0x1011c180..0x1011c190.

Strings presence/getter and presentation-map equivalents through 0x1011c7ac. Raw signed cmpwi 0x2f890000 and NOT-GT branches at 0x1011c584/0x1011c588 and 0x1011c734/0x1011c738 reject version<=0; getter halfword stores at 0x1011c69c/0x1011c790.
Account-tier count, advertising flag and API-key presence/read helpers through 0x1011c860; key reader clears output before validity/key tests.

endpoint_resolution.description: Endpoint resolver f_1011c34c takes (view, endpointType, destination, capacity). It returns false for an invalid view, requested type zero, zero stored endpoint count or no matching row. It scans all stored endpoint rows in order and compares type exactly. If destination is null or capacity is zero, it skips URL writing but still returns true when a matching type is present, even if that row URI is empty. With output enabled it processes every matching row rather than returning at the first; later matches overwrite earlier output unless an earlier relative-join failure has already returned false. No-match/invalid exits do not clear the destination. A true result therefore establishes neither a nonempty URL nor lossless output. For a matching URI whose first byte is slash and a nonempty view base, the resolver copies the entire base with strlcpy and requires capacity>returned source length. It removes exactly one trailing slash from the copied base, then appends the endpoint URI verbatim with strlcat and again requires capacity>attempted length. This joins strings against descriptor SecureUri; it does not resolve a leading slash against just the URI origin or discard an existing base path. For example, base https://host/service and endpoint /report produce https://host/service/report/ after the final slash step. It then appends a trailing slash if the resulting nonempty output lacks one. A leading-slash endpoint with an empty base takes the direct-copy path instead. Non-leading-slash URIs are copied directly without scheme or absolute-URI validation by this resolver. The relative base-copy and endpoint-append length failures return false after possibly writing a truncated or partial destination. In contrast, the direct strlcpy return is ignored. Its output can be truncated and still reach success. The final trailing-slash strlcat result is checked only to decide whether to emit the Added trailing slash diagnostic: capacity>attempted length logs, while insufficient room still continues with success. Empty copied output skips slash insertion and also continues with success. Thus complete relative joining, direct copying and final slash insertion have different success criteria. The resolver makes no network request.

evidence.notes: Validity/type/count gates, ordered scan and output mode. Raw isel 0x7d004f9e at 0x1011c398 selects write=false when destination==0; zero capacity goes to the same mode at 0x1011c520.
Leading slash plus nonempty base selects concatenation. Base trailing-slash removal is raw stbx 0x7edc49ae at 0x1011c55c; it is not an isel. Whole base text is used, not parsed URI authority.

Direct strlcpy result ignored. Final-slash check 0x419d00b8 at 0x1011c470 branches on unsigned capacity>attempted length only for logging. Relative-copy 0x409d003c at 0x1011c4a0 and append 0x419dff64 at 0x1011c4d8 use actual failure/continue gates.

endpoint_callers.description: The direct caller at 0x104c9ccc requests endpoint type 2, binding this resolver to the reporting vocabulary entry. Its enclosing f_104c9bd8 constructs the runtime view and first requires its separate provider gate f_104c9acc to succeed. After the resolver call it destroys the view and returns the original destination pointer from r30, without testing or returning the resolver boolean. If the gate fails it returns null. Therefore a nonnull result from this wrapper is not proof that a reporting endpoint was found or fitted; caller buffer initialization and subsequent request construction still need tracing. Playback-side caller 0x102c4588 uses endpoint-selection wrapper f_1011caec with a 1025-byte destination, then f_1011c864 constructs the subsequent URL. Failure of the latter sets local result 0x320 (800) at 0x102c45c0. f_1011c864 parses the item identifier/URI, combines a base with derived path using %s%s/, and requires cloud-queue version helper f_10338a34 to return nonzero. The selector branches, component bounds, percent encoding and version gates are documented in svc_manifest.details.playback_uri_selection and version_strings. Complete identifier classification/decoding and request/error propagation still require tracing; this caller link does not establish a complete cloud-queue request contract. Reporting gate f_104c9acc first invokes provider slot +0x1c; a nonnull pointer with nonzero first byte immediately returns true. Otherwise an empty item URI returns false; a nonempty URI must pass f_101477e4 and service-ID extraction f_1071aeb0, after which it constructs a manifest view and queries endpoint type 2 through f_1011c29c. That presence helper compares stored type values without requiring nonempty URI or an output buffer. Consequently this gate is not a universal endpoint-URL validity check. The exact provider-slot string meaning and the full URI predicate/extraction grammar remain to be traced.

Playback caller chain: endpoint selection -> f_1011c864 -> local failure800 at 0x102c45c0; destination capacities1025. URL/version helper call at 0x1011c9b4.

playback_uri_selection.description: Playback endpoint selector f_1011caec selects radio enum 1 for the literal case-sensitive x-sonosapi-radio: prefix through f_10147928 -> f_101478ec; the broader f_101477e4 predicate also recognizes that prefix. For a non-radio URI, f_10148478 requires x-rincon-cpcontainer:, parses its identifier through f_1071b3dc/f_1071d5c4 and returns true only when the parsed kind word equals 0x13. That case selects endpoint enum 3 (audiobook). Other inputs select zero, which f_1011c34c rejects. This wrapper does not choose browse enum 4 merely because an input is a container or another music-service URI. The parser/identifier-kind internals and alternate callers remain separate work. CQ URL builder f_1011c864 takes endpoint base, item URI, destination and capacity. The cpcontainer path branch copies at most 256 bytes of the URI path, terminates it, passes identifier classification/validation through f_1071b3dc/f_1071b458 and canonicalizes it with f_1071d5c4/f_1071b5a0 into another 257-byte buffer. The other branch extracts/percent-decodes item path text through f_1071ac00, which recognizes x-sonos prefixes or x-rincon-cpcontainer and requires a nonempty parsed path. For x-sonos-http and x-sonosprog-http that helper strips the final dot/extension before decoding. The builder then percent-encodes the selected item text into a 257-byte scratch buffer with f_10c3a294, appends endpoint base + encoded text + slash using snprintf, and validates the resulting URL version with f_10338a34. Component truncation and formatter return values are ignored here; success is not a lossless-construction guarantee. Full identifier classification and decoder error/embedded-null behavior remain open. Percent-encoder wrapper f_10c3a294 passes the literal allow-list $-_.!*'(), to f_10c3a0f4. That helper copies isalnum bytes or allow-listed bytes and encodes every other byte through format %%%02x, using lowercase hexadecimal. Slash, colon, percent, query and fragment punctuation are therefore encoded unless already removed by earlier item parsing. A raw copied byte needs room for itself plus a terminator; an escape needs room for three bytes plus a terminator. If capacity cannot fit the next unit it stops, null-terminates and returns the number of bytes written, without a separate truncation error. f_1011c864 ignores that returned count. This encoder does not normalize already encoded percent sequences; a percent byte is encoded again.

x-rincon-cpcontainer prefix and identifier parse; xori0x13/cntlzw boolean at 0x101484f8..0x10148504. Radio literal comparison f_101478ec.

version_strings.description: Shared version parser f_10483e28 takes a begin/end text span and an output structure. It requires decimal major, a literal dot and decimal minor, with an optional dot plus decimal patch. f_10483c1c first requires an ASCII digit, then clears errno and calls strtoul(base10) with an end pointer; errno 22 or 34 rejects. Leading zeroes are not rejected. Whitespace/sign prefixes are rejected by the first-byte guard. Patch is written only when present; the caller must initialize it otherwise. After the numeric components, either span end must be reached or a hyphen/pre-release and/or plus/build suffix is processed. Each suffix must start with isalnum, but subsequent bytes are copied without per-byte validation. Pre-release ends at the first plus or span end; build metadata consumes the remaining span. Each stored suffix is truncated to 32 bytes plus terminator while the cursor advances across the full suffix. Success requires cursor==span end. This is the implemented grammar, not complete enforcement of Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. Exact libc locale/overflow ABI and reads at malformed span boundaries still need verification. Manifest schema callback f_10118580 uses the shared version-string parser, then compares only unsigned major/minor through f_104840f8 against supported 1.0. Patch and suffix data are not part of that comparison. Thus a lexical value accepted by f_10483e28 can carry a patch or suffix without affecting the supported-pair decision. This is distinct from catalog XML versions, which use sscanf(%d.%d), and from the cloud-queue path regex, which restricts candidate version substrings before calling the shared parser. Cloud-queue version extractor f_10483cf0 lazily compiles the literal regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$) with flags 1, parses the URI into components using f_10c3a920 and runs regexec from the path pointer. It uses the first regex match, starts the selected version span two bytes after the match start (after /v), and normally ends at the URI path end. If the final byte of the match is slash, it ends the span at that slash instead. There is no independent check that this slash is the last path separator. Consequently a matching version segment followed by more path can supply the accepted version, despite the error text saying the path must end with a version. An earlier matching version segment is chosen before a later one. No match returns 1; regex compilation failure returns 2. Candidate suffix syntax is narrower than the shared parser because the regex permits only letters in pre-release and letters/dots in build metadata. Cloud-queue version checker f_10338a34 first calls that extractor, then f_10483e28. It returns 2 only when parsing succeeds and the major word equals 2; other outcomes return zero. It does not compare minor or patch against a supported maximum. The optional diagnostic object receives code 0x48 and distinct text for missing version, malformed version or unsupported major when the relevant failure is recognized. Callers including f_1011c864 pass null for that diagnostic object and only test the numeric return as nonzero/zero. Diagnostics are therefore not proof that the stricter grammar described in their text is enforced.

evidence.notes: Numeric components, optional patch and suffix paths through 0x10484004. Raw isel 0x7fff489e at 0x10483fa8 selects pre-release length from plus position or span remainder; 0x7f49ff5e/0x7feaff5e clamp stored suffixes to32.
ASCII-digit test, errno reset, strtoul and errno22/34 rejection. Raw NOT-GT digit branch 0x409d0040 at 0x10483c60.
Literal regex at 0x10ed4198, URI-path lookup, first regexec match, /v offset and match-final slash/end-pointer selection at 0x10483d94..0x10483e20.

cache_lookup.description: Manifest lookup f_1011a650 takes this, service ID and a nonnull output row. It formats service ID with %u and searches the three-entry memory cache by key length plus memcmp under mutex this+0x1f8. A hit refreshes entry+4 with the current clock word, copies the entire row from entry+0x20 through f_10118f64, unlocks and returns true. It does not compare a requested manifest version, cached row version, public SID/version index or cache entry+0 time word before returning a hit. There is no requested-version argument in this lookup. A cache miss unlocks, loads svcmanifests.json into a fresh 34-row scratch table through f_1011a5d0, finds the requested sid by exact word equality and copies it to output. Load failure or absent SID returns false. A successful file load can still update stored source/version/index even when the requested SID is absent. This lookup performs no HTTP download. The memory cache is separate from the 34-row persisted table. Constructor f_10119a2c sets its capacity to three; entries have stride0x51c and contain a time-derived word at +0, last-access word at +4, string key object at +8 and full manifest row at +0x20. f_1011be38 and the miss-fill code inside f_1011a650 replace an existing equal key if found; otherwise they choose the entry with the smallest unsigned last-access word. The comparison uses strict LT, so ties keep the earliest selected entry, initially index zero. There is no separate empty-entry priority beyond zero-valued initial timestamps. Both insertion paths stamp last access with the clock word. Lookup fill stores clock+1 at entry+0; f_1011be38 stores clock+its fourth argument there, and the download worker passes one. The inspected hit path does not consume this word as an expiration gate. Unsigned timestamp ordering has no wrap compensation in these selection loops. The constructor-installed clock interface at this+0x1f0 uses vtable0x11089e3c, slot+8=f_1098b4c0. With the default slot+0xc=f_1098b408 it calls sonosClockGetTime with clock id1 and returns the first 32-bit output word. The lookup hit updates last access; miss-fill and explicit insertion also record that word. These observations establish the comparison values without assuming a wall-clock freshness guarantee or a general TTL contract for the otherwise stored entry+0 word. Clock replacement sites and behavior at system time-word wrap remain caller/state audit work. Full row copies f_10118f64 preserve the 32-bit version at row+4. Memory cache hits can therefore retain a full version word written by the download worker. The file emitter writes only its low16 bits, and the public index stores a halfword. A later file reload can return the saved low-halfword version while an uninvalidated in-memory row can retain its earlier full word. No version reconciliation check occurs on a hit; each representation and update path has its own width.

evidence.notes: Lookup: decimal SID key, key-length/memcmp scan, hit timestamp/copy at0x1011a944..0x1011a980, miss file load/SID scan at0x1011a87c..0x1011a8cc, and fill through0x1011aab4. No version or entry+0 expiration comparison in the hit path.

Default clock interface reads first word after sonosClockGetTime(1). Vtable0x11089e3c slots+8/+0xc point here and f_1098b408 respectively.

cache_invalidation.description: Local download success inserts/replaces its decimal-SID entry through f_1011be38; it does not invalidate unrelated cached SIDs. Accepted replication f_1011a204 clears every cache key and both time words after the incoming file is renamed into place. Successful local deletion f_1011b310 clears only the matching decimal-SID key and its two time words after the save worker succeeds. Clearing these paths does not overwrite the old row model stored at entry+0x20; subsequent keyed lookup cannot match an empty cleared key. A cache hit otherwise has no file modification check, so out-of-band file changes are not revalidated by that hit path. Disk reload and cache invalidation must not be treated as the same operation.

evidence.notes: Replicated revision gate, incoming file parse, rename, caller-source/revision metadata commit, full key/time invalidation and unconditional kind13 call through0x1011a4b4.

replication_acceptance.description: Manifest replication worker f_1011a204 holds the file mutex, applies revision comparator f_10660e58 to current stored source/revision and incoming source/revision supplied in r6/r7, opens the incoming path supplied in r8 and parses it into a fresh scratch row table. Failed revision acceptance, open, parse or rename returns false. After rename succeeds it copies the caller-supplied source (capacity25) and revision into object state, rebuilds the SID/version index from parsed rows, clears all three cache keys/time words, invokes observer slot+0x14 with (kind13, stored source, stored revision, zero), and returns true. deletion.description: Local deletion f_1011b310 initializes a fresh table and output revision zero, acquires the file mutex and loads the current file through f_1011a4bc. On load failure it returns false. Compactor f_101195ac removes every row whose SID equals the requested SID, copies survivors forward in order and stores the survivor count; it returns whether any match was removed. No match returns false without saving. A removal calls f_1011ad40; only a true save result leads to matching-key cache invalidation and true return. The save worker header-only fallback is shared here, so true deletion is not proof that all surviving rows were persisted. An observer kind13 call is made only when the output revision is nonzero. Loading can already change stored metadata/index before a later no-match or save-failure false result, and no rollback is performed for those earlier load effects.

catalog_freshness.description: The catalog embeds its manifest-file object at +0x13ad0, constructed by f_100c6950 calling f_10119a2c. Predicate f_100c6b38 obtains the SID descriptor through catalog slot+0x20. A missing descriptor or absent capability0x400000 returns false. Otherwise it passes descriptor manifestVersion, read as an unsigned halfword at descriptor+0x128, to f_10119c80 and inverts that result. The locked index predicate scans object+0xcc entries of stride8 using count+0xc8. It returns true when a matching SID has an unsigned stored halfword version greater than or equal to the requested version. The isel at0x10119d10 keeps the previous result on unsigned less-than and sets one otherwise. This check does not load the file, compare the URI or consult the three-entry row cache. Duplicate matching index entries make true sticky. Thus a row-cache hit and the catalog freshness decision are separate policies.

At0x1028c540 it derives SID by shifting the supplied account type right8. It looks up that SID descriptor through manager slot+0x2c and requires capability0x400000. It then calls f_10570e34 on the table at stack+0x39c with the original account type, null username and selector zero. Only a null result enters the manifest removal branch. The manager obtains its catalog through zone slot+0x130, with a direct field+0x11a4 fast path when the getter equals f_1012ba78. At0x1028c5dc it calls f_100c6d14 with the derived SID; that wrapper adjusts this to catalog+0x13ad0 and tail-calls f_1011b310. The boolean manifest-deletion result is discarded. Both that branch and the skip branch continue through manager slot+0x28 with literal del and the account record. For this null-username/zero-selector call, f_10570e34 returns a record when a normalized-type-family match with flags&1 clear supplies either its special candidate or its smallest-serial candidate. The smallest-serial scan starts at0xffffffff and requires strict unsigned less-than, so a row with serial0xffffffff supplies no fallback candidate by itself. healthcheck.name: healthcheck: periodic health probe
healthcheck.summary: Maintains a diagnostic-check deadline, initially one day ahead. Update scheduling can request a deadline 30 minutes before an update check, and a group change can request one 45 seconds later. In this firmware the background worker waits, handles rescheduling and shutdown, and logs when the deadline has expired. It does not perform a self-test, fetch server instructions or submit diagnostics. The name can therefore be misleading: the recovered timer is deadline bookkeeping rather than proof that the player periodically tests its own health.

It accepts known length<1024, exact read and nested ServerDiagInstructions/SubmitPermission text bounded to31 bytes; strncmp(text,yes,3)==0 stores permission+0x188. Fetch/parse failures preserve the prior flag. No remote-command executor is present. See shared_primitives/healthcheck for scheduler predicates, caller timings and evidence.

Target-selection algorithm proven (media_player_autoplay.cxx, MpAutoPlay_/MpAp domains): on a linein-class source ({object.item.audioItem.linein.homeTheater, .airplay, .bluetooth} + x-sonos-vli URIs with vliType {RCA,...}) autoplay resolves a target: the group coordinator via autoplay couldnt determine coordinator of %s -> AVT control URI via couldnt determine AVT control URI of coordinator %s -> zone control URI via couldnt determine control URI of zone %s; invisible or proto-incompatible members are skipped (Not executing on invisible/node proto incompatible ZP %s). Dispatch: for controlURI [%s] for coordinator [%s]. programURI [%s]. %d - %d sends the program URI to http://%s:%u AVT control; autoplay: %d; become gc: %d decides whether the player becomes coordinator. Params {vol, useVol, includeZones} with airplay include zones: %d + AirplayIncludeGroupedEvt; silence gating via autoplay. Ignore Silence Threshold (%d). The raw isel words at 0x107c9d0c/0x107c9e24 select the input on unsigned greater-than, the floor otherwise. They are not shift instructions. A changed value is written under the mutex, bumps config revision and triggers notification; an unchanged value unlocks and returns success without a change notification. The parse wrappers do not supply an end pointer, so empty/nonnumeric input follows strtol zero into the lower bound rather than a distinct parser error. Indexed paired load/store uses explicit unsigned index 0x81f8; counter at +0x8200 saturates at four. Earlier +0x40 attribution contradicted by instruction operands.
GNU e500 decoding proves sample scaling/division and weighted estimator arithmetic at 0x10481f78.

Next: resolve the call supplied stack+0x28 at 0x10482b18, trace its writes through the stack+0x28/+0x2c loads at 0x10482c04/0x10482c0c, and inspect timestamp initialization and guards around 0x10482bbc-0x10482c1c before naming the measured throughput quantity.
resolved_findings: Resolved: DS-selection = the rung switcher emits New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d on a successful switch; on ladder exhaustion it reports Unable to select another DS and either waits to fetch new playlist or fetches now depending on urgency; InitFramerForTrackList failure is a distinct exhaustion path; state is dumped via <ABRState>/<ABREvents numEvents=%u> diagnostics.

DS-selection predicate decoded (literal block 0x10ed3xxx-0x10ed4xxx): each data source is ranked by a happiness test - happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d compares measured fetch rate a against a threshold, with a saturated-buffer override happy (saturated): %d %d; hysteresis via was happy: %d / unhappy: %d counters plus Underruns %u accounting; rate update: a=1 (was %.2lf) resets the estimator. Bitrate switching logs New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d and persists Last estimated bitrate %u (Reset ABR state: start bitrate %u). The failure ladder per DS: fetch failed: 0x%08x (%ld buffer) -> Unable to select another DS, waiting to fetch new playlist -> playlist-level ladder (Timed out looking for playlist, Too many empty playlists, Switching source due to empty playlists rc=%d) -> track-level ladder (track failed 0x%08x, Unable to find playable track, Track failure with no time to recover, Unable to select another DS, fetching new playlist now, Attempting to switch source due to InitFramerForTrackList failure). Prebuffer gate: prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec; URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d paces the playlist refresh. Codec filtering uses the mp4a.40. prefix plus a URI version regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$). Status page emits <ABRState Name="ABR State"> with <NodeTXBuffer>%.3lf sec</NodeTXBuffer> and <ProcessRate>%.0lf bps</ProcessRate>.

Instruction-level correction: f_10481b30 keeps the counter at object+0x8200 (r30=object+0x10000, lwz/stw -0x7e00). It increments the counter at 0x10481bbc, compares signed against 4 at 0x10481bc0, and clamps values greater than 4 to 4 at 0x10481fbc. Thus this is a saturating counter, not evidence of an unbounded cumulative mean. The paired load/store at 0x10481f6c/0x10481f8c uses index r8=0x81f8 into r31=object, not object+0x40. The neighboring path at 0x10481bf0-0x10481bf8 reads the same offset. f_104801f0, called at 0x10481f18, accesses object+0x8204 and checks virtual slot +0x70 against f_10483b8c. These are concrete object offsets; interpreting the incompletely decoded SPE arithmetic as a named upstream statistic remains unresolved.

SPE decoded with GNU powerpc-linux-gnu-objdump -WN -M e500: f_10481b30 merges the incoming r5:r6 words into double r25 with evmergelo at 0x10481b58, converts unsigned r7 to double at 0x10481bd0, loads 1000.0 from 0x10ea2398 and computes sample x = r25*1000.0/unsigned(r7) at 0x10481be0-0x10481be4. The branch with object+0x8630 zero reaches 0x10481f5c, loads old estimate E from +0x81f8 and executes E = ((n-1)*E+x)/n via efdcfsi/efdmul/efdadd/efddiv at 0x10481f78-0x10481f8c. Counter n at +0x8200 increments and saturates at four; after saturation this is a 3/4 old plus 1/4 new update, not a cumulative mean over all observations. No zero-denominator guard occurs in sample formation; caller constraints on elapsed time remain to be established. The nonzero +0x8630 path bypasses this averaging branch, so the equation is not universal for all modes.

Caller provenance advanced: the direct call at 0x10482c1c supplies r5:r6 from stack+0x28/+0x2c and r7 from r28. r28 is the result of timevalDiff at 0x10482bc8 using the current clock value from sonosClockGetTime(1,...) at 0x10482bbc and the prior stack+0x3c timestamp. The numerator pair is not converted by the callee, so it is already a double representation. That call path establishes an elapsed-time input but establishes milliseconds via the shipped libsonos-time-c.so.1 timevalDiff implementation, but not the upstream semantic meaning of the numerator. The previous inability to decode the update arithmetic is resolved; source-statistic binding remains genuinely open.

Elapsed-time unit recovered independently from the imported implementation: libsonos-time-c.so.1 timevalDiff at 0x12a4-0x12e4 computes (seconds difference)*1000 + trunc_toward_zero((microseconds difference)/1000), using signed mulhw and arithmetic-shift correction for the division. The anacapad call at 0x10482bc8 saves this result in r28 and forwards it unchanged to r7 at 0x10482c14. Thus sample formation multiplies the numerator by 1000 and divides by elapsed milliseconds, not elapsed microseconds. The out-pointer passed as stack+0x28 at 0x10482b18 must still be joined to the later numerator loads; units of the numerator and a nonzero elapsed-time guarantee are not established by the time helper.

devmode.internals: statement files {debug/devmode.bin,/devmode.bin,/tmp/devmode.tmp.bin} format "0x%s %d.%d-%d.%d" (id+version range); x-rincon-enc3 encryption; R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL "may not be persisted" gate + "Removing persistent statement with R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL" + "Loaded persistent statement"; notify {processes,listeners} on change
resolved_findings: Resolved: internals = the devmode toggle writing conf/rdmconfig + conf/rdmlocation; gate call sites = the per-route flag checks on the admin/debug surface.

devmode = a signed statement system (devmode.cxx): a /devmode.bin blob (fetched as debug/devmode.bin, staged via /tmp/devmode.tmp.bin) carries statements formatted 0x%s %d.%d-%d.%d (statement id + supported version range). Statements can be persistent or temporary - persistence is restricted per statement (R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL may not be persisted; Removing persistent statement with R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL) so the SSH-pubkey-install capability only ever applies to the running boot. Changes fan out to listeners and processes (Failed to notify listeners/processes about the change). Blob is x-rincon-enc3 wrapped (signed/encoded). So devmode = a secure policy door where a signed blob enables specific capabilities (e.g. SSH pubkey install) without an open flag file.

Resolved: the x-rincon-enc3 verifying algorithm is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 - the libsonoscrypto verifier imports mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_verify directly, and the parse+verify entry (ZZ0137) decodes a byte-swapped header with magic check cmpwi 0x1E71 before delegating to the RSA verify helpers ZZ0068/ZZ0064. The PEM key path is a caller-supplied arg to the key loader ZZ0053 (not a compiled-in filename).

Key selection proven: ZZ0053 (libsonoscrypto 0x6318) takes a key-container blob pointer, not a file path - it parses a magic-checked header (XOR-magic 0x779B99CA at blob+0, byte-swapped fields) and selects numbered signing keys ({Unknown %s signing key!, %s signing key %u is revoked!, %s signed with key %u} vocabulary). There is no PEM/key-file literal in the image - verifying key material is delivered inside the signed container itself.
Established: signed /devmode.bin statement blob, per-statement persistence policy, R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL capability, x-rincon-enc3 wrapping, listener fan-out.

cache_checker_transport.read_and_timer: Request path0x105850dc can track a target IPv4 among four entries and writes one NUL byte to pipeWrite+0x108 at0x10585254. resolved_findings: Resolved: Too many discontinuities triggers the FIFO reset path - drops pending segments and re-anchors the consumer to the next produced frame.

Resolved: afifo layout (audio_fifo.cxx) - byte ring bounds at +0x8/+0xc (capacity = end-start), used-byte counter +0xfc, flag bytes {+0xf8 eof, +0xf9 flush/discard, +0xfa rendering}, a second window pair +0x100/+0x104/+0x108/+0x10c/+0x110, 0x18-byte record array at +0x114 indexed by +0x118, pending boundary record +0x198 (-1=none), +0x19c flag. Record list exhausts -> '*** not enough fifo records to handle this write'; write overflow -> 'truncated write!'. Boundary EOF markers support 'audio fifo read at boundary eof'/'consumed exactly to the eof marker' and logical boundary at offset N. eSDK producer path logs 'Waited %ums for audio from the eSDK (fifo used: %zu)'; prebuffer completes with 'Finished prebuffering in %u ms (st: %d, flush: %d), fifo used: %zu / %zu'. Constant 0x7a120 (~500KB headroom term) appears in the used/total calc at 0x105899d4-0x105899e4.

Resolved: afifo ctor f_1058924c (vptr 0x10ef04d8, log domain audiofifo, file audio_fifo.cxx) has exactly two instantiation sites and both pass capacity 0x40000 (256 KiB): spotsmapicontrol ctor 0x102233b0 embeds the afifo at +0xb8 (call at 0x102234ac, r5 = addis 0x4 = 0x40000 at 0x10219a18) and RSpotifyAudioInput ctor 0x104db630 embeds it at +0x288 (call at 0x104db7b8, r6 = 0x40000 at 0x10219900). The ctor stores the capacity arg at both +0x8 and +0xc, points +0x114 at the object itself, and initializes a FIXED 5-element embedded record array at +0x120 via a mtctr 5 loop (0x18-byte records ending at +0x198) - record count is a compile-time 5, not a ctor arg.

Resolved: ctor arg r4 (stored via the embedded window subobject at +0x4, sibling pair +0x8/+0xc seeded from r5) is the byte-ring backing-store base pointer supplied by the caller. Call census over the whole afifo module (0x10588600-0x10589600) shows NO call to malloc/realloc/calloc/free (imports resolved via .dynsym: malloc=0x11099628, realloc=0x11098418, calloc=0x11099230, free=0x110991a0 - none referenced) - the ring memory is allocated by each owner (spotsmapicontrol / RSpotifyAudioInput), so no lazy first-write allocation exists. response_length.description: The f_10541e00 helper reports response-length availability, not body availability. It returns false when byte +0x44b4 is clear or gzip flag +0x4a8 is set; otherwise it writes the unsigned total at +0x44b8 to the caller and returns the availability byte. The HTTP header parser fills that total from Content-Length or supported Content-Range forms. Content-Encoding:gzip sets +0x4a8. Therefore a modified catalog with no usable advertised length, including the gzip path, selects 801 before body streaming; a reported total >=0x20000 selects 804. The gate is not a measurement of actual streamed or normalized XML size.

evidence.notes: thermal/status blocks

Objdump and raw word 0x54a5043e at 0x103f747c establish SH=0,MB=16,ME=31,Rc=0: retain the low 16 bits of r5, with no right shift. Incoming r4 is saved in r30 at 0x103f73ec; the Master getter at virtual +0x18 receives stack+0x1a output. cmpwi/bne at 0x103f741c/0x103f7420 leave on nonzero getter result; lhz and unsigned cmpl/bgt at 0x103f7424-0x103f742c enter adjustment only for returned>requested. Raw subf 0x7cbe2850 at 0x103f7468 forms returned-requested, then the mask feeds virtual +0xac at 0x103f7494. Because returned is a u16 and is unsigned-greater than requested, this difference fits u16; masking does not divide it or generally reduce it to zero. All other comparisons take the return path without adjustment. The log uses original requested r30 at 0x103f74bc, not the masked delta.

Raw big-endian LimelightThermalSensors rows and relocations: CPU95/99, AMP98/105, terminated after two entries. Reachable call from i2c_initLimelightDevices text0x7cd4 -> thermalsensor_InitDriver0x84b4; copies0x8578-0x85ac into runtime stride88. thermalsensor_GetStatus0x8ea4 checks runtime fault+0x20 before warning+0x1c, after successful thermalSensor_GetTemperature. Proc prefix comparisons0x8204-0x8254 call setters0x828c/0x829c/0x82ac; SetWarnTemp0x8070 and SetFaultTemp0x7f94 distinguish nonzero override from zero default restoration. GNU objdump relocations/raw section words used; the prefix consumers are not DT lookups.

resolved_findings: Resolved: the read path is hal_thermal_open -> hal_thermal_get_temps(buf,3) -> hal_thermal_close (f_1018261c). Three channels {cpu, amp, soc} (log 'cpu:%d, amp:%d, soc:%d'); absent-sensor sentinel is -213 (0xffffff2b, cmpwi -0xd5 per channel). Valid temps are filed under {cpu,amp,soc} into a telemetry KVP batch posted as {stat/hardware/temperature_volume/volume/ampstate} via the report-mgr sink. Reporting cadence = a rolling u8 counter at obj-0x854 (incremented, mod 256) gated by a strtol'd config value ('5' default literal). ClampVolume consumer f_103f73c0: reads a u16 'Master' value through rc virtual +0x18 into stack+0x1a. Only getter result 0 and unsigned returned value > requested limit (saved r4) enter the adjustment branch. It computes (returned-requested)&0xffff, not a right shift, and passes that difference as r5 to rc virtual +0xac with r4=0, r6=2, r7=original r5 and r8=1. The diagnostic logs the requested limit: 'Hardware %s; clamping volume to %d%%'.
Resolved: the thermal emit vocabulary is proven in the 0x10ef4fc8 enum: TEMP_WARNING=28, TEMP_FAULT=29, TEMP_OK=30 (and HW_ERROR=26/HW_OK=27) - the temperature-state names the clamp logic reports.

Compiled thresholds are available in shipped audiodev.ko, not absent device-tree data. LimelightThermalSensors is a terminated stride40 table at .data+0x400: CPU/id0 has warning95 and fault99 Celsius; AMP/id1 has warning98 and fault105 Celsius. Name relocations at .data+0x400/+0x428 resolve to CPU/AMP at .rodata.str1.4+0x24e8/+0x24ec. These are defaults for the compiled Limelight initialization path, not a census of every Sonos board or all DSP thermal policies.

i2c_initLimelightDevices calls thermalsensor_InitDriver at module text0x7cd4. On successful device creation the initializer copies table warning/fault words+0x10/+0x14 into runtime sensor+0x1c/+0x20 and the status flags+0x1c/+0x20 into runtime+0x28/+0x2c. thermalsensor_GetStatus first requires a successful temperature read, then checks a nonzero fault threshold with temperature>=threshold; otherwise it checks a nonzero warning threshold. It ORs the selected flags across initialized sensors. CPU warning/fault flags are0x80000/0x40000; AMP flags are0x20000/0x10000. A read failure skips that sensor; no selected flags yields0.

The temp-, warn- and fault- strings are command prefixes in thermalsensor_proc_write, not composed device-tree properties. thermalsensor_proc_init creates driver/temp-sensor; the write path parses a number with strict_strtol and calls the debug-temperature, warning-threshold or fault-threshold setter for the named sensor. In thermalsensor_SetWarnTemp and thermalsensor_SetFaultTemp, a nonzero supplied value replaces the runtime threshold, while zero restores the compiled table default; unknown names take a diagnostic path. Therefore running thresholds can differ from these compiled defaults. The previous absent-DTB/DSP-only threshold boundary is withdrawn.

resolved_findings: Resolved: guard emit plumbing decoded - each reject string is wrapped by an emitter fn (0x10185cd8 PoE+eth, 0x10185d58 water-sensor, 0x10185ddc mic-switch, 0x10185e60 not-subwoofer, 0x10185f6c suspendable, 0x10186068 battery) that stamps {code 0x48/0x5a, message} via f_101a2ba8 then calls the reply thunk f_109db780. Each emitter is reached through a tiny vtable thunk (0x10185d50-family: 'addi r4,-0x56dc; b emitter') stored in the settings-object vtable block 0x10e97ef8-0x10e97f38 - no direct bl callers exist; the capability-bit test itself runs in the checker vfunc that selects the thunk.

Launch-capability premise disproven in the executable: main f_1006a690 dispatches option character C through relative jump-table 0x10e706a4 to 0x1006a8f4, where the next argv pointer is selected into r22. The u case at 0x1006a858 selects username into r25. At 0x1006a7b4-0x1006a7bc those values are passed as (r25,r22) to sonos_auth_become_capable@plt. Shipped opt/bin/anacapactl line 5 supplies -u anacapa -C all=eip. This is the process-user/privilege path, not a device-model feature mask source. The usage text calling the argument caps was insufficient to identify it as product capabilities.

Literal feature masks are encoded in startup instructions, not inferred from string ordinal: f_1008e7c4 constructs a name/mask dictionary. Stores at 0x1008e848/0x1008e854 bind AUDIO_IN_MASK=0xff; 0x1008e860/0x1008e86c bind RCA_LINE_IN=1; 0x1008e878/0x1008e884 bind 35MM_LINE_IN=2; 0x1008e890/0x1008e89c bind DOCK_ANALOG_IN=4; 0x1008e8a8/0x1008e8b4 bind USB_LINEIN=8; 0x1008e8c0-0x1008e8d0 bind HTAUDIO_IN_MASK=0xff00; 0x1008e8dc-0x1008e8ec bind TOSLINK_HT_IN=0x8000; 0x1008e8f8 binds HDMI_ARC=0x4000. Independent initializer f_10095d04 constructs the same initial pairs at 0x10095da8 onward. AUDIO_IN_MASK is therefore a grouped mask and array index one is not bit one. This directly refutes the universal feature-bit-order interpretation of the contiguous strings.

Actual name-selection path: f_1062192c calls f_106214f4 at 0x10621970 to create a vector of feature names. f_106214f4 first obtains object+0xd0 via f_10908ce8 at 0x10621568, walks dictionary nodes from global 0x110a89c4+8, intersects the feature word with node+4 at 0x1062158c-0x10621594, filters names containing MASK via f_108327fc, and copies selected names into a vector. It next obtains object+0xd4 via f_10908cf8 at 0x10621608. Accessors f_10908d08/f_10908d18 similarly read +0xd8/+0xdc. The RMuseFeature-array size warning at 0x10621b50 compares resulting vector count to caller capacity; this path does not index a literal 77-entry bit-name array. These verified reads locate the required model-word writer investigation, but do not establish its result or justify the previous S9 live/dead guard claims, which are withdrawn.

evidence.notes: extaudiosrc block

resolved_findings: Resolved: job-priority = the 16-entry extaudiosrc job-type enum ordered by priority; exclusivity = single-source-per-stream rules in the stream-compatibility map.

Job arbitration decoded (extaudiosrc_playid tags): two queues - playStream (immediate, skipping stream due to exclusivity when a non-shareable type is playing) vs playDeferredStream (deferred j:%zu d:%zu counts, bounded by too many deferred jobs! [%u]). Clip-type enum complete {COMMON, AUDIOCLIP, AVT_HACK, ALEXA_TTS, ALEXA_WELCOME, ALEXA_FAILURE, ALEXA_ALERT, GOOGLE_MEDIA, GOOGLE_ALARM, GOOGLE_TTS, SPS, SVE_TTS, VOCAL_GUIDANCE, ALERT, SETUP_CHIRP, DISCOVERY} each carrying an interrupt flag (processing type %d (intr=%d)). Job lifecycle: queuing job %u (total=%zu) -> playing job %u -> WaitForComplete (state=%d, term=%d) -> removing job %u (a:%d) -> done processJob (state=%d, jobs=%zu); defects logged as playing job %u is missing! / current job %u gone. Per-job volume override with ramp syntax [from, to - target over %ums] or fixed [a, b]. Decode constraints: stereo-only (unsupported channel count > 2: %zu), decoder abort honored (decoder flagged playback stop), start-time resolution required (failed to get start time (offset %u), aborting / new offset %u), zero-length frames dropped (Unexpected zero len frame).

Resolved: complete job-type name table @0x10ec0000 (18 rows): {DISCARDED, COMMON, AUDIOCLIP, CHIRP, AVT_HACK, ALEXA_TTS, ALEXA_WELCOME, ALEXA_FAILURE, ALEXA_ALERT, GOOGLE_MEDIA, GOOGLE_ALARM, GOOGLE_TTS, SPS, SVE_TTS, VOCAL_GUIDANCE, ALERT, SETUP_CHIRP, DISCOVERY}; the "processing type %s %d (intr=%d)" intr byte is a per-JOB flag (*(job+4)), not a type property.

Resolved: exclusivity is driven by job flag bit 0x10 @0x1037841c - when the incoming job carries the exclusive bit and a non-shareable type is playing, playStream logs "skipping stream due to exclusivity" and drops it; otherwise the job queues. There is no static per-type preempt matrix: the preempt-vs-queue-vs-skip decision is {job flags bit0x10, current playing job type} at runtime.

resolved_findings: Resolved: stream type %d values = the framer-factory ordinals matching the accepted_mimes codec ids.

Stream architecture decoded (fileio/fileDataProvider/fileDataMgr/asyncfileio tags): URIs open through a stream-class dispatch (Success opening URI %s; stream type %d / Failed opening URI status 0x%x / getStreamInternal: ppstrm is null) whose classes cover http, smb, memory-resident, and directory - File is in memory; not opening HTTP stream is the cache hit; directory opens are mutually exclusive with file opens (already opened as a directory / as SMB directory) and SMB listings serialize as application/xml; listing via readdir. Async notification registers per stream (%p: registering async / async enabled / unregistering). Framer factory: mime type for %s is %s drives parser selection; no framer found in factory is the unreachable-default guard.

Stream-type dispatch table recovered: URI-pattern -> MIME -> extension triples {sonos.com-http:*:audio/mpeg3:*, sonos.com-http:*:audio/x-ms-wma:*, sonos.com-http:*:audio/wma:*, sonos.com-http:*:audio/wav:* (.wav), sonos.com-http:*:audio/aiff:* (.aiff), sonos.com-http:*:audio/flac:* (.flac), sonos.com-spotify:*:audio/x-spotify:*, sonos.com-http:*:application/ogg:*, sonos.com-rtrecent:*:audio/x-sonos-recent:*, x-sonosapi-hls-static:*:*:*, sonos.com-http:*:application/dash+xml:* (.mpd), sonos.com-http:*:application/octet-stream:* (.unknown), audio/vnd.radiotime, x-sonosapi-hls:*:*:*} terminating in Unsupported mime.

Resolved: the mime->framer-row binder is a strcasecmp ladder (f_10721458 ff., dispatcher family 0x10721458-0x107221xx) writing 12-byte rows {+0 scheme-override, +4 protocolInfo triple, +8 extension-or-0}. Rows proven: audio/x-ms-wma -> {x-sonosprog-mms: | x-sonos-mms: alias, sonos.com-mms:*:audio/x-ms-wma:*, ext 0}; audio/mp3 -> {x-sonosprog-http:, sonos.com-http:*:audio/mpeg3:*, .mp3}. resolved_findings: Native entry f_1039dd7c loads unsigned halfwords from owner+0xd296 and owner+0xd28e, converts both with efscfui and divides the first by the second at 0x1039dd80-0x1039dd90. Call that floating ratio sg. It converts sg to unsigned integer with efsctuiz and retains its low sixteen bits at 0x1039dd94-0x1039dd98 before comparison with target argument r5. Equality returns the member snapshot halfword at record+0x68e unchanged (0x1039deac). Thus the sg load path is no longer an opaque SPE gap, but the producing aggregate fields still need semantic binding.

For the non-equality path, GNU e500 disassembly establishes nv = sv + (ng-sg)*(cap-sv)/(cap-sg), where sv is unsigned halfword member+0x68e, ng is incoming r5, and sg is the ratio above. The comparison at 0x1039ddc8 selects cap=100.0 from 0x10ec3998 when sg<ng, otherwise cap=0.0 from 0x10ec399c. The arithmetic is efssub/efsmul/efsdiv/efsadd at 0x1039ddf0-0x1039de14. No explicit clamp to 0..100 or denominator-zero guard appears in this local calculation; caller constraints remain to be traced. The previous fixed-volume endpoint-selection and universal clamp assertions are withdrawn.

Return conversion corrected independently of the audit report: 0x1039de70 calls roundf, 0x1039de78 executes efsctuiz, and 0x1039de94 is clrlwi r3,r3,16. The result is the low sixteen bits of the converted rounded integer, not a Q16 value shifted right sixteen. The direct snapshot return at 0x1039deac is an independent counterexample to the claimed universal fixed-point return convention.

Member eligibility helper f_1039deb4 addresses records at stride 0x694. It requires a nonzero byte at record+0, then (halfword_at_0x68c & 3)==3 at 0x1039ded4-0x1039dee0 and (halfword & 4)!=0 at 0x1039deec-0x1039def0. It exposes the record through the output pointer, rejects nonzero byte +0x693, otherwise computes and stores the target through f_1039dd7c at 0x1039df1c-0x1039df20. The surrounding group-volume path snapshots member state, logs calculateVolume with sg/ng/sv/nv labels, applies local and remote changes and reports total/partial/fixed-volume/in-progress faults. healthcheck_contact.name: healthcheck: server instructions
healthcheck_contact.summary: Contains a separate compiled helper for reading a server's diagnostic-submission permission. It requests a household-specific XML file with a two-minute deadline, requires a known body length below 1,024 bytes and an exact read, then accepts nested SubmitPermission text beginning with yes. A successful parse updates the remembered permission; a download or parsing failure leaves its previous value intact. No caller of this helper was found in this binary, and the health-check timer does not invoke it. The response is a permission value, rather than a general channel for executing remote maintenance commands.

evidence.notes: hls blocks

storeStream calls f_103bca4c with the parsed bandwidth at 0x103bdd70. Exact bandwidth equality (raw 0x7f8a2000, 0x419e0050 at 0x103bca70-74) appends to the existing bucket; otherwise the first empty slot among 16 is used. Per-bucket count <=3 admits the next record, giving four streams (unsigned cmplwi raw 0x2b890003 and branch 0x41bdffd8 at 0x103bcadc-e0). Stream stride is 0x2068; bucket stride 0x81a8. Sorting f_103bc6c0 compares unsigned adjacent bandwidth words (raw 0x7f895040) and skips swap unless left < right (raw 0x409c0044); three memcpy calls swap entire buckets. Master parsing stores, sorts, then applies context at 0x103be9a0/0x103be9c0/0x103be9d0. Context selection f_103bd1f4 reads through f_10804148; its ordinary path walks descending buckets until context bitrate >= the next bucket, bounded by bucket count, with index zero fallback when context >= maximum or no buckets. Stream index is stored only when below bucket count (0x103bd310-318). Context callback f_103b9328 forwards the tuple through f_103bd4d0 at 0x103b9474; the latter tail-branches to f_1080422c. Ascending/descending adaptation helpers f_103bcf24/f_103bcd64 change bucket index and reset stream index, not the bucket order. Runtime threshold r4 may stop their walk; no stable-estimator key participates in these comparison/sort functions.

Start validates context bit 0 via f_10804120, then f_10804148 copies words +0/+4 and the pair +8/+12 into bitrate/stream/segment log arguments. No variant comparison occurs here. The source-switch path tests bytes object+0xff77d and +0xff77c and calls f_103bd098 with r4=0. That helper compares variant count against 1, increments object+0x81de8, compares the unsigned new index against count, and wraps it to zero when out of range (0x103bd0dc-0x103bd0f8, 0x103bd188). This is index traversal, not evidence of bandwidth-tier ranking.

HLS construction first calls the segaudio constructor at 0x103baba0, then installs vtable 0x10ec4ec8 at 0x103babb0. Its +0x64 slot (0x10ec4f2c) is f_103b96b8, +0x70 is f_103b8348, +0x78 is f_103b85b8 and +0x7c is f_103b8634. The segaudio worker f_104829d8 calls +0x64 at 0x10482b74 with r5=&sp+0x28. HLS preserves that pointer in r22 at 0x103b96fc and passes it at outgoing sp+0x10 to the selected framer's virtual +0x1c at 0x103b9cbc. The result is media seconds, also logged through the same pointer as '%f secs processed' at 0x103ba070-0x103ba090; cached advancement can seed it at 0x103b9fd0-0x103b9fdc. The worker times the call using sonosClockGetTime(1) at 0x10482abc/0x10482bbc and timevalDiff at 0x10482bc8, and forwards the reported double in r5:r6 and elapsed value in r7 to f_10481b30 at 0x10482c1c. A nonzero processing return or the stop out-byte bypasses this estimator call (0x10482b80-0x10482b8c), as does the zero-media-seconds comparison at 0x10482ba8-0x10482bac. This is a media-advancement/time measurement, not a direct network-byte counter.

SPE instructions at 0x10481bd0-0x10481be4 form sample S = reported media seconds * 1000.0 / unsigned elapsed value; 1000.0 is the double at 0x10ea2398. The sample counter at object+0x8200 increments and clamps to four (0x10481bbc-0x10481bc8, 0x10481fbc-0x10481fc4). If object+0x8630 is zero, 0x10481f5c-0x10481f8c updates the double A at +0x81f8 to ((n-1)*A+S)/n; otherwise 0x10481bf8 reuses A. HLS overrides virtual +0x70, so the non-default branch at 0x10481c0c reaches 0x10481fac, calling f_103b8348 -> f_103bcba0 for the current bucket's declared bandwidth B. At 0x10481fb4 this unsigned B is converted to double, and 0x10481c1c/0x10481c24/0x10481c2c multiply B*A, truncate to unsigned and store the estimated bitrate E at object+0x81ec. State +0x8634 and the first-three-sample guard at 0x10481c28-0x10481c3c can defer the later adaptation predicates, not this estimate store. Happy/hysteresis paths dispatch virtual +0x78 at 0x1048207c or 0x104828b0; the unhappy path dispatches +0x7c at 0x10482888. After a selected-bitrate change, 0x10481f24-0x10481f50 renormalizes A by old B/new B. Constructor f_1047fd10 zeros E at 0x1047fd68; the changed-stream ABR reset in f_10482f50 zeros E and the sample counter at 0x104830b0-0x104830b8.

Upgrade first requires f_103bcf04 to report a nonzero bucket index. It loads E from owner+0x81ec at 0x103b85fc and uses SPE efdcfui, efdmul and efdctuiz (raw 0x108022f0/0x10844ae8/0x108022f8 at 0x103b8614/0x103b8624/0x103b862c) with the 0.9 double at 0x10ec4f70, then tail-calls f_103bcf24 at 0x103b8630 with r4=trunc_unsigned(0.9*E). The helper moves at least one bucket toward index zero, then can continue while the threshold reaches the next higher bucket; raw unsigned cmpl 0x7f9e3840 and branch 0x419c0078 at 0x103bcfa0-0x103bcfa4 stop before a next bucket above the threshold. A zero threshold takes the first-step exit at 0x103bcf90. Downgrade wrapper f_103b8634 instead supplies literal r4=0 at 0x103b867c, so f_103bcd64 takes its first-step exit at 0x103bcdec and does not seek an estimator-selected bandwidth. Both other direct downgrade callers also set r4=0: f_103bd098 at 0x103bd1a4 and f_103bd1f4 at 0x103bd434. The source-switch worker calls virtual +0x68 at 0x10482e80, bound to f_103b84a4 by 0x10ec4f30. That wrapper always passes r4=0 to f_103bd098 at 0x103b84f8: counts above one cycle within the current bucket, while count <=1 returns false at 0x103bd194-0x103bd19c. Its downgrade tail-call is reachable only for other callers supplying a nonzero fallback flag. Thus the observed source-switch selection does not consume E or compare bandwidth estimates.

Raw rotate audit with corrected decoder: 0x56d6063e at 0x10481c5c has SH=0,MB=24,ME=31,Rc=0 and keeps the low byte; similarly 0x10481ca0/0x10481cac keep boolean bytes, 0x10481e7c keeps six bits and 0x10481ed4 four. None divides the estimator. Valid-context raw 0x546307fe at 0x1080412c keeps bit 0, without shifting. S=1000*seconds/elapsed uses SPE efdmul/efddiv at 0x10481be0/0x10481be4, mean division uses efddiv at 0x10481f88, and upgrade scaling uses efdmul/efdctuiz at 0x103b8624/0x103b862c. Bucket count/strides use literal 16 at 0x103bca54, cmplwi 3 at 0x103bcadc, mulli 0x2068 at 0x103bcae4 and literal 0x81a8 memcpy sizes 0x103bc734/0x103bc748/0x103bc75c. Corrected disassembly therefore leaves the documented estimator, bucket ordering and source-switch distinction unchanged.

resolved_findings: Bitrate ordering is an unsigned descending sort of 16 fixed-size buckets, not a comparison of two bandwidth estimators: f_103bc6c0 compares adjacent bitrate words and swaps entire 0x81a8-byte buckets only when left < right. Equal bitrates are grouped by f_103bca4c, which appends stream records in arrival order (up to four per bucket); new bitrates use the first empty bucket (up to 16). f_103be9a0 stores parsed streams, f_103be9c0 sorts, and f_103be9d0 applies the saved context. f_103bd1f4 selects the first descending bucket with bitrate <= the context bitrate, falling back to the last populated bucket below the minimum or bucket zero at/above the maximum, then uses the saved stream index only if below that bucket's count. The context setter f_103bd4d0 delegates to f_1080422c; it preserves the supplied resume tuple rather than estimating bandwidth. Upgrade f_103bcf24 walks toward index zero; downgrade f_103bcd64 walks toward the final populated bucket. Their numeric threshold argument is a runtime input, not another sorting key. f_103bd098 cycles streams within the selected bucket with wraparound. Thus the same-bitrate tie-break is playlist arrival order followed by saved/current stream index, not a stable-estimator comparison.

The runtime upgrade threshold is derived, not an unidentified external bandwidth input. The segaudio worker f_104829d8 times HLS processing, takes its reported media-seconds advancement, and passes both to f_10481b30. That function forms S=1000*seconds/elapsed, maintains a gated running mean A at object+0x81f8 with sample count capped at four, and stores E=trunc_unsigned(current declared bandwidth*A) at +0x81ec. HLS upgrade wrapper f_103b85b8 supplies trunc_unsigned(0.9*E) to f_103bcf24. The generic happy/hysteresis predicates determine whether upgrade is attempted; the threshold can then extend the walk beyond its first higher bucket. The unhappy downgrade wrapper f_103b8634 passes zero, requesting one lower bucket rather than searching against E. The measurement, current bitrate and adaptation predicates influence runtime selection, but none is a second key in the playlist sort. After changing bitrate the common path rescales A by old/new declared bandwidth.

Source switching is separate from bandwidth adaptation: the worker's virtual +0x68 calls f_103b84a4, which supplies a zero fallback flag to f_103bd098. With multiple streams in the current equal-bandwidth bucket, that helper advances the stream index in playlist order and wraps; with zero or one stream it returns false without downgrading. Its conditional downgrade fallback is disabled for this caller. Neither the source-switch wrapper nor this selected path reads the bitrate estimate, and the context-selection downgrade fallback also supplies a literal zero threshold. Actual playlist entries, processed media time and elapsed time remain runtime values, not missing static ranking rules.

Variant/segment machinery decoded (hlsaudio + segaudio tags): multi-codec-variant playlists force a re-source (forcing a source switch due to multiple codec variants in playlist) gated on group codec capability (requires group capabilities %u - all members must decode the variant). Playback starts at a chosen variant (starting at bitrate %u stream %u segment %llu offset %zu); seek maps time to segment+offset (seek to time %.3f (%lu:%02lu:%02lu) / from start of current segm) validated against the ADTS-derived position (cached seconds advanced %f does not line up with seek, offset %f MD: %ld.%06ld; ADTS metadata: %s / no ADTS metadata, bumping seconds advanced %f). Encryption: SAMPLE-AES sets up audio-framer decryption (SAMPLE-AES detected. Setting up audio framer decryption), missing key URI/data fail closed (encrypted, but no key URI / no data from key URI), absent IV falls back to media sequence number (No IV, using seq. num.), undefined method is unreachable (undefined encryption method). EXT-X-MAP byte-range maps need the file size (could not get file size from http headers for map / found offset %zu). Track init runs InitFramerForTrackList with time-offset bookkeeping (pEntry->m_dTimeOffset, Trim offset required). Adjacent float constants 0.05 and 0.25 are the seek/position tolerances.

todo: Established: static alarms/audioClip namespace tables, name getters, the complete eight-entry alarms verb-factory switch and dispatcher missing-command versus missing-implementation paths. Remaining: complete the namespace->generated class->verb-command->concrete domain implementation join for the cloud namespace set, including the writers of namespace+4 and command+4 and their startup/setupWholeDevicePointers injection paths. Start with alarms vtable 0x10f9fc44, f_10ac47ac and factories f_10ac5140/f_10ac5464, then repeat for areas vtable/name getter f_10acc504 and other namespace classes. HTTP prefix rows and name literals are not sufficient to certify this census; the old route-only and no-static-pair limitation is withdrawn. This is actionable static reverse engineering.
resolved_findings: The old route-only/no-name-reference premise for cloud namespaces is false. f_10ac78b4 returns the alarms literal at 0x10e7bf5c; f_10acc504 returns areas at 0x10e7c0e4. Alarms static namespace vtable 0x10f9fc44 binds +0x18=f_10ac47ac (verb selection/factory), +0x1c=f_10ac78b4 (name), +0x20=f_10ac78a4 (current command), +0x24=f_109eac1c and +0x28=f_109eb04c (dispatch). AudioClip provides a counterexample to treating these functions as registration calls: f_10ad03b8 only returns a name, and its static namespace vtable is 0x10fa03d4. Static namespace class identity is therefore recoverable without relying on HTTP route adjacency.

Alarms namespace f_10ac47ac builds eight {verb,factory} entries on its stack: subscribe->f_10ac4ec4, unsubscribe->f_10ac5000, getAlarms->f_10ac5140, fetchAlarm->f_10ac5464, createAlarm->f_10ac56e8, updateAlarm->f_10ac5a20, snoozeAlarm->f_10ac5d24, removeAlarm->f_10ac5fd4. It compares the incoming command name at command-info+0x26 using strcmp and stride 8. No match returns null. A match invokes the factory with namespace+4 as an argument, replaces namespace+0x38 with the returned command object, and destroys the previous object if present. The +0x38 slot is not itself proof of a permanent domain actor/module mapping.

f_109eb04c is a dispatcher, not the namespace-registration function previously claimed. It calls the namespace virtual +0x20 at 0x109eb1d4; the default implementation or a null returned command produces status 0x5a. It initializes the command and executes the subsequent pipeline. The Namespace may be missing actor diagnostic is gated later on status 0x59 at 0x109eb708. A concrete alarms command path separately checks its implementation pointer at command+4: null yields 0x59 and Namespace has no actor, while non-null calls implementation virtual +8. Thus absence of a command and absence of its injected implementation are distinct failures, not evidence that all cloud namespace code lives outside the image.
muse_engine.summary: Muse dispatches commands through generated namespace objects with static method tables and per-verb factories. A namespace object can hold the currently constructed command at +0x38; this is distinct from its injected implementation/context pointer. HTTP route literals alone do not bind the underlying domain actor.

Reader and validation independently checked: f_107e1264 reads one 48-byte metadata item with fread and returns 2 on failure. It byte-reverses packed words at offsets 1,5,0x0b and u16 sample count at 9; the file values are little-endian. The count shifted left three is stored at reader+0x40. Flag byte 0x27 bit 0x80 selects the signal-loss log/return-4 path; metadata is still copied to reader+0x10. f_107e1e44 checks version byte 1 and walks complete metadata/audio records, retaining a valid prefix if its size exceeds 47 bytes. Empty input or an invalid first packet closes the file; truncated audio or metadata after a complete prefix stops validation at that prefix. f_107e1a88 bounds reads by remaining packet/file bytes, returns 2 on short fread, and reverses audio word byte order on this big-endian target. These details match audio_taps, not a separate compressed-block grammar.

Producer traced: f_107d8624 zeroes 48 bytes at stack+0x4c and writes version 1 at 0x107d8730-0x107d8740. Its clock-provider object +0x8d0 vtable+0x0c fills an eight-byte result copied into metadata offsets 1 and 5; the same pair is returned through the caller timestamp output. At 0x107d89e0-0x107d8a20 it sets sample count to (payload_bytes>>3)&0xffff and metadata+0x0b to TV processor +0xf1c. Playback compares that word with the current TV rate and logs the explicit sample-rate-mismatch diagnostic at 0x107d8838, proving it is sample rate rather than an unnamed counter. f_107dede8 copies the cached 24-byte block at processor+0x1a68 to metadata+0x0f. The error path ORs 0x80 into metadata+0x27 and invokes the writer with null audio and zero bytes at 0x107d8bd8-0x107d8bf8. Writer f_107e1720 copies and byte-reverses the scalar fields, writes exactly 48 metadata bytes via sink virtual+8, then, for non-null/nonzero audio, writes the word-byte-reversed payload through the same sink (0x107e1894-0x107e1a2c). Clock units/domain and cached status-byte meanings remain unresolved.

Compression boundary checked in f_103d1ca8: deflateInit2_ receives default level -1, method 8, windowBits 12, memLevel 5 and strategy 0, using zlib version 1.2.11. This is a zlib-wrapped DEFLATE stream, not gzip or an additional per-packet block schema. f_1034308c emits the <SPDIFTap> export wrapper and opens the file before using a 0x4000-byte file-reader buffer. That buffer size is not a fixed metadata section.

Bit-field audit with GNU e500 and the fixed repository listing: 0x107d89f0 is rlwinm r10,r5,29,16,31, equivalent to (payload_bytes>>3)&0xffff, not an unlimited-width quotient. Two byte stores at 0x107d8a18/0x107d8a1c serialize that sixteen-bit count. Reader 0x107e1420 shifts the reconstructed count left three and stores audio bytes remaining at +0x40; 0x107e147c tests metadata byte 0x27 with andi. 0x80. The count narrowing is explicit and shared with audio_taps; no oversized-payload acceptance or saturation is implied.

psk_hierarchy.name: 4-PSK household crypto hierarchy + rotation
psk_hierarchy.summary: Household-related PSKs are concrete0xb0-byte records containing an identifier,32 raw random key bytes and generation metadata, with current/backup pairs. Identifiers use sonos.<purpose>.1.<context>.<random suffix>. Diagnostic XML emits IDs, but the local netsettings.json writer also emits a transformed key field. The former opaque-keystore and IDs-only-everywhere claims are withdrawn; replication and inverse-loading joins remain unfinished.

evidence.notes: netsettings block

Alphabet-based8-character suffix;32-byte RNG destination record+81; genVersion+a4/+a8 and genTime+ac. snprintf operands purpose,1,context,suffix. Context owner+fd is copied from constructor arg r10 at0x10627e78, supplied via stack+154 at startup0x10199150. Purpose-specific calls and0xb0 record spacing at0x106280e8 onward. No context semantic label claimed.

ELF exported symbol bounds plus PPC objdump: ZZ0071 invokes mbedtls_ctr_drbg_random; ZZ0154 invokes alphabet-index helper ZZ0153, which requests RNG through ZZ0071. Existing anacapad imports at0x11098980/0x11098ee8 bind these symbols. This is direct random generation, not proof of derivation from another PSK.

Persistence reaches conditional current/backup record writer. It reads raw key+81 length20hex, Base64-encodes, invokes ZZ0197 at0x1062e798 with netsettings/key labels, formats version, then writes id,key,genVersion,genTime. Failure returns false before object emission. Diagnostic XML at0x1062a2a4 instead formats only identifier. Material transformation details and replication join remain explicitly unproven.

HH Base64 source owner+921 = record8a0+81; length20hex and error diagnostic at0x1062dd90. Rotation invokes generator for purpose control into temporary record at0x1062c47c, with separate failure/update handling. These paths contradict key-bytes-never-leave-record assertions but do not alone certify full replicated wire format.

todo: Established: exact generated identifier format, four purpose strings, in-process key/metadata layout, RNG boundary, ID-only diagnostic XML versus material-bearing local JSON, and concrete HH material encoding. Remaining: bind identifier context owner+0xfd back through constructor r10/startup0x10199150 to its semantic source; trace inverse key loading and ZZ0197/its decode counterpart, then join replication/netstartd serializers and receiving consumers for each current/backup pair. Start with f_1062e668, f_10630580, f_1062d948 and settings replication callbacks. Do not infer IDs-only replication or an opaque external key store from diagnostic XML. This is actionable static work.
resolved_findings: Generator f_10626df8 builds sonos.%s.%d.%s.%s from purpose r3, literal1, context r4 and an8-character random hexadecimal suffix. It requests8 characters from alphabet0123456789abcdef through ZZ0154 and32 random key bytes through ZZ0071 into record+0x81. Record+0 holds the identifier (bounded0x81-byte destination),+0xa4/+0xa8 hold generation-version words from f_1090b418 and+0xac holds generation time. A zero result from either random call or invalid generation-version state returns failure. Time uses time() with a lower bound0x6a8f3ce0; this is generation metadata, not evidence of expiration or periodic rotation.

Purpose literals are hh/control/roomenc/lanswap at calls0x106280f8/0x10628120/0x10628148/0x10628170. Current records are at netsettings-owner+0x8a0/+0xa00/+0xb60/+0xcc0, backups at the next0xb0-byte record. Context in this path is owner+0xfd, copied with bound0x21 from constructor f_10627da8 argument r10 at0x10627e78. Startup caller0x10199170 loads that argument from stack+0x154. Its earlier producer and semantic identity are not yet bound; it must not be guessed to be a household ID or a key-store handle.

Raw material is held in anacapad memory, not only behind a crypto key-store boundary. In the shipped libsonoscrypto.so.3, ZZ0071 at0x75c0 calls mbedtls_ctr_drbg_random at0x75ec; ZZ0154 at0x7780 calls ZZ0153, which also reaches ZZ0071. The four purpose strings select independent generator invocations, not a proven derivation chain from a registration-signing key. The earlier secure-registration/device-discovery/settings-auth consumer map is withdrawn; the registration JWT key has its separately traced lifecycle.

The identifiers-only claim conflated different outputs. Diagnostic XML f_1062a030 formats <HhPsk id="%s"/> and backup counterparts using record starts. In contrast persistence f_10627b14 calls JSON writer f_10630580 at0x10627c5c; its conditional PSK arms invoke f_1062e668. That helper reads32 bytes at record+0x81, Base64-encodes them, passes the result through ZZ0197 with netsettings/key context labels, then emits an object with id,key,genVersion,genTime. The key value is transformed material, not merely another identifier. The outer file path uses temporary-file writing and rename; transformation/Base64/version failures return failure rather than emitting a completed PSK object.

Concrete consumer preparation f_1062d948 separately Base64-encodes the HH key from owner+0x921 (=current HH record+0x81) at0x1062dd64 and has the Encoding DTLS HH PSK failed guard. This disproves an IDs-only handoff assumption, but the transport serializer and receivers still require a full join before claiming exactly which bytes replicate. Rotation f_1062c2cc invokes the same generator into temporary records and reports generation/settings-update failure paths; no fixed periodic rotation interval follows from these strings.

Reachable401 gate, nonempty service config, injected store slotsc/20, callback constructor and service call inspected. Missing account and false validation/reload branches disprove unconditional filename/token-use assumptions.

todo: Established: reachable401 refresh path, per-account synchronization, injected-store read/validation/reload slots and service-request callback, with missing-account/store-failure/transaction-timeout branches. Remaining: bind concrete writers of receiver+0x1208 to its store vtable+0xc/+0x20, follow the f_101b7cb4 callback back into persistence, and prove the exact base+accounts.xml composition/load/save path before assigning this file. Separately recover expiry/refresh-age producers rather than equating60000 transaction age with token lifetime. Start at0x1038eb24,0x1038edf8,0x1038f1bc and the service request constructor f_10723fbc. This remains actionable static work.
resolved_findings: The accounts.xml literal0x10eabd60 still does not establish a reachable filename-composition writer. The checked refresh path instead reaches an injected account-store interface at receiver+0x1208; filesystem-family conclusions must remain separate from binding this exact file.

Reachability is concrete: caller0x1038f8dc, after checking serialized request length against0x5fff, invokes response worker f_1038e82c. HTTP401 at0x1038e93c enters the account refresh path when receiver+0x11fc is nonnull and nonempty. It loads account data through receiver+0x1208 virtual+0xc, keyed by receiver+0x1200; missing accounts log Refresh token failed. Could not find account and leave without proving a file read.

Per-account refresh synchronization uses a shared serial-number keyed tree under its mutex. f_1038edc4 requests new token-refresh synchronization, while the wait arm at0x1038f058 handles an existing transaction; missing expected synchronization entries log and call RabortIfUnlocked. This is not evidence for one periodic, unconditional refresh timer.

For a new refresh,0x1038edf4 rotates/masks the account service identifier before store virtual+0x20, then f_101b7cb4 constructs a callback holding store pointer at+4 and that identifier at+8. f_10723fbc constructs the service request and f_10725488 invokes the credentials/SMAPI path through its virtual+8 specialization. Store failure branches to0x1038f4a4 before the request call.

After waiting,0x1038f1b0 again calls store virtual+0xc, tests success, and only then copies the loaded token via f_1056f07c and resets request state before receiver virtual+0x30. Failure branches to0x1038f244 rather than silently using a purported persisted token. This proves an injected-store reload/retry contract, not the accounts.xml path.

At0x1038f42c sonosClockGetTime(1) and timevalDiff compare elapsed time since the per-account entry timestamp against60000; an over-threshold branch reaches last refresh token for load timed out. This is a transaction-age decision, not proof of token expiry, a universal refresh cadence or a timer derived from account-store filename.
