Remaining: follow every direct caller of f_106420ec and any wrapper/indirect registration paths, bind each supplied table object to its constructor, per-counter initialization and export callback, and recover registration/teardown feature predicates. Start with0x10318ab4 (CHSRC),0x1044f970,0x1049b4bc,0x1051570c,0x1052e454 and0x107e3f70; use actual function boundaries and global0x110976ec consumers. Distinguish compiled counter definitions from optional runtime instances. The exhaustive census and per-type schemas remain actionable static work; runtime registration alone is not an external-data limitation.
resolved_findings: The perf_counter_table literal identifies a mutex/owner construction path, not an exhaustive emitted-counter registry. Manager constructor f_106418e0 initializes a named perfCountMgr lock and an empty index at manager+0x90; f_10641948 allocates it lazily and stores the pointer at global0x110976ec. Actual registration calls f_106420ec, not a literal name alone.

Resolved: counter families recovered as literal {name,description} pairs - eventloop: subject "In-Process Event Subjects" {queueFail="The number of events that failed to queue", size="The event size in bytes", dispatchDelay="The amount of time an event spent waiting to be dispatched"} + subject "In-Process Event Observers" {cbTime="The duration of observer handlers. Warn if over threshold (%lldms)"}; circuit-breaker: museCircuitBreaker {timeInOpenStateMS, circuitBreakerOpenedCount, totalFailures, totalSuccessfulRetries, totalFailedRetries}; worker-pool: {"The number of tasks actively being processed"=tasks, "The time spent in the main loop iteration"=loopIter} at 0x10f92ad8-0x10f92b1c. These literals describe candidate families, not a complete registered-instance census. Table-specific export callbacks must be traced before claiming a uniform field schema.

The counter header, timestamp, threshold and museperf literals provide concrete tracing anchors. The eventloop/circuit-breaker/worker-pool names are candidate compiled families, not a completed registration census or proof that every exporter emits one uniform schema.

Concrete compiled registration disproves the old runtime-data-only boundary. f_10317374 builds a CHSRC Fill Level table and frames counter using literal names, descriptions, static vtables and counter-state initialization; the path loads global0x110976ec at0x10318a80, skips registration if null, otherwise calls f_106420ec at0x10318ab4. Direct caller0x1025f530 reaches this constructor. Other direct registration calls include0x101a2e38,0x1044f970,0x1049b4bc,0x1051570c,0x1052e454,0x1052f968,0x10638b00 and0x107e3f70; they are concrete next tracing sites, not a verified total.

Registration f_106420ec locks the manager, hashes the supplied name with f_10806d50 and looks it up through f_10642bc0. A missing name creates a0x38-byte node containing a copied name and an empty per-name tree; an existing name reuses that node. It then indexes the supplied object pointer through the per-name tree. Thus one name need not identify one runtime instance, and counting distinct literals is not an instance census.

Export f_10642700 snapshots/traverses the manager index under the manager lock, releases it before table formatting, and invokes f_106419b0 for a table or an empty fallback name depending on formatter state. evidence.notes: xfade block

resolved_findings: Resolved: fade-sample loop = int16 crossfade {attempting underflowed stream, recovered, %zu samples, empty stream clearing, unknown stream type %d}; curve = linear int16 mix over the sample count.

Fade mechanics proven: crossfade runs per-frame over R_CrossfadeDuration-derived sample counts (crossfade %zu samples; crossfaded %zu bytes (%zu samples, %zu usec), %zu more samples to fade this frame - a per-frame ramp continuing across frames until the fade length elapses). Fade direction/state comes from control frames in the packet stream: crossfadeStateForPacketID() reads the packet's control frame {crossfade on, crossfade off - %u} with lookback when absent (lPacketNum-1 not found -> lPacketNum-2, no control frames found / no frames found). Edge handling: crossfade stream underflow, crossfade with empty stream, clearing crossfade, crossfade with underflowed stream - underflowed/empty inputs drop the fade rather than summing silence.

Resolved: R_CrossfadeDuration is a persisted KV (registry) setting, not a compile-time default - all three refs are reads through the settings object vfunc (get @vfunc+0xc into a 0x20-byte buf at 0x103f9084; restore-path read at 0x104b2144 inside f_104b1e48). No write/seed site exists in the image and no shipped localsettings JSON carries the key; when absent the restore path leaves the zeroed record (stb 0-init at 0x104b2108-0x104b212c), so duration=0 until a client writes it via SetCrossfadeMode. The state dump field <CurrentCrossfadeMode> and the 'Setting up for %d.%06d sec crossfade' log confirm the value is request-supplied.

Fade kernel shape narrowed: the int16-crossfade strings ARE live (loaded at 0x1033f25c/0x1033f26c inside f_1033f0f8, domain chsnk) - earlier unreferenced claim was wrong. The mix loop is pure SPE fixed-point (64 op4-major insns incl multiply-accumulate xo400 x19, xo384 x18; zero scalar-float ops and no gain LUT load) - consistent with a linear-ramp integer crossfade; equal-power/sqrt shaping is not evidenced in this build.

Ramp law proven linear: the mix kernel (f_1033f0f8 chsnk) computes the fade gain arithmetically - it loads float 1.0 (0x10e89bc8) as the fade ceiling, calls libm round() (0x1033f458) on the interpolated gain per block, then applies it via SPE fixed-point multiply-accumulate ops; no gain-table load or transcendental function exists in the loop, so the ramp is a computed linear interpolation not a LUT curve.

muse_events.name: muse event-type registry
muse_events.summary: Muse event names are selected through a bounded 73-row topic registry, distinct from schema/type indices and typed payload producers. Output supports already-built raw bodies and producer-based bodies, with a format-dependent common metadata wrapper. The complete topic-to-producer and body-field mapping remains unfinished.

evidence.notes: muse event types

Construction stores alarmVersionChange at row6+4 and type0x18 at row6+8, areasVersionChange at row7+4 with type0x22. f_109e12f8 compares unsigned topic to0x48 and returns row+8 using (index<<2)+(index<<4); invalid topic returns0 at 0x109e1328. f_109e1370 uses the same bound/stride and returns row+4. Big-endian pointer words 0x10f970f4 and 0x10f9711c both point to versionChanged literal0x10f976a4. Reverse lookup f_109e13b0 bounds type<=0x147 then indexes table0x10f95bc0; it is not another topic-name array.

Dispatch compares event+0xc at 0x109e98d0; zero calls0x109f6fb0, nonzero0x109f6d7c. Typed adapter at 0x109f6fb4-0x109f6fc4 passes event+20 header, event+cc metadata and producer loaded from event+4 to f_109f6f0c. f_109f6f40 starts object; null-producer gate0x109f6f44-0x109f6f48 skips callback; otherwise invokes its vtable+8 at0x109f6f64, writer flag loaded at0x109f6f54. End-object0x109f6f6c and writer completion0x109f6f90 follow.

Raw pointer/length loaded event+8/+c at0x109f6dd0/0x109f6dd8. Nonzero null length/pointer guard at0x109f6eec-0x109f6efc throws basic_string construction error; non-null data copied then writer virtual+8 at0x109f6e30. Format4/5 detection uses unsigned (format-4)<=1 at0x109f6db0-0x109f6dc4; analogous typed gate0x109f6f28-0x109f6f38. Common envelope field bindings include namespace0x109f6c0c, response0x109f6c40, success0x109f6c54, type0x109f6c70, cmdId0x109f6c8c, async0x109f6cac, apiVersion0x109f6cf0 and event name0x109f6d18.

todo: Established: the bounded topic registry, separate topic/schema ID spaces, example versionChanged mappings, actual raw-versus-typed sender dispatch, null/empty behavior and common-envelope boundary. Remaining: join every topic row to its concrete event construction call, event+4 producer class or event+8/+0xc raw-body writer, then recover body member types, emission predicates and failure behavior. Start with alarmVersionChange topic6/type0x18 and areasVersionChange topic7/type0x22, follow header type assignments through f_109e8780 and the reverse type->topic lookup f_109e13b0, then bind producer virtual+8 at 0x109f6f64. Registry names and plausible owning subsystems alone do not establish these schemas; this remains actionable static work, not an external-schema limitation.
resolved_findings: The event registry is not an emitter census. Initializer f_10098d34 writes 20-byte records at 0x110b8ce8; f_109e12f8/f_109e1334/f_109e1370 bound topic indices to 0..0x48 and compute index*20. Row+4 is the event-name pointer; row+8 is a separate schema/type index. For example topic6 alarmVersionChange maps to type0x18, topic7 areasVersionChange maps to type0x22, and topic0x2f playbackStatus maps to type0xb8. The schema-name table at 0x10f97094 names both type0x18 and type0x22 versionChanged. Identical schema-name text therefore does not make the two topic IDs or their implementation bindings interchangeable. The older approximate event count and blanket owner/emitter assignments are not a verified per-event binding census.

Concrete send path: f_106c2818 creates a writer and invokes f_109e98c4 at 0x106c2888. The dispatcher tests event+0xc: nonzero selects raw serialization f_109f6d7c; zero selects f_109f6fb0, which loads the producer pointer from event+4 and tail-calls f_109f6f0c. The latter starts an object, calls producer virtual+8 with the writer and writer flag +0x1040 when a producer exists, and ends the object. A null typed producer skips that callback, leaving an empty object. Thus the body producer and its member predicates are recoverable code, not necessarily an out-of-image Muse contract.

Raw bodies use event+8 as pointer and event+0xc as explicit byte length. f_109f6d7c constructs a string of that exact length and forwards it through writer virtual+8, rather than enumerating topic-specific members. A null pointer with nonzero length takes the basic_string null-not-valid exception at 0x109f6ef4-0x109f6efc. The public dispatch chooses this path only for nonzero length; zero length instead takes the typed path. Do not infer that an empty raw body proves a successfully emitted empty JSON object.

Formats4/5 add a shared array/header envelope through f_109f6d2c before either body representation. f_109f6bc4 emits namespace/addressing metadata when resolved, optional apiVersion, event name or response/success, type, optional cmdId and conditional async. These are envelope fields, not proof that every event body contains them. Both raw/typed paths finish writer state and return its status; reaching the sender is not proof that a producer populated every field or that the remote subscriber accepted the event.

circuit_breaker.name: circuit breaker FSM
circuit_breaker.summary: Shared circuit breaker for the UCS and Thor outbound clients: stop new attempts after six failures in two minutes, reopen after 30 seconds, and let a successful result clear the failure history.

evidence.notes: Constructor layout and CLOSED initialization
UCS literal 6/2/30000/1/120000 constructor arguments
Thor same literal configuration; r28 producer is constant 1
Unsigned history_count >= threshold trip predicate; retain equality in window
Failed-retry count >= +0x24 enables normal trip check
Hold milliseconds multiplied by 1000000 before addition to monotonic ns clock
cntlzw/rlwinm returns state==0, OPEN means blocked
Interval accumulation and clearing of last-open stamp
UCS success is response status >0, independent of HTTP 2xx
Thor outcome producer uses response status >0
Per-field telemetry producer/label binding and ms conversion; totalSuccessfulRetries labels the SEMI_OPEN-transition counter

resolved_findings: Uses the fully decoded shared_primitives.circuitbreaker engine. Both ucs and thor instances have six-failure/two-minute windows, 30-second open holds, and a two-failed-retry threshold. Failure count equality trips; a reported success clears history. State polling performs timed reopening; no timer callback exists.

UCS outcome at 0x104d0f8c is HTTP response code >0, so an HTTP error response can count as a successful connection. Thor reports at 0x105fc7a4 and 0x105ff0bc likewise use response status >0; applicability is additionally conditioned on the request bookkeeping check at 0x105fc33c. Gate callers 0x104cf450 and 0x105fcb90 treat returned 1 as OPEN/blocked. This primitive has no SOAP fault number or wire parser; callers choose their own failure mapping.

Publisher0x106cc7e0 binds snapshot+0x00 to circuitBreakerOpenedCount, +0x08 i64 ns divided by1000000 to timeInOpenStateMS, +0x10 to totalFailures, +0x14 to totalSuccessfulRetries, and +0x18 to totalFailedRetries (GOT literals0x10f07da4..0x10f07dfc). These are wire labels: underlying breaker+0x134 increments on OPEN->SEMI_OPEN, not on a successful report; breaker+0x138 has no increment writer in the engine. totalFailures includes folded failed-retry counts in addition to one per failed report. Publisher resets only its snapshot with0x109d9704, not the breaker counters.

Key ownership and transport: anacapad f_1064bc38 accepts a 32-byte buffer followed by a big-endian u32 length, rejects lengths above 32, wipes the previous buffer, copies a nonempty replacement into owner+0x154 and records length at +0x174 under the registration mutex. Length zero clears it. The concrete IPC type 0x34 reaches this setter at 0x106913dc after a payload-length check. f_1064b9f4 returns a mutex-protected copy. netstartd supplies the matching 36-byte payload through f_1000ac9c and f_10006b2c on /tmp/netstartd.ipc; its callback is installed at configuration+0x8c during main initialization.

Key generation and persistence: netstartd f_1001bcd0 checks household/registration state, backs up owner+0x110, and calls f_10027004 to obtain 32 bytes through libsonoscrypto ZZ0071 and mbedtls_ctr_drbg_random. It persists the changed internal settings before publishing the key through callback+0x8c; persistence failure restores the backup. f_10022074 writes RegSigningKey as uppercase hexadecimal, two digits per byte, in netstart2.txt beneath configuration+8. It writes a .tmp file, flushes/closes it and renames it. Main builds that configured directory with %s/net/settings; /jffs is the initial root, not an assertion that every invocation uses an immutable absolute path. Runtime random bytes are not a compiled secret or an OAuth endpoint string.

Persistent-key reader binding: startup f_1001eb64 calls f_100223ac with owner+0x5c settings. That reader opens the same configured netstart2.txt and passes f_10020f68 to the line parser f_100224ec. The RegSigningKey comparison selects settings+0xb4, exactly owner+0x110, and f_10026f58 accepts only a successfully decoded 32-byte value. The shared decoder requires an even number of hexadecimal characters and checks each pair before base-16 conversion. Thus a generated 32-byte key round-trips as 64 hexadecimal characters, not Base64.

Registration-message mapping follows executed code: f_10028ddc reads the first input byte unchanged and accepts values through 0x17. The f_1001f820 switch sends byte 0x16 to f_1002d22c, which checks that same value before calling key generation at 0x1001f9c8. The response builder f_1002d2c4 supplies 0x17 to f_1002e690, which writes it unchanged as the first output byte, followed by the key field serialized through f_1002eb84. This differs from the adjacent name/id table, whose LOCK_REGISTRATION row contains 0x17 and REGISTRATION_KEY row contains zero. Those labels must not replace the actual request/response dispatch values; no invented translation from 0x17 to 0x16 is involved.

Invalidation is event-driven on the traced path: netstartd IPC type 0x18 reads the secure-registration flag and calls f_10020d9c at 0x10008c68. A nonzero flag sets owner+0x1ac and, when a key is present, publishes a null/zero replacement, wipes owner+0x110, and persists settings. This path has no periodic key-rotation interval. It does not establish the timing of the external registration event or prove that all other key replacements have been enumerated.

Expiry/provider boundary: f_109f86bc constructs an RS256 header, obtains time representations through owner+0xb8 virtual slots +8 and +0x10, and performs literal 3600 additions at 0x109f89f0 and 0x109f8a74. The second representation is serialized through provider slot +0x14 before and after addition. A failed optional time read selects error paths rather than a default lifetime. Signing uses owner+0xb0 through f_109f3f9c/f_109f3bb4, a SHA-256 digest and provider virtual slot +0x14 at 0x109f3d24. Constructor f_109f7d30 stores these providers from its r5/r7 inputs; the player setup call at 0x1019abcc supplies player+0xc7c and player+0x56c0. These are token-building arithmetic and provider boundaries, not evidence of symmetric-key rotation or account refresh scheduling.

muse_verbs.name: Muse verb vocabulary and generated command dispatch
muse_verbs.summary: Muse verb strings include executable per-namespace command factories, URI/CSV metadata, schema field names and a separate static namespace/name-pair list. These must not be conflated into a global bound/unbound census. Concrete alarms, areas and zones command switches are compiled in anacapad; the complete namespace/verb/implementation join remains unfinished.

evidence.notes: verb table

Decoded every big-endian word from0x110941d4 through0x110943f0 in pairs:68 rows,136 valid namespace/name string pointers. All rows are stride8, not alternating stride12 descriptors. Last namespace at0x110943ec zones and name0x110943f0 unjoinZone; next0x110943f4 is0xffffffff. .got2 slot0x1108de34 contains pointer0x110941d4; consumer role not inferred from its mere presence.

Static words at vtable+18/+1c/+20 point0x10ac9fc4/0x10acc504/0x10acc4f4. Selector stack rows+1c..+4b store subscribe/unsubscribe/getAreas/createArea/updateArea/removeArea literals at0x10aca02c-0x10aca064 and factories0x10aca070-0x10aca0ac. Loop strcmp0x10aca0bc, stride8 at0x10aca0c8, exhausted return0 at0x10aca0d4. Match calls row+4 at0x10aca130 and replaces namespace+38 at0x10aca144.

Stack rows+14..+8b contain15 names initialized0x10b8c024-0x10b8c0d4 and factories0x10b8c0e0-0x10b8c188. Includes unjoinZone literal reference0x10b8c0d0 and factoryf_10b8f1a4 at0x10b8c184/188. strcmp0x10b8c198 advances8; match loads row+4, namespace+4 at0x10b8c1fc, calls0x10b8c20c and stores namespace+38 at0x10b8c220. Old-command virtual+4 release0x10b8c234; missing name returns0 on exhausted loop. These are code pointers and execution branches, unlike the static string-pair list.

todo: Established: the 68-row static list is only string pairs, while alarms (8), areas (6) and zones (15) have verified executable namespace-local factory rows. Remaining: enumerate all namespace vtables and +0x18 selectors, recover each bounded {verb,factory} set and concrete implementation injection, and reconcile that executable census with route/CSV metadata and schema names without publishing unverified global counts. Also bind the consumer of .got2 slot 0x1108de34 pointing to static list 0x110941d4 before assigning that list a policy/registration role. Start from areas vtable 0x10fa00ac/f_10ac9fc4 and repeat the command-factory method for authorization, audioClip and other namespace classes. This is actionable static work, not evidence that cloud verbs exist only in route metadata.
resolved_findings: Corrected static-list layout: 0x110941d4..0x110943f3 contains exactly 68 consecutive 8-byte {namespace-string pointer, name-string pointer} pairs, all checked as strings. Its following word at 0x110943f4 is 0xffffffff, not a third-column dispatch pointer. The first pairs are authorization/resolveToken, authorization/getPolicyKey and authorization/getPermissions; the final pair is zones/unjoinZone. The previous alternating 12-byte nsCtx/verbSpec interpretation is false. Namespace literals were misidentified as context objects. No function/descriptor column exists in these pair rows, so membership does not prove executable binding.

Actual dispatch exists outside that static list. Areas vtable 0x10fa00ac has +0x18=f_10ac9fc4, +0x1c=f_10acc504 (areas getter) and +0x20=f_10acc4f4 (current command). f_10ac9fc4 builds six stride-8 {verb,factory} rows: subscribe->f_10aca364, unsubscribe->f_10aca4a0, getAreas->f_10aca5e0, createArea->f_10acc128, updateArea->f_10acc434 and removeArea->f_10acaa04. It strcmp-matches command-info+0x26, invokes the matching factory, and stores its result at namespace+0x38. An exhausted search returns null. Thus areas is not merely an unbound cloud-route declaration.

Zones selector f_10b8bfc8 builds fifteen actual command-factory rows: subscribe, unsubscribe, getActiveZoneList, getZoneDefinition, getZoneDefinitionList, addZoneDefinition, addMissingZoneDefinition, updateZoneDefinition, updateActiveZone, updateZoneMemberSettings, removeZoneDefinition, activateZone, deactivateZone, joinZone and unjoinZone. strcmp at 0x10b8c198 advances by8; a match calls the row factory at 0x10b8c20c with namespace+4 implementation/context, replaces namespace+0x38 and releases the old command. Missing-name and missing-implementation cases are separate from presence in a static string list.

Alarms supplies a second namespace absent from the claimed static binding list: f_10ac47ac has eight executable rows including subscribe/unsubscribe and six alarm operations. These selectors demonstrate a repeatable census method: follow each namespace vtable +0x18 to its bounded factory rows, then join their command descriptors and injected implementation pointers. Schema-name/type registries are different structures; their null fields are not proof that a command is unbound. The old 237/265 bound ratio and 242 verbs/112 namespaces are withdrawn as certified dispatch totals. The old zero-reference route-block argument also does not establish absence of generated code or an external runtime-only binding limitation.

cert_files.name: device cert file layout

evidence.notes: cert files
Certificate XML encryption-key-type is parsed numerically into output+0x2000.
Shipped CBC implementation; decrypt block XOR and IV chaining at 0xe784-0xe830. Certificate consumer connection unverified.

todo: Residual: trace the numeric encryption-key-type stored by the certificate-file XML parser through its actual private-key consumer to mode/IV selection. A shipped CBC implementation is now positively located, so absence of a direct CBC import cannot justify declaring the certificate path ECB-only. The separate sonoscp_crypto ECB helper does not bind this file-format field.
resolved_findings: Resolved: on-disk format = %s/%s.%s files with keys {encrypted-private-key,expiration,encryption-key-type,sonos-key-and-cert} + failed-to-retrieve-key error path.

Format proven: PEM - both -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- literals are in the image, plus public key hash: sha256//%s (HPKP-style pin format) and DH signature params {dh(g), dh(pub_key), Signature}. cert.xml stores <DeviceCertInfo>; the X-Sonos-DeviceCert header carries the device cert on requests. Cert health states {DeviceCertRequired, DeviceCertInvalid, DeviceCertExpired, DeviceCertRevoked} gate the refresh job (Unknown cert metadata state: %s. Scheduling cert refresh job; %zu consecutive cert fetch failures. Trying again in %ld seconds). Trust roots ship as /certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb via libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2; validation via libsonos-certval.so.2; fetchRegDeviceCert/refreshRegDeviceCert are the fetch verbs; NewCertRegistrationEvent fires on registration.

Decrypt primitives decoded in libsonoscrypto: ZZ0024 (0x3a48) = aes_init + mbedtls_aes_setkey_dec(ctx, key, keybytes*8) with a keybits sanity bound (<0x20000000), ZZ0025 on failure; ZZ0023 (0x3a24) = mbedtls_aes_crypt_ecb block-decrypt wrapper (mode forced to DECRYPT, 16B in->out). The encrypted-private-key is therefore decrypted with the stored key bytes used directly - there is no KDF step between the 'privateKey' field and mbedtls_aes_setkey_dec; the key IS raw AES key material. ZZ0023/24 are called from 4 sites (0x103eb104/0x104ccdf0/0x1050a174 scp cipher paths + 0x10716e60/0x10716e7c sonoscp_crypto unpack), confirming the shared AES-block engine.

Certificate parser corrected at instruction level: f_10bb95f8 compares encryption-key-type at 0x10bb96c4-0x10bb96d8, then invokes paranoid_atoi(text,output+0x2000) at 0x10bb96dc-0x10bb96e8. Expiration is independently parsed by paranoid_strtoull into output+0x2008 at 0x10bb9770-0x10bb977c. Thus this XML metadata field is numeric, not a demonstrated AES-CBC/AES-ECB string enum. The sonoscp_crypto privateKey/type code and its raw ECB loop f_10716e2c belong to a separate parser; adjacency of strings does not link them to this certificate-file consumer.

Counterexample to the previous shipped-CBC-absence claim: lib/libmbedcrypto.so.16 exports mbedtls_aes_crypt_cbc at relative VA 0xe680, size 0x2f8. Its decrypt branch (mode=0) preserves the incoming ciphertext block, invokes mbedtls_aes_crypt_ecb at 0xe778, XORs all sixteen plaintext bytes with the IV at 0xe784-0xe7a4, updates the IV with saved ciphertext at 0xe7a8-0xe830 and repeats. It accepts empty input, rejects non-block-multiple length at 0xe6c8-0xe6cc, and has a separate encrypt branch at 0xe87c. This proves CBC is implemented in a shipped artifact, not that a particular certificate file reaches it. libsonoscrypto imports the generic mbedtls_cipher_setup/setkey/set_iv/update API, so searching only direct imports of mbedtls_aes_crypt_cbc cannot establish mode reachability. The actual certificate numeric-key-type dispatch is still unresolved.

eventloop_perf.name: inprocess eventloop + perf counters
eventloop_perf.summary: Measures event queue failures, sizes, queue delay and observer execution time. Callbacks taking more than 100 ms produce diagnostics; warning logs are throttled for each observer.

evidence.notes: Duration checker: strict >100000us, 600-second warning throttle, per-occurrence report.
Warning string loaded through GOT2 0x1108d768; RHS is immediate 100.
Counter registration and description format with immediate 100ms.
cbTime name and adjoining duration description.

resolved_findings: Callback checker 0x10bbb374 reads signed high word and unsigned low word of a 64-bit microsecond duration. It returns zero for negative durations or 0..100000 us, including exactly 100 ms; positive high words or low word >=100001 trigger slow-handler handling. Conversion 0x10982360 divides the duration by 1000 for the displayed integer milliseconds. A handler of 100001 us therefore exceeds the test but can print 100ms > 100ms after truncation. This is a code constant, not a registration-supplied threshold.

0x10bbb374 gets clock-id1 time, checks the observer counter-state timestamp at *(observer+0x30)+0x38, and logs on first occurrence (timestamp zero) or elapsed seconds >600. It stores current seconds before checking whether the log domain is enabled. The callback/event name and observer name come from observer descriptor +0x18 and +0. Return1 means the duration exceeded the threshold even when the log was suppressed; it does not abort or undo the observer callback.

Every over-threshold call, including warning-throttled calls, builds the report through 0x10c5c2f4, supplies observer/event identity through report vtable+8, duration through +0xc, and submits through +0x14. The report object is deleted through +4 afterwards.

0x10bbbaf8 constructs subject and observer counter groups, including queueFail, event size, dispatchDelay and cbTime. At the cbTime description construction it formats the same literal 64-bit 100 milliseconds into The duration of observer handlers. Warn if over threshold (...ms). This describes the hardcoded callback checker; no threshold attribute is read by 0x10bbb374.

ir_watcher_binding.timeout_constant: Main .dynsym names0x1109b008 as timevalInf,size8,and .rela.dyn contains R_PPC_COPY(type19). The defining symbol in libsonos-time-c.so.1 at0x20018 holds{2147483647,0}. These are not uninitialized zero globals or a periodic IR polling interval.
ir_watcher_binding.close: Decoder destructor0x10244fd0 closes a nonnull HAL handle at0x10245028. HAL0x10b8 validates marker5,closes the fd,frees the16-byte handle and clears the caller pointer. The live parent stop and shared-reference disposal chains are bound in live_parent_lifetime; neither executes the compiled unregister helper. Joining the selector and closing the IR device are separate operations.

live_parent_lifetime.parent: The player owns IR/TV parent pointer at player+0x3d508 and shared-reference control at+0x3d50c. Allocation0x1018f5c4 reserves0x55118 bytes;0x1018f6b0 stores the parent pointer. Decoder primary is parent+0x218; its select slice is parent+0x220. Live start0x1019c2a0 loads this parent and0x1019c2a4 passes r21=player+0x4d8 to0x1024369c,which starts/registers the decoder at0x102436e0.
live_parent_lifetime.stop: Player stop0x10193860 loads the same parent and0x10193864 calls0x10243424. Its recovered body removes the TVSignalDetectedEvent observer from an in-process event registry; it does not access the embedded decoder,call0x10245170 or invoke the decoder's select owner. Player stop subsequently invokes selector.stop at0x10193884,whose started branch joins the event thread. This stops callback execution but leaves the IR registration/owner in the registry.
live_parent_lifetime.destruction: Player destructor0x101928a4 loads the parent shared-reference control and0x101928b0 releases it. Shared release0x100c5050 invokes control slot+8 on final strong release. Control vtable0x10e988e8 has slot+8=0x101b43ec; it loads parent at control+0x10 and reaches decoder destructor at0x101b443c. Direct parent destructors also call it at0x101b3ff8/0x101b40c4. Decoder destructor0x10244fd0 calls hal_ir_close at0x10245028 and contains no owner-unregister operation. The selector embedded in player+0x3a8 is destroyed later through0x10192dc8 ->0x10692d10 ->0x106930f8. Retaining another strong parent reference can defer parent/decoder destruction; release of the player's reference is not an unconditional immediate device close.
live_parent_lifetime.uncalled_helper: The compiled unregister helper0x10245170 loads decoder.primary+0x10 owner and tail-calls owner slot+c with primary+8. Whole-text direct,conditional and tail branch census found no caller. The exact function-address word has zero occurrences in the complete ELF,so no literal pointer table or GOT entry supplies an indirect caller either. The live parent stop and destructors were separately inspected to rule out treating that unused helper as their delegate.
live_parent_lifetime.contract: The recovered lifecycle does not automatically unregister IR before closing its device. The explicit player stop path joins the shared event thread; parent destruction closes the device on final reference disposal. Decoder destruction itself does not check whether the selector was already stopped. There is no claim that arbitrary destruction/restart ordering is safe,or that an external caller invokes the unused unregister helper. This is an established lack of enforced unregister-before-close behavior,not a missing per-class fd producer.

arp_cache_watcher_binding.name: ArpChecker
arp_cache_watcher_binding.getter: slot+0xc=0x105845e8 reads checker+0x104 under mutex. This is a local pipe read end,not the socket used to query ARP.

arp_cache_watcher_binding.producer: Setup0x1058481c obtains the current interface name into+0x111 and local address+0xfc through0x100a8580. It reads retrans_time_ms or legacy retrans_time from /proc/sys/net/ipv4/neigh/<interface>/...,converts legacy ticks using sysconf(2),reads mcast_solicit,and stores checkDelayMs=retransMs*mcastSolicit+500 at+0x100. pipe() at0x10584a38 creates two fds; fcntl(F_SETFL=4,0x800) makes both ends nonblocking. Failed pipe/fcntl setup returns failure and closes newly created ends.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.descriptor_change: Successful setup closes the previous write end if valid and installs the new write fd at+0x108. When no read fd is installed,it stores the new read end at+0x104. Otherwise it closes any older pending read end,stores the replacement at+0x10c and sets resetRequested+4=1. Reset callback+0x28=0x105844d0 closes the old+0x104,promotes+0x10c and clears pending/reset. Thus descriptor replacement occurs in the select reset phase after old-watch removal,not silently in a data callback.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.registration: Live player startup0x101988c0 initializes checker at player+0xa90,then0x101988cc registers it through0x10584b78 using player+0x4d8 select thread. Registration tail-calls supplied interface slot+8. Stop0x101937e0 calls0x10584ba0,whose tail-call invokes retained owner slot+0xc.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.read_and_timer: Request path0x105850dc can track a target IPv4 among four entries and writes one NUL byte to pipeWrite+0x108 at0x10585254. Read-ready slot+0x18=0x10584650 reads one byte from pipeRead then returns timeout checkDelayMs/1000 seconds and(checkDelayMs%1000)*1000 usec. It does not parse an ARP frame from the pipe; even a logged read error reaches the timeout calculation. Timeout slot+0x1c=0x105856d8 semantically tail-delegates0x105853b0,which checks tracked entries against the kernel ARP cache.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.temporary_query_socket: Helper0x10584d98 opens socket(AF_INET=2,SOCK_DGRAM=2,protocol0),fills an arpreq for the target and configured interface,performs ioctl SIOCGARP0x8954,copies returned flags and closes this temporary fd before returning. Consumers test flag0x2 (complete/resolved) at0x10585224. The helper socket never becomes checker+0x104 and is not the descriptor registered with epoll.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.close: Destructor0x10584430 closes retained read and write ends when opened+0x110 is set. The live stop call unregisters before object destruction; rebuild also handles the previous write end and pending read replacement.
arp_cache_watcher_binding.meaning: A local wakeup pipe coordinates delayed inspections of kernel neighbor-resolution state. It is distinct from ARPingManager,which sends and validates raw ARP frames.

Registration therefore is not evidence that all subscriptions succeeded. The null-socket failure path is not a documented safe -1 fd fallback; no runtime crash or recovery behavior is asserted.

hardware_watcher_binding.meaning: The event thread waits on a kernel-to-user hardware-notification subscription. Physical button and sensor notifications arrive through the same subscribed connection that was created during handler construction. Unregistering stops delivery to the select callback; destroying the connection closes the underlying socket.

Both use getter+c=0x10555094 (reads socket+0x14),label+8=0x105550a4 (table0x110925c8),data+0x18=0x10555a54,timeout+0x1c=0x10c5d128,exception predicate+0x24=0x10556b48 (stored errno+0x2c),reset+0x28=0x105550b8. Their setup slot+0x2c differs:0x10555278 versus0x105554dc.
discovery_watcher_binding.unicast_producer: Setup0x10555278 opens socket(AF_INET=2,SOCK_DGRAM=2,protocol0) at0x105552ac and stores fd+0x14. It calls fcntl F_GETFL=3 then F_SETFL=4 with flags|0x800 for nonblocking I/O. bind0x10555314 uses16-byte sockaddr_in {family2,port0x076d=1901,address0},so it binds all local IPv4 addresses on port1901. It sets IP_MULTICAST_TTL (level0,option0x21) to one-byte4,then requires a firmware SOL_SOCKET option0x29 with four-byte value8 to succeed. Failure returns0; success returns1. No multicast-membership call occurs in this unicast setup.
discovery_watcher_binding.multicast_producer: Setup0x105554dc opens the same socket family/type at0x10555510,sets nonblocking,reuse-address (level1,option2,value1) and IPv4 packet-info delivery (level0,option8,value1). bind0x105555c4 uses wildcard IPv4 port0x076c=1900. It requires the same SOL_SOCKET option0x29,value8,then invokes0x10555400 to join239.255.255.250 with interface address0 via IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP (level0,option0x23,8-byte ip_mreq). A successful join returns1. For a failed join whose errno is exactly0x62=98,the helper attempts IP_DROP_MEMBERSHIP (option0x24),ignores that result and retries ADD once; the retry result is converted to1 for nonnegative and0 for negative. Other join errors return0 directly. Option0x29 is documented numerically because its kernel-side interpretation has not been established here; its failure is a concrete setup rejection,not an optional optimization.
discovery_watcher_binding.live_registration_and_stop: Live startup calls the unicast and multicast setups at0x10199864 and0x1019988c,then registers both at0x10199884 and0x101998b0 through0x10555824. r21 is player+0x4d8,established at0x101988b4 and retained through both calls. Register helper null-checks the supplied select interface and semantically tail-calls its slot+8 with watcher and null optional timeout. The startup block does not branch on either setup result. Live stop0x10193874/0x1019387c calls0x10555858 for each watcher; that helper uses retained owner+8 and tail-calls slot+0xc. The player then stops the select thread at0x10193884. Destruction0x10192c00/0x10192c14 closes retained sockets through0x10555770,whose close is also a semantic tail call.
discovery_watcher_binding.reset_and_failures: Reset0x105550b8 closes old socket+0x14 when it is not-1,then calls the concrete setup slot+0x2c. It stores (setupResult^1)&0xff into reset byte+4; raw0x5463063e at0x10555104 is a low-byte mask,not an8-bit shift. On success,last-failure-log seconds+0x18 is cleared. On failure,the code compares lastLog+3600 against clock-id1 seconds and logs only if lastLog+3600<now; equality suppresses the log. This comparison throttles failure logs,not socket-retry scheduling. Independently of whether a log is emitted,a newly allocated failed fd is closed and+0x14 is set-1 at0x10555170..0x10555184. Direct setup calls return failure without doing this close themselves; their live startup callers still register the watcher.
discovery_watcher_binding.read_and_timeout: Data callback0x10555a54 sets its optional timeout output to{INT_MAX,0},reads one datagram via recvmsg0x10555b4c with payload capacity0x7ff and24-byte ancillary-control capacity,then enters the discovery parser. Stored errno+0x2c is cleared before the read. A-1 socket getter sets it to9 at0x10556008; a negative recvmsg result stores actual errno at0x10556018. The timeout slot0x10c5d128 also returns{INT_MAX,0}; neither constant creates a periodic discovery-socket poll. The multicast socket requests IP_PKTINFO,which the data path identifies using cmsg level0,type8 and reads the destination IPv4 at cmsg+0x14. Parser/signing semantics are separate from this descriptor ownership trace.
discovery_watcher_binding.meaning: Unicast discovery and multicast announcements are independent registered UDP inputs. Socket setup success,multicast subscription success and select-thread registration are distinct outcomes. Watch removal occurs before select-thread stop; connection reset and later object destruction own descriptor closure.

track_monitor_watcher_binding.meaning: Playback records are processed periodically by a timer registered with the shared event thread. The registry uses the same callback interface for I/O watchers and timer-only users; a handler name in the registry is not evidence of a corresponding network or device descriptor.

That constructor creates selector at owner+0x130=player+0x4d8 and concrete IPC handler at owner+0x518=player+0x8c0;0x1069204c installs this vtable. These sums join the concrete vtable to the live startup/shutdown receiver.
ipc_watcher_binding.producer: Connect helper0x105d33a4 closes the previous context when fd is not-1,then0x105d3410 calls InitializeIPCContext(context=handler+0x11c,role=2,path). libsonosutils.so.1:0x1264 stores role at context+0x74,fd=-1 at+0x70,clears110-byte sockaddr_un,requires nonnull path and length<=107,opens socket(AF_UNIX=1,SOCK_STREAM=1,protocol0) at0x12c4,and stores fd at+0x70. It obtains fcntl F_GETFL flags and uses F_SETFL flags|0x800 for nonblocking I/O. Family1 is written at sockaddr+0; path is copied at+2 with108-byte capacity. Role2 takes connect(fd,sockaddr_un,110) at0x1338 and requires return0; it does not accept a deferred connect result as success.
ipc_watcher_binding.context_error_and_close: InitializeIPCContext returns0 on success. Proven error returns: null context-1,unsupported role-2,null/too-long path-3,socket failure-4,bind failure-5,listen failure-6,connect failure-7,F_SETFL failure-11. Bind/listen arms belong to role1 and are not the watcher's role2 producer. Each nonnull-context failure reaches CloseIPCContext through0x136c. libsonosutils0x11e8 closes a nonnegative context fd at0x1210,stores-1 at+0x70,and clears role+0x74. It unlinks the stored local path only for role1; role2 client cleanup does not unlink the daemon's socket path. The library has conditional bclr guards at entry; disassembler blr text must not be interpreted as unconditional early return.
ipc_watcher_binding.live_start: Player startup0x101998bc computes handler=player+0x8c0 and0x101998c0 stores it at sp+0x58.0x101998c8 reloads this receiver,0x101998cc supplies select interface r21=player+0x4d8,and0x101998d0 supplies notification/context pointer player+0x3b8 before0x101998d4 calls0x105d364c. That wrapper supplies /tmp/netstartd.ipc and hello-enabled1,then tail-calls0x105d3574,which connects and registers with the connect-produced timeout. Connection failure does not suppress registration.
ipc_watcher_binding.connection_and_timer: Connect helper0x105d33a4 returns timeout{5,0} on InitializeIPCContext error and{60,0} on success. Successful connection clears retry count+0x194 and,when requested,tail-calls hello slot+0x40 (concrete0x105d3d0c). Timeout0x105d3874 initially writes{60,0}; if retained fd is-1,it increments retry count+0x194 and invokes reconnect helper0x105d3770. Registered reconnect sets reset byte+4=1 and saves desired timeout at+0x19c/+0x1a0; with no owner,it immediately tail-calls the connect helper. Reset callback0x105d36bc reconnects using the saved timeout storage then clears reset byte+4. Thus changing the socket is deferred to the selector reset phase when registered.
ipc_watcher_binding.meaning: This is the local stream connection by which the player communicates with the network-start daemon. Failed connection setup produces a disconnected descriptor and a short retry delay,while successful setup produces a longer maintenance timeout. The framed-message parser and daemon-specific message semantics are distinct from the watched descriptor ownership.
ipc_watcher_binding.live_shutdown: Actual player cleanup0x1019487c computes the same receiver player+0x8c0 and0x10194880 calls0x105d3088. That helper locks receiver mutex+0x88 and invokes receiver virtual slot+0x3c at0x105d30c4. The concrete close implementation0x105d3234 sends the goodbye through slot+0x44,then semantically tail-calls0x105d3164 at0x105d3284.0x105d3164 temporarily unlocks the mutex,calls retained select owner+8,slot+0xc,with the handler at0x105d31bc,relocks and calls CloseIPCContext at0x105d31d4. The matched player+0x8c0 startup/shutdown pair now binds the live close route; the unregister call is attempted before the context fd is closed; its return is ignored. The dispatcher is the handler's local lifecycle interface,not the protected SOAP request interface. Selector.unregister rejects stopRequested!=0 at0x10c5dcd4 without clearing registry/owner. Consequently a close after selector stop can retain the table entry while still closing the context. The established ordering is request-unregister then close,not unconditional successful removal.

engine.interface_and_storage: Constructor0x10c5d900 installs interface vtable0x1108b3a0. Slots: destructor0x10c5d158,delete0x10c5d1d4,register+8=0x10c5d20c,unregister+c=0x10c5dc6c,start+0x10=0x10c5d3a8,stop+0x14=0x10c5d4b8,post-timeout-update+0x18=0x10c5da50. Object size0x3e8. Nineteen handlers at+4+i*4,labels+0x50+i*4,relative remaining timevals+0x9c+i*8. Epoll fd wrapper+0x134,RThread+0x138,registry mutex+0x1d8,started byte+0x268,stopRequested byte+0x269,update mutex+0x270,nineteen12-byte update rows+0x300+i*12={handler,timeval},owned eventfd+0x3e4. Constructor zeroes arrays and both flags. Thread name RSelectThread,mutex names RSelectThreadMutex and SelthrdUpdateMutex are PIC GOT-resolved literals.
engine.owned_fds: Epoll wrapper constructor0x109bc478 calls epoll_create1(0x80000) and stores its fd. Selector0x10c5d9b8 calls eventfd(0,0),stores fd+0x3e4,and logs allocation failure without an immediate abort. Wake0x10c5da28 checks fd>=0 and tail-calls eventfd_write(fd,1). Start0x10c5d40c adds eventfd with event mask1 and null user-data. libsonosminiutils.so.1:sonos_epoll_add_data0x6d6c fills a16-byte epoll-event row (events+0,user pointer+8),uses EPOLL_CTL_ADD1 and returns1 for syscall success or-1 for failure. Its remove0x6ec0 uses EPOLL_CTL_DEL2 with null event pointer and the same1/-1 convention. Selector destructor closes eventfd,then destroys mutex/thread storage and tail-destroys epoll wrapper0x109bc4ac,which closes the epoll fd.
engine.registration: Register0x10c5d20c obtains handler label through slot+8,locks registry mutex,rejects stopRequested!=0 with return0,then writes handler.owner+8 before free-slot search. First null slot is used; no duplicate-registration test exists. Success copies caller timeval or stores{INT_MAX,0},initializes handler.cachedFD+c=-1/eventMask+0x10=0,and returns1. Full19-slot table logs too many users and invokes RabortIfUnlocked before return0; owner was already stored. Registration itself does not write eventfd. Unregister0x10c5dc6c returns0 for null retained owner or stopRequested!=0. Otherwise it clears handler.owner+8,removes matching watched fd and compacts handlers/labels/timevals,clears final slot,and returns whether a matching handler was found. It does not propagate epoll-delete failure as its API return. Stop is not equivalent to this unregister operation.
engine.watch_install_and_reset: At loop start,resetRequested at handler+4 causes cached-watch removal,then reset slot+0x28 executes. Event mask+0x10 is cleared. Getter-1 removes a cached watch and skips that handler in wait-minimum selection. Other negative values do not install an epoll watch but can contribute a timer; RTrackPlayMonitor deliberately returns-2. Nonnegative getters install read mask1; a nonzero result from slot+0x14 adds exceptional bits for mask0x201b. Slot+0x14 is an exception-watch selector,not a timeout-order flag. Install0x10c5ddd4 skips unchanged cached descriptors,removes any previous watch,adds fd with handler user-data,and updates cache+c. Negative getters are skipped using record-form mr. at0x10c5de28,not an unconditional stale-condition test.
engine.wait_and_clock: Loop entry0x10c5e024 holds registry mutex while preparing handlers. It chooses min({5,0},each eligible handler remaining timeout),releases the mutex,reads clock-id1 before and after waiting,and computes elapsed=max(post-pre,0). When at least one ordinary fd was eligible,it calls epoll_wait through tail-wrapper0x109bc510,with maxevents equal to eligible fd count and timeout milliseconds=sec*1000+ceil(usec/1000) for normalized nonnegative timevals. Raw reciprocal multiply/high-word arithmetic0x10c5e200..0x10c5e220 was verified at0,1,999,1000,1001,999999 usec and1/5 sec. When no ordinary fd is eligible,it calls usleep(sec*1000000+usec) instead; the wakeup eventfd is not counted as an ordinary handler. Thus no-fd sleep is not interrupted merely by writing that eventfd. Supplied timevals are copied without validating sign or normalization; the ordinary normalized domain is a convention,not an enforced input range.
engine.returned_events: Each returned16-byte epoll row uses events at+0,user pointer at+8. Nonnull pointers receive events at handler+0x10 before registry mutex reacquisition. Null user-data identifies the selector eventfd; a returned read bit triggers eventfd_read at0x10c5e640. Once the mutex is reacquired,the current registered table is traversed. Raw0x57ff07fe at0x10c5e318 selects eventMask&1,not a right shift. Exceptional bits are tested with mask0x201a at0x10c5e314. These masks and the handler flag determine callback ordering.
engine.callback_order_and_timers: Slot+0x10 is the timer-first policy: nonzero means run the timer helper before exception/data handling on every pass; zero means an actual data-ready callback or exception callback replaces the timer processing for that pass. For timer-first handlers the order is timer,exception if exceptional bits,data if read bit. For others it is exception then data when those events occur,or timer when neither occurs. Negative-fd handlers still reach timer processing. Timer helper0x10c5d6b4 compares measured wait elapsed against relative remaining timeval; elapsed>=remaining invokes timeout slot+0x1c with that same storage as next-delay output,else subtracts elapsed from remaining. libsonos-time-c.so.1:timevalGeq0x1334 and timevalSubtract0x125c were inspected; subtraction has no special INT_MAX infinity exemption. Timers therefore account for measured wait time,not the entire wall time spent inside callbacks. Long callback processing can extend actual intervals. Each data/exception/timer wrapper samples getter before and after its callback; any change from a starting getter other than-1 invokes the descriptor-change diagnostic,whose call to RabortIfUnlocked is a semantic tail call.
engine.updates: Post-timeout-update0x10c5da50 locks update mutex,rejects stopRequested!=0,and searches19 rows for an empty row or the same handler. Reposting the same handler overwrites its queued timeval. A null timeout stores{INT_MAX,0}; a full queue of different handlers returns without an additional row. Successful posting writes eventfd. After callback processing,the worker locks update mutex,matches each queued handler against the live registry,copies the queued relative timeout into that handler slot,and clears the row. An absent handler logs Update error stu ... not in st ... and the row is still cleared. Pending updates are applied after callbacks,so they can replace a callback-produced delay.
engine.errors_and_recovery: A failed epoll add/remove logs the operation. Removal clears cachedFD to-1 even on failure and returns0 to its caller. In the worker,a failed watch change routes through0x10c5df90,which resets all registered cached descriptors to-1 and tail-calls epoll-reset wrapper0x109bc4cc; that wrapper closes and recreates the epoll fd. The worker then invokes descriptor-change diagnostic0x10c5d600. The reset helper does not reinstall the null-user-data eventfd watch; start0x10c5d40c is the explicit eventfd-add site. This is a concrete recovery-path limitation,not evidence of reliable wakeup delivery after epoll recreation. Negative epoll_wait results are logged and skip callback/update processing for that iteration; no per-errno special case is present in this loop. The five-second wait ceiling also bounds routine rescans when no earlier handler timeout is selected.
engine.start_stop_and_retained_state: Start0x10c5d3a8 locks registry mutex,returns without a second start if started+0x268!=0,adds the wakeup watch,sets started1/stopRequested0,unlocks and starts RThread with entry0x10c5e648,which calls worker0x10c5e024. Wake-watch add failure logs and invokes RabortIfUnlocked; if that helper returns,start continues. Stop0x10c5d4b8 returns early when stopRequested is already set. Its started branch sets stopRequested1,unlocks and joins the RThread through0x1098aa34,which tail-calls0x1098a8b0 and pthread_join at0x1098a9fc. It then removes the wakeup watch and clears started. Neither stop nor destructor iterates the19 handlers to unregister them,clear their retained owners or close their device sockets. Stop also does not explicitly write eventfd before the join. Individual handler owners must manage their own descriptor lifetime; calling stop is not proof that those registrations were erased. The stopRequested-clear but started-clear branch also joins and removes the wakeup watch (0x10c5d520..0x10c5d550),without first setting stopRequested; it is not a separate no-op guard for a never-started selector. Start does not inspect the RThread start return,and constructor does not check epoll_create1 before proceeding to other initialization.

select_thread.completion_basis: Per-record completion: all eight named handler inputs and supplied select owners are bound; the last IPC live cleanup is matched to player+0x8c0; the IR parent start/stop/final-reference disposal chains establish absence of automatic unregister; the selector vtable,19-slot tables,fd wrappers,relative timer arithmetic,callback policies,update queue,state flags,recovery paths and side effects are instruction-traced. Runtime fd numbers and thread/packet timing are dynamic results,not unresolved constants. No live experiment or universal caller-ordering guarantee is claimed.

evidence.notes: leds_zp

Vtable at 0x10fba500 has +0x30=0x10c8e7e0. xori r7,r4,1; mask high r5=0, low r6=0x100; virtual+0xc reaches f_10c8ea78, which chooses set versus clear mask and dispatches virtual+0x10=f_10c8e934. Updater reads owner+0xa0/+0xa4 at 0x10c8e980/0x10c8e984 and stores at 0x10c8e99c/0x10c8e9a0. Equal-word guard 0x10c8e9a4/0x10c8ea00 avoids reapply; changed flags call f_10c8f06c at 0x10c8e9ac.

Gate f_10c8ee44 called at 0x10c8f178 checks ready/bypass; build uses flags +0xa0/+0xa4 -> request+0x10/+0x14 at 0x10c8f1e4/0x10c8f1ec/0x10c8f230/0x10c8f234. Status/mute capabilities owner+0xba/+0xb9 -> request+0x18/+0x19, Bluetooth owner+0xaa/+0xab -> request+0x1a/+0x1b. f_10c8eca8 computes useOnlyStatusLED from +0xbb/+0xbc. Call f_10c8ff2c at 0x10c8f254 -> f_10c918a0 at 0x10c8ffcc.

Complete selector 0x10c918a0-0x10c926dc: low loaded +0x14, high +0x10; low&0x100 and signed high>=0 branch to suppression setup 0x10c91b08. All named predicate masks 0x10c919a0-0x10c91a58 exclude 0x200. !HHID precedes TRANSFER_REGISTRATION; final HHID fallback 0x10c925a4. Resume f_10c92acc through 0x10c92fbc uses low at +0xc/high +8 and likewise has no 0x200 predicate. No raw-word srwi pseudo-decode was used for these masks.

Hardware feature setter stores microphone/mute/status/only-status/swap/white-brightness booleans at owner+0xb8..+0xbd. Diagnostic 0x10fba55c supplies ordering; selector uses separate capability bytes, not a microphone bit inferred from numeric gap 0x100.

Sibling selector 0x100036a4-0x10004524 has the same word loads, 0x100/signed-high predicate, and named mask sequence at 0x100037a4-0x1000385c. No 0x200 test. This independently checks the main-image map rather than transferring mismatched word offsets. .gnu_debuglink is present but no .symtab or DWARF enum definitions in the shipped ELF.

resolved_findings: The named mode map has 24 entries: 21 low-word modes and three high-word modes. It is recovered from each selector predicate and its logged r7:r8 mask, not inferred from adjacent literal names. Hardware capabilities, mode bits and the software suppression/control bit are separate inputs.

Main-image selector f_10c918a0 is reached from applyLEDModeLocked f_10c8f06c through f_10c8ff2c. The priority sequence is UPGRADE, BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH_OPEN, JOIN_HH, BEGIN_SETUP_MODE, IN_SETUP_MODE, WAC, WAC_TIMEOUT, BREAK_POP, SHUTDOWN, !HHID, TRANSFER_REGISTRATION, CONTROL_FEEDBACK, IDENTIFY_PLAYER, AUDIO_OFF, MUTED, FAULT, WAITING_TO_PLAY, WAITING_TO_PAUSE, PLAYING, WARN, DEMO_MODE, DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR, with HHID as fallback. Suppression and available-light inputs also affect colors and auxiliary output; the mode name alone is not a complete hardware pattern description. Resume uses the subset BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH, BEGIN_SETUP_MODE, IN_SETUP_MODE, then when HHID is set MUTED, AUDIO_OFF, PLAYING and HHID fallback.

The former 0x100 mic/aux premise is withdrawn. The concrete software setter f_10c8e7e0 transforms a boolean into the inverse 0x100 flag, while hardware capability bytes are installed independently by f_10c8eac4. In the selector request +0x18/+0x19 are status/mute light capabilities and +0x1c is useOnlyStatusLED; +0x1a/+0x1b carry exclusive-Bluetooth/connected state. The initial 0x100 predicate also checks signed(high)>=0, not high!=0. Its CR7 branch polarity was checked against raw word 0x409c01f8 at 0x10c91910.

The 0x200 numeric gap does not leave a missing mode branch: complete apply and resume selector audits in anacapad and sonosledmgrd find no predicate or logged arm for it. The generic RLEDsZP updater is (old & ~clearMask) | setMask and re-applies only on a changed word, including unrecognized bits. Thus an unknown bit can cause a redundant reapply without selecting a new pattern. The map deliberately makes no claim about an original source-only enum name for an unused position. Both ELF images lack .symtab/debug enum definitions; a source-level name would require matching source/debug material rather than inventing a physical sensor meaning.

Readiness/suspend-bypass gates f_10c8ee44 precede selector invocation. Hardware requests are built only after those gates, so a requested flag update is not proof of a HAL write or visible light change. Empty/unchanged updates return current flags without reapplying. Hardware capabilities set separately include microphone, mute/status LEDs, only-status policy, hardware LED swap and adjustable white brightness.

flag_words.storage: Big-endian 64-bit flags: RLEDsZP owner+0xa0 high word and +0xa4 low word. applyLEDMode request+0x10 is high and +0x14 low. resumeDefaultLEDPattern uses a different request layout: +8 high and +0xc low. These are two words, not a third-word flag namespace.
flag_words.low_0x100: Software suppression/control bit. Vtable+0x30 entry f_10c8e7e0 inverts its boolean argument and updates mask 0x100 through virtual+0xc: input 0 sets the bit, input 1 clears it. The selector computes suppression = (low & 0x100)!=0 AND signed(high)>=0. This is not a decoded microphone-mute or aux-insertion signal. The high sign bit bypasses that suppression test; no original enum name is asserted.
flag_words.low_0x200: No selector binding: full apply/resume predicates in both shipped implementations do not test this bit. Generic update can preserve it and notice that the entire flag word changed, causing mode reapplication, but it has no separate pattern arm in these selectors. Neither dead-code provenance nor a third flag word follows from the numeric gap. An original unused/reserved enum identifier is not encoded in these stripped images.

evidence.notes: libFLAC

resolved_findings: Resolved: decoder creation = reference libFLAC 1.3.4 via the stream framer; error/status enums documented.

Integration layer proven: FLAC enters three ways - (1) the HTTP stream MIME route sonos.com-http:*:audio/flac:* with .flac extension mapping in the stream-format dispatch table; (2) MP4-container FLAC via the m4a-flac codec variant ({m4a-m4a, m4a-alac, m4a-flac, m4a-opus, m4a-ec3}); (3) the eSDK stream format flac/flac-24bit (with {ogg/vorbis, mp4/aac-lc, spac/aac-he-v2, video-manifest}). Exact build: reference libFLAC 1.3.4 20220220. Subframe vocabulary {LEFT_SIDE, RIGHT_SIDE, MID_SIDE, CONSTANT, VERBATIM, PARTITIONED_RICE, PARTITIONED_RICE2} confirms the full decoder including stereo decorrelation modes.

evidence.notes: tp enums

Raw PPC and pointer-table contents establish bounds and r3<<2 lookup, unknown fallback, spatial0..15 versus processing0..3. Negative input takes unsigned out-of-range. No executed Playbar/DSP writer join certified.

todo: Established: bounded numeric-to-name maps and separate spatial/processing channel enum domains, with explicit unknown fallback. Remaining: bind the actual model/configuration readers carrying speaker, array, direction and channel values to their DSP parameter writers; recover per-array conversion/default/rejection behavior and prove the Playbar path rather than assuming the diagnostic string lookups execute. Start with enum table0x10fbf1d4+0xc and reader-side value producers, then join selected array constructors to parameter serialization. The name getters alone neither establish a DSP map nor an external-config-only limitation. This remains actionable static work.
resolved_findings: Static enum-to-name lookup f_10caa06c accepts unsigned0..5 and indexes table0x10fbe650 with value times4; out-of-range, including negative inputs interpreted unsigned, returns unknown at0x10f92d18. Numeric speaker masks0..5 are UNSPECIFIED,THREE_DOT_ONE,FIVE_DOT_ONE,FIVE_DOT_ONE_DOT_TWO,SEVEN_DOT_ONE,NINE_DOT_ONE_DOT_FOUR. These names do not prove Playbar enables every layout or that numeric enums are bit masks.

Spatial channel names use f_10caa0a0, bound0..15 and table0x10fbef08. Processing channel names instead use f_10caa1b0, bound0..3 and table0x10fbfed4: UNSPECIFIED,INPUT,OUTPUT,SCRATCH. Both start at0; merging them into one19-value enum was wrong. Channel direction f_10caa0d4 accepts0..3 from the first table+0x40.

Array subsystem lookup f_10caa140 accepts0..6 at table0x10fbf1d4+0xc: UNSPECIFIED,BRAVO,FURY,OPTIMO2,OPTIMO2_SURROUND,LASSO,APOLLO. Tone handler f_10caa10c separately accepts0..2 from that table base, while voltage-gain calculator f_10caa178 accepts0..3 from+0x28. Each out-of-range branch returns unknown rather than selecting an unspecified default configuration.

Orientation f_10caa1e4 accepts0..8 from0x10fbff4c. Measurement/sub-polarity/tuning lookups f_10caa218/f_10caa250/f_10caa288 each accept0..2 from that base+0x24/+0x30/+0x3c. Raw PPC verifies unsigned bounds, r3-times4 indexing and separate offsets; none of these functions writes a DSP parameter.

No direct relative branch or aligned pointer-table reference to the checked speaker-mask/array-name lookup entrypoints was found in this pass. Consequently these bounded functions prove static name maps, not that the Playbar runtime executes them. resolved_findings: Used-vs-dead split proven: the anacapad consumer surface is the room-detection sender path - muse verb chirpRequest and route chirp/{playId} drive a chirp audio stream through ChirpExtAudioSrc (ChirpExtAudioSrc does not exist!, Chirp setup failed - chirp sender does not exist!). Runtime behavior: chirping with unique device value:%d payload, playId tracking (chirp with playId %d / differ than m_chirpPlayId), concurrent-play guard (chirp signal is already playing with playId %d), volume calibration gate (Chirp volume not yet calibrated, chirp output volume: %d), payload allowlist (Chirp payload %s not supported), and a playback-collision policy (ChirpIfPlayingSwappableAudio, chirp only). Precise version: chirp-core 4.2.1_7265 (the core lib) under the 4.2.3 SDK wrapper, with FSK + CDMA decoder/encoder pairs, reed-solomon, wavetable/biquad/multitone/FFT DSP, voter+scorer+peaks decode path - all compiled in; the APIs anacapad exercises are init/config/send/process + the send-path encoder; the FSK/CDMA decoder side is present but only the sender path has anacapad consumers.
Established: sender-side usage via ChirpExtAudioSrc under muse chirpRequest/chirp/{playId}; playId arbitration; calibrated volume gate; chirp-core 4.2.1_7265.

Consumer boundary closed using executable call sites rather than name-literal absence. The SDK constructor is f_10cc4030: its name comes through GOT cell 0x1108e5c0 at 0x10cc4064. Room-detection code actually calls it at 0x104f5734 and handles null at 0x104f5740. The same application function configures the SDK, calls send entry f_10cc5bc4 at 0x104f5ac8, tests its result, then calls chirp_sdk_process_shorts_output=f_10cc53fc at 0x104f5ae8 and tests its result at 0x104f5aec-0x104f5af4. Output consumes a sample count, grows a float workspace, synthesizes through core dispatch at 0x10cc54d8/0x10cc5520, and converts to shorts via f_10cc6030. No payload waveform grammar is inferred from these calls.

Receive-consumer census: scanning relative branch targets across the executable finds no application call to shorts-input f_10cc55ac. Its only direct caller is the vendored combined input/output wrapper f_10cc571c at 0x10cc5778; that wrapper has no direct call sites. Neither entry address occurs as a stored big-endian pointer in the ELF. The SDK entry-range 0x10cc4030-0x10cc6440 application callers are confined to the room-detection block 0x104f5734-0x104f5e10 (creation, configuration, send, output, state and destruction). Input/output processing in the wrapper remains linked but is not an application receive path. This establishes sender-only application usage for this build, not removal or impossibility of the internal decoder algorithms.

The failed literal-only negative test was explicitly checked: process_shorts_output has no direct string xref, yet 0x10cc5534/0x10cc5574 load its name via GOT cell 0x1108e684 and 0x104f5ae8 calls its implementation. Thus the receive conclusion rests on entrypoint branch/pointer census, not on the earlier invalid no-string-xrefs argument. The resolved scope is SDK identity, application consumers and their sender/receive boundary; the vendored core waveform/forward-error-correction algorithms are not claimed to be reverse engineered.

Room-detection stop path f_104f6414 returns distinct results for null playId, absent source, mismatched active playId and unsuccessful stop. Only a matching owner+0x98 playId reaches the source virtual +0x20 call at 0x104f65c0-0x104f65d4; successful stop clears that active playId. Start path f_104f669c checks the source and requires a nonzero calibration lookup at 0x104f6710-0x104f672c before proceeding. These are real application predicates, not merely SDK diagnostic vocabulary.

resolved_findings: Static facade census: the sixty-two named SDK wrappers occupy 0x10cf4f60-0x10cf8558. Their names are formed from SpInit literal base 0x10fd3910 plus per-wrapper offsets, so a literal-only xref search misses most names. Native instruction/address-formation and branch scans, plus aligned rodata/data/sdata pointer scans, distinguish forty-two wrappers with application call instructions from twenty with no incoming static reference. None of these facade addresses has a stored pointer or text address-formation reference in that scan; the application uses direct branches. This is a static build census, not a claim that every application branch executes on every device or session.

The twenty unreferenced facade entries are SpRegisterDeviceAliasCallbacks=0x10cf51f8, SpPlaybackCycleRepeatMode=0x10cf5dec, SpConnectionLoginBlob=0x10cf5ec8, SpGetCanonicalUsername=0x10cf6288, SpGetLoginUsername=0x10cf6358, SpPlaybackSetAvailableToPlay=0x10cf6428, SpPlaybackSetDeviceControllable=0x10cf65a0, SpSetDeviceAliases=0x10cf6d44, SpSetAdUserAgent=0x10cf6e18, SpZeroConfAnnouncePause=0x10cf6f88, SpZeroConfAnnounceResume=0x10cf7058, SpConnectionLoginZeroConf=0x10cf7128, SpPlayContextUri=0x10cf74e0, SpGetDefaultDnsHALCallbacks=0x10cf78d4, SpRegisterSocketHALCallbacks=0x10cf79ac, SpGetDefaultSocketHALCallbacks=0x10cf7a94, SpPlaybackSetBandwidthLimit=0x10cf7c64, SpLogRegisterTraceObject=0x10cf8374, SpRestrictDrmMediaFormats=0x10cf8478 and SpRestoreDrmMediaFormats=0x10cf8558. Their literal presence does not prove Sonos integration, contrary to the earlier blanket registration claim.

Positive application bindings include SpInit at 0x102141f4, debug registration at 0x102141e0, connection/playback/stream registration at 0x102142a8/0x102142b4/0x102142c0, volume-step setup at 0x102142c8, pump at 0x102298dc and free at 0x10229b7c. Playback play facade f_10cf5598 has three direct application callers at 0x1021daf0/0x102216a0/0x10225a4c; pause has four at 0x1021d818/0x10225b08/0x10226644/0x102266cc. LoginOauthToken reaches f_10cf5fc0 at 0x10227a10; DNS HAL registration reaches f_10cf77ec at 0x1021a500 and 0x104e8578; TLS registration reaches f_10cf7b7c at 0x104e8d4c. These counterexamples disprove both an all-dead vendored facade and an all-live literal list.

Facade execution is guarded independently of reference presence. For example f_10cf5598 logs conditionally, forwards to f_10cfc1f0 and pumps pending work through f_10cfbdb0 only on zero status. Playback-registration delegate f_10cfc0f8 returns status 6 when the SDK singleton is absent, 16 when its +0xba4 condition is set, and 4 for null callback input; valid input copies twelve callback bytes and calls f_10d3a638. These guards mean application reference is not unconditional registration success. The code is in the image and was traced; vendor ownership is not a residual.

Reconnect/LoggedIn/Disconnect/TemporaryError are notification vocabulary, not demonstrated AP-state integers. The earlier equality between these enums and the logged numeric states is withdrawn.

The actual mod_ap_conn pump is f_10d0b3f8 and reads a state byte at connection+7, with separate retry counter at +6. Its dispatch at 0x10d0b5d8-0x10d0b680 handles states 0..6 through an earlier branch group and explicitly distinguishes 7/8/9 at 0x10d0b930-0x10d0b960. State 7 calls f_10d0af44; success stores state 8 and calls f_10d39f64(1) at 0x10d0be14-0x10d0be34. State 8 dispatches a separate message type at connection+0x80, including 10/65/74/105 at 0x10d0bdc8-0x10d0bdf8. Thus there are nested state and message-type dispatches, not one notification table.

Handshake code is reachable from that pump: hello construction f_10d42270 at 0x10d0baac and response verification f_10d42658 at 0x10d0bbc0. Socket OS errors are recorded at +0x64a4 before f_10d0a234 handles failure at 0x10d0b484-0x10d0b4cc. The no-response timeout logs at 0x10d0b754, stores 10000 at +0x5c and takes that same failure path with -66. f_10d0c51c separately computes a reconnect delay using +0x64b0/+0x64b4, while f_10d0c5bc returns the saved OS error. The generic modular exponentiation helper f_10d3d5e0 receives a 0x100-byte modulus/result for the signature operation at 0x10d42998, followed by a 0x100-byte comparison at 0x10d429a8; a mismatch takes the failure exit 0x10d4274c. The next exponentiation uses 0x60-byte operands/output at 0x10d429b4-0x10d429dc. The 2048-bit signature workspace therefore must not be used to label every handshake operand RSA-2048 or to assert an SRP protocol from the filename.

KDF dataflow recovered in f_10d42658: 0x10d429dc writes a 96-byte shared result at work base r31. For counter bytes 1 through 5, 0x10d429e8-0x10d42a44 initializes keyed hashing with those 96 bytes, updates with hello base r28 and length *(r28+0xa4), then response base r26/length r25, then one counter byte, and writes a twenty-byte digest at work+0x60+20*(counter-1). The first twenty derived bytes key another HMAC over the same hello/response transcript at 0x10d42a48-0x10d42a80. The next thirty-two bytes at work+0x74 initialize context r28+8 through f_10d4682c, and the following thirty-two at work+0x94 initialize r28+0xd8 at 0x10d42a84-0x10d42aa0. evidence.notes: httpio
CDN fiber waits for one HTTP transaction before handling its response.
Request write continuation, followed by header processing.
Response header read uses the same socket subcontext.
Single request-format call in the request fiber.

resolved_findings: Numeric HTTP pipeline depth is one outstanding transaction per httpio context. CDN fiber f_10d2e6c0 calls f_10d304b8 at 0x10d2eaec and waits on its continuation before examining response status. Only completion reaches 0x10d2ee74, obtains response metadata through f_10d31710 and accepts status 200/206 at 0x10d2ee98-0x10d2eea4. It does not issue another request while that call is suspended. This is a per-context bound, not a global bound on simultaneous SDK sockets or contexts.

The request fiber owns one socketio subcontext at context+0x10 and one continuation at +0x190. Its request formatting call f_10d4e9f8 is at 0x10d30898; it writes the request through f_10d4fa54 at 0x10d30718, suspending with continuation 0x5a while socketio+0xac is nonzero (context+0xbc). The response-header operation f_10d4fdac at 0x10d30618 similarly suspends with continuation 0x79; header extraction f_10d4f438 follows at 0x10d307e4. The same request buffer/state is reused, not a ring of pending requests. Error exits set the result at context+0 and clear +0x190 at 0x10d306a4-0x10d306b4; completion also clears it at 0x10d306f4-0x10d306fc.

Request formatter f_10d4e9f8 builds HTTP/1.1 requests with Host, identity encoding, SDK user-agent and keep-alive headers, adding bounded or open-ended Range headers according to offsets. Keep-alive preserves a connection; it does not imply HTTP pipelining. The independent serialized request/write/header-read continuations disprove interpreting the keep-alive literal as multiple outstanding requests. The response parser retains explicit unsupported transfer/content-encoding, redirect and invalid content-range error paths. Multiple independently allocated contexts are not excluded by this result.

rootfs_boot_chain.summary: The shipped inittab runs /etc/Configure as sysinit and respawns daemon wrappers. Configure creates RAM/persistent trees and invokes an optional /etc/dsmf_setup before mdputil and hostname setup, but this image does not contain that hook. SSH unlock and console-enable gating are separate mechanisms. The mapper name crroot does not itself prove a particular encryption or integrity target.

touch /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led; /sbin/frcheck -> factory-reset check: rc!=1 -> sonosledmgrd --fr (FR LED flash); rc==0 -> netstartd --hard-reset; rc==2 -> netstartd --soft-reset
create jffs trees: app/{run,log,debug,debug/dsp,settings}, sys/{run,log,debug,settings}, net/{run,log,debug,settings}, persist
optional /etc/dsmf_setup; /bin/mdputil -B (mfg data init); hostname=Sonos-<SERIAL[:12]> via mdputil|keyval ^SERIAL|cut
if /jffs/Configure exists -> exec it INSTEAD of remaining steps (whole-boot override hook)
UNLOCK PATH: /etc/unlocked_build_flag OR /jffs/system/Configure.dev -> ln -s /opt/htdocs_locked /tmp/htdocs_locked + touch /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; Configure.dev then executed every boot (dev hook)

rootfs_boot_chain.notes: Configure tests only -f /etc/dsmf_setup before executing it; the script has no set -e and does not test its return code, so a hook failure does not itself abort the following mdputil/hostname steps. The hook is absent in the shipped tree, and arch_attrs contains LACKS_DSMF. Its position is established; factory-provisioning internals and acronym expansion are not certified by position alone.
rootfs_boot_chain.security_files: fstab names /dev/mapper/crroot with auto filesystem type and noatime,nodiratime,defaults; it does not name a device-mapper target, dm-verity or dm-crypt and does not itself specify read-only mounting. /dev/shm is tmpfs with noexec,nodev,nosuid,mode600. run_sshd.sh waits for /tmp/device_unlocked_flag before exec dropbear -R -F. In contrast secure_console_login.sh waits on console_enable only if /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable exists; when absent it proceeds to getty. inittab supplies secure_console.sh, which execs login -f root. This passwordless console path is not gated by the SSH unlock flag. No password hash is needed to explain it. chrony/DHCP roles are unchanged.

In this shipped corpus, a full regular-file byte-string scan finds only Configure and arch_attrs occurrences; neither expands it. Configure proves presence-only invocation before mdputil/hostname and no explicit abort on hook failure. Do not infer provisioning operations or an acronym expansion from hook position or LACKS_DSMF.
resolved_findings: Resolved: supervisor layer details proven - /etc/rundaemon.sh supplies waitfordns (blocks on /var/run/waitforip + resolv.conf nameserver), waitwhiletrue 10s retry, and trackrestart (per-daemon /var/run/<name>.start stamp log with restart throttle). runledmgrd adds stale-pid detection writing to /opt/log/sonosledmgrd.log. runchrony creates /jffs/chrony after waitfordns and honors /var/run/stopchrony (step-vs-slew noted: one step per run). runmdns honors /var/run/stopmdns, execs mdnsd -f. secure_console_login gates getty on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable==1 (default-on when the lock file is absent).

Resolved: the shipped identity map - passwd has root(uid0,/bin/sh) + chrony(uid19) + anacapa(uid20,/bin/false) as the only Sonos users; group sonos gid20. anacapad's -u anacapa drops to uid20/gid20; the secure-console 'login -f root' is passwordless and gated purely by /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable.

The script sequence, optional-hook presence gate and failure continuation are established from the shipped files. A /jffs/Configure file exec-replaces the remaining Configure steps; later Configure.dev is invoked with sh and does not exec-replace the parent. A failing optional DSMF or Configure.dev command is not explicitly fatal. Missing-hook behavior is observable statically; manufacturing internals are not.

The earlier integrity-protected/read-only-root and universal unlock prerequisite assertions are withdrawn. fstab proves only the mapper device path and mount options. inittab reaches the console wrapper independently of run_sshd.sh; console_enable absence is explicitly default-allow in the wrapper. These two entry paths must be audited independently rather than inferring a common credential/unlock gate.
