bin_upgrade.name: upgrade / upgrade_mgr daemons
bin_upgrade.summary: Firmware-update pair: /bin/upgrade performs one upgrade transaction (download, verify, flash, reboot); /bin/upgrade_mgr is the orchestrating daemon that the anacapad update machinery kicks (/var/run/upgradeinfo) and that exposes an SSDP-advertised status server. All evidence below is from stripped 32-bit MSB (PPC) ELF string/dyn-symbol tables plus /etc/runanacapa and /etc/init.d/rcK.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): failure/rollback = the upgrade binary pair handles verify-then-write with fallback partition; consolidated into the record - anacapad hands off via update_machinery; binaries themselves are outside the anacapad static surface but the call contract is documented.

bin/upgrade I/O contract: reads /var/run/upgradeinfo ('Error reading upgradeinfo file'); supports a no-op mode ('No-op mode - download/reboot will be skipped' and 'Detected /jffs/VERSION, performing no-op update'); builds the image URL as '%s%s-%u-%u.upd?cmaj=%u&cmin=%u&cbld=%u&subm=%u&rev=%u&reg=%u&serial=%s' plus '&sonosid=%s&householdid=%s'; and ends by calling reboot().

bin/upgrade .upd container: typed sections with a magic header ('Invalid section header. Bad magic value.'), a required/optional split ('Required section %u missing', 'Skipping checks for section %u', 'Unknown section %u', 'Multiple sections of type %u'), a signature section verified via sonosRcbVerifySig ('invalid Sonos signature section length', 'encrypted signature section not supported'), per-section enveloped-data decryption via mbedtls ('Enveloped data parse/decrypt init/decrypt/decrypt final failed', 'Encrypted section too small', 'Out of space while decrypting section'), and cert bundles saved under /jffs/sys/run/rcb/ as upd_cert_bundle.rcb and %s-%s.rcb.

bin/upgrade hardware gating: mutes and powers off amps through libsyslib_hal before flashing ('warning: failed to mute/power off amps'), reads the boot section via hal_flash_get_bootsection, enforces a HW-feature compatibility matrix ('Critical UPD feature (%s: %s) not supported by player', 'Critical player feature not supported by UPD', 'Upgrade supports all my legacy hw features'), skips M4 and BOOTSOUND sections when no partition exists, and writes /var/upgradescript for post-reboot execution.

bin/upgrade client-server mode: can listen on a TCP port for a household controller ('client-server mode: listening on port %d', CONNECT/DOWNLOAD/DOWNLOAD_DONE states, 'waiting for connection from HH', monitored attach/detach) and streams progress to that client ('Failure sending progresss to client. Lost connection to client.'); writes the upgrade report to /jffs/upgrade_sys_report.log (prev rotated to _prev) and /var/run/upgrade_report.txt.

bin/upgrade housekeeping: wipes /jffs/app/install, writes /jffs/sys/run/updateID, references deactivation markers /jffs/persist/deactivation_pending_state.json + deactivated_state, devmode image path /jffs/debug/devmode.bin, and manages /tmp/upgrade_mgr.pid + /var/run/stopupgrade.

bin/upgrade_mgr state machine: verbs {HELLO, STATUS, PING, DOWNLOAD, FLASHWRITE, REBOOT, COMPLETE, ERROR, 'Unrecognized command'} and states {UNDEFINED, INIT, CONNECT, HELLO_DONE, WAIT, DOWNLOAD_DONE, FLASHWRITE_DONE, REBOOTING_DONE, FINISHED}; the status server binds a TCP port ('status server: listening on port %d') and announces itself over SSDP with NT/USN urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:SonosUpgradeMgr:1, X-RINCON-HOUSEHOLD, and 'X-RINCON-REASON: hh-upgrade'.

bin/upgrade_mgr reporting: daemonizes (daemon()), reads its info file (ReportFilename must be set), and emits a JSON report to /jffs/app/run/%s with fields {Serial, Type, CurrentVersion, TargetVersion, UpdateID, HardwareVersion, State, ServerIP, ErrorMsg, ExtendedError}; its update-check URL carries '?Version=%s.%s-%s&Auto=%s&Client=%s'.

bin/upgrade .upm section machinery (decoded from the shipped binary): per-section header {+0x4: type, +0xc: flags (bit0x2=tolerated-when-unknown), +0x10: payload offset}; section types accepted in range 3..0x16. Dispatch iterates a stride-28 handler table {+0x10: arg, +0x14: already-seen flag producing 'Multiple sections of type %u', +0x28: flags with bit0='Skipping checks for section %u'}. File body is mmap64'd (work buffer rounded to 0x200 granularity). Section flag bit0x1 rejects as 'encrypted signature section not supported' and bit0x4 selects the unsupported-encryption reject. The cert-bundle section is verified by sonosRcbParseHeader+sonosRcbVerifySig and written to /jffs/sys/run/rcb/%s-%s.rcb.

upgrade_mgr wire vocabularies are ALSO embedded in anacapad rodata as {char* name,u32 len,u32 id} stride-12 tables: verb table @0x10fad660 {1=UNDEFINED,2=CONNECT,3=HELLO,4=DOWNLOAD,5=FLASHWRITE,6=WAIT,7=REBOOT,8=ERROR,9=FINISHED} and state table @0x10fad6d8 {1=INIT,2=HELLO,3=HELLO_DONE,4=DOWNLOAD,5=DOWNLOAD_DONE,6=FLASHWRITE,7=FLASHWRITE_DONE,8=REBOOT,9=REBOOTING_DONE} - the coordinator-side client marshals/parses these exactly.

.upm envelope wire layout decoded from f_100045c8: reads an 8-byte prefix {word0 (first u32), word1 at bytes 4..7 = big-endian envelope-header-length N (validated N>7 and N<=total)}; then reads N-8 more header bytes; ZZ0053 parses the N-byte header into an envelope struct (wrapped key + IV); ZZ0052 decrypts the payload using that struct + key-source 0x100409b8(ZZ0070). So the .upm section payload is a length-prefixed envelope: [u32][u32 BE hdr_len][hdr_len-8 byte envelope hdr][ciphertext]. Errors: short prefix = Encrypted section too small; hdr_len<=7 or >total = Malformed enveloped data header; ZZ0053 fail = Enveloped data parse failed; missing key = No decryption key.

Resolved: the N-byte envelope header layout decoded from libsonoscrypto ZZ0053 (@0x6318): {+0 u32 magic 0x886499ca, +4 u32 declared-length (must be <= actual N), +8 u16 version==1, +10 u16 flags word, +12 u32 key-record count (<8), +16: count x 264-byte input key records each expanded by the record parser into a 2572-byte internal record carrying a <=2047-byte blob field and a <=512-byte blob field}. After the key records comes a u8 count of secondary records (parsed per-record with u32 len + data memcpy) and trailing u32 fields at out+7276/7280. ZZ0070 (the key-source selector) is a no-op stub {stwu;addi;blr} - there is no key-source id bound in this build.

bin_mdputil.name: mdputil
bin_mdputil.summary: Reads factory identity/configuration, stages command-line edits, verifies manufacturing-bundle signatures and erases/writes manufacturing flash. The512-byte identity page and4096-byte second page have distinct layouts. CLI, repair, signature inputs and flash failures are traced; driver-side serial/check commands, geometry and remaining hardware-field consumers still require work.
todo: Residual: identify the live flash backend installed in the kernel MTD callback slot +0xa4 and decode its device-command parameters, including whether/how it changes the requested serial-data extent. The matching kernel ioctl dispatcher and user-copy sizes are now located. Kernel sysword consumers, remaining manufacturing tail fields and individual manifest hardware-code consumers still require tracing.
resolved_findings: ELF SHA256 and explicit stack buffers join the512-byte MDP1 and4096-byte MDP2 read paths. MDP1 magic is0xce10e47d;MDP2 magics are0xca989b4a/0xfa87b921. Raw XOR/signed-immediate equations were checked rather than using the operand fragments as magic.

Printer arguments at0x10001664..0x10001ab0 bind the named MDP1 fields and widths. FUSEVAL is+0x88;SWFEATURES+0x8c;SERIES_ID+0x98;DATECODE+0xac;DCOFS+0x100. Derived status/color/FSN lines have separate helper chains.

libflash read success does not compare stored CRC. Flags/version normalization can zero fields in the returned view even when raw page bytes were nonzero. The CLI preparation helper separately stores CRC over508 bytes.

0x10002928 requires260 payload bytes and128 signature bytes, hashes a supplied identity header plus that payload with MD5, and performs RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification. The260 comparison is not a field index or table length.
Hardware-manifest output is one-based1..8. Editable indices are1..7 with per-entry numeric ranges;0 and8 reject. Null-check printer wrapper uses conditional bclr and fall-through,not a dead delegate.
REGION edit is option-e:0x10000eb4 stores the supplied value at staged MDP1+0x1c. Thus the documented command mdputil -fwe 2 supplies new REGION value2;2 is not a field index.

/etc/Configure line74 invokes mdputil-B. At0x10001190 the option can check existing MDP2 through/dev/chk, then requests a forced write when original old-version>6. Otherwise it exits early unless-w has already appeared. It is not merely a printing option.
Application MDP flag cleanup has the concrete predicate and bit effects in application_flag_consumer. It clears printk/console bits and sets marker0x20;it is not an inverted capability predicate.

Kernel-side ioctl dispatch located by decompressing the shipped package/86.10-80260-1-9-kernel.uImage gzip payload after its 64-byte uImage header. Addresses here are offsets in that decompressed raw image, not asserted ELF VAs. At raw+0x1aea38-0x1aea44 the dispatch compares request 0x80244d23, reaching raw+0x1aec40; at raw+0x1aed6c-0x1aed74 it compares 0x40044d24. The latter selects device-structure+0x184 as source and copies four bytes to the user argument at raw+0x1aed94-0x1aed9c. This binds the library first ioctl output to a stored device word, not a direct chip command issued by that arm. The exact device initialization producing this word still needs tracing.

For 0x80244d23 the kernel copies a 36-byte request from the user argument into stack+8 at raw+0x1aec58-0x1aec68, rejects a missing callback at device+0xa4 with -95 at raw+0x1af45c, allocates the requested first-word byte count, and checks request words at +8 and +0x14 against 8 at raw+0x1aec94-0x1aecac. The accepted path calls device+0xa4 with (device, local request, allocated buffer) at raw+0x1af324-0x1af338, propagates a nonzero result, and uses the request first word as the return-copy extent at raw+0x1af354 onward. Thus the 36-byte ioctl header size is not itself the serial-data extent. The library hal_flash_read_fsn requests 256 bytes and separately reports/extracts smaller serial lengths. Backend identity and command-field meanings are not established merely by matching ioctl constants, and remain open rather than claiming a complete kernel trace.

binary_identity.working_buffers: main0x10000ad4 has MDP1 read at sp+0x1c,512-byte edit/template buffer at sp+0x21c,MDP2 read at sp+0x41c (4096 bytes),and separate4096-byte prepared/key-bundle area at sp+0x141c. Default template is .data0x10020018.

read_contract.physical_sizes_and_headers: libflash.so.1 hal_flash_get_mdp0x2120 reads512 bytes;hal_flash_get_mdp2 at0x23c0 reads4096 bytes. The first magic is0xce10e47d. Raw xoris at0x21bc XORs high0x31ef;cmpwi at0x21c0 compares against sign-extended0xffffe47d,so solving the comparison gives high0xce10,not0x31ef. The default mdputil template also starts0xce10e47d. MDP2 accepts0xca989b4a or0xfa87b921,not the XOR operand fragments. Reads use flash-info-derived offsets;MDP1 offset info+0x50,and MDP2 offset info+0x50+info+0x40.
read_contract.io_and_status: read_from_offset at libflash0x1f78 opens read-only,checks the64-bit seek result when offset is nonzero,and accumulates partial reads until the requested count is reached. It retries read errno4(EINTR). Return0 means the full requested read;1=open failure,2=seek mismatch,3=short/failed read. MDP readers add9=null flash context and12=bad page magic. MDP1 failure clears its512-byte output then supplies Vendor1,Region1 and the library's current-model value;the original error is still returned. MDP2 failure clears4096 bytes. mdputil does not treat these library fallback values as proof that a valid stored page exists.
read_contract.normalization: For valid MDP1 magic,FLAGS&4 absent clears HWFEATURES+0x68. FLAGS&0x10 absent clears+0x70/+74/+78/+7c/+80. The reader then computes a version for normalization:old+70 when old<=5; for old>5, nonzero new+84 or old. Version<=1 clears+84/+88/+8c;<=2 clears+90..+97;<=3 clears SERIES_ID+98..+9b. For later versions it retains SERIES_ID only if first byte isA-Z and the next three are digits. Version<=5 clears+a0 and then+a4..+ab/+ac;version6 clears+a4..+ab/+ac;version7 clears+ac;later versions retain those tail areas. This is in-memory normalization,not a flash write. Unprinted tail fields still need semantic consumer joins.
read_contract.checksum_limitation: hal_flash_get_mdp invokes crc32(seed0,buffer,508) at0x2298 but neither compares its result with stored+0x1fc nor stores it;the result is discarded before returning the read status. The underlying read_from_offset does not validate CRC either. In contrast,mdputil preparation helper0x10002bf8 stores computed CRC at+0x1fc at0x10002c7c and its alternate branches. Basic read success therefore establishes length/magic and normalization,not CRC/signature acceptance.
read_contract.printing: COPYRIGHT is forcibly terminated at+0x63. Effective MDPVERSION selection is old+70 unless old>5 and new+84 is nonzero. WIFITYPE=N is a literal output line,not a radio-type probe. Invalid DATECODE values are zeroed only in the display buffer. VARIANT,SERIALSIG,UNITSIG,FSN and NANDID are derived helper results and are not interchangeable with fixed MDP1 byte fields.

series_and_variant.series: Stored and derived SERIES_ID behavior, complete fallback-model table, copy/return conventions and setter-prefix validation are traced in identity_format_contract. The dynamic annotation denotes derived source, including fallback X999; it is not a success/failure label.
series_and_variant.variant: sonosGetCertColorVariant at libsonos-mdp0x964 takes MDP1 and MDP2 as separate pointers. For MDP2 magic0xca989b4a,it requires MDP1+74>3 (minimum4) and reads MDP2+0x44c. For0xfa87b921,it requires+74>4 (minimum5) and reads MDP2+0xa10. Accepted value domain is0..18. It returns0 on failure and optionally writes status-2(bad pointer),-3(unknown magic),-4(unsupported version),-5(index out of range);these are not negative color return values. mdputil0x100018f4 passes a null error-output pointer,so VARIANT=0 alone cannot distinguish color0 from decoder failure.
series_and_variant.wildcard_final: sonosGetFinalColorVariant at libsonos-mdp0x9fc first calls GetCertColorVariant. Any result other than11 passes through unchanged. For wildcard11 it keeps11 if effective MDP1 version<=4, otherwise reads override+9c. Unsigned override<=18 returns directly; larger values return0 and write optional status-5. This is distinct from-V accepting an unchecked decimal value: the later consumer supplies the range check. Effective version uses old directly for old<=5 and a nonzero new version only for old>5. mdputil prints WILDCARD_VARIANT from+9c when its certification/version gates pass.

color_names.producer: sonosGetColorVariantString at libsonos-mdp0xac8: unsigned index<=18 selects a base-relative19-entry table at0xfb0, reached through PIC GOT0x27eac. Index0 and11 return a valid pointer to an empty string at0x10e0, not a null pointer. Recognized entries optionally store status0. Out-of-range unsigned values, including negative inputs reinterpreted as unsigned, return Unexpected color and optionally store-1. It returns static strings; no allocation or page access occurs.
color_names.quirk: Different numeric certification variants can share the same display name. The string alone cannot distinguish White1/3/4 or Black2/5/6. Wildcard11 has an empty direct name; a separate final-color decoder can apply the stored override before naming.

manifest_addressing.layout: Header+0xb0=0x7a61670e;40-byte area starts+b4. Display indices1..8 are LED at+b5,AMP+b6,TEMP_SENSOR(AMP)+b7,TEMP_SENSOR(CPU)+b8,ALS+b9,ACCELEROMETER+ba,FUEL_GAUGE+bb,RADIO+bc. Printer0x10002218 increments the base before loading each entry.
manifest_addressing.edit_domain: 0x10002320 parses %d=%d,checks unsigned index<=8 then<=7,and uses the base-relative table0x100031f4. Index0 rejects. Allowed edits:1(LED)=1..3,2(AMP)=1..5,3/4(temperature)=1..3,5/6/7=1..2. Index8(RADIO) is displayed but cannot be set by this path. Write at0x100024a0 is byte mdp+b4+index. Values outside these ranges,including0,reject;existing/cleared page bytes can still be0 or other raw byte values. Meaning of individual hardware selection codes is still open.
manifest_addressing.clear_and_show: clear zeros the40-byte area and clears the header;show/print reports an invalid header but still displays all eight numeric entries. Setting an accepted entry re-arms the header without validating other entry bytes. Wrapper0x10002210 has raw conditional bclr0x4d820020 at0x10002214:it returns for null input,otherwise falls through into0x10002218. It is not an unconditional empty stub.

application_flag_consumer.source: anacapad getter0x10909620 loads cached device-info+0x168,which is its MDP buffer+0x104 plus FLAGS offset0x64. It is an MDP flags word,not a capability word.
application_flag_consumer.predicate: Cleanup0x105e64fc proceeds only when cached(flags&0x20)==0 and cached(flags&3)!=0,proven by0x105e6524/0x105e6528 and0x105e6564/0x105e6568. The earlier documentation reversed both gates.
application_flag_consumer.effect: It reads current MDP1 from flash and optional MDP2,then computes newFlags=(flashFlags&0xfffffffc)|0x20 at0x105e65f8/0x105e65fc and writes via0x10d54658. This clears named numeric bits0x1(printk) and0x2(console) and sets a cleanup marker0x20. A set cached marker skips this path. The record does not claim a refresh of the cached flags after writing or an upgrade-only trigger.

cli_edit_contract.selection_and_output: Option string0x10003688 is Aa:whfv:V:M:m:r:Nn:e:s:S:Ik:F:C:P:T:i:d:D:Bpj:u. Table0x10003214 is base-relative. Edits target sp+0x21c; ordinary no-write field output uses original r28. -w requests writing; overwriting a valid original requires-f, but initializing an absent original does not. No original and no write returns1. -k without a write returns1. -h increments the ignore-key-validation-error counter, not a help flag. -p is a recognized no-op; A,a,j,u dispatch to unsupported and return1.
cli_edit_contract.decimal_fields: strtol(arg,NULL,10) stores-v VENDOR+4,-M MODEL+8,-m SUBMODEL+c,-r REVISION+10,-e REGION+1c,-D DATECODE+ac; -i stores the low byte at+6c. No end-pointer, errno or range check follows these conversions. Numeric prefixes can be accepted despite trailing text; no numeric prefix produces0. Signed values are stored in the destination width. -V stores+9c after original MDP1/MDP2 certification variant equals11 at0x10000f80; no local0..18 range check. Importing a later-k bundle does not change that original-data eligibility test.
cli_edit_contract.serial_and_series: -s clears8 bytes at staged+14 and accepts hexadecimal digits with colon/hyphen separators. It processes at most13 nibbles, does not require12, and ignores remaining input after that limit; the13th nibble occupies the high half of+1a beyond the six identity bytes. Invalid nonhex input before the limit returns1. -S accepts an uppercase letter followed by three digits through sonosSetSeriesID; a longer argument with that valid prefix also succeeds.
cli_edit_contract.flag_operations: Helper0x10002190 parses strtoul(NULL endptr,base0). Leading| means OR with the original word; leading& means AND with the original word; otherwise replacement. Repeated-F/-T recompute from original values rather than accumulating earlier staged operations. -T changes HWFEATURES and sets flag4 iff the new word is nonzero. -F preserves currently staged bits0x14 while replacing other bits; a plain replacement is deprecated but accepted. -P/-C enable printk1/console2 for any nonzero strtoul result, clear them for0. Option order therefore matters: a later-F may overwrite earlier-P/-C.
cli_edit_contract.reset_and_manifest: -I copies the default512-byte template into the stage only, discarding preceding edits but retaining original read pointers. -N and-n show print the staged manifest immediately; -n clear and-n index=value edit it. None requests a flash write by itself. Manifest numeric parsing uses sscanf with two conversions and does not require end-of-input.
cli_edit_contract.dc_offsets: -d parses colon-separated decimal tokens with strtok, delimiter at0x10003610. First token initializes all four DCOFS words+100/+104/+108/+10c. A second token replaces+104 and+10c; a third replaces+108; a fourth replaces+10c. Thus one value broadcasts, two become[a,b,a,b], three become[a,b,c,b], four become[a,b,c,d]. Extra tokens are ignored. Conversions use strtol(NULL,10) without range/end checks. The first strtok result is passed to strtol without a null guard, so an empty/all-separator argument is not safely rejected by this path. These edits are allowed independently of model; only model17 prints them.

boot_repair_contract.check: At0x10001190, original MDP1 plus original MDP2 with successful helper0x100024c4 validation leads to open(/dev/chk,O_RDWR), ioctl0x8004f302 with pointer to word0x1996, then close. Open or ioctl failure returns1. Missing/invalid MDP2 skips this device check. The shipped chk driver copies the supplied word into kernel-global sysword; see boot_flag_driver. Kernel consumers of that global remain untraced.
boot_repair_contract.repair_and_order: Unsigned original old-version+70>6 branches0x10001208 to0x100013ac, prints Fixing bad MDP version and increments both write and force counters. Version<=6 prints MDP version ok. If write count is still0, -B returns0 immediately and skips later options. Thus-Bw exits before-w for old<=6, while-wB proceeds. Missing original also exits0 at-B unless a preceding-w requested creation. Repair uses the common preparation/write path rather than a dedicated single-word patch.

write_contract.preparation: 0x10002bf8 sets FLAGS|0x10, old-version+70=6, new-version+84=8 and PAGESPRESENT bit1. With MDP2 it sets low page bits3; if MDP2 version is0 it infers1 from payload length836 or2 from964, otherwise retains the version. Without MDP2 it clears page bit2 and version+74. It stores crc32(seed0,MDP1,508) at+1fc. This mutates the caller staging buffer before data is written.
write_contract.erase: 0x10002fac builds descriptor words from flash-info+3c,+40,+50; byte+20c==3 substitutes first-page write span512. 0x10002ef0 opens/dev/mtd/0 read/write and issues ioctl0x80084d02 with two words: offset(info+50) and erase length(info+3c). Returns1 for open failure,5 for ioctl failure,0 for success. It closes the descriptor. The descriptor fields are bound to erase-block/write-page sizes in flash_geometry_contract.
write_contract.write: After successful erase,0x10002d58 opens/dev/mtd/0 read/write, checks both halves of lseek64 against the requested offset, then prepares MDP1. A span>512 allocates a zeroed span and copies512 bytes; smaller/equal spans use MDP1 directly. It makes one write for the span, then one4096-byte write if MDP2 is present. Negative or short writes fail; there is no retry/partial-write loop. It frees padding storage and closes the file.
write_contract.errors: Writer statuses1=open,2=seek mismatch,4=write failure,15=padding allocation failure. Outer wrapper returns9 for null flash context and collapses erase/write failures to14. Main prints mdp_write failed and returns1 on failure. Erase occurs first, so later failure can leave erased or partially replaced manufacturing data; no rollback path is present.
write_contract.bundle_import: -k - removes the second page from the write. Other filenames require an original MDP1. One read of up to4088 bytes into prepared MDP2+8 must return836,964,1092 or1096; corresponding MDP2 versions are1,2,3,4. Header is0xca989b4a; payload length is836 for the first format and964 for the others. Validation0x100024c4 binds against original serial+14, even after staged-s edits. Version>3 additionally calls0x10002a5c. -h permits continuation after these validation failures. The two signature contracts and their distinct original/staged identity inputs are documented in bundle_signature_contract.

bundle_signature_contract.crypto_binding: libsonoscrypto.so.3 ZZ0062 at0x6b30 initializes a112-byte tagged hash state: selector1=SHA256,2=MD5,3=SHA1. ZZ0064 at0x6c08 tail-branches to the matching mbedtls hash update; ZZ0061 at0x6c4c finishes then tail-branches to hash-context free. Both mdputil checks select2, so their16-byte digest is MD5. ZZ0109 at0x8ec4 requires signature algorithm selector1, key size<=512 bytes and signature length exactly the key size; hash selector2 maps to mbedtls digest enum3. It calls mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_verify and returns1 only when that call returns0. These are signature checks, not decrypt operations.
bundle_signature_contract.embedded_keys: ZZ0087 at0x74a8 passes162 DER bytes at0xd5d4 to ZZ0101; ZZ0083 at0x7570 passes162 DER bytes at0xd71c. GOT entries use R_PPC_RELATIVE addends0xd090 and0xd71c; the first getter adds0x544. Independent OpenSSL DER decoding confirms each is a1024-bit RSA public key with exponent65537. SHA256 of the DER blobs: first cbbff75214c4b677643ed3c091ed710b8e75a3aa8b6ae02887050eae669e4407; second5e6c832fb6bb1f30370e41fd6cf02d2b9f207d38374f95227f8c6c1a4fec1d1e. ZZ0101 at0x84e4 attempts X509 then public-key parsing then its legacy parser, requires RSA type and rsa_check_pubkey success, and exports modulus/exponent; the supplied DER uses the public-key parse route.
bundle_signature_contract.serial_flash_signature: 0x100024c4 requires nonnull MDP2 and six-byte serial pointers, loads the first embedded public key, then opens/dev/mtd/0 read-only. ioctl0x40044d24 retrieves a device ID. ioctl0x80244d23 receives a36-byte parameter block whose first word is0x100 and next word points to stack+10c; remaining command bytes depend on device ID. The returned bytes are searched in serial/complement pairs: each corresponding byte must XOR to0xff. On a valid pair, the serial is copied, the device closed, and MD5 is computed over six original identity bytes followed by8 or16 flash-serial bytes. For magic0xca989b4a and payload-length word>963, the128-byte signature at MDP2+34c is verified against that digest using the first key. The bundle payload itself is not hashed by this check.
bundle_signature_contract.flash_serial_commands: IDs0x1da,0x1f1,0x2caa,0x2cda,0x2cf1 use16-byte serials, a16-pair search limit, parameter word+8=0, word+14hex=5 and word+20hex=0xed. IDs0x98d1,0x98da,0x98f1 also use16-byte serials and16-pair limit but word+8=2, bytes+c/d=5a/b5. ID0x20aa uses8-byte serials, one-pair limit, word+8=4, bytes+c..f=29/16/02/19. All use pointer/0x100 setup above. The loop advances by twice the serial width per rejected pair. Driver interpretation of these parameters and the amount of returned serial data remain open; do not equate the parameter0x100 with a verified byte-count contract.
bundle_signature_contract.serial_result_domain: 0x100024c4 returns-1 for null page/serial; -2 for embedded public-key load failure; -3 for device open, unsupported device ID, ioctl failure or exhausted complement-pair search; -4 for unsupported MDP2 magic or payload length<=963 after obtaining the serial; -6 for signature mismatch;0 for success. Raw isel0x7fe04f9e at0x100026e0 selects literal0 when verification returns1, otherwise-6. No path in this helper returns-5, although the caller diagnostic table includes a Decrypt error entry for-5. Key resources are freed on the normal/error return paths. Consequently the accepted836-byte import size maps to version1/header length836 but does not pass this validator; it reaches-4 after successful flash-serial acquisition. File-size acceptance is separate from signature acceptance, and-h can bypass that rejection.
bundle_signature_contract.identity_header: 0x10002a5c takes MDP1 then MDP2, loads the second embedded key and obtains constant0x3c6852eb through ZZ0086 at0x75ac. It constructs exactly26 bytes: u32BE constant;6 serial bytes from MDP1+14;u32BE MODEL from MDP1+8;u32BE SUBMODEL from MDP1+c;u32BE certification color from MDP2+44c;4 zero bytes. The halfword stores at0x10002b40..0x10002b54 preserve the PPC big-endian order of the three32-bit fields. Vendor, revision, region and wildcard override are not part of this header.
bundle_signature_contract.identity_payload_signature: 0x10002928 hashes the supplied header followed by exactly260 bytes from MDP2+8. It verifies128 signature bytes from MDP2+3cc using the second public key. Parameter guard requires nonzero header length, data length260, signature length128 and nonnull key; other input pointers are not locally checked. Hash-init failure prints Bad hash and returns0; bad guarded parameters print Bad parm and return0; otherwise it returns the verification boolean. Raw SPE instructions0x10e10b21/0x10e10b01 at0x100029c4/0x100029e0 and0x10002a0c/0x10002a30 save/restore the signature-pointer register around volatile hash calls; the pointer is not an accidental post-call r7 value. 0x10002a5c prints Bad mdp for null pages or Bad key for key failure, frees the key and returns0; success returns1. It does not independently check page magic or version.
bundle_signature_contract.callers_and_edit_asymmetry: Main-B0x100011a8 and imported-bundle check0x100014c8 call the serial/flash checker with original serial, which is also called by standalone read wrapper0x100028d0. Imported versions>3 call the identity checker at0x10001dec with the staged MDP1; this binds edited model/submodel/serial to the imported signature. Printer0x10001d30 calls it with original pages for displayed UNITSIG status. Thus changing-s can leave the first check tied to the old serial while the second checks the edited serial. -h permits write continuation after either import check fails. A successful first signature alone does not establish that the payload or edited identity passed the second signature.

flash_geometry_contract.producer: libflash.so.1 SHA256454a6c5e2bde42f0f6fa64854dc738a3d1b4731a99f4af6c9272576ca2ff641d: hal_flash_info_init0x1ba8 takes an output-pointer address, sets it null, allocates a zeroed0x210-byte object and stores the geometry-device pathname at+208. PIC GOT reconstruction uses LR anchor0x1bb4, addend loaded at0x1ba4 and R_PPC_RELATIVE GOT addend0x3bec, which resolves /dev/mtd8. This is distinct from the /dev/mtd/0 used by page reads and mdputil writes.
flash_geometry_contract.geometry_fields: After opening /dev/mtd8 read-only, ioctl0x40244d01 receives a stack information structure at sp+18. Successful extraction maps info[0]=returned u32 at+8(total size), info+3c=returned+0c(erase-block size), info+40=returned+10(write-page size), info+50=erase-block size, info+48=0 and info+20c=returned type byte. The rest of the allocation stays zero. Exported get_pagesize0x1b00, get_blocksize0x1b2c and get_type0x1ad4 independently confirm the field roles. The leading type/size/erase/write layout agrees with Linux MTD ABI; the actual binary ioctl encodes36 bytes, so unspecified trailing ABI fields are not inferred.
flash_geometry_contract.manufacturing_layout: MDP1 reads512 bytes from /dev/mtd/0 at offset erase-block size, the start of the second erase block. MDP2 reads4096 bytes at erase-block size + write-page size, proven libflash0x23f4..0x240c. The CLI erase descriptor uses erase-block size as erase length and offset; its first-page write span is write-page size, except type3(NOR flash) forces512 in0x10002fe4..0x10003048. The MDP2 reader does not apply that NOR span override. These are geometry-derived positions, not a hard-coded512-byte separation for every flash type.
flash_geometry_contract.initialization_errors: Allocation failure returns7 with the output null. Negative ioctl result closes the file, frees the object and returns7. Open failure at0x1c1c instead branches directly to0x1c4c: it falls through the field-copy path, publishes the allocated object and returns0 although the stack information structure was never initialized by ioctl. Size remains the allocation zero, but type/erase/write/offset fields are loaded from uninitialized stack slots. Thus initializer success alone does not establish valid geometry. No null guard protects the output-pointer argument. info_exit0x1cc8 tail-branches to free.

boot_flag_driver.binary: modules/chk.ko SHA256f099055a15c41e29074bd0855c3c0add5f30d23df2a5d7c14f172bc3df00978e; ELF ET_REL, not stripped. Addresses in this block are section-relative offsets, not runtime virtual addresses. .symtab names chk_ioctl at.text+8(size408), chk_open at+1a0 and chk_release at+0. Relocations identify sysword as an undefined kernel-global symbol.
boot_flag_driver.dispatch: chk_ioctl extracts command&0xff at.text+0c and (command>>16)&0x1fff at+20. Number1 copies sysword to user; number2 copies from user into a stack word then assigns sysword at+0xb4. The handler does not compare the type/magic or direction bits, or require encoded length4. Unknown command numbers print Unknown IOCTL called and return0. User-copy failures print the matching copy error and return-14(EFAULT); successful copies return0. It uses task address-limit checks and __copy_tofrom_user, with boundary handling for the user address region. It performs no signature/hardware-validation call.
boot_flag_driver.issued_command: mdputil-B at0x100011e4 issues0x8004f302, which this handler decodes as number2,length4. It copies the four-byte word0x1996 into sysword. The value is a kernel RAM assignment, not an erase/write to manufacturing flash. mdputil makes this assignment only after its existing MDP2 serial/flash signature check succeeds. The chk handler itself does not test that signature or the value0x1996. Downstream kernel consumers of sysword remain to be located before assigning a wider system-mode meaning.
boot_flag_driver.registration_and_lifetime: The .data file-operation table relocations at+28,+34,+3c point to chk_ioctl(+8), chk_open(+1a0), chk_release(+0). Open/release simply return0; no per-open state is allocated. .init.text allocates one character-device number with minor0/name chk, initializes a cdev with chk_fops, assigns module owner, adds it and calls sonos_device_create with name chk. Allocation errors propagate; cdev-add failure unregisters the range; device-create error deletes cdev and unregisters. Success logs Registered chk driver. .exit.text destroys the device, deletes cdev, unregisters the range and tail-branches to printk for Unregistered chk driver. The initial devno word0x0f300000 is passed by address to alloc_chrdev_region and overwritten; it is not proof of a fixed major243 allocation.

flash_serial_display_contract.interface: libflash.so.1 hal_flash_read_fsn0x2d78 takes u32* length output(r3),serial-byte destination(r4),optional u32* device-ID output(r5). It opens /dev/mtd/0 read-only, gets device ID with ioctl0x40044d24, writes the optional ID immediately after a successful query, and issues serial command ioctl0x80244d23. Required length/destination pointers have no local null/capacity guard. Serial byte count is8 or16 depending on the device ID. This is the helper used for mdputil FSN/NANDID output, not the older in-executable helper used for SERIALSIG.
flash_serial_display_contract.parameter_layout: The ioctl receives a36-byte stack parameter block at sp+1c, initially zeroed: word+0=0x100;word+4 points to buffer sp+44;word+8 and bytes+c..f select a command sequence;word+14 specifies a per-family numeric parameter;word+18 is explicitly cleared through a variable-length memset in ordinary paths;byte+1c stays0;word+20 may be0xed. These field purposes below the kernel boundary remain untraced. The function reserves2048 returned-data bytes plus8 trailing bytes before its stack canary. Unlike the old utility checker, it also consumes returned marker bytes at buffer+0x800 for one family. Neither caller proves that the word0x100 is a transfer-byte count.

device_families.marker: Require55 aa in at least one of four two-byte positions at returned buffer+0x800,+0x802,+0x804,+0x806 before searching serial pairs.

flash_serial_display_contract.acceptance: For each candidate, compare serial bytes with the following equal-width complement bytes and require each XOR==0xff. A rejection advances the candidate start by twice the serial width. First complete match copies exactly8/16 serial bytes to the destination; no textual/hex conversion occurs here. For0xecaa, marker validation precedes serial-pair acceptance; it still permits up to8 serial/complement pairs. memcpy return is compared with the destination pointer; the alternate failure is defensive under the standard memcpy return contract.
flash_serial_display_contract.results_and_outputs: Return0=serial copied;1=device open failure or negative device-ID ioctl;7=unsupported device ID;15=negative serial ioctl, absent required0xecaa marker, or exhausted complement search. The FD closes on all paths after successful open. Optional device ID may be available even on later unsupported/retrieval failure. Length is assigned after successful serial ioctl but before complement search (and before the0xecaa marker check), so a nonzero length output is not proof of success. Serial destination is copied only on acceptance; it is not cleared on failure.
flash_serial_display_contract.cli_output: mdputil0x1000192c calls this helper with sp+18 length,sp+241c serial destination andsp+14 ID. Success prints NANDID=%04x then FSN= followed by exactly length bytes using%02x, lowercase hexadecimal without separators. Failure branches0x10001934 to0x10001b1c and prints FSN=INVALID without the NANDID line. It then continues to later signature/display checks rather than aborting the utility. Thus FSN retrieval status and SERIALSIG/UNITSIG status are distinct.

identity_format_contract.serial_formatter: sonosMdpSerialToString at libsonos-mdp0xbdc takes six-byte identity pointer(r3),destination(r4),capacity(r5). It assembles source bytes2..5 into unsigned32-bit big-endian n. Raw mulhwu at0xc18 uses0xf0f0f0f1; shift-right4 of the high product yields floor(n/17). The code subtracts17*quotient and renders remainder0..9 as0..9,10..16 asA..G. Format string at0x1084 is %02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%c, giving12 uppercase hexadecimal digits plus one derived suffix. The first two source bytes are printed but do not contribute to the suffix. This formatter performs no serial validity check.
identity_format_contract.serial_output_contract: Formatter calls __snprintf_chk with caller capacity,flag1 and object-size sentinel-1, returning its result unchanged. A complete output needs14 bytes including NUL; smaller capacities truncate according to snprintf while reporting the would-be13-character length. It still reads all six identity bytes. mdputil0x100016c0 supplies capacity32 and prints SERIAL from that output. Its-s edit does not consume/check this suffix as a separate validation character. The boot script consumes only the initial12 hexadecimal characters for the hostname.
identity_format_contract.stored_series: sonosGetSeriesID0xcb0 takes destination(r3),capacity(r4),MDP1(r5). If effective version>=4 and byte+98 is nonzero, it copies bytes+98..9b to a five-byte temporary with trailingNUL, strlcpy-copies to the destination and returns1. It only tests the first stored byte here; no four-character lexical validation occurs inside this getter. EmbeddedNULs can shorten the copied text. Read-time normalization and the setter have separate lexical checks. Return1 describes the chosen stored source even if capacity truncates the output.
identity_format_contract.derived_series: When stored data is ineligible/empty, the getter dispatches MODEL8..22 through15-entry base-relative table0x10a0 (PIC GOT0x27ef0-0x7fd8). Other models, including unsigned underflow below8, use X999. The selected static string is copied with strlcpy and return0 identifies derivation, not failure. The getter does not reject X999 and does not return a copied-length result.

identity_format_contract.series_setter: sonosSetSeriesID0xe64 takes input(r3),MDP1(r4). It checks first byteA-Z then next three bytes0-9. Invalid prefix returns-1 without storing the four-byte field. bin_frcheck.name: frcheck
bin_frcheck.summary: At each normal startup, frcheck decides whether this Playbar should keep its saved configuration, perform a settings reset or perform a full factory reset. A persisted request whose first four bytes are SOFT selects the settings reset; an empty, unreadable or different request selects a full reset. It attempts to delete the request file after reading, before the hardware check; the deletion result is ignored. Holding the play/pause button overrides a soft request and selects a full reset. The checker only returns a decision: the boot script shows the reset light and asks the network-startup daemon to carry it out. It does not itself erase storage, validate the filesystem or reboot the player.
resolved_findings: Full decision chain verified: first-four-byte request parsing, one-shot unlink attempt, normal/soft/full result selection, device-open/read failures, three exact u32 predicates and boot-script consumers.

The previously unresolved eight-word button map is now resolved against the shipped kernel producer: indices0..2 are play/pause,volume-up,volume-down states1=pressed/2=released; indices3..7 are zero placeholders. frcheck tests0,3,7 and therefore only the live play/pause input can force a reset on model9.

Corrections: frcheck is not a filesystem-integrity checker; its predicate is not byte1; the HAL extracts words7..14 from a244-byte ioctl output, not the first eight words; the alternative path uses the same ioctl, with0x80002 as open flags. button_sim_matches ids are source ids, not event classes.

Read>0 and strcmp(firstFourBytes,SOFT)==0 selects2 via isel0x10000660 (0x7feaf79e: r31=CR7.eq?r10:r30, r10=2,r30=0); failed/empty or other content selects0. Bytes after the first four are not read. unlink at0x10000668 consumes the request regardless of unlink result; an unlink failure can leave it present for a later boot. Then open64(/dev/audioctl,O_RDONLY) at0x10000594; open failure retains the file/default result. Helper0x10000904 returns0 on HAL success or-1 on failure. Negative result at0x100005b0 retains the decision; a successful read compares u32 words at main sp+0x2c,sp+0x38,sp+0x48 with1, corresponding to returned button indices0,3,7. First two matches branch to result0; the final isel0x100005dc (0x7fe0ff9e: r31=CR7.eq?0:r31) handles index7. File-derived result remains when no tested word is1. The opened fd is closed on every successful-open path. It is not passed through to the HAL call: wrapper replaces r3 with its own output pointer.

It does not inspect byte1. libsyslib_hal.so.1 hal_inputs_get_buttons_state0x13cc issues ioctl0x40f4fc3e into a244-byte block at sp+0x18, then copies block+0x1c,+0x20,+0x24,+0x28,+0x2c,+0x30,+0x34,+0x38 to the eight-word output (loads0x1450..0x1488). The checker itself only consumes the request file and opens/closes device access; destructive reset behavior belongs to the daemon invoked by the script. Other results, e.g. signal termination, enter the reset-light branch but do not match either reset-daemon option in this script. No request/service dispatcher or vtable participates in this standalone program.

bin_sddpd.name: sddpd (Sonos discovery daemon)
bin_sddpd.summary: Control4 SDDP (Simple Device Discovery Protocol) daemon (/sbin/sddpd), a third-party discovery channel parallel to SSDP/mDNS so Control4 remotes find the player. Respawned by inittab via /etc/runsddp after waitfordns; -n keeps it foregrounded, /jffs/dev_sddp.conf overrides /etc/sddpd.conf.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): sddpd.conf knobs = the SDDP announce/probe config; wire protocol boundary noted - daemon is external; role = Sonos device discovery parallel to SSDP/mDNS.

Wire surface from strings: builds periodic NOTIFY-style advertisements ('Sending SDDP advertisement', 'Sending Periodic SDDP advertisement', 'SDDP send failed'), answers SEARCH requests when the search target matches ('SEARCH', 'SDDP Search target MATCH'), emits identify on demand ('Sending SDDP identify'), and rejects foreign packets ('Unsupported SDDP request/response packet version: %s', 'Unrecognized SDDP packet: %s'); packet bodies start with the 'SDDP/' version token.

Sockets: one multicast listener + one unicast socket per interface - sets SO_REUSEADDR, IP_PKTINFO, IP_MULTICAST_TTL, joins a multicast group per interface ('Joining multicast group for %s'), enforces a minimum advertise period ('Setting SDDP max_age to minimum of %d seconds').

Config: /etc/sddpd.conf ships Type=sonos:Zoneplayer, PrimaryProxy=media_service, Proxies=media_service,amplifier, Manufacturer=Sonos, Model=Zoneplayer, Driver=sonos.c4z, MaxAge=1800; loader validates the file ('Incomplete config file', 'SDDPSetHost failed: host param too long', 'Unable to set device (index = %d)') and usage is '%s -n'.

bin_mdnsd.name: mdnsd (Sonos mDNS fork)
bin_mdnsd.summary: Stock Apple mDNSResponder daemon (/sbin/sddpd-adjacent /sbin/mdnsd), run foregrounded as 'mdnsd -f' by /etc/runmdns behind the waitwhiletrue /var/run/stopmdns gate. Sonos ships the posix mDNSResponder, not avahi.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): zone/group advertising = the _sonos._tcp announce flow driven by anacapad registration calls (mdns_controller); daemon-side config documented via shipped conf.

Binary is upstream mDNSResponder with the standard internals (mDNSCore*, mDNSPosix::tcpListenCallback, mDNSPlatform{SendUDP,TCPListen,TCPConnect,TCPWritable}, 'mDNSResponder Build %d.%02d.%02d' state-log banner, '---- BEGIN/END STATE LOG ----').

Privileges/sandboxing: attempts setgid+setuid to nobody and warns on failure ('WARNING: mdnsd continuing as group root / as root because setgid/setuid to nobody failed'); usage is '%s [-debug]' (-f foreground flag comes from mDNSPosix main).

Client surface: a dns_sd unix-domain-socket server is compiled in ('ExitCallback: udsserver_exit failed', 'requestIOEvents called with fd %d > FD_SETSIZE') - this is how anacapad registers the _sonos._tcp service/TXT records documented under the mdns record; interface tracking registers/deregisters interfaces at runtime ('Registered interface %s', 'Deregistered interface %s').

Divergence check: no Sonos-patched protocol strings found; the advertised zone/group semantics all live in anacapad's registration calls, not in the daemon. /etc/mdnsd.conf is referenced but absent from the rootfs, so the daemon runs with built-in defaults plus client registrations.

Exact compiled release recovered from executable instructions, disproving the earlier no-version-marker/window claim: the state-log format at 0x1005a9bc is ---- BEGIN STATE LOG ---- (%s mDNSResponder Build %d.%02d.%02d). Its pointer is loaded into r20 at 0x10003f7c and passed as format r5 at 0x1000411c. The call at 0x1000412c passes r7=1311, r8=40, r9=1, loaded immediately before it at 0x1000410c-0x10004114. The END STATE LOG arm independently passes the same triple at 0x100040dc-0x100040fc. Thus this image identifies its mDNSResponder build as 1311.40.01 (release tuple 1311.40.1), not merely 878.x-1310.x. The Engineering Build string at 0x1005a7d8 is an additional build-time banner, not evidence that no numeric release exists.

Independent version check, not only the banner: handler f_10048c4c compares the incoming property string against DaemonVersion at 0x10048cd4 and, on equality, constructs a response. At 0x10048d7c/0x10048d88 it materializes 0x00c81a91=13114001, matching 1311*10000+40*100+1; 0x10048d90 serializes that value and 0x10048da8 sends the 12-byte response. A nonmatching name takes the four-byte response at 0x10048ce0-0x10048cec. These two reachable output paths bind the compiled daemon version despite the missing textual mDNSResponder-XXX release tag. This identifies the image release constant, not byte-for-byte identity with an unmodified upstream source checkout.

evidence.notes: State-log call passes literal release triple 1311,40,1.
DaemonVersion response embeds integer 13114001, independently matching release triple.

setup_client_hello_payload.validation_and_defaults: Fixed-width readers invalidate the cursor for a wrong tag or wrong2/4-byte width. String reader0x1002e1bc requires length+1<=destination capacity, uses %.*s (no UTF8/content validation), and can display a shorter string if a value containsNUL. Blob reader0x1002e2c8 rejects declared length beyond caller-supplied capacity; on success it copies and updates the length output. Advancer invalidates the cursor on a second occurrence of any of these five fields (their schema modes are0/1, not repeatable2). Finalizer0x1002db94 rejects missing required tags and initializes absent optional outputs to zero/empty. Unknown tags are skipped without a presence requirement, including tags40..255. The decoded protocol value is not range-checked by this field parser.
setup_client_hello_payload.trailing_frame_quirk: When header parsing0x1002d898 cannot read a complete field header/value, iterator0x1002de0c returns0 without clearing the cursor-valid byte. The hello loop then runs the finalizer. Consequently, after valid required fields have appeared, incomplete/malformed trailing bytes can be ignored and the parser can still succeed. This differs from a fully encountered recognized field with the wrong width/oversize output, which its typed reader marks invalid. Full byte consumption is not a prerequisite for this parser success.

That helper accepts setup modes1..3 without blob verification, rejects mode<1 or>6, and for modes4..6 requires exactly32 blob bytes and compares them against32 locally derived bytes via ZZ0199; it caches the comparison boolean at context+2d4. Successful comparison logs greeting fields, caches optional session text, calls response builder0x1001e4d0 and writes its result via0x10026798 when construction succeeds.
