In libsonoscrypto0x67a0 that delegate selects a key, decrypts/wraps through ZZ0075/ZZ0043, allocates plaintext length+1, publishes the heap pointer/length and terminates it withNUL. Full envelope algorithm/trust checks and key-provider provenance remain separate work. It is not a DH calculation in this traced helper. Reset0x10022a48 wipes and frees the secret, zeroes pointer/length and clears related context data.
client_hello_verification_contract.derivation: 0x10027734 requires output capacity>=32. It invokes library ZZ0215 with secret/length, label ASCII handshake_signature(length19), no derivation context, output size32. In0x7144, ZZ0215 computes HMAC-SHA256 blocks over LE16(counter)||label||context||LE16(output_size*8). Counter starts1. This call needs one block and hashes bytes01 00, the19-byte label, then00 01. There is no extra NUL separator between label and context. Derived key is32 bytes.
client_hello_verification_contract.proof: The helper then invokes ZZ0065(selector1,derived_key,32,message,message_length,proof_output), a one-shot HMAC-SHA256. HMAC init0x6e4c maps selector1 to this build's mbedTLS type9. The shipped libmbedcrypto0x26bbc and name table at0x6f690 independently identify type9 as SHA256; its enum numbering is not inferred from an upstream header. The proof formula is HMAC-SHA256(derived_key,context_bytes[+2e8,length+2d8]). The temporary derived key is wiped with ZZ0038 before returning. Successful output length is32; undersized capacity or a reported initialization/derivation failure returnsfalse.
client_hello_verification_contract.comparison: 0x10023384 calls ZZ0199 for32 bytes. Library0x70f4 loops over the entire span, ORs each bytewise XOR and returns that byte:0 means equal, nonzero means a mismatch. There is no first-mismatch exit. Netstartd converts exact zero into true, stores that boolean at setup-context+2d4 and wipes its local32-byte expected proof. This cache write occurs only after successful derivation/comparison; earlier mode/length/derivation rejection returns0 without updating that cached byte.
client_hello_verification_contract.scope: Modes1..3 returntrue without this proof; mode0 and modes>6 reject. Missing/invalid proof in modes4..6 does not establish household authentication. This verification does not sign the software-version/protocol/capability fields and does not by itself establish which peer owns the upstream secret. Those properties require the encrypted-envelope and surrounding setup-state traces.

server_hello_legacy_builder.entry_and_opcode: Response builder0x1001e4d0 accepts output buffer/capacity plus a crypto-layout selector and an optional-extra-data flag. Both layout paths eventually call serializer0x10029e10, which initializes opcode4 at0x10029ef8..0x10029f04. This is SETUP_SERVER_HELLO_LEGACY, not opcode3. Protocol version is independently emitted as u16 value42 at field0; it is not the leading message opcode.
server_hello_legacy_builder.capability40: First client-greeting handler computes selector=((client_capabilities^0x40)>>6)&1 at0x1001eaac..0x1001eab4. Selector0 therefore means the client advertised bit0x40. It attempts0x1002399c, which serializes the current public key and computes its SHA256 fingerprint through ZZ0152 selector1 into32 bytes. On success the builder uses the32-byte fingerprint field and skips the larger crypto-parameter producer. Fingerprint failure falls back to that producer. Selector1 goes directly to the older crypto-parameter path. The stateful client-greeting receiver supplies selector1 unconditionally, so the capability preference in the first handler does not describe every state.
server_hello_legacy_builder.schema: Sixteen rows at0x1003627c define required tags0,1,25,2 and optional5,6,7,4,8,9,38,32,33,34,35,36. Serializer emits required fields in order0(u16 protocol42),2(u32 capability bitmap),1(software-version string),25(u16 configuration value from caller config+4). Daemon main initializes tag25 source to literal2, separate from manufacturing MODEL/tag32; its wider discriminator meaning remains open. All fields use the same u8 tag/u16BE length framing as the client greeting.
server_hello_legacy_builder.optional_fields: Tags32..36 are u32 values emitted only when nonzero, sourced from setup-context getters0x10023d90..0x10023dd0 (fields+138,+13c,+140,+144,+148). Binary fields5,6,7,4,8 are emitted when their supplied byte lengths are nonzero. Tag5 is public-key DER from0x10023a10; tags6/7 are that helper's auxiliary crypto outputs; tag8 is the optional-extra-data output of0x10023c40; tag4 is the32-byte public-key fingerprint in the successful selector0 path. Tags9 and38 are emitted as strings when their pointers are nonnull, including empty strings. Tags32..36 are now bound to MODEL,SUBMODEL,REVISION,final color andREGION in server_greeting_verification_and_factory_fields; remaining auxiliary/string roles stay open.
server_hello_legacy_builder.crypto_field_source: Tag5 contains serialized public-key DER from the MDP2 public handle. Exact tag6 identity-metadata and tag7 signature-block choices are mapped in setup_key_provider_contract, including capacity/failure omission and the two MDP2 offsets. No manufacturing-signature verification is performed by the extractor.
server_hello_legacy_builder.capability_bitmap: The response bitmap accumulates local predicates and callback results, including bits0x8,0x10/0x20,0x80,0x100,0x200,0x400,0x800,0x1000,0x2000/0x4000,0x8000,0x10000,0x20000,0x40000. Some high bits are driven by session+1a4 bit0 and byte+1ac; other bits use callbacks from the configuration block and setup-context predicates. Their actual feature meanings remain open. Bit presence is not treated as a guarantee of setup completion.
server_hello_legacy_builder.validation_and_result: Output capacity in the two greeting receivers is0x586(1414) bytes. Serializer uses the shared typed writers and ignores their individual returns; finalizer0x1002e714 checks the cursor-valid byte and required-field presence, then stores the number of bytes produced. An initialization/cursor or required-field failure returnsfalse. The enclosing greeting handler calls send wrapper0x10026798 only after builder success. It does not inspect that send return. Thus a constructed response does not prove it was delivered or accepted by the peer.
server_hello_legacy_builder.send_boundary: 0x10026798 tail-branches to0x10026648 with its two optional arguments0. The delegate rejects size>1414, obtains optional time/context data through a callback, passes payload into0x100281a8 and then calls0x1002500c when framing succeeds. It returns a boolean; negative framing results log failure and returnfalse. Complete framing/transport/state semantics remain to be traced. No assertion that the peer received a complete response follows from the caller's ignored boolean.
server_hello_legacy_builder.stack_argument_join: The serializer frame is0x240 bytes. Its incoming stack+8/+c pair maps to tag6,stack+10/+14 to tag7,stack+18/+1c to tag4,stack+20/+24 to tag8. At0x1001e800..0x1001e81c, caller places fingerprint pointer r21 at+18 and length r22 at+1c, while optional verification pointer r20 is+20 and its length+24. Loads at0x10029eb4/+eb8 followed by emission0x1002a148/+a168 bind tag4=fingerprint and tag8=optional verification. This corrects the initially swapped tag assignment.

server_greeting_verification_and_factory.verification_source: Optional server tag8 is produced by0x10023c40, which requires nonzero setup-context+2d8 length. It hashes the first stored setup byte sequence(context+2dc,length+2d8) with ZZ0058 selector1=SHA256, then signs the32-byte digest using private-key handle context+15c through ZZ0104(signature selector1,digest selector1). This differs from client tag8: the client HMACs the second sequence at+2e8 using a derived secret key. Context copier0x10022978 supplies these two arrays from source+100/+10c with shared length<=12.
server_greeting_verification_and_factory.signature_delegate: libsonoscrypto ZZ0104 at0x8d38 obtains the RSA key size in bytes via ZZ0106, requires signature selector1,key size<=512 and sufficient caller output capacity, maps digest1 to shipped mbedTLS SHA256(type9), and calls mbedtls_rsa_rsassa_pkcs1_v15_sign at0x8e7c. Success returns1 and writes actual signature length equal to key size; failure returns0 and writes output length0. Netstartd supplies capacity256 in this server builder, so larger keys are rejected here even though the generic signer supports up to512. The caller0x10023cd4 ignores the hash helper boolean before signing; no stronger failure propagation is inferred.
server_greeting_verification_and_factory.verification_omission: The server builder requests this signature only when its optional-extra-data flag is nonzero. Missing session input or signature failure clears the outgoing length to0, so tag8 is omitted while response construction proceeds. A zero session-input length returnsfalse before invoking the signer and does not establish any peer-verification state. The private key comes from the concrete MDP2 provider in setup_key_provider_contract; broader manufacturing/client trust checks remain separate.
server_greeting_verification_and_factory.factory_producer_binding: Daemon main constructs its NS2 configuration at stack+1c. It installs callback0x1000a35c at configuration+38 (store0x10002eac). Setup-context constructor0x100227d8 invokes this callback at0x100228dc with manufacturing-ID output and five u32 addresses at context+138/+13c/+140/+144/+148. This binds the numeric server-greeting getter fields to the concrete manufacturing reader, rather than a generic platform guess.
server_greeting_verification_and_factory.factory_status_quirks: 0x1000a35c requires at least6 bytes of identifier output capacity and successful hal_flash_get_mdp_wrapper. It copies the six MDP identity bytes, sets their length6 and populates model/submodel/revision outputs. Successful MDP2 read calls GetFinalColorVariant; MDP2-read failure stores color0. It also outputs region, four stored SERIES_ID bytes, DATECODE and LOCATION to other outputs. The numeric server serializer omits each tag32..36 when its value is0, so missing color output does not distinguish a legitimate zero color from second-page/decoder failure. Revision0 also produces an absent tag34. Typed values remain u32BE when emitted.
server_greeting_verification_and_factory.required_build_fields: Daemon main stores software string86.10-80260 at configuration+0 and u16 literal2 at+4 (0x10002e44/+e54). Server builder reads these as software-version field1 and required tag25. Tag25 is therefore constant2 in this build and is separate from MODEL at optional tag32. Its cross-build discriminator meaning remains to be traced; it is not labeled as a hardware-model field.

setup_key_provider_contract.binding: Daemon main installs0x1000a4f4 at NS2 config+40 (stack+5c at0x10002eb8). Setup-context constructor calls it at0x10022928 with public/private-key output addresses context+4/+15c, a28-byte identity-metadata output at+110, byte buffers at+8/+8c and their capacities at+88/+10c. Callback clears outputs, reads512-byte MDP1 and4096-byte MDP2 through library wrappers, rejects read errors, then delegates to0x10015278. Both key handles are derived from the same manufacturing key material rather than chosen from a runtime key file in this callback.
setup_key_provider_contract.key_material: Extractor0x100150c8 accepts MDP2 magic0xca989b4a, proven raw xoris0x3567 plus signed cmpwi0xffff9b4a. It requires header payload length>=708, copies708 bytes from MDP2+8, and returns1 even when optional signature blocks are absent. Adapter0x10015278 calls ZZ0101 on the first260 bytes to load a public key and ZZ0098 on the708-byte block to load a private key; these library parsers have their own format/key checks. The adapter stores both returned handles but does not branch on either beingnull before returning the extraction status. A true provider result therefore does not alone prove both handles loaded successfully.
setup_key_provider_contract.signature_sources: If header payload length>=836, extractor copies128 bytes from MDP2+2cc into its first signature buffer and records length128; smaller payloads log MDP signature missing and leave its length0. If MDP1+74>3, it additionally copies128 bytes from MDP2+3cc and records that length. This later copy is gated by MDP1 version, not an additional payload-length bound; the full4096-byte MDP2 buffer supplies the accessed storage. These are raw copied signature blocks, not verified by this extractor.
setup_key_provider_contract.adapter_mapping: Temporary extraction buffer starts at adapter stack+14. Its later-block length at temporary+3c8 is loaded via sp+3dc, and bytes at temporary+348 via sp+35c are copied to callback output/context+8, with length+88. The earlier-block length temporary+344 is loaded via sp+358, and bytes temporary+2c4 via sp+2d8 go to context+8c, with length+10c. The names first/second callback buffers are therefore not chronological MDP offsets. Caller-capacity checks can omit a block by zeroing its output length when insufficient.
setup_key_provider_contract.identity_metadata: When the later block is available and fits, adapter copies seven words into metadata output: magic0x3c6852eb from ZZ0086, six MDP1 identity bytes with two zero padding bytes,MODEL,SUBMODEL,MDP2+44c color and zero reserved word. Extractor imports identity/model/submodel directly from MDP1+14/+8/+c and color from MDP2+44c; it does not call final-color/wildcard override for this signed-metadata representation. Server producer0x10023a10 removes the internal two-byte padding and emits a26-byte sequence:magic,identity6,MODEL,SUBMODEL,color,reserved4.
setup_key_provider_contract.server_auxiliary_choice: The greeting crypto helper always produces public-key DER for tag5 when successful. If context+10c (the MDP2+2cc block length) is nonzero, it emits the26-byte identity metadata as tag6 and copies MDP2+2cc block bytes into tag7. If that length iszero, tag6 is omitted and tag7 uses context+8, sourced from MDP2+3cc. Producer output capacities can reject these copies; the caller resets all three lengths on producer failure. The metadata may remain zeroed when the later block was unavailable, even while an earlier block enables the26-byte branch. No assumption about equivalence of these signature layouts is made.
setup_key_provider_contract.trust_boundary: The basic flash wrappers establish read/header/normalization, not CRC/signature validity. This provider/extractor copies signature blocks but performs no verification of either block. Public/private key parsing is separate from establishing trust in the manufacturing data. The client-side verification of the advertised signature/metadata layouts and the encrypted setup-secret key-selection path remain open.

encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.binding: 0x100233b0 passes the received encrypted envelope to ZZ0056 and then ZZ0051 with outputs setup-context+304/+308. The callback loaded at0x10023438 is relocation cell0x1004fce8 (GOT base0x10057cd0 minus0x7fe8), R_PPC_ADDR32 symbol ZZ0070. Callback context is the MDP2 private-key handle at setup-context+15c; optional release callback r8 is0. This is the concrete shipped callback, not an assumed key-ID lookup.
encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.selector: ZZ0070 at libsonoscrypto0x6b14 is stwu/addi/blr and preserves r3. ZZ0051 invokes it with r3=callback context,r4=entry identifier type,r5=identifier bytes,r6=identifier length. Consequently it returns the supplied private-key handle for every identifier/type, or null for every entry if the handle is null. It performs no identifier comparison, certificate lookup, hash comparison or key-file read. With a nonnull private handle, the first entry is always selected.
encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.wire_header: ZZ0053 at0x6318 reads big-endian magic0x886499ca (xoris0x779b,cmpwi signed0x99ca), u32 declared total size at+4, u16 version1 at+8, two copied bytes at+a not subsequently validated here, and u32 metadata count at+c constrained<=8. Metadata entries are parsed by ZZ0026 into264-byte-stride(0x108) slots. After metadata comes one byte recipient count, required1 or2. Each recipient is u32BE identifier length<=2047,u8 identifier type1..5,identifier bytes,u32BE key-wrap selector1..2,u32BE wrapped-key length<=512,wrapped-key bytes. After the recipients come u32BE symmetric-cipher selector and u32BE ciphertext length, then ciphertext. The cipher-selector predicate ZZ0054 accepts1,2,3,4 by clearing bit1 and requiring the result1 or2. Metadata-specific value validation remains in ZZ0026 and is not replaced by this framing description.
encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.length_contract: Every copied variable span is checked against the actual input end. Declared total size must not exceed actual supplied length, and parsed header size must not exceed declared total size. ZZ0056 at0x66ec then requires parsed-header end plus ciphertext length<=actual input end and stores a borrowed ciphertext pointer at parsed-object+1c74. It returns header size plus ciphertext size, not a strict whole-input-consumed boolean. It does not require this sum to equal either declared total size or actual supplied length. Thus trailing bytes are accepted, and the ciphertext extent may exceed the declared total if actual input storage permits it. Netstartd tests only nonzero parse result. Parser arithmetic is the shipped32-bit pointer arithmetic; these checks are not described as a comprehensive integer-overflow defense.
encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.decrypt_order: ZZ0051 at0x67a0 initially writes null/0 to output pointer/length and iterates recipient entries only while selector returns null. Once a key is returned it computes output capacity with ZZ0045, allocates capacity+1, unwraps that entry through ZZ0075 into512-byte scratch, then decrypts the borrowed ciphertext through ZZ0043 with no additional-data pointer/length. Failure at capacity/allocation/unwrap/cipher stages terminates this call; it never retries the second recipient after a selected first entry fails. Successful output is heap-owned and has a zero byte appended after its actual plaintext length. The length remains authoritative, so an embedded zero does not shorten the stored secret.
encrypted_setup_envelope_selection.cleanup_and_trust: Failure after allocation frees that output and resets pointer/length; both normal result paths wipe the512-byte unwrapped-key scratch through ZZ0038. An optional release callback would receive the selected key, but the daemon passes none. Initial output reset does not itself free any previous pointer; no ownership claim about prior attempts is inferred without tracing callers. This path checks supported framing/version/selectors and delegates RSA key unwrap and symmetric decryption. It does not authenticate the envelope metadata or advertised recipient identifier through this selector, and neither this parser nor selector verifies a manufacturing signature. Cipher-specific padding/tag checks and RSA-wrap branches are documented in setup_envelope_cipher_contract. Selector2 RSA-context padding defaults and surrounding setup-mode acceptance/state effects remain unresolved.

setup_envelope_cipher_contract.rsa_unwrap: ZZ0075 at libsonoscrypto0x7c50 obtains modulus byte size through ZZ0106=(pk_bitlen+7)>>3, rejects size>512, accepts only wrap selectors1 or2, and requires supplied wrapped-key length>=modulus bytes. Equality is not required, so extra wrapped-key bytes are not rejected by this guard. Selector1 imports N,P,Q,D,E from key-handle MPI fields+c,+24,+2c,+1c,+14 into a fresh RSA context, completes it, then sets padding1 and digest5. Shipped mbedtls_rsa_pkcs1_decrypt dispatch0x460bc identifies padding1 as RSAES-OAEP with empty label; digest name table0x6f678 identifies5 as SHA1. Selector2 uses the existing mbedTLS RSA context after a key-type==RSA check, with its current padding configuration, rather than changing it here. For the freshly loaded manufacturing handle its context starts with padding0, so this branch initially uses PKCS1-v1.5; an independently mutated external handle would retain whatever setting it had. Both variants delegate the actual padding/private-RSA operation, return1 on zero library error, and on failure return0 with unwrapped length0. Netstartd supplies512-byte scratch capacity.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.key_handle_join: ZZ0098 tail-calls ZZ0183 at0x8394. ZZ0183 allocates52 bytes containing mbedTLS pk context plus legacy MPI fields, attempts mbedtls_pk_parse_key and then the custom ZZ0100 fallback, requires RSA key type, checks private-key consistency via mbedtls_rsa_check_privkey and exports N/P/Q/D/E into the fields used by wrap selector1. Failures free the handle and returnnull. Thus a nonnull manufacturing private handle has these key checks; the higher-level provider still does not inspect its null result before returning extraction success. The freshly loaded RSA context has padding0; its producer/default trace is in manufacturing_rsa_loader_contract.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.cipher_table: Internal cipher table at libsonoscrypto0x2004c contains16-byte rows {selector,mbedTLS cipher type,initialized info pointer,tag bytes}. Constructor0x36b4 resolves each info pointer through mbedtls_cipher_info_from_type. Rows1..4 are {1,5,ptr,0},{2,14,ptr,16},{3,14,ptr,4},{4,77,ptr,16}. Shipped libmbedcrypto definitions0x6eff0 and info structures0x6f168/0x6f130/0x6f080 name these AES-128-CBC,AES-128-GCM,CHACHA20-POLY1305. Cipher-info packed fields, not upstream enum assumptions, supply key lengths16,16,16,32 and IV lengths16,12,12,12 respectively. The envelope parser admits only these four selectors although the library table has additional AES256 rows5..7.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.ciphertext_layout: Encrypted span starts with IV bytes, then encrypted data, then a tag for selectors2..4. ZZ0045 computes capacity: selector1 requires ciphertext length>=32 and returns ciphertext length-16; selectors2/3/4 require ciphertext length>=IV length+tag length and return ciphertext length-IV length-tag length. Equality permits zero-sized plaintext capacity in authenticated modes; unwrap/init still require correct key material. ZZ0048 requires unwrapped key length to exactly match the selected algorithm, so surplus decrypted key bytes are rejected. ZZ0050 consumes the leading IV before decrypting data and retains the trailing tag for final verification.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.authentication_and_padding: ZZ0043 initializes the decrypt context, updates through ZZ0050 and finalizes through ZZ0047. Netstartd passes null/0 additional authenticated data and options0, so the envelope header/metadata/recipient IDs are not supplied as AEAD additional data. CBC setup chooses padding mode0, the shipped PKCS7 default, and mbedtls_cipher_finish rejects invalid padding or incomplete blocks. GCM and ChaCha modes call mbedtls_cipher_update_ad with the empty additional-data span and final mbedtls_cipher_check_tag with the table-selected tag length. Selector3 therefore checks a4-byte tag, whereas2 and4 check16 bytes. A successful CBC decrypt supplies no independent authentication tag. Authenticated decrypt verifies payload under the unwrapped key, not a sender certificate or ignored recipient identifier.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.error_and_output_contract: ZZ0043 returns0 on success and writes update+finish plaintext length. On init/update/final failure it returns the delegate error and sets output length0. Final helper0x4fa4 maps mbedTLS invalid padding(-25088) to5,bad input(-24832) to3,incomplete full block(-25216) to4, insufficient output capacity to6, tag-size/mismatch to8, and other final/update failures to9. Init maps its allocation-specific error(-24960) to2 and other setup/key/IV errors to3. These library integers are not asserted to be NS2 wire error codes. Decrypt may have written partial plaintext before a later failure; ZZ0051 frees that newly allocated buffer and clears outputs rather than exposing it as a successful setup secret. No recipient retry follows these failures.
setup_envelope_cipher_contract.remaining: Trace metadata value semantics, envelope callers/setup-mode transitions and peer manufacturing-signature verification independently. Those unresolved chains keep the subsystem TODO open.

manufacturing_rsa_loader_contract.scope_and_defaults: This block resolves the concrete handle returned to setup-context+15c by ZZ0098/ZZ0183. Shipped RSA allocator0x2c554 calls calloc(1,0x94), then mbedtls_rsa_init0x445b4. Init zeros0x94 bytes including padding+70/hash+74, then sets version word+0=1 and initializes its mutex. The standard RSA private-key parser0x46950 imports/completes/checks components without changing padding. The PKCS8 RSA branch0x2e0a4 delegates to that same parser after pk_setup. ZZ0100 fallback also obtains its RSA context through pk_setup and does not change padding. Thus these successful load routes produce padding0, dispatched by mbedtls_rsa_pkcs1_decrypt0x460bc to RSAES-PKCS1-v1.5. This proves the newly loaded handle default, not invariance under arbitrary later context mutation.
manufacturing_rsa_loader_contract.fallback_entry: ZZ0100 at0x8d04 tail-branches to0x8ac4 with r6=0 (private-key layout). The sibling public-key wrapper at0x8cf4 sets r6=1. Private mode requires input length>=0x2c4(708); public mode>=0x104(260). It copies exactly that fixed length to stack scratch and accepts first BE word0x00000400 or0x00040000. These are accepted markers, not separately enforced RSA modulus bit counts. Remaining input beyond the fixed extent is not used by this fallback. The code does not infer a format from a filename.
manufacturing_rsa_loader_contract.component_layout: After the four-byte marker, mbedtls_mpi_read_binary imports unsigned big-endian components. Public layout has N at+4 length128 and E at+84 length128. Private layout additionally has D at+104 length128,P at+184 length64,Q at+1c4 length64,DP at+204 length64,DQ at+244 length64,QP at+284 length64. These offsets sum to708 bytes. The fallback writes RSA context length+4 from actual mbedtls_mpi_size(N), rather than trusting the marker or forcing128. Component slots are RSA context+8/+10/+18/+20/+28/+30/+38/+40 respectively.
manufacturing_rsa_loader_contract.validation_and_cleanup: Fallback requires successful pk_setup and every MPI import. Failure frees the pk context, wipes the708-byte stack scratch and returns0; success wipes that scratch and returns1. The private handle outer ZZ0183 then requires RSA type, checks mbedtls_rsa_check_privkey and exports N/P/Q/D/E to its legacy MPI fields for wrap1. Successful raw imports alone therefore do not bypass private-key consistency validation. The standard parser is tried first and this fixed-layout fallback only runs on its failure. A parse failure may still produce null output while the manufacturing provider reports its separate extraction success, as already documented.

setup_envelope_metadata_contract.shared_parser: Envelope parser ZZ0053 invokes shared entry parser ZZ0026 at0x3fd4, once per metadata entry, with the actual input-end pointer and caller cursor. It stores entries in264-byte(0x108) slots beginning parsed-object+10. The declared metadata count is<=8, duplicates have no separate rejection, and count0 is accepted. The same entry parser supplies signed developer statements; findings are shared parser behavior, while each consumer interpretation remains individual.
setup_envelope_metadata_contract.ordinary_entry: Entry starts with u32BE raw type. The decoder normalizes type by clearing high bit0x80000000 but stores the raw word. For ordinary entries it reads u32BE value length<=256, checks value extent against actual end, and copies value bytes into slot+8. Known normalized types1..6 pass specific validation. Unknown raw types with high bit clear, including0, are skipped successfully after copying their bounded value. Unknown raw types with high bit set fail. This required/optional unknown-type behavior is concrete: ZZ0069 says whether normalized type is1..6; raw signed cmpwi at0x40e0 rejects negative unknown types. There is no duplicate-type policy in ZZ0026.

known_value_domains.domain: Any ordinary value length0..256; no content check in this parser.

Value must be33 bytes, first byte exactly1 via ZZ0118; remaining32 bytes are copied without further local check. The developer-statement verifier separately interprets this as a SHA256 digest. Setup decrypt does not compare it.
Exactly4 bytes; no numeric range check here.
Exactly1 byte; no byte-value range check here.
Special marker/format/count/borrowed-array representation, not an ordinary bounded value.
Exactly4 bytes; no numeric range check here.

setup_envelope_metadata_contract.type5_layout: After raw type5 or0x80000005, the next four bytes are copied to slot+4 as a metadata word. ZZ0026 immediately tail-branches to ZZ0179 at0x3d24, preserving its semantic call and return. It does not apply ordinary value-length<=256 to that word. The following bytes must be31-byte marker56ea9f16215431a5ba0f50abf164fa176dabb010c4b5719e333159c682ba4c,u8 format1..3,u32BE count,then array bytes. Format1 consumes8 bytes per entry,2 consumes6,3 consumes16. Count0 passes. Validator copies a40-byte internal descriptor into slot+8, including a borrowed array pointer, and advances cursor; it neither copies array data nor validates individual elements.
setup_envelope_metadata_contract.type5_bounds_quirk: ZZ0179 bounds-checks the36-byte marker/format/count prefix and computed array end. Array-size shifts/subtraction wrap modulo2^32, with no independent count bound or multiplication overflow check. Format1 count2^29,format2 count2^31 andformat3 count2^28 each compute byte span0 and can pass this local end-pointer check without their mathematical array extent. This documents static arithmetic/branches; array strides alone do not establish IPv4/IPv6/MAC or any other element role.
setup_envelope_metadata_contract.setup_consumer_effect: ZZ0051 recipient/key unwrap and payload decrypt read recipient descriptors,cipher selector,length and ciphertext pointer; they do not read metadata count or slots. Netstartd0x100233b0 parses then decrypts but likewise does not extract these metadata values. network_shutdown_and_utility_release.shutdown_consequence: Main invokes network-owner cleanup before NS2/netlink cleanup, then daemon-resource cleanup and its reference-counted utility release, then registry shutdown. wireless_interface_control_contract.errors_and_partial_changes: Socket failure logs errno and returns-1. Any ioctl failure returns-1 before updating the disable/test latches; previously successful interface changes are not rolled back. Therefore the software latches can disagree with actual interface UP flags after a partial failure. All-ioctl success or an empty iteration returns0 after bookkeeping. The helper does not wait for association, DHCP, link readiness or a driver result event.

dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.time_difference: The repeated PPC arithmetic computes D(A,B)=signed32(A.seconds-B.seconds)*1000 + trunc_toward_zero(signed32(A.microseconds-B.microseconds)/1000), with subtraction modulo2^32 before signed interpretation and signed64 multiplication/addition. Timestamp fields are seconds/u32 and microseconds/u32 pairs. It does not normalize the difference by borrowing a second before dividing. At0x10027934 srawi r3,r4,31 sign-extends the microsecond difference; the __divdi3 call at0x1002793c receives that signed difference and divisor1000;0x10027940 sign-extends the seconds difference. The rotate/subfc/subfe/addc/adde sequence forms seconds*1000, then adds the quotient. Final0x1002798c raw0x7d434a15 is add. with Rc1, so the following CR0 branches inspect the computed signed high word. Independently emulating the raw arithmetic for slot-age, due and next-deadline expressions matched this formula for30000 cases, including negative fractions and second crossings.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.millisecond_boundaries: For valid normalized timestamps, a same-second future deadline999us ahead yields D(now,deadline)=0 and is treated as due; exactly1000us ahead gives-1 and is not due. A deadline500us ahead across a second boundary, now10.999500/deadline11.000000, gives-1 rather than0. Reversing that pair gives1. Consequently the calculation can distinguish sub-millisecond gaps across a second boundary while treating the same-second gap as a tie. The helpers perform no pointer, timestamp normalization or clock-wrap validation. The signed32 seconds subtraction also means ordinary chronological descriptions assume differences within the signed32 seconds domain.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.slot_allocation: 0x100278b0 examines the three slots in physical order. The first in-use byte+0==0 wins immediately, is marked1, becomes context current+0x1840, and receives the supplied timestamp at slot+0x604/+0x608. That free-slot path does not clear the rest of the slot. Only when all three are in use does it reclaim: eligible byte+0x5f4!=0 and exclusion byte+1==0; first eligible becomes candidate, later eligible replaces it iff D(candidate.creation,later.creation)>0. Thus it selects the oldest eligible creation time at the helper's quantized precision and retains the first candidate on ties. It does not use retry deadlines or the supplied current time to impose a minimum age. If selected equals previous pointer+0x1844, that pointer is cleared. Reclaimed slot is memset0 for0x61c bytes, marked in use, assigned current and given the supplied timestamp. No eligible slot returnsNULL without clearing or updating existing current/previous pointers.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.due_selection: 0x10027b40(queue,now) scans the same three slots, requiring in-use byte+0!=0 and current retry interval u32+0x600!=0. It computes lateness D(now,slot.deadline), rejects negative signed64 values, and selects the greatest remaining lateness. Ties retain the first physical slot. Its initial comparison value is signed64 minimum {high0x80000000,low0}. Signed high comparison, unsigned high equality and unsigned low comparison at0x10027c14/+0x1c/0x10027c70 prove greatest-lateness selection, not first-due selection. It does not test exclusion byte+1 or byte+0x5f4. No eligible due slot returnsNULL and no queue field is mutated.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.next_deadline: 0x10027c80(queue,now,optional_delay_u32) requires exactly the same in-use/nonzero-current-interval gates. It computes remaining D(slot.deadline,now) and skips negative signed64 values, rather than returning an overdue slot with a clamped zero. First nonnegative candidate is retained unless D(selected.deadline,later.deadline)>0, in which case the later candidate becomes selected. Equal quantized deadline comparisons retain the first. Return is selected slot pointer orNULL. If selected and output pointer nonnull, stored delay is the low32 bits when the nonnegative high word is0; positive high word stores0xffffffff. No selection leaves the output untouched. Zero is a valid delay. The saturation is a u32-millisecond delay cap, not an error or a promise that every overdue packet was considered.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.deadline_initialization: 0x10027ab0(slot,min_ms,max_ms,now) stores min+0x5f8, max+0x5fc, current+0x600=min and deadline now+min milliseconds. Unsigned multiply-high0x10624dd3 and shift6 implement /1000; remainder*1000 adds microseconds. When signed microsecond sum>999999 it carries the quotient of /1000000 into seconds and subtracts that many microseconds. Equivalent code is inlined in application builder0x10028268, close builder0x100284b8 and successful backoff0x10028640. There is no input validation or checked seconds overflow. For valid normalized now and configured1000/60000ms values, deadlines are normalized seconds/microseconds pairs; backoff uses fresh supplied now, not the previous deadline.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.verified_consumers: Close-notify retry0x100249a0 uses due selection, restores cached bytes, advances backoff, sends and rescans; reaching maximum invokes cleanup rather than another write. If no due slot,0x10024b28 uses next-deadline and schedules0x100240ac only on nonnull selection. Close output pump0x10024ec8 likewise schedules only with a selected deadline. Connected-state retry helper0x1002526c/0x100252b0/0x1002533c uses the same greatest-lateness selector, restores ciphertext and advances backoff; successful advance calls output pump0x1002500c, and expired backoff invokes0x100247c0 if state nonzero. A clock callback missing in those consumers supplies {0,0}. Full connected-state input/output error behavior and clock callback producers remain separate work.
dtls_queue_slot_and_deadline_selection.flag_writer_boundary: ACK capture0x10027f54 allocates a slot using the supplied creation time, copies eight received-record bytes via SSLcontext+0x5c into slot+2, serializes ACK and sets slot+0x5f4=1 before ssl_write. Only positive ssl_write caches working ciphertext into slot+0x18, length+0x14 and context ACK-plaintext-length word+0x5e4. Negative or zero results do not perform that cache copy here. Application builder0x10028254 and close ACK prelude clear+0x5f4 on their established nonnegative-success paths. This joins a concrete producer to the reclaim predicate, but does not finish every flag writer, incoming identifier domain or serializer/caller transition.

dtls_connected_output_and_submission.working_buffer_and_send: 0x1002500c drains queue working ciphertext, not plaintext. Transport+0x758 is cursor, +0x75c remaining count, +0x760 working buffer. Saved endpoint send callback+0x174 receives (transport,buffer+cursor,remaining). Nonnegative results advance cursor and subtract from remaining, then repeat until remaining0. Raw mr.0x7c7d1b79 at0x100250b8 and branch BO4/BI0 at0x100250bc prove zero is accepted by this loop: it advances by0, leaves remaining unchanged and calls send again. There is no zero-progress guard. The callback is assumed to return no more than requested; the pump does not enforce that upper bound. A callback repeatedly returning0 with bytes pending can therefore spin in this synchronous loop.
dtls_connected_output_and_submission.drain_and_next_timer: When remaining is0 initially or becomes0, call0x10027e8c: wipe1500 working bytes, clear cursor/count/replay fields, save current slot as previous and clear current. Cached saved-slot ciphertext remains available. Obtain time through config+0x24(cookie+0x28,&time), or use {0,0} if absent; call next-deadline0x10027c80. A nonnull result schedules0x100240ac with the returned millisecond delay. A null result makes no timer-registration call here; the pump does not separately cancel an earlier retry timer on that branch. Drain path returns0 and does not itself force transport state CONNECTED4.
dtls_connected_output_and_submission.wait_and_error: Negative send -0x6900 WANT_READ and -0x6880 WANT_WRITE log, set transport+0x16c direction0/read or1/write, and move state+0x170 to WRITING5 unless already5. Exact isel at0x100251b8 selects literal0 when CR4.eq from result==-0x6900, otherwise1. It returns0 while preserving the remaining buffer and current-slot pointer, without drain or next-deadline selection. Other negative sends log, run cleanup0x100247c0 when state!=0, and return the original negative result. Cleanup results are not substituted for the send error. No application plaintext is re-encrypted in this send loop.
dtls_connected_output_and_submission.writing_state_resume: State-table0x1004f7c4 row5 read-handler is0x10025b68; its write-handler slot isNULL. Resume helper calls0x1002500c. A negative return propagates and skips its later work. Every nonnegative return, including the pump's0 for WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE, clears direction+0x16c and writes CONNECTED4 unless already4. It then calls mbedtls_ssl_check_pending on SSLcontext transport+8; nonzero semantically tail-calls connected read-handler0x1002539c, while zero returns the pump result. Thus this wrapper can immediately undo the pump's WRITING5/direction request when another WANT condition occurs. Pending ciphertext can still remain. Do not describe the wrapper's nonnegative return as proof that all output drained. The subsequent connected read-handler behavior and final registration decisions remain separate caller/state-machine work.
dtls_connected_output_and_submission.connected_retry_handler: State4 write-handler0x100251f8 gets current time or{0,0}, selects the most overdue eligible slot through0x10027b40, restores cached ciphertext with0x1002808c, and advances backoff0x10028614. It always sets0x80 and selects0x10 when that return is0 (byte0==1), otherwise0x20. This is a mutually selected pair, not two independent capability gates. GNU e500 decodes the isel at0x1001e66c.
server_greeting_capability_predicates.bit_100: At0x1001e670-0x1001e684, bit0x100 is added only if f_10023ff8 returns nonzero. That helper requires a nonnull configuration callback+0x48, its nonzero result and setup mode+0x2cc !=3 (0x10024024-0x10024050). Daemon main stores f_1000a6ec in that slot at0x10002ed0. The concrete callback returns boolean(global u32@0x1005010c !=0). Callback presence alone does not advertise this bit; the mode veto still applies.
server_greeting_capability_predicates.bit_400: At0x1001e6ac-0x1001e6cc the builder calls optional configuration callback+0x4c and adds0x400 on nonzero. Main installs f_1000a6c0 at0x10002edc. It calls f_1000cc30 (load global u32@0x10050bd8), then normalizes nonzero to1. This joins the actual configured callback rather than leaving an unbound generic predicate.
server_greeting_capability_predicates.high_bits: At0x1001e73c-0x1001e758 session+0x1a4 bit0 adds BOTH0x10000 and0x8000. At0x1001e75c-0x1001e774 session byte+0x1ac !=0 adds0x20000. These conditions are directly before serializer argument assembly; they describe advertised bitmap values, not peer acceptance or completed setup.
server_greeting_capability_predicates.residual: The native predicates above do not establish names for the advertised capabilities. The two globals, setup/session flags and remaining configuration callbacks still require full producer/meaning traces. Other bitmap arms are not claimed complete.

bin_wacd.name: wacd (wireless access config)
bin_wacd.summary: wacd (/wifi/wacd): the Apple WAC (Wireless Accessory Configuration) provisioning agent. It opens the temporary WAC soft-AP, advertises an Apple Device IE built from the unit's MDP identity, and reports provisioning progress to netstartd over a dedicated IPC socket.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): WAC provisioning handoff = the /var/run/wac_mode state machine + wpa_supplicant/netstartd IPC transitions documented under wac_mode.

IPC channel: connects to /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc and sends WAC_AP_OPEN, WAC_AP_CLOSE, WAC_STA, WAC_DONE, WAC_TMO, WAC_STOP, WAC_ERROR notifications ('Send WAC AP Open/Close/Timeout/Done/Stop/Error msg fail'); owns /tmp/wacd.pid; SIGUSR1 simulates a WAC timeout ('USR1 signal received - simulating WAC timeout'); logs a 'Staying aliiiivveee' keepalive.

WAC payload: builds the WAC SSID via WifiFuncsWacFillBinarySsid and Base64-encodes it ('Could not initialize WAC SSID', 'Base64 encoded WAC SSID exceeds max length of SSID'), creates the AppleDeviceIE ('Create Apple Device IE fail', 'Setting up IE and bailing'), and starts the platform software AP ('Platform SW AP start fail').

Identity source: reads MDP page1 (model - 'Could not read MDP page1 data, cannot determine model') and MDP page2 (variant - 'unknown variant', 'Unexpected variant value %u') through the libflash/hal_flash wrappers so the WAC advertisement matches the hardware SKU.

Resolved: wacd internals - links libwifi (WifiFuncsWacFillBinarySsid, PlatformSoftwareAccessPoint{Start,Stop}), libsonosutils IPC (InitializeIPCContext -> /tmp/netstartd_wac.ipc), libsonos-mdp (sonosMdpSerialToString + sonosGetFinalColorVariant + sonosGetColorVariantString) and libflash (hal_flash_get_mdp{,2}). The WAC soft-AP SSID is built from MDP: serial hex + color-variant name, base64-encoded with a length guard ('Base64 encoded WAC SSID exceeds max length of SSID'). Advertised Bonjour service type literal 'com.sonos.protocol.WirelessSetup'. Milestone strings {Configuration Started, Configuration Received, Configuration Complete} feed WAC_STA progress. Control: SIGUSR1 = 'simulating WAC timeout' test hook; 'Setting up IE and bailing' = IE-broadcast-only mode (no soft-AP); 'Staying aliiiivveee' keepalive log.

Resolved: failure ladder - 'Could not get flash info' (hal_flash_info_init), 'Could not read MDP page1 data, cannot determine model' (fatal), 'Could not read MDP page2 data, unknown variant'/'Unexpected variant value %u' (warn-only), 'Platform SW AP start fail %u', 'Create Apple Device IE fail %u'. Outbound message set to netstartd proven: WAC_AP_OPEN, WAC_AP_CLOSE, WAC_TMO(timeout), WAC_DONE, WAC_STOP, WAC_ERROR.

Resolved: the WAC milestone channel carries NO credential payload - the dispatcher (0x10002b60) maps state r31->{4:'Send WAC Done msg fail',5:'Send WAC Stop',6:'Send WAC Error'} and calls sender f_10002a68 with a bare u32 message id {9=AP_DONE path, 0xb=STOP, 0xc=ERROR}; no field bytes are serialized. The Apple credential handshake (MFi WAC) rides the soft-AP WirelessSetup bonjour service entirely outside this IPC - anacapad/netstartd see only the milestone ids.
Established: full wacd flow - MDP->SSID synthesis, soft-AP + Apple Device IE, WirelessSetup bonjour service, 6-msg progress channel to netstartd, USR1 timeout test hook.

bin_wpa_supplicant.name: wpa_supplicant (Sonos build)
bin_wpa_supplicant.summary: wpa_supplicant v2.10 (/wifi/wpa_supplicant) with a custom '-D sonos' driver wrapper instead of nl80211, bound to ath0 and bridge br0. Config is generated on the fly by /wifi/wpaconfig (or manually by /wifi/sta-assoc) rather than shipped.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Sonos build = stock supplicant driven through wpaconfig/sta-assoc + htapsatwpa.conf; control-interface events feed netstartd.

Launch contract (from sta-assoc): 'wpa_supplicant -s -B -D sonos -i ath0 -b br0 -c <conf>' - syslog logging, daemonized, custom 'sonos' driver, bridged to br0; sta-assoc then pokes udhcpc with SIGUSR1 to force a DHCP attempt.

Config generation (/wifi/wpaconfig): writes /var/run/wpa_supplicant.conf with eapol_version=1 + ap_scan=1, then one 'network={ssid=<hex>,scan_ssid=1,psk=<hex>,priority=2}' block per credential plus an open 'key_mgmt=NONE' fallback block for each SSID; sources credentials from NFWSSID/NFWPwd keyval fields of a settings file, or from an SSID-list file of 'SSID=<hexssid>:<hexkey>' lines (SSID_FILE=1 mode).

Driver-side mirroring: wpaconfig pushes the allowed STA SSID list into the Atheros driver with 'athconfig stassidlistclr ath0', 'athconfig wossidclr ath0' and 'athconfig stassidlistadd ath0 <SSIDHEX> <KEYLEN>' - the driver enforces the SSID whitelist independently of supplicant scanning.
Debug knobs: /jffs/debug/wpa_proto, /jffs/debug/wpa_ptk, /jffs/debug/wpa_gtk inject proto=/pairwise=/group= overrides into generated configs.

Build surface: strings show the standard v2.10 feature set (SAE, PMF/IGTK/BIGTK install paths, RRM, Gas/ANQP, bssid_ignore/bssid_accept, roaming_consortiums) plus the 'sonos' driver wrapper ('Override interface parameter: driver/ctrl_interface/bridge'); the Sonos-specific part is the driver shim, the supplicant core is upstream.

Resolved: the '-D sonos' driver ops surface is fully enumerable in rodata (0x1004c2d4-0x1004c460): wpa_driver_ops 'sonos' desc 'SONOS Station Mode Driver' binds {sonos_driver_init, deinit, get_capa, get_mac, get_state, get_bssid, get_ssid, get_scan_results, associate, deauthenticate, set_countermeasures, set_key, flush_pmkid, remove_pmkid, add_pmkid} plus the event channel {sonos_nl_event, sonos_nl_event_receive} and the raw dispatcher sonos_ioctl. Failure text 'IOCTL %ld failed r: %d m: %s' logs every private-ioctl return inside the wrapper at ~0x10037d54.

Driver ops table fully bound (wpa_driver_ops 'sonos'/'SONOS Station Mode Driver' at rodata 0x1004c480, custom slot order): slot2=get_bssid(0x1003818c), 3=get_ssid(0x10038238), 4=set_key(0x10037f80), 5=init(0x100374f8), 6=deinit(0x100371dc), slot7 NULL, 8=set_countermeasures(0x10037f18), 9=deauthenticate(0x10037eb0), 10=associate(0x10037e2c), 11=add_pmkid(0x10037148), 12=remove_pmkid(0x10037108), 13=flush_pmkid(0x100370cc), 14=get_capa(0x10037188), slot18=get_mac(0x10037380), slot24=get_scan_results(0x100382c8), slot31=scan(0x10037da4, logs 'scan requested'). Handler presence alone does not prove a transport operation; the PMKSA slots are logging/no-op stubs as established below.

Private ioctl argument map closed in f_10037cb0: the ifreq at stack+0x2c contains the interface name copied with a 16-byte bound and explicitly terminated at byte 15; ifreq+0x10 points to the five-word block at stack+0x18. Stores at 0x10037cd4-0x10037cec bind block offsets {0:r4 subcommand,4:r5 operand or buffer pointer,8:r6 length/secondary operand,0xc:r7,0x10:r8}. All examined command callers explicitly zero the last two operands. The wrapper issues ioctl(fd stored at driver+0x24,0x89f0,&ifreq) at 0x10037d1c and preserves the ioctl result, logging and returning -1 on negative results. errno 11 additionally invokes f_10037304 before return; this is not a retry of the ioctl within the wrapper.

Concrete per-command bindings, including scalar rather than pointer operands: scan f_10037da4 passes {0x130,0,0,0,0}. Associate f_10037e2c passes {0x131,params[+0x4c],params[+0x50],0,0}. Deauthenticate f_10037eb0 passes {0x139,incoming reason r5,0,0,0}; countermeasures f_10037f18 passes {0x138,incoming enable r4,0,0,0}. Query f_100380d0 passes {0x12e,stack-buffer,1076,0,0}, rejects a zero BSSID checked at buffer+0x35, and copies the buffer to driver+0x2c only on success. Thus the old universal {cmd,buf,len} description is incomplete: command-specific scalar operands share the same words.

Set-key f_10037f80 has two concrete layouts: when key-params+4 is zero it sends {0x133,params+0xc value,params+8 value,0,0} (0x10038004-0x10038018). Otherwise it zeroes a 56-byte payload, copies optional six-byte peer address to payload+0, key bytes from params+0x1c into payload+6 with length params+0x20, stores that length at payload+0x28, params+0xc at payload+0x30 and params+0x10 at payload+0x34, then sends {0x132,payload,56,0,0}. The fortified key copy has remaining bound 50 (0x10038034-0x10038040), not an invented wire length. A null peer pointer leaves the zeroed address intact. These offsets describe the binary ABI without assigning unproven names to every source-structure field.

The alleged PMKSA/get_capa nl_event residual is false. The registered handlers at 0x100370cc (flush), 0x10037108 (remove) and 0x10037148 (add) each log and return zero without a socket, ioctl or send call. get_capa at 0x10037188 copies exactly 168 bytes from driver+0x460 to the supplied output and returns zero at 0x100371c0-0x100371d8. Independent check of the claimed transport helper addresses: f_1001411c allocates a timeout-list record, adds seconds/microseconds, normalizes at 1000000 and stores a callback; f_10014268 matches/removes such list entries. They implement timer registration/cancellation, not nl_event message send/receive. The scan path uses them to cancel/register f_10037304 after an ioctl. Therefore no PMKSA/get_capa event-message layout exists on these registered operation paths. This does not assert that the separate real driver event receiver has no payload.

evidence.notes: Five-word ioctl ABI built directly from r4-r8 and referenced by ifreq+0x10.
Set-key payload length, index/flags source offsets and command selection.
PMKSA handlers log and return zero; get_capa copies cached 168-byte record at 0x100371c0.
Previously claimed event-send helper is timer-list registration; 0x10014268 cancels timers.

bin_athconfig.name: athconfig / radartool (Atheros tools)
bin_athconfig.summary: athconfig (/wifi/athconfig) is the Atheros radio control utility that every other network component shells out to; radartool (/wifi/N/radartool) is its DFS companion. Together they own channel/Freq control, key cache, SSID allowlists, QoS EDCA, scan, antenna, neighbor blocking, and radar/CAC/NOL management on ath0/ath1.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Atheros radio config + DFS - radar events coordinate channel vacate through dfs.ko with the athconfig ioctls.

Verb catalog from usage strings: setantswitch V|A|B; get/setchannel (+getchannels); scanstart TYPE [SSID], scangetresults, scanclearssid, getacs (auto channel select w/ DFS/CAC/NOL/Radar columns); setopenmode; stassidlistadd netif SSIDINHEX KEYLEN, stassidlistclr, wossidclr; stasetkeylen, setwepkey WEPkey|disable, keycache {0=init,1=free/all,2=clrhw/all,3=bad/all,10=free/4,20=clrhw/4,30=bad/4}, forcegtkrekey; sethhid, setuuid; setnetsettings mode data; ssidinbeaconenable, nsprobeenable, blockadvertisedpath, neighbor MAC allow/filter; getwirelesscnx, getnchains (maxspatialstreams RX/TX), getmcs, getlinkstats [threshTx threshLat], getmibcc, getqosedca/setqosedca qosidx aifsn cwmin cwmax [txop] [minfbp], sethptxqretries ms each total, gettxbackpressure, setlatencybucket ms, settxpower, setintrmitig ath0 rxfirst rxlast txfirst txlast, txtrigger [seqnum], conttx ifs/count/size/burst, senddeauth DA SUBTYPE REASON, packet-sniffer mode (count/mac-filter/len-filter/timeout/conttx), testpoint get/set.

Stats output fields: 'Freq = %u; PHY error count = %u', 'GTKFailMode = %u; GTKFailCount = %u NoGCFailCount = %u', 'SSID = %.*s', 'Security keyMgmt: %s Peer: %s Group: %s', per-neighbor 'Tx pkts/min %d; rssiFrom %d; rssiTo %d; PER %d', rates as 'ath rate: %d Mbps / MCS %d', QoS table 'Q(%d) %3d %4d %4d %5d %3d %2d %3d %5d'.

DFS handling: dfs.ko is loaded by /etc/Configure when present; athconfig verbs nolclear, nolenable 0|1, setnoltimeout, cacenable 0|1, cactimeout, cacreset, bangradar manage the channel-availability-check and non-occupancy-list lifecycle; getacs prints a channel table with FREQ/CM/AGE/CU/APs/LLs/Radar/Flags columns.

radartool: separate diagnostic binary ('radartool (-i <interface>) [cmd]') with commands bangradar, dfstime, dfsdebug, firpwr, rrssi, maxlen, numdetects, en_relpwr_check, relpwr, en_block_check - radar-detection tuning for the Atheros DFS block (some knobs AR5413-only).

bin_dropbearmulti.name: dropbearmulti (SSH)
bin_dropbearmulti.summary: Dropbear SSH multi-call binary v2020.81 (/bin/dropbearmulti). Launched only on unlocked devices: /etc/scripts/run_sshd.sh waits for /tmp/device_unlocked_flag then execs 'dropbear -R -F'.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): consolidated unlock/key story - device_unlock writes the flag + ssh_authorized_keys append path; factory vs dev keys under cert_files.

Version/config: Dropbear 2020.81 built from upstream source (paths ../dropbear-2020.81/... embedded), multi-call dispatch ('Dropbear SSH multi-purpose v%s', applets include dropbear and dropbearkey, 'SSH-2.0-dropbear_2020.81' banner).

Launch gate: inittab respawns run_sshd.sh -> trackrestart dropbear -> waitwhiletrue '[ ! -f /tmp/device_unlocked_flag ]' -> 'dropbear -R -F' (regenerate host keys as needed, foreground). The flag is created by Configure when /etc/unlocked_build_flag or /jffs/system/Configure.dev exists.

Keys: host key /jffs/persist/ssh/dropbear_ecdsa_host_key (ECDSA, regenerated if empty); authorized_keys at /jffs/sys/debug/ssh/authorized_keys (created empty if missing). Console login is a separate channel: inittab respawns secure_console_login.sh on /dev/ttyS0 gated on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable.

bin_chronyd.name: chronyd / chronyc (time sync)
bin_chronyd.summary: Stock chronyd (/sbin/chronyd) + chronyc (/bin/chronyc) NTP client pair against Sonos pool names; the system clock they maintain feeds the household time consensus (anacapad sntp_server) and muse systemTime/time resources.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): sources from chrony.conf + sntp.txt; feeds household clock via SNTP coordinator (sntp_server); muse systemTime/time resources + AC.* vars consume it.
Build flags string: '+CMDMON +NTP +REFCLOCK +RTC +PRIVDROP -SCFILTER -SIGND +ASYNCDNS -NTS -SECHASH +IPV6 -DEBUG' - async DNS and privdrop on; SCFILTER/SIGND/NTS/SECHASH off; no NTS.

chrony.conf: four pools 0-3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org each 'iburst maxsources 1' (resolve multiple addrs per pool name, stop polling pool once one source answers); driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift; logging {tracking,rawmeasurements,statistics} to /var/log/chrony; 'makestep 60 1' + 'maxchange 60 1 0' (step clock only once per operation and only when error >60s); 'port 0' disables NTP serving entirely.
Launch: /etc/runchrony via inittab - trackrestart chrony, waitfordns gate (chronyd cannot make progress before IP+DNS), stop flag /var/run/stopchrony, mkdir -p /jffs/chrony.
Sockets/pid: /var/run/chrony/chronyd.sock (chronyc command socket) and chronyd.pid; the diagprocessd menu item 18 runs 'chronyc -n sources -v' for diagnostics.

Resolved: shipped /etc/chrony.conf - pools 0..3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org iburst maxsources 1, driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift, logging {tracking,rawmeasurements,statistics} to /var/log/chrony, makestep 60 1 (step once per run iff error >60s), maxchange 60 1 0, port 0 (NTP serve disabled).

bin_net_utils.name: udhcpc / brctl / dhcp.script
bin_net_utils.summary: The DHCP/bridge plumbing trio: sbin/udhcpc is a Sonos-forked udhcp 0.9.8 client ('udhcpcd'), etc/dhcp.script is its event hook, and usr/sbin/brctl carries Sonos-specific bridge extensions.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): DHCP client + bridge control feed netconfig_fsm events; bridge topology = SonosNet mesh vs STA mode bridging.

udhcpc fork deltas (strings): signal-gated start ('Waiting up to 60s for a signal to start' / 'Timed out ... starting anyway'), renew steering via /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option (numeric renew type -> 'DHCP confirm/extend lease renew' vs 'init-reboot renew' vs deconfig->SELECTING), a dedicated SSID-change listener socket ('FATAL: couldn't listen for SSID change'), a raw ARP listener socket, gratuitous ARP + zero-conf probe ('Sending zc arp probe', '/tmp/udhcpc_resp_mac_addr'), internal FSMs named TDP and IODP, per-request counters 'rna/rns/rnn/rqa/rqs/rqn/zc/dup', pid /tmp/udhcpc.pid, and a hostname DHCP option.

dhcp.script event emission (etc/dhcp.script): invoked as 'dhcp.script {nak|deconfig|renew|bound}' by udhcpc - deconfig zeroes the interface and installs the 255.255.255.255 + 224.0.0.0/4 local multicast routes; renew|bound rewrites /etc/resolv.conf (search + nameserver lines), ifconfigs the lease ip/broadcast/netmask, replaces default gw routes, re-adds the link-local/multicast routes, and removes /var/run/waitforip to release boot waiters; nak only logs.

Bridge topology: brctl is stock bridge-utils plus the Sonos verbs {setmac, uplink, showstats, showstp}; Configure creates the bridge environment (bridge.ko), setmac assigns eth%d/ath0/ath1/br0 MACs, wpa_supplicant binds ath0 into br0 (-b br0), and SonosNet/STP stats are exposed through showstats/showstp (diagprocessd menu items 11-14).

bin_keyval.name: keyval
bin_keyval.summary: keyval (/usr/sbin/keyval): a KEY=value line extractor used by boot and config scripts, not a persistent store - each call re-parses the given file.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): keyval = the boot/update script KV store; consumers = boot scripts + update machinery.
Semantics: 'keyval ^KEY [file]' scans KEY=value lines and prints the value; -d<sep> and -s change delimiters.

Consumers proven in-tree: /etc/Configure ('mdputil | keyval ^SERIAL' for hostname), /wifi/wpaconfig ('keyval ^NFWSSID', 'keyval ^NFWPwd', 'keyval ^SSID' for WPA config and ssid-list parsing), opt/bin/anacapactl, and the netstartd/wacd flows that read netsettings.txt/localsettings.txt fields.

bin_setmac.name: setmac
bin_setmac.summary: setmac (/usr/sbin/setmac): assigns interface MAC addresses during /etc/Configure, deriving them from the MDP identity page.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): target interfaces = wifi + ethernet MACs sourced from the manufacturing data partition.

Behavior from strings: reads the MDP serial via libsonos-mdp ('Using MDP serial number %s'), reads the radio MAC from /tmp/wifi_card_mac_addr ('Current wifi address'), programs eth%d, ath0, ath1 and br0 via SIOCSIFHWADDR ('SIOCSIFHWADDR for (%s, %s)', refuses overwrite 'mac address already set for (%s)'), and prints 'br0=%s' in keyval form for scripts.

bin_capsh.name: capsh
bin_capsh.summary: capsh (/sbin/capsh): stock libcap capability shell - present in the image but unused by any shipped script or binary.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): capability-shell used by daemon launcher wrappers to drop privileges; identified consumers = the service start scripts.
Binary is upstream capsh: --caps=, --drop=, --keep=, --chroot=, --secbits=, --inh=, --addamb/--delamb/--noamb, --has-ambient, --modes, --strict, --print surface.

No invocation found: a rootfs-wide grep across etc/, opt/, wifi/, init scripts and binary string tables shows zero references; anacapad drops privileges itself via '-u anacapa -C all=eip' in anacapactl. Residual: it is a provisioned-but-dormant tool (available for dev shells on unlocked devices).

bin_pcap.name: pcap
bin_pcap.summary: pcap (/bin/pcap): a libpcap capture wrapper invoked by anacapad's hidden /pcap status route to produce downloadable packet captures.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): output = trace.pcap streamed via the /pcap route; invocation = /bin/pcap with filter args from network_tools.

CLI: 'usage: %s [-B N] [-c N] [-i name] [-P] [-s N] <savefile> [pcap filter]' - buffer size, packet count, interface, promiscuous flag, snaplen, output file, and a compiled bpf filter; implemented directly on libpcap (pcap_create/set_buffer_size/set_snaplen/set_promisc/set_timeout/activate/compile/setfilter/dump_open/dump_flush).

Invocation path: anacapad's /pcap local route builds the command '/bin/pcap - not (host %s and port %d)' - i.e. captures everything except the controller connection that triggered it - and returns the file as 'attachment; filename="trace.pcap"'. Output location/rotation is the caller-specified savefile; no daemon-side rotation exists.

bin_sonosledmgrd.name: sonosledmgrd
bin_sonosledmgrd.summary: sonosledmgrd (/opt/bin/sonosledmgrd): LED manager daemon with seven compiled startup/fallback mode selectors, pattern construction and guarded hardware ioctl application. Full runtime coverage of anacapad R_LED_* modes and their transport join is not established.
bin_sonosledmgrd.todo: Established: complete built-in selector map 0..6 from 0x100ec9d0, pattern-ID arguments and out-of-range rejection are traced; argv --fr selects mode 0 and the boot-marker path selects mode 1, followed by the guarded ioctl chain. Unknown: additional runtime operation/transport attribution, any per-mode join from the larger anacapad R_LED vocabulary, and detailed constructed pattern/request semantics. Next: trace registered callbacks and callers of f_10002a80/f_100050a0 beyond the argv/startup paths, joining actual external reads to runtime operations if present; follow f_10003504 pattern construction and f_1000c980 request packing into the 0x1000caf4 ioctl before claiming full R_LED coverage or numeric runtime message layouts.
resolved_findings: The daemon logger configuration and anacapad-side R_LED names are separate evidence from the daemon startup-to-pattern path. They do not independently establish a daemon IPC command schema.

The former claim that this daemon applies every anacapad R_LED_* mode is withdrawn: shared vocabulary and anacapad-side logs do not demonstrate a daemon transport/dispatch join for every mode. Independently recovered daemon selectors 0..6 are FACTORY_RESET, BOOTING, JOIN_HH, JOIN_HH_OPEN, BYPASS_BLOCKED, BYPASS and CLONE_CHECK_FAIL, as named by the diagnostic string referenced in each native arm. These bounded built-in selectors must not be equated with the larger anacapad runtime enum.

Pattern record format: 'cksum=%08x, flags=%04x repeats=%u num_steps=%u led_ids=%08x' with per-step 'step[%d]= r=%02x, g=%02x b=%02x hold_time=%u fade=%u' - RGB step sequences with hold/fade timing, repeated and bitmasked across LED ids; writes through hal_led_open/brightness with a hal token guard (led_get_hal_token), plus led_set_feedbackFlash and captouch default-color control.

Lifecycle: /etc/runledmgrd respawns it with trackrestart and a stale-pid watchdog loop; --fr runs the factory-reset flash pattern (driven by frcheck rc != 1 in Configure); /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led marks boot-time LED activity; writes /var/run/sonosledmgrd.pid.

Logger: /opt/conf/sonosledmgrd_logger.toml (/jffs/conf/ override first) - sonosledmgrd.log at 256KB rotating 64KB preserved, defaultLevel=4 (WARN), domains {ledmgrd, LEDManager, ledmgr-server, leds_zp} at level 6 (INFO).

Prior inline-dispatch premise disproved at instruction level: f_10080e4c seeds a 624-word state array using multiplier 0x6c078965 (0x10080ec4-0x10080ecc), iterates indices 1..623, then stores index 624 at object+0x9c0. f_10081160 combines adjacent high/low bits, xors state word index+397, shifts by one, and conditionally xors 0x9908b0df (0x100811d4-0x10081218). f_100810a0 consumes that state and tempers the returned word with shifts 11/7/15/18 and masks 0x9d2c5680/0xefc60000 at 0x100810e0-0x10081138. These exact constants and dataflow identify MT19937 random-number generation. Bounds 226 and 622 divide the twist passes; they are neither a request-kind domain nor message-length bounds. No socket or LED-handler call occurs in the alleged dispatch loop.

Independent falsification of the earlier framing claim: instructions at 0x100e854c/0x100e856c/0x100e8588 only load r5=4 and call f_1004623c, not read(fd,buf,4). f_1004623c forwards its arguments to wmemcpy@plt at 0x1004627c (unless count zero), showing wide-character memory movement in an object operation, not connection reads. Also hostPort at 0x100ed394 is adjacent to logging-destination fields UDP, hostIP and STDERR, not a proven LED IPC field. Socket imports and these unrelated library helpers therefore do not establish a wire format. Any additional runtime command path still requires a demonstrated transport/dispatch join and is not assigned fabricated numeric ids.

Reachable startup-to-hardware path in the daemon itself: 0x100024c4 sets mode argument 1 and 0x100024c8 calls f_10002a80. That function selects a pattern through f_1000452c at 0x10002acc; a zero selection result returns without applying it. On nonzero selection it calls f_10002858, and only a nonzero result proceeds to f_100050a0 at 0x10002b10. The apply routine requires a non-null token at 0x100050d0-0x100050d4 and calls f_1000ca54 at 0x100050e0. That callee checks handle/state fields, constructs the request through f_1000c980 and calls ioctl at 0x1000caf4 with request 0x800cfc9c. This establishes a conditional startup pattern path, not a census proving or disproving an external request server.

Complete built-in selector dispatch: f_1000452c compares unsigned r4 with 6 at 0x10004534, rejects larger values through zero-result path 0x10004890, and dispatches via signed offsets from fixed table base 0x100ec9d0 at 0x10004560-0x1000456c. Rows 0..6 target 0x10004690/0x100046e0/0x10004770/0x100047c0/0x10004840/0x10004570/0x10004600 respectively. Following shared tails as well as local arms gives pattern-ID arguments to f_10003504 of {0:4 then 9, 1:9 then 7, 2:4 then 7, 3:4 only, 4:10 then 4, 5:1 then 4, 6:0 then 9}. Each call supplies r6=750 and r7=0; no time unit is assigned here. Two-call cases pass the pattern destinations at the loaded object+0xc pointer and that pointer+8. Selector 3 additionally sets owner byte+0xb to 1 at 0x10004818. All seven handled selectors return 1, not a proof that hardware application succeeded.

A known external input is argv, not an inferred runtime IPC request: when argc>1, 0x1000236c-0x10002378 compares argv[1] case-insensitively with --fr at literal 0x100ec6d8. Equality leaves r3=0 from strcasecmp and 0x10002388 passes that value to f_10002a80, selecting FACTORY_RESET mode 0. The separate boot-marker path passes literal mode 1 at 0x100024c4-0x100024c8. Neither branch demonstrates that all anacapad R_LED operations are dispatched by this daemon.

evidence.notes: MT19937 twist constant 0x9908b0df; state seeding and tempering corroborate, not IPC dispatch.
Alleged four-byte reads actually call wmemcpy.
Startup supplies mode 1 to f_10002a80; selection and token gates precede apply at 0x10002b10.
f_100050a0 calls guarded f_1000ca54, which constructs the request and issues ioctl 0x800cfc9c.
Seven signed fixed-base offsets independently read and joined to selector arms and pattern-ID calls; unsigned selectors above 6 return zero.
Case-insensitive argv[1] comparison with --fr; equal return zero becomes mode-0 argument to f_10002a80 at 0x10002388.

bin_busybox_applets.name: busybox applet inventory
bin_busybox_applets.summary: BusyBox v1.35.0 multi-call binary (/bin/busybox, 526KB PPC MSB) providing init and the shell/utilities the boot and daemon scripts run on.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): Sonos-relevant applets = the applet table lists available commands (httpd not present; flash/tftp tools per config).

Full compiled-in applet list (133, extracted from the packed applet_names table): [[ arping ash awk basename blkid cat chgrp chmod chown chvt clear cmp cp cttyhack cut date dd df dirname dmesg dnsdomainname du echo egrep env expand expr false fbset fgrep find fold free ftpget ftpput getopt getty grep gunzip gzip halt head hexdump hostname hwclock ifconfig ifdown ifup init insmod iostat kill killall ln login ls lsmod lsof lspci makedevs md5sum mdev mkdir mkfifo mknod modinfo more mount mpstat mv nc netstat nslookup od patch pidof ping ping6 pmap poweroff printf ps pwd reboot reset rm rmdir rmmod route rtcwake rx sed seq sh sha1sum sha256sum sha512sum sleep sort strings stty sync sysctl tail tar taskset tee test time top touch traceroute traceroute6 true tty umount uname uniq uptime usleep uudecode uuencode vi watchdog wc wget which xargs yes zcat

Sonos-relevant subset: init (parses /etc/inittab: sysinit=/etc/Configure, respawn for sshd/ledmgrd/netstartd/mdnsd/diagprocessd/anacapad/chronyd/sddpd/console-login, shutdown=/etc/init.d/rcK, ctrlaltdel=reboot), insmod/lsmod/rmmod for the /modules + /wifi/N .ko stack, ifconfig/route/netstat + mdev for device nodes, hwclock/rtcwake, watchdog, dmesg, killall/pidof used by rundaemon.sh helpers, wget/nc for diagnostics, and getty is bypassed in favor of secure_console_login.sh.
