kmod_sonos.name: Sonos kernel modules
kmod_sonos.summary: Sonos kernel modules under /modules (loaded by /etc/Configure in this order): sonos_device.ko -> chk.ko -> hwevent_queue.ko -> audiodev.ko -> ir_rcvr.ko (optional). All are Dual BSD/GPL, vermagic 2.6.35-yocto-standard.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): hwevent_queue consumer = the hw_events readEvent path; device nodes {chk, ir_rcvr, audiodev, sonos_device} with ioctl surfaces documented per consumer.

sonos_device.ko: the substrate - 'Sonos device driver' creating the sonos_dev device class (sonos_device_create/destroy exports, device_create_vargs); every other Sonos kmod registers its char node through it ('Error creating <x> sonos device').
chk.ko: 'chk driver' - registers the /dev/chk character device used by anacapad's watchdog health-check; ioctl-based ('Unknown IOCTL called', copy_to/from_user guards).

hwevent_queue.ko: 'Driver for Hardware Event Notifications' - the kernel side of the hw-event ring (hwevtq_send_event_defer); consumed by anacapad's hw_events readEvent dispatch and surfaced to userland via libhwmessagelib netlink multicast groups {AUDIO,BATTERY,BUTTON,BUTTON_POWER,CAPZONE,HT,LED,SENSOR,TEMP,WAKEUP,SWITCH}.

audiodev.ko: the Limelight audio controller - 'Limelight audioctl driver' + Freescale 'TDM Driver For MPC8xxx' + 'MPC8453Q accelerometer driver' merged. Devices/procs: /dev/audioctl char node (buttons via hal_inputs_get_buttons_state, amp power/mute through tas5708_* calls, 'automatically muting amps due to fault', fault latching 'latched faults cleared on mute'), the TDM dsp char node (mpc8xxx_tdm_ioctl, TDM Transmit/Receive Under-Run + Sync error logs), /proc/driver/ledctl, /proc/driver/mma8453q + mma7660 accel + orient procs, thermalsensor proc, fpga_reg/fpga_data/fpga_all procs, SPDIF interrupt counters (lock/block/parity), button simulation ('Simulating %s button press for %dms'), exported audioctl_updateIrSelect.

ir_rcvr.ko: 'IR Receiver driver' - read() returns raw decoded symbols ('Read must be at least %d bytes (1 max-length symbol)', 'IR Data: %08x'), ioctls set IR timeout and runt-filter duration, write/seek unsupported.

kmod_ath_wifi.name: Atheros WiFi modules
kmod_ath_wifi.summary: The Qualcomm Atheros 802.11 stack under /wifi/N plus the bridge module: load order enforced by /etc/Configure is adf.ko -> asf.ko -> ath_hal.ko -> dfs.ko (if present) -> ath_driver.ko, then /wifi/bridge.ko.
todo: Established: the correct table base and REL32 formula reduce the supposed ~300 leaf cases to 119 non-default slots, with 117 distinct non-default entry PCs; two slots are epilogue-only, and 266 slots share the fallback after ath_lmac_ioctl declines. Outer ioctl framing and selected household-id, UUID, deauth and chain-count bindings are documented. Remaining: join the actual inline/marshal parameter arms to athconfig verbs and field meanings, and audit the other named-handler payloads rather than assign semantics from the first call. Candidate inline/marshal slots requiring that join are 0x4,0xc,0xe,0xf,0x15-0x17,0x19-0x1b,0x1d,0x1f-0x21,0x23,0x27,0x2d,0x2e,0x30,0x35-0x3a,0x49-0x4c,0x53,0x54,0x64,0x66,0x67,0x9b,0xce-0xd0,0xd3,0xdc,0xdd,0xe3-0xe5,0xe7,0xe8,0x137,0x13a-0x13c,0x164,0x16b,0x176,0x17e-0x180. Trace their corrected case entry PCs through shared copy paths and cross-reference the userspace five-word envelope builders. Lower-layer ath_lmac_ioctl handling precedes this switch and must also be checked before interpreting a fallback slot as globally unsupported.
resolved_findings: Resolved (boundary): DFS channel-vacate = radar event -> dfs.ko -> channel switch coordinated with athconfig.

Load order/dependencies (modinfo): adf.ko 'Qualcomm Atheros Device Framework' (no deps), asf.ko 'Atheros Device Module' (adf services), ath_hal.ko 'Atheros HAL' (depends=asf, the proprietary HAL by Errno Consulting/Sam Leffler), dfs.ko 'DFS Support for Atheros 802.11' (optional), ath_driver.ko 'Sonos WiFi driver' (depends=dfs - the Sonos-customized driver on top of the HAL), bridge.ko (GPL, ethernet bridging for br0).

SonosNet control surface: userland does not ioctls the driver directly - it shells to /wifi/athconfig verbs (see bin_athconfig: setchannel/getacs, stassidlistadd/clr, keycache, sethhid/setuuid, ssidinbeaconenable, nsprobeenable, blockadvertisedpath, setnetsettings, txtrigger, conttx, senddeauth) which map onto ath_driver ioctls; wpa_supplicant binds through the custom '-D sonos' driver wrapper.

DFS flow: dfs.ko supplies radar detection; athconfig owns the CAC/NOL lifecycle verbs (cacenable/cactimeout/cacreset, nolenable/setnoltimeout/nolclear) and test injection (bangradar); radartool tunes detector thresholds (firpwr, rrssi, dfstime, numdetects, relpwr/block checks). Channel vacate on radar = driver event -> dfs.ko NOL entry -> netstartd channel reselection via getacs.

Corrected dispatch census: ath_ioctl at .text+0xf85c checks capable(12), then calls ath_lmac_ioctl with an out-parameter indicating whether the lower layer handled the request. Only a declined request reaches the cmd<=0x180 switch. Its table at .rodata+0x5c uses R_PPC_REL32 relocations: runtime target = .text + relocation_addend - 4*cmd, because each relocation subtracts its own entry address but dispatch adds the table base. There are 385 entries and 118 distinct entry PCs. Of these, 266 entries go to .text+0x11524, the printk/-95 fallback, not individual field setters. Values above 0x180 also reach that fallback after lower-layer decline. The previous approximately 300 leaf-arm claim and both incompatible command maps are withdrawn.

Concrete reachability: Linux ioctl 0x89f0 reaches ath_do_ioctl (.text+0x12ddc). It reads the ifreq pointer at +0x10, copies a 20-byte envelope from userspace, and passes its five words as cmd,r5,r6,r7,r8 to ath_ioctl at .text+0x12e7c. This is distinct from outer requests 0x89f1 and 0x89f2. The switch values 0..0x180 are envelope command words, not Linux ioctl request numbers; .text+0x11524 is not an outer SIOCDEVPRIVATE dispatcher.

Verified corrected handler bindings: envelope cmd 0x2 enters .text+0x11428 and calls ath_ioctl_set_hhid at +0x114a8; cmd 0x3b enters +0x10394 and reaches ath_ioctl_set_uuid at +0x11780; cmd 0x13 enters +0x114fc and calls ath_ioctl_set_nchains at +0x11504. Cmds 0x2a and 0x2b share +0x11118 and ath_ctl_deauth_sta_ioctl at +0x11120. Cmds 0x138 and 0x139 both enter the shared epilogue +0xfa18 without another operation after lower-layer decline. These examples independently check the relocation formula; reading each relocation addend as an absolute case PC, or using .rodata+0 as the table start, produces different and incorrect command bindings.

Household-id input contract on cmd 0x2: envelope word 1 (r5) is an unsigned length checked <=32 at .text+0x11428. The arm zeroes a 33-byte local buffer, copies that length from the user pointer in envelope word 3 (r7), checks copy failure, and passes the buffer and low-byte length to ath_ioctl_set_hhid. It does not treat word 1 as a pointer. This is one concrete semantic binding across the shared marshalling paths, not evidence that every arm uses the same word layout.

Chain-count input contract on cmd 0x13: envelope word 1 is passed directly to ath_ioctl_set_nchains. Positive values 1,2,3,4 select masks 1,3,7,15. Negative inputs select the low eight bits of the negated word, accepted only when that result is <=15; this is not a general full-width negative-mask range check. Other nonnegative values return -22. The selected mask is compared with driver bytes +0x552c/+0x552d, then written to both, with spatial-stream counts written at +0x552e/+0x552f. A present HAL callback at +0x8c receives the masks; callback failure returns -22 after the stored bytes have already changed.

evidence.notes: capable(12) at +0xf8a4 and ath_lmac_ioctl at +0xf8cc precede switch. Out-parameter at stack+0x6c gates fallback. cmplwi 0x180, lwzx at +0xf8f4 and table-base add at +0xf8f8; 385 R_PPC_REL32 rows at .rela.rodata offsets 0x5c..0x65c yield 118 unique targets, 266 to +0x11524. Cmd 2 relocation .rodata+0x64 addend 0x11430 yields 0x11428; cmd 0x3b yields 0x10394. Fallback +0x11534 returns -95 through +0xfa18.

Raw outer request 0x89f0 selects 20-byte copy from ifreq+0x10; five stack words loaded at +0x12e64..+0x12e78 become ath_ioctl r4..r8. Outer 0x89f1/0x89f2 use separate branches. Copy/access failure branches at +0x13018/+0x13028.

Cmd 2 length<=32, 33-byte zeroed buffer, user pointer r27 (original r7), copy at +0x1148c or shared +0x11d94, then ath_ioctl_set_hhid; too-long branch +0x12d54. Cmd 0x3b reaches +0x10394 and set_uuid call +0x11780. Shared deauth cases 0x2a/0x2b target +0x11118/call +0x11120; 0x138/0x139 target epilogue +0xfa18.

Cmd 0x13 target +0x114fc. Count tests at +0x8170/+0x8184/+0x818c/+0x824c select masks 1/3/7/15. Negative path +0x8270..+0x8288 negates, masks low byte, compares <=15. Driver mask/count bytes updated at +0x81c0..+0x81dc before optional HAL callback +0x8200; failure +0x828c returns -22.

Rotate audit of .text+0x827c: raw 0x549e063e has SH=0,MB=24,ME=31,Rc=0: r30=(-input)&0xff after neg at +0x8278, not (-input)>>8. Unsigned compare <=15 at +0x8280 follows this byte mask. The previously documented negative-input contract already describes low-byte truncation and remains unchanged.

fmt_upd.name: .upd package format
fmt_upd.summary: The .upd container format, now decoded from package/86.10-80260-1-9.upd. Sections are a linear chain of 16-byte records {magic u32 0x497f1635 (bytes 49 7f 16 35), type u32 LE, length u32 LE including the header, reserved u32} followed by the payload.
resolved_findings: Outer section framing is byte magic49 7f 16 35 followed by u32LE type, total length including the sixteen-byte header, and flags. The shipped chain has version type1 (86,10,80260), feature-text type0x15, three range records type2, certificate bundle0x16, encrypted payload types3/6/4/0xd and final signature0x11. Payload flag4 means enveloped data in this image; version/feature/bundle flags are0 and signature flag1. The feature text includes UBI_RED_KEY_WITH_NONCE, but that string does not establish the inner cipher or an IV/key/tag field split.

The residual forty-byte-block premise was false. For type3 at outer file offset0x249af, the inner header starts at +0x10 with bytes88 64 99 ca. ZZ0053 at library0x6318 copies fields in byte order and reads them natively big-endian: magic0x886499ca, declared header length314 at inner+4, version1 at +8, u16 flags0 at +0xa, recipient-record count0 at +0xc. Byte+0x10 is envelope count1. There is no third magic0x779b99ca and no key-slot selector at +4; the old xoris/cmpwi interpretation and selector claim are withdrawn.

The single envelope is parsed by 0x6534-0x6668: u32BE identifier length20 at inner+0x11; identifier scheme byte3 at +0x15; twenty identifier bytes at +0x16; u32BE unwrap scheme1 at +0x2a; u32BE wrapped-key length256 at +0x2e; wrapped-key bytes at +0x32..+0x131. The tail has u32BE content-cipher selector1 at +0x132 and u32BE encrypted-stream length1616 at +0x136. Header end +0x13a equals314. Thus the alleged keyId/nonce/wrapped-key/tag block conflated a variable-length key identifier, an RSA-size wrapped key and later stream bytes.

Parser bounds and failures are concrete: ZZ0053 accepts version1 only; recipient count <=8; envelope count1 or2; identifier length <=0x7ff; wrapped length <=0x200; and registered identifier/unwrap/cipher schemes. It requires declared header length <= supplied extent at 0x6428-0x6430 and consumed field bytes <= declared length at 0x66b8-0x66e8. Success returns the DECLARED length loaded at 0x66b8, not the consumed-byte count; failure returns0 at0x6380. Thus fewer bytes may be consumed than declared, leaving uninterpreted trailing bytes inside the header extent. /bin/upgrade 0x1000472c-0x1000473c requires 7 < declared length <= section payload size, supplies that length as the parser extent at 0x1000477c-0x10004788 and compares the returned declared length at 0x1000478c. This comparison does not impose exact cursor consumption. After parser success it calls ZZ0052 for key lookup, unwrap and cipher initialization at 0x100047d0; only after that succeeds does 0x100047dc-0x100047e8 require parsed stream length == section payload size minus declared header length.

Native unwrap reachability: /bin/upgrade 0x100047b8-0x100047d0 passes parsed object, ZZ0070 lookup callback and caller key context into ZZ0052. Its loop at0x6a00-0x6a64 walks the parsed envelope count with internal stride0xa0c (not a wire-record size), calls lookup with identifier length/scheme/bytes, and only after a match invokes ZZ0075 with unwrap scheme and wrapped-key bytes. Scheme1 in ZZ0075 imports the RSA operands, completes the key and selects padding1/digest5 at0x7da8-0x7df0 before mbedtls_rsa_pkcs1_decrypt. In shipped libmbedcrypto.so.16, padding1 dispatches to RSAES-OAEP at0x460c8-0x460fc, not PKCS1-v1.5 (padding0 takes the separate branch0x4611c). The unwrap driver wipes the temporary512-byte session-key workspace via ZZ0038; key material is not a plaintext field of the UPD header.

Cipher selection is resolved from shipped binaries, not generic AEAD strings. libsonoscrypto table VA0x2004c row1 is {selector1, mbedTLS type5, runtime descriptor, tail-size0}; initializer ZZ0146 at0x36b4 calls mbedtls_cipher_info_from_type and stores descriptors. In shipped libmbedcrypto.so.16 the type5 pair at0x6f008 points to descriptor0x6f168, whose name pointer resolves to AES-128-CBC at0x4cd78 and packed descriptor word is0x84220500. ZZ0029/ZZ0212 extract key length16 and IV length16; ZZ0213 returns the row tail-size0. Relevant rlwinm fields were cross-checked with GNU e500. The current selector is CBC with no per-stream AEAD tag, despite other library cipher modes supporting tags.

The encrypted-stream split is therefore sixteen raw IV bytes followed by CBC ciphertext, with no integer byte order assigned to IV/key/ciphertext bytes. ZZ0050 buffers the first IV-length bytes at object+0x95, calls ZZ0033 with that IV at0x5b60-0x5be0 and advances the input by the consumed IV count. For selector1 the tag reserve is0. ZZ0047 takes its decryption branch at0x5d08-0x5d1c and delegates finish/padding handling to ZZ0147 -> mbedtls_cipher_finish. ZZ0033 selects padding mode0 for the default decryption flags at0x4cf4-0x4d08. Invalid/incomplete state and finish errors clear output and reset through ZZ0044; they are not accepted plaintext. The outer package signature is distinct from this CBC stream and is not an appended per-payload AEAD tag.

Artifact cross-check: the type3 stream begins at absolute file0x249af+16+314. Its first16 bytes are the IV and its remaining1600 bytes are CBC ciphertext; the declared encrypted size is1616. The other encrypted payload records have the same header layout and cipher selector. Certificate bundle/signature records remain separate top-level types0x16/0x11; the established updater verifier rejects unsupported encrypted signatures, missing required sections, duplicate sections and sections after the signature.

Boundary correction: /bin/upgrade compares payload size r30 with header size r25 at 0x10004734 and bge at 0x10004738 accepts equality. The >7 lower bound remains strict. Equality only passes this precheck: ZZ0053 must return the declared header length, which allows consumed field bytes <= that length. After ZZ0052 lookup/unwrap/initialization succeeds, the stream-extent check requires the parsed encrypted-stream length to equal zero. The loop termination at 0x100048c4 subsequently reaches ZZ0047 at 0x100048dc; the zero-stream case rejects as traced below, despite passing the header-size precheck.

The equality/zero-stream case is fully determined on the shipped updater path. After the header precheck and parser-return validation, /bin/upgrade calls ZZ0052 at 0x100047d0; lookup and unwrap execute inside ZZ0052 at library 0x6a2c/0x6a60. On success, ZZ0052 supplies r9=0 to ZZ0048 at 0x6adc-0x6af4; ZZ0048 preserves it in r26 at 0x5768, clears the context at 0x57fc and stores state byte +0x94=1 through the zero-input isel at 0x5828-0x5844. Only after ZZ0052 returns success does upgrade check the stream extent at 0x100047dc-0x100047e8. If that check and the subsequent output-size gate pass with zero encrypted length, upgrade takes 0x10004854 -> 0x100048c4 without any ZZ0050 call, so the IV-ready mask 0x02 (normally set at library 0x5bd8-0x5bdc) remains clear, as does mask 0x04. ZZ0047 tests mask 0x02 at 0x5ce4, branches through 0x5cec to 0x5d9c, selects return 4, sees mask 0x04 clear and reaches 0x5d44-0x5d54: writes output length zero, resets through ZZ0044 and returns 4. Upgrade branches on this nonzero finalizer result at 0x100048e4 and sets its return to 49 at 0x10004990. Earlier lookup/unwrap/parser/size failures can reject earlier, but cannot turn the zero-stream path into successful plaintext output. Empty encrypted input never reaches CBC finish as a valid IV-initialized stream on this path.

evidence.notes: Declared inner header length and parser-return checks precede ZZ0052 lookup/unwrap; encrypted extent is checked afterward. +4 is not a key selector.
Envelope identifier, scheme, RSA-wrapped bytes and tail fields are variable-length BE metadata.
Selector1 maps to mbedTLS type5 and tail size0; ZZ0146 installs runtime descriptors.
Type5 -> descriptor0x6f168 -> AES-128-CBC string0x4cd78; key/IV extraction each yields16.
Decrypt stream accumulates and consumes IV before cipher data; final CBC branch at0x5d08.
cmplw payload/header followed by bge accepts equality; 0x1000478c validates the parser-returned declared length, not exact consumption. Stream extent at 0x100047e4 is checked after ZZ0052.
Zero remaining input reaches the ZZ0047 finalizer call at 0x100048dc, not an unconditional decrypt-success return.
ZZ0052 passes r9=0 to ZZ0048 at 0x6af4; initialization preserves the flag and sets context state +0x94 to 1 at 0x5844.
Missing IV-ready mask 0x02 takes 0x5d9c; mask 0x04 is also clear, so return 4, output zero and reset at 0x5d44-0x5d54.
Zero stream skips ZZ0050; nonzero ZZ0047 result at 0x100048e4 leads to updater return 49 at 0x10004990.
Loads declared header length into return r3; computes consumed bytes at 0x66bc and returns success for consumed <= declared via 0x66cc/0x66e4. Earlier 0x642c requires declared <= supplied extent.
ZZ0052 performs lookup callback at library 0x6a2c and unwrap at 0x6a60. Success is tested at 0x100047d4-0x100047d8 before stream extent comparison at 0x100047e4.

fmt_device_payload.name: device-payload.bin format
fmt_device_payload.summary: The standalone device-payload artifact has a .bit-style FPGA configuration header and one binary body. It is separate from kernel.uImage and rootfs.squashfs. Earlier manufacturing/calibration-TLV interpretations were caused by a wrong-width length read.
fmt_device_payload.todo: Established: complete outer extents, an initial length-consistent sixteen-bit Type-1/Type-2 configuration packet interpretation after sync at file+0x7d, and libflash.so.1 FPGA writer 0x3a78-0x3a90. Unknown: actual updater type0x0d-to-file/programming/boot join, per-register/configuration effects and hardware behavior. Next: join type0x0d updater output to libflash.so.1 hal_flash_reprogram_flash at 0x373c and its f_34c0 writer; validate packet/count handling after the +0xd3 extended-count block against the concrete consumer and bind register writes before assigning hardware effects. The body is not a demonstrated calibration TLV stream.
resolved_findings: Byte-exact framing disproves the calibration-TLV interpretation. The 54757-byte shipped artifact starts with u16BE value9 at file+0, nine prologue bytes 0ff00ff00ff00ff000 at +2, then u16BE value1 at +0xb and ASCII a at +0xd. The a record has u16BE length32 at +0xe and NUL-terminated top_level.ncd;UserID=0xFFFFFFFF at +0x10. Thus 0x0161 was a conflation of the preceding word and the a tag, not a sixteen-bit record ID.

The b/c/d records use one-byte tags and u16BE lengths: b at +0x30 has length11 and string 3s50avq100; c at +0x3e has length11 and string 2012/06/14; d at +0x4c has length9 and string 23:19:49. The part-like value, NCD source filename and framing are consistent with a Xilinx .bit-style FPGA configuration artifact, not evidence of per-channel gain or radio calibration arrays.

The decisive extent is tag e at file+0x58. Its next FOUR bytes 00 00 d5 88 form u32BE length54664. Its binary value starts +0x5d and ends at +0xd5e5, exactly EOF. The first32 value bytes are ff, with aa99 at absolute +0x7d. There is no tag0xd5, no length35071 calibration record, and no separate trailing pages at +0x895d. The previously alleged nested TLVs were arbitrary words inside this one binary payload.

Native support for an FPGA flash target exists independently: libflash.so.1 hal_flash_reprogram_flash at 0x373c scans partition descriptors, and 0x3a78-0x3a90 emits Writing fpga to partition %d using the relocation at library VA0x1ff18 -> string0x3eb4 before calling its write helper f_34c0. This establishes a real FPGA writer, not yet the full type0x0d-to-standalone-file join or the packet/register semantics of the binary body. Those require further native tracing; no claim of an unreachable proprietary calibration producer remains.

As a falsification check on the proposed packet lengths, walking the entire body after sync with sixteen-bit Type-1 counts and the Type-2 extended count yields 49 packets ending exactly at file+0xd5e5 (EOF), without an overrun or unclassified header. The large block ends at +0xd599; the suffix consists of further count-consistent write/NOP candidates. This strengthens the packet-framing interpretation but does not independently identify register names or configuration effects.

Initial e-body framing is recoverable from the artifact without a boot-consumer join: sync word 0xaa99 at file+0x7d is followed by big-endian sixteen-bit words 0x30a1 0x0007, 0x2000 and 0x3161 0x09ee. These are consistent with Type-1 write/NOP packets: top-three-bit type 1, opcode bits, register field and low-five-bit data count; the count-one writes consume their following word while 0x2000 has count zero. At +0xd3, header 0x5060 is followed by extended count words 0x0000 0x6a60 at +0xd5/+0xd7, consistent with a Type-2 write carrying 27232 sixteen-bit words from +0xd9. Thus aa99 is a configuration synchronization candidate, not a nested calibration record. Packet-grammar interpretation is supported by consecutive length-consistent headers, but per-register and hardware-effect names are not established by this byte pattern alone.

sonos_custom_libs.name: Sonos-custom shared libraries
sonos_custom_libs.summary: Sonos-built shared libraries supply manufacturing, hardware, IPC, time, crypto and telemetry functions. Concrete direct-import consumers are recoverable from ELF relocation names and executable branch sites; a daemon-level dependency or export name alone does not establish all per-export callers or runtime binding.
todo: Established: concrete IPC/reset/telemetry/crypto export-to-consumer edges, symbol definition addresses and direct-PLT reconstruction method. Remaining: reconcile all libsonos* definitions with consumer relocation imports, verify ambiguous shared symbol owners against DT_NEEDED/loader lookup, then propagate indirect/GOT callbacks, data exports and dlsym names into their actual call sites. Start with ReadIPCHeader and report_event sampled edges, then audit unassigned imports and crypto-wrapper dispatch. Do not equate a needed library, an exported symbol or a bounded direct-branch scan with an exhaustive consumer map. This remains actionable static work.
resolved_findings: The custom-library boundary is established by shipped objects and exported functions, but the old per-lib-owner map is not an exhaustive per-export call graph. Defined symbols shared between objects and indirect/GOT/dlsym dispatch require separate treatment.

Sonos-built set: libsonosutils.so.1 (IPC helpers incl. ReadIPCHeader/WriteIPCMessage + sonosFactoryResetFull + arch info), libsonosminiutils.so.1 (file/int helpers, syslog glue), libsonos-mdp.so.1 (MDP serial/series/cert-variant accessors), libsonoscrypto.so.3 (mbedtls-wrapped crypto incl. sonosRcbVerifySig for .upd/rcb), libsonos-certval.so.2 + libsonos-root-cert-bundle.so.2 (cert validation + bundled roots), libsonos-time-c.so.1 (timeval math + sonosClockGetTime), libsonoseventreporter.so.1 (report_event telemetry), libsonossbcpacket.so.1 (satellite SBC packet codec), libsonossyslog.so.1 (syslog extension used by wpa_supplicant), libflash.so.1 (hal_flash_* mtd/MDP/FSN access), libsyslib_hal.so.1 (the hal_* device layer: audioctl, inputs/buttons/captouch/orientation, amps power/mute/hipower/rails, detect cable states, thermal, IR, gpio switches), libhwmessagelib.so.1 (hw-event netlink multicast groups AUDIO/BATTERY/BUTTON/BUTTON_POWER/CAPZONE/HT/LED/SENSOR/TEMP/WAKEUP/SWITCH), libwifi.so.1 (the 72-export WifiFuncs* API consumed by netstartd/wacd).

Stock third-party set: glibc family (libc/libm/libdl/libpthread/libresolv/libanl/libatomic/libcrypt/libutil/libthread_db/libnss_*/ld.so.1), libgcc_s, libz 1.2.11, mbedtls 2.x trio (mbedcrypto.16/mbedtls.21/mbedx509.7), ffmpeg libavcodec.59/libavformat.59/libavutil.57 (WMA etc.), libmpg123 (mp3), libdcadec (DTS), libsbc (Bluetooth SBC), libsmb2 (SMB2 client), libsqlite3, libdns_sd (mDNSResponder client to sbin/mdnsd), libpcap, libnl-3/libnl-genl-3, libuuid, libtomlc99, libprotobuf-nanopb.

ReadIPCHeader is defined by libsonosutils.so.1 at0x1508 (size0x150). Direct imported calls occur at anacapad0x105d39a8 and netstartd0x10009744. sonosFactoryResetFull is exported at library0x1c2c and directly called at anacapad0x105e8ce4 and netstartd0x10004d64. These concrete export-to-consumer edges are more specific than saying only that a daemon links libsonosutils.

Telemetry export report_event from libsonoseventreporter.so.1 has direct consumers anacapad0x1068cca4 and netstartd0x1000ae68/0x1000b088. Crypto ZZ0023 from libsonoscrypto.so.3 at0x3a24 is called by anacapad0x10716e7c; its body delegates to mbedtls_aes_crypt_ecb. This separates an imported wrapper edge from the underlying third-party primitive.

A regular-file ELF32BE scan reconstructs per-symbol owner candidates from defined global/weak function dynsyms and matches direct branch targets against .rela.plt symbol entries in shipped consumers. Its output is a bounded direct-edge inventory, not a complete call graph: symlink aliases, data exports, function pointers/GOT, dlsym, static/internal calls and loader symbol interposition are not certified by that procedure. No global complete-export-consumer count is asserted.

evidence.notes: Defined dynsym functions and direct PLT relocation targets joined across shipped ELF objects. No runtime binding trace or exhaustive reachability of every daemon mode is claimed.

Direct executable call words and PLT names identify wrapper imports; library body of ZZ0023 delegates to AES ECB. Large direct-edge census retained separately for continuation, with exclusions explicit.

bin_udhcpc.name: udhcpc (Sonos-patched DHCP client)
bin_udhcpc.summary: sbin/udhcpc = a Sonos-modified udhcpc 0.9.8 (banner 'udhcpcd, version %s'). Beyond stock busybox DHCP it adds: a file-based renew IPC (/tmp/udhcpc_renew_option carrying a renew-type integer {confirm/extend, init-reboot, deconfig}), IP-mode sentinels (/var/run/{specialIP,normalIP}), responder bookkeeping (/tmp/udhcpc_resp_mac_addr records the DHCP server MAC for diagnostics + cloud-reg dhcpMac input), IPv4LL fallback ('Force Zeroconf'/'Starting zeroconf process' with address-conflict detect 'Address duplication detected, INITIATING NEW DHCP'), startup gating on a netstartd signal ('Waiting up to 60s for a signal to start'/'Timed out waiting for a signal to start, starting anyway!!!'), and netif readiness waits ('Bridge is %s ready','Driver is %s ready').
resolved_findings: Decoded: renew-IPC contract - the renewer writes an integer type to /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option; udhcpc reads it ('Renew type: %d', 'Error: invalid renew type %d from file %s: Using %d instead' default fallback) and deletes it after consumption ('Error: unable to delete the file %s'). perform_renew() maps types to {confirm/extend-lease renew, init-reboot renew, deconfig-then-SELECTING}; 'Already requested a renew, now deconfig' collapses a second request.

Decoded: result counter line 'rna:%d rns:%d rnn:%d rqa:%d rqs:%d rqn:%d zc:%d dup:%d %s %s %s %s %s' plus named event literals {DHCP_RN_FAIL, DHCP_RQ_FAIL, DHCP_RN_NAK, DHCP_RQ_NAK, DHCP_DUP} - renew/request ack/nak counters, zeroconf count, duplicate-address count.

Decoded: lease lifecycle - 'No lease, forking to background'/'No lease, failing' (daemonize policy), 'Lease lost, entering init state', 'Received DHCP NAK' -> init, 'No lease time with ACK, using 1 hour lease' fallback, 'Sending gratuitous ARP' after bind, lease/renewal/bound/deconfig state names.

Decoded: monitoring - an 'address monitor' socket watches the assigned address, an ARP socket watches for conflicts, and an SSID-change listener triggers re-DHCP ('FATAL: couldn't listen for SSID change'). Reads /jffs/netsettings.txt for static-net config.

Resolved: the client hook is /etc/dhcp.script - verbs {nak,deconfig,renew,bound}; deconfig ifconfigs the iface to 0.0.0.0 and installs 255.255.255.255 + 224.0.0.0/4 multicast routes; renew|bound rewrites /etc/resolv.conf {search <domain>, nameserver per $dns} and sets broadcast/netmask. Launch contract from netconfig.sh: udhcpc -f -s /etc/dhcp.script -i br0 -w ath0 -h <hostname> -d access.bestbuy.com with -z on station/satellite/sta_and_sat and -F -W 20 on island.

Resolved: the /tmp/udhcpc_renew_option type enum is {0=init-reboot renew, 1=confirm/extend lease renew} - the file is fscanf'd '%d\n', one-shot deleted, values >1 clamp to 0 ('Error: invalid renew type %d from file %s: Using %d instead'); perform_renew(type): type==0 enters the state-indexed init-reboot flow (jump tables 0x100070c8/0x100070a4 over the 9-state DHCP FSM), type==1 runs the confirm/extend path ('Performing a DHCP confirm/extend lease renew' -> renew send, unicast/broadcast by flag); in the wrong states it logs 'Already requested a renew, now deconfig' or 'Renew requested in state %d, back to SELECTING'

catalog_and_accounts.description: Use /MusicServices/Control for ListAvailableServices, GetSessionId and UpdateAvailableServices. Catalog presence describes an integration, not a saved login or successful playback. Use /SystemProperties/Control for account add/replace/remove, credentials, nickname and metadata commands. The audited OAuth actions have explicit byte-length limits in their argument records; valid GetWebCode requests return800 in this build. Password editing reaches the account modifier rather than a no-op. See music_services, music_accounts, account_actions, smapi_descriptor and svc_manifest.

custom_services.description: The /customsd form configures local descriptor overrides using a CSRF token and exact URL-encoded form content type. Its accepted custom SIDs are240..253 or255. The form exposes authentication method, endpoint, resources and capabilities. An accepted descriptor update and account reconciliation request do not prove that the external service will authenticate or supply playable media. See customsd and music_service_catalog.

modern_account_routes.description: The recovered route inventory exposes household account matching and preferred-account get/set, plus group startDirectControlEx and endDirectControl with optional household path scope. It does not list general add/edit/remove-account routes in this resource. Nearby field strings and candidate vtables do not establish an exact request/response schema or every operation result. The household match route has nearby vocabulary userIdHashCode, nickname, serviceId, linkCode and linkDeviceId; preferred operations have accountId; direct-control start has appId/serviceId/linkCode/linkDeviceId/restartToken/accountId. These remain vocabulary, not a claim that every field is required or belongs to the request. Do not use this resource as evidence of generic JSON account CRUD.

modern_bridge_and_events.description: Recovered routes expose a player-scoped call bridge plus subscription creation, renewal by logicalSID and deletion by logicalSID, with household-qualified aliases. The bridge vocabulary includes method, input, output and headers; subscription vocabulary includes durationSecs and logicalSID. Exact schemas, lifetime bounds, callback delivery and individual action reachability still require executor binding. Catalog-change notifications and subscription management are distinct from successful service login. Do not assume a logicalSID subscription path value is interchangeable with the numeric service SID in catalog/account operations. The extracted slot+0xc candidate addresses are interface members; their presence does not prove command execution.

browse_and_playback.description: ContentDirectory documents Browse and related object-navigation commands. Service identifier families are described by browse_ids, browse_prefixes and URI formats. load_content documents content selection and resolution, while cloud_queue and stream_fetcher describe queue-window and stream-fetch paths. Selecting or resolving an item is distinct from playback starting. Runtime service manifest consumers select radio, reporting and audiobook endpoints; endpoint presence alone is not a valid-resource or successful-fetch guarantee. See svc_manifest endpoint and playback-consumer details.

authentication_and_protection.description: smapi_client covers session/device-token requests, authentication-method gates, credential headers, certificate setup and result layers. token_refresh covers refresh states and transaction coordination; account_cert_lifecycle and drm_content_keys cover certificate/key-related records. Stored credentials, a successful SOAP wrapper, an idle transport loop and an external provider accepting credentials are distinct observations. Full refresh scheduling, response policy and key lifetime remain bounded uncertainties.

reporting_history_integrations.description: reporting, scrobbler and play_history distinguish playback reports, Last.fm submissions and household history; they do not imply that every track is uploaded. Spotify records cover discovery, SDK/Connect control and service integration. Shipped TuneIn and legacy migration records describe additional integration-specific paths. Keep service-specific schemas and availability separate from generic SMAPI capabilities.

coverage_limits.description: The strongest audited contracts are catalog/descriptor/manifest handling, public account wrapper validation and concrete settings delegation, custom-service HTTP submission and selected endpoint/playback consumers. Muse schemas/execution, full account persistence and direct-control effects, complete transport/retry policy, reporting triggers, service-specific authentication details and cross-build behavior still carry targeted reverse-engineering work. A route registration, string inventory or passing documentation build is not proof of those behaviors.

music_services_interfaces.todo: Established: the public interface map separates audited SOAP/custom-service contracts from route/vocabulary inventories and connects all main music-service topic families. Remaining: finish the user-visible Muse schemas/results and direct-control effects, account persistence/notifications, browse/playback failures, reporting policy and service-specific authentication gaps identified in their records; verify claims against the relevant implementation before promoting inventory evidence to behavior.

muse.description: the complete muse route registration table recovered from rodata: 603 route records across 67 resources / 332 distinct operations. Each record is 24 bytes {path_template*, flags, 0, handler*, 0, csv_descriptor*}. The csv descriptor 'scope,resource,verb[,subparam]' names the operation; the path template carries {param} bindings. Most ops exist twice: unscoped (v1/players/{playerId}/...) and household-scoped (v1/households/{householdId}/players/{playerId}/...). All muse routes are mounted under the /api prefix: the master HTTP table registers '/api' -> f_100d2cf8 which installs the muse dispatcher (stubs f_100d36c0/f_100d36e4 -> pipeline f_100d2e18), so on the wire paths are /api/v1/... .
muse.flags_decode: flags low byte = HTTP method bitmask: 0x01 GET, 0x02 POST, 0x04 PUT, 0x08 DELETE, 0x10 PATCH (settings-only). Bit 0x100 set = household/settings-class routes; clear (0x2000000x) = playback/volume-class (playback, groupVolume, playerVolume, playbackMetadata). 0x20000000 = muse marker bit on all records.
muse.dispatch: two stubs only: f_100d36c0 (r8=0) serves 332 records, f_100d36e4 (r8=1) 271; both tail-call f_100d2e18 which normalizes the request into a 0x2a00-byte context (header/flag block at +0x416.., buf +0x2594) and dispatches on the parsed csv op name. r6==NULL fast-path returns 0.

muse.descriptor_stream_note: Ordered {spec-pairs, verb literals, op vtables} stream recovered from .data.rel.ro 0x10f9f8c4-0x10fae2d0: the static op-descriptor array consumed by the per-op registration copiers (f_1009a8a4-family). Each descriptor block: {u32,u32} field-spec pairs terminated by 0xffffffff,0xffffffff, padding + op-count, the block's verb literals and param/field names, then one 23-slot op vtable per channel/subparam variant (exec at +0x0c). Verb->vtable binding is positional; where a group's vtable count is an exact multiple of its verb count the vtables split evenly per verb in declaration order.

spec_pairs.layout: per-block: aligned {u32 tag, u32 val} array -> FFFFFFFF,FFFFFFFF -> pad -> verb/param literal run -> op vtables (23-slot spine)

spec_pairs.accessors: confirmed: generated accessor functions (0x20-byte stride, e.g. f_10ac459c..f_10ac4678) each form descriptor-base and write &spec[k] to caller out-slot; spec array is AT descriptor offset 0: per-param {tag,val} descriptor array indexed by param position

f_10927c84 compares its r4 argument against type-like indices; for case 0x70 the packed value in r5 contributes to stores at 0x10927d00 and 0x10927d04. This verifies the local switch behavior, not a direct call from the alarms pair range.
spec_pairs.consumer: The layout switch includes comparisons at 0x10927c84 through 0x10927cb0 and packed-word decode into slots +0x348/+0x34c; a direct join from this block's pairs to each case has not been demonstrated.
spec_pairs.tag_enumeration: census across all ffffffff/ffffffff-terminated pair runs in .rodata: dominant a-tags 0x82 (577x, the type-ref/member-descriptor tag), 0xae (191x, local-REST-op field), 0x86 (57x), 0x12e/0x131 (60x each, paired count fields), 0xb9 (44x), plus the unique-id field space (0x13-0x141 ascending, one per op/field). Dominant b-values are name-table type indices: 0x34 (380x, upnpEvent wrapper), 0x3f (204x), 0x47 (95x), 0x48 (81x), 0x66 (45x), 0x59 (44x), 0x42 (57x), 0x5a (28x), 0x41 (26x), 0x50 (19x), 0x4c (11x) - each resolves to a member type name in the 331-entry name table.

dispatch_mechanism.provenance: f_109eb04c disassembled: it is vtable slot+32 on op objects AND the generic command dispatcher ("Dispatching command (ns=v%u/%s, cmd=%s)")
dispatch_mechanism.flow: dispatcher reads *(this->vt+32) exec slot; if == f_109ec9e0 (null stub returning 0) -> result 90 ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND; else bctrl the real exec; result object built via setter family 0x109dbxxx; iterates sub-target objects at stride 304 (IBT fan-out); refcounted via lwarx/stwcx.
dispatch_mechanism.exec_slot: vtable index 8 (+0x20): real exec fn or null stub: this IS the feature-gate / compiled-out-op mechanism (unsupported ops keep the stub and fault 90)
dispatch_mechanism.exec_family: f_1015xxxx generated serializers: install primary+secondary vtables (secondary-vtable back-offset pattern), then walk member arrays at obj+92..+96 and obj+144..+148 serializing each member: household/VRC/registration ops exec by serializing their descriptor into the lechmere envelope
dispatch_mechanism.auth_gate: f_109db080 (tag "museauth") is invoked inside dispatch: emits "Secure connection required" (cmd needs WSS/secure transport), "Credential is missing", "Scope is insufficient", "Client auth exception": the enforcement point of the per-op role/scope model; result codes flow back through the 107-entry muse_result_codes table
dispatch_mechanism.exec_call: cmd->vt[8](cmd, ctx...) invoked via bctrl; cmd object passed in r4->r27; response object r29 built with fields at +160/+180; targets iterated at stride 304 with refcounted (lwarx/stwcx) sub-objects

evidence.notes: Index-to-label helper uses pointer table 0x10f97094, compares against 326 and returns none for out-of-range values. Reverse lookup f_109ecb90 calls strcmp at 0x109ecbd4. Label lookup does not establish field/type or object/status semantics.

Eight accessors through f_10ac4678 write pointers at byte offsets 0,8,16,24,40,80,120,152 into 0x10f9fc74 and return counts 1,1,1,2,5,5,4,3. These cover 22 pairs before the sentinel at 0x10f9fd24/0x10f9fd28. Every-consumer dataflow and operation/direction ownership remain unresolved.

spec_pair_decode_v2.structure: {u32 a, u32 b} runs terminated by {ffffffff,ffffffff} inside each op-descriptor block, positioned between the 23-slot vtable and the verb literals + count fields
spec_pair_decode_v2.observed_grammar: entries are bimodal: {0x82, 0x21-0x6a} (a=const, b=index-like value across 74 distinct values) vs {X, 0x34} (b=const 0x34, a=wide id space 0x13-0x141 incl. the unique ascending ids previously read as cmd-ids) plus small {n,n} pairs (counts) and occasional b=0x36/0x38/0x33/0x6a/0x4e variants
spec_pair_decode_v2.working_model: Unresolved: both words can be looked up in the name table, but label lookup alone establishes neither a field/type schema nor an object/status contract. A universal semantic interpretation is not established.
spec_pair_decode_v2.unresolved: The semantic contract of both words, every runtime consumer and the operation/direction owning each counted pair range remain unverified. A dataflow join from these static pairs to f_10927c1c has not been demonstrated.
spec_pair_decode_v2.decoded_block_structure: op-descriptor blocks decode further: N x 0x80-byte op records (e.g. alarms: 6 recs @ 0x10f9f8c4..fc44, each {2 data ptrs, 0x109c9854, vtable_ptr, ~9 thunk ptrs into 101c06xx, shared 109d9770, per-op vtable ptr, thunks, 109d973c x2, 10ac45xx impl-vtable, ffffff88, 0, then 10acXXXX impl ptr, 10acXXXX, 109e8570, 109e857c, 109e858c, 0, 0}) followed by a shared 12-ptr block, then the {u32,u32} spec-pair stream terminated by ffffffff/ffffffff, then zero padding + a u32 op-count (alarms: 2), then the verb-name string pool + default-value literals (snoozeAlarm default 'PT0H5M0S' ISO-8601 duration sits in the pool after the verb names). The 101c06xx entries are trivial this-adjusting vfunc trampolines (stwu/addi/blr), confirming the records are vtable-bound polymorphic op descriptors.
spec_pair_decode_v2.pair_tag_hypothesis: Observed labels only: 0xae maps to ok, 0x34 to upnpEvent, 0x82 to globalError and 0x47 to channelMapPair through 0x10f97094. These names do not identify either word as a field, type, object or status.
spec_pair_decode_v2.consumer_layout_dispatch: f_10927c1c dispatches on r4 and consumes r5 to update runtime state, including stores at +0x380/+0x384, +0x394, +0x3a2 and +0x3ac. This does not establish a layout calculator. Its reference at 0x10f7f728 is not a demonstrated dataflow join from the spec pairs, so it is not a verified consumer of this table.
spec_pair_decode_v2.grammar_decoded: The alarms range at 0x10f9fc74 contains 22 pairs before the sentinel at 0x10f9fd24/0x10f9fd28. Label lookup yields ok/upnpEvent, alarmList/upnpEvent, alarm/upnpEvent and globalError/channelMapPair, among others. Field/type and object/status remain competing interpretations, not decoded grammar.
spec_pair_decode_v2.extracted: The extracted streams preserve raw word pairs and name-table labels. The member_name_idx/type_name_idx headings in docs/muse_spec_streams.json are interpretive metadata, not independently established runtime semantics. A complete consumer census is still required before asserting a universal grammar.
todo: Established: f_109ecb5c maps indices through 0x10f97094 and f_109ecb90 searches labels with strcmp; alarms accessors f_10ac459c..f_10ac4678 return counted subranges of 22 pairs at 0x10f9fc74. Unknown: the semantic contract of both words, every runtime consumer, each accessor's owning operation/direction and the post-sentinel words; neither field/type nor object/status is established universally. Next: enumerate every accessor vtable reference, follow pointer/count through each pair walker and both downstream arguments, and compare request, response, event and error paths before assigning semantics.
resolved_findings: The alarms counterexample disproves a universal one-word-per-verb interpretation. The seven zero words plus 2 and trailing zero occupy 0x10f9fd2c..0x10f9fd4f; six names follow. The string table gives the pair labels independently of the post-terminator words.
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_decode: Build 86.10-80260 alarms block: after 22 pairs from 0x10f9fc74, the terminator words are at 0x10f9fd24/0x10f9fd28. There are seven zero words, then 2 at 0x10f9fd48, another zero at 0x10f9fd4c, and getAlarms at 0x10f9fd50. The pool contains six verbs and the PT0H5M0S literal.
spec_pair_decode_v2.per_op_grouping: Accessors f_10ac459c..f_10ac4678 return pointers at byte offsets 0,8,16,24,40,80,120,152 into 0x10f9fc74 and counts 1,1,1,2,5,5,4,3. Each successive pointer advances by the preceding count times eight bytes. The 22 pairs therefore have counted subranges, but their operation/direction ownership remains unverified.
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_grammar: The pair terminator, aligned u32 words, and neighboring NUL-terminated strings are distinct regions. The u32 region does not universally contain one nonzero word per verb.
spec_pair_decode_v2.arity_table: Observed u32 runs include repeated small values and a mixed settings pattern containing 4,1,6. Per-operation arity is not established; the alarms counterexample has six verb strings and only one nonzero post-terminator word before the first verb.

muse.spec_binding_note: Per-op spec binding RESOLVED: each op vtable (route impl.vtables) carries spec accessors at slot +0x58 returning {classId, blob ptr into packed u32 rodata pools}. The index->name lookup is f_109ecb5c (cmplwi 0x146 bound, slwi x4, lwzux on base 0x10f97094 = name-table slot 3) and the name->index reverse lookup is f_109ecb90 (strcmp walk from 'none'). SEMANTIC INDEX i MAPS TO TABLE SLOT 3+i: the first three pointer-table slots at 0x10f97088 are function pointers (f_10809540...), semantic index 0 = 'none'. 331 name entries, 383 object-spec descriptors across 0x10e9ba80 (96) + 0x10f9f87c (287), ~0x80B each, common accessor +0x58, classIds 1-12. Blob grammar = flat {fieldName, typeName} pairs: field slots carry wire keys (ok leads 170 response specs; globalError 561x; upnpResponse/upnpError for bridge ops; accountError/sessionError/playbackError), type slots carry 'upnpEvent' (the universal value wrapper) or concrete types. Repeated field name = type union (e.g. globalError:{chirpRequest|accessoryId|none|wiredSubStatus}); 'none' marks absent/optional slots. 'networkTestId' is an ordinary optional request field (16 ops, typed upnpEvent) whose name comes from the real resource v1/players/{playerId}/networkTest/{networkTestId} -- not an envelope marker. ~1116/1206 routes bound; ~45 unbound routes are outbound/client ops (no impl vtables) whose request shape is the per-namespace verb vocabulary.
muse.outbound_ops_note: ~45 ops ({authorization,catalog,entitlements,groups,history,playback,smartplay,systemReporting,zones} verbs (the full {ns,verb} registry at .data 0x110941d4-0x110943f4) are registered as 'outbound_registry': the player is the CLIENT, requests forward to the cloud over lechmere/WSS. They carry no local impl vtables and no +0x58 spec accessor BY DESIGN) the request body is serialized from the per-namespace field vocabulary (shared_primitives outbound vocab extraction). Per-verb field subsetting is code-driven and not statically enumerable.

(processUpdateAllSettings() GET %s conditional [%s|%llu]); 'v1/devices', 'v1/log_event' (emitted as hm://hwp-events/v1/log_event), 'v1/websocket' (as /api/v1/websocket -- 'could not initialize ws client'), 'v1/config?' (as /features/v1/config?); catalog form 'v1/households/%s/services/%u/accounts/%u/catalog/%ss/%s'. In build 86.10-80260, f_105a7dac calls f_1055030c at 0x105a8274 between clock_gettime calls (0x105a8214 and 0x105a829c). Only afterward does it populate the object at sp+0xb4 (0x105a8300 onward); 0x105a8388 sets eventType to the literal download and f_10559024 at 0x105a83b4 returns a singleton without using the incoming event pointer. The caller loads vtable slot +0x1c at 0x105a83d0, sets r4 to sp+0xb4 at 0x105a83d8, and passes the object to that slot at 0x105a83e0. Those fields do not describe the HTTP response.
